entries.literal: In Liang he again fled to Shu because of a crime; Shu, because he was a frontier man skilled at riding and shooting, made him a personal guard.

entries.zh: 蜀後主王衍，幼年襲位，其政多僻。
entries.en: Shu's young ruler Wang Yan came to the throne as a boy, and his rule was deeply erratic.
entries.literal: The Later Lord of Shu, Wang Yan, succeeded to the throne in his youth; his government was largely perverse.

entries.zh: 宦官王承休居中用事，與成都尹韓昭內外相結，專采擇聲色，以固寵幸。
entries.en: The eunuch Wang Chengxiu dominated the court, conspiring with the Chengdu prefect Han Zhao to stock the palace with entertainers and secure their hold on the emperor's favor.
entries.literal: The eunuch Wang Chengxiu held power at court and, with the Chengdu prefect Han Zhao linking inside and outside, devoted themselves solely to gathering music and beauty to secure favor.

entries.zh: 武臣宿將，居常切齒。
entries.en: The old military commanders ground their teeth in rage.
entries.literal: Martial officials and veteran generals constantly gnashed their teeth.

entries.zh: 重霸諂事承休，特見委信。
entries.en: Zhongba curried favor with Chengxiu and won his special trust.
entries.literal: Zhongba flattered and served Chengxiu and was especially entrusted.

entries.zh: 梁末，岐下削弱，蜀人奪取秦、成、階等州，重霸說承休求鎮秦州。
entries.en: Late in Liang, as Qi weakened, Shu seized Qin, Cheng, Jie, and neighboring prefectures; Zhongba urged Chengxiu to seek the Qinzhou commission.
entries.literal: At the end of Liang, Qi territory was weakened and the Shu seized Qin, Cheng, Jie, and other prefectures; Zhongba persuaded Chengxiu to request garrison of Qinzhou.

entries.zh: 仍於軍中選山東驍果，得數千人，號龍武都，以承休為軍帥，重霸副焉，俱在天水。
entries.en: From the army he picked several thousand fierce fighters from the east, called them the Dragon Martial Division, made Chengxiu their commander with Zhongba as deputy, and stationed them at Tianshui.
entries.literal: He also selected from the army fierce fighters from Shandong, obtaining several thousand men, styled the Dragon Martial Division; Chengxiu was made army commander and Zhongba his deputy, both at Tianshui.

entries.zh: 歲餘，承休欲求旄鉞，乃以隴西花木入獻，又稱秦州山水之美，人物之盛，請後主臨幸，而韓昭讚成之。
entries.en: After a year Chengxiu wanted a full military commission; he sent Longxi flowers and trees as tribute, praised Qinzhou's scenery and beauties, and asked the emperor to visit in person, with Han Zhao seconding the plan.
entries.literal: After more than a year Chengxiu wished to obtain the commander's baton and axe; he therefore presented flowers and trees of Longxi as tribute, and again praised the beauty of Qinzhou's mountains and waters and the abundance of its people, requesting that the Later Lord visit in person, while Han Zhao urged it on.

entries.zh: 〈（《太平廣記》引《王氏見聞錄》云：承休請從諸軍揀選官健，得驍勇數千，號龍武軍，承休自為統帥，並特加衣糧，日有優給。
entries.en: (The 《Taiping Guangji》, citing the 《Wangshi Jianwenlu》: Chengxiu asked to select troops from every army and gathered several thousand elite fighters called the Dragon Martial army under his own command, with extra rations and daily allowances.)
entries.literal: (The 《Taiping Guangji》 cites the 《Wangshi Jianwenlu》 as saying: Chengxiu requested to pick out officers and soldiers from the various armies and obtained several thousand fierce warriors, styled the Dragon Martial army; Chengxiu himself was commander, and they were all given extra clothing and grain with daily preferential allowances.)

entries.zh: 因乞秦州節度使，且云：「願與陛下於秦州采掇美麗。」
entries.en: He then asked for the Qinzhou commission, saying, "I wish to gather beauties at Qinzhou together with Your Majesty."
entries.literal: He therefore begged for military commissioner of Qinzhou and said: "I wish together with Your Majesty to gather beauties at Qinzhou."

entries.zh: 且說秦州風土，多出國色，仍請幸天水。
entries.en: He added that Qinzhou's countrywomen were famed for their beauty and again asked the emperor to visit Tianshui.
entries.literal: He also said that Qinzhou's customs produce many beauties of the realm, and again requested that the emperor visit Tianshui.

entries.zh: 少主甚悅，即遣仗節赴鎮，應所選龍武精銳，並充衙隊從行。）〉
entries.en: The young emperor was delighted, sent him off with credentials to his post, and made the Dragon Martial elite his escort on the march.)〉
entries.literal: The young lord was greatly pleased, immediately sent credentials to take up the commission, and all the selected Dragon Martial elite served as his escort guard on the journey.) 〉

entries.zh: 袁建豐，武皇破巢時得於華陰，年方九歲，愛其精神爽俊，俾收養之。
entries.en: Yuan Jianfeng was taken at Huayin when the Martial Emperor defeated Huang Chao; he was only nine, and his bright bearing led the emperor to adopt him.
entries.literal: Yuan Jianfeng was obtained at Huayin when the Martial Emperor defeated Huang Chao; he was only nine years old, and because his spirit was bright and handsome he was taken in and reared.

entries.zh: 漸長，列於左右，復習騎射，補鐵林都虞候。
entries.en: As he grew he served at court, trained in horsemanship and archery, and became deputy commander of the Iron Forest guard.
entries.literal: As he grew he was placed at the ruler's side, again studied riding and archery, and was appointed deputy commander of the Iron Forest guard.

entries.zh: 從破邠州王行瑜，以功遷左親騎軍使，轉突騎指揮使。
entries.en: He fought in the defeat of Wang Xingyu of Bin and was promoted to commander of the Left Personal Cavalry, then of the shock cavalry.
entries.literal: He followed in the defeat of Wang Xingyu of Binzhou and, for merit, was promoted to commander of the Left Personal Cavalry and then commander of the shock cavalry.

entries.zh: 從莊宗解圍上黨，破柏鄉陣，累功遷右僕射、左廂馬軍指揮使。
entries.en: He relieved Shangdang with Zhuangzong, broke the enemy at Baixiang, and rose through merit to Right Vice Director and commander of the left cavalry wing.
entries.literal: He followed Emperor Zhuangzong in relieving the siege of Shangdang, broke the formation at Baixiang, and through repeated merit was promoted to Right Vice Director and commander of the left wing of the horse army.

entries.zh: 明宗為內衙指揮使，建豐為副。
entries.en: When Mingzong commanded the inner guard, Jianfeng served as his deputy.
entries.literal: When Mingzong was commander of the inner palace guard, Jianfeng was his deputy.

entries.zh: 北討劉守光，常身先士伍，轉都教練使，權蕃漢副總管。
entries.en: Campaigning north against Liu Shouguang he often led from the front; he became chief training officer and acting deputy overseer of the combined frontier forces.
entries.literal: In the northern campaign against Liu Shouguang he constantly led the ranks in person; he was transferred to chief training officer and acting deputy overseer of the frontier and Chinese forces.

entries.zh: 莊宗入鄴，以心腹幹能，選為魏府都巡檢使。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong entered Ye he chose Jianfeng, a trusted and capable man, as chief inspector of the Wei prefecture.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Ye, because he was a trusted man of ability he was chosen as chief inspector of the Wei prefecture.

entries.zh: 從征劉鄩，下衛、磁、洺有功，加檢校司空，授州洺州刺史。
entries.en: In the campaign against Liu Xun he captured Wei, Ci, and Ming, was made acting Minister of Works, and appointed prefect of Ming.
entries.literal: He followed the campaign against Liu Xun, took Wei, Ci, and Ming with merit, was added acting Minister of Works, and appointed prefect of Mingzhou.

entries.zh: 於臨洺西敗梁將王遷數千人，生獲將領七十餘人，俄拜相州刺史。
entries.en: West of Linming he routed several thousand men under the Liang general Wang Qian and took more than seventy officers alive; he was soon made prefect of Xiang.
entries.literal: West of Linming he defeated several thousand men under the Liang general Wang Qian and captured more than seventy officers alive; soon he was appointed prefect of Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 征赴河上，豫戰於胡柳陂。
entries.en: Marching to the Yellow River front he fought at Huliu Ford.
entries.literal: On campaign to the Yellow River he fought beforehand at Huliu Ford.

entries.zh: 建豐領相州軍士，行營在外，委州事於小人，失於撫馭，指揮使孟守謙據城以叛，建豐引兵討平之。
entries.en: With his army in the field Jianfeng left Xiang in the hands of unworthy subordinates; Commander Meng Shouqian rebelled and seized the city, and Jianfeng returned to crush him.
entries.literal: Jianfeng led the Xiangzhou troops with his field camp abroad; he entrusted prefectural affairs to petty men and failed in governing and control, so Commander Meng Shouqian seized the city in rebellion; Jianfeng led troops to suppress and pacify it.

entries.zh: 改隰州刺史，染風痹於任。
entries.en: He was transferred to Xi prefecture and contracted paralysis while in office.
entries.literal: He was changed to prefect of Xizhou and contracted wind paralysis in office.

entries.zh: 明宗嗣位，念及平昔副貳之舊，詔赴洛下，親幸其第，撫問隆厚，加檢校太傅，遙授鎮南節度使，俾請俸自給。
entries.en: When Mingzong succeeded he recalled their old partnership, summoned Jianfeng to Luoyang, visited his home with warm condolences, made him acting Grand Tutor and titular commissioner of Zhennan, and allowed him to draw a salary for his upkeep.
entries.literal: When Emperor Mingzong succeeded, remembering their old ties as chief and deputy, he ordered him to Luoyang, personally visited his residence with generous consolation, added acting Grand Tutor, and remotely appointed him military commissioner of Zhennan, allowing him to draw salary for his own support.

entries.zh: 後卒於洛陽，年五十六。
entries.en: He later died in Luoyang at fifty-six.
entries.literal: Later he died at Luoyang at the age of fifty-six.

entries.zh: 廢朝一日，贈太尉。
entries.en: The emperor suspended court for a day and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: Court audiences were suspended for one day; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 安金全，代北人。
entries.en: An Jinquan came from northern Dai.
entries.literal: An Jinquan was a man of northern Dai.

entries.zh: 世為邊將，少驍果，便騎射。
entries.en: His family had served for generations as frontier commanders; from youth he was bold and adept at mounted archery.
entries.literal: For generations his family had been frontier generals; in youth he was valiant and resolute, skilled at riding and archery.

entries.zh: 武皇時為騎將，屢從征討。
entries.en: Under the Martial Emperor he served as a cavalry commander and took part in many campaigns.
entries.literal: In the Martial Emperor's time he served as a cavalry officer and repeatedly followed campaigns.

entries.zh: 莊宗之救潞州及平河朔，皆有戰功，累為刺史，以老病退居太原。
entries.en: He distinguished himself when Emperor Zhuangzong relieved Luzhou and pacified Heshuo, rose through several prefectural posts, and finally retired to Taiyuan because of age and infirmity.
entries.literal: In Emperor Zhuangzong's relief of Luzhou and pacification of Heshuo he had merit in battle; he was repeatedly made prefect and, owing to age and illness, retired to Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 天祐中，汴將王檀率師三萬，乘莊宗在鄴，來襲并州。
entries.en: During the Tianyou reign the Liang general Wang Tan marched thirty thousand men against Bingzhou while Emperor Zhuangzong was away at Ye.
entries.literal: In the Tianyou era the Bian general Wang Tan led thirty thousand troops and, taking advantage of Emperor Zhuangzong's being at Ye, came to attack Bingzhou.

entries.zh: 時城無備兵，敵軍奄至，監軍張承業大恐，計無所出，閱諸司丁匠，登陴禦捍。
entries.en: The city had no garrison on hand when the enemy appeared without warning. Army Supervisor Zhang Chengye was terrified and at a loss until he mustered artisans and laborers from the government workshops to man the ramparts.
entries.literal: At the time the city had no ready troops; the enemy army arrived suddenly. Army Supervisor Zhang Chengye was greatly alarmed and could think of no plan, so he reviewed the laborers and artisans of the various offices and had them mount the walls to defend.

entries.zh: 外攻甚急，金全遽出謂承業曰：「老夫退居抱病，不任軍事。
entries.en: As the assault grew fierce, Jinquan came forward at once and told Chengye, "I have retired and am ill; I am in no condition to command.
entries.literal: The outside assault was very pressing. Jinquan hurried out and said to Chengye: "This old man has retired and is ill; I am not fit for military affairs.

entries.zh: 然吾王家屬在此，王業本根之地，如一旦為敵所有，大事去矣。
entries.en: But the royal household is here—this is the foundation of the throne. If the enemy takes it in a day, everything is lost.
entries.literal: Yet the royal clan is here, and this is the rootland of the imperial enterprise. If it should in a single day fall to the enemy, the great affair is lost.

entries.zh: 請以庫甲見授，為公備寇。」
entries.en: Give me what armor the storehouses hold, and I will help you repel them."
entries.literal: Please grant me the armory armor; I will prepare against the invaders for you."

entries.zh: 承業即時授之。
entries.en: Chengye handed over the arms immediately.
entries.literal: Chengye at once handed them over.

entries.zh: 金全被甲跨馬，召率子弟及退閑諸將，得數百人。
entries.en: He armored himself, mounted, and rallied his sons and kinsmen along with retired officers until he had several hundred men.
entries.literal: Jinquan donned armor, mounted a horse, summoned and led his sons and younger kin together with retired and idle generals, and gathered several hundred men.

entries.zh: 夜出北門，擊賊於羊馬城內，梁人驚潰，由是退卻。
entries.en: That night he sallied from the north gate and struck the enemy in the livestock pens outside the wall; the Liang troops broke in panic and drew off.
entries.literal: At night he went out the north gate and struck the bandits within the sheep-and-horse enclosure; the Liang men were startled and routed, and thereby withdrew.

entries.zh: 俄而石君立自潞州至，汴軍退走。
entries.en: Soon afterward Shi Junli came up from Luzhou, and the Liang army withdrew.
entries.literal: Before long Shi Junli arrived from Luzhou and the Bian army retreated and fled.

entries.zh: 微金全之奮命，城幾危矣。
entries.en: Without Jinquan's desperate stand, the city would almost certainly have fallen.
entries.literal: But for Jinquan's staking his life, the city would nearly have been lost.

entries.zh: 莊宗性矜伐，凡大將立功，不時行賞，故金全終莊宗世，名位不進。
entries.en: Emperor Zhuangzong was vain and slow to reward victorious commanders, and Jinquan therefore gained no further promotion throughout Zhuangzong's reign.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong was by nature proud and boastful; whenever great generals achieved merit he did not reward them promptly, so Jinquan through Emperor Zhuangzong's entire reign did not advance in fame or rank.

entries.zh: 明宗與之有舊，及登極，授金全同平章事，充振武軍節度使。
entries.en: Emperor Mingzong had known him long before; on taking the throne he made Jinquan Associate Grand Councillor and commissioner of the Zhenwu circuit.
entries.literal: Emperor Mingzong had old ties with him; when he ascended the throne he appointed Jinquan Associate Grand Councillor and made him military commissioner of the Zhenwu army.

entries.zh: 在任二年，治民為政非所長，詔赴闕，俄而病卒。
entries.en: After two years in the post—civil administration was never his strength—he was recalled to court and died of illness shortly after.
entries.literal: After two years in office, governing the people and administering affairs were not his strengths; he was ordered to the capital and soon died of illness.

entries.zh: 廢視朝二日。
entries.en: The emperor suspended court audiences for two days.
entries.literal: Court audiences were suspended for two days.

entries.zh: 初，南北對壘，汴之遊騎每出，必為金全所獲，故梁之偵邏者鹹懼，目之為「安五道」，蓋比鬼將有五道之名也。
entries.en: Earlier, while the two sides faced each other along the front, Liang raiders sent out were almost always taken by Jinquan; Liang scouts dreaded him and nicknamed him "An of the Five Roads," after a demon general of that name.
entries.literal: Earlier, when north and south faced each other in camp, whenever Bian raiding cavalry went out they were invariably captured by Jinquan, so Liang scouts all feared him and called him "An of the Five Roads," likening him to the demon general who bears the name of the Five Roads.

entries.zh: 其從弟洺州刺史遷，素得士心，眾乃推為留後，求援於汴。
entries.en: His cousin Qian, prefect of Mingzhou, had long enjoyed the soldiers' trust; the army then acclaimed him acting governor and appealed to Bian for help.
entries.literal: His younger cousin Qian, prefect of Ming, had long won the hearts of the soldiers; the troops thereupon pushed him as acting governor and sought aid from Bian.

entries.zh: 時梁祖方攻時溥，援兵不出。
entries.en: The Liang founder was then besieging Shi Pu, and no relief force was sent.
entries.literal: At that time the Liang founder was just attacking Shi Pu, and relief troops did not go out.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：全忠遣大將王虔裕將精甲數百，間道入邢州共守。）〉
entries.en: (The Zizhi Tongjian records that Quanzhong dispatched his general Wang Yuyu with several hundred elite troops by a secret path into Xingzhou to help hold the city.)〉
entries.literal: (The Comprehensive Mirror states: Quanzhong sent the great general Wang Yuyu with several hundred picked armored men by a hidden route into Xing Prefecture to hold it jointly.)〉

entries.zh: 大順元年，遷執王虔裕等乞降，武皇令安金俊代之。
entries.en: In 890 Qian seized Wang Yuyu and his men and offered surrender; the Martial Emperor sent An Jinjun to take over.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dashun, Qian seized Wang Yuyu and the others and begged to surrender; the Martial Emperor ordered An Jinjun to replace him.

entries.zh: 〈（案《孟方立傳》，原本闕佚。
entries.en: (The original biography of Meng Fangli is incomplete.
entries.literal: (The biography of Meng Fangli in the original text is defective.

entries.zh: 考《新唐書》列傳云：孟方立，邢州人。
entries.en: The New Book of Tang biography records that Meng Fangli was a native of Xingzhou.
entries.literal: Consulting the biographies in the New Book of Tang it states: Meng Fangli was a man of Xing Prefecture.

entries.zh: 始為澤州天井戍將，稍遷遊奕使。
entries.en: He began as garrison commander at Tianjing in Zezhou and was later promoted to roaming patrol commissioner.
entries.literal: He first served as garrison commander of Tianjing in Ze Prefecture and was gradually promoted to roaming patrol commissioner.

entries.zh: 中和元年，昭義節度使高鄩擊黃巢，戰石橋，不勝，保華州，為裨將成鄰所殺。
entries.en: In 881 the Zhaoyi governor Gao Yun attacked Huang Chao, was defeated at Shiqiao, withdrew to Huazhou, and was killed by his subordinate Cheng Lin.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhonghe the Zhaoyi military governor Gao Yun attacked Huang Chao, fought at Shiqiao, was defeated, held Hua Prefecture, and was killed by the staff officer Cheng Lin.

entries.zh: 還據潞州，眾怒，方立率兵攻鄰，斬之。
entries.en: Cheng Lin then held Luzhou, but the army was furious; Fangli marched against him, killed him, and took the city.
entries.literal: Returning he seized Luzhou; the troops were enraged, and Fangli led soldiers to attack Lin and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 自稱留後，擅裂邢、洺、磁為鎮，治邢為府，號昭義軍。
entries.en: He proclaimed himself acting governor, carved Xing, Ming, and Ci into a separate command with his seat at Xingzhou, and styled it the Zhaoyi army.
entries.literal: He styled himself acting governor, on his own authority split Xing, Ming, and Ci into a commandery, made Xing his seat, and called it the Zhaoyi army.

entries.zh: 潞人請監軍使吳全勖知兵馬留後。
entries.en: The people of Luzhou asked that army supervisor Wu Quanxu be appointed acting military governor.
entries.literal: The people of Lu asked that the army supervisor Wu Quanxu be made acting governor in charge of troops and horses.

entries.zh: 時王鐸領諸道行營都統，以潞未定，墨製假方立檢校左散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，知邢州事。
entries.en: Wang Duo then commanded the allied armies; with Luzhou still unsettled, he issued an informal commission naming Fangli acting Left Regular Attendant and Grand Censor to govern Xingzhou.
entries.literal: At that time Wang Duo led the allied armies as supreme commander; because Lu was not settled, an informal commission made Fangli acting Left Regular Attendant and concurrent Grand Censor, in charge of Xing Prefecture affairs.

entries.zh: 方立不受，囚全勖，以書請鐸，願得儒臣守潞。
entries.en: Fangli refused the commission, imprisoned Quanxu, and wrote to Duo asking that a scholar-official be sent to govern Luzhou.
entries.literal: Fangli did not accept, imprisoned Quanxu, and by letter asked Duo, wishing to obtain a Confucian minister to guard Lu.

entries.zh: 鐸使參謀、中書舍人鄭昌圖知昭義留事，欲遂為帥。
entries.en: Duo sent his adviser, Secretariat Drafter Zheng Changtu, to handle Zhaoyi affairs, hoping eventually to take command himself.
entries.literal: Duo sent his staff adviser, Secretariat Drafter Zheng Changtu, to manage Zhaoyi acting affairs, intending to become commander himself.

entries.zh: 僖宗自用舊宰相王徽領節度。
entries.en: Emperor Xizong personally appointed the former chief minister Wang Hui as military governor.
entries.literal: Emperor Xizong on his own employed the former chief minister Wang Hui to lead the circuit.

entries.zh: 時天子在西，河、關雲擾，方立擅地，而李克用窺潞州，徽度朝廷未能製，乃固讓昌圖。
entries.en: The emperor was then in the west, the Yellow River region in chaos, Fangli holding his own ground, and Li Keyong eyeing Luzhou. Wang Hui concluded the court could not enforce its will and firmly declined in favor of Changtu.
entries.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was in the west; the Yellow and Pass regions were in turmoil; Fangli held territory on his own authority, while Li Keyong watched Luzhou. Hui judged that the court could not control matters and firmly yielded to Changtu.

entries.zh: 昌圖治不三月輒去。
entries.en: Changtu governed less than three months before departing.
entries.literal: Changtu governed less than three months and then left.

entries.zh: 方立更表李殷銳為刺史，謂潞險而人悍，數賊大帥為亂，欲銷懦之，乃徙治龍岡州，豪傑重遷，有懟言。
entries.en: Fangli then recommended Li Yinrui as prefect, arguing that Luzhou was rugged and its people fierce, that successive governors had rebelled, and that he would break their spirit by moving the seat to Longgangzhou; local magnates resented the move and murmured in protest.
entries.literal: Fangli further memorialized Li Yinrui as prefect, saying Lu was perilous and its people fierce, that great commanders had repeatedly rebelled, and wishing to break their spirit he moved the seat to Longgang Prefecture; the powerful gentry resented the relocation and there was angry talk.

entries.zh: 會克用為河東節度使，昭義監軍祁審誨乞師求復昭義軍；
entries.en: When Keyong became Hedong military governor, Zhaoyi army supervisor Qi Shenhui appealed for troops to restore the Zhaoyi command;
entries.literal: It happened that Keyong became military governor of Hedong; the Zhaoyi army supervisor Qi Shenhui begged troops to restore the Zhaoyi army;

entries.zh: 克用遣賀公雅、李筠、安金俊三部將擊潞州，為方立所破。
entries.en: Keyong sent He Gongya, Li Jun, and An Jinjun against Luzhou, but Fangli defeated them.
entries.literal: Keyong sent the three generals He Gongya, Li Jun, and An Jinjun to strike Luzhou, and they were defeated by Fangli.

entries.zh: 又使李克修攻敗之，殺殷銳，遂並潞州，表克修為節度留後。
entries.en: He then sent Li Kexiu, who defeated Fangli's forces, killed Yinrui, seized Luzhou, and recommended Kexiu as acting governor.
entries.literal: He again sent Li Kexiu to attack and defeat them, killed Yinrui, thereupon annexed Luzhou, and memorialized Kexiu as acting military governor.

entries.zh: 初，昭義有潞、邢、洺、磁四州。
entries.en: Originally the Zhaoyi circuit comprised Luzhou, Xingzhou, Mingzhou, and Cizhou.
entries.literal: Earlier Zhaoyi had the four prefectures of Lu, Xing, Ming, and Ci.

entries.zh: 至是，方立自以山東三州為昭義，朝廷亦命克修，以潞州舊軍畀之，昭義有兩節自此始。
entries.en: Fangli now held the three eastern prefectures as his own Zhaoyi command while the court appointed Kexiu over Luzhou with its former garrison—thus the circuit was split in two.
entries.literal: At this point Fangli on his own took the three eastern prefectures as Zhaoyi; the court also appointed Kexiu and gave him the old Lu army, and from this time there were two Zhaoyi commands.

entries.zh: 克修，字崇遠，克用從父弟。
entries.en: Kexiu, courtesy name Chongyuan, was Li Keyong's paternal cousin.
entries.literal: Kexiu, style name Chongyuan, was Keyong's younger cousin on the father's side.

entries.zh: 精馳射，常從征伐，自左營軍使擢留後，進檢校司空。
entries.en: An expert horseman and archer, he campaigned constantly, rose from commander of the Left Camp to acting governor, and was promoted to acting Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Skilled at mounted archery, he often followed campaigns; from Left Camp army commander he was promoted to acting governor and advanced to acting Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 方立倚朱全忠為助，故無用擊邢、洺、磁無虛歲，地為鬥場，人不能稼。
entries.en: Fangli leaned on Zhu Quanzhong for support, yet Xing, Ming, and Ci were attacked every year without respite until the region was nothing but a battlefield and farming ceased.
entries.literal: Fangli relied on Zhu Quanzhong for aid, so year after year there were attacks on Xing, Ming, and Ci without pause; the land became a battleground and people could not farm.

entries.zh: 光啟二年，克修擊邢州，取故鎮，進攻武安，方立將呂臻、馬爽戰焦岡，為克修所破，斬首萬級，執臻等，拔武安、臨洺、邯鄲、沙河。
entries.en: In 886 Kexiu attacked Xingzhou, recovered the old seat, and pressed on Wu'an; Fangli's generals Lü Zhen and Ma Shuang met him at Jiaogang and were routed—ten thousand heads were taken, Zhen captured, and Wu'an, Linming, Handan, and Shahe fell.
entries.literal: In the second year of Guangqi, Kexiu attacked Xing Prefecture, took the old seat, and advanced on Wu'an; Fangli's generals Lü Zhen and Ma Shuang fought at Jiaogang, were defeated by Kexiu, ten thousand heads were cut off, Zhen and the others were seized, and Wu'an, Linming, Handan, and Shahe were taken.

entries.zh: 克用以安金俊為邢州刺史招撫之。
entries.en: Keyong appointed An Jinjun prefect of Xingzhou to pacify the region.
entries.literal: Keyong used An Jinjun as prefect of Xing to win them over and pacify them.

entries.zh: 方立丐兵於王鎔，鎔以兵三萬赴之，克修還。
entries.en: Fangli appealed to Wang Rong for troops; Rong sent thirty thousand men, and Kexiu withdrew.
entries.literal: Fangli begged troops from Wang Rong; Rong sent thirty thousand men to his aid, and Kexiu withdrew.

entries.zh: 後二年，方立督部將奚忠信兵三萬攻遼州，以金啖赫連鐸與連和。
entries.en: Two years later Fangli led his general Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand men against Liaozhou, bribing Helian Duo to join the campaign.
entries.literal: Two years later Fangli supervised his subordinate general Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand troops to attack Lia Prefecture, using gold to win Helian Duo to join in alliance.

entries.zh: 會契丹攻鐸師失期，忠信三分其兵，鼓而行，克用伏兵於險，忠信前軍沒，既戰，大敗，執忠信，餘眾走脫，歸者才十二。
entries.en: When Khitan raids delayed Duo's army, Zhongxin split his force in three columns and marched with drums beating; Keyong ambushed him in a pass, destroyed his vanguard, and routed the main body; Zhongxin was captured, and only twelve men made it back.
entries.literal: It happened that the Khitan attack on Duo made his army miss the rendezvous; Zhongxin divided his force in three and advanced with drums; Keyong set ambush in a defile; Zhongxin's vanguard was destroyed, and once battle was joined he was utterly defeated; Zhongxin was seized, the rest fled, and only twelve returned.

entries.zh: 龍紀元年，克用使李罕之、李存孝擊邢，攻磁、洺，方立戰琉璃陂，大敗，禽其二將，被斧鑕，徇邢壘，呼曰：「孟公速降，有能斬其首者，假三州節度使。」
entries.en: In 889 Keyong sent Li Hanzhi and Li Cunxiao against Xingzhou and into Ci and Ming; Fangli met them at Liuli Dam, was crushed, and lost both generals; the captives were shackled and displayed before the walls of Xing with the cry, "Lord Meng, surrender at once! Whoever brings me his head shall govern the three prefectures."
entries.literal: In the first year of Longji, Keyong sent Li Hanzhi and Li Cunxiao to strike Xing and attack Ci and Ming; Fangli fought at Liuli Dam, was utterly defeated, and the two generals were captured; they were put in cangues and paraded before the Xing ramparts, crying: "Lord Meng, surrender quickly! Whoever can cut off his head shall be given acting governor of the three prefectures."

entries.zh: 方立力屈，又屬州殘墮，人心恐，性剛急，待下少恩，夜自行陴，兵皆倨告勞，自顧不可復振，乃還，引鴆自殺。
entries.en: His strength was spent, his prefectures in ruins, and morale shattered; harsh by nature and sparing of kindness, he toured the walls at night while the troops answered with insolent complaints of exhaustion. Convinced he could not recover, he went back inside, drank poison, and died.
entries.literal: Fangli's strength was spent; moreover the prefectures were ruined and crumbling, hearts were fearful; his nature was stern and impatient, his kindness to subordinates slight; he walked the parapets at night, and the soldiers were all insolent in reporting fatigue; seeing he could not recover, he returned, took poison, and killed himself.

entries.zh: 從弟遷，素得士心，眾推為節度留後，請援於全忠。
entries.en: His cousin Qian, beloved by the troops, was acclaimed acting governor and appealed to Quanzhong for aid.
entries.literal: His cousin Qian, who had long won the soldiers' hearts, was pushed by the masses as acting military governor and asked aid of Quanzhong.

entries.zh: 全忠方攻時溥，不即至，命王虔裕以精甲數百赴之，假道羅宏信，不許，乃趨間入邢州。
entries.en: Quanzhong was besieging Shi Pu and could not come immediately; he sent Wang Yuyu with several hundred elite troops by a secret path after Luo Hongxin refused passage, and they slipped into Xingzhou.
entries.literal: Quanzhong was just attacking Shi Pu and did not arrive at once; he ordered Wang Yuyu with several hundred picked armored men to go to his aid; he asked passage through Luo Hongxin, who refused, and so hurried by a hidden route into Xing.

entries.zh: 大順元年，存孝復攻邢，遷挈邢、洺、磁三州降，執王虔裕三百人獻之；
entries.en: In 890 Cunxiao attacked Xingzhou again; Qian surrendered the three prefectures of Xing, Ming, and Ci and handed over Wang Yuyu and three hundred of his men;
entries.literal: In the first year of Dashun, Cunxiao again attacked Xing; Qian brought the three prefectures of Xing, Ming, and Ci to surrender, seized three hundred men including Wang Yuyu and presented them;

entries.zh: 遂遷太原，表安金俊為邢、洺、磁團練使，以遷為汾州刺史。
entries.en: Qian was then transferred to Taiyuan while An Jinjun was appointed training commissioner over the three prefectures and Qian named prefect of Fenzhou.
entries.literal: thereupon he was moved to Taiyuan; An Jinjun was memorialized as training commissioner of Xing, Ming, and Ci, and Qian was made prefect of Fen.

entries.zh: 《歐陽史》云：天復元年，梁遣氏叔琮攻晉，出天井關，遷開門降，為梁兵鄉道以攻太原，不克；
entries.en: Ouyang Xiu's history records that in 901 the Liang sent Shi Shuzong against Jin through Tianjing Pass; Qian opened the gates, guided the Liang army toward Taiyuan, and failed to take the city;
entries.literal: Ouyang Xiu's history states: In the first year of Tianfu the Liang sent Shi Shuzong to attack Jin, coming out through Tianjing Pass; Qian opened the gates and surrendered, guiding the Liang army to attack Taiyuan, but they did not take it;

entries.zh: 叔琮軍還過潞，以遷歸於梁。
entries.en: on the return march Shuzong passed through Luzhou and delivered Qian to the Liang.
entries.literal: Shuzong's army on returning passed through Lu and handed Qian over to the Liang.

entries.zh: 梁太祖惡其反覆，殺之。）〉
entries.en: The Liang founder despised his treachery and had him executed.)〉
entries.literal: The Liang founder hated his fickleness and killed him.)〉

entries.zh: 張文禮，燕人也。
entries.en: Zhang Wenli was a native of Yan.
entries.literal: Zhang Wenli was a man of Yan.

entries.zh: 初為劉仁恭裨將，性凶險，多奸謀，辭氣庸下，與人交言，癖於不遜，自少及長，專蓄異謀。
entries.en: He began as a staff officer under Liu Rengong, a man fierce and treacherous, coarse in speech and habitually insolent in conversation; from youth he had nursed one conspiracy after another.
entries.literal: He first served as staff officer to Liu Rengong; his nature was fierce and perilous, full of treacherous schemes; his speech and manner were base; in conversing with others he was addicted to insolence; from youth to age he constantly harbored strange plots.

entries.zh: 及從劉守文之滄州，委將偏師。
entries.en: When he followed Liu Shouwen to Cangzhou, he was given command of a detached force.
entries.literal: When he followed Liu Shouwen to Cang Prefecture, he was entrusted with a detached division.

entries.zh: 守文省父燕薊，據城為亂。
entries.en: Shouwen went up to Yan and Ji to visit his father, then seized the city and rebelled.
entries.literal: Shouwen went to visit his father in Yan and Ji, seized the city, and rebelled.

entries.zh: 及敗，奔於王鎔。
entries.en: When the rebellion collapsed he fled to Wang Rong.
entries.literal: When defeated he fled to Wang Rong.

entries.zh: 察鎔不親政事，遂曲事當權者，以求衒達。
entries.en: Seeing that Rong neglected government, he cultivated those in power to advance himself.
entries.literal: Seeing that Rong did not attend to government himself, he thereupon curried favor with those in power to seek display and advancement.

entries.zh: 每對鎔自言有將才，孫、吳、韓、白，莫己若也。
entries.en: He told Rong repeatedly that as a commander he stood with Sun Wu, Wu Qi, Han Xin, and Bai Qi—and that none surpassed him.
entries.literal: Whenever he faced Rong he declared himself possessed of general's talent—none could compare with him to Sun Wu, Wu Qi, Han Xin, or Bai Qi.

entries.zh: 鎔賞其言，給遺甚厚，因錄為義男，賜姓，名德明，由是每令將兵。
entries.en: Rong was impressed, lavished gifts on him, adopted him as a son, granted him the surname and the name Deming, and thereafter regularly put him in command.
entries.literal: Rong prized his words and gave him very generous gifts; he was thereupon enrolled as an adopted son, granted the clan name, and named Deming; from this he was repeatedly ordered to lead troops.

entries.zh: 自柏鄉戰勝之後，常從莊宗行營。
entries.en: After the victory at Baixiang he often campaigned with Emperor Zhuangzong's headquarters.
entries.literal: After the victory at Bai Township he often followed Emperor Zhuangzong's field headquarters.

entries.zh: 素不知書，亦無方略，惟於懦兵之中萋菲上將，言甲不知進退，乙不識軍機，以此軍人推為良將。
entries.en: Illiterate and devoid of strategy, he won favor among timid soldiers by slandering their commanders—one knew nothing of advance or retreat, another nothing of tactics—and on that basis the men hailed him as a fine general.
entries.literal: He had never known books and had no strategy; only among cowardly soldiers did he slander superiors, saying that A did not know advance and retreat and B did not understand military affairs—by this the troops pushed him as a good general.

entries.zh: 初，梁將楊師厚在魏州，文禮領趙兵三萬夜掠經、宗，因侵貝郡。
entries.en: When the Liang general Yang Shihou held Weizhou, Wenli led thirty thousand Zhao troops on a night raid into Jing and Zong and pressed into Bei commandery.
entries.literal: Earlier the Liang general Yang Shihou was at Wei Prefecture; Wenli led thirty thousand Zhao troops by night to plunder Jing and Zong and thereby invaded Bei commandery.

entries.zh: 師厚先率步騎數千人，設伏於唐店。
entries.en: Shihou marched ahead with several thousand foot and horse and laid an ambush at Tangdian.
entries.literal: Shihou first led several thousand infantry and cavalry and set an ambush at Tang Inn.

entries.zh: 文禮大掠而旋，士皆卷甲束兵，夜凱歌，行至唐店，師厚伏兵四面圍合，殺戮殆盡，文禮單騎僅免。
entries.en: Wenli looted heavily and withdrew with his men singing victory songs in the night, armor bundled on their backs; at Tangdian Shihou's ambush closed on every side and slaughtered them almost to a man—Wenli alone escaped on horseback.
entries.literal: Wenli plundered greatly and turned back; the soldiers all rolled up their armor and bound their weapons, singing victory songs at night; when they reached Tang Inn, Shihou's hidden troops closed in on all sides and slaughtered them nearly to the last man; Wenli alone on horseback barely escaped.

entries.zh: 自爾猶對諸將大言，或讓之曰：「唐店之功，不須多伐。」
entries.en: Even afterward he bragged before the other generals until one reproved him: "The affair at Tangdian is hardly something to boast about."
entries.literal: From then on he still boasted greatly before the generals; someone reproached him, saying: "The achievement at Tang Inn needs no great boasting."

entries.zh: 文禮大慚。
entries.en: Wenli flushed with shame.
entries.literal: Wenli was deeply ashamed.

entries.zh: 在鎮州既久，見其政荒人僻，常蓄異圖；
entries.en: After long service at Zhenzhou he saw negligent government and an isolated populace, and constantly nursed rebellious designs;
entries.literal: Having been long at Zhen Prefecture, he saw that its government was negligent and its people remote, and constantly harbored strange designs;

entries.zh: 酒酣之後，對左右每泄惡言，聞者莫不寒心。
entries.en: when drunk he would vent vicious threats to his attendants, chilling everyone who heard him.
entries.literal: after wine had gone deep he often let fall evil words to those beside him, and hearers were all chilled in heart.

entries.zh: 惟王鎔略無猜間，漸為腹心，乃以符習代其行營，以文禮為防城使，自此專伺間隙。
entries.en: Wang Rong alone remained unsuspecting and drew him into his inner circle; he replaced Wenli in the field army with Fu Xi and made Wenli commissioner of city defense, after which Wenli watched only for his chance.
entries.literal: Only Wang Rong was slightly without suspicion; Wenli gradually became his intimate, and Rong then replaced him in the field camp with Fu Xi and made Wenli city-defense commissioner—from this time he devoted himself solely to watching for openings.

entries.zh: 及鎔殺李宏規，委政於其子昭祚。
entries.en: When Rong executed Li Honggui he handed power to his son Zhaozuo.
entries.literal: When Rong killed Li Honggui he entrusted government to his son Zhaozuo.

entries.zh: 昭祚性逼戾，未識人間情偽，素養名持重，坐作貴人，既事權在手，朝夕欲代其父，向來附勢之徒，無不族滅。
entries.en: Zhaozuo was harsh and ignorant of human affairs, having long cultivated an air of lofty dignity; once power was his he plotted day and night to supplant his father and exterminated to the last man every courtier who had once curried favor.
entries.literal: Zhaozuo's nature was harsh and overbearing; he did not know the truth and falsity of human affairs; he had long cultivated reputation and gravity, sitting and acting as a noble; once power was in his hands he morning and evening wished to replace his father; those who had formerly clung to power were without exception exterminated to the clan.

entries.zh: 初，李宏規、李藹持權用事，樹立親舊，分董要職，故奸宄之心不能搖動，文禮頗深畏憚。
entries.en: Earlier Li Honggui and Li Ai had held real power, placing kin and allies in every key post, so that would-be traitors could not stir—and Wenli feared them deeply.
entries.literal: Earlier Li Honggui and Li Ai held power and managed affairs, set up kin and old associates, and divided supervision of key posts, so the hearts of traitors could not be stirred; Wenli was quite deeply fearful and restrained.

entries.zh: 及宏規見殺，其部下五百人懼罪，將欲奔竄，聚泣偶語，未有所之。
entries.en: After Honggui's execution his five hundred followers, fearing punishment, gathered in tears and whispered among themselves, unsure where to flee.
entries.literal: When Honggui was killed, his five hundred followers feared punishment and were about to flee; they gathered weeping and speaking in low voices, not yet knowing where to go.

entries.zh: 文禮因其離心，密以奸辭激之曰：「令公命我盡坑爾曹，我念爾十餘年荷戈隨我，為家為國，我若不即殺爾，則得罪於令公；
entries.en: Wenli exploited their disaffection and secretly incited them: "The lord has ordered me to bury you all alive. I remember how for more than ten years you bore arms and followed me, for family and state; if I do not kill you at once, I offend the lord;
entries.literal: Wenli, because of their alienation of heart, secretly used treacherous words to incite them, saying: "The lord has ordered me to bury you all alive. I think of how for more than ten years you bore weapons and followed me for home and state; if I do not kill you at once I offend the lord;

entries.zh: 我若不言，又負爾輩。」
entries.en: if I keep silent, I fail you."
entries.literal: if I do not speak, I again fail you all."

entries.zh: 眾軍皆泣。
entries.en: The soldiers wept.
entries.literal: All the troops wept.

entries.zh: 是夜作亂，殺王鎔父子，舉族灰滅，惟留王昭祚妻朱氏通梁人；
entries.en: That night they rose in mutiny, killed Wang Rong and his son, and annihilated the clan—only Zhaozuo's wife Lady Zhu, who had connections with the Liang, was spared;
entries.literal: That night they mutinied, killed Wang Rong father and son, and wiped out the whole clan to ashes; only Wang Zhaozuo's wife the Lady Zhu, who had ties to Liang men, was spared;

entries.zh: 尋間道告於梁曰：「王氏喪於亂軍，普寧公主無恙。」
entries.en: she soon sent word by a secret path to the Liang: "The Wang house has fallen to mutineers, but Princess Puning is safe."
entries.literal: soon by a hidden route she reported to the Liang: "The Wang house has perished among the mutinous troops; Princess Puning is unharmed."

entries.zh: 文禮徇賊帥張友順所請，因為留後，於潭城視事。
entries.en: Wenli acceded to the bandit leader Zhang Youshun's request, took the title of acting governor, and administered affairs from Tancheng.
entries.literal: Wenli yielded to the request of the bandit chief Zhang Youshun and thereupon became acting governor, conducting affairs at Tancheng.

entries.zh: 以事上聞，兼要節旄，尋亦奉箋勸進，莊宗姑示含容，乃可其請。
entries.en: He reported to the throne and demanded the commissioner's insignia; he soon sent a memorial urging Zhuangzong's accession, and Zhuangzong, for the moment forbearing, granted his request.
entries.literal: He reported the matter upward and also demanded the commander's banner; soon he also submitted a memorial urging advancement; Emperor Zhuangzong for the moment showed forbearance and approved his request.

entries.zh: 文禮比廝役小人，驟居人上，行步動息，皆不自安。
entries.en: A menial who had risen overnight, Wenli could not compose himself in gait or breath.
entries.literal: Wenli compared to a menial servant and petty man, suddenly placed above others—his walking, moving, and breathing were all without ease.

entries.zh: 出則千餘人露刃相隨，日殺不辜，道路以目，常慮我師問罪，奸心百端。
entries.en: Whenever he went abroad more than a thousand men with drawn swords followed; he killed innocents daily until travelers dared only glance sideways; he constantly feared imperial retribution and spun endless plots.
entries.literal: When he went out more than a thousand men with bared blades followed; daily he killed the innocent; people in the road looked with eyes alone; he constantly feared our army would call him to account, and his treacherous heart had a hundred schemes.

entries.zh: 南通朱氏，北結契丹，往往擒獲其使，莊宗遣人送還，文禮由是愈恐。
entries.en: He courted the Zhu clan in the south and the Khitan in the north, often seizing their envoys until Zhuangzong returned them—which only deepened Wenli's terror.
entries.literal: South he connected with the Zhu clan, north he joined the Khitan; he often seized their envoys; Zhuangzong sent men to return them, and Wenli from this grew ever more fearful.

entries.zh: 是歲八月，莊宗遣閻寶、史建瑭及趙將符習等率王鎔本軍進討。
entries.en: In the eighth month Zhuangzong sent Yan Bao, Shi Jiantan, and the Zhao general Fu Xi with Wang Rong's former army to suppress him.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of that year Zhuangzong sent Yan Bao, Shi Jiantan, and the Zhao general Fu Xi and others to lead Wang Rong's original army forward to punish him.

entries.zh: 師興，文禮病疽腹，及聞史建瑭攻下趙州，驚悸而卒。
entries.en: As the campaign opened Wenli lay ill with an abdominal abscess; when he heard that Shi Jiantan had taken Zhaozhou he died of shock.
entries.literal: When the army rose, Wenli was ill with carbuncle in the belly; when he heard that Shi Jiantan had taken Zhao Prefecture he died of shock and palpitation.

entries.zh: 其子處瑾、處球秘不發喪，軍府內外，皆不知之，每日於寢宮問安。
entries.en: His sons Chujin and Chuqiu concealed the death; inside and outside headquarters none knew, and each day they sent greetings to the bedchamber as if their father still lived.
entries.literal: His sons Chujin and Chuqiu concealed the death and did not announce the mourning; inside and outside the military headquarters none knew; daily at the sleeping palace they inquired after his health.

entries.zh: 處瑾與其腹心韓正時參決大事，同謀奸惡。
entries.en: Chujin and his confidant Han Zhengshi decided major affairs together and plotted further treachery.
entries.literal: Chujin with his intimate Han Zhengshi jointly decided great affairs and conspired in treacherous evil.

entries.zh: 初，文禮疽未發時，舉家咸見鬼物，昏瞑之後或歌或哭，又野河色變如血，遊魚多死，浮於水上，識者知其必敗。
entries.en: Before Wenli's abscess broke, his household saw apparitions; after dark there were songs and wails; the wild river turned the color of blood and fish died in shoals upon the surface—those who read omens knew he was doomed.
entries.literal: Earlier, before Wenli's carbuncle broke out, the whole household all saw ghostly things; after dusk there was singing or weeping; moreover the wild river changed color like blood, wandering fish mostly died and floated on the water—those who knew saw he must fail.

entries.zh: 其年秋，詔削奪璋在身官爵，命天雄軍節度使石敬瑭為東川行營招討使，率師以討之。
entries.en: That autumn an edict stripped Zhang of his ranks and appointed Tianxiong governor Shi Jingtang Eastern Chuan campaign commissioner to lead troops against him.
entries.literal: That autumn an edict stripped Zhang of all ranks he held; Tianxiong military governor Shi Jingtang was ordered as Eastern Chuan campaign commissioner to lead troops to punish him.

entries.zh: 璋之子宮苑使光業並其族，並斬於洛陽。
entries.en: Zhang's son Guangye, palace park commissioner, and his entire clan were executed at Luoyang.
entries.literal: Zhang's son palace park commissioner Guangye and his entire clan were all executed at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 及石敬瑭率師進討，以糧運不接，班師。
entries.en: When Shi Jingtang marched against him, supply lines failed and the army withdrew.
entries.literal: When Shi Jingtang led the army forward to punish him, because grain transport could not connect he withdrew the army.

entries.zh: 明宗方務懷柔，乃放西川進奏官蘇願、東川軍將劉澄各歸本道，別無詔旨，隻云「兩務求安」。
entries.en: Mingzong pursued conciliation, released Western Chuan memorial officer Su Yuan and Eastern Chuan officer Liu Cheng to their circuits, and issued no further orders beyond the phrase "both sides seek peace."
entries.literal: Mingzong was then pursuing gentle appeasement, and released Western Chuan memorial officer Su Yuan and Eastern Chuan army officer Liu Cheng each to return to their circuits, with no other edict, only saying "both sides seek peace."

entries.zh: 時孟知祥其骨肉在京師者俱無恙焉，因遣使報璋，欲連表稱謝。
entries.en: Zhixiang's kin in the capital had been spared; he sent word to Zhang proposing a joint memorial of thanks to the throne.
entries.literal: At that time Meng Zhixiang's kin in the capital were all unharmed; he thereupon sent an envoy to report to Zhang, wishing jointly to submit a memorial of thanks.

entries.zh: 璋怒曰：「西川存得弟侄，遂欲再通朝廷，璋之兒孫已入黃泉，何謝之有！」
entries.en: Zhang raged: "Western Chuan still has brothers and nephews alive, so you wish to reopen ties with the court—my sons and grandsons are already in the grave; what thanks is there to offer!"
entries.literal: Zhang angrily said: "Western Chuan preserved brother and nephew, so they wish to reconnect with the court—Zhang's sons and grandsons have already entered the yellow springs; what thanks is there!"

entries.zh: 自是璋疑知祥背己，始構隙矣。
entries.en: From that moment Zhang suspected Zhixiang had betrayed him, and the rift between them began.
entries.literal: From this Zhang suspected Zhixiang had turned against him and first formed a breach.

entries.zh: 三年四月，璋率所部兵萬餘人以襲知祥。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the third year Zhang led more than ten thousand men in a surprise attack on Zhixiang.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the third year Zhang led more than ten thousand of his troops to strike Zhixiang.

entries.zh: 〈（《九國誌·趙季良傳》：季良嘗與知祥從容語曰：「璋性狼戾，若堅守一城，攻之難克。」
entries.en: (From the biography of Zhao Jiliang in the Records of the Nine Kingdoms: Jiliang once told Zhixiang in private, "Zhang is brutal and savage; if he holds a single city firm, he will be hard to defeat."
entries.literal: (From the Biography of Zhao Jiliang in the Records of the Nine Kingdoms: Jiliang once spoke at ease with Zhixiang, saying: "Zhang's nature is wolfish and violent; if he firmly holds one city, attacking him is hard to overcome."

entries.zh: 及聞璋起兵，知祥憂形於色。
entries.en: When news came that Zhang had taken the field, worry showed on Zhixiang's face.
entries.literal: When he heard Zhang had raised troops, Zhixiang's worry showed on his face.

entries.zh: 季良曰：「璋不守巢穴，此天以授公也。」
entries.en: Jiliang said, "Zhang has left his base undefended—Heaven is handing victory to you."
entries.literal: Jiliang said: "Zhang does not guard his nest—Heaven thereby gives this to you, my lord."

entries.zh: 既而璋果敗。）〉
entries.en: Zhang was indeed defeated soon after.)〉
entries.literal: Before long Zhang indeed was defeated.)〉

entries.zh: 知祥與諸將率師拒之，戰於漢州之彌牟鎮。
entries.en: Zhixiang and his generals marched to meet him and fought at Mizhen in Hanzhou.
entries.literal: Zhixiang with the various generals led troops to resist, fighting at Mizhen in Han Prefecture.

entries.zh: 璋軍大敗，得數十騎，復奔於東川。
entries.en: Zhang's army was shattered; he escaped with only a few dozen horsemen back to Eastern Chuan.
entries.literal: Zhang's army was utterly defeated; he had only several dozen horsemen and again fled to Eastern Chuan.

entries.zh: 〈（《九國誌·趙廷隱傳》：董璋襲廣漢，將攻成都，時東川廩藏充實，部下多敢死之士，其來也，眾皆畏之。
entries.en: (From the biography of Zhao Tingyin in the Records of the Nine Kingdoms: Dong Zhang raided Guanghan and was marching on Chengdu; Eastern Chuan's stores were full and his men were fearless; his advance struck terror into every heart.
entries.literal: (From the Biography of Zhao Tingyin in the Records of the Nine Kingdoms: Dong Zhang raided Guanghan and was about to attack Chengdu; at that time Eastern Chuan's granaries were full and his subordinates were mostly men who dared death; when they came, all were fearful.

entries.zh: 知祥親督諸將，與璋戰雞縱橋前，頗為所挫。
entries.en: Zhixiang personally led his generals against Zhang before Jizong Bridge and was driven back.
entries.literal: Zhixiang personally supervised the generals and fought Zhang before Jizong Bridge, and was quite beaten back by him.

entries.zh: 廷隱偽遁，璋逐之，知祥與張公鐸繼進，璋軍亂不成列，廷隱整陣，與知祥合擊之，璋軍大敗。）〉
entries.en: Tingyin feigned retreat; Zhang pursued; Zhixiang and Zhang Gongduo pressed forward; Zhang's army fell into disorder; Tingyin reformed his line and joined Zhixiang in a combined assault that shattered Zhang's force.)〉
entries.literal: Tingyin feigned flight; Zhang pursued him; Zhixiang with Zhang Gongduo followed in advance; Zhang's army was disordered and could not form ranks; Tingyin reformed the array and with Zhixiang jointly struck him; Zhang's army was utterly defeated.)〉

entries.zh: 先是，前陵州刺史王暉為璋所邀，寓於東川，至是因璋之敗，率眾以害之，傳其首於西川。
entries.en: Earlier the former Lingzhou prefect Wang Hui, whom Zhang had brought to Eastern Chuan, took advantage of Zhang's defeat, led troops to kill him, and sent his head to Western Chuan.
entries.literal: Earlier former Ling prefect Wang Hui had been invited by Zhang and lodged in Eastern Chuan; on this occasion because of Zhang's defeat he led troops to kill him and sent his head to Western Chuan.

entries.zh: 孟方立，
entries.en: Meng Fangli,
entries.literal: Meng Fangli,

entries.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》雲邢州人，《通鑒》雲汧州人。）〉
entries.en: (Ouyang Xiu's history says he was from Xingzhou; the Zizhi Tongjian says from Qianzhou.)〉
entries.literal: (Ouyang Xiu's history states he was a man of Xing Prefecture; the Comprehensive Mirror states he was a man of Qian Prefecture.)〉

entries.zh: 中和二年，為澤州天井關戍將。
entries.en: In 882 he was posted as garrison commander at Tianjing Pass in Zezhou.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe he served as garrison commander of Tianjing Pass in Ze Prefecture.

entries.zh: 時黃巢犯關輔，州郡易帥，有同博奕。
entries.en: Huang Chao was then ravaging the capital region, and commanders changed across the provinces as unpredictably as at dice.
entries.literal: At that time Huang Chao invaded the capital region; prefectures and districts changed commanders as if at dice.

entries.zh: 先是，沈詢、高湜相繼為昭義節度，怠於軍政。
entries.en: Earlier Shen Xun and then Gao Shi had held the Zhaoyi command, both neglectful of military affairs.
entries.literal: Previously Shen Xun and Gao Shi had succeeded one another as military governors of Zhaoyi, negligent in military administration.

entries.zh: 及有歸秦、劉廣之亂，方立見潞帥交代之際，乘其無備，率戍扶徑入潞州，自稱留後。
entries.en: During the rebellions of Gui Qin and Liu Guang, Fangli seized the interval when the Lu commander was changing hands, caught the city off guard, marched his garrison forces straight into Luzhou, and proclaimed himself acting military governor.
entries.literal: When the troubles of Gui Qin and Liu Guang arose, Fangli saw the moment of change in the Lu commander, took them unawares, led his garrison troops by a direct route into Luzhou, and styled himself acting governor.

entries.zh: 以邢為府，以審誨知潞州。
entries.en: He established his seat at Xingzhou and appointed Shen Hui to administer Luzhou.
entries.literal: He made Xing his headquarters and put Shen Hui in charge of Luzhou.

entries.zh: 〈（案：此二句上下有脫文。
entries.en: (Editorial note: There is missing text before and after these two sentences.
entries.literal: (Note: The text above and below these two sentences is defective.

entries.zh: 今無可復考。）〉
entries.en: It can no longer be recovered.)〉
entries.literal: It can no longer be reconstructed.)〉

entries.zh: 六月，李存孝下洺、磁兩郡，方立遣馬溉、袁奉韜盡率其眾，逆戰於琉璃陂。
entries.en: In the sixth month Li Cunxiao captured Mingzhou and Cizhou; Fangli sent Ma Gai and Yuan Fengtao with his entire army to give battle at Liuli Dam.
entries.literal: In the sixth month Li Cunxiao took the two prefectures of Ming and Ci; Fangli sent Ma Gai and Yuan Fengtao to lead out all his forces and meet them in battle at Liuli Dam.

entries.zh: 存孝擊之盡殪，生獲馬溉、奉韜。
entries.en: Cunxiao annihilated their force and took Ma Gai and Fengtao alive.
entries.literal: Cunxiao struck them and slaughtered them to the last man, taking Ma Gai and Fengtao alive.

entries.zh: 初，方立性苛急，恩不逮下，攻圍累旬，夜自巡城慰諭，守陴者皆倨。
entries.en: Fangli had long been harsh and impatient, and his favor never reached the ranks. After weeks of siege he toured the walls at night to rally the defenders, but the men on the battlements met him with insolence.
entries.literal: Earlier Fangli's nature had been harsh and impatient; his kindness did not reach those below. The siege lasted many tens of days; he himself patrolled the walls at night to comfort and instruct, yet the defenders on the parapets were all insolent.

entries.zh: 方立知其不可用，乃飲鴆而卒。
entries.en: Seeing that the troops were beyond recall, Fangli drank poison and died.
entries.literal: Fangli knew they could not be used, and thereupon drank poison and died.

entries.zh: 天祐十七年，友謙襲取同州，以其子令德為帥，請節鉞於梁，不獲。
entries.en: In 920 Youqian seized Tongzhou, installed his son Lingde as commander, and asked the Liang for formal investiture but was refused.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year of Tianyou, Youqian surprised and took Tongzhou, made his son Lingde commander, and requested the command banner and axe from Liang but did not obtain it.

entries.zh: 友謙即請之於莊宗，令幕客王正言以節旄賜之，梁將劉鄩、尹皓攻同州，友謙來告急，莊宗遣李嗣昭、李存審將兵赴之，敗汴軍於滑北，解圍而還。
entries.en: He then asked Zhuangzong, who had his aide Wang Zhengyan grant the commission; when Liang generals Liu Yan and Yin Hao besieged Tongzhou, Youqian appealed for help; Zhuangzong sent Li Sizhao and Li Cunshen, who defeated the Bian army north of Huazhou and lifted the siege.
entries.literal: Youqian then requested it from Emperor Zhuangzong and had his staff member Wang Zhengyan bestow the command regalia; Liang generals Liu Yan and Yin Hao attacked Tongzhou; Youqian came to report urgency; Zhuangzong sent Li Sizhao and Li Cunshen to lead troops thither, defeated the Bian army north of Hua, lifted the siege, and returned.

entries.zh: 初，劉鄩兵至蒲中，倉儲匱乏，人心離貳，軍民將校，鹹欲歸梁。
entries.en: When Liu Yan first reached central Pu, stores ran low, morale split, and soldiers and civilians alike wanted to go over to the Liang.
entries.literal: At first when Liu Yan's troops reached the center of Pu, granaries and stores were exhausted, men's hearts were divided in two, and army and people, commanders and officers—all wished to return to Liang.

entries.zh: 友謙諸子令錫等亦說其父曰：「晉王雖推心於我，然懸兵赴援，急維相應，寧我負人，擇福宜重。
entries.en: Youqian's sons, including Lingxi, also urged him, "The Prince of Jin may trust us, but his army is far away and the crisis is near—better to wrong a friend than miss our chance; choose the stronger side.
entries.literal: Youqian's sons Lingxi and others also urged their father, saying: "Although the Prince of Jin opens his heart to us, yet with distant troops rushing to aid, urgent ties must correspond—better that I wrong others; in choosing fortune one should weigh heavily.

entries.zh: 請納款於梁，候劉鄩兵退後，與晉王修好。」
entries.en: Submit to the Liang now, and after Liu Yan withdraws restore friendship with Jin."
entries.literal: Please submit allegiance to Liang; wait until Liu Yan's troops withdraw, then renew good relations with the Prince of Jin."

entries.zh: 友謙曰：「晉王親赴予急，夜半秉燭戰賊，麵為盟誓，不負初心。
entries.en: Youqian replied, "The Prince of Jin came in person to my aid, fought the enemy by candlelight at midnight, and swore face to face—I will not betray that bond.
entries.literal: Youqian said: "The Prince of Jin personally came to my aid, fought the enemy by torchlight at midnight, made a covenant with me face to face, and has not betrayed his original commitment.

entries.zh: 昨聞吾告難，命將星行，助我資糧，分我衣屨，而欲翻覆背惠，所謂鄧祁侯云『人將不食吾餘』也。」
entries.en: When I called for help he sent his generals at once, supplied my army, and shared his own clothing—yet you would turn traitor to such kindness? That is the warning of Duke Qi of Deng: men will refuse the leavings of one who breaks faith."
entries.literal: Only recently, upon hearing my appeal for aid, he ordered his generals to march by starlight, supplied me with provisions, and shared his clothing and footwear with me; yet you would reverse course and betray his kindness. This is what Duke Qi of Deng meant when he said, 'Men will not eat what I leave behind.'"

entries.zh: 及破梁軍，加守太尉、西平王。
entries.en: After the Liang army was defeated, he was made Guardian Grand Commandant and Prince of Xiping.
entries.literal: When the Liang army was broken, he was added Guardian Grand Commandant and Prince of Xiping.

entries.zh: 張全義，字國維，濮州臨濮人。
entries.en: Zhang Quanyi, whose courtesy name was Guowei, came from Linpu in Puzhou.
entries.literal: Zhang Quanyi, styled Guowei, was a native of Linpu in Puzhou.

entries.zh: 初名居言，賜名全義，梁祖改為宗奭；
entries.en: He was originally named Juyan, was granted the name Quanyi, and the Liang Founder renamed him Zongyi;
entries.literal: His original name was Juyan; he was granted the name Quanyi; the Founder of Liang changed it to Zongyi;

entries.zh: 莊宗定河南，復名全義。
entries.en: After Emperor Zhuangzong secured Henan, his name was restored to Quanyi.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Henan, he was again named Quanyi.

entries.zh: 祖璉，父誠，世為田農。
entries.en: His grandfather Lian and his father Cheng had been farmers for generations.
entries.literal: His grandfather was Lian, his father Cheng; for generations they were field farmers.

entries.zh: 全義為縣嗇夫，嘗為令所辱。
entries.en: Quanyi worked as a county grain clerk and had once been humiliated by the local magistrate.
entries.literal: Quanyi served as a district grain clerk and was once humiliated by the magistrate.

entries.zh: 乾符末，黃巢起冤句，全義亡命入巢軍。
entries.en: When Huang Chao rebelled at Yuanqu in the final years of Qianfu, Quanyi fled and joined his forces.
entries.literal: At the end of the Qianfu era, Huang Chao rose at Yuanqu; Quanyi fled for his life and entered Chao's army.

entries.zh: 巢入長安，以全義為吏部尚書，充水運使。
entries.en: After Chao took Chang'an, he made Quanyi Minister of the Civil Office and Superintendent of Water Transport.
entries.literal: When Chao entered Chang'an, he appointed Quanyi Minister of the Civil Office and made him Water Transport Commissioner.

entries.zh: 巢敗，依諸葛爽於河陽，累遷至裨校，屢有戰功，爽表為澤州刺史。
entries.en: When Chao fell, Quanyi attached himself to Zhuge Shuang at Heyang, rose through the ranks to junior officer with repeated distinctions in battle, and Shuang recommended him as prefect of Zezhou.
entries.literal: When Chao was defeated, he joined Zhuge Shuang at Heyang; he was repeatedly promoted to junior officer, had repeated battle achievements, and Shuang memorialized for him to be Prefect of Zezhou.

entries.zh: 光啟初，爽卒，其子仲方為留後。
entries.en: Early in Guangqi, Shuang died and his son Zhongfang took over as acting governor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi, Shuang died; his son Zhongfang became acting military governor.

entries.zh: 部將劉經與李罕之爭據洛陽，罕之敗經於聖善寺，乘勝欲攻河陽，營於洛口。
entries.en: Subordinate Liu Jing and Li Hanzhi fought over Luoyang; Hanzhi defeated Liu at Shengshan Temple and, pressing his advantage, moved to attack Heyang, encamping at Luokou.
entries.literal: The subordinate general Liu Jing and Li Hanzhi contested possession of Luoyang; Hanzhi defeated Jing at Shengshan Temple; seizing victory, he wished to attack Heyang and encamped at Luokou.

entries.zh: 經遣全義拒之，全義乃與罕之同盟結義，返攻經於河陽，為經所敗，收合餘眾，與罕之據懷州，乞師於武皇。
entries.en: Liu sent Quanyi to oppose him, but Quanyi instead allied with Hanzhi and turned on Liu at Heyang; defeated, he regrouped, joined Hanzhi in holding Huaizhou, and sought aid from the Martial Emperor.
entries.literal: Jing dispatched Quanyi to resist him; Quanyi then formed a sworn alliance with Hanzhi, returned to attack Jing at Heyang, was defeated by Jing, gathered his remaining troops, and with Hanzhi held Huaizhou, begging troops from the Martial Emperor.

entries.zh: 武皇遣澤州刺史安金俊助之，進攻河陽，劉經、仲方委城奔汴，罕之遂自領河陽，表全義為河南尹。
entries.en: The Martial Emperor sent An Jinjun, prefect of Zezhou, to help; they attacked Heyang; Liu and Zhongfang abandoned the city for Bian; Hanzhi took Heyang himself and recommended Quanyi as Intendant of Henan.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor sent the prefect of Zezhou An Jinjun to assist them; they advanced to attack Heyang; Liu Jing and Zhongfang abandoned the city and fled to Bian; Hanzhi then himself took over Heyang and memorialized Quanyi as Intendant of Henan.

entries.zh: 李建及，許州人。
entries.en: Li Jianji was from Xu Prefecture.
entries.literal: Li Jianji was a native of Xu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 本姓王，父質。
entries.en: His family name had originally been Wang; his father was named Zhi.
entries.literal: His original surname was Wang; his father's name was Zhi.

entries.zh: 建及少事李罕之為紀綱，光啟中，罕之謁武皇於晉陽，因選部下驍勇者百人以獻，建及在籍中。
entries.en: As a young man Jianji served Li Hanzhi as a camp officer. During the Guangqi reign Hanzhi called on the Martial Emperor at Jinyang and presented a hundred picked warriors from his command; Jianji was among them.
entries.literal: In his youth Jianji served Li Hanzhi as a camp disciplinarian. In the Guangqi era Hanzhi visited the Martial Emperor at Jinyang and, selecting a hundred valiant men from his subordinates to present, Jianji was on the roster.

entries.zh: 後以功署牙職，典義兒軍，及賜姓名。
entries.en: He later earned appointment to the guard staff, command of the adopted-sons corps, and the gift of a surname and given name.
entries.literal: Later, for merit he was appointed to a guard-office post, placed in charge of the adopted-sons army, and granted a surname and personal name.

entries.zh: 天祐七年，改匡衛軍都校。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Tianyou he was made commandant of the Kuangwei Army.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Tianyou he was changed to commandant of the Kuangwei Army.

entries.zh: 柏鄉之役，汴將韓追周德威至高邑南野河上，鎮、定兵扼橋道，韓選精兵先奪之。
entries.en: At Baixiang the Bian commander Han Zhui pressed Zhou Dewei to the open country south of Gaoyi along the river. The Zhen and Ding forces blocked the bridge approach, and Han sent picked troops to take it first.
entries.literal: In the campaign at Baixiang, the Bian general Han Zhui pursued Zhou Dewei to the wilds south of Gaoyi on the river; the Zhen and Ding troops held the bridge road, and Han chose elite troops to seize it first.

entries.zh: 莊宗登高而望，鎮、定兵將衄，謂建及曰：「如賊過橋，則勢不可遏，卿計若何？」
entries.en: Emperor Zhuangzong took a vantage point and saw the Zhen and Ding lines buckling. He asked Jianji, "If they get across that bridge we cannot stop them—what do you advise?"
entries.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong climbed high to look; the Zhen and Ding troops were about to be driven back, and he said to Jianji, "If the enemy cross the bridge, their momentum cannot be checked—what is your plan?"

entries.zh: 建及於部選士二百，挺槍大噪，禦汴軍，卻之於橋下。
entries.en: Jianji picked two hundred men from his command, charged with leveled spears and a thunderous cry, and threw the Bian troops back from the bridge.
entries.literal: Jianji from his unit chose two hundred men, levelled spears with a great shout, and met the Bian army, driving them back below the bridge.

entries.zh: 二月，王師攻魏，魏人夜出犯我營，建及設伏待之，扼其歸路，盡殪之。
entries.en: In the second month the imperial army besieged Wei. Wei forces raided the camp by night; Jianji laid an ambush, cut off their retreat, and wiped them out.
entries.literal: In the second month the royal army attacked Wei; the Wei men came out by night to strike our camp. Jianji set an ambush and waited, blocked their return route, and annihilated them.

entries.zh: 劉鄩之營莘縣，月餘不出，忽一旦縱兵攻鎮、定之營，軍中騰亂，建及率銀槍勁兵千人赴之，擊敗汴軍，追奔至其壘。
entries.en: Liu Yan had camped at Huaxian and for more than a month refused battle, then one day suddenly struck the Zhen and Ding encampment. As the army churned in panic, Jianji rushed up with a thousand silver-spear veterans, routed the Bian force, and chased them to their walls.
entries.literal: Liu Yan's camp was at Huaxian; for more than a month he did not come out, then suddenly one day he loosed his troops to attack the Zhen and Ding camp. The army was thrown into uproar; Jianji led a thousand silver-spear crack troops to the spot, defeated the Bian army, and pursued them to their ramparts.

entries.zh: 元城之戰，建及首陷其陣，授天雄軍教練使。
entries.en: At Yuancheng Jianji led the breach of the enemy line and was made drill instructor of the Tianxiong Army.
entries.literal: In the battle of Yuancheng Jianji was first to break their line and was appointed instructor of the Tianxiong Army.

entries.zh: 八月，遷遼州刺史。
entries.en: In the eighth month he was transferred to the prefecture of Liao.
entries.literal: In the eighth month he was transferred to be prefect of Liaozhou.

entries.zh: 十四年，從擊契丹於幽州，破之。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year he joined the campaign against the Khitan at Youzhou and routed them.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed the attack on the Khitan at Youzhou and defeated them.

entries.zh: 十二月，從攻楊劉，自寅至午，汴軍嬰城拒守，建及自負葭葦堙塹，率先登梯，遂拔之。
entries.en: In the twelfth month he took part in the assault on Yangliu. From dawn to midday the Bian garrison held the walls. Jianji carried bundles of reeds to fill the ditch, was first on the scaling ladder, and the city fell.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month he followed the assault on Yangliu; from the hour yin to the hour wu the Bian army clung to the walls in defense. Jianji shouldered reed bundles to fill the moat, was first up the ladder, and the place was taken.

entries.zh: 胡柳之役，前軍逗撓，際晚，汴軍登土山，建及一戰奪之。
entries.en: At Huliu the forward units stalled. Toward dusk the Bian troops seized a hillock; Jianji retook it in a single clash.
entries.literal: In the battle of Huliu the vanguard hung back; toward evening the Bian army climbed an earthen hill, and Jianji in one fight wrested it from them.

entries.zh: 莊宗欲收軍，詰朝合戰。
entries.en: Emperor Zhuangzong wanted to pull the army back and fight again at dawn.
entries.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong wished to withdraw the army and join battle at dawn the next day.

entries.zh: 建及橫槊當前，曰：「賊大將已亡，乘此易擊，王但登山，觀臣破賊！」
entries.en: Jianji planted his spear in their path and said, "Their chief commander is already dead—this is the moment to hit them while they are easy prey. Your Majesty has only to take the hill and watch me smash the foe!"
entries.literal: Jianji set his spear across the front and said, "The enemy's great general is already dead; press this advantage while it is easy to strike. Your Majesty need only climb the hill and watch your servant break the enemy!"

entries.zh: 即引銀槍效節大呼奮擊，三軍增氣，由是王師復振，以功授檢校司空、魏博內外衙都將。
entries.en: He immediately led the silver-spear Xiaojie guard in a roaring charge; morale surged through the army, and the imperial force rallied. For this he received the acting title of Sikong and command of Weibo's inner and outer gate troops.
entries.literal: At once he led the silver-spear Xiaojie troops in a great shout and fierce attack; the three armies took heart, and thereby the royal army revived. For merit he was appointed acting Sikong and commander of the inner and outer gates of Weibo.

entries.zh: 張廷裕，代北人也。
entries.en: Zhang Tingyu came from the northern frontier of Dai.
entries.literal: Zhang Tingyu was a man of the northern Dai region.

entries.zh: 幼事武皇於雲中，從平黃巢，討王行瑜，自行間漸升為小將。
entries.en: As a youth he served the Martial Emperor at Yunzhong, followed him against Huang Chao and Wang Xingyu, and slowly rose from the ranks to junior command.
entries.literal: In his youth he served the Martial Emperor at Yunzhong; he followed in the pacification of Huang Chao and the campaign against Wang Xingyu and gradually rose from the ranks to become a junior general.

entries.zh: 莊宗定魏，補天雄軍左廂馬步都虞候，曆蔚、慈、隰三州刺史。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong secured Wei he was made left-wing horse-and-foot commandant of the Tianxiong Army and later held the prefectures of Wei, Ci, and Xi in succession.
entries.literal: When the Emperor Zhuangzong settled Wei he was appointed left-wing horse-and-foot commandant of the Tianxiong Army and successively served as prefect of Wei, Ci, and Xi.

entries.zh: 同光三年，除新州節度使。
entries.en: In the third year of Tongguang he was appointed military commissioner of Xin.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tongguang he was made military commissioner of Xinzhou.

entries.zh: 塞上多事，廷裕無控製之術，邊鄙常聳。
entries.en: The northern marches were in constant turmoil; Tingyu lacked the skill to hold them, and the frontier stayed on edge.
entries.literal: The frontier was troubled with many affairs; Tingyu had no art of control, and the borderlands were often alarmed.

entries.zh: 天成三年，卒於治所。
entries.en: In the third year of Tiancheng he died in office.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng he died at his headquarters.

entries.zh: 詔贈太保。
entries.en: The court posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 王思同，幽州人也。
entries.en: Wang Sitong was a native of Youzhou.
entries.literal: Wang Sitong was a man of Youzhou.

entries.zh: 父敬柔，曆瀛、平、儒、檀、營五州刺史。
entries.en: His father Jingrou had been prefect in turn of Ying, Ping, Ru, Tan, and a second Ying Prefecture.
entries.literal: His father Jingrou successively served as prefect of Ying, Ping, Ru, Tan, and Ying prefectures.

entries.zh: 思同母即劉仁恭之女也，故思同初事仁恭為帳下軍校。
entries.en: Sitong's mother was a daughter of Liu Rengong, so he first served Rengong as an officer in his personal guard.
entries.literal: Sitong's mother was a daughter of Liu Rengong; therefore Sitong at first served Rengong as a guard officer under his tent.

entries.zh: 會劉守光攻仁恭於大安山，思同以部下兵歸太原，時年十六，武皇命為飛騰指揮使。
entries.en: When Liu Shouguang besieged Rengong at Mount Da'an, Sitong brought his men over to Taiyuan. He was sixteen; the Martial Emperor made him commander of the Feiteng guard.
entries.literal: When Liu Shouguang attacked Rengong at Da'an Mountain, Sitong led his subordinate troops to Taiyuan; he was then sixteen, and the Martial Emperor appointed him commander of the Feiteng guard.

entries.zh: 從莊宗平定山東，累典諸軍。
entries.en: He followed Zhuangzong in the pacification of Shandong and held a series of army commands.
entries.literal: He followed the Emperor Zhuangzong in pacifying Shandong and successively held command of various armies.

entries.zh: 石君立，趙州昭慶人也，亦謂之石家財。
entries.en: Shi Junli came from Zhaqing in Zhao Prefecture and was also known as Shi Jiacai.
entries.literal: Shi Junli was a native of Zhao Prefecture, Zhaqing district; he was also called Shi Jiacai.

entries.zh: 初事代州刺史李克柔，後隸李嗣昭為牙校，曆典諸軍。
entries.en: He first served Li Kerou, prefect of Dai, then entered Li Sizhao's guard and rose through commands over several armies.
entries.literal: At first he served the Daizhou prefect Li Kerou; later he came under Li Sizhao as a guard officer and successively held command of various armies.

entries.zh: 夾城之役，君立每出挑戰，壞汴軍柵壘，俘擒而還。
entries.en: At Jiacheng he repeatedly rode out to challenge the foe, tore up Bian stockades and walls, and came back with prisoners.
entries.literal: In the campaign at Jiacheng Junli each time went out to challenge the enemy, destroyed Bian palisades and ramparts, and returned with captives.

entries.zh: 八年，與汴軍戰於龍化園，敗之，獲其大將卜渥以獻。
entries.en: In the eighth year he met the Bian army at Longhua Garden, routed them, and sent up their commander Bu Wo as a captive.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he fought the Bian army at Longhua Garden, defeated them, and presented their great general Bu Wo as captive.

entries.zh: 嗣昭每出征，俾君立為前鋒，敵人畏之。
entries.en: Whenever Sizhao took the field he put Junli in the van, and enemies learned to dread the name.
entries.literal: Whenever Sizhao went on campaign he made Junli his vanguard; the enemy feared him.

entries.zh: 王檀之逼晉陽也，城中無備，安金全驅市人以登陴，保聚不完。
entries.en: When Wang Tan closed on Taiyuan the city was unprepared. An Jinquan pressed townsfolk onto the ramparts, but the defenses were still patchwork.
entries.literal: When Wang Tan pressed on Taiyuan the city had no preparations; An Jinquan drove townspeople onto the walls, but the defenses were incomplete.

entries.zh: 時莊宗在魏博，救應不暇，人心危懼，嗣昭遣君立率五百騎，自上黨朝發暮至。
entries.en: Zhuangzong was in Weibo and could not break away to help; panic spread. Sizhao dispatched Junli with five hundred cavalry from Shangdang—they left at dawn and reached Taiyuan by nightfall.
entries.literal: The Emperor Zhuangzong was then in Weibo and could not spare relief; hearts were fearful. Sizhao sent Junli with five hundred horsemen, who set out from Shangdang at dawn and arrived at dusk.

entries.zh: 王檀遊軍扼汾橋，君立一戰敗之，徑至城下，馳突斬擊，出入如神，大呼曰：「昭義侍中大軍至矣！」
entries.en: Wang Tan's scouts held the Fen Bridge; Junli smashed them in one clash, raced to the wall, and wheeled through the Bian ranks like a force of nature, roaring, "The Grand Preceptor of Zhaoyi is here with the main host!"
entries.literal: Wang Tan's roaming detachments held the Fen Bridge; Junli defeated them in one fight, went straight to the foot of the wall, and charged in and out like a spirit, shouting loudly, "The Grand Preceptor of Zhaoyi has arrived with the great army!"

entries.zh: 是夜入城，與安金全等分出諸門擊殺於外，遲明，梁軍敗走。
entries.en: He entered the city that night. With An Jinquan and others he sent parties out every gate to cut down the enemy outside; by first light the Liang army broke and ran.
entries.literal: That night he entered the city; with An Jinquan and others he sent men out through the various gates to strike and kill outside. At the light of dawn the Liang army was defeated and fled.

entries.zh: 十七年，將兵屯德勝。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year he garrisoned Desheng with his troops.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he led troops to garrison Desheng.

entries.zh: 時汴軍自滑州轉餉以給楊村寨，莊宗親率騎軍於河外，循岸而上，邀擊之。
entries.en: The Bian forces were shipping grain from Huazhou to Yangcun village; Zhuangzong himself led cavalry along the north bank upstream to intercept the convoys.
entries.literal: At that time the Bian army turned supplies from Huazhou to feed the stockade at Yangcun; the Emperor Zhuangzong personally led cavalry along the riverbank upstream to intercept them.

entries.zh: 汴人距楊村五十里，於河曲潘張村築壘以貯軍儲，莊宗令諸軍攻之。
entries.en: Fifty li short of Yangcun the enemy threw up a depot at Panzhang Village in the river bend; Zhuangzong ordered a general assault.
entries.literal: The Bian men, fifty li from Yangcun, built a stockade at Panzhang Village on the river bend to store provisions, and the Emperor Zhuangzong ordered the armies to attack it.

entries.zh: 汴人設伏於要路，逆戰偽敗，王師乘之，蹙入壘門，梁伏兵起，因與血戰。
entries.en: The Bian laid an ambush on the approach, offered a sham retreat, and drew the imperial troops charging through the gate. Liang men hidden inside sprang up and a savage melee followed.
entries.literal: The Bian men set an ambush on the critical road, met them in battle with a feigned defeat; the royal army pressed the pursuit and was crowded into the stockade gate. Liang hidden troops rose, and a bloody fight ensued.

entries.zh: 君立與鎮州大將王釗陷入賊壘，時諸將部校陷賊者十餘人，君立被執，送於汴。
entries.en: Junli and the Zhen commander Wang Zhao were caught inside the enemy fort along with more than a dozen other officers. Junli was taken and sent to Bian.
entries.literal: Junli and the Zhenzhou great general Wang Zhao fell into the enemy stockade; at the time more than ten generals and officers of various commands were trapped in the enemy works. Junli was seized and sent to Bian.

entries.zh: 梁祖素知其驍勇，欲用之為將，械而下獄。
entries.en: The Liang founder had long admired his fighting name and wanted him as a commander; they shackled him and threw him in prison.
entries.literal: The Liang Founder had long known his valor and wished to use him as a general; he was put in fetters and cast into prison.

entries.zh: 久之，梁主遣人誘之，君立曰：「敗軍之將，難與議勇，如欲將我，我雖真誠效命，能信我乎？
entries.en: After a long interval the Liang ruler sent envoys to win him over. Junli answered, "A beaten general is no one to talk bravery with. Even if I meant every word of loyalty, would you believe me?
entries.literal: After a long while the Liang ruler sent men to entice him. Junli said, "A defeated commander is a poor man to discuss valor with. If you wish to employ me, though I would serve you in all sincerity, could you trust me?

entries.zh: 人皆有君，吾何忍反為仇人哉！」
entries.en: Every man already has his sovereign—how could I stomach serving the man who is my foe?"
entries.literal: Every man has his lord—how could I bear to turn and serve my enemy?"

entries.zh: 既而諸將被戮，尚惜君立不之害。
entries.en: Before long the other captured officers were put to death, but they still kept Junli alive.
entries.literal: Soon after, the other captured generals were executed, yet they still spared Junli and did not kill him.

entries.zh: 同光元年，莊宗至汴前一日，梁主始令殺之。
entries.en: In the first year of Tongguang, the day before Zhuangzong entered Bian, the Liang ruler finally had him executed.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tongguang, on the day before the Emperor Zhuangzong reached Bian, the Liang ruler at last ordered him killed.

entries.zh: 思同性疏俊，粗有文，性喜為詩什，與人唱和，自稱薊門戰客。
entries.en: Sitong was easy in manner and not without book learning; he loved to write verse, traded poems with friends, and called himself the Battle Guest of Jimen.
entries.literal: Sitong was by nature open and handsome, had some learning in letters, delighted in composing verse, exchanged poems with others, and styled himself the Battle Guest of Jimen.

entries.zh: 魏王繼岌待之若子。
entries.en: The Prince of Wei, Jiji, treated him almost as a son.
entries.literal: Prince of Wei Jiji treated him like a son.

entries.zh: 時內養呂知柔侍興聖宮，頗用事，思同不平之。
entries.en: The palace eunuch Lü Zhirou, who served the Xingsheng Palace, had grown powerful; Sitong chafed at it.
entries.literal: At that time the inner attendant Lü Zhirou attended the Xingsheng Palace and wielded considerable power; Sitong resented this.

entries.zh: 呂為終南山詩，末句有「頭」字，思同和曰：「料伊直擬衝霄漢，賴有青天壓著頭。」
entries.en: Lü wrote a poem on Mount Zhongnan ending with the word "head"; Sitong answered, "You seem ready to punch through the sky—lucky for you the blue heaven still weighs on your head."
entries.literal: Lü composed a poem on Mount Zhongnan whose closing line contained the character "head"; Sitong replied in verse, "I suppose you mean to pierce the heavens—fortunately blue heaven still presses on your head."

entries.zh: 其所為詩句，皆此類也。
entries.en: His verses were all barbs of that kind.
entries.literal: The lines he wrote in his poems were all of this sort.

entries.zh: 每從征，必在興聖帳下，然同光朝，位止鄭州刺史。
entries.en: He campaigned always in the Xingsheng train, yet under Tongguang he rose no higher than prefect of Zheng.
entries.literal: Whenever he followed on campaign he was always under the Xingsheng tent, yet in the Tongguang reign his rank stopped at prefect of Zheng.

entries.zh: 明宗在軍時，素知之，即位後，用為同州節度使，未幾，移鎮隴右。
entries.en: Mingzong had known him in the field; once enthroned he made him commissioner of Tong, then soon moved him to Longyou.
entries.literal: The Emperor Mingzong had known him well when in the army; after he took the throne he used him as military commissioner of Tongzhou, and before long transferred him to garrison Longyou.

entries.zh: 思同好文士，無賢不肖，必館接賄遺，歲費數十萬。
