entries.en: Sitong cultivated scholars high and low, housed them and showered gifts until he spent hundreds of thousands each year.
entries.literal: Sitong favored literary men; whether worthy or base he would lodge and entertain them with gifts, spending several hundred thousand a year.

entries.zh: 在秦州累年，邊民懷惠，華戎寧息。
entries.en: Through long years at Qin the frontier people felt his kindness, and Chinese and tribesmen alike kept the peace.
entries.literal: For many years at Qinzhou the border people cherished his kindness, and Chinese and barbarians were at peace.

entries.zh: 長興元年，入朝，見於中興殿。
entries.en: In the first year of Changxing he came to court and was received in the Zhongxing Hall.
entries.literal: In the first year of Changxing he entered court and was received at the Zhongxing Hall.

entries.zh: 明宗問秦州邊事，對曰：「秦州與吐蕃接境，蕃部多違法度。
entries.en: Mingzong asked about the Qin frontier. He answered, "Qin marches on Tibet, and many tribesmen ignore our laws.
entries.literal: The Emperor Mingzong asked about Qinzhou frontier affairs; he replied, "Qinzhou borders the Tibetans, and many of the tribal peoples violate the law.

entries.zh: 臣設法招懷，沿邊置寨四十餘所，控其要害。
entries.en: I devised ways to win them and strung more than forty stockades along the border to hold the passes.
entries.literal: I devised measures to win them over and along the border set up more than forty stockades to control the strategic points.

entries.zh: 每蕃人互市、飲食之界上，令納器械。」
entries.en: Whenever Tibetans came to market or ate at the border markets, I required them to hand over their arms."
entries.literal: Whenever Tibetans met to trade or took food at the border, I had them surrender their weapons."

entries.zh: 因手指畫秦州山川要害控扼處。
entries.en: As he spoke he traced with his finger the mountains, rivers, and choke points of Qin on the map.
entries.literal: Thereupon with his finger he traced on the map the mountains, rivers, strategic points, and points of control at Qinzhou.

entries.zh: 明宗曰：「人言思同不管事，豈及此耶！」
entries.en: Mingzong said, "They say Sitong never tends to business—yet look at this!"
entries.literal: The Emperor Mingzong said, "People say Sitong pays no attention to affairs—could it reach even to this!"

entries.zh: 時兩川叛，欲用之，且留左右，故授右武衛將軍。
entries.en: With both Sichuan circuits in revolt the court wanted his service but also wanted him close, so they made him General of the Right Martial Guard.
entries.literal: At that time the two Sichuan circuits were in rebellion; they wished to use him but also keep him at court, and therefore appointed him General of the Right Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 八月，授西南面行營馬步都虞候。
entries.en: In the eighth month he was named horse-and-foot commandant of the southwestern expedition.
entries.literal: In the eighth month he was appointed horse-and-foot commandant of the southwestern campaign army.

entries.zh: 九月，遷京兆尹、西京留守。
entries.en: In the ninth month he became metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao and custodian of the western capital.
entries.literal: In the ninth month he was transferred to metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao and custodian of the western capital.

entries.zh: 伐蜀之役，為先鋒指揮使。
entries.en: In the Shu campaign he commanded the vanguard.
entries.literal: In the campaign against Shu he served as vanguard commander.

entries.zh: 石敬瑭入大散關。
entries.en: Shi Jingtang pushed through Dasan Pass.
entries.literal: Shi Jingtang entered Dasan Pass.

entries.zh: 思同恃勇先入劍門，大軍未相繼，復被董璋兵逐出之。
entries.en: Sitong, trusting his bravery, rushed into Jianmen before the main host could follow and was thrown back out by Dong Zhang's men.
entries.literal: Sitong, relying on his valor, entered Jianmen first; the main army had not followed in succession, and he was again driven out by Dong Zhang's troops.

entries.zh: 及敬瑭班師，思同以曾獲劍門之功，移鎮山南西道。
entries.en: When Jingtang pulled the army back, Sitong was shifted to Shannan West Circuit for his earlier success at Jianmen.
entries.literal: When Jingtang withdrew the army, Sitong for his former merit in taking Jianmen was transferred to garrison Shannan West Circuit.

entries.zh: 二十二日，潞王至昭應，前鋒執思同來獻。
entries.en: On the twenty-second the Prince of Lu reached Zhaoying; the van took Sitong and brought him in as prisoner.
entries.literal: On the twenty-second the Prince of Lu reached Zhaoying; the vanguard seized Sitong and brought him forward as captive.

entries.zh: 王謂左右曰：「思同計乖於事，然盡心於所奉，亦可嘉也。」
entries.en: The prince told his attendants, "Sitong chose the losing side, but he gave his whole heart to his lord—that still deserves praise."
entries.literal: The prince said to those at his side, "Sitong's plans went awry in the affair, yet he gave his whole heart to what he served—that too can be praised."

entries.zh: 顧謂趙守鈞曰：「思同爾之故人，可行迓之於路，達予撫慰之意。」
entries.en: He said to Zhao Shoujun, "Sitong is your old friend—go meet him on the road and tell him I mean to treat him kindly."
entries.literal: He turned to Zhao Shoujun and said, "Sitong is an old friend of yours; you may go meet him on the road and convey my intent to comfort him."

entries.zh: 思同至，潞王讓之曰：「賊臣傾我國家，殘害骨肉，非予弟之過。
entries.en: When Sitong came up, the Prince of Lu rebuked him: "Traitors have wrecked the realm and hurt the imperial house—that is not my brother's fault.
entries.literal: When Sitong arrived the Prince of Lu reproached him, saying, "Traitorous ministers have overturned our state and harmed the imperial kin—that is no fault of your younger brother.

entries.zh: 我起兵岐山，蓋誅一二賊臣耳，爾何首鼠兩端，多方誤我，今日之罪，其可逃乎！」
entries.en: I marched from Qishan to kill only a handful of villains. Why did you hedge like a cornered rat and lead me astray at every turn? Can you escape punishment today?!"
entries.literal: I raised the army at Qishan to execute only one or two traitor ministers; why did you waver like a rat, misleading me in so many ways? Today's guilt—can it be escaped?!"

entries.zh: 思同曰：「臣起自行間，受先朝爵命，秉旄仗鉞，累曆重藩，終無顯效以答殊遇。
entries.en: Sitong answered, "I came up from the ranks, took titles from the late emperor, bore commander's insignia, and held one great post after another, yet never repaid that grace with any deed worth the name.
entries.literal: Sitong said, "Your servant rose from the ranks, received titles from the former court, bore the banner and battle-axe, and successively held great frontier posts, yet in the end had no outstanding achievement to repay extraordinary favor.

entries.zh: 臣非不知攀龍附鳳則福多，扶衰救弱則禍速，但恐瞑目之後，無麵見先帝。
entries.en: I know perfectly well that siding with the winner brings fortune and backing the loser brings ruin—but when I shut my eyes I could not face the late emperor.
entries.literal: Your servant is not unaware that to cling to the rising dragon and phoenix brings many blessings, while to support the declining and save the weak brings swift calamity—but I fear that after I close my eyes I would have no face to meet the late emperor.

entries.zh: 釁鼓膏原，縲囚之常分也。」
entries.en: War drums and the executioner's field, the captive's proper fate—that is the law of such days."
entries.literal: Beating the war drum and smearing the plain with grease, and the bound prisoner's allotted portion—these are the constant rules."

entries.zh: 潞王為之改容，徐謂之曰：「且憩歇。」
entries.en: The prince's face softened. He said gently, "Rest awhile."
entries.literal: The Prince of Lu changed countenance for him and slowly said, "Rest for a while."

entries.zh: 潞王欲用之，而楊思權之徒恥見其面，屢啟劉延朗，言「思同不可留，慮失士心。」
entries.en: The prince meant to keep him, but Yang Siquan and the others could not bear to look on him. They told Liu Yanlang again and again, "Sitong must not stay or we will lose the army's loyalty."
entries.literal: The Prince of Lu wished to employ him, but Yang Siquan and his sort were ashamed to see his face; they repeatedly told Liu Yanlang, saying, "Sitong cannot be kept—we fear losing the soldiers' hearts."

entries.zh: 又，潞王入長安時，尹暉盡得思同家財及諸妓女，故尤惡思同，與劉延朗亟言之。
entries.en: When the prince entered Chang'an, Yin Hui had plundered Sitong's house and his singing girls, so he hated Sitong all the more and pressed Liu Yanlang to act.
entries.literal: Moreover, when the Prince of Lu entered Chang'an, Yin Hui had seized all of Sitong's family wealth and courtesans; therefore he especially hated Sitong and urged Liu Yanlang with him repeatedly.

entries.zh: 屬王醉，不待報，殺思同並其子德勝。
entries.en: While the prince was drunk they did not wait for orders and killed Sitong and his son Desheng.
entries.literal: When the prince was drunk they did not wait for word and killed Sitong together with his son Desheng.

entries.zh: 潞王醒，召思同，左右報已誅之矣。
entries.en: When the prince woke he called for Sitong; his attendants said the man was already dead.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Lu awoke he summoned Sitong; those at his side reported that he had already been executed.

entries.zh: 潞王怒延朗，累日嗟惜之。
entries.en: The prince raged at Yanlang and mourned the deed for days.
entries.literal: The Prince of Lu was angry with Yanlang and for many days sighed in regret.

entries.zh: 及漢高祖即位，詔贈侍中。
entries.en: When Gaozu of Later Han came to the throne, the court posthumously made him Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: When the Gaozu of Han took the throne, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 時以東川帥董璋恃險難製，乃以武虔裕為綿州刺史，董璋益懷疑忌，遂縶虔裕以叛。
entries.en: Eastern Chuan's Dong Zhang held difficult country and defied control; when Wu Qianyu was sent to Mianzhou, Zhang's suspicions deepened and he imprisoned Yu and rebelled.
entries.literal: At the time Eastern Chuan commander Dong Zhang relied on rugged terrain and was hard to control; Wuyou Yu was made Mianzhou prefect, and Zhang grew more suspicious, then imprisoned Yu and rebelled.

entries.zh: 及石敬瑭領王師伐蜀，峽路艱阻，糧運不繼，明宗憂之，而重誨請行。
entries.en: Shi Jingtang's expedition into Shu stalled on bad passes and broken supply lines; Mingzong worried, and Chonghui volunteered to go west.
entries.literal: When Shi Jingtang led the imperial army to conquer Shu, the gorge routes were arduous and grain could not follow; Mingzong worried, and Chonghui asked to go in person.

entries.zh: 翌日，領數騎而出，日馳數百里，西諸侯聞之，莫不惶駭。
entries.en: Next day he rode out with a few escorts, covering hundreds of li a day; western governors were terrified.
entries.literal: The next day he led several horsemen and set out, galloping several hundred li a day; western lords hearing of it were all terrified.

entries.zh: 所在錢帛糧料，星夜輦運，人乘斃踣於山路者不可勝紀，百姓苦之。
entries.en: Cash, grain, and fodder were rushed by night wherever he went; men and horses littered the roads dead beyond count, and the people groaned under it.
entries.literal: Wherever he passed, cash, silk, and grain were transported by night; men and horses collapsed dead on mountain roads beyond counting, and the people suffered bitterly.

entries.zh: 重誨至鳳翔，節度使朱弘昭延於寢室，令妻子奉食器，敬事尤謹。
entries.en: At Fengxiang, commissioner Zhu Hongzhao welcomed him to his private quarters; wife and children served food with deepest respect.
entries.literal: When Chonghui reached Fengxiang, military commissioner Zhu Hongzhao received him in the bedchamber and had wife and children present food vessels, serving with utmost deference.

entries.zh: 重誨坐中言及：「昨有人讒構，幾不保全，賴聖上保鑒，苟獲全族。」
entries.en: Over the meal Chonghui said, "Yesterday slander nearly destroyed me; only the Emperor's grace spared my house."
entries.literal: Seated, Chonghui spoke of how "yesterday someone slandered me and I nearly did not survive; relying on the sacred sovereign's protection I barely preserved my clan."

entries.zh: 因泣下。
entries.en: He wept.
entries.literal: He thereupon wept.

entries.zh: 重誨既辭，弘昭遣人具奏：「重誨怨望出惡言，不可令至行營，恐奪石敬瑭兵柄。」
entries.en: After he left, Hongzhao reported, "Chonghui spoke bitterly in resentment; keep him from the front lest he steal Shi's command."
entries.literal: After Chonghui took leave, Hongzhao sent men to memorialize: "Chonghui harbors resentment and spoke evil words; he must not be allowed to reach the camp, lest he seize Shi Jingtang's command."

entries.zh: 而宣徽使孟漢瓊自西回，亦奏重誨過惡。
entries.en: Xuanhui commissioner Meng Hanqiong, back from the west, also denounced Chonghui.
entries.literal: Meanwhile Xuanhui commissioner Meng Hanqiong, returning from the west, also memorialized Chonghui's offenses.

entries.zh: 重誨已至三泉，復令歸闕。
entries.en: Chonghui had reached Sanquan when orders recalled him to court.
entries.literal: Chonghui had already reached Sanquan when he was ordered to return to court.

entries.zh: 再過鳳翔，朱弘昭拒而不納，重誨懼，急騎奔程，未至京師，製授河中帥。
entries.en: Passing Fengxiang again, Hongzhao shut him out; in fear he raced on, and before the capital an edict made him Hedong commander.
entries.literal: Passing Fengxiang again, Zhu Hongzhao refused entry; Chonghui was afraid, spurred his horse on the road, and before reaching the capital was appointed Hedong commander by edict.

entries.zh: 既至鎮，心不自安，遂請致仕。
entries.en: At his post he could not rest easy and asked to retire.
entries.literal: Once at his post he was ill at ease in mind and asked to retire.

entries.zh: 製初下，其子崇讚、崇緒走歸河中。
entries.en: When the edict issued, sons Chongzan and Chongxu fled to him at Hedong.
entries.literal: When the edict first came down, his sons Chongzan and Chongxu fled to Hedong.

entries.zh: 二子初至，重誨駭然曰：「渠安得來？」
entries.en: At their arrival Chonghui cried, "How did they get here?"
entries.literal: When the two sons first arrived, Chonghui said in alarm, "How could they come?"

entries.zh: 家人欲問故，重誨曰：「吾知之矣，此非渠意，是他人教來。
entries.en: His family asked why; he said, "I know—they did not choose this; someone sent them.
entries.literal: The household wished to ask the reason; Chonghui said, "I know already—this is not their wish; others taught them to come.

entries.zh: 吾但以一死報國家，餘復何言！」
entries.en: I owe the state only my death—nothing more to say!"
entries.literal: I will repay the state with death alone—what more is there to say!"

entries.zh: 翌日，中使至，見重誨，號泣久之。
entries.en: Next day an imperial messenger came and wept long at the sight of him.
entries.literal: The next day an imperial messenger came; seeing Chonghui, he wept a long while.

entries.zh: 重誨曰：「公但言其故，勿過相湣。」
entries.en: Chonghui said, "Speak your errand—do not pity me so."
entries.literal: Chonghui said, "Sir, speak only the reason—do not pity me overmuch."

entries.zh: 中使曰：「人言令公據城異志矣！」
entries.en: The messenger said, "They say you hold the city in rebellion!"
entries.literal: The messenger said, "People say my lord holds the city with alien intent!"

entries.zh: 重誨曰：「吾一死未塞責，已負君親，安敢輒懷異志，遽勞朝廷興師，增聖上宵旰，則仆之罪更萬萬矣！」
entries.en: Chonghui said, "One death cannot answer my debt—I have failed emperor and kin; how dare I rebel and trouble the court and your sleepless nights—my guilt would only multiply!"
entries.literal: Chonghui said, "My death alone does not discharge my duty—I have already failed lord and kin; how dare I harbor alien intent, hastily to trouble the court with troops and add to the sacred sovereign's sleepless nights—then my guilt would be ten thousandfold greater!"

entries.zh: 朱弘昭，太原人也。
entries.en: Zhu Hongzhao was from Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Zhu Hongzhao was a man of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 祖玟，父叔宗，皆為本府牙將。
entries.en: His grandfather Min and father Shuzong were both staff officers of the Taiyuan command.
entries.literal: Ancestor Min, father Shuzong—both were junior officers of the native commandery.

entries.zh: 弘昭事明宗，在藩方為典客。
entries.en: He served Mingzong as guest-reception officer in the prince's domain.
entries.literal: Hongzhao served Mingzong; in the frontier post he was guest-reception officer.

entries.zh: 天成元年，為文思使，曆東川副使，二年餘，除左衛大將軍，充內客省使。
entries.en: Tiancheng 1 he became Literary Thought commissioner; after two years as Eastern Chuan deputy he was Left Guard senior general and Inner Guest Service commissioner.
entries.literal: In Tiancheng year 1 he was Literary Thought commissioner; he passed through Eastern Chuan deputy commissioner for more than two years, then was made Left Guard senior general and Inner Guest Service commissioner.

entries.zh: 三年，轉宣徽南院使。
entries.en: Year 3 he became Southern Xuanhui commissioner.
entries.literal: In year 3 he was transferred Southern Xuanhui commissioner.

entries.zh: 明宗親祀南郊，弘昭為大內留守，加檢校太傅。
entries.en: At Mingzong's southern suburban sacrifice Hongzhao was grand inner custodian and made acting Grand Mentor.
entries.literal: When Mingzong personally sacrificed at the southern suburb, Hongzhao was grand inner custodian and was given acting Grand Mentor.

entries.zh: 出鎮鳳翔，會朝廷命石敬塘帥師伐蜀，久未成功，安重誨自請西行。
entries.en: He took Fengxiang; Shi Jingtang's Shu campaign stalled; An Chonghui volunteered to go west.
entries.literal: He went out to hold Fengxiang; the court appointed Shi Jingtang to command troops against Shu; long without success, An Chonghui asked to go west himself.

entries.zh: 至鳳翔，弘昭迎謁馬首，請館於府署，妻子羅拜，捧卮為壽。
entries.en: At Fengxiang Hongzhao met him on the road, lodged him at his mansion, and had wife and children bow and toast his health.
entries.literal: Reaching Fengxiang, Hongzhao met him at his horse's head and asked him to lodge at the commissioner's residence; wife and children kowtowed, raised cups to wish long life.

entries.zh: 弘昭密遣人謂敬瑭曰：「安公親來勞軍，觀其舉措孟浪，儻令得至，恐士心迎合，則不戰而自潰也。
entries.en: He secretly told Jingtang, "Lord An comes to oversee the army; he acts rashly—if he reaches camp the men may rally to him and you will collapse without fighting.
entries.literal: Hongzhao secretly sent word to Jingtang: "Lord An has come in person to comfort the army; observing his conduct he is rash; if he is allowed to arrive, I fear the soldiers' hearts will align with him and the army will collapse without battle.

entries.zh: 可速拒之，必不敢前，則師徒萬全也。」
entries.en: Turn him back at once—he will not dare advance, and all will be safe."
entries.literal: Quickly refuse him—he will surely not advance, and then master and troops will be wholly secure."

entries.zh: 敬瑭聞其言大懼，即日燒營遁還。
entries.en: Jingtang, terrified, burned camp and retreated the same day.
entries.literal: Jingtang, hearing the words, was greatly afraid and that day burned camp and fled back.

entries.zh: 重誨聞之，不敢西行，因返旆東還。
entries.en: Chonghui, hearing this, dared not go west and turned back east.
entries.literal: Chonghui, hearing of it, did not dare go west and therefore turned his banners east.

entries.zh: 復過鳳翔，弘昭拒而不納。
entries.en: Passing Fengxiang again, Hongzhao shut him out.
entries.literal: Passing Fengxiang again, Hongzhao refused entry.

entries.zh: 及重誨得罪，其年弘昭入朝，授左武衛上將軍，充宣徽南院使。
entries.en: When Chonghui fell, Hongzhao came to court as Left Martial Guard senior general and Southern Xuanhui commissioner.
entries.literal: When Chonghui fell from grace, that year Hongzhao entered court and was made Left Martial Guard senior general and Southern Xuanhui commissioner.

entries.zh: 長興三年十二月，代康義誠為襄州節度使。
entries.en: Changxing 3, month 12, he replaced Kang Yicheng at Xiangyang.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of Changxing year 3 he replaced Kang Yicheng as Xiangzhou military commissioner.

entries.zh: 四年，秦王從榮為元帥，屢宣惡言，執政大臣皆懼，謀出避之。
entries.en: Year 4 the Prince of Qin Congrong was marshal and spoke threats; ministers feared and sought posts away from court.
entries.literal: In year 4 Prince of Qin Congrong was marshal; he repeatedly proclaimed evil words; the chief ministers all feared and plotted to leave and avoid him.

entries.zh: 樞密使范延光、趙延壽日夕更見，涕泣求去，明宗怒而不許。
entries.en: Commissioners Fan Yanguang and Zhao Yanshou wept daily for release; Mingzong refused in anger.
entries.literal: Privy Council commissioners Fan Yanguang and Zhao Yanshou saw the emperor morning and evening in turn, weeping and begging to leave; Mingzong was angry and did not permit it.

entries.zh: 延壽使其妻興平公主入言於中，延光亦因孟漢瓊、王淑妃進說，故皆得免。
entries.en: Yanshou's wife the Princess of Xingping pleaded within; Yanguang used Meng Hanqiong and Consort Wang—both won leave.
entries.literal: Yanshou had his wife Princess of Xingping speak within the palace; Yanguang also advanced persuasion through Meng Hanqiong and Consort Wang—thus both were released.

entries.zh: 未幾，趙延壽出鎮汴州，召弘昭於襄陽，代為樞密使，加同平章事。
entries.en: Soon Zhao Yanshou went to Bian; Hongzhao was recalled from Xiangyang as Privy Council commissioner with co-chief councilor rank.
entries.literal: Before long Zhao Yanshou went out to hold Bianzhou; Hongzhao was summoned from Xiangyang to replace him as Privy Council commissioner and was given co-chief councilor.

entries.zh: 十月，范延光出鎮常山，以三司使馮贇與弘昭對掌樞務，與康義誠、孟漢瓊同謀以殺秦王。
entries.en: Month 10 Fan Yanguang went to Changshan; Feng Yun shared the Privy Council with Hongzhao; they joined Kang Yicheng and Meng Hanqiong to plot the Prince of Qin's death.
entries.literal: In the tenth month Fan Yanguang went out to hold Changshan; Revenue commissioner Feng Yun and Hongzhao jointly held Privy affairs, and with Kang Yicheng and Meng Hanqiong conspired to kill the Prince of Qin.

entries.zh: 閔帝即位，弘昭以為由己得立，故於庶事高下在心，及赦後覃恩，弘昭首自平章事超加中書令。
entries.en: Emperor Min's accession Hongzhao credited to himself; he dictated policy; after the general amnesty he jumped from co-chief councilor to chief councilor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Min ascended, Hongzhao thought he had been enthroned through himself and therefore in common affairs high and low rested in his heart; after the amnesty and broad grace, Hongzhao was first to leap from co-chief councilor to chief councilor.

entries.zh: 素猜忌潞王，致其釁隙，以致禍敗。
entries.en: He always distrusted the Prince of Lu, widened the breach, and brought disaster.
entries.literal: He always suspected the Prince of Lu and provoked their rift, bringing calamity and ruin.

entries.zh: 潞王至陝，閔帝懼，欲奔，馳手詔弘昭圖之。
entries.en: At the Prince of Lu's arrival in Shan, Emperor Min panicked and meant to flee; he sent an urgent hand edict to Hongzhao to act.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Lu reached Shan, Emperor Min was afraid and wished to flee; he sent a hand edict by express to Hongzhao to plot against him.

entries.zh: 時將軍穆延輝在弘昭第，曰：「急召，罪我也，其如之何？
entries.en: General Mu Yanhui was at his house and said, "They summon in haste—the blame is mine; what now?
entries.literal: At the time General Mu Yanhui was at Hongzhao's residence and said, "Urgent summons—the guilt is mine; what is to be done?

entries.zh: 吾兒婦，君之女也，可速迎歸，無令受禍。」
entries.en: My son's wife is your daughter—fetch her at once lest she be harmed."
entries.literal: My son's wife is your daughter—quickly welcome her back, lest she suffer calamity."

entries.zh: 中使繼至，弘昭援劍大哭，至後庭欲自裁，家人力止之。
entries.en: Messengers followed; Hongzhao drew his sword, wept, and went to the rear court to die; his family restrained him.
entries.literal: Imperial messengers came in succession; Hongzhao drew his sword and wept greatly, went to the rear court intending to kill himself, and the household forcibly stopped him.

entries.zh: 使促之急，弘昭曰：「窮至此耶！」
entries.en: Pressed hard, Hongzhao cried, "Brought to this pass!"
entries.literal: The messenger pressed urgently; Hongzhao said, "Reduced to this!"

entries.zh: 乃自投於井。
entries.en: He threw himself into a well.
entries.literal: He thereupon threw himself into a well.

entries.zh: 安從進既殺馮贇，斷弘昭首，俱傳於陝州。
entries.en: An Congjin killed Feng Yun, took Hongzhao's head, and both were rushed to Shan.
entries.literal: An Congjin, having killed Feng Yun, severed Hongzhao's head; both were sent in relay to Shanzhou.

entries.zh: 及漢高祖即位，贈尚書令。
entries.en: Later Han Gaozu posthumously made him Minister of Works.
entries.literal: When Gaozu of Later Han ascended, he was posthumously made Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 藥彥稠，沙陀三部落人。
entries.en: Yao Yanchou came from the three Shatuo tribes.
entries.literal: Yao Yanchou was a man of the three Shatuo tribal groups.

entries.zh: 幼以騎射事明宗，累遷至列校。
entries.en: Young he rode for Mingzong and rose to company rank.
entries.literal: In youth he served Mingzong with mounted archery and rose through the ranks to company commander.

entries.zh: 明宗踐阼，領澄州刺史、河陽馬步都將。
entries.en: At Mingzong's accession he held Cheng and commanded Heyang horse and foot.
entries.literal: When Mingzong ascended he held Chengzhou and was Heyang Horse and Foot commander.

entries.zh: 從王晏球討王都於定州，平之，領壽州節度使、侍衛步軍都虞候。
entries.en: With Wang Yanqiu he pacified Wang Du at Ding and received Shou and Foot Army deputy command.
entries.literal: Following Wang Yanqiu against Wang Du at Dingzhou, when it was pacified he held Shouzhou and was Palace Guard Foot Army deputy commander.

entries.zh: 屬河中指揮使楊彥溫作亂，彥稠改侍衛步軍都指揮使，充河中副招討使，將兵討平之。
entries.en: Yang Yanwen's Hedong revolt made him Foot commander and deputy pacifier; he crushed the rebellion.
entries.literal: When Hedong commander Yang Yanwen rebelled, Yanchou was made Foot Army commander and Hedong deputy pacification commissioner and led troops to pacify it.

entries.zh: 無幾，党項劫回鶻入朝使，詔彥稠屯朔方，就討党項之叛命者，搜索盜賊，盡獲回鶻所貢駝馬、寶玉，擒首領而還。
entries.en: Tangut raiders struck the Uighur tribute mission; Yanchou camped at Shuofang, hunted rebels and bandits, recovered the tribute camels, horses, and gems, and returned with chiefs captive.
entries.literal: Before long the Tangut raided the Uighur tribute mission to court; an edict ordered Yanchou to camp at Shuofang and pursue the Tangut rebels, search out bandits, recover all the camels, horses, and gems the Uighurs had presented, and return having captured the chiefs.

entries.zh: 尋授邠州節度使。
entries.en: Soon he was commissioner of Bin.
entries.literal: Soon he was made Binzhou military commissioner.

entries.zh: 遣會兵製置鹽州，蕃戎逃遁，獲陷蕃士庶千餘人，遣復鄉里。
entries.en: Ordered to secure Salt Prefecture, the tribes fled; over a thousand captives were restored to their homes.
entries.literal: He was ordered to join forces and establish control at Salt Prefecture; the frontier tribes fled; more than a thousand commoners and soldiers lost to the tribes were recovered and sent home.

entries.zh: 受詔與延州節度使，
entries.en: He joined the Yanzhou commissioner,
entries.literal: He received orders with the Yanzhou military commissioner,

entries.zh: 〈（案：原本闕二字。）〉
entries.en: (Two characters are missing in the original.)〉
entries.literal: (Note: The original text lacks two characters.)〉

entries.zh: 進攻夏州，累月不克，兵罷歸鎮。
entries.en: to attack Xiazhou; months passed without success; the army withdrew.
entries.literal: to attack Xiazhou; for many months they could not take it; the army ceased and returned to post.

entries.zh: 閔帝嗣位，與王思同攻鳳翔，為副招討使。
entries.en: Under Emperor Min he attacked Fengxiang with Wang Sitong as deputy pacifier.
entries.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded, with Wang Sitong he attacked Fengxiang as deputy pacification commissioner.

entries.zh: 禁軍之潰，彥稠欲沿流而遁，為軍士所擒而獻之。
entries.en: When the palace guard broke, Yanchou tried to flee downstream but soldiers seized and handed him over.
entries.literal: When the Forbidden Army collapsed, Yanchou wished to flee downriver but was seized by soldiers and presented.

entries.zh: 時末帝已至華州，令拘於獄，誅之。
entries.en: The Last Emperor was at Hua; he was jailed and killed.
entries.literal: At the time the Last Emperor had reached Hua; he ordered him imprisoned and executed.

entries.zh: 漢高祖即位，與王思同並製贈侍中。
entries.en: Later Han Gaozu posthumously made him and Wang Sitong Palace Attendants.
entries.literal: When Gaozu of Later Han ascended, he and Wang Sitong were both posthumously made Palace Attendant by edict.

entries.zh: 康義誠，字信臣，代北三部落人也。
entries.en: Kang Yicheng, style Xinchen, came from the three northern tribal groups.
entries.literal: Kang Yicheng, styled Xinchen, was a man of the three tribal groups of northern Dai.

entries.zh: 少以騎射事武皇，從莊宗入魏博，補突騎使，累遷本軍都指揮使。
entries.en: Young he rode for the Martial Emperor; entering Weibo with Zhuangzong he became a Swift Cavalry officer and rose to command the household guard.
entries.literal: In youth he served the Martial Emperor with mounted archery; following Zhuangzong into Weibo he was made Swift Cavalry officer and rose to commander of the native army.

entries.zh: 同光末，從明宗討鄴城，軍亂，迫明宗為主，明宗不然。
entries.en: At Tongguang's end he followed Mingzong against Ye; mutineers pressed Mingzong to rule and he refused.
entries.literal: At the end of Tongguang he followed Mingzong to campaign at Ye city; the army mutinied and forced Mingzong to be ruler; Mingzong did not agree.

entries.zh: 義誠進曰：「主上不慮社稷阽危，不思戰士勞苦，荒耽禽色，溺於酒樂。
entries.en: Yicheng urged, "The throne ignores peril and the soldiers' pain, drowning in sport and wine.
entries.literal: Yicheng advanced and said, "The sovereign above does not consider the altars in peril, does not think of the soldiers' toil, indulges in birds and beasts, and drowns in wine and music.

entries.zh: 今從眾則有歸，守節則將死。」
entries.en: Follow the crowd and we live; hold to loyalty and we die."
entries.literal: Now if we follow the multitude there is return; if we hold to integrity we will die."

entries.zh: 明宗納其言，由是委之心膂。
entries.en: Mingzong took his counsel and trusted him with his inmost thoughts.
entries.literal: Mingzong accepted his words; from this he entrusted him with his innermost counsel.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，加檢校司空，領富州刺史，總突騎如故。
entries.en: At Mingzong's accession he became acting Minister of Works, governed Fu, and kept the Swift Cavalry.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he was given acting Minister of Works, held Fuzhou, and still commanded the Swift Cavalry.

entries.zh: 尋轉捧聖都指揮使，鎮邠州刺史。
entries.en: Soon he commanded the Sacred Guard and held Bin.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to commander of the Sacred Guard and military commissioner of Bin.

entries.zh: 明宗幸汴，平朱守殷，改侍衛馬軍都指揮使，領江西節度使。
entries.en: At Bian he pacified Zhu Shouyin and became Horse Army commander and Jiangxi commissioner.
entries.literal: When Mingzong visited Bian and pacified Zhu Shouyin, he was made Palace Guard Horse Army commander and Jiangxi military commissioner.

entries.zh: 車駕歸洛，授侍衛馬步軍都指揮使、河陽節度使。
entries.en: Back in Luoyang he held Horse and Foot command and Heyang.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang he was made Palace Guard Horse and Foot commander and Heyang military commissioner.

entries.zh: 長興末，加同平章事。
entries.en: Late Changxing he became co-chief councilor.
entries.literal: At the end of Changxing he was given co-chief councilor.

entries.zh: 〈（《玉堂閑話》云：長興中，侍衛使康義誠，嘗軍中差人於大宅充院子，亦曾小有笞責。
entries.en: (The 《Idle Talk from the Jade Hall》: Changxing-era commissioner Kang Yicheng once took a man from a great house as yard servant and had him lightly beaten.
entries.literal: (《Idle Talk from the Jade Hall》 says: In Changxing, Palace Guard commissioner Kang Yicheng once detailed a man from a great mansion as courtyard servant and had also lightly flogged him.

entries.zh: 忽一日，憐其老而詰其姓氏，則曰：「姓康。」
entries.en: One day pitying his age he asked his name: "Kang."
entries.literal: Suddenly one day, pitying his age, he questioned his surname; he said, "The surname is Kang."

entries.zh: 別詰其鄉土、親族、息嗣，方知是父，遂相持而泣，聞者莫不驚異。）〉
entries.en: Further questions on home, kin, and children revealed his father; they embraced and wept; all who heard were astonished.)〉
entries.literal: Questioning further his native place, kin, and offspring, he then knew it was his father; they thereupon embraced and wept; hearers were all startled.)〉

entries.zh: 長興末，加同平章事。
entries.en: Late Changxing he became co-chief councilor.
entries.literal: At the end of Changxing he was given co-chief councilor.

entries.zh: 秦王為天下兵馬元帥，氣焰熏灼，大臣皆懼，求為外任。
entries.en: The Prince of Qin became commander of all armies; his arrogance blazed; ministers feared him and sought posts away from court.
entries.literal: The Prince of Qin was marshal of all armies under heaven; his arrogance blazed hot; the chief ministers all feared and sought posts away from court.

entries.zh: 義誠以明宗委遇，無以解退，乃令其子以弓馬事秦王以自結。
entries.en: Favored by Mingzong, Yicheng could not resign; he had his son serve the Prince of Qin in archery and horsemanship to win favor.
entries.literal: Yicheng, owing to Mingzong's favor, had no way to resign; he therefore had his son serve the Prince of Qin in archery and horsemanship to curry favor.

entries.zh: 明宗不豫，秦王諷義誠為助，義誠曲意承奉，亦非真誠。
entries.en: When Mingzong fell ill, the Prince of Qin urged Yicheng to aid him; Yicheng flattered him insincerely.
entries.literal: When Mingzong fell ill, the Prince of Qin urged Yicheng to help; Yicheng bent to flatter him, yet it was not sincere.

entries.zh: 及朱弘昭、馮贇等懼禍，謀於義誠，但云：「仆為將校，不敢預議，但相公所使耳。」
entries.en: When Zhu Hongzhao, Feng Yun, and the rest feared disaster and plotted with Yicheng, he only said, "I am a military officer; I dare not take part in counsel—I do only as the chief councilor orders."
entries.literal: When Zhu Hongzhao, Feng Yun, and the rest feared calamity and plotted with Yicheng, he only said, "I am a military officer; I dare not join deliberations—I do only as the chief councilor commands."

entries.zh: 及秦王既誅，明宗宴駕，閔帝即位，加檢校太尉、兼侍中，判六軍諸衛事。
entries.en: After the Prince of Qin was killed, Mingzong died, and Emperor Min took the throne; Yicheng was made acting Grand Commandant and Palace Attendant and put in charge of the Six Armies and all guards.
entries.literal: After the Prince of Qin was executed, Mingzong died, and Emperor Min ascended; Yicheng was given acting Grand Commandant and concurrent Palace Attendant, and directed the Six Armies and all guards.

entries.zh: 未幾，鳳翔變起，西軍不利，義誠懼，乃請行，蓋欲盡率駕下諸軍送降於潞王求免也。
entries.en: Soon the Fengxiang revolt broke out; the western army fared badly; Yicheng, afraid, asked to march—likely meaning to lead the emperor's troops in surrender to the Prince of Lu to save himself.
entries.literal: Before long the Fengxiang revolt rose; the western army fared poorly; Yicheng feared and asked to march—likely intending to lead all troops at the emperor's side in surrender to the Prince of Lu to save himself.

entries.zh: 會與朱洪實議事不葉，洪實因厲聲言義誠苞藏之志，閔帝曖昧，不能明辨，而誅洪實。
entries.en: He disputed strategy with Zhu Hongshi; Hongshi cried that Yicheng harbored treachery; Emperor Min, confused, could not judge and had Hongshi executed.
entries.literal: He happened to dispute strategy with Zhu Hongshi; Hongshi cried out that Yicheng harbored treacherous intent; Emperor Min, bewildered, could not judge clearly and executed Hongshi.

entries.zh: 及義誠率軍至新安，諸軍爭先趨陝，解甲迎降，義誠以部下數十人見潞王請罪，潞王雖罪其奸回，未欲行法。
entries.en: When Yicheng reached Xin'an, the troops raced to Shan, laid down arms, and surrendered; Yicheng came with several dozen men to beg pardon of the Prince of Lu; though the prince blamed his treachery, he did not yet punish him.
entries.literal: When Yicheng led the army to Xin'an, the troops raced ahead to Shan, laid down arms and welcomed surrender; Yicheng came with several dozen followers to beg pardon of the Prince of Lu; though the prince blamed his treachery, he did not yet wish to punish.

entries.zh: 清泰元年四月，斬於興教門外，夷其族。
entries.en: In the fourth month of Qingtai 1 he was beheaded outside the Xingjiao Gate and his clan was wiped out.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of Qingtai year 1 he was beheaded outside the Xingjiao Gate and his clan was exterminated.

entries.zh: 安重誨，其先本北部豪長。
entries.en: An Chonghui came from a line of great chiefs among the northern tribes.
entries.literal: An Chonghui—his ancestors were originally great chiefs of the northern tribes.

entries.zh: 父福遷，為河東將，救兗、鄆而沒。
entries.en: His father Fuqian was a Hedong general who perished in the relief of Yan and Yun.
entries.literal: His father Fuqian served as a Hedong general and died while rescuing Yan and Yun.

entries.zh: 重誨自明宗龍潛時得給事左右。
entries.en: Chonghui had served at Mingzong's side since before he took the throne.
entries.literal: Chonghui came to attend at the ruler's side from the time when Mingzong was still heir-apparent.

entries.zh: 及鎮邢州，以重誨為中門使。
entries.en: When Mingzong held Xingzhou, he appointed Chonghui Central Gate commissioner.
entries.literal: When he took charge of Xingzhou, Chonghui was made Central Gate commissioner.

entries.zh: 隨從征討，凡十餘年，委信無間，勤勞亦至。
entries.en: For more than ten years he followed Mingzong on campaign; trust never wavered, and his exertions were beyond measure.
entries.literal: Following him on campaigns for more than ten years, trust was never interrupted, and his labor reached the utmost.

entries.zh: 洎鄴城之變，佐命之功，獨居其右。
entries.en: At the Ye city crisis, his service in securing the throne stood above all others.
entries.literal: When the Ye city affair came, his merit in assisting the mandate stood alone at the foremost.

entries.zh: 明宗踐祚，領樞密使，俄遷左領軍衛大將軍充職。
entries.en: When Mingzong took the throne, Chonghui headed the Privy Council and soon also held the post of senior general of the Left Army Guard.
entries.literal: When Mingzong ascended the throne, he headed the Privy Council; soon he was transferred to Left Army Guard senior general while retaining the post.

entries.zh: 〈（案：以下有闕文。）〉
entries.en: (The text below is lost.)〉
entries.literal: (Note: Below there is missing text.)〉

entries.zh: 明宗遣回鶻侯三馳傳至其國，侯三至醴泉縣，地素僻，無驛馬，縣令劉知章出獵，不時給馬，侯三遽以聞。
entries.en: Mingzong sent the Uighur envoy Hou San post-haste to his homeland. At remote Liquan County there were no relay mounts; the magistrate Liu Zhizhang was out hunting and failed to provide horses promptly, and Hou San reported the delay at once.
entries.literal: Mingzong sent the Uighur envoy Hou San on express relay to his country; when Hou reached Liquan County, the place was by nature remote and had no relay horses; magistrate Liu Zhizhang had gone hunting and did not supply horses in time; Hou San immediately reported it.

entries.zh: 明宗大怒，械知章至京師，將殺之；
entries.en: Mingzong flew into a rage, had Zhizhang shackled and sent to the capital, and meant to put him to death;
entries.literal: Mingzong was greatly angered, had Zhizhang shackled and brought to the capital, and was about to execute him;

entries.zh: 重誨從容為言，乃得不死。
entries.en: Chonghui pleaded for him calmly, and Zhizhang was spared.
entries.literal: Chonghui spoke calmly on his behalf, and he thus escaped death.

entries.zh: 明宗幸汴州，重誨建議欲因以伐吳，而明宗難之。
entries.en: On a visit to Bianzhou, Chonghui urged using the occasion to strike Wu, but Mingzong hesitated.
entries.literal: When Mingzong visited Bianzhou, Chonghui proposed taking the opportunity to attack Wu, but Mingzong found it difficult.

entries.zh: 其後，戶部尚書李鏻吳諜者言：「徐知誥欲奉吳國以稱藩，願得安公一言以為信。」
entries.en: Later Minister of Revenue Li Lin relayed a Wu spy's message: "Xu Zhigao wishes to submit Wu as a tributary state and asks for Lord An's word as assurance."
entries.literal: Later, Minister of Revenue Li Lin, through a Wu spy, said: "Xu Zhigao wishes to offer Wu as a vassal state and seeks one word from Lord An as pledge."

entries.zh: 鏻即引諜者見重誨。
entries.en: Li Lin at once brought the spy before Chonghui.
entries.literal: Lin immediately led the spy to see Chonghui.

entries.zh: 重誨大喜，以為然，乃以玉帶與諜者，使遺知誥為信，其直千緡。
entries.en: Chonghui was delighted, took it for truth, and gave the spy a jade belt to carry to Zhigao as token—worth a thousand strings of cash.
entries.literal: Chonghui was greatly pleased, believed it true, and gave the spy a jade belt to send to Zhigao as pledge; it was worth a thousand strings of cash.

entries.zh: 任圜，京兆三原人。
entries.en: Ren Huan was a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.
entries.literal: Ren Huan, a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 祖清，成都少尹。
entries.en: His grandfather Qing served as vice governor of Chengdu.
entries.literal: His grandfather Qing was vice governor of Chengdu.

entries.zh: 父茂宏，避地太原，奏授西河令；
entries.en: His father Maohong fled the turmoil to Taiyuan, where he was appointed by memorial as magistrate of Xihe.
entries.literal: His father Maohong, fleeing disorder, reached Taiyuan and was appointed by memorial as magistrate of Xihe;

entries.zh: 有子五人，曰圖、回、圜、團、冏，風彩俱異。
entries.en: He had five sons — Tu, Hui, Huan, Tuan, and Jiong — each with a striking bearing.
entries.literal: He had five sons, named Tu, Hui, Huan, Tuan, and Jiong — each with striking presence.

entries.zh: 武皇愛之，以宗女妻團，歷代、憲二郡刺史。
entries.en: Emperor Wu favored the family and married an imperial clanswoman to Tuan, who served successively as prefect of Dai and Xian.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu favored them; he married an imperial clanswoman to Tuan, who served successively as prefect of Dai and Xian.

entries.zh: 豆盧革，祖籍，同州刺史。
entries.en: Dou Luge's grandfather Ji served as prefect of Tongzhou.
entries.literal: Dou Luge; ancestral register; Tongzhou prefect.

entries.zh: 父瓚，舒州刺史。
entries.en: His father Zan was prefect of Shuzhou.
entries.literal: His father Zan was prefect of Shu.

entries.zh: 〈（《宣和書譜》云：失其世係。）〉
entries.en: (The Xuanhe Calligraphy Catalogue notes that his pedigree is lost.)〉
entries.literal: (The Xuanhe Calligraphy Catalogue states: his genealogical line is lost.)〉

entries.zh: 革少值亂離，避地鄜、延，轉入中山，王處直禮之，辟於幕下，有奏記之譽。
entries.en: In his youth Ge lived through war and exile, taking refuge in Fu and Yan before moving on to Zhongshan. Wang Chuzhi honored him and brought him onto his staff, where he gained a reputation for polished memorials and dispatches.
entries.literal: Ge in youth encountered turmoil and dispersal, fled to Fu and Yan, then moved into Zhongshan; Wang Chuzhi treated him with courtesy and recruited him to his staff, where he won renown for memorials and letters.

entries.zh: 因牡丹會賦詩，諷處直以桑柘為意，言甚古雅，漸加器仰，轉節度判官。
entries.en: At a peony festival he wrote a poem that, through mulberry and ramie, gently admonished Chuzhi. The verse was so refined and archaic in tone that Chuzhi came to esteem him ever more highly and promoted him to adjutant of the military commission.
entries.literal: At a peony gathering he composed a poem, admonishing Chuzhi with mulberry and ramie as his theme; his language was very antique and elegant, and Chuzhi came increasingly to esteem him, promoting him to military commissioner adjutant.

entries.zh: 而理家無法，獨請謁處直，處直慮布政有缺，有所規諫，斂版出迎，乃為嬖人祈軍職矣。
entries.en: Yet he ran his household without discipline. When he alone sought an audience with Chuzhi, the lord, worried that his own governance might be at fault, came to remonstrate with him. Ge put away his tablet and came out to receive him — only to ask a military appointment for a favorite.
entries.literal: Yet in managing his household he had no discipline; he alone requested audience with Chuzhi. Chuzhi, fearing a gap in his governance, went to remonstrate; Ge folded his tablet and came out to meet him — only to beg a military post for a favorite.

entries.zh: 薛廷珪，其先河東人也。
entries.en: Xue Tinggui came of a Hedong family.
entries.literal: Xue Tinggui — his ancestors were people of Hedong.

entries.zh: 父逢，咸通中為秘書監，以才名著於時。
entries.en: His father Feng served as Director of the Palace Library under Emperor Yizong and was widely celebrated for his gifts as a writer.
entries.literal: His father Feng, during the Xiantong reign period served as Director of the Palace Library, and was renowned in his time for literary talent.

entries.zh: 廷珪，中和年在西川登進士第，累曆台省。
entries.en: Tinggui earned his jinshi degree in Sichuan during the Zhonghe era and rose through a series of central-government posts.
entries.literal: Tinggui, in the Zhonghe years passed the jinshi examination in Xichuan, and successively held posts in the central secretariats.

entries.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》：大順初，累遷司勳員外郎、知制誥。）〉
entries.en: (According to the Old Book of Tang, in early Dashun he was promoted in succession to Vice Director in the Bureau of Merit and commissioner for drafting imperial edicts.)〉
entries.literal: (Old Book of Tang: At the beginning of the Dashun reign he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Bureau of Merit and to Drafting Commissioner.)〉

entries.zh: 乾寧中，為中書舍人。
entries.en: During the Qianning era he served as a drafting secretary in the Secretariat.
entries.literal: During Qianning, he was a Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 駕在華州，改散騎常侍，尋請致仕，客遊蜀川。
entries.en: While the court was at Huazhou he was made Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, then soon asked to retire and lived for a time as a guest in Sichuan.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage was at Huazhou, he was reassigned as Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; soon he requested retirement from office and traveled as a guest in Shu.

entries.zh: 昭宗遷洛陽，征為禮部侍郎。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhaozong relocated to Luoyang, Tinggui was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, he was summoned as Vice Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》：光化中，復為中書舍人，遷邢部、吏部二侍郎，權知禮部貢舉，拜尚書左丞。）〉
entries.en: (The Old Book of Tang adds that in the Guanghua era he again became a Secretariat drafting secretary, rose to vice minister of punishments and of personnel, temporarily supervised the civil-service examinations for the Ministry of Rites, and was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.)〉
entries.literal: (Old Book of Tang: In Guanghua he again became Secretariat Drafting Secretary, was promoted to Vice Ministers of Punishments and of Personnel, acted as provisional overseer of the Ministry of Rites examination, and was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.)〉

entries.zh: 時柳璨屠害朝士，衣冠畢罹其毒，廷珪以居常退讓獲全。
entries.en: When Liu Can was butchering court officials, the entire official class fell victim to him; Tinggui alone escaped harm through his habitual modesty and restraint.
entries.literal: At that time Liu Can slaughtered court officials; the gentry all suffered his poison, but Tinggui was spared because of his usual modesty and yielding conduct.

entries.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：朱全忠兼四鎮，廷珪以官告使至汴，客將先見，諷其拜。
entries.en: (The New Book of Tang records that when Zhu Quanzhong held four military circuits at once, Tinggui came to Bian as the bearer of his commission of office. A host officer received him first and suggested obliquely that he should bow.
entries.literal: (New Book of Tang: Zhu Quanzhong held four circuits concurrently; Tinggui arrived at Bian as commissioner bearing the patent of office, and a guest officer who met him first hinted that he should bow.

entries.zh: 廷珪佯不曉，曰：「吾何德，敢受令公拜乎！」
entries.en: Tinggui feigned not to understand and said, "What merit have I that I should accept a bow from Your Lordship!"
entries.literal: Tinggui pretended not to understand, saying: "What virtue do I have, that I dare receive the Lord Commander's bow!"

entries.zh: 及見，卒不肯加禮。）〉
entries.en: When they met face to face, he still refused to offer the courtesy.)〉
entries.literal: When they met, he in the end refused to add the courtesy.)〉

entries.zh: 入梁為禮部尚書。
entries.en: Under the Liang he became Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: Entering Liang service, he became Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 莊宗平定河南，以廷珪年老，除太子少師致仕。
entries.en: After Zhuangzong pacified Henan, Tinggui was granted retirement as Mentor of the Heir Apparent on account of his advanced age.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Henan, because Tinggui was old he was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent with junior third rank and retired.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：廷珪與李琪嘗為太祖冊禮使。）〉
entries.en: (The Zizhi Tongjian notes that Tinggui and Li Qi had once served together as ritual commissioners for Taizu's investiture.)〉
entries.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: Tinggui and Li Qi once served as enfeoffment ritual commissioners for Taizu.)〉

entries.zh: 同光三年九月卒。
entries.en: He died in the ninth month of Tongguang 3 (925).
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Tongguang he died.

entries.zh: 贈右僕射。
entries.en: He was posthumously ennobled as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: He was posthumously awarded Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 所著《鳳閣詞書》十卷、《克家志》五卷，並行於世。
entries.en: His works Phoenix Pavilion Literary Writings, in ten fascicles, and Record of Honoring the Family, in five fascicles, both circulated widely.
entries.literal: His works Phoenix Pavilion Literary Writings in ten fascicles and Record of Honoring the Family in five fascicles both circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 初，廷珪父逢，著《鑿混沌》、《真珠簾》等賦，大為時人所稱。
entries.en: Tinggui's father Feng had earlier written celebrated rhapsodies such as Boring Through Chaos and Pearl Curtain that won wide praise in their day.
entries.literal: Earlier, Tinggui's father Feng had composed rhapsodies such as Boring Through Chaos and Pearl Curtain, which were greatly praised by people of the time.

entries.zh: 廷珪既壯，亦著賦數十篇，同為一集，故目曰《克家志》。
entries.en: When Tinggui came of age he too wrote several dozen rhapsodies and collected them in one volume, which he titled Record of Honoring the Family.
entries.literal: When Tinggui reached maturity, he also composed several dozen rhapsodies, gathered into one collection, hence its title Record of Honoring the Family.

entries.zh: 崔沂，
entries.en: Cui Yi,
entries.literal: Cui Yi,

entries.zh: 〈（《新唐書·宰相世係表》：沂，字德潤。）〉
entries.en: (The New Book of Tang's tables of chief ministers give his style name as Derun.)〉
entries.literal: (New Book of Tang, Genealogical Tables of Chief Ministers: Yi, style name Derun.)〉

entries.zh: 大中時宰相魏公鉉之幼子也。
entries.en: He was the youngest son of Cui Xuan, Duke of Wei, who had served as chief councilor in the Dazhong era.
entries.literal: He was the youngest son of Grand Councilor Duke of Wei Gongxuan of the Dazhong era.

entries.zh: 兄沆，廣明初亦為宰輔。
entries.en: His elder brother Hong likewise reached the chief ministership early in the Guangming era.
entries.literal: His elder brother Hong, at the beginning of Guangming also became a chief minister.

entries.zh: 沂舉進士第，曆監察、補闕。
entries.en: Yi passed the jinshi examination and served in succession as investigating censor and remonstrance official.
entries.literal: Yi passed the jinshi examination and successively served as Investigating Censor and Reminder.

entries.zh: 昭宗時，累遷至員外郎、知制誥。
entries.en: Under Emperor Zhaozong he rose in stages to outer-court director and drafting commissioner.
entries.literal: During Zhaozong's reign he was repeatedly promoted to Outer Court Director and Drafting Commissioner.

entries.zh: 性抗厲守道，而文藻非優，嘗與同舍顏蕘、錢珝俱秉筆，見蕘、珝贍速，草制數十，無妨譚笑，而沂自愧。
entries.en: Firm and principled by nature, he was not a gifted stylist. Once, drafting edicts alongside colleagues Yan Rao and Qian Pei, he watched them turn out dozens of documents with ease, chatting and laughing all the while, and was mortified by his own slowness.
entries.literal: By nature he was stern and upheld the Way, but his literary polish was not superior; once he drafted together with colleagues Yan Rao and Qian Pei, and seeing Rao and Pei swift and ample, drafting several dozen edicts without hindering banter, Yi felt ashamed of himself.

entries.zh: 翌日，謁國相訴曰：「沂疏淺，不足以供詞翰之職。」
entries.en: The next day he called on the chief minister and said, "I am too shallow a writer to hold a drafting post."
entries.literal: The next day he called on the chief minister and pleaded: "Yi is shallow and insufficient to fulfill the duties of literary drafting."

entries.zh: 相輔然之，移為諫議大夫。
entries.en: The minister concurred and moved him to the post of Grand Master of Remonstrance.
entries.literal: The minister agreed and transferred him to Grand Censor.

entries.zh: 入梁，為御史司憲，糾繆繩違，不避豪右。
entries.en: Under the Liang he headed the Censorate, correcting abuses and enforcing the law without fear of the powerful.
entries.literal: Entering Liang service, he became Director of the Censorate, correcting errors and restraining violations, not avoiding powerful families.

entries.zh: 開平中，金吾街使寇彥卿入朝，過天津橋，市民梁現者不時回避，前導伍伯捽之，投石欄以致斃。
entries.en: During Kaiping, Jinwu street commissioner Kou Yanqing came to court and crossed Tianjin Bridge. A townsman named Liang Xian failed to clear the way in time; Kou's escort guards seized him and hurled him against a stone railing, killing him.
entries.literal: During Kaiping, Jinwu Street Commissioner Kou Yanqing entered court audience, passed Tianjin Bridge, and a townsman named Liang Xian failed to withdraw in time; the forward escort guards seized him and threw him against a stone railing, causing death.

entries.zh: 彥卿自前白於梁祖，梁祖命通事舍人趙可封宣諭，令出私財與死者之家，以贖其罪。
entries.en: Yanqing reported the matter himself to the Liang founder, who ordered palace usher Zhao Kefeng to announce that Yanqing should pay compensation from his private funds to the victim's family in lieu of punishment.
entries.literal: Yanqing himself went forward to report to the Liang founder; the founder ordered Palace Usher Zhao Kefeng to announce the instruction, directing him to pay private funds to the dead man's family to redeem his offense.

entries.zh: 沂奏劾曰：「彥卿位是人臣，無專殺之理。
entries.en: Yi submitted an impeachment memorial: "Yanqing is a subject of the throne and has no right to kill on his own authority.
entries.literal: Yi memorialized in impeachment: "Yanqing's position is that of a subject; there is no principle of unauthorized killing.

entries.zh: 況天津橋御路之要，正對端門，當車駕出入之途，非街使震怒之所。
entries.en: Moreover Tianjin Bridge lies on the main imperial thoroughfare, directly before the Gate of Propriety, on the very path the imperial carriage takes; it is no place for a street commissioner to vent his anger.
entries.literal: Moreover Tianjin Bridge is a vital point on the imperial roadway, directly facing the Gate of Propriety, on the route of the imperial carriage's coming and going — not a place for a street commissioner to vent rage.

entries.zh: 況梁現不時回避，其過止於鞭笞。
entries.en: As for Liang Xian's failure to clear the way in time, the offense warranted no more than a beating.
entries.literal: Moreover Liang Xian's failure to withdraw in time — his offense goes no further than flogging.

entries.zh: 捽首投驅，深乖朝憲，請論之以法。」
entries.en: To seize a man and dash him to death so flagrantly violates the statutes; I ask that he be prosecuted according to law."
entries.literal: Seizing him by the head and casting him to death deeply violates court statutes; I request that he be judged by law."

entries.zh: 梁祖惜彥卿，令沂以過失論，沂引鬥競律，以怙勢力為罪首，下手者減一等。
entries.en: The Liang founder was reluctant to punish Yanqing and told Yi to treat the case as negligence. Yi cited the statute on brawling, naming abuse of power as the principal offense and reducing the penalty by one degree for those who carried out the act.
entries.literal: The Liang founder valued Yanqing and ordered Yi to judge it as a case of negligence; Yi cited the statute on brawling, making reliance on power the chief offense and reducing one degree for those who carried it out.

entries.zh: 又鬥毆條，不鬥故毆傷人者，加傷罪一等。
entries.en: He also invoked the article on assault: anyone who, without a prior fight, deliberately beats and injures another has the injury charge increased by one degree.
entries.literal: He also cited the article on fighting: one who without fighting deliberately beats and injures a person has the injury offense increased by one degree.

entries.zh: 沂表入，責授彥卿遊擊將軍、左衛中郎將。
entries.en: When Yi's memorial was received, Yanqing was demoted to general of the patrol and middle general of the Left Guard.
entries.literal: When Yi's memorial entered, Yanqing was demoted and appointed General of the Patrol and Middle General of the Left Guard.

entries.zh: 沂剛正守法，人士多之。
entries.en: Yi's stern integrity in upholding the law won him wide admiration among the official class.
entries.literal: Yi was upright and upheld the law; scholars and officials greatly admired him.

entries.zh: 遷左司侍郎，改太常卿，轉禮部尚書。
entries.en: He was promoted to vice director of the left secretariat, then made director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and later minister of rites.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Left Secretariat, changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and transferred to Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 貞明中，帶本官充西京副留守。
entries.en: During Zhenming he served as deputy protector-general of the Western Capital while retaining his ministerial title.
entries.literal: During Zhenming, while retaining his original office he served as Deputy Protector-General of the Western Capital.

entries.zh: 時張全義留守、天下兵馬副元帥、河南尹、判六軍諸衛事、守太尉、中書令、魏王，名位之重，冠絕中外。
entries.en: Zhang Quanyi then held the posts of protector-general, deputy commander-in-chief of all forces, prefect of Henan, controller of the six armies and all guards, acting grand preceptor, grand secretariat director, and Prince of Wei — titles whose weight surpassed every other figure at court or in the provinces.
entries.literal: At the time Zhang Quanyi was Protector-General, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven, Prefect of Henan, Controller of the Six Armies and All Guards, Acting Grand Preceptor, Grand Secretariat Director, and Prince of Wei — the weight of his titles and position surpassed all within and without the court.

entries.zh: 沂至府，客將白以副留守合行廷禮，沂曰：「張公官位至重，然尚帶府尹之名，不知副留守見尹之儀何如？」
entries.en: When Yi arrived at headquarters, a staff officer told him that as deputy protector he was expected to perform court ceremony. Yi replied, "Lord Zhang's rank is immense, yet he still holds the title of prefect — I am not sure what protocol a deputy protector should follow in meeting a prefect?"
entries.literal: When Yi arrived at the headquarters, a guest officer reported that as deputy protector he ought to perform court ritual; Yi said: "Lord Zhang's office and rank are extremely weighty, yet he still bears the title of prefect — I do not know what ceremony the deputy protector should use in meeting the prefect."

entries.zh: 全義知之，遽引見沂，勞曰：「彼此有禮，俱老矣，勿相勞煩。」
entries.en: Quanyi heard of this, summoned Yi at once, and said kindly, "Let us observe courtesy between equals — we are both old men; spare each other the formalities."
entries.literal: Quanyi learned of this, hurriedly received Yi in audience, and comforted him: "Between us there is mutual courtesy; we are both old — do not trouble each other with formalities."

entries.zh: 莊宗興復唐室，復用為左丞，判吏部尚書銓選司，坐累謫石州司馬。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong restored the Tang, Yi was again appointed left vice director and placed in charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection bureau; he was later demoted to defender of Shizhou on accumulated charges.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong restored the Tang house, Yi was again employed as Left Vice Director, concurrently overseeing the Ministry of Personnel selection bureau; through accumulated offenses he was demoted to Defender of Shizhou.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，召還，復為左丞。
entries.en: When Mingzong came to the throne, Yi was recalled and restored as left vice director.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he was recalled and again made Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 以衰疾告老，授太子少保致仕。
entries.en: Citing age and illness, he petitioned to retire and was granted the post of junior mentor of the heir apparent with retirement honors.
entries.literal: Because of age and illness he requested retirement and was granted Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent with retirement.

entries.zh: 卒於龍門之別墅，時年七十餘。
entries.en: He died at his villa in Longmen at over seventy years of age.
entries.literal: He died at a villa in Longmen, aged over seventy.

entries.zh: 贈太子少傅。
entries.en: He was posthumously ennobled as junior tutor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: He was posthumously awarded Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 歸藹，字文彥，吳郡人也。
entries.en: Gui Ai, whose style was Wenyan, was a native of Wu Commandery.
entries.literal: Gui Ai, style name Wenyan, was a native of Wu Commandery.

entries.zh: 曾祖登，祖融，父仁澤，位皆至列曹尚書、觀察使。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Deng, grandfather Rong, and father Renze all rose to ranking secretariat posts and military commissioner.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Deng, grandfather Rong, and father Renze all rose to the posts of ranking secretary in the boards and military commissioner.

entries.zh: 藹登進士第，及升朝，遍曆三署。
entries.en: Ai passed the jinshi examination and, once he entered court service, served in turn in all three secretariat offices.
entries.literal: Ai passed the jinshi examination; when he entered court service he served in turn in all three secretariat offices.

entries.zh: （案：以下疑有闕文。
entries.en: (Below there is suspected missing text.
entries.literal: (Note: below there is suspected missing text.

entries.zh: 據《舊唐書·昭宗紀》：天祐元年七月，宴於文思殿。
entries.en: According to the Annals of Zhaozong in the Old Book of Tang, in the seventh month of Tianyou 1 (904) a banquet was held in Wensi Hall.
entries.literal: According to the Annals of Zhaozong in the Old Book of Tang: In the seventh month of the first year of Tianyou, a banquet was held in the Wensi Hall.

entries.zh: 朱全忠入，百官或坐於廊下，全忠怒，笞通引官何凝。
entries.en: When Zhu Quanzhong entered, some officials were seated in the corridor below. Quanzhong was enraged and had the usher He Ning flogged.
entries.literal: Zhu Quanzhong entered; some of the hundred officials were seated in the corridor below, and Quanzhong was angered and had the usher He Ning flogged.

entries.zh: 丙寅，製金紫光祿大夫、行御史中丞、上柱國韓儀責授棣州司馬，侍御史歸藹責授登州司戶，坐百官傲全忠也。）
entries.en: On bingyin an edict demoted Han Yi, grand master of the golden glow and purple ornament, acting censor, and supreme pillar of state, to defender of Dizhou, and remonstrating censor Gui Ai to registrar of Dengzhou, for the offense of officials' arrogance toward Quanzhong.)
entries.literal: On bingyin, an edict demoted Grand Master of the Golden Glow and Purple Ornament, Acting Censor, and Supreme Pillar of State Han Yi to defender of Dizhou, and Remonstrating Censor Gui Ai to registrar of Dengzhou—for the offense of the hundred officials' arrogance toward Quanzhong.)

entries.zh: 同光初，為尚書右丞，遷刑、戶二部侍郎，以太子賓客致仕，卒年七十六。
entries.en: Early in Tongguang he served as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to vice minister of punishments and households, retired as honorary attendant to the crown prince, and died at seventy-six.
entries.literal: Early in Tongguang he served as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to vice minister of punishments and households, retired as Honorary Attendant to the Crown Prince, and died at seventy-six.

entries.zh: 劉岳，字昭輔。
entries.en: Liu Yue, whose style was Zhaofu.
entries.literal: Liu Yue, style name Zhaofu.

entries.zh: 其先遼東襄平人，元魏平定遼東，徙家於代，隨孝文遷洛，遂為洛陽人。
entries.en: His forebears came from Xiangping in Liaodong. When the Northern Wei pacified the northeast the family was moved to Dai; they followed Emperor Xiaowen to Luoyang and became Luoyang natives.
entries.literal: His ancestors were people of Xiangping in Liaodong; when Northern Wei pacified Liaodong the family moved to Dai, followed Emperor Xiaowen in the move to Luoyang, and thus became Luoyang people.

entries.zh: 八代祖民部尚書渝國公政會，武德時功臣。
entries.en: Eight generations back stood Zhenghui, minister of the household and Duke of Yu, a founding merit-holder of the Wude era.
entries.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Zhenghui, Minister of the Household and Duke of Yu of the Yu State, was a meritorious minister of the Wude era.

entries.zh: 祖符，蔡州刺史。
entries.en: His grandfather Fu had been prefect of Cai.
entries.literal: His grandfather Fu was Prefect of Cai.

entries.zh: 父珪，洪洞縣令。
entries.en: His father Gui served as magistrate of Hongtong County.
entries.literal: His father Gui was Magistrate of Hongtong County.

entries.zh: 符有子八人，皆登進士第。
entries.en: Fu had eight sons, every one of whom passed the jinshi examination.
entries.literal: Fu had eight sons, all of whom passed the jinshi examination.

entries.zh: 珪之母弟瑰、玕，異母弟崇夷、崇龜、崇望、崇魯、崇謨。
entries.en: The father Gui's full brothers were Kui and Gan; his half-brothers were Chongyi, Chonggui, Chongwang, Chonglu, and Chongmo.
entries.literal: Gui the father's younger brothers by the same mother were Kui and Gan; younger brothers by a different mother were Chongyi, Chonggui, Chongwang, Chonglu, and Chongmo.

entries.zh: 崇龜，乾寧中廣南節度使；
entries.en: Chonggui served as military commissioner of Guangnan during Qianning;
entries.literal: Chonggui, during Qianning was Military Commissioner of Guangnan;

entries.zh: 崇望，乾寧中宰相；
entries.en: Chongwang was chief minister in the same era;
entries.literal: Chongwang, during Qianning was chief minister;

entries.zh: 崇魯、崇謨、崇夷，並曆朝省。
entries.en: Chonglu, Chongmo, and Chongyi all held posts in the central ministries.
entries.literal: Chonglu, Chongmo, and Chongyi all successively served in the central ministries.

entries.zh: 嶽少孤，亦進士擢第，曆戶部巡官、鄭縣簿、直史館，轉左拾遺、侍御史。
entries.en: Orphaned young, Yue also earned his jinshi degree and served in succession as a touring official in the Ministry of Revenue, registrar of Zheng County, and direct historian in the History Office, then as left remonstrance official and attending censor.
entries.literal: Yue was orphaned young; he also passed the jinshi examination, successively served as touring official of the Ministry of Revenue, registrar of Zheng County, and direct historian of the History Office, and was transferred to Left Reminder and Attending Censor.

entries.zh: 梁貞明初，召入翰林為學士。
entries.en: Early in Liang Zhenming he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as an academician.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Liang Zhenming he was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as academician.

entries.zh: 嶽為文敏速，尤善談諧，在職累遷戶部侍郎，在翰林十二年。
entries.en: Yue wrote with quick facility and had a gift for witty conversation. He rose to vice minister of revenue and spent twelve years in the Hanlin.
entries.literal: Yue wrote with quick facility and was especially skilled at witty conversation; in office he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, and served in the Hanlin for twelve years.

entries.zh: 莊宗入汴，隨例貶均州司馬，尋丁母憂，許自貶所奔喪，服闋，授太子詹事。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong took Bian, Yue was demoted under the usual purge to defender of Junzhou. He soon entered mourning for his mother and was allowed to leave his post of exile for the funeral; when the mourning ended he was appointed grand mentor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, following precedent he was demoted to Defender of Junzhou; soon he entered mourning for his mother, was permitted to rush home for the funeral from his place of demotion, and after the mourning period was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，曆兵部吏部侍郎、秘書監、太常卿。
entries.en: Under Mingzong he served in succession as vice minister of war, vice minister of personnel, director of the Palace Library, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he successively served as Vice Minister of War, Vice Minister of Personnel, Director of the Palace Library, and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 卒年五十六。
entries.en: He died at fifty-six.
entries.literal: He died at age fifty-six.

entries.zh: 贈吏部尚書。
entries.en: He was posthumously ennobled as minister of personnel.
entries.literal: He was posthumously awarded Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 岳文學之外，通於典禮。
entries.en: Apart from his literary gifts, Yue was deeply versed in ritual protocol.
entries.literal: Beyond his literary learning, Yue was versed in ritual regulations.

entries.zh: 天成中，奉詔撰《新書儀》一部，文約而理當，今行於世。
entries.en: During Tiancheng he was ordered to compile the New Book of Ritual — concise in wording and sound in principle — which remains in use today.
entries.literal: During Tiancheng, by imperial order he compiled one work, New Book of Ritual, concise in text and correct in principle, which circulates in the world today.

entries.zh: 張文寶，昭宗朝諫議大夫顗之子也。
entries.en: Zhang Wenbao was the son of Grand Censor Yi, who had served under Emperor Zhaozong.
entries.literal: Zhang Wenbao was the son of Grand Censor Yi of Zhaozong's reign.

entries.zh: 文寶初，依河中朱友謙為從事。
entries.en: Early in his career Wenbao served on the staff of Zhu Youqian in Hezhong.
entries.literal: Early in Wenbao's career he relied on Zhu Youqian of Hezhong as staff member.

entries.zh: 莊宗即位於魏州，以文寶知制誥，曆中書舍人、刑部侍郎、左散騎常侍、知貢舉，遷吏部侍郎。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong took the throne at Weizhou, Wenbao was made drafting commissioner and rose through the posts of Secretariat drafting secretary, vice minister of punishments, left honorary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and examination supervisor before becoming vice minister of personnel.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne at Weizhou, Wenbao was made Drafting Commissioner, successively served as Secretariat Drafting Secretary, Vice Minister of Punishments, Left Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and overseer of examinations, and was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 文寶性雅淡稽古。
entries.en: Wenbao was refined, reserved, and devoted to classical learning.
entries.literal: Wenbao's nature was refined, restrained, and devoted to antiquity.

entries.zh: 長興初，奉使浙中，泛海船壞，水工以小舟救，文寶與副使吏部郎中張絢信風至淮南界，偽吳楊溥禮待甚至，兼厚遺錢幣、食物。
entries.en: Early in Changxing, on a mission to Zhe, his ship was wrecked at sea and sailors rescued him and his party in small boats. Wenbao and his deputy, Personnel Bureau director Zhang Xuan, drifted on the wind to the Huainan border, where Yang Pu of Wu received them with exceptional courtesy and lavished money and provisions on them.
entries.literal: Early in Changxing, on a mission to Zhe, his seagoing vessel was wrecked; sailors rescued them in small boats. Wenbao and the vice-envoy, Personnel Bureau Director Zhang Xuan, trusted the wind and reached the Huainan border; the false Wu ruler Yang Pu received them with extreme courtesy and also gave generous gifts of money and food.

entries.zh: 文寶受其食物，反其錢幣，吳人善之，送文寶等復至杭州宣國命，還青州，卒。
entries.en: Wenbao accepted the food but returned the money, which won the Wu people's admiration. They escorted him back to Hangzhou to deliver the imperial commission, then he returned to Qingzhou and died.
entries.literal: Wenbao accepted their food but returned their money; the Wu people approved, sent Wenbao and the others back to Hangzhou to announce the imperial command, returned to Qingzhou, and died.

entries.zh: 陳乂，薊門人也。
entries.en: Chen Yi was a native of Jimen.
entries.literal: Chen Yi was a man of Jimen.

entries.zh: 少好學，善屬文。
entries.en: From youth he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
entries.literal: In youth he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.

entries.zh: 因避亂，客於浮陽，轉徙於大梁。
entries.en: To escape the turmoil he lived as a guest in Fuyang and then moved to Daliang.
entries.literal: To escape the turmoil he stayed as a guest in Fuyang and then moved to Daliang.

entries.zh: 梁將張漢傑延於私邸，表授太子舍人。
entries.en: The Liang general Zhang Hanjie invited him to his private residence and memorialized his appointment as attendant of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: The Liang general Zhang Hanjie invited him to his private residence and memorialized his appointment as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 莊宗平梁，郭崇韜遙領常山，召居賓榻。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong pacified Liang, Guo Chongtao held distant charge of Changshan and summoned him to his guest couch.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Liang, Guo Chongtao held distant charge of Changshan and summoned him to his guest couch.

entries.zh: 崇韜從魏王繼岌伐蜀，署為招討判官。
entries.en: When Chongtao followed the Prince of Wei Jiji in the campaign against Shu, he appointed him pacification commissioner-assessor.
entries.literal: When Chongtao followed the Prince of Wei Jiji in the campaign against Shu, he appointed him pacification commissioner-assessor.

entries.zh: 崇韜死，明宗即位，隨任圜歸闕，圜薦之於朝，除膳部員外郎、知制誥，累遷中書舍人。
entries.en: After Chongtao died and Mingzong took the throne, he followed Ren Yuan back to court. Yuan recommended him, and he was appointed vice director of the Board of Provisions and drafting commissioner, then rose to Secretariat drafting secretary.
entries.literal: After Chongtao died and Mingzong took the throne, he followed Ren Yuan back to court; Yuan recommended him to the court, and he was appointed Vice Director of the Board of Provisions and Drafting Commissioner, then successively promoted to Secretariat Drafting Secretary.

entries.zh: 乂性陰僻，寡與人合，不為當路所與。
entries.en: Yi was secretive and withdrawn, seldom got along with others, and was not favored by those in power.
entries.literal: Yi's nature was dark and withdrawn; he seldom got along with others and was not favored by those in power.

entries.zh: 尋移左散騎常侍，由是忿以成疾，逾月而卒。
entries.en: Soon he was transferred to left honorary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary. Resentment turned to illness, and after more than a month he died.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; thereby resentment became illness, and after more than a month he died.

entries.zh: 乂微有才術，嘗自恃其能。
entries.en: Yi had modest talent and once relied heavily on his own ability.
entries.literal: Yi had modest talent and skill and once relied on his own ability.

entries.zh: 為判官日，人有造者，垂帷深處，罕見其面。
entries.en: While serving as an assessor, when visitors came he hung curtains deep within and rarely showed his face.
entries.literal: When he was an assessor, if someone came to visit him he would hang curtains deep within and rarely show his face.

entries.zh: 及居西掖，而姿態愈倨，位竟不至公卿，蓋器度促狹者也。
entries.en: Once he held office in the western secretariat his bearing grew all the more haughty. In the end his rank never reached the highest offices—likely because his capacity was narrow.
entries.literal: When he held office in the western secretariat his bearing became all the more haughty; in the end his rank never reached the highest offices—likely because his capacity was narrow and cramped.

entries.zh: 然乂性孤執，尤廉於財。
entries.en: Yet Yi was solitary and stubborn and especially scrupulous about money.
entries.literal: Yet Yi's nature was solitary and stubborn, and he was especially scrupulous about money.

entries.zh: 長興中，嘗自舍人銜命冊晉國公主石氏於太原，晉高祖善待之，但訝其高岸。
entries.en: During Changxing, as drafting secretary he carried orders to invest Princess Shi of Jin at Taiyuan. The Gaozu of Jin treated him well but was surprised at his lofty and stern bearing.
entries.literal: During Changxing, as drafting secretary he carried orders to invest Princess Shi of the Jin state at Taiyuan; the Gaozu of Jin treated him well but was surprised at his lofty and stern bearing.

entries.zh: 人或有獻可於乂，宜陳一謳頌以稱晉高祖之美，可邀其厚賄耳。
entries.en: Some advised Yi to present a eulogy praising the Gaozu of Jin and thereby win a generous reward.
entries.literal: Some advised Yi that he should present a eulogy praising the beauty of the Gaozu of Jin and thereby win a generous reward.

entries.zh: 乂曰：「人生貧富，咸有定分，未有持天子命違禮以求利，既損國綱，且虧士行，乂今生所不為也。」
entries.en: Yi said, "Whether life is poor or rich has its fixed allotment. No one who bears Heaven's Son's command should violate ritual to seek profit—this harms the state's norms and shames a scholar's conduct. That is something I will never do in this life."
entries.literal: Yi said: "Whether one's life is poor or rich has its fixed allotment; there has never been one who held Heaven's Son's command yet violated ritual to seek profit—this harms the state's norms and moreover shames the scholar's conduct; this is something Yi will never do in this life."

entries.zh: 聞者嘉之。
entries.en: Those who heard praised him.
entries.literal: Those who heard praised him.

entries.zh: 晉高祖即位，贈禮部尚書。
entries.en: When the Gaozu of Jin took the throne, Yi was posthumously awarded minister of rites.
entries.literal: When the Gaozu of Jin took the throne, he was posthumously awarded Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 劉讚，魏州人也。
entries.en: Liu Zan was a native of Weizhou.
entries.literal: Liu Zan was a native of Weizhou.

entries.zh: 幼有文性。
entries.en: He showed literary promise from childhood.
entries.literal: In youth he had literary aptitude.

entries.zh: 父比，為令錄，誨以詩書，夏月令服青襦單衫。
entries.en: His father Bi was a county recorder who taught him the classics and, in summer, made him wear only a plain blue jacket and single-layer shirt.
entries.literal: His father Bi served as county recorder; he instructed him with poetry and books, and in summer months ordered him to wear a blue jacket and single-layer shirt.

entries.zh: 比每肉食，別置蔬食以飯讚，謂之曰：「肉食，君之祿也。
entries.en: Whenever Bi ate meat he set vegetables before Zan and said, "Meat is an official's perquisite.
entries.literal: Whenever Bi ate meat, he set aside vegetable food to feed Zan, saying to him: "Meat is the ruler's salary.

entries.zh: 爾欲食肉，當苦心文藝，自可致之，吾祿不可分也。」
entries.en: If you want meat, earn it through your own literary merit. I cannot share my salary with you."
entries.literal: If you wish to eat meat, you must labor at literary arts — you can obtain it yourself; my salary cannot be shared."

entries.zh: 由是讚及冠有文辭，年三十餘登進士第。
entries.en: Zan grew into a polished writer and passed the jinshi examination in his thirties.
entries.literal: From this Zan by the capping age had literary compositions; in his thirties he passed the jinshi examination.

entries.zh: 魏州節度使羅紹威署巡官，罷歸京師，依開封尹劉鄩。
entries.en: Luo Shaowei, military commissioner of Weizhou, appointed him touring officer. When that post ended he went to the capital and attached himself to Kaifeng prefect Liu Yan.
entries.literal: Weizhou Military Commissioner Luo Shaowei appointed him touring officer; when dismissed he returned to the capital and relied on Kaifeng Prefect Liu Yan.

entries.zh: 久之，租庸使趙岩表為巡官，累遷至戶部員外郎，職如故。
entries.en: Eventually Grain-Tax Commissioner Zhao Yan recommended him as touring officer, and he rose to outer-court director in the Ministry of Revenue while keeping the same duties.
entries.literal: After a long time, Grain-Tax Commissioner Zhao Yan memorialized him as touring officer; he was repeatedly promoted to Outer Court Director of the Ministry of Revenue, his duties as before.

entries.zh: 莊宗入汴，租庸副使孔謙以讚里人，表為鹽鐵判官。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong took Bian, Deputy Grain-Tax Commissioner Kong Qian, a fellow townsman, recommended Zan as salt and iron commissioner.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Deputy Grain-Tax Commissioner Kong Qian, as Zan's fellow townsman, memorialized him as Salt and Iron Commissioner.

entries.zh: 天成中，曆知制誥、中書舍人。
entries.en: During Tiancheng he served in succession as drafting commissioner and Secretariat drafting secretary.
entries.literal: During Tiancheng he successively served as Drafting Commissioner and Secretariat Drafting Secretary.

entries.zh: 與學士竇夢徵同年登第，鄰居友善，夢徵卒，讚與同年楊凝式緦麻為位而哭，其家無嫡長，與視喪事，恤其孀稚，人士稱之。
entries.en: He had passed the jinshi in the same year as Hanlin academician Dou Mengzheng, and they were friendly neighbors. When Mengzheng died, Zan and his year-mate Yang Ningshi donned hemp mourning and wept at the bier. The family had no eldest son, so Zan helped manage the funeral and cared for the widow and children — conduct widely praised.
entries.literal: With academician Dou Mengzheng he had passed the examination in the same year and were friendly neighbors; when Mengzheng died, Zan with his year-mate Yang Ningshi wore hemp mourning and set up a mourning place to weep; the family had no eldest legitimate son — he assisted in overseeing the funeral, comforted the widow and young, and men of cultivation praised him.

entries.zh: 改御史中丞、刑部侍郎。
entries.en: He was made censor-in-chief and vice minister of punishments.
entries.literal: He was changed to Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Punishments.

entries.zh: 莊宗為行軍司馬，廣延髦俊，素知憲名，令朱守殷齎書幣延之。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong served as acting commander on campaign, he widely gathered eminent talents and, knowing Xian's reputation by name, had Zhu Shouyin bring letters and gifts to invite him.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong served as acting commander on campaign, he widely extended invitations to eminent talents, had long known Xian's name, and ordered Zhu Shouyin to bring letters and gifts to invite him.

entries.zh: 歲餘，釋褐交城令，秩滿，莊宗嗣世，補太原府司錄參軍。
entries.en: After more than a year he left the white collar as magistrate of Jiaocheng; when his term ended and Zhuangzong succeeded to the throne, he was appointed recorder in the Taiyuan prefectural office.
entries.literal: After more than a year he left the white collar as magistrate of Jiaocheng; when his term ended and Zhuangzong succeeded to the succession, he was appointed recorder in the Taiyuan prefectural office.

entries.zh: 時霸府初開，幕客馬鬱、王緘，燕中名士，盡與之遊。
