entries.en: At that time the chief's headquarters had just been opened; the staff members Ma Yu and Wang Jian, both celebrated names from Yan, all associated with him.
entries.literal: At that time the chief's headquarters had just been opened; the staff members Ma Yu and Wang Jian, both celebrated names from Yan, all associated with him.

entries.zh: 十二年，莊宗平河朔，念藩邸之舊，征赴行台。
entries.en: In the twelfth year Zhuangzong pacified Hebei and, mindful of old ties from the princely residence, summoned him to the field headquarters.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year Zhuangzong pacified Hebei and, mindful of old ties from the princely residence, summoned him to the field headquarters.

entries.zh: 十三年，授監察，賜緋，署魏博推官，自是恒簪筆扈從。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he was appointed surveillance censor, granted scarlet robes, and made investigating officer for Weibo; from then on he constantly wore the brush and followed in attendance.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed surveillance censor, granted scarlet robes, and made investigating officer for Weibo; from then on he constantly wore the brush and followed in attendance.

entries.zh: 十五年，王師戰胡柳，周德威軍不利，憲與同列奔馬北渡；
entries.en: In the fifteenth year the imperial army fought at Huliu; Zhou Dewei's army fared ill, and Xian fled north across the river with his colleagues on horseback;
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year the imperial army fought at Huliu; Zhou Dewei's army fared ill, and Xian fled north across the river with his colleagues on horseback;

entries.zh: 梁軍急追，殆將不濟。
entries.en: The Liang army pressed in pursuit and he was nearly unable to cross.
entries.literal: The Liang army pressed in pursuit and he was nearly unable to cross.

entries.zh: 至晚渡河，人皆陷水而沒，憲與從子朗履冰而行；
entries.en: Toward evening they crossed the river; many men sank in the water and drowned. Xian and his nephew Lang walked on the ice;
entries.literal: Toward evening they crossed the river; many men sank in the water and drowned. Xian and his nephew Lang walked on the ice;

entries.zh: 將及岸，冰陷，朗泣，以馬箠引之，憲曰：「吾兒去矣，勿使俱陷。」
entries.en: As they neared the bank the ice gave way. Lang wept; Xian pulled him with a riding crop and said, "My boy, go on—do not let us both fall in."
entries.literal: As they neared the bank the ice gave way. Lang wept; Xian pulled him with a riding crop and said, "My boy, go on—do not let us both fall in."

entries.zh: 朗曰：「忍季父如此，俱死無恨。」
entries.en: Lang said, "How could I bear to leave my uncle like this? Dying together leaves no regret."
entries.literal: Lang said, "How could I bear my uncle like this? Dying together leaves no regret."

entries.zh: 朗偃伏引箠，憲躍身而出。
entries.en: Lang lay prostrate and held out the crop; Xian leapt free.
entries.literal: Lang lay prostrate and held out the crop; Xian leapt free.

entries.zh: 是夜，莊宗令於軍中求憲，或曰：「與王緘俱歿矣！」
entries.en: That night Zhuangzong ordered a search for Xian in the army; someone said, "He perished together with Wang Jian!"
entries.literal: That night Zhuangzong ordered a search for Xian in the army; someone said, "He perished together with Wang Jian!"

entries.zh: 莊宗垂涕求屍，數日，聞其免也，遣使慰勞。
entries.en: Zhuangzong wept and sought his corpse; after several days word came that he had escaped, and he sent an envoy to comfort and reward him.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong wept and sought his corpse; after several days word came that he had escaped, and he sent an envoy to comfort and reward him.

entries.zh: 尋改掌書記、水部郎中，賜金紫，曆魏博觀察判官。
entries.en: Soon he was made chief secretary and director in the Ministry of Works, granted gold and purple, and served in succession as investigating officer for the Weibo surveillance commission.
entries.literal: Soon he was made chief secretary and director in the Ministry of Works, granted gold and purple, and served in succession as investigating officer for the Weibo surveillance commission.

entries.zh: 從討張文禮，鎮州平，授魏、博、鎮、冀十郡觀察判官，改考功郎中，兼御史中丞，權鎮州留事。
entries.en: He followed the campaign against Zhang Wenli; when Zhenzhou was pacified he was appointed investigating officer for the ten prefectures of Wei, Bo, Zhen, and Ji, then promoted to director in the Bureau of Merit, made concurrent vice censor-in-chief, and given charge of Zhenzhou as acting administrator.
entries.literal: He followed the campaign against Zhang Wenli; when Zhenzhou was pacified he was appointed investigating officer for the ten prefectures of Wei, Bo, Zhen, and Ji, then promoted to director in the Bureau of Merit, concurrently made vice censor-in-chief, and given charge of Zhenzhou as acting administrator.

entries.zh: 莊宗即位，詔還魏都，授尚書工部侍郎，充租庸使。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was ordered back to the Wei capital, appointed vice minister of works in the Secretariat, and made commissioner of the transport and corvée tax.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was ordered back to the Wei capital, appointed vice minister of works in the Secretariat, and made commissioner of the transport and corvée tax.

entries.zh: 八月，改刑部侍郎，判吏部銓，兼太清宮副使。
entries.en: In the eighth month he was transferred to vice minister of punishments, given charge of civil-service selection in the Ministry of Personnel, and made deputy commissioner of the Taiqing Palace.
entries.literal: In the eighth month he was transferred to vice minister of punishments, given charge of civil-service selection in the Ministry of Personnel, and made deputy commissioner of the Taiqing Palace.

entries.zh: 莊宗遷洛陽，以憲檢校吏部尚書、興唐尹、東京副留守，知留守事。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong moved to Luoyang, Xian was made acting minister of personnel, prefect of Xingtang, deputy eastern capital intendant, and given charge of the intendant's affairs.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong moved to Luoyang, Xian was made acting minister of personnel, prefect of Xingtang, deputy eastern capital intendant, and given charge of the intendant's affairs.

entries.zh: 憲學識優深，尤精吏道，剖析聽斷，人不敢欺。
entries.en: Xian's learning was superior and profound; he was especially skilled in administrative practice, dissecting cases in judgment and hearing, and no one dared deceive him.
entries.literal: Xian's learning was superior and profound; he was especially skilled in administrative practice, dissecting cases in judgment and hearing, and no one dared deceive him.

entries.zh: 胡裝，禮部尚書曾之孫。
entries.en: Hu Zhuang was the grandson of Zeng, minister of rites.
entries.literal: Hu Zhuang was the grandson of Zeng, minister of rites.

entries.zh: 汴將楊師厚之鎮魏州，裝與副使李嗣業有舊，因往依之，薦授貴鄉令。
entries.en: When the Bian general Yang Shihou was posted to Weizhou, Zhuang had old ties with the deputy commissioner Li Siye and went to rely on him; he was recommended and appointed magistrate of Guixiang.
entries.literal: When the Bian general Yang Shihou was posted to Weizhou, Zhuang had old ties with the deputy commissioner Li Siye and went to rely on him; he was recommended and appointed magistrate of Guixiang.

entries.zh: 及張彥之亂，嗣業遇害，裝罷秩，客於魏州。
entries.en: When Zhang Yan's rebellion broke out, Siye was killed; Zhuang lost his post and lived as a guest in Weizhou.
entries.literal: When Zhang Yan's rebellion broke out, Siye met with disaster; Zhuang lost his post and lived as a guest in Weizhou.

entries.zh: 莊宗初至，裝謁見，求假官，司空頲以其居官貪濁，不得調者久之。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong first arrived, Zhuang called on him and sought a provisional appointment; Sikong Ting, because Zhuang had been corrupt in office, long kept him from receiving a transfer.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong first arrived, Zhuang called on him and sought a provisional appointment; Sikong Ting, because Zhuang had been corrupt in office, long kept him from receiving a transfer.

entries.zh: 十三年，莊宗還太原，裝候於離亭；
entries.en: In the thirteenth year Zhuangzong returned to Taiyuan; Zhuang waited at the parting pavilion;
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year Zhuangzong returned to Taiyuan; Zhuang waited at the parting pavilion;

entries.zh: 謁者不內，乃排闥而入，曰：「臣本朝公卿子孫，從兵至此。
entries.en: the usher would not admit him, so he forced the door and entered, saying, "I am a descendant of this dynasty's dukes and ministers and have followed the army to this place.
entries.literal: the usher would not admit him, so he forced the door and entered, saying, "Your servant is a descendant of this dynasty's dukes and ministers and has followed the army to this place.

entries.zh: 殿下比襲唐祚，勤求英俊，以壯霸圖。
entries.en: Your Highness has lately assumed the Tang succession and diligently seeks outstanding men to strengthen your hegemonic design.
entries.literal: Your Highness has lately assumed the Tang succession and diligently seeks outstanding men to strengthen the hegemonic design.

entries.zh: 臣雖不才，比於進九九，納豎刁、頭須，亦所庶幾。
entries.en: Though I lack talent, I am scarcely inferior to those who advanced Jiu Jiu or welcomed Shu Diao and Tou Xu to court.
entries.literal: Though your servant lacks talent, compared with advancing Jiu Jiu or welcoming Shu Diao and Tou Xu, he is not far from their measure.

entries.zh: 而羈旅累年，執事者不垂顧錄，臣不能赴海觸樹，走胡適越，今日歸死於殿下也！」
entries.en: Yet for years in exile those in charge have not extended their regard. I cannot throw myself into the sea or dash against a tree, nor flee to Hu or Yue—today I return to die before Your Highness!"
entries.literal: Yet for years in exile those in charge have not extended regard or enrollment. Your servant cannot throw himself into the sea or dash against a tree, nor flee to Hu or Yue—today he returns to die before Your Highness!"

entries.zh: 莊宗愕然曰：「孤未之知，何至如是！」
entries.en: Zhuangzong said in astonishment, "I did not know of this—how could it come to such a pass!"
entries.literal: Zhuangzong said in astonishment, "I did not know of this—how could it come to such a pass!"

entries.zh: 賜酒食慰遣之，謂郭崇韜曰：「便與擬議。」
entries.en: He bestowed wine and food to comfort and dismiss him, and told Guo Chongtao, "Draw up a proposal at once."
entries.literal: He bestowed wine and food to comfort and dismiss him, and told Guo Chongtao, "Draw up a proposal at once."

entries.zh: 是歲，署館驛巡官。
entries.en: That year he was appointed touring officer of the post stations.
entries.literal: That year he was appointed touring officer of the post stations.

entries.zh: 未幾，授監察御史裏行，遷節度巡官，賜緋魚袋；
entries.en: Before long he was made acting surveillance censor, promoted to touring officer of the military commission, and granted scarlet robes and the fish bag;
entries.literal: Before long he was made acting surveillance censor, promoted to touring officer of the military commission, and granted scarlet robes and the fish bag;

entries.zh: 尋曆推官、檢校員外郎。
entries.en: soon he served in succession as investigating officer and acting director in a bureau.
entries.literal: soon he served in succession as investigating officer and acting director in a bureau.

entries.zh: 裝學書無師法，工詩非作者，僻於題壁，所至宮亭寺觀，必書爵裏，人或譏之，不以為愧。
entries.en: Zhuang studied calligraphy without proper training and wrote poetry without being a true poet; he was fond of inscribing walls, and wherever he went among palaces, pavilions, temples, and shrines he always wrote his rank and residence—people sometimes mocked him, but he felt no shame.
entries.literal: Zhuang studied calligraphy without proper method and wrote poetry without being a true author; he was fond of inscribing walls, and wherever he went among palaces, pavilions, temples, and shrines he always wrote his rank and residence—people sometimes mocked him, but he felt no shame.

entries.zh: 時四鎮幕賓皆金紫，裝獨恥銀艾。
entries.en: At that time staff guests of the four commands all wore gold and purple; Zhuang alone was ashamed of silver and green.
entries.literal: At that time staff guests of the four commands all wore gold and purple; Zhuang alone was ashamed of silver and green.

entries.zh: 十七年，莊宗自魏州之德勝，與賓僚城樓餞別，既而群僚離席，裝獨留，獻詩三篇，意在章服。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year Zhuangzong went from Weizhou to Desheng; on the city tower he gave a farewell feast for his guests and staff. When the group had left their seats Zhuang alone remained and presented three poems, his aim being official robes and insignia.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year Zhuangzong went from Weizhou to Desheng; on the city tower he gave a farewell feast for his guests and staff. When the group had left their seats Zhuang alone remained and presented three poems, his aim being official robes and insignia.

entries.zh: 莊宗舉大鍾屬裝曰：「員外能釂此乎？」
entries.en: Zhuangzong raised a great bell-cup and handed it to Zhuang, saying, "Director, can you drain this?"
entries.literal: Zhuangzong raised a great bell-cup and handed it to Zhuang, saying, "Director, can you drain this?"

entries.zh: 裝飲酒素少，略無難色，為之一舉而釂，莊宗即解紫袍賜之。
entries.en: Zhuang ordinarily drank little but showed hardly any difficulty and drained it in one draft; Zhuangzong at once removed his purple robe and bestowed it on him.
entries.literal: Zhuang ordinarily drank little but showed hardly any difficulty and drained it in one draft; Zhuangzong at once removed his purple robe and bestowed it on him.

entries.zh: 同光初，以裝為給事中，從幸洛陽。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tongguang he was made attendant in the Secretariat and followed the emperor to Luoyang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was made attendant in the Secretariat and followed the emperor to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 時連年大水，百官多窘，裝求為襄州副使。
entries.en: At that time floods came year after year and many officials were in straits; Zhuang sought to be deputy commissioner of Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: At that time floods came year after year and many officials were in straits; Zhuang sought to be deputy commissioner of Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 四年，洛陽變擾，節度使劉訓以私忿族裝，誣奏雲裝欲謀亂，人士冤之。
entries.en: In the fourth year Luoyang was thrown into turmoil; the military commissioner Liu Xun, from private resentment, exterminated Zhuang's clan and falsely memorialized that Zhuang intended rebellion; men of standing held it a grievous injustice.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Luoyang was thrown into turmoil; the military commissioner Liu Xun, from private resentment, exterminated Zhuang's clan and falsely memorialized that Zhuang intended rebellion; men of standing held it a grievous injustice.

entries.zh: 延朗有心計，善理繁劇。
entries.en: Yanlang was resourceful and skilled at managing complexity.
entries.literal: Yanlang had schemes in his mind and was skilled at managing complexity.

entries.zh: 晉高祖在太原，朝廷猜忌，不欲令有積聚，係官財貨留使之外，延朗悉遣取之，晉高祖深銜其事。
entries.en: When the Gaozu of Jin was at Taiyuan the court was suspicious and did not wish him to accumulate stores; apart from official goods left with the commissioner, Yanlang sent men to take them all, and the Gaozu of Jin deeply resented the matter.
entries.literal: When the Gaozu of Jin was at Taiyuan the court was suspicious and did not wish him to accumulate stores; apart from official goods left with the commissioner, Yanlang sent men to take them all, and the Gaozu of Jin deeply resented the matter.

entries.zh: 及晉陽起兵，末帝議親征，然亦采浮論，不能果決；
entries.en: When troops rose at Jinyang the Last Emperor deliberated on a personal campaign, yet he also adopted floating opinion and could not decide firmly;
entries.literal: When troops rose at Jinyang the Last Emperor deliberated on a personal campaign, yet he also adopted floating opinion and could not decide firmly;

entries.zh: 延朗獨排眾議，請末帝北行，識者韙之。
entries.en: Yanlang alone rejected the crowd's opinion and asked the Last Emperor to march north—men of insight approved him.
entries.literal: Yanlang alone rejected the crowd's opinion and asked the Last Emperor to march north—men of insight approved him.

entries.zh: 晉高祖入洛，送台獄以誅之。
entries.en: When the Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang he sent him to the metropolitan prison and executed him.
entries.literal: When the Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang he sent him to the metropolitan prison and executed him.

entries.zh: 其後以選求計使，難得其人，甚追悔焉。
entries.en: Afterward, in selecting and seeking a commissioner of accounts, it was hard to obtain the right man, and he deeply regretted it.
entries.literal: Afterward, in selecting and seeking a commissioner of accounts, it was hard to obtain the right man, and he deeply regretted it.

entries.zh: 劉延皓，應州渾元人。
entries.en: Liu Yanhao was a native of Hunyuan in Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Liu Yanhao was a man of Hunyuan in Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 祖建立，父茂成，皆以軍功推為邊將。
entries.en: His grandfather Jianli and his father Maocheng were both promoted to frontier generals for military merit.
entries.literal: His grandfather Jianli and his father Maocheng were both promoted to frontier generals for military merit.

entries.zh: 延皓即劉後之弟也。
entries.en: Yanhao was the younger brother of Empress Liu.
entries.literal: Yanhao was the younger brother of Empress Liu.

entries.zh: 末帝鎮鳳翔，署延皓元隨都校，奏加檢校戶部尚書。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor was posted at Fengxiang he appointed Yanhao commander of his original followers and memorialized to add acting minister of revenue.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor was posted at Fengxiang he appointed Yanhao commander of his original followers and memorialized to add acting minister of revenue.

entries.zh: 清泰元年，除宮苑使，加檢校司空。
entries.en: In the first year of Qingtai he was made palace park commissioner and promoted to acting minister of works.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qingtai he was made palace park commissioner and promoted to acting minister of works.

entries.zh: 俄改宣徽南院使、檢校司徒。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was changed to commissioner of the southern bureau of the Palace Domestic Service and acting Grand Mentor.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was changed to commissioner of the southern bureau of the Palace Domestic Service and acting Grand Mentor.

entries.zh: 二年，遷樞密使、太保，出為鄴都留守、檢校太傅。
entries.en: In the second year he was transferred to commissioner of military affairs and Grand Guardian, then sent out as intendant at Ye and acting Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: In the second year he was transferred to commissioner of military affairs and Grand Guardian, then sent out as intendant at Ye and acting Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 延皓禦軍失政，為屯將張令昭所逐，出奔相州，尋詔停所任。
entries.en: Yanhao governed the army badly; the garrison officer Zhang Lingzhao expelled him, he fled to Xiangzhou, and soon an edict stripped him of office.
entries.literal: Yanhao governed the army badly; the garrison officer Zhang Lingzhao expelled him, he fled to Xiangzhou, and soon an edict stripped him of office.

entries.zh: 及晉高祖入洛，延皓逃匿龍門廣化寺，數日，自經而死。
entries.en: When the Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang, Yanhao hid in Guanghua Temple at Longmen; after several days he hanged himself.
entries.literal: When the Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang, Yanhao hid in the Guanghua Temple at Longmen; after several days he hanged himself.

entries.zh: 延皓始以後戚自藩邸出入左右，甚以溫厚見稱，故末帝嗣位之後，委居近密。
entries.en: At first Yanhao, as a maternal relative from the princely household, came and went at the sovereign's side and was greatly praised for his mildness; therefore after the Last Emperor succeeded to the throne he was entrusted with intimate duties.
entries.literal: At first Yanhao, as a maternal relative from the princely household, came and went at the sovereign's side and was greatly praised for his mildness; therefore after the Last Emperor succeeded to the throne he was entrusted with intimate duties.

entries.zh: 及出鎮大名，而所執一變，掠人財賄，納人園宅，聚歌僮為長夜之飲，而三軍所給不時，內外怨之，因為令昭所逐。
entries.en: But when he went out to command at Daming his conduct changed entirely: he seized people's wealth as bribes, took their gardens and residences, gathered singing boys for all-night drinking, and paid the three armies' supplies irregularly; inside and outside complained of him, and thereby he was expelled by Lingzhao.
entries.literal: But when he went out to command at Daming his conduct changed entirely: he seized people's wealth as bribes, took their gardens and residences, gathered singing boys for all-night drinking, and paid the three armies' supplies irregularly; inside and outside complained of him, and thereby he was expelled by Lingzhao.

entries.zh: 時執政以延皓失守，請舉舊章，末帝以劉後內政之故，止從罷免而已，由是清泰之政弊矣。
entries.en: At the time the chief ministers, because Yanhao had lost his command, asked to apply the old regulations; the Last Emperor, because of Empress Liu's influence in the inner court, only went so far as dismissal—thereby the government of Qingtai was harmed.
entries.literal: At the time the chief ministers, because Yanhao had lost his command, asked to apply the old regulations; the Last Emperor, because of Empress Liu's influence in the inner court, only went so far as dismissal—thereby the government of Qingtai was harmed.

entries.zh: 劉延朗，宋州虞城人也。
entries.en: Liu Yanlang was a native of Yucheng in Songzhou.
entries.literal: Liu Yanlang was a man of Yucheng in Songzhou.

entries.zh: 末帝鎮河中時，為鄆城馬步都虞候，後納為腹心。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor was posted to Hezhong he was chief inspector of cavalry and infantry at Yancheng; later he was taken in as a trusted confidant.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor was posted to Hezhong he was chief inspector of cavalry and infantry at Yancheng; later he was taken in as a trusted confidant.

entries.zh: 及鎮鳳翔，署為孔目吏。
entries.en: When he was posted to Fengxiang he was appointed a clerical officer.
entries.literal: When he was posted to Fengxiang he was appointed a clerical officer.

entries.zh: 末帝將圖起義，為捍禦之備，延朗計公私粟帛，以贍其急。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor was planning to raise an uprising and made preparations for defense, Yanlang calculated public and private grain and cloth to supply the urgent need.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor was planning to raise an uprising and made preparations for defense, Yanlang calculated public and private grain and cloth to supply the urgent need.

entries.zh: 及西師納降，末帝赴洛，皆無所闕焉，末帝甚賞之。
entries.en: When the western army submitted and the Last Emperor went to Luoyang, nothing was lacking in any respect, and the Last Emperor greatly rewarded him.
entries.literal: When the western army submitted and the Last Emperor went to Luoyang, nothing was lacking in any respect, and the Last Emperor greatly rewarded him.

entries.zh: 清泰初，除宣徽北院使，俄以劉延皓守鄴，改副樞密使，累官至檢校太傅。
entries.en: At the beginning of Qingtai he was made commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Domestic Service; soon, because Liu Yanhao was intendant at Ye, he was changed to deputy commissioner of military affairs and rose in succession to acting Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was made commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Domestic Service; soon, because Liu Yanhao was intendant at Ye, he was changed to deputy commissioner of military affairs and rose in succession to acting Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 時房皓為樞密使，但高枕閑眠，啟奏除授，一歸延朗，由是得志。
entries.en: At that time Fang Hao was commissioner of military affairs but only rested his head high and slept at leisure; memorials for appointments and dismissals all went to Yanlang, and thereby he got his way.
entries.literal: At that time Fang Hao was commissioner of military affairs but only rested his head high and slept at leisure; memorials for appointments and dismissals all went to Yanlang, and thereby he got his way.

entries.zh: 凡藩侯郡牧，自外入者，必先賂延朗，後議進貢，賂厚者先居內地，賂薄者晚出邊藩，故諸將屢有怨訕，末帝不能察之。
entries.en: Whenever frontier lords and prefects came in from outside, they had first to bribe Yanlang and only afterward discuss advancing tribute; those who bribed heavily were first placed in inner territories, those who bribed lightly were sent out late to border commands—therefore the generals often had resentful complaints, which the Last Emperor could not perceive.
entries.literal: Whenever frontier lords and prefects came in from outside, they had first to bribe Yanlang and only afterward discuss advancing tribute; those who bribed heavily were first placed in inner territories, those who bribed lightly were sent out late to border commands—therefore the generals often had resentful complaints, which the Last Emperor could not perceive.

entries.zh: 及晉高祖入洛，延朗將竄於南山，與從者數輩，過其私第，指而歎曰：「我有錢三十萬貫聚於此，不知為何人所得。」
entries.en: When the Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang, Yanlang was about to flee into the southern mountains; with several followers he passed his private residence, pointed at it, and sighed, "I have three hundred thousand strings of cash gathered here—I do not know who will obtain it."
entries.literal: When the Gaozu of Jin entered Luoyang, Yanlang was about to flee into the southern mountains; with several followers he passed his private residence, pointed at it, and sighed, "I have three hundred thousand strings of cash gathered here—I do not know who will obtain it."

entries.zh: 其愚暗如此。
entries.en: His foolish darkness was such as this.
entries.literal: His foolish darkness was such as this.

entries.zh: 尋捕而殺之。
entries.en: Soon he was captured and killed.
entries.literal: Soon he was captured and killed.

entries.zh: 張憲，字允中，晉陽人，世以軍功為牙校。
entries.en: Zhang Xian, styled Yunzhong, was a native of Jinyang. For generations his family had risen through military service to the rank of yaxiao.
entries.literal: Zhang Xian, styled Yunzhong, was a man of Jinyang; for generations his family had held the rank of yaxiao through military achievement.

entries.zh: 憲始童丱，喜儒學，勵志橫經，不舍晝夜。
entries.en: From childhood Xian delighted in Confucian learning, applying himself to mastering the classics day and night without respite.
entries.literal: From his earliest childhood Xian delighted in Confucian learning, resolved to master the classics horizontally, and did not rest day or night.

entries.zh: 太原地雄邊服，人多尚武，恥於學業，惟憲與里人藥縱之精力遊學，弱冠盡通諸經，尤精《左傳》。
entries.en: Taiyuan lay in a powerful frontier region where men prized martial prowess and looked down on scholarly pursuits; only Xian and a townsman named Yao Zongzhi devoted their energies to travel and study. By his weak-capping year he had mastered all the classics, with particular mastery of the Zuo Commentary.
entries.literal: Taiyuan lay in a powerful frontier region; its people mostly honored martial affairs and were ashamed of scholarly study. Only Xian and a townsman, Yao Zongzhi, devoted their energies to travel and study. By weak-capping he had thoroughly mastered all the classics, especially the Zuo Commentary.

entries.zh: 嘗袖行所業，謁判官李襲吉，一見欣歎。
entries.en: Once he carried his writings in his sleeve and called on the judge Li Xiji, who at a single meeting expressed delighted admiration.
entries.literal: Once he carried his recent work in his sleeve and called on the judge Li Xiji, who at a single meeting expressed delighted admiration.

entries.zh: 既辭，謂憲曰：「子勉之，將來必成佳器。」
entries.en: When Xian took his leave, Li said to him, "Apply yourself diligently—you will surely become an outstanding talent in time."
entries.literal: When he took his leave, he said to Xian, "Apply yourself diligently—you will surely become an outstanding vessel in time."

entries.zh: 石州刺史楊守業喜聚書，以家書示之，聞見日博。
entries.en: The prefect of Shizhou, Yang Shouye, loved to collect books and showed him his family library, so his learning broadened day by day.
entries.literal: The prefect of Shizhou, Yang Shouye, loved to collect books and showed him his family library, so his knowledge and experience broadened day by day.

entries.zh: 夏魯奇，字邦傑，青州人也。
entries.en: Xia Luqi, courtesy name Bangjie, was a native of Qingzhou.
entries.literal: Xia Luqi, styled Bangjie, was a man of Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 初事宣武軍為軍校，與主將不協，遂歸於莊宗，以為護衛指揮使。
entries.en: He first served the Xuanwu army as a regimental officer. At odds with his commander, he defected to Zhuangzong, who appointed him commander of the imperial guard.
entries.literal: At first he served the Xuanwu army as a military officer; he did not get along with his commander and therefore went over to Zhuangzong, who made him commander of the guard.

entries.zh: 從周德威攻幽州，燕將有單廷珪、元行欽，時稱驍勇，魯奇與之鬥，兩不能解，將士皆釋兵縱觀。
entries.en: Under Zhou Dewei he attacked Youzhou. The Yan generals Shan Tinggui and Yuan Xingqin were then renowned for valor. Luqi fought them to a standstill, and soldiers on both sides set down their weapons to watch.
entries.literal: Following Zhou Dewei in the attack on Youzhou, the Yan generals Shan Tinggui and Yuan Xingqin were then famed for fierceness; Luqi fought them and neither could overcome the other; officers and men all laid down their weapons to watch.

entries.zh: 幽州平，魯奇功居多。
entries.en: When Youzhou fell, Luqi's contribution was the greatest of all.
entries.literal: When Youzhou was pacified, Luqi's merit was greatest.

entries.zh: 梁將劉鄩在洹水，莊宗深入致師，鄩設伏於魏縣西南葭蘆中。
entries.en: The Liang general Liu Yun held Huanshui. Zhuangzong pushed deep to bring him to battle, and Yun laid an ambush in the reed beds southwest of Wei County.
entries.literal: The Liang general Liu Yun was at Huanshui; Zhuangzong advanced deep to offer battle; Yun set an ambush in the reed marshes southwest of Wei County.

entries.zh: 莊宗不滿千騎，汴人伏兵萬餘，大噪而起，圍莊宗數重。
entries.en: Zhuangzong had fewer than a thousand horsemen with him. More than ten thousand Bian troops in ambush rose with a deafening roar and closed around him in ring after ring.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong had fewer than a thousand horsemen; the Bian men had more than ten thousand ambush troops, who rose with a great clamor and surrounded Zhuangzong in several rings.

entries.zh: 魯奇與王門關、烏德兒等奮命決戰，自午至申，俄而李存審兵至方解。
entries.en: Luqi, Wang Menguan, Wude'er, and others fought for their lives from noon until mid-afternoon. Li Cunshen's troops arrived soon afterward and the encirclement was broken.
entries.literal: Luqi, Wang Menguan, Wude'er and others fought desperately from noon to the shen hour; presently Li Cunshen's troops arrived and the siege was broken.

entries.zh: 魯奇持槍攜劍，獨衛莊宗，手殺百餘人。
entries.en: Spear in one hand and sword in the other, Luqi alone shielded Zhuangzong and killed more than a hundred men himself.
entries.literal: Luqi bore spear and sword and alone guarded Zhuangzong, killing more than a hundred men with his own hand.

entries.zh: 烏德兒等被擒，魯奇傷痍遍體，自是莊宗尤憐之，曆磁州刺史。
entries.en: Wude'er and the others were taken prisoner. Luqi was covered with wounds, and from then on Zhuangzong favored him all the more. He later served as prefect of Cizhou.
entries.literal: Wude'er and others were captured; Luqi was wounded all over; from then on Zhuangzong pitied him especially and he served as prefect of Cizhou.

entries.zh: 中都之戰，汴人大敗，魯奇見王彥章，識之，單馬追及，槍擬其頸；
entries.en: At the battle of Zhongdu the Bian army was routed. Luqi spotted Wang Yanzhang, recognized him, rode after him alone, and set a spear against his neck;
entries.literal: At the battle of Zhongdu the Bian forces were utterly defeated; Luqi saw Wang Yanzhang, recognized him, chased him alone on horseback and pressed a spear to his neck;

entries.zh: 彥章顧曰：「爾非餘故人乎？」
entries.en: Yanzhang looked back and said, "Aren't you my old friend?"
entries.literal: Yanzhang looked back and said: "Are you not my old friend?"

entries.zh: 即擒之以獻。
entries.en: He seized him on the spot and brought him in as his prize.
entries.literal: He at once seized him and presented him [as a captive].

entries.zh: 莊宗壯之，賞絹千匹。
entries.en: Zhuangzong was impressed and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of silk.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong admired this and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 〈（《九國誌·趙庭隱傳》：王彥章守中都，庭隱在其軍中。
entries.en: (From the Biography of Zhao Tingyin in the Jiuguo Zhi: Wang Yanzhang defended Zhongdu, and Tingyin served in his army.
entries.literal: (From the Biography of Zhao Tingyin in the Jiuguo Zhi: Wang Yanzhang held Zhongdu, and Tingyin was in his army.

entries.zh: 及彥章敗，庭隱為莊宗所獲，將以就戮，大將夏魯奇奏曰：「此矬也，其材可用。」
entries.en: When Yanzhang was defeated, Tingyin was taken by Zhuangzong and was about to be executed. The great general Xia Luqi memorialized, "He is a short man, but his abilities are worth keeping."
entries.literal: When Yanzhang was defeated, Tingyin was captured by Zhuangzong and was about to be put to death; the great general Xia Luqi memorialized, saying: "This is a dwarf, but his talent can be used."

entries.zh: 遂釋之。）〉
entries.en: He was then released.)〉
entries.literal: He was then released.)〉

entries.zh: 梁平，授鄭州防禦使。
entries.en: After Liang was conquered, he was made defender of Zhengzhou.
entries.literal: When Liang was pacified, he was appointed defender of Zhengzhou.

entries.zh: 四年，授河陽節度使。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was appointed military governor of Heyang.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed military governor of Heyang.

entries.zh: 天成初，移鎮許州，加同平章事。
entries.en: At the start of the Tiancheng era he was transferred to Xuzhou as military governor and made Chief Minister.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was transferred to govern Xuzhou and made Chief Minister.

entries.zh: 李嚴，幽州人，本名讓坤。
entries.en: Li Yan was a native of Youzhou; his birth name was Rangkun.
entries.literal: Li Yan was a man of Youzhou; his original name was Rangkun.

entries.zh: 初仕燕，為刺史，涉獵書傳，便弓馬，有口辯，多遊藝，以功名自許。
entries.en: He first served Yan as a prefect, read widely in the classics, was adept at archery and horsemanship, had a ready tongue, delighted in many arts, and set his heart on achievement and renown.
entries.literal: At first he served Yan as a prefect; he read widely in books and histories, was skilled in archery and horsemanship, had a ready tongue, enjoyed many pastimes, and aspired to merit and fame.

entries.zh: 同光中，為客省使。
entries.en: During the Tongguang era he served as commissioner of the Reception Bureau.
entries.literal: During Tongguang he was commissioner of the Reception Bureau.

entries.zh: 奉使於蜀，及與王衍相見，陳使者之禮，因於笏記中具述莊宗興復之功，其警句云：「才過汶水，縛王彥章於馬前；
entries.en: Sent on embassy to Shu, he met Wang Yan and performed the rites due an envoy. In the notes on his tablet he recounted Zhuangzong's deeds of restoration, with this striking line: "Hardly past the Wen River, Wang Yanzhang was bound before his horse;
entries.literal: Sent as envoy to Shu, when he met Wang Yan he performed the ambassador's rites and in his tablet notes set forth Zhuangzong's achievements in restoration; a striking line ran: "Barely past the Wen River, Wang Yanzhang was bound before his horse;

entries.zh: 旋及夷門，斬朱友貞於樓上。」
entries.en: and soon at the Yimen Gate Zhu Youzhen was beheaded on the tower."
entries.literal: and soon at the Yimen Gate Zhu Youzhen was beheaded on the tower."

entries.zh: 嚴復聲韻清亮，蜀人聽之愕然。
entries.en: Yan recited it again in a clear, ringing voice, and the men of Shu listened in stunned silence.
entries.literal: Yan repeated this in a clear, resonant voice; the men of Shu listened in astonishment.

entries.zh: 時蜀偽樞密使宋光嗣召嚴曲宴，因以近事訊於嚴。
entries.en: Song Guangsi, the bogus Shu commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, invited Yan to a private banquet and questioned him about recent affairs.
entries.literal: The Shu pretender's Bureau of Military Affairs chief Song Guangsi invited Yan to a private banquet and questioned him about recent events.

entries.zh: 嚴對曰：「吾皇前年四月即位於鄴宮，當月下鄆州。
entries.en: Yan replied, "Our Emperor took the throne at the Ye palace in the fourth month of the year before last and that same month marched on Yanzhou.
entries.literal: Yan replied: "Our Emperor took the throne at the Ye palace in the fourth month of the year before last and that same month descended on Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 十月四日，親統萬騎破賊中都，乘勝鼓行，遂誅汴孽，偽梁尚有兵三十萬，謀臣猛將，解甲倒戈。
entries.en: On the fourth day of the tenth month he personally led ten thousand horsemen and crushed the rebels at Zhongdu. Drums rolling, he pressed the victory forward, executed the Bian scourge, and though the false Liang still had three hundred thousand men, its strategists and fierce generals stripped off their armor and turned their swords around.
entries.literal: On the fourth day of the tenth month he personally commanded ten thousand horsemen and smashed the rebels at Zhongdu; pressing the victory with drum and march, he then executed the Bian scourge; the false Liang still had three hundred thousand troops, but stratagem-makers and fierce generals laid down armor and turned their blades.

entries.zh: 西盡甘、涼，東漸海外，南逾閩、浙，北極幽陵。
entries.en: In the west his realm reached Gan and Liang; in the east it stretched to the open sea; in the south it crossed Min and Zhe; in the north it ran to Youling.
entries.literal: In the west it reached Gan and Liang; in the east it extended to the outer sea; in the south it crossed Min and Zhe; in the north it reached Youling.

entries.zh: 牧伯侯王，稱藩不暇，家財入貢，府實上供。
entries.en: Regional lords and feudal princes scarcely had time to call themselves vassals; they sent household wealth as tribute and emptied their treasuries for the court.
entries.literal: Regional lords and marquises had no leisure to style themselves vassals; household wealth went as tribute and treasury stores as upland supply.

entries.zh: 吳國本朝舊臣，岐下先皇元老，遣子入侍，述職稱藩。
entries.en: Wu was a longtime subject of our house; below Qi stood an elder of the former emperor who sent his son to court and fulfilled vassal duties.
entries.literal: Wu was an old subject of our dynasty; below Qi stood a senior of the former emperor; he sent sons to attend court and rendered duty as a vassal.

entries.zh: 淮、海之君，卑辭厚貢，湖湘、荊楚，杭越、甌閩，異貨奇珍，府無虛月。
entries.en: Rulers of the Huai and coastal regions sent humble embassies and lavish gifts; from the lakes and rivers of Hunan and Hubei to Hangzhou, Yue, Wenzhou, and Fujian, exotic goods and rarities arrived so that the court storehouses knew no idle month.
entries.literal: Lords of the Huai and the sea used humble words and rich tribute; from Hunan, Hubei, Hang-Yue, and Ou-Min came exotic goods and rare treasures, and the treasury had no empty month.

entries.zh: 吾皇以德懷來，以威款附。
entries.en: Our Emperor wins men by virtue and binds them by power.
entries.literal: Our Emperor with virtue embraces those who come and with might wins their attachment.

entries.zh: 順則涵之以恩澤，逆則問之以干戈，四海車書，大同非晚。」
entries.en: The obedient he shelters in grace; the defiant he meets with arms. When chariots and writing unite the four seas, universal rule will come soon."
entries.literal: If they submit, he bathes them in grace; if they rebel, he questions them with arms; within the four seas chariots and writing unite, and great unity is not far off."

entries.zh: 光嗣曰：「餘所未知，惟岐下宋公，我之姻好，洞見其心，反覆多端，專謀跋扈，大不足信也。
entries.en: Guangsi said, "I cannot speak for the rest, but Duke Song below Qi is my kinsman by marriage, and I know his heart. He is changeable and scheming, bent on domineering power, and is not to be trusted at all.
entries.literal: Guangsi said: "Of the rest I do not know; only Duke Song below Qi, my marriage kin—I see through his heart: shifting and many-sided, bent on overbearing ambition, wholly unworthy of trust.

entries.zh: 似聞契丹部族，近日稍強，大國可無慮乎？」
entries.en: I hear the Khitan tribes have grown stronger of late. Surely your great state has no cause for worry?"
entries.literal: I seem to hear that the Khitan tribes have lately grown somewhat strong—can your great state be without concern?"

entries.zh: 嚴曰：「子言契丹之強盛，孰若偽梁？」
entries.en: Yan said, "You speak of Khitan might—compared with what? The false Liang?"
entries.literal: Yan said: "You speak of Khitan strength—compared with whom, the false Liang?"

entries.zh: 曰：「比梁差劣也。」
entries.en: He replied, "They are somewhat weaker than Liang was."
entries.literal: He said: "Compared with Liang they are rather inferior."

entries.zh: 嚴曰：「吾國視契丹如蚤虱耳，以其無害，不足爬搔。
entries.en: Yan said, "Our realm looks on the Khitan as fleas and lice. They do no harm, so they are not worth troubling over.
entries.literal: Yan said: "Our state regards the Khitan as fleas and lice; because they do no harm, they are not worth scratching.

entries.zh: 吾良將勁兵布天下，彼不勞一郡之兵，一校之眾，則懸首槀街，盡為奴擄。
entries.en: Our finest generals and strongest troops are posted across the empire. We would not need even one prefecture's force or one command's men to hang their heads at the execution ground and take them all as captives.
entries.literal: Our good generals and strong soldiers are spread across the realm; they would need neither a single prefecture's troops nor a single command's men, and Khitan heads would hang at the drying rack, all taken as slaves.

entries.zh: 但以天生四夷，當置度外，不在九州之本，未欲窮兵黷武也。」
entries.en: Only because the barbarians of the four quarters are born beyond our realm, they should be left outside our concern, outside the heartland of the Nine Provinces. We have no wish yet to wear out the army in endless war."
entries.literal: Only because the Four Barbarians are born by nature, they should be set beyond measure, outside the root of the Nine Provinces; we do not yet wish to exhaust the army in reckless war."

entries.zh: 光嗣聞辯對，畏而奇之。
entries.en: Guangsi heard this sharp reply and was both afraid and astonished.
entries.literal: Guangsi heard this eloquent reply and was both afraid and struck with wonder.

entries.zh: 時王衍失政，嚴知其可取，使還具奏，故平蜀之謀，始於嚴。
entries.en: Wang Yan's rule was failing, and Yan saw that Shu could be taken. He returned and reported in full, and thus the plan to conquer Shu began with Yan.
entries.literal: At that time Wang Yan's government was failing; Yan knew Shu could be taken, had him return and report in full, and so the plan to pacify Shu began with Yan.

entries.zh: 郭崇韜起軍之日，以嚴為三川招撫使，嚴與先鋒使康延孝將兵五千，先驅閣道，或馳以詞說，或威以兵鋒，大軍未及，所在降下。
entries.en: When Guo Chongtao took the field, Yan was made pacification commissioner of the Three Rivers. Yan and the vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao led five thousand men ahead along the mountain roads, winning some places by persuasion and others by force. Before the main army arrived, city after city surrendered.
entries.literal: On the day Guo Chongtao raised the army, Yan was made pacification commissioner of the Three Rivers; Yan and the vanguard commissioner Kang Yanxiao led five thousand troops, advancing first along the plank roads, sometimes galloping with words to persuade, sometimes threatening with the edge of arms; before the main army arrived, wherever they went submitted.

entries.zh: 延孝在漢州，王衍與書曰：「 可請李司空先來，餘即舉城納款。」
entries.en: Yanxiao was at Hanzhou when Wang Yan wrote to him: "Please ask Minister Li to come first, and I will surrender the city at once."
entries.literal: Yanxiao was at Hanzhou; Wang Yan wrote to him, saying: " You may ask Minister Li to come first; I will then surrender the city."

entries.zh: 眾咸以討蜀之謀始於嚴，衍以甘言，將誘而殺之，欲不令往。
entries.en: The troops all said the Shu campaign had begun with Yan, that Wang Yan's flattering words were a trap to lure and kill him, and they wanted to keep him from going.
entries.literal: All held that the plan to attack Shu had begun with Yan, that Yan's sweet words were meant to lure and kill him, and they wished not to let him go.

entries.zh: 嚴聞之喜，即馳騎入益州，衍見嚴於母前，以母、妻為托。
entries.en: Yan was delighted to hear it and rode at once into Yizhou. Wang Yan received him before his mother and entrusted his mother and wife to Yan's care.
entries.literal: Yan heard this with joy and at once galloped into Yizhou; Wang Yan received Yan before his mother and entrusted his mother and wife to Yan.

entries.zh: 即日，引蜀使歐陽彬迎謁魏王繼岌。
entries.en: That same day he brought the Shu envoy Ouyang Bin to pay homage to Prince Jiji of Wei.
entries.literal: That same day he led the Shu envoy Ouyang Bin to welcome and pay court to Prince Jiji of Wei.

entries.zh: 蜀平班師，會明宗即位，遷泗州防禦使兼客省使。
entries.en: After Shu was pacified the army withdrew. Mingzong then took the throne, and Yan was made defender of Sizhou while keeping his post as commissioner of the Reception Bureau.
entries.literal: When Shu was pacified the army returned; it happened that Mingzong took the throne, and Yan was transferred to defender of Sizhou while retaining the post of commissioner of the Reception Bureau.

entries.zh: 長興初，安重誨謀欲控製兩川，嚴乃求為西川兵馬都監，庶效方略。
entries.en: Early in the Changxing era, An Chonghui schemed to control the Two Chuan, and Yan asked to be made military inspector of Xichuan so he could put his plans into effect.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Changxing, An Chonghui plotted to control the Two Chuan; Yan then asked to be military inspector of Xichuan, hoping to put his stratagems to use.

entries.zh: 孟知祥覺之，既至，執而害之。
entries.en: Meng Zhixiang saw through him, and when Yan arrived he seized and executed him.
entries.literal: Meng Zhixiang perceived this; once Yan arrived, he seized and killed him.

entries.zh: 〈（《九國誌·王彥銖傳》：李嚴之為監軍也，密懷異謀，知祥數其過，命彥銖擒斬之，嚴之左右無敢動者。）〉
entries.en: (From the Biography of Wang Yanyin in the Records of the Nine Kingdoms: When Li Yan served as military inspector, he secretly plotted rebellion. Zhixiang listed his offenses and ordered Yanyin to seize and execute him, and none of Yan's attendants dared stir.)〉
entries.literal: (From the Biography of Wang Yanyin in the Records of the Nine Kingdoms: When Li Yan served as military inspector, he secretly harbored a different design; Zhixiang counted his offenses and ordered Yanyin to seize and behead him, and none of Yan's attendants dared move.)〉

entries.zh: 贈太保。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 康思立，晉陽人也。
entries.en: Kang Sili was a native of Jinyang.
entries.literal: Kang Sili was a man of Jinyang.

entries.zh: 少善騎射，事武皇為爪牙，署河東親騎軍使。
entries.en: In youth he excelled at mounted archery, served Emperor Wu as a trusted fighter, and was appointed commander of the Hedong Personal Cavalry.
entries.literal: In youth he excelled at mounted archery, served Emperor Wu as a claw-and-fang man, and was appointed commander of the Hedong Personal Cavalry.

entries.zh: 莊宗嗣位，從解圍於上黨，敗梁人於柏鄉，及平薊兵，後戰於河上，皆有功，累承製加檢校戶部尚書，右突騎指揮使。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong succeeded, he helped lift the siege at Shangdang, defeated the Liang at Baixiang, pacified the Ji forces, and later fought along the Yellow River, winning merit in every campaign. He was repeatedly promoted by edict to acting Minister of Revenue and commander of the Right Vanguard Cavalry.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong succeeded, he followed in relieving the siege at Shangdang, defeated Liang men at Baixiang, pacified the Ji troops, and later fought on the Yellow River—all with merit; he was repeatedly appointed by edict as acting Minister of Revenue and commander of the Right Vanguard Cavalry.

entries.zh: 莊宗即位，繼改軍帥，賜忠勇拱衛功臣，加檢校尚書右僕射。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he was again made an army commander, granted the title Loyal Brave Arch-guard Merit Subject, and promoted to acting Vice Director of the Right Secretariat.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he was again changed to army commander, granted the title of merit subject Loyal Brave Arch-guard, and made acting Vice Director of the Right Secretariat.

entries.zh: 天成元年，授應州刺史，尋移嵐州，充北面諸蕃部族都監。
entries.en: In the first year of Tiancheng he was made prefect of Yingzhou, soon transferred to Lanzhou, and appointed overall supervisor of the northern frontier tribes.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he was appointed prefect of Yingzhou, soon moved to Lanzhou, and served as overall supervisor of the northern frontier tribal peoples.

entries.zh: 三年，遷宿州團練使。
entries.en: In the third year he was transferred to training commissioner of Suzhou.
entries.literal: In the third year he was transferred to training commissioner of Suzhou.

entries.zh: 四年，領昭武軍節度、利巴集等州觀察處置等使。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was made military governor of the Zhaowu army and commissioner for observation and disposition of Li, Ba, Ji, and other prefectures.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he led the Zhaowu army as military governor and commissioner for observation and disposition of Li, Ba, Ji, and other prefectures.

entries.zh: 改賜耀忠保節功臣。
entries.en: He was granted the new merit title Yao Loyalty Preserving Festival.
entries.literal: He was again granted the merit title Yao Loyalty Preserving Festival.

entries.zh: 長興初，朝廷舉兵討東川董璋，詔監西面行營軍馬都指揮使。
entries.en: Early in the Changxing era the court raised troops against Dong Zhang of Eastern Chuan and ordered him to supervise the western campaign as overall commander of the army's horse units.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Changxing the court raised troops against Dong Zhang of Eastern Chuan and ordered him to supervise the western campaign army as overall horse commander.

entries.zh: 二年，移鎮陝州。
entries.en: In the second year he was transferred to govern Shaanzhou.
entries.literal: In the second year he was transferred to govern Shaanzhou.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：潞王至靈寶，思立謀固守陝城以俟康義誠。
entries.en: (From the Comprehensive Mirror: When Prince Lu reached Lingbao, Sili planned to hold Shaan city and await Kang Yicheng.
entries.literal: (From the Comprehensive Mirror: When the Prince of Lu reached Lingbao, Sili planned to hold Shaan city firm and await Kang Yicheng.

entries.zh: 先是，捧聖五百騎戍陝，為潞王前鋒，至城下，呼城上人曰：「禁軍十萬已奉新帝，爾輩數人奚為！
entries.en: Earlier, five hundred Pingsheng cavalry had garrisoned Shaan as the Prince of Lu's vanguard. Reaching the foot of the wall, they shouted up, "A hundred thousand men of the imperial guard have already acclaimed the new emperor. What are you few men still doing here!
entries.literal: Earlier, five hundred Pingsheng horsemen garrisoned Shaan as the Prince of Lu's vanguard; reaching below the wall, they called to those above: "The imperial army of a hundred thousand has already honored the new emperor—what are you few men doing!

entries.zh: 徒累一城人塗地耳！」
entries.en: You will only bring bloodshed on a whole city for nothing!"
entries.literal: You will only heap one city's people in blood on the ground!"

entries.zh: 於是捧聖卒爭出迎，思立不能禁，不得已，亦出迎。）〉
entries.en: Then the Pingsheng troops rushed out to welcome them. Sili could not stop them and, with no choice left, went out to welcome them as well.)〉
entries.literal: Then the Pingsheng soldiers vied to go out and welcome them; Sili could not forbid it and, having no choice, also went out to welcome them.)〉

entries.zh: 清泰初，改授邢台，累官至檢校太傅，封會稽郡開國侯。
entries.en: Early in the Qingtai era he was reassigned to Xingtai, rose to acting Grand Preceptor, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Kuaiji.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was reassigned to Xingtai, rose cumulatively to acting Grand Preceptor, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 二年，入為右神武統軍。
entries.en: In the second year he entered the capital as commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.
entries.literal: In the second year he entered the capital as commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.

entries.zh: 三年，充北面行營馬軍都指揮使。
entries.en: In the third year he served as overall commander of the horse units in the northern campaign.
entries.literal: In the third year he served as overall commander of the northern campaign's horse army.

entries.zh: 是歲閏十一月，卒於軍，年六十三。
entries.en: That year, in the intercalary eleventh month, he died in camp at the age of sixty-three.
entries.literal: That year, in the intercalary eleventh month, he died in the army at the age of sixty-three.

entries.zh: 張敬達，字志通，代州人，小字生鐵。
entries.en: Zhang Jingda, courtesy name Zhigong, was a native of Daizhou; his childhood name was Raw Iron.
entries.literal: Zhang Jingda, style Zhigong, was a man of Daizhou; his childhood name was Raw Iron.

entries.zh: 父審，素有勇，事武皇為列校，曆廳直軍使，同光初，卒於軍。
entries.en: His father Shen was brave by nature, served Emperor Wu as a column commander, rose to Hall Direct army commander, and died in service early in the Tongguang era.
entries.literal: His father Shen had valor by nature, served Emperor Wu as a column commander, passed through the post of Hall Direct army commander, and in early Tongguang died in the army.

entries.zh: 敬達少以騎射著名，莊宗知之，召令繼父職；
entries.en: Jingda was famed in youth for mounted archery. Zhuangzong knew of him and summoned him to inherit his father's post;
entries.literal: Jingda in youth was famed for mounted archery; Zhuangzong knew of it and summoned him to inherit his father's post;

entries.zh: 平河南有功，繼加檢校工部尚書。
entries.en: he won merit pacifying Henan and was then made acting Minister of Works.
entries.literal: in pacifying Henan he had merit and was then made acting Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，曆捧聖指揮使、檢校尚書左僕射。
entries.en: When Mingzong took the throne, he served as commander of the Pingsheng guard and acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he passed through commander of the Pingsheng guard and acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 長興中，改河東馬步軍都指揮使，超授檢校司徒，領欽州刺史。
entries.en: During the Changxing era he was made overall commander of the Hedong horse and foot armies, promoted in one step to acting Minister of Education, and appointed prefect of Qinzhou.
entries.literal: During Changxing he was changed to overall commander of the Hedong horse and foot armies, superseded in appointment to acting Minister of Education, and led Qinzhou as prefect.

entries.zh: 三年，加檢校太保、應州節度使。
entries.en: In the third year he was made acting Grand Guardian and military governor of Yingzhou.
entries.literal: In the third year he was made acting Grand Guardian and military governor of Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 四年，遷雲州。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was transferred to Yunzhou.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Yunzhou.

entries.zh: 時以契丹率族帳自黑榆林挎剌泊至沒越泊，雲借漢界水草，敬達每聚兵塞下，以遏其衝。
entries.en: At that time the Khitan led their clans from Heilinlin through Kulabo to Moyuebo, grazing on Han borderlands. Jingda repeatedly massed troops below the passes to block their advance.
entries.literal: At that time the Khitan led their clan tents from Heilinlin through Kulabo to Moyuebo; Yun borrowed Han border water and grass, and Jingda each time gathered troops below the pass to block their thrust.

entries.zh: 契丹竟不敢南牧，邊人賴之。
entries.en: The Khitan ultimately did not dare drive their herds south, and the border people owed their safety to him.
entries.literal: The Khitan ultimately did not dare pasture south, and the border people relied on him.

entries.zh: 清泰中，自彭門移鎮平陽，加檢校太傅，從石敬瑭為北面兵馬副總管，仍屯兵雁門。
entries.en: During the Qingtai era he was transferred from Pengmen to Pingyang, made acting Grand Preceptor, and served under Shi Jingtang as deputy overall commander of the northern forces while keeping his troops at Yanmen.
entries.literal: During Qingtai he was moved from Pengmen to govern Pingyang, made acting Grand Preceptor, followed Shi Jingtang as deputy overall commander of the northern army and horse forces, and still garrisoned troops at Yanmen.

entries.zh: 未幾，晉高祖建義，末帝詔以敬達為北面行營都招討使，仍使悉引部下兵圍太原，以定州節度使楊光遠副焉。
entries.en: Before long, when the Jin founder rose in revolt, the Last Emperor appointed Jingda overall pacification commissioner of the northern campaign and ordered him to lead all his troops to besiege Taiyuan, with Yang Guangyuan, military governor of Dingzhou, as his deputy.
entries.literal: Before long, when Jin Gaozu raised the righteous army, the Last Emperor issued an edict making Jingda overall pacification commissioner of the northern campaign and still had him lead all his subordinate troops to besiege Taiyuan, with Yang Guangyuan, military governor of Dingzhou, as deputy.

entries.zh: 尋統兵三萬，營於晉安鄉。
entries.en: Soon he took command of thirty thousand men and encamped at Jin'an.
entries.literal: Soon he commanded thirty thousand troops and encamped at Jin'an village.

entries.zh: 末帝自六月繼有詔促令攻取，敬達設長城連柵、雲梯飛炮，使工者運其巧思，窮土木之力。
entries.en: From the sixth month onward the Last Emperor repeatedly ordered him to take the city. Jingda built long walls and linked palisades, cloud ladders and siege engines, set artisans to every device, and exhausted every effort of engineering.
entries.literal: From the sixth month the Last Emperor repeatedly issued edicts urging capture; Jingda set long walls and linked palisades, cloud ladders and flying cannon, had artisans apply their clever designs, and exhausted the power of earth and wood.

entries.zh: 時督事者每有所構，則暴風大雨，平地水深數尺，而城柵崩墮，竟不能合其圍。
entries.en: Whenever the builders raised some new work, violent storms followed. Water on the plain stood several feet deep, walls and palisades collapsed, and in the end they could not close the siege ring.
entries.literal: Whenever those supervising the work set up something, violent wind and great rain followed; on level ground the water was several feet deep, city palisades collapsed and fell, and in the end they could not close the encirclement.

entries.zh: 九月，契丹至，敬達大敗，尋為所圍。
entries.en: In the ninth month the Khitan arrived. Jingda suffered a crushing defeat and was soon surrounded.
entries.literal: In the ninth month the Khitan arrived; Jingda was greatly defeated and soon was besieged.

entries.zh: 晉高祖及蕃眾自晉安寨南門外，長百餘里，闊五十里，布以氈帳，用毛索掛鈴，而部伍多犬，以備警急。
entries.en: The Jin founder and the barbarian hosts spread from beyond the south gate of the Jin'an camp for more than a hundred li in length and fifty li across, pitching felt tents and hanging bells on hair ropes. Most units kept dogs to sound the alarm.
entries.literal: Jin Gaozu and the barbarian masses from outside the south gate of the Jin'an stockade stretched more than a hundred li in length and fifty li in breadth, spread with felt tents, using hair ropes hung with bells, and the units mostly had dogs to guard against sudden alarm.

entries.zh: 營中嘗有夜遁者，出則犬吠鈴動，跬步不能行焉。
entries.en: When men in the camp tried to flee by night, the dogs barked and the bells rang at the first step, and they could not move.
entries.literal: In the camp there were once men who fled by night; when they went out the dogs barked and the bells moved, and they could not advance a half step.

entries.zh: 自是敬達與麾下部曲五萬人，馬萬匹，無由四奔，但見穹廬如崗阜相屬，諸軍相顧失色。
entries.en: From then on Jingda and his fifty thousand men and ten thousand horses had no escape in any direction. They saw only dome tents stretching like linked hills, and the armies looked at one another in dismay.
entries.literal: From this Jingda and the fifty thousand men and ten thousand horses under his command had no way to flee in the four directions; they only saw domed tents like hill ranges joined, and the armies looked at one another and lost color.

entries.zh: 始則削木篩糞，以飼其馬，日望朝廷救軍，及漸羸死，則與將士分食之，馬盡食殫。
entries.en: At first they shaved wood and sifted dung to feed the horses, daily hoping for relief from court. As the horses weakened and died, officers and men shared the meat until every horse was eaten.
entries.literal: At first they shaved wood and sifted dung to feed their horses, daily hoping for the court's relief army; as the horses gradually weakened and died, they divided and ate them with the generals and soldiers until the horses were all eaten up.

entries.zh: 副將楊光遠、次將安審琦知不濟，勸敬達宜早降以求自安。
entries.en: The deputy Yang Guangyuan and the second-in-command An Shenqi saw that all was lost and urged Jingda to surrender early and save himself.
entries.literal: The deputy Yang Guangyuan and the second commander An Shenqi knew the cause was lost and urged Jingda to surrender early to seek his own safety.

entries.zh: 敬達曰：「吾受恩於明宗，位曆方鎮，主上授我大柄，而失律如此，已有愧於心也。
entries.en: Jingda said, "I owe my rise to Mingzong. I have held regional command, and the sovereign entrusted me with great authority. To fail so badly already shames me to the heart.
entries.literal: Jingda said: "I received grace from Mingzong, held posts across the regional commands, and the sovereign entrusted me with great authority—yet I have lost discipline like this and already have shame in my heart.

entries.zh: 今救軍在近，旦暮雪恥有期，諸公何相迫耶！
entries.en: Relief is near, and we may yet wipe away this shame. Why do you press me so!
entries.literal: Now the relief army is near; dawn and dusk will bring a day to wipe away shame—why do you gentlemen press me so!

entries.zh: 待勢窮，則請殺吾，攜首以降，亦未為晚。」
entries.en: When all is truly lost, you may kill me and carry my head to surrender. That will not be too late."
entries.literal: Wait until the situation is exhausted, then ask to kill me and carry my head to surrender—it will not yet be too late."

entries.zh: 光遠、審琦知敬達意未決，恐坐成魚肉，遂斬敬達以降。
entries.en: Guangyuan and Shenqi saw that Jingda had not made up his mind and feared that if they waited they would become helpless prey. They beheaded Jingda and surrendered.
entries.literal: Guangyuan and Shenqi knew Jingda's mind was not yet settled and feared sitting still would make them fish on the chopping block; they then beheaded Jingda and surrendered.

entries.zh: 〈（《契丹國志》：楊光遠謀害張敬達，諸將高行周陰為之備，敬達疏於防禦，推遠行周等。
entries.en: (From the Khitan State Annals: Yang Guangyuan plotted to kill Zhang Jingda. General Gao Xingzhou secretly prepared against it, but Jingda was lax in his defenses and kept Gao Xingzhou and the others at a distance.
entries.literal: (From the Khitan State Annals: Yang Guangyuan plotted to harm Zhang Jingda; the generals Gao Xingzhou secretly prepared against it; Jingda was lax in defense and kept Gao Xingzhou and the others at a distance.

entries.zh: 清晨，光遠上謁，見敬達左右無人，遂殺之。）〉）
entries.en: At dawn Guangyuan came to call on him, found no one at Jingda's side, and killed him.)〉
entries.literal: At early dawn Guangyuan went to an audience, saw no one at Jingda's side, and then killed him.)〉

entries.zh: 末帝聞其歿也，愴慟久之。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor heard of his death, he mourned deeply for a long time.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor heard of his death, he mourned deeply for a long time.

entries.zh: 契丹主告其部曲及漢之降者曰：「為臣當如此人！」
entries.en: The Khitan ruler told his followers and the Han who had surrendered, "A subject ought to be like this man!"
entries.literal: The Khitan ruler told his subordinates and the Han who had surrendered, saying: "A subject ought to be like this man!"

entries.zh: 令部人收葬之。
entries.en: He ordered his men to gather and bury him.
entries.literal: He ordered his followers to gather and bury him.

entries.zh: 晉高祖即位後，所有田宅，鹹賜其妻子焉。
entries.en: After Jin Gaozu took the throne, all his fields and residences were bestowed upon his wife and children.
entries.literal: After Jin Gaozu took the throne, all his fields and residences were bestowed upon his wife and children.

entries.zh: 時議者以敬達嘗事數帝，亟立軍功，及領藩郡，不聞其濫，繼屯守塞垣，復能撫下，而臨難固執，不求苟免，乃近代之忠臣也。
entries.en: Commentators held that Jingda had served several emperors, won repeated military honors, and when governing frontier prefectures was never known to abuse his power; he then guarded the border, could still win over his men, and when facing hardship stood firm rather than seek escape—a loyal minister of recent times.
entries.literal: Commentators of the time held that Jingda had served several emperors, repeatedly won military merit, and when governing frontier prefectures was never heard to abuse his power; he then guarded the border ramparts, could still comfort his subordinates, and when facing hardship stood firm and did not seek to escape at any cost—he was a loyal minister of recent times.

entries.zh: 晉有天下，不能追懋官封，賞其事跡，非激忠之道也。
entries.en: Yet once Jin held the realm it failed to posthumously ennoble him with high honors and reward his deeds—hardly the way to stir loyalty.
entries.literal: Yet when Jin possessed the realm it could not posthumously ennoble him with high offices and reward his deeds—this was no way to stir loyalty.

entries.zh: 思立本出陰山諸部，性純厚，善撫將士，明宗素重之，故即位之始，以應州所生之地授焉。
entries.en: Sili was originally from the Yinshan tribes. Pure and generous by nature, he was skilled at winning over officers and soldiers. Mingzong had long valued him, and at the start of his reign granted him his birthplace in Ying Prefecture.
entries.literal: Sili was originally from the tribes of Yinshan. His nature was pure and generous, and he was skilled at comforting officers and soldiers. Mingzong had long valued him, so at the start of his enthronement he granted him the place of his birth in Ying Prefecture.

entries.zh: 其後曆三郡三鎮，皆得百姓之譽。
entries.en: He later served in three prefectures and three garrisons, winning the people's praise in each.
entries.literal: Afterward he passed through three prefectures and three garrisons, and in each won the praise of the common people.

entries.zh: 末帝以其年高，征居環衛。
entries.en: Because of his advanced age, the Last Emperor summoned him to serve in the palace guard.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor, because of his advanced age, summoned him to dwell in the palace guard.

entries.zh: 及出幸懷州，以北師不利，乃命思立統駕下騎軍赴團柏穀以益軍勢，俄而楊光遠以大軍降於太原，思立因憤激，疾作而卒焉。
entries.en: When the emperor visited Huaizhou and the northern army fared poorly, he ordered Sili to lead the cavalry of the imperial escort to Tuanbai Valley to reinforce the army. Soon Yang Guangyuan surrendered his great army at Taiyuan; stirred to fury, Sili fell ill and died.
entries.literal: When the emperor went on an excursion to Huaizhou and the northern army fared poorly, he ordered Sili to command the cavalry under the imperial escort to Tuanbai Valley to strengthen the army. Soon afterward Yang Guangyuan surrendered his great army at Taiyuan; Sili, stirred by indignation, fell ill and died.

entries.zh: 晉高祖即位，追其宿舊，為輟朝一日，贈太子少師。
entries.en: When Jin Gaozu took the throne, he honored their old friendship by halting court for one day and posthumously enfeoffing him as Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne, he recalled their old friendship, halted court for one day, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 元行欽，本幽州劉守光之愛將。
entries.en: Yuan Xingqin had begun as a favorite commander of Liu Shouguang of Youzhou.
entries.literal: Yuan Xingqin was originally a favorite commander of Liu Shouguang of Youzhou.

entries.zh: 守光之奪父位也，令行欽攻大恩山，又令殺諸兄弟。
entries.en: When Shouguang seized his father's throne, he sent Xingqin against Da'en Mountain and ordered him to kill his brothers as well.
entries.literal: When Shouguang seized his father's position, he ordered Xingqin to attack Da'en Mountain and also ordered him to kill his brothers.

entries.zh: 天祐九年，周德威攻圍山州，守光困蹙，令行欽於山北募兵，以應契丹。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Tianyou, Zhou Dewei besieged Shanzhou. Shouguang, cornered, ordered Xingqin to raise troops north of the mountains to link up with the Khitan.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Tianyou, Zhou Dewei besieged Shanzhou; Shouguang was hard pressed and ordered Xingqin to recruit troops north of the mountains to cooperate with the Khitan.

entries.zh: 時明宗為將，攻行欽於山北，與之接戰，矢及明宗馬鞍，既而以勢迫來降。
entries.en: Mingzong was then a field commander. He attacked Xingqin in the northern hills, and in the fighting an arrow struck Mingzong's saddle. Soon afterward, hard pressed, Xingqin surrendered.
entries.literal: At that time Mingzong was a general; he attacked Xingqin north of the mountains and joined battle with him; an arrow reached Mingzong's saddle; afterward, pressed by circumstances, [Xingqin] came over in surrender.

entries.zh: 明宗憐其有勇，奏隸為假子，後因從征討，恩禮特隆。
entries.en: Mingzong admired his courage and had him registered as an adopted son. Thereafter, on campaign after campaign, he was treated with exceptional favor.
entries.literal: Mingzong pitied him for his bravery, memorialized to have him enrolled as an adoptive son, and later, because he followed on campaigns, favored him with exceptional courtesy.

entries.zh: 常臨敵擒生，必有所獲，名聞軍中。
entries.en: Whenever he met the enemy he took prisoners, and he always came away with something to show for it; his reputation spread through the army.
entries.literal: Whenever he faced the enemy and took prisoners alive, he always gained something; his name was known throughout the army.

entries.zh: 莊宗東定趙、魏，選驍健置之麾下，因索行欽，莊宗不得已而遣之。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong pacified Zhao and Wei in the east, he picked out the fiercest fighters for his personal command and asked for Xingqin. Zhuangzong, unable to refuse, sent him on.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong secured Zhao and Wei in the east, he selected the bravest and placed them under his command; he thus demanded Xingqin, and Zhuangzong, having no choice, sent him away.

entries.zh: 時有散指揮都頭，名為散員，命行欽為都部署，賜姓，名紹榮。
entries.en: There was then a corps of scattered guard commanders called the "scattered guards." Zhuangzong made Xingqin their overall commander, granted him the imperial surname, and gave him the name Shaorong.
entries.literal: At the time there were scattered command heads of the guard called "scattered guards"; he appointed Xingqin overall commander, granted him a surname, and named him Shaorong.

entries.zh: 莊宗好戰，勇於大敵，或臨陣有急兵，行欽必橫身解鬥翼衛之。
entries.en: Zhuangzong loved combat and was fearless before strong foes. Whenever danger closed in on the field, Xingqin would throw himself into the melee and fight at Zhuangzong's side to cover him.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong loved battle and was bold before great enemies; whenever on the field there was an emergency, Xingqin always threw himself across [Zhuangzong] to break the fight and shield him on the wings.

entries.zh: 莊宗營於德勝也，與汴軍戰於潘張，王師不利，諸軍奔亂。
entries.en: While Zhuangzong was encamped at Desheng, he fought the Bian army at Panzhang. The imperial forces were beaten and the ranks broke in flight.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong encamped at Desheng and fought the Bian army at Panzhang, the imperial army fared badly and the forces fled in disorder.

entries.zh: 莊宗得三四騎而旋，中野為汴軍數百騎攢槊攻之，事將不測，行欽識其幟，急馳一騎，奮劍斷二矛，斬一級，汴軍乃解圍，翼莊宗還宮。
entries.en: Zhuangzong got away with only three or four riders. In the open field several hundred Bian horsemen closed on him with leveled spears, and the outcome hung by a thread. Xingqin recognized their banners, spurred forward alone, slashed two spears apart with his sword, and cut down one man. The Bian troops broke off, and he escorted Zhuangzong back to camp.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong escaped with only three or four horsemen; in open country several hundred Bian horsemen closed in with spears; the situation was dire; Xingqin recognized their banners, galloped forward alone, swung his sword and cut two spears, beheaded one man; the Bian army then broke the encirclement and escorted Zhuangzong back to the palace.

entries.zh: 莊宗因流涕言曰：「富貴與卿共之。」
entries.en: Zhuangzong wept and said, "Whatever wealth and rank are mine shall be yours as well."
entries.literal: Zhuangzong wept and said: "Wealth and honor shall be yours as well as mine."

entries.zh: 自是寵冠諸將，官至檢校太傅、忻州刺史。
entries.en: From that day his favor outstripped every other general's, and he rose to Grand Guardian in Examinership and prefect of Xinzhou.
entries.literal: From then on his favor surpassed all generals; he reached the posts of Grand Guardian in Examinership and prefect of Xinzhou.

entries.zh: 及莊宗平梁，授武寧軍節度使。
entries.en: After Zhuangzong conquered Liang, he was made military governor of Wuning.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Liang, he was appointed military governor of Wuning.

entries.zh: 嘗因內宴群臣，使相預會，行欽官為保傅，當地褥下坐。
entries.en: Once Zhuangzong gave an inner banquet for his ministers and invited the commissioners as well. Xingqin held the post of guardian-tutor and was to sit below the floor cushions.
entries.literal: Once at an inner banquet for ministers, commissioners were also invited; Xingqin's post was guardian-tutor and he should sit below the floor cushions.

entries.zh: 酒酣樂作，莊宗敘生平戰陣之事，因左右顧視，曰：「紹榮安在？」
entries.en: As the wine warmed and the music began, Zhuangzong recounted the battles of his life, then glanced about and asked, "Where is Shaorong?"
entries.literal: When the wine was warm and music played, Zhuangzong recounted battles of his life and looked about, saying: "Where is Shaorong?"

entries.zh: 所司奏云：「有敕，使相預會，紹榮散官，殿上無位。」
entries.en: The master of ceremonies replied, "By imperial order the commissioners were invited to this gathering. Shaorong holds a scattered rank and has no place on the dais."
entries.literal: The department reported: "By imperial order, commissioners are invited to attend; Shaorong holds a scattered rank and has no seat in the hall."

entries.zh: 莊宗徹會不懌。
entries.en: Zhuangzong broke up the banquet in displeasure.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong dissolved the banquet displeased.

entries.zh: 翌日，以行欽為同平章事，由是不宴百官於內殿，但宴武臣而已，
entries.en: The next day he made Xingqin Chief Minister. After that he no longer entertained all the civil officials in the inner hall, but only his military commanders,
entries.literal: The next day he made Xingqin Chief Minister; henceforth he no longer feasted all officials in the inner hall but only military men,

entries.zh: 馬郁，其先范陽人。
entries.en: Ma Yu came from a Fanyang family.
entries.literal: Ma Yu—his ancestors were from Fanyang.

entries.zh: 郁少警悟，有俊才智數，言辯縱橫，下筆成文。
entries.en: From youth he was quick-witted and gifted with rare talent and resourcefulness; his speech was bold and fluent, and essays flowed from his brush as if unbidden.
entries.literal: As a youth Yu was alert and perceptive; he possessed outstanding talent and clever calculation, spoke with fluent and forceful eloquence, and produced compositions the moment he set brush to paper.

entries.zh: 乾寧末，為幽州府刀筆小吏。
entries.en: In the closing years of Qianning he was a low-ranking clerical officer in the Youzhou government.
entries.literal: At the end of the Qianning era he served as a minor clerk handling documents in the Youzhou prefectural office.

entries.zh: 李匡威為王鎔所殺，鎔書報其弟匡儔。
entries.en: When Li Kuangwei was killed by Wang Rong, Rong sent a written report to Kuangchou, his brother.
entries.literal: Li Kuangwei was killed by Wang Rong, and Rong wrote a letter informing his brother Kuangchou.

entries.zh: 匡儔遣使於鎔，問謀亂本末，幕客為書，多不如旨。
entries.en: Kuangchou sent a messenger to Rong to ask how the conspiracy had unfolded; several secretaries drafted replies, yet most missed what he wanted.
entries.literal: Kuangchou dispatched an envoy to Rong to inquire into the beginning and end of the plotting and rebellion; staff members drafted letters, but most failed to satisfy his intent.

entries.zh: 郁時直記室，即起草，為之條列事狀，雲可疑者十，詞理俊贍，以此知名。
entries.en: Yu, then serving in the records office, promptly drafted a memorial laying out the circumstances and ten suspicious points in elegant, forceful prose, and with that made his name.
entries.literal: At that time Yu was on duty in the secretariat; he immediately drafted a document, itemizing the facts of the case and citing ten points that seemed suspicious—the language was polished and ample, and he became famous for this.

entries.zh: 嘗聘王鎔於鎮州，官妓有轉轉者，美麗善歌舞，因宴席，郁累挑之。
entries.en: On an embassy to Wang Rong at Zhenzhou he took notice of an official courtesan named Zhuanzhuan, renowned for her beauty and dancing; during the feast Yu kept pressing his attentions on her.
entries.literal: Once when he was visiting Wang Rong at Zhenzhou on a diplomatic mission, there was a government entertainer named Zhuanzhuan who was beautiful and skilled in song and dance; at a banquet Yu repeatedly flirted with her.

entries.zh: 幕客張澤亦以文章名，謂郁曰：「子能座上成賦，可以此妓奉酬。」
entries.en: Zhang Ze, another celebrated writer on the staff, challenged him: "Compose a fu here at the banquet, and the girl is yours."
entries.literal: The staff member Zhang Ze, who was also famed for his writing, said to Yu: "If you can compose a fu at the table, you may have this entertainer as your reward."

entries.zh: 郁抽筆操紙，即時成賦，擁妓而去。
entries.en: Yu seized brush and paper, finished the piece on the spot, and walked off with the girl in his arms.
entries.literal: Yu drew out his brush, took up paper, immediately completed the fu, and left embracing the entertainer.

entries.zh: 郁在武皇幕，累官至檢校司空、秘書監。
entries.en: In Li Keyong's service he rose through the ranks to honorary Minister of Works and Director of the Imperial Library.
entries.literal: While Yu served on Emperor Wu's staff, he rose in successive posts to Acting Minister of Works and Director of the Imperial Library.

entries.zh: 武皇與莊宗禮遇俱厚，給賜優異。
entries.en: Li Keyong and his son Zhuangzong both honored him richly and showered him with exceptional rewards.
entries.literal: Both Emperor Wu and Emperor Zhuangzong treated him with generous courtesy and gave him outstanding gifts and allowances.

entries.zh: 監軍張承業，本朝舊人，權貴任事，人士脅肩低首候之。
entries.en: The supervising commissioner Zhang Chengye, a veteran of the founding court, held real power; officials shrank before him and waited on him with bowed heads.
entries.literal: The army supervisor Zhang Chengye was an elder of the founding house, wielded power as a favored official, and men of rank hunched their shoulders and bowed their heads waiting on him.

entries.zh: 郁以滑稽侮狎，其往如歸，有時直造臥內。
entries.en: Yu treated him with jesting familiarity, coming and going as freely as at home and sometimes walking straight into his bedchamber.
entries.literal: Yu treated him with witty mockery and familiar disrespect; his visits were like returning home, and sometimes he went straight into the sleeping chamber.

entries.zh: 每賓僚宴集，承業出珍果陳列於前，食之必盡。
entries.en: At every banquet Chengye put out choice fruit before the guests, and Yu always ate every piece.
entries.literal: Whenever guests and colleagues feasted together, Chengye set out rare fruits before them, and Yu invariably ate every one.

entries.zh: 承業私戒主膳者曰：「他日馬監至，唯以乾藕子置前而已。」
entries.en: Chengye quietly told the head cook, "When Director Ma comes again, he should be served nothing but dried lotus seeds."
entries.literal: Chengye privately warned the chief caterer: "When Director Ma comes another day, place only dried lotus seed before him."

entries.zh: 郁至，窺其不可啖；
entries.en: When Yu arrived he saw they were inedible;
entries.literal: When Yu arrived, he saw that they could not be eaten;

entries.zh: 異日，靴中出一鐵楇，碎而食之。
entries.en: On another visit he produced an iron pestle from his boot, crushed the seeds, and ate them.
entries.literal: On another day he pulled an iron pestle from his boot, broke it into pieces, and ate them.

entries.zh: 承業大笑曰：「為公設異饌，勿敗餘食案。」
entries.en: Chengye roared with laughter: "This is a special feast just for you—please don't spoil the rest of my table."
entries.literal: Chengye laughed loudly and said: "A special dish has been set out for you—do not ruin my remaining spread of food."

entries.zh: 其俊率如此。
entries.en: Such was the measure of his wit and audacity.
entries.literal: His wit and boldness were of this sort.

entries.zh: 賈馥，故鎮州節度使王鎔判官也。
entries.en: Jia Fu had served as secretary to Wang Rong, the former military commissioner of Zhenzhou.
entries.literal: Jia Fu had been secretary to Wang Rong, former military commissioner of Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 家聚書三千卷，手自刊校。
entries.en: His family library held three thousand scrolls, which he collated and proofread with his own hand.
entries.literal: His household collected three thousand scrolls of books, which he personally collated and proofread.

entries.zh: 張文禮殺王鎔，時莊宗未即尊位，文禮遣馥至鄴都勸進，因留鄴下，棲遲郵舍。
entries.en: After Zhang Wenli killed Wang Rong, while Zhuangzong had not yet taken the throne, Wenli sent Fu to Yedu to urge his accession; Fu stayed on there, lodging at the post station.
entries.literal: When Zhang Wenli killed Wang Rong, Zhuangzong had not yet taken the throne; Wenli sent Fu to Yedu to urge his accession, and Fu remained below Yedu, lingering at the post station.

entries.zh: 莊宗即位，授鴻臚少卿。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong ascended the throne he appointed Fu Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he appointed Fu Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial.

entries.zh: 後以鴻臚卿致仕，復歸鎮州，結茅於別墅，自課兒孫耕牧為事。
entries.en: He later retired as Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, returned to Zhenzhou, built a thatched cottage on his estate, and taught his sons and grandsons to farm and herd.
entries.literal: Later he retired as Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, returned to Zhenzhou, built a thatched dwelling at his country estate, and set his sons and grandsons to farming and herding as their occupation.

entries.zh: 馥初累為鎮、冀屬邑令，所蒞有能政，性恬澹，與物無競，乃鎮州士人之秀者也。
entries.en: He had served repeatedly as magistrate in counties under Zhen and Ji, governing capably wherever he went; tranquil by nature and free of worldly striving, he was counted among the finest scholars of Zhenzhou.
