entries.literal: Fu had repeatedly served as magistrate of subordinate counties in Zhen and Ji; wherever he governed he showed capable administration; by nature he was tranquil and uncontentious, and he was among the finest gentlemen of Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 蕭希甫，宋州人也。
entries.en: Xiao Xifu came from Songzhou.
entries.literal: Xiao Xifu was a man of Songzhou.

entries.zh: 少舉進士，為梁開封尹袁象先書記。
entries.en: As a young man he passed the jinshi examination and became secretary to Yuan Xiangxian, prefect of Kaifeng under Liang.
entries.literal: In youth he took the jinshi examination and served as secretary to Yuan Xiangxian, Liang's prefect of Kaifeng.

entries.zh: 象先為青州節度使，以希甫為巡官，希甫不樂。
entries.en: When Xiangxian became military commissioner of Qingzhou he made Xifu a touring officer, a post Xifu disliked.
entries.literal: When Xiangxian became military commissioner of Qingzhou, he appointed Xifu as touring officer, but Xifu was displeased.

entries.zh: 乃棄其母妻，變姓名，亡之鎮州，自稱青州掌書記，進謁王鎔。
entries.en: He abandoned his mother and wife, changed his name, fled to Zhenzhou, presented himself to Wang Rong as chief secretary of Qingzhou, and sought an audience.
entries.literal: He then abandoned his mother and wife, changed his name, fled to Zhenzhou, called himself chief secretary of Qingzhou, and presented himself to Wang Rong.

entries.zh: 鎔以希甫為參軍，尤不樂，居歲餘，又亡之易州，削髮為僧，居百丈山。
entries.en: Rong appointed him a staff adjutant, which he liked even less; after a year he fled to Yizhou, took the tonsure, and lived as a monk on Mount Baizhang.
entries.literal: Rong made Xifu a staff adjutant, which pleased him even less; after more than a year he fled again to Yizhou, shaved his head, became a monk, and lived on Mount Baizhang.

entries.zh: 莊宗將建國，置百官，李紹宏薦為魏州推官。
entries.en: As Zhuangzong prepared to found his dynasty and fill the bureaucracy, Li Shaohong recommended him as investigating officer at Weizhou.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong was about to found the state and appoint the full bureaucracy, Li Shaohong recommended him as investigating officer of Weizhou.

entries.zh: 同光初，有詔定內宴儀，問希甫樞密使得坐否，希甫以為不可。
entries.en: Early in the Tongguang era, when court protocol for inner banquets was being set, he was asked whether the commissioner of military affairs should have a seat; Xifu said no.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Tongguang era an edict was issued to fix the protocol for inner banquets; Xifu was asked whether the commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs might be seated, and he said it was not permissible.

entries.zh: 樞密使張居翰聞之怒，謂希甫曰：「老夫曆事三朝天子，見內宴數百，子本田舍兒，安知宮禁事！」
entries.en: Commissioner Zhang Juhan flew into a rage: "I have served three emperors and attended hundreds of inner banquets—you're a country bumpkin; what do you know of palace protocol!"
entries.literal: The commissioner Zhang Juhan heard this and grew angry; he said to Xifu: "This old man has served three dynasties of Son of Heaven and witnessed hundreds of inner banquets—you, a rustic farm boy, what do you know of palace regulations!"

entries.zh: 希甫不能對。
entries.en: Xifu had no answer.
entries.literal: Xifu could not reply.

entries.zh: 初，莊宗欲以希甫知制誥，宰相豆盧革等附居翰，共排斥之，以為駕部郎中。
entries.en: Zhuangzong had wanted to make him a drafter of edicts, but Chief Ministers Doulu Ge and others, siding with Zhang Juhan, blocked him and gave him only a post as director in the Transport Department.
entries.literal: Earlier Zhuangzong had wished to make Xifu drafter of edicts; the chief ministers Dou Luge and others sided with Zhang Juhan and jointly pushed him aside, appointing him director in the Department of Transport.

entries.zh: 希甫失誌，尤怏怏。
entries.en: Frustrated in his ambitions, he grew especially bitter.
entries.literal: Xifu lost his ambition and was especially resentful.

entries.zh: 莊宗滅梁室，遣希甫宣慰青、齊，希甫始知其母已死，妻袁氏亦改嫁。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang he sent Xifu to console Qing and Qi; only then did he learn his mother was dead and his wife of the Yuan clan had remarried.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong destroyed the Liang house, he sent Xifu to announce consolation in Qing and Qi; only then did Xifu learn that his mother had died and that his wife, the Yuan clan, had remarried.

entries.zh: 希甫乃發哀服喪，居於魏州。
entries.en: He donned mourning and observed the rites while living at Weizhou.
entries.literal: Xifu then put on mourning garb and observed the funeral rites, residing at Weizhou.

entries.zh: 人有引漢李陵書以譏之曰：「老母終堂，生妻去室。」
entries.en: Someone mocked him with a line from Li Ling's letter to the Han: "His old mother died at home; his living wife abandoned their house."
entries.literal: Someone quoted Li Ling's letter from Han to mock him, saying: "An aged mother reached her end in the hall; a living wife left the chamber."

entries.zh: 天成初，欲召為諫議，豆盧革、韋說沮之。
entries.en: Early in the Tiancheng era he was to be recalled as remonstrating censor, but Dou Luge and Wei Shuo blocked the appointment.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Tiancheng era he was to be summoned as remonstrating censor, but Dou Luge and Wei Shuo obstructed it.

entries.zh: 明宗卒以希甫為諫議大夫，復為匭函使。
entries.en: Emperor Mingzong at last made him Remonstrating Grand Master and restored him as commissioner of the suggestion box.
entries.literal: Emperor Mingzong finally made Xifu Remonstrating Grand Master and again appointed him commissioner of the suggestion box.

entries.zh: 其後革、說為安重誨所惡，希甫希旨，誣奏革縱田客殺人，而說與鄰人爭井，井有寶貨。
entries.en: When Luge and Shuo later fell afoul of An Chonghui, Xifu curried favor with false charges that Luge had let tenant farmers commit murder and that Shuo had fought a neighbor over a treasure-filled well.
entries.literal: Later, when Luge and Shuo were hated by An Chonghui, Xifu curried favor and falsely memorialized that Luge had allowed his tenant farmers to kill people, and that Shuo had quarreled with a neighbor over a well said to contain treasure.

entries.zh: 有司推勘井中，惟破釜而已，革、說卒皆貶死。
entries.en: Officials searched the well and found only a broken pot; Luge and Shuo were demoted and died in exile.
entries.literal: The authorities investigated the well and found only a broken cauldron; Luge and Shuo were finally demoted and died in exile.

entries.zh: 希甫拜左散騎常侍，躁進尤甚，引告變人李筠夜扣內門，通變書云：「修堤兵士，欲取郊天日舉火為叛。」
entries.en: Promoted to Left Regular Attendant, he grew ever more reckless; he brought in an informer, Li Yun, who knocked at the inner gate by night with a report that "dike-repair soldiers meant to rebel by fire on the day of the suburban sacrifice."
entries.literal: Xifu was appointed Left Regular Attendant and grew ever more frantic in his advancement; he brought in an informer named Li Yun, who knocked on the inner gate at night and submitted a report of treason, saying: "Soldiers repairing the dikes plan to raise fire in rebellion on the day of the suburban sacrifice."

entries.zh: 安重誨不信之。
entries.en: An Chonghui did not believe him.
entries.literal: An Chonghui did not believe it.

entries.zh: 斬告變者，軍人訴屈，請希甫啖之。
entries.en: The informer was executed; the soldiers protested their wrong and clamored to have Xifu torn apart.
entries.literal: The informer was beheaded; the soldiers complained of injustice and asked that Xifu be eaten alive.

entries.zh: 既而詔曰：「左散騎常侍、集賢殿學士判院事蕭希甫，身處班行，職非警察，輒引凶狂之輩，上陳誣骫之詞，逼近郊禋，扇搖軍眾。
entries.en: An edict followed: "Xiao Xifu, Left Regular Attendant and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies—though he stands in court ranks, policing is not his charge—yet he introduced violent men and submitted deceitful charges, stirring the troops on the eve of the suburban sacrifice.
entries.literal: Soon an edict said: "Xiao Xifu, Left Regular Attendant and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the institute—though he stands in the court ranks, policing is not his office—yet he rashly introduced violent and reckless men and submitted deceitful and crooked words, approaching the suburban sacrifice and inciting the army masses.

entries.zh: 李筠既當誅戮，希甫寧免謫遷，可貶嵐州司戶參軍，仍馳驛發遣。」
entries.en: Li Yun was executed; Xifu could not escape demotion—to registrar of Lanzhou, dispatched at once by relay."
entries.literal: Since Li Yun deserved execution, how could Xifu escape demotion and exile? He is demoted to registrar of Lanzhou and is to be dispatched post-haste by relay."

entries.zh: 長興中，卒於貶所。
entries.en: He died in exile during the Changxing era.
entries.literal: During the Changxing era he died at his place of exile.

entries.zh: 張格，字承之，故宰相浚之子也。
entries.en: Zhang Ge, styled Chengzhi, was the son of the former chief minister Zhang Jun.
entries.literal: Zhang Ge, courtesy name Chengzhi, was the son of the former chief minister Jun.

entries.zh: 浚為梁祖所忌，潛遣人害於長水。
entries.en: Jun was hated by the Liang founder, who secretly had him killed at Changshui.
entries.literal: Jun was hated by the Liang founder, who secretly sent men to kill him at Changshui.

entries.zh: 格易姓名，流轉入蜀。
entries.en: Ge changed his name and made his way into Shu.
entries.literal: Ge changed his name and wandered into Shu.

entries.zh: 〈（《舊唐書·張浚傳》：永寧縣吏葉彥者，張氏待之素厚，告格曰：「相公之禍不可免，郎君宜自為計。」
entries.en: (The Old Book of Tang, biography of Zhang Jun: Ye Yan, a Yongning county clerk whom the Zhangs had long favored, told Ge, "Your father's doom cannot be avoided—you must save yourself."
entries.literal: (The Old Book of Tang, biography of Zhang Jun: Ye Yan, a clerk of Yongning County, whom the Zhang family had long treated well, told Ge: "The chief minister's disaster cannot be avoided—you, young master, should make your own plans."

entries.zh: 浚曰：「留則並命，去或可免，冀存後嗣。」
entries.en: Jun said, "If you stay we die together; if you go you may live—I hope our line survives."
entries.literal: Jun said: "If you stay we die together; if you go you may escape—I hope to preserve our descendants."

entries.zh: 格拜辭而去，葉彥率義士三十人送渡漢江而旋。
entries.en: Ge took his leave; Ye Yan led thirty volunteers to see him across the Han River and then turned back.
entries.literal: Ge bowed in farewell and left; Ye Yan led thirty righteous men to escort him across the Han River and then returned.

entries.zh: 格由荊江上峽入蜀。）〉
entries.en: Ge entered Shu through the Yangtze gorges.)〉
entries.literal: Ge entered Shu by way of the Jing River gorges.)〉

entries.zh: 王建僭號，以格為宰相。
entries.en: When Wang Jian declared himself emperor, he made Ge his chief minister.
entries.literal: When Wang Jian usurped the title, he made Ge chief minister.

entries.zh: 格所生母，當浚之遇害，潛匿於民間，落發為尼，流浪於函、洛。
entries.en: When Jun was killed, Ge's mother went into hiding among the people, took the tonsure, and wandered between the Hangu Pass and Luoyang.
entries.literal: Ge's birth mother, when Jun met his death, hid among the people, shaved her head and became a nun, and wandered between Hangu and Luoyang.

entries.zh: 王建聞之，潛使人迎之入蜀，賜紫，加號慈福大師。
entries.en: Wang Jian heard of it and secretly had her brought to Shu, granted her the purple robe, and gave her the title Great Master Cifu.
entries.literal: Wang Jian heard of this and secretly sent men to welcome her into Shu, granted her the purple robe, and gave her the title Great Master Cifu.

entries.zh: 及建卒，蜀人以格為山陵使，格有難色。
entries.en: When Jian died, Shu made Ge commissioner for the imperial tombs, and Ge looked uneasy.
entries.literal: When Jian died, the people of Shu appointed Ge commissioner for the imperial tombs, and Ge showed a troubled expression.

entries.zh: 未幾得罪，出為茂州刺史，偽製責詞云：「送往辭命，不忠也；
entries.en: Soon he fell from favor and was sent out as prefect of Maozhou; a forged reprimand charged, "Sent on an errand yet refusing the commission—disloyalty;
entries.literal: Before long he offended and was sent out as prefect of Maozhou; a forged reprimand read: "Sent off yet declining the commission—this is disloyalty;

entries.zh: 喪母匿喪，非孝也。」
entries.en: concealing his mother's death and hiding mourning—unfilial."
entries.literal: his mother's death concealed and mourning hidden—this is unfilial."

entries.zh: 王衍嗣偽位後數年，復用為宰相。
entries.en: Several years after Wang Yan took the throne, he was again made chief minister.
entries.literal: Several years after Wang Yan succeeded to the usurped throne, Ge was again employed as chief minister.

entries.zh: 同光末，蜀平，格至洛陽，
entries.en: When Shu fell at the end of Tongguang, Ge came to Luoyang,
entries.literal: At the end of the Tongguang era Shu was pacified, and Ge came to Luoyang,

entries.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》：任圜攜格還洛，格感葉彥之惠，訪之，身已歿，厚恤其家。
entries.en: (The Old Book of Tang: Ren Yuan brought Ge back to Luoyang; remembering Ye Yan's kindness, Ge sought him out, found him dead, and generously provided for his family.
entries.literal: (The Old Book of Tang: Ren Yuan brought Ge back to Luoyang; Ge, grateful for Ye Yan's kindness, sought him out, but he was already dead, and Ge generously provided for his family.

entries.zh: 又考張浚第三子仕吳，改名李儼，見《九國志》。）〉
entries.en: It also records that Zhang Jun's third son served Wu under the name Li Yan, as noted in the Jiuguo Zhi.)〉
entries.literal: It is also recorded that Zhang Jun's third son served Wu and changed his name to Li Yan, as seen in the Jiuguo Zhi.)〉

entries.zh: 授太子賓客。
entries.en: The court made him Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: He was appointed Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 任圜愛其才，奏為三司副使，尋卒於位。
entries.en: Ren Yuan admired his talent and had him made deputy commissioner of the Three Offices; he soon died in office.
entries.literal: Ren Yuan admired his talent and memorialized to make him deputy commissioner of the Three Offices; he soon died in office.

entries.zh: 格有文章，明吏事，時頗稱之。
entries.en: Ge was a capable writer and administrator, and his contemporaries spoke well of him.
entries.literal: Ge had literary talent and understood administrative affairs; his contemporaries spoke well of him.

entries.zh: 許寂，字閑閑。
entries.en: Xu Ji, styled Xianxian.
entries.literal: Xu Ji, courtesy name Xianxian.

entries.zh: 祖秘，名聞會稽。
entries.en: His grandfather Mi was renowned in Kuaiji.
entries.literal: His grandfather Mi was famed in Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 寂少有山水之好，泛覽經史，窮三式，尤明《易》象。
entries.en: From youth he loved landscape; he read widely in the classics and histories, mastered the Three Styles of divination, and was especially versed in the imagery of the Book of Changes.
entries.literal: Ji in youth loved mountains and waters; he read widely in the classics and histories, mastered the Three Styles, and was especially skilled in the imagery of the Changes.

entries.zh: 〈（《太平廣記》云：寂學《易》於晉徵君。）〉
entries.en: (The Taiping Guangji records that Ji studied the Changes under the Jin Recluse.)〉
entries.literal: (The Taiping Guangji says: Ji studied the Changes under the Jin Recluse.)〉

entries.zh: 久棲四明山，不幹時譽。
entries.en: He lived long on Mount Siming and shunned worldly renown.
entries.literal: He long dwelt on Mount Siming and did not seek the fame of the age.

entries.zh: 昭宗聞其名，征赴闕，召對於內殿。
entries.en: Emperor Zhaozong heard of him, summoned him to court, and received him in the inner hall.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhaozong heard his name and summoned him to court, calling him to audience in the inner hall.

entries.zh: 會昭宗方與伶人調品篳篥，事訖，方命坐賜果，問《易》義。
entries.en: Zhaozong happened to be tuning a pipe with his actor-favorites; when they finished, he had Ji seated, gave him fruit, and questioned him on the Changes.
entries.literal: It happened that Zhaozong was just tuning the pitch of the bili pipe with actor-favorites; when that was finished, he ordered Ji seated, granted fruit, and asked about the meaning of the Changes.

entries.zh: 既退，寂謂人曰：「君淫在聲，不在政矣。
entries.en: After leaving audience he told others, "The ruler's excess lies in music, not in government.
entries.literal: After he withdrew, Ji said to others: "The ruler's excess lies in sound, not in government.

entries.zh: 寂聞君人者，將昭德塞違，以臨照百官，百官或象之。
entries.en: He had heard that a ruler should display virtue and restrain wrongdoing to oversee his officials, and that officials would mirror him.
entries.literal: Ji had heard that a ruler should display virtue and block wrongdoing to oversee the hundred officials, and that the hundred officials would mirror him.

entries.zh: 今不厭賤事，自求其工，君道替矣。」
entries.en: Now he does not disdain petty tasks but pursues his own skill in them—the way of rulership is failing."
entries.literal: Now he does not disdain base tasks but seeks his own skill in them—the way of rulership is in decline."

entries.zh: 尋請還山，寓居於江陵，以茹芝絕粒，自適其性。
entries.en: He soon asked to return to the mountains, settled at Jiangling, lived on fungus and abstained from grain, and followed his own inclinations.
entries.literal: Soon he asked to return to the mountains, lodged at Jiangling, ate fungus and abstained from grain, and suited his own nature.

entries.zh: 天祐末，節度使趙匡凝昆季深禮遇之，師授保養之道。
entries.en: At the end of Tianyou the Zhao brothers, military commissioners of the region, honored him deeply and studied the arts of nurturing life under him.
entries.literal: At the end of the Tianyou era the military commissioners Zhao Kuangning and his brothers treated him with deep courtesy and learned from him the ways of nurturing life.

entries.zh: 唐末，除諫官，不起，漢南謂之徵君。
entries.en: Late in Tang he was offered a remonstrating post but declined; south of the Han they called him the Recluse.
entries.literal: At the end of Tang he was appointed remonstrating official but did not take office; south of the Han they called him the Recluse.

entries.zh: 梁攻襄陽，匡凝兄弟棄鎮奔蜀，寂偕行。
entries.en: When Liang attacked Xiangyang, the Kuangning brothers abandoned their post and fled to Shu, and Ji went with them.
entries.literal: When Liang attacked Xiangyang, the Kuangning brothers abandoned their command and fled to Shu, and Ji went with them.

entries.zh: 歲餘，蜀主王建待以師禮，位至蜀相。
entries.en: Within a year Wang Jian of Shu treated him as a teacher and raised him to chief minister.
entries.literal: After more than a year the Shu ruler Wang Jian treated him with the courtesy due a teacher, and he rose to chief minister of Shu.

entries.zh: 同光末，平蜀，與王衍俱從於東，授工部尚書致仕，卜居於洛。
entries.en: When Shu fell at the end of Tongguang he followed Wang Yan east, retired as Minister of Works, and settled at Luoyang.
entries.literal: At the end of Tongguang Shu was pacified; he followed Wang Yan east, was appointed Minister of Works and retired, and chose his dwelling at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 時寂已年高，精彩猶健，衝漠寡言，時蜀語云「可怪可怪」，人莫知其際。
entries.en: By then he was old, yet still vigorous and remote, saying little. In Shu they said "how strange, how strange," and no one knew what he meant.
entries.literal: By then Ji was advanced in years, yet his spirit was still vigorous; he was remote and sparing of speech. A saying in Shu ran "strange, strange," and no one knew what he meant.

entries.zh: 清泰三年六月卒，時年八十餘。
entries.en: He died in the sixth month of Qingtai 3, past eighty years old.
entries.literal: He died in the sixth month of the third year of Qingtai, at over eighty years of age.

entries.zh: 子孫位至省郎。
entries.en: His descendants rose to posts as Secretariat directors.
entries.literal: His descendants rose to Secretariat directors.

entries.zh: 張承業，字繼元，本姓康，同州人。
entries.en: Zhang Chengye, styled Jiyuan, was originally of the Kang clan and came from Tong Prefecture.
entries.literal: Zhang Chengye, styled Jiyuan, was originally surnamed Kang and was a native of Tong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 咸通中，內常侍張泰畜為假子。
entries.en: During the Xiantong era, the palace attendant Zhang Tai took him in as an adopted son.
entries.literal: During the Xiantong reign, Palace Attendant Zhang Tai raised him as an adopted son.

entries.zh: 光啟中，主郃陽軍事，賜紫，入為內供奉。
entries.en: In the Guangqi era he took charge of military affairs at Heyang, received the purple robe, and entered the palace as an inner attendant.
entries.literal: During the Guangqi reign, he was placed in charge of military affairs at Heyang, granted purple robes, and entered service as an inner palace attendant.

entries.zh: 武皇之討王行瑜，承業累奉使渭北，因留監武皇軍事，賊平，改酒坊使。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu marched against Wang Xingyu, Chengye was sent repeatedly as envoy to the country north of the Wei River and then stayed on to supervise the army. After the rebels were crushed, he was made Commissioner of the Wine Monopoly.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu campaigned against Wang Xingyu, Chengye repeatedly served as envoy north of the Wei River and was then left behind to supervise Emperor Wu's military affairs. After the rebels were pacified, he was reassigned as Commissioner of the Wine Monopoly.

entries.zh: 三年，昭宗將幸太原，以承業與武皇善，用除為河東監軍，密令迎駕。
entries.en: In the third year, as Emperor Zhaozong prepared to visit Taiyuan, Chengye—who was on good terms with Emperor Wu—was appointed Hedong army supervisor and secretly ordered to welcome the emperor.
entries.literal: In the third year, when Emperor Zhaozong was about to travel to Taiyuan, because Chengye was on good terms with Emperor Wu, he was appointed army supervisor of Hedong and secretly ordered to welcome the imperial carriage.

entries.zh: 既而昭宗幸華州，就加左監門衛將軍。
entries.en: Soon afterward Emperor Zhaozong went to Hua Prefecture, and Chengye was promoted on the spot to General of the Left Gate Guard.
entries.literal: Before long Emperor Zhaozong went to Hua Prefecture, and Chengye was promoted on the spot to General of the Left Gate Guard.

entries.zh: 駕在鳳翔，承業屢請出師晉、絳，以為岐人掎角。
entries.en: While the court was at Fengxiang, Chengye repeatedly urged sending troops from Jin and Jiang to pin down the Qi forces from the flank.
entries.literal: While the imperial carriage was at Fengxiang, Chengye repeatedly asked to march troops from Jin and Jiang so as to threaten the Qi forces from a flanking position.

entries.zh: 崔魏公之誅宦官也，武皇偽戮罪人首級以奉詔，匿承業於斛律寺，昭宗遇弑，乃復請為監軍。
entries.en: When Duke Cui moved against the eunuchs, Emperor Wu pretended to execute condemned criminals' heads to satisfy the edict and hid Chengye at Huli Temple. After Emperor Zhaozong was murdered, Chengye again asked to serve as army supervisor.
entries.literal: When Duke Cui executed the eunuchs, Emperor Wu feigned slaying the heads of condemned criminals to comply with the edict and hid Chengye at Huli Temple. After Emperor Zhaozong was assassinated, Chengye again requested to serve as army supervisor.

entries.zh: 夾城之役，遣承業求援於鳳翔。
entries.en: During the siege of Jiachcheng, Chengye was dispatched to Fengxiang to seek aid.
entries.literal: During the campaign at Jiachcheng, Chengye was sent to Fengxiang to seek reinforcements.

entries.zh: 時河中阻絕，自離石渡河，春冰方泮，淩澌奔蹙，艤舟不得渡，因禱河神。
entries.en: The route through Hezhong was cut off. He crossed from Lishi, but the spring ice was just breaking up; floes surged and piled together, and his boat could not reach the bank. He prayed to the River God.
entries.literal: The route through Hezhong was blocked. Crossing the river from Lishi, the spring ice had just begun to melt; floes surged and piled up, and the boat could not reach shore to cross, so he prayed to the River God.

entries.zh: 是夜，夢神人謂曰：「子但渡，流冰無患。」
entries.en: That night he dreamed a divine being say to him, "Just cross — the drifting ice will not harm you."
entries.literal: That night he dreamed a divine being say to him, "You have only to cross — the drifting ice will do you no harm."

entries.zh: 既寤，津吏報曰：「河冰合矣。」
entries.en: When he awoke, the ferry officer reported, "The river has frozen over."
entries.literal: When he awoke, the ferry officer reported, "The river ice has frozen solid."

entries.zh: 淩晨，躡冰而濟，旋踵冰解。
entries.en: At daybreak he crossed on the ice, and the moment he reached the far bank the ice broke up.
entries.literal: At daybreak he crossed on the ice; the instant he reached the other bank, the ice broke apart.

entries.zh: 使還，武皇病篤，啟手之夕，召承業屬之曰：「吾兒孤弱，群臣縱橫，後事公善籌之。」
entries.en: When he returned from the mission, Emperor Wu was dying. On the night of his death he summoned Chengye and said, "My son is young and weak, and the ministers are unruly. You must plan carefully for what comes next."
entries.literal: On his return from the mission, Emperor Wu was gravely ill. On the night he passed away, he summoned Chengye and entrusted him, saying, "My son is young and weak, and the ministers are unruly; you must take good thought for what follows."

entries.zh: 承業奉遺顧，爰立嗣王，平內難，策略居多。
entries.en: Chengye carried out the dying charge, established the heir as king, and quelled the internal crisis — in all of this, strategy was largely his work.
entries.literal: Chengye fulfilled the dying charge, established the heir as king, and pacified internal turmoil — in these matters strategic planning was largely his.

entries.zh: 既終易月之制，即請出師救潞，破賊夾城。
entries.en: When the one-month mourning period ended, he immediately asked to march out and relieve Lu, defeating the enemy at Jiachcheng.
entries.literal: Once the one-month mourning period was complete, he immediately asked to lead troops to rescue Lu and broke the enemy at Jiachcheng.

entries.zh: 莊宗深感其意，兄事之，親幸承業私第，升堂拜母，賜遺優厚。
entries.en: Zhuangzong was deeply moved and treated Chengye as an elder brother. He visited Chengye's home in person, entered the hall to bow to his mother, and gave him lavish gifts.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong was deeply moved by this devotion and treated Chengye as an elder brother. He personally visited Chengye's private residence, entered the hall to pay respects to his mother, and lavished generous gifts upon him.

entries.zh: 時莊宗初行墨製，凡除拜之命，皆成於盧汝弼之手。
entries.en: At that time Zhuangzong had just begun issuing appointments in his own hand, and every commission was drafted by Lu Rubi.
entries.literal: At that time Zhuangzong had just begun issuing orders in his own hand; every appointment and commission was drafted by Lu Rubi.

entries.zh: 汝弼既自為戶部侍郎，乃請與承業改官及開國邑，承業拒而不受。
entries.en: After Rubi had made himself Vice Minister of Revenue, he asked to have Chengye's title and noble domain changed. Chengye refused.
entries.literal: After Rubi had made himself Vice Minister of Revenue, he asked to have Chengye's office and noble domain changed; Chengye refused and would not accept.

entries.zh: 其後，但稱本朝舊官而已。
entries.en: After that he used only his original Tang title.
entries.literal: Thereafter he referred only to his original Tang title.

entries.zh: 柏鄉之役，王師既逼汴營，周德威慮其奔衝，堅請退舍。
entries.en: At Baixiang the royal army had already pressed the Bian camp. Zhou Dewei, fearing a sudden charge, strongly urged a withdrawal.
entries.literal: At the battle of Baixiang, the royal army had already pressed close to the Bian camp. Zhou Dewei, fearing a sudden charge, strongly urged falling back.

entries.zh: 莊宗怒其懦，不聽，垂帳而寢，諸將不敢言事，鹹詣監軍請白。
entries.en: Zhuangzong, angry at what he took for cowardice, refused to listen. He lowered his curtain and went to sleep. The generals dared not speak and all went to the army supervisor to ask him to intervene.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong, angered at what he saw as cowardice, would not listen. He lowered his curtain and went to sleep; the generals dared not speak up and all went to the army supervisor to ask him to intercede.

entries.zh: 承業遽至牙門，褰帳而入，撫莊宗曰：「此非王安寢時，周德威老將，洞識兵勢，姑務萬全，言不可忽。」
entries.en: Chengye hurried to headquarters, lifted the curtain, and went in. Placing a hand on Zhuangzong he said, "This is no time to sleep. Zhou Dewei is a veteran who knows the battlefield inside out. For now seek complete safety — do not ignore what he says."
entries.literal: Chengye hastened to the headquarters gate, lifted the curtain, and entered. Placing a hand on Zhuangzong he said, "This is no time for Your Highness to sleep. Zhou Dewei is a veteran general who thoroughly understands battlefield conditions; for the moment seek absolute safety — his words must not be ignored."

entries.zh: 莊宗蹶然而興曰：「予方思之。」
entries.en: Zhuangzong started up at once and said, "I was just thinking about that."
entries.literal: Zhuangzong started up suddenly and said, "I was just thinking about it."

entries.zh: 其夕，收軍保鄗邑。
entries.en: That evening he pulled the army back and held Haoyi.
entries.literal: That evening he drew the army back and held Haoyi.

entries.zh: 德威討劉守光，令承業往視賊勢，因請莊宗自行，果成大捷。
entries.en: When Dewei marched against Liu Shouguang, he sent Chengye to scout the enemy and urged Zhuangzong to take command in person. The result was a great victory.
entries.literal: When Dewei marched against Liu Shouguang, he sent Chengye to observe the enemy's strength and urged Zhuangzong to take the field himself; the result was a great victory.

entries.zh: 承業感武皇厚遇，自莊宗在魏州垂十年，太原軍國政事，一委承業；
entries.en: Grateful for Emperor Wu's generous treatment, and with Zhuangzong at Weizhou for nearly ten years, all military and civil affairs at Taiyuan were entrusted entirely to Chengye;
entries.literal: Grateful for Emperor Wu's generous treatment of him, and with Zhuangzong at Weizhou for nearly ten years, all military and civil affairs of Taiyuan were entrusted solely to Chengye;

entries.zh: 而積聚庾帑，收兵市馬，招懷流散，勸課農桑，成是霸基者，承業之忠力也。
entries.en: It was Chengye's loyal exertions that stockpiled grain, gathered troops and bought horses, brought back the displaced, and encouraged farming — all of which built the foundation of hegemony.
entries.literal: It was through Chengye's loyal exertions that grain was stockpiled, troops gathered and horses purchased, displaced people brought back, and agriculture encouraged — all of which built the foundation of hegemony.

entries.zh: 時貞簡太后，韓德妃、伊淑妃、諸宅王之貴，洎王之介弟在晉陽宮，或不以其道幹於承業，悉不聽，逾法禁者必懲，由是貴戚斂手，民俗丕變。
entries.en: At that time the Empress Dowager Zhenjian, the consorts Han Defei and Yi Shufei, the household princes, and the king's younger brothers at the Jinyang palace — some tried to influence Chengye by improper means, but he refused them all and punished anyone who broke the law. The imperial kin held back, and popular customs changed greatly.
entries.literal: At that time the Empress Dowager Zhenjian, the honored consorts Han Defei and Yi Shufei, the various princes of the household, and the king's younger brothers who lived in the Jinyang palace — some tried to influence Chengye by improper means, but he refused them all; anyone who exceeded the legal prohibitions was punished. Thereupon the imperial kin held back their hands, and popular customs changed greatly.

entries.zh: 或有中傷承業於莊宗者，言專弄威柄，廣納賂遺。
entries.en: Some slandered Chengye to Zhuangzong, saying he wielded power alone and accepted bribes on a wide scale.
entries.literal: Some slandered Chengye to Zhuangzong, saying he monopolized power and widely accepted bribes.

entries.zh: 莊宗歲時還晉陽宮省太后，須錢蒱博、給伶官，嘗置酒於泉府，莊宗酣飲，命興聖宮使李繼岌為承業起舞，既竟，承業出寶帶幣馬奉之。
entries.en: Each year when Zhuangzong returned to the Jinyang palace to visit the empress dowager, he needed money for gambling and to pay the entertainers. Once he held a feast at the treasury. Zhuangzong drank heavily and ordered Li Jiya, commissioner of the Xingsheng Palace, to dance for Chengye. When the dance was done, Chengye presented a precious belt, coins, and a horse as gifts.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong returned to the Jinyang palace each year to visit the empress dowager, he needed money for gambling and to pay the entertainers. Once he held a feast at the treasury office. Zhuangzong drank deeply and ordered Li Jiya, commissioner of the Xingsheng Palace, to dance for Chengye; when it was done, Chengye produced a precious belt, coins, and a horse as gifts.

entries.zh: 莊宗指錢積謂承業曰：「和哥無錢使，七哥與此一積，寶馬非殊惠也。」
entries.en: Zhuangzong pointed to a pile of money and said to Chengye, "Hege has no spending money — Seventh Elder Brother, give him this pile. The fine horse is no special favor."
entries.literal: Zhuangzong pointed to a pile of money and said to Chengye, "Hege has no money to spend — Seventh Elder Brother, give him this pile. The fine horse is no extraordinary favor."

entries.zh: 承業謝曰：「郎君哥勞，承業自出己俸錢。
entries.en: Chengye declined, saying, "For the young lord's service, Chengye will pay from his own salary.
entries.literal: Chengye declined, saying, "The young lord's labors — Chengye will pay from his own salary.

entries.zh: 此錢是大王庫物，準擬支贍三軍，不敢以公物為私禮也。」
entries.en: This money belongs to the Great King's treasury and is earmarked to supply the three armies. I dare not use public funds as a private gift."
entries.literal: This money belongs to the Great King's treasury, earmarked to supply the three armies. I dare not use public goods as a private gift."

entries.zh: 莊宗不悅，使酒侵承業。
entries.en: Zhuangzong was displeased and, drunk, insulted Chengye.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong was displeased and, in his cups, insulted Chengye.

entries.zh: 承業曰：「臣老敕使。
entries.en: Chengye said, "Your servant is an old imperial envoy.
entries.literal: Chengye said, "Your servant is an old imperial envoy.

entries.zh: 非為子孫之謀，惜錢為大王基業，王若自要散施，何妨老夫，不過財盡兵散，一事無成。」
entries.en: I am not hoarding it for my descendants — I am hoarding it for the Great King's foundation. If Your Highness insists on giving it away, what can an old man do? Nothing more than exhaust the treasury, scatter the troops, and achieve nothing."
entries.literal: It is not for my descendants' sake that I spare this money — I spare it for the Great King's foundation. If Your Highness insists on giving it away, what harm can an old man do? Nothing more than that wealth will be exhausted, troops dispersed, and nothing achieved."

entries.zh: 〈（案：《通鑒》作王自取用之，何問仆為！）〉
entries.en: (Note: The Zizhi Tongjian has: "The king may take and use it himself — why ask your servant!")〉
entries.literal: (Note: The Zizhi Tongjian reads: "The king may take and use it himself — why ask your servant!")〉

entries.zh: 莊宗怒，顧元行欽曰：「取劍來！」
entries.en: Zhuangzong flew into a rage and turned to Yuan Xingqin, saying, "Bring a sword!"
entries.literal: Zhuangzong flew into a rage and turned to Yuan Xingqin, saying, "Bring a sword!"

entries.zh: 承業引莊宗衣，泣而言曰：「仆荷先王遺顧，誓為本朝誅汴賊，為王惜庫物，斬承業首，死亦無愧於先王，今日請死！」
entries.en: Chengye seized Zhuangzong's robe and said through tears, "Your servant received the late king's dying charge and swore to destroy the Bian rebels for the dynasty and to guard the treasury for the king. Cut off Chengye's head and I will die without shame before the late king — I ask to die today!"
entries.literal: Chengye seized Zhuangzong's robe and said through tears, "Your servant received the late king's dying charge and swore to exterminate the Bian rebels for the dynasty and to husband the treasury stores for the king. If you cut off Chengye's head, I will die without shame before the late king — I ask to die today!"

entries.zh: 閻寶解承業手，令退。
entries.en: Yan Bao loosened Chengye's grip and made him withdraw.
entries.literal: Yan Bao loosened Chengye's grip and had him withdraw.

entries.zh: 承業詬寶曰：「黨朱溫逆賊，未嘗有一言效忠，而敢依阿諂附。」
entries.en: Chengye reviled Bao, saying, "You sided with the rebel Zhu Wen and never once spoke a word of loyalty — yet you dare fawn and flatter."
entries.literal: Chengye reviled Bao, saying, "You sided with the rebel Zhu Wen and never once spoke a word of loyalty — yet you dare fawn and flatter."

entries.zh: 揮拳踣之。
entries.en: He swung his fist and knocked him down.
entries.literal: He swung his fist and knocked him down.

entries.zh: 太后聞莊宗酒失，急召入。
entries.en: The empress dowager, hearing of Zhuangzong's drunken outburst, urgently summoned him.
entries.literal: The empress dowager, hearing of Zhuangzong's drunken offense, urgently summoned him in.

entries.zh: 莊宗性至孝，聞太后召，叩頭謝阿業曰：「吾杯酒之間，忤於七哥，太后必怪吾。
entries.en: Zhuangzong was deeply filial. Hearing the empress dowager's summons, he kowtowed and apologized to Aye: "Over a few cups of wine I offended Seventh Elder Brother — the empress dowager is sure to blame me.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong was exceedingly filial; hearing the empress dowager's summons, he kowtowed and apologized to Aye: "Between a few cups of wine I offended Seventh Elder Brother — the empress dowager is sure to blame me.

entries.zh: 七哥為痛飲兩卮分謗，可乎？」
entries.en: Seventh Elder Brother, will you drink two cups in earnest to share the blame?"
entries.literal: Seventh Elder Brother, will you drink two cups in earnest to share the blame?"

entries.zh: 莊宗連飲四鍾，勸承業，竟不飲。
entries.en: Zhuangzong drank four cups in a row and urged Chengye to drink, but Chengye would not.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong drank four cups in succession and urged Chengye to drink, but he would not.

entries.zh: 莊宗歸宮，太后使人謂承業曰：「小兒忤特進，已笞矣，可歸第。」
entries.en: When Zhuangzong returned to the palace, the empress dowager sent word to Chengye: "The boy offended the Special Advancement and has already been flogged. You may go home."
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong returned to the palace, the empress dowager sent someone to tell Chengye, "The boy offended the Special Advancement — he has already been flogged. You may return home."

entries.zh: 翌日，太后與莊宗俱幸其第，慰勞之。
entries.en: The next day the empress dowager and Zhuangzong both visited his home to comfort him.
entries.literal: The next day the empress dowager and Zhuangzong both visited his residence to comfort him.

entries.zh: 自是私謁幾絕。
entries.en: From then on private visits nearly ceased.
entries.literal: From then on private audiences nearly ceased.

entries.zh: 十八年，莊宗受諸道勸進，將纂帝位。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year the various circuits urged Zhuangzong to take the throne, and he was about to claim the imperial title.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year the various circuits urged Zhuangzong to ascend, and he was about to seize the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 承業以為晉王三代有功於國，先人怒朱氏弑逆，將復舊邦，讎既未平，不宜輕受推戴。
entries.en: Chengye held that the Prince of Jin's house had served the state with merit across three generations and that his forebears, angered by the Zhu family's usurpation, meant to restore the old realm. With the enemy not yet subdued, one ought not lightly accept elevation.
entries.literal: Chengye held that the Prince of Jin's house had served the state with merit across three generations; his forebears, angered by the Zhu family's usurpation, meant to restore the old realm. With the enemy not yet subdued, one ought not lightly accept elevation.

entries.zh: 方疾作，肩輿之鄴宮，見莊宗曰：「王父子血戰三十餘年，蓋言報國仇讎，復唐宗社。
entries.en: Though he was ill, he was carried in a litter to the palace at Ye, where he saw Zhuangzong and said, "Your Highness and your father have fought in blood for more than thirty years — all to avenge the state's enemy and restore the Tang imperial altar.
entries.literal: Though he was ill, he was carried in a litter to the palace at Ye, where he saw Zhuangzong and said, "Your Highness and your father have fought in blood for more than thirty years — all to speak of avenging the state's enemy and restoring the Tang imperial altar.

entries.zh: 今元凶未滅，民賦已殫，而遽先大號，蠹耗財力，臣以為不可一也。
entries.en: The chief culprit is not yet destroyed and the people's taxes are already exhausted, yet you would hastily assume the great title and squander resources. Your servant holds this inadvisable — first point.
entries.literal: The chief culprit is not yet destroyed, and the people's taxes are already exhausted — yet you would hastily assume the great title first, squandering resources. Your servant holds this inadvisable — first point.

entries.zh: 臣自咸通已來，伏事宮掖，每見國家冊命大禮，儀仗法物，百司庶務，經年草定，臨事猶有不可。
entries.en: Your servant has served the palace since the Xiantong era and has seen every grand state investiture — regalia, ritual objects, and the myriad duties of the hundred offices, drafted over years — and even then flaws remain.
entries.literal: Your servant has served the palace since the Xiantong reign and has seen every grand state investiture — regalia, ritual objects, and the myriad duties of the hundred offices, drafted over years — and even at the event there are still flaws.

entries.zh: 王若化家為國，新立廟朝，不可乖於制度。
entries.en: If Your Highness transforms a household into a state and newly establishes ancestral temples and courts, you must not depart from established codes.
entries.literal: If Your Highness transforms a household into a state and newly establishes ancestral temples and courts, you must not deviate from the established codes.

entries.zh: 制禮作樂，未見其人，臣以為不可二也。
entries.en: To establish rites and compose music — no suitable person has yet appeared. Your servant holds this inadvisable — second point.
entries.literal: To establish rites and compose music — no suitable person has yet appeared. Your servant holds this inadvisable — second point.

entries.zh: 舉事量力而行，不可信於遊譚也。」
entries.en: Undertake affairs according to what your strength allows; do not trust in idle talk."
entries.literal: Undertake affairs according to what your strength allows; do not trust in idle talk."

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒考異》引秦再思《洛中記異》云：承業諫帝曰：「大王何不待誅克梁孽，更平吳、蜀，俾天下一家，且先求唐氏子孫立之，後更以天下讓有功者，何人輒敢當之！
entries.en: (The 《Examination of Discrepancies in the Zizhi Tongjian》 cites Qin Zaisi's 《Records of Strange Events in Luoyang》: Chengye remonstrated with the emperor, saying, "Why does Your Highness not wait until the Liang rebels are destroyed and Wu and Shu are pacified, so that the realm becomes one family? First find a descendant of the Tang house and install him, then later yield the realm to the man of merit — who would dare take it!
entries.literal: (The 《Examination of Discrepancies in the Zizhi Tongjian》 cites Qin Zaisi's 《Records of Strange Events in Luoyang》: Chengye remonstrated with the emperor, saying, "Why does Your Highness not wait until the Liang rebels are destroyed and Wu and Shu are pacified, so that the realm becomes one family? First seek out a descendant of the Tang house and install him, then later yield the realm to the man of merit — who would dare take it!

entries.zh: 讓一月即一月牢，讓一年即一年牢。
entries.en: Yield for one month and it holds firm for one month; yield for one year and it holds firm for one year.
entries.literal: Yield for one month and it holds firm for one month; yield for one year and it holds firm for one year.

entries.zh: 設使高祖再生，太宗復出，又胡為哉！
entries.en: Even if Gaozu were reborn and Taizong reappeared, what could they do!
entries.literal: Even if Gaozu were reborn and Taizong reappeared, what could they do!

entries.zh: 今大王一旦自立，頓失從前仗義征伐之旨，人情怠矣。
entries.en: If Your Highness now proclaims yourself sovereign in a single stroke, you will at once lose the righteous purpose that has guided these campaigns, and men's hearts will slacken.
entries.literal: If Your Highness now proclaims yourself sovereign in a single stroke, you will at once lose the righteous purpose that has guided these campaigns, and men's hearts will slacken.

entries.zh: 老夫是閹官，不愛大王官職富貴，直以受先王付屬之重，欲為大王立萬年之基爾。」）〉
entries.en: I am an old eunuch — I care nothing for Your Highness's offices and riches. I speak only because I bore the late king's heavy charge and wish to lay a foundation that will endure ten thousand years.")〉
entries.literal: I am an old eunuch — I care nothing for Your Highness's offices and riches; I speak only because I bore the late king's heavy charge and wish to lay a foundation that will endure ten thousand years.")〉

entries.zh: 莊宗曰：「奈諸將何？」
entries.en: Zhuangzong said, "What am I to do about the generals?"
entries.literal: Zhuangzong said, "What am I to do about the generals?"

entries.zh: 承業知莊宗不從，因號泣而言之。
entries.en: Chengye knew Zhuangzong would not follow his advice and spoke while weeping aloud.
entries.literal: Chengye knew Zhuangzong would not follow his advice and spoke while weeping aloud.

entries.zh: 十九年十一月二日，以疾卒於晉陽之第，時年七十七。
entries.en: On the second day of the eleventh month of the nineteenth year he died of illness at his residence in Jinyang, aged seventy-seven.
entries.literal: On the second day of the eleventh month of the nineteenth year he died of illness at his residence in Jinyang, aged seventy-seven.

entries.zh: 貞簡太后聞喪，遽至其第盡哀，為之行服，如兒侄禮。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Zhenjian, hearing of his death, hurried to his residence to mourn fully, donned mourning garments, and observed the rites as a son or nephew would.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Zhenjian, hearing of his death, hurried to his residence to mourn fully, donned mourning garments, and observed the rites as a son or nephew would.

entries.zh: 同光初，贈左武衛上將軍，諡曰貞憲。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tongguang he was posthumously granted General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard and given the posthumous name Zhenxian.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was posthumously granted General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard and given the posthumous name Zhenxian.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代史闕文》：莊宗將即位於魏州，承業自太原至，謂莊宗曰：「吾王世奉唐家，最為忠孝，自貞觀以來，王室有難，未嘗不從。
entries.en: From the 《Lost Writings on the History of the Five Dynasties》: When Zhuangzong was about to take the throne at Weizhou, Chengye came from Taiyuan and said to Zhuangzong, "Our princely house has served the Tang with utmost loyalty and filial piety. Since the Zhenguan era, whenever the royal house faced crisis, we have never failed to respond.
entries.literal: (From the 《Lost Writings on the History of the Five Dynasties》: When Zhuangzong was about to ascend the throne at Weizhou, Chengye came from Taiyuan and said to Zhuangzong, "Our princely house has served the Tang with utmost loyalty and filial piety. Since the Zhenguan reign, whenever the royal house faced crisis, we have never failed to respond.

entries.zh: 所以老奴三十餘年為吾王捃拾財賦、召補軍馬者，誓滅逆賊朱溫，復本朝宗社耳。
entries.en: That is why this old slave for more than thirty years has gathered revenue and recruited troops and horses for our prince — swearing to destroy the rebel Zhu Wen and restore our dynasty's imperial altar.
entries.literal: That is why this old slave for more than thirty years has gathered revenue and recruited troops and horses for our prince — swearing to destroy the rebel Zhu Wen and restore our dynasty's imperial altar.

entries.zh: 今河朔甫定，朱氏尚存，吾王遽即大位，可乎？」
entries.en: Now the Hebei region has just been pacified and the Zhu clan still survives — can our prince hastily assume the throne?"
entries.literal: Now the Hebei region has just been pacified and the Zhu clan still survives — can our prince hastily assume the great position?"

entries.zh: 云云。
entries.en: And so on.
entries.literal: And so on.

entries.zh: 莊宗曰：「奈諸將意何！」
entries.en: Zhuangzong said, "What of the generals' wishes!"
entries.literal: Zhuangzong said, "What of the generals' wishes!"

entries.zh: 承業知不可諫止，乃慟哭曰：「諸侯血戰者，本為李家，今吾王自取之，誤老奴矣！」
entries.en: Chengye knew he could not dissuade him and wailed, "The feudal lords fought in blood for the Li family — now our prince takes it for himself. You have misled this old slave!"
entries.literal: Chengye knew he could not dissuade him and wailed, "The feudal lords fought in blood for the Li family — now our prince takes it for himself. You have misled this old slave!"

entries.zh: 即歸太原，不食而死。
entries.en: He returned to Taiyuan and died by fasting.
entries.literal: He returned to Taiyuan and died by fasting.

entries.zh: 臣謹按：《莊宗實錄》敘承業諫即位事甚詳，惟「吾王自取」之言不書，史官諱之也。）〉
entries.en: Your servant respectfully notes: The 《Veritable Records of Zhuangzong》 narrates Chengye's remonstrance against enthronement in great detail but does not record the words "our prince takes it for himself" — the historiographers suppressed it.)〉
entries.literal: Your servant respectfully notes: The 《Veritable Records of Zhuangzong》 narrates Chengye's remonstrance against enthronement in great detail, but does not record the words "our prince takes it for himself" — the historiographers suppressed it.)〉

entries.zh: 張居翰，字德卿。
entries.en: Zhang Juhan, styled Deqing.
entries.literal: Zhang Juhan, styled Deqing.

entries.zh: 咸通初，掖庭令張從玫養之為子，以蔭入仕。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Xiantong era, the palace ward director Zhang Congmei raised him as a son, and he entered office by inherited privilege.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Xiantong reign, Palace Ward Director Zhang Congmei raised him as a son, and he entered office by inherited privilege.

entries.zh: 中和三年，自容管監軍判官入為學士院判官，遷樞密承旨、內府令，賜緋。
entries.en: In the third year of Zhonghe, from adjutant to the army supervisor of Rongguan he entered service as Hanlin Academy adjutant, was promoted to Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Director of the Inner Palace, and was granted scarlet robes.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhonghe, from adjutant to the army supervisor of Rongguan he entered service as adjutant to the Hanlin Academy, was promoted to Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Director of the Inner Palace, and was granted scarlet robes.

entries.zh: 昭宗在華下，超授內常侍，出監幽州軍事，秩滿詔歸，節度使劉仁恭表留之。
entries.en: While Emperor Zhaozong was at Hua, Juhan was promoted out of turn to palace attendant and sent to supervise military affairs at Youzhou. When his term expired an edict ordered his return, but military commissioner Liu Rengong memorialized to retain him.
entries.literal: While Emperor Zhaozong was below Hua, Juhan was promoted out of turn to Palace Attendant, sent out to supervise military affairs at You Prefecture, and when his term expired an edict ordered his return — but military commissioner Liu Rengong memorialized to retain him.

entries.zh: 天復中，詔誅宦官，仁恭紿奏殺之，匿於大安山之北溪。
entries.en: During the Tianfu era, an edict ordered the execution of eunuchs. Rengong falsely reported that he had killed Juhan and hid him in a northern stream valley of Mount Da'an.
entries.literal: During the Tianfu reign, an edict ordered the execution of eunuchs. Rengong falsely reported that he had killed Juhan and hid him in a northern stream valley of Mount Da'an.

entries.zh: 天祐三年，汴人攻滄州，仁恭求援於武皇，乃遣居翰與書記馬鬱等率兵助武皇同攻潞州，武皇因留之不遣。
entries.en: In the third year of Tianyou, when the Bian army attacked Cangzhou, Rengong sought aid from Emperor Wu and sent Juhan with secretary Ma Yu and others to lead troops to help Emperor Wu jointly attack Luzhou. Emperor Wu then retained Juhan and would not send him back.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianyou, when the Bian army attacked Cang Prefecture, Rengong sought aid from Emperor Wu and sent Juhan with secretary Ma Yu and others to lead troops to help Emperor Wu jointly attack Lu Prefecture. Emperor Wu then retained Juhan and would not send him back.

entries.zh: 李嗣昭節制昭義，以居翰監其軍，以燕軍三千為部下。
entries.en: Li Siyao commanded Zhaoyi Circuit and made Juhan supervisor of his army, with three thousand Yan troops under his command.
entries.literal: Li Siyao commanded Zhaoyi Circuit and made Juhan supervisor of his army, with three thousand Yan troops as his command.

entries.zh: 俄而汴將李思安築夾城以圍潞州，居翰與嗣昭登城保守，以至解圍。
entries.en: Before long the Bian general Li Si'an built Jiachcheng to besiege Luzhou. Juhan and Siyao mounted the walls to hold firm until the siege was lifted.
entries.literal: Before long the Bian general Li Si'an built Jiachcheng to besiege Lu Prefecture. Juhan and Siyao mounted the walls to hold firm until the siege was lifted.

entries.zh: 自是嗣昭每出征，令居翰知留後事。
entries.en: From then on, whenever Siyao marched out, he left Juhan in charge of rear affairs.
entries.literal: From then on, whenever Siyao marched out, he left Juhan in charge of rear affairs.

entries.zh: 同光元年夏四月，召為樞密使，加特進，與郭崇韜對掌機務。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer in the first year of Tongguang he was summoned as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, granted Special Advancement, and shared control of state affairs with Guo Chongtao.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the first year of Tongguang he was summoned as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, granted Special Advancement, and shared control of state affairs with Guo Chongtao.

entries.zh: 十月，莊宗將渡河，留居翰與李紹宏同守魏州。
entries.en: In the tenth month, as Zhuangzong prepared to cross the river, he left Juhan and Li Shaohong to hold Weizhou together.
entries.literal: In the tenth month, as Zhuangzong was about to cross the river, he left Juhan and Li Shaohong together to hold Weizhou.

entries.zh: 莊宗入汴，加驃騎大將軍，知內侍省事，依前充樞密使。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Juhan was promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, made Director of Palace Affairs, and continued as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Juhan was promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, made Director of Palace Affairs, and continued as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 同光時，宦官幹政，邦家之務皆出於郭崇韜。
entries.en: During the Tongguang era, eunuchs meddled in government, but state affairs all issued from Guo Chongtao.
entries.literal: During Tongguang, eunuchs meddled in government, but state affairs all issued from Guo Chongtao.

entries.zh: 居翰自以羈旅乘時，擢居重地，每於宣授，不敢有所是非，承顏免過而已，以此脫季年之禍。
entries.en: Juhan saw himself as an outsider who had seized the moment to rise to high office. At every appointment he dared express no opinion, merely deferring to the ruler's mood to avoid blame — and by this escaped disaster in his later years.
entries.literal: Juhan considered himself a wanderer who had seized the moment to rise to a weighty post; at every appointment announcement he dared express no approval or disapproval, merely accepting the ruler's countenance to avoid fault — and by this escaped disaster in his later years.

entries.zh: 四年三月，偽蜀王衍既降，詔遷其族於洛陽。
entries.en: In the third month of the fourth year, after the Shu ruler Wang Yan had surrendered, an edict ordered his clan relocated to Luoyang.
entries.literal: In the third month of the fourth year, after the false Shu king Wang Yan had surrendered, an edict ordered his clan relocated to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 行及秦川，時關東已亂，莊宗慮衍為變，遣中官向延嗣馳騎齎詔殺之。
entries.en: When they reached Qinchuan, the region east of the pass was already in turmoil. Zhuangzong feared Yan might stir up trouble and sent the palace eunuch Xiang Yansi galloping with an edict to kill him.
entries.literal: When they reached Qinchuan, the east of the pass was already in turmoil. Zhuangzong feared Yan might stir up trouble and sent the palace eunuch Xiang Yansi galloping with an edict to kill him.

entries.zh: 詔云：「王衍一行，並宜殺戮。」
entries.en: The edict read, "Wang Yan's entire party should be put to death."
entries.literal: The edict read: "Wang Yan's entire party should be put to death."

entries.zh: 其詔已經印畫，時居翰在密地，覆視其詔，即就殿柱揩云「行」字，改書「家」字。
entries.en: The edict had already been sealed and signed. Juhan was in a private room; he looked the edict over again, went to a hall pillar, erased the character for "party," and changed it to the character for "family."
entries.literal: The edict had already been sealed and signed. Juhan was then in a private room; he looked the edict over again, went to a hall pillar, erased the character for "party," and changed it to the character for "family."

entries.zh: 及衍就戮於秦川驛，止族其近屬而已，其偽官及從行者尚千餘人，皆免其枉濫，居翰之力也。
entries.en: When Yan was executed at the Qinchuan post station, only his close kin were killed. More than a thousand former Shu officials and attendants who accompanied him were all spared from wrongful slaughter — this was Juhan's doing.
entries.literal: When Yan was executed at the Qinchuan post station, only his close kin were killed. More than a thousand former Shu officials and attendants who accompanied him were all spared from wrongful slaughter — this was Juhan's doing.

entries.zh: 明宗入洛，居翰謁見於至德宮，待罪雪涕，乞歸田里，詔許之，乃辭歸長安。
entries.en: When Mingzong entered Luoyang, Juhan had an audience at the Zhide Palace, confessed his faults in tears, and begged to return home. An edict granted this, and he took leave to return to Chang'an.
entries.literal: When Mingzong entered Luoyang, Juhan had an audience at the Zhide Palace, confessed his faults with tears, and begged to return to his home district. An edict granted this, and he took leave to return to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 仍以其子延貴為西京職事，以供侍養。
entries.en: His son Yangui was also given a post in the Western Capital to support and care for him.
entries.literal: His son Yangui was also given a post in the Western Capital to support and serve him.

entries.zh: 天成三年四月，以疾卒於長安，時年七十一。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the third year of Tiancheng he died of illness at Chang'an, aged seventy-one.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Tiancheng he died of illness at Chang'an, aged seventy-one.

entries.zh: 居翰性和而靜，諳悉舊事。
entries.en: Juhan was gentle and quiet by nature and well versed in old precedents.
entries.literal: Juhan's nature was gentle and quiet, and he was well versed in old precedents.

entries.zh: 在潞州累年，每春課人育蔬種樹，敦本惠農，有仁者之心焉。
entries.en: During his many years at Luzhou, every spring he set people to raising vegetables and planting trees, encouraging agriculture and benefiting farmers — he had the heart of a benevolent man.
entries.literal: During his many years at Lu Prefecture, every spring he set people to raising vegetables and planting trees, encouraging the fundamentals and benefiting farmers — he had the heart of a benevolent man.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：承業感武皇之大惠，佐莊宗之中興，既義且忠，何以階也。
entries.en: The historiographer says: Chengye, grateful for Emperor Wu's great kindness, assisted Zhuangzong's restoration — righteous and loyal. To what rank could such a man be compared?
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Chengye, grateful for Emperor Wu's great kindness, assisted Zhuangzong's restoration — righteous and loyal; to what rank could such a man be compared?

entries.zh: 夫如是，則晉之勃貂，秦之景監，去之遠矣。
entries.en: If so, then Bo Diao of Jin and Jing Jian of Qin stand far removed from him.
entries.literal: If so, then Bo Diao of Jin and Jing Jian of Qin stand far removed from him.

entries.zh: 居翰改一字於詔書，救千人之濫死，可不謂之仁人矣乎！
entries.en: Juhan changed one character in an edict and saved a thousand people from wrongful death — can he not be called a man of benevolence!
entries.literal: Juhan changed one character in an edict and saved a thousand people from wrongful death — can he not be called a man of benevolence!

entries.zh: 如紹宏之爭權，漢瓊之構禍，乃宦者之常態也，又何足以道哉！
entries.en: As for Shaohong's struggle for power and Hanqiong's sowing of disaster — these are the usual ways of eunuchs. What is there worth mentioning!
entries.literal: As for Shaohong's struggle for power and Hanqiong's sowing of disaster — these are the usual ways of eunuchs; what is there worth mentioning!

entries.zh: 孟漢瓊，本鎮州王鎔之小豎也。
entries.en: Meng Hanqiong was originally a young attendant of Wang Rong of Zhenzhou.
entries.literal: Meng Hanqiong was originally a young attendant of Wang Rong of Zhen Prefecture.

entries.zh: 明宗鎮常山，得侍左右。
entries.en: When Mingzong governed Changshan, Hanqiong came to serve at his side.
entries.literal: When Mingzong governed Changshan, Hanqiong came to serve at his side.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，自諸司使累遷宣徽南院使。
entries.en: When Mingzong ascended the throne, Hanqiong rose in succession from various bureau commissioner posts to Commissioner of the Southern Court of the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: When Mingzong ascended the throne, Hanqiong rose in succession from various bureau commissioner posts to Commissioner of the Southern Court of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 漢瓊性通黠，善交構。
entries.en: Hanqiong was clever and shrewd by nature and skilled at intrigue.
entries.literal: Hanqiong was clever and shrewd by nature and skilled at intrigue.

entries.zh: 初見秦王權重，及挾王淑妃勢，傾心事之；
entries.en: At first, seeing the Prince of Qin's great power and the backing of Consort Wang Shufei, he devoted himself wholeheartedly to serving him;
entries.literal: At first, seeing the Prince of Qin's great power and the backing of Consort Wang Shufei, he devoted himself wholeheartedly to serving him;

entries.zh: 及朱、馮用事，又與之締結。
entries.en: when Zhu and Feng came to power, he allied with them as well.
entries.literal: when Zhu and Feng came to power, he allied with them as well.

entries.zh: 秦王領兵至天津橋，時漢瓊與朱、馮及康義誠方會議於內庭，謀猶未決，漢瓊獨出死力，先入殿門，奏於明宗，語在《秦王傳》。
entries.en: When the Prince of Qin led troops to the Tianjin Bridge, Hanqiong was meeting with Zhu, Feng, and Kang Yicheng in the inner court; the plot was still undecided. Hanqiong alone exerted himself to the utmost, entered the palace gate first, and reported to Mingzong — the account is in the 《Biography of the Prince of Qin》.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Qin led troops to the Tianjin Bridge, Hanqiong was at that moment meeting with Zhu, Feng, and Kang Yicheng in the inner court; the plot was still undecided. Hanqiong alone exerted himself to the utmost, entered the palace gate first, and reported to Mingzong — the account is in the 《Biography of the Prince of Qin》.

entries.zh: 漢瓊即自介馬以召禁軍。
entries.en: Hanqiong then mounted a horse himself to summon the palace guard.
entries.literal: Hanqiong then mounted a horse himself to summon the palace guard.

entries.zh: 秦王既誅，翌日，令漢瓊馳騎召閔帝於鄴。
entries.en: After the Prince of Qin was executed, the next day Hanqiong was ordered to ride post-haste to Ye to summon Emperor Min.
entries.literal: After the Prince of Qin was executed, the next day Hanqiong was ordered to ride post-haste to Ye to summon Emperor Min.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：遣漢瓊征從厚，且權知天雄軍府事。）〉
entries.en: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》: Hanqiong was dispatched to summon Conghou and was also made acting administrator of the Tianxiong military governorship.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》: Hanqiong was dispatched to summon Conghou and was also made acting administrator of the Tianxiong military governorship.)〉

entries.zh: 閔帝嗣位，尤恃恩寵，期月之內，累加開府儀同三司、驃騎大將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Min succeeded to the throne, Hanqiong relied especially on imperial favor. Within a single month he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Preceptor with ceremonials equal to the Three Dukes and Grand General of Agile Cavalry.
entries.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded to the throne, Hanqiong relied especially on imperial favor; within a single month he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Preceptor with ceremonials equal to the Three Dukes and Grand General of Agile Cavalry.

entries.zh: 西軍既叛，閔帝急召漢瓊，欲令先入於鄴，漢瓊藏匿不行。
entries.en: When the western army rebelled, Emperor Min urgently summoned Hanqiong, wishing to send him ahead into Ye first, but Hanqiong hid himself and would not go.
entries.literal: When the western army rebelled, Emperor Min urgently summoned Hanqiong, wishing to send him ahead into Ye first, but Hanqiong hid himself and would not go.

entries.zh: 潞王行及陝州，乃悉召諸妓妾訣別，欲手刃之，眾知其心，率皆藏竄。
entries.en: When the Prince of Lu reached Shanzhou, he summoned all his courtesans and concubines to bid farewell, intending to kill them with his own hand. Everyone knew his intent and mostly hid themselves away.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Lu reached Shan Prefecture, he summoned all his courtesans and concubines to bid farewell, intending to kill them with his own hand. Everyone knew his intent and mostly hid themselves away.

entries.zh: 初，潞王失守於河中，勒歸於清化裏第。
entries.en: Earlier, when the Prince of Lu lost his post at Hezhong, he was compelled to return to his residence in Qinghua Lane.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the Prince of Lu lost his post at Hezhong, he was compelled to return to his residence in Qinghua Lane.

entries.zh: 時王淑妃恒令漢瓊傳教旨於潞王，王善待之，故漢瓊自謂潞王於己有恩。
entries.en: At that time Consort Wang Shufei constantly had Hanqiong convey imperial instructions to the Prince of Lu, and the prince treated him well. Hanqiong therefore considered that the Prince of Lu owed him a debt of gratitude.
entries.literal: At that time Consort Wang Shufei constantly had Hanqiong convey imperial instructions to the Prince of Lu, and the prince treated him well; therefore Hanqiong considered that the Prince of Lu owed him a debt of gratitude.

entries.zh: 至是，乃單騎至澠池謁見潞王，因自慟哭，欲有所陳。
entries.en: At this point he rode alone to Mianchi to have an audience with the Prince of Lu, whereupon he wept bitterly, wishing to say something.
entries.literal: At this point he rode alone to Mianchi to have an audience with the Prince of Lu, whereupon he wept bitterly himself, wishing to say something.

entries.zh: 潞王曰：「 諸事不言可知。」
entries.en: The Prince of Lu said, "Of all matters, none need be spoken to be understood."
entries.literal: The Prince of Lu said, "Of all matters, none need be spoken to be understood."

entries.zh: 漢瓊即自預從臣之列，尋戮於路左。
entries.en: Hanqiong then placed himself among the followers in advance, and soon afterward was executed by the roadside.
entries.literal: Hanqiong then placed himself among the followers in advance, and soon afterward was executed by the roadside.

entries.zh: 璋既家富於財，有蜀之妓樂，驕僭自大，動多不法，招致部下，繕理兵仗。
entries.en: Flush with wealth and in possession of Shu's courtesans and musicians, Zhang grew arrogant and overbearing. He habitually flouted the law, gathering followers and stockpiling arms.
entries.literal: Zhang was now wealthy and possessed the entertainers and musicians of Shu. He became arrogant and overbearing, frequently acting unlawfully, recruiting followers, and outfitting weapons and armor.

entries.zh: 朝廷移授昭義節度使，璋謀欲不奉詔，判官邊蔚密言規責，乃僶勉承命。
entries.en: When the court reassigned him to the Zhaoyi circuit, Zhang considered defying the order. Only after his secretary Bian Wei quietly reprimanded him did he grudgingly accept.
entries.literal: The court transferred him to the Zhaoyi military commissionership. Zhang planned to refuse the decree, but his aide Bian Wei privately admonished him, and he reluctantly accepted.

entries.zh: 洎至潞州，狂妄不悛，每擁川妓於山亭院，服赭黃，縱酒，令為王衍在蜀之戲。
entries.en: Once at Luzhou he remained as reckless as ever. He often gathered Sichuan courtesans in the Mountain Pavilion courtyard, dressed in imperial ochre-yellow, drank heavily, and had them reenact the amusements of Wang Yan's court in Shu.
entries.literal: When he reached Luzhou, he remained brazen and unrepentant. He regularly surrounded himself with Sichuan courtesans in the Mountain Pavilion courtyard, wore ochre-yellow robes, indulged in wine, and had them perform the entertainments Wang Yan had enjoyed in Shu.

entries.zh: 事聞於朝，征為金吾上將軍。
entries.en: When the court learned of this, he was recalled to serve as Senior General of the Golden Guard.
entries.literal: When word reached the court, he was summoned to serve as Senior General of the Golden Guard.

entries.zh: 其年秋，東川節度使董璋上言：「毛璋男廷贇齎父書往西川，慮有陰事。」
entries.en: That autumn, Dong Zhang, military commissioner of Dongchuan, memorialized: "Mao Zhang's son Tingyun is carrying a letter from his father to western Sichuan, and I fear some covert design lies behind the journey."
entries.literal: That autumn, Dongchuan military commissioner Dong Zhang memorialized: "Mao Zhang's son Tingyun, bearing a letter from his father, is going to western Sichuan; I fear there is a secret plot."

entries.zh: 因追廷贇及同行人趙延祚，與璋俱下御史台獄。
entries.en: On that basis Tingyun and his traveling companion Zhao Yanzuo were seized, and Mao Zhang was imprisoned by the censorate as well.
entries.literal: On this account Tingyun and his companion Zhao Yanzuo were apprehended, and Mao Zhang was also sent to the censorate prison.

entries.zh: 廷贇乃璋之假侄，稱有叔在蜀，欲往省之，亦無私書，詔停任，令歸私第。
entries.en: Tingyun was Zhang's adoptive nephew. He said he had an uncle in Shu whom he wished to visit, and no secret letter was found. An edict relieved Zhang of his post and ordered him home.
entries.literal: Tingyun was Zhang's adoptive nephew. He claimed to have an uncle in Shu and wished to visit him, and there was in fact no secret letter. An edict suspended Zhang's office and ordered him to return to his private residence.

entries.zh: 初，延祚在獄，多言璋陰事，璋許重賂，以塞其口。
entries.en: While Zhao Yanzuo was in custody, he testified at length about Zhang's covert activities. Zhang promised him a large bribe to keep quiet.
entries.literal: At first, while in prison Zhao Yanzuo spoke at length of Zhang's secret dealings. Zhang promised him a heavy bribe to silence him.

entries.zh: 及免，延祚征其賂，璋拒而不與，以至延祚詣台訴璋翻覆，復下御史台訊鞫。
entries.en: After Yanzuo was freed, he demanded payment, but Zhang refused. Yanzuo then returned to the censorate and accused Zhang of going back on his word, and Zhang was again taken into custody for questioning.
entries.literal: When he was released, Yanzuo demanded the bribe, but Zhang refused to pay. Yanzuo therefore went to the censorate and accused Zhang of duplicity, and Zhang was again imprisoned for interrogation.

entries.zh: 中丞呂夢奇以璋前蒙昭雪，今延祚以責賂之故，復加織羅，故稍佑璋。
entries.en: Censor-in-chief Lü Mengqi felt that Zhang had already been cleared once and that Yanzuo was now pressing the case only because a promised bribe had not been paid. Believing the new accusations were contrived, he leaned somewhat in Zhang's favor.
entries.literal: Censor-in-chief Lü Mengqi, considering that Zhang had previously been cleared and that Yanzuo, now pursuing him over a failed bribe, was fabricating charges again, and thus he slightly favored Zhang.

entries.zh: 及款狀上聞，或云夢奇受璋賂，所以獄不盡情，執之，移於軍巡。
entries.en: When the written confession reached the throne, some said Lü Mengqi had taken a bribe from Zhang and had therefore not pursued the case fully. Mengqi was arrested himself, and the investigation was transferred to the military patrol office.
entries.literal: When the confession was reported upward, some said Mengqi had accepted a bribe from Zhang, and therefore the investigation was not fully pursued. He was arrested and the case transferred to the military patrol office.

entries.zh: 璋具狀曾許延祚賂未與，又云曾借馬與夢奇，別無行賂之事。
entries.en: Zhang's full statement acknowledged that he had promised Yanzuo a bribe but never paid it, and that he had once lent a horse to Mengqi, but denied any other bribery.
entries.literal: Zhang stated in full that he had promised Yanzuo a bribe but had not paid it, and also that he had once lent a horse to Mengqi, but that there was no other bribery.

entries.zh: 朝廷懲其宿惡，長流儒州，賜死於路。
entries.en: The court, punishing his long record of misconduct, banished him to Ruzhou and ordered him put to death on the way.
entries.literal: The court punished his long-standing wickedness by banishing him to Ruzhou and ordering his death en route.

entries.zh: 毛璋，本滄州小校。
entries.en: Mao Zhang had begun his career as a low-ranking officer in Cangzhou.
entries.literal: Mao Zhang was originally a petty officer of Cangzhou.

entries.zh: 梁將戴思遠帥滄州，時莊宗已定魏博，思遠勢蹙，棄州遁去，璋據城歸莊宗，
entries.en: When Liang general Dai Siyuan held Cangzhou, Emperor Zhuangzong had already secured Weibo. With his position collapsing, Siyuan abandoned the prefecture and fled, and Zhang seized the city and submitted to Zhuangzong,
entries.literal: Liang general Dai Siyuan commanded Cangzhou. At that time Emperor Zhuangzong had already pacified Weibo; Siyuan's position was desperate, and he abandoned the prefecture and fled. Zhang held the city and submitted to Zhuangzong,

entries.zh: 〈（《玉堂閑話》：戴思遠任浮陽日，有部曲毛璋，為性輕悍。
entries.en: (According to Tales from the Jade Hall: While Dai Siyuan was governing Fuyang, one of his retainers was Mao Zhang, known for his reckless, aggressive nature.
entries.literal: (Tales from the Jade Hall: When Dai Siyuan was stationed at Fuyang, among his troops was Mao Zhang, a man of rash and fierce temperament.

entries.zh: 嘗與數十卒追捕盜賊，還宿於逆旅，毛枕劍而寢。
entries.en: On one occasion he took several dozen men in pursuit of bandits. On the way back they put up at an inn, and Mao went to sleep with his sword under his head.
entries.literal: Once, with several dozen soldiers, he pursued bandits and on the return lodged at an inn; Mao slept with his sword as a pillow.

entries.zh: 夜分，其劍忽大吼，躍出鞘外，從卒聞者愕然驚異，毛亦神之。
entries.en: At midnight his sword suddenly gave a great roar and jumped clear of its scabbard. The soldiers who heard it were stunned; Mao, too, regarded the event as an omen.
entries.literal: In the middle of the night, his sword suddenly roared and leapt from its scabbard. The accompanying soldiers who heard it were startled and amazed; Mao also took it as a supernatural sign.

entries.zh: 乃持劍祝曰：「某若異日有此山河，爾當更鳴躍，否則已。」
entries.en: Taking the sword in hand, he addressed it: "If I should one day come to rule these lands, you will roar and leap again; if not, let this be the end of it."
entries.literal: He then took up the sword and prayed: "If I one day come to possess this realm of mountains and rivers, you shall roar and leap again; if not, let it be so no more."

entries.zh: 毛復寢，未熟，劍吼躍如初，毛深自負。
entries.en: Mao went back to sleep. Before he had settled into deep slumber, the sword roared and leapt again just as before. From that moment he was convinced of his destiny.
entries.literal: Mao slept again, and before he had fallen deeply asleep, the sword roared and leapt as before. Mao greatly congratulated himself.

entries.zh: 其後戴離鎮，毛請留，戴從之。
entries.en: When Dai later left his command, Mao asked to stay behind, and Dai agreed.
entries.literal: Later, when Dai left his post, Mao asked to remain behind, and Dai granted his request.

entries.zh: 未幾，毛以州歸命於唐莊宗，莊宗以毛為其州刺史，後竟帥滄海。）〉
entries.en: Not long afterward Mao turned the prefecture over to Tang Emperor Zhuangzong, who made him prefect of that prefecture; he eventually rose to command the Canghai circuit.)〉
entries.literal: Before long, Mao surrendered the prefecture to Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong, who appointed Mao prefect of that prefecture; in the end he came to command the Canghai circuit.)〉

entries.zh: 曆貝州、遼州刺史。
entries.en: He later served in turn as prefect of Beizhou and Liaozhou.
entries.literal: He successively served as prefect of Beizhou and Liaozhou.

entries.zh: 璋性凶悖，有膽略，從征河上，屢有戰功。
entries.en: Zhang was violent and lawless by nature, yet bold and capable. On campaigns along the Yellow River he won repeated martial honors.
entries.literal: Zhang was by nature violent and defiant, but bold and resourceful. Campaigning on the Yellow River front, he repeatedly distinguished himself in battle.

entries.zh: 梁平，授滄州節度使。
entries.en: After the Liang dynasty fell, he was made military commissioner of Cangzhou.
entries.literal: When the Liang was pacified, he was appointed military commissioner of Cangzhou.

entries.zh: 王師討蜀，以璋為行營右廂馬軍都指揮使；
entries.en: During the imperial campaign against Shu, he was appointed overall commander of the right-wing cavalry in the field headquarters;
entries.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Shu, Zhang was made commander-in-chief of the right-wing cavalry of the field headquarters;

entries.zh: 蜀平，璋功居多。
entries.en: After Shu was pacified, Zhang's contribution ranked among the greatest.
entries.literal: When Shu was pacified, Zhang's achievements ranked foremost among all.

entries.zh: 明年，蕭牆禍起，繼岌自西川至渭南，部下散亡，其川貨妓樂，為璋所掠。
entries.en: The following year, palace intrigue erupted into disaster. As Li Jiji made his way from western Sichuan to Weinan, his forces melted away, and Zhang seized the Sichuan wealth, entertainers, and musicians in his train.
entries.literal: The next year, calamity arose within the palace walls. Jiji came from western Sichuan to Weinan; his followers scattered and fled, and the Sichuan goods, courtesans, and musicians were plundered by Zhang.

entries.zh: 明宗嗣位，錄平蜀功，授邠州節度使。
entries.en: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Zhang's role in the conquest of Shu was formally acknowledged, and he was given Binzhou as his circuit.
entries.literal: When Emperor Mingzong succeeded to the throne, Zhang's service in pacifying Shu was recognized, and he was appointed military commissioner of Binzhou.

entries.zh: 段凝，開封人也。
entries.en: Duan Ning was a native of Kaifeng.
entries.literal: Duan Ning was a native of Kaifeng.

entries.zh: 本名明遠，少穎悟，多智數。
entries.en: His original name was Mingyuan. As a youth he was quick-witted and adept at intrigue.
entries.literal: His original name was Mingyuan. In youth he was quick-witted and full of stratagems.

entries.zh: 初為澠池簿，脫荷衣以事梁祖，梁祖漸器之。
entries.en: He began as a clerk in Mianchi County, then cast off his scholar's robe to enter the service of the Liang founder, who gradually came to esteem him.
entries.literal: At first he was clerk of Mianchi County. He cast off his plain robe to serve the Liang founder, who gradually came to value him.

entries.zh: 開平三年十月，自東頭供奉官授右威衛大將軍，充左軍巡使兼水北巡檢使。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the third year of Kaiping he was promoted from Eastern Head Attendant to General of the Right Weiwu Guard, with concurrent duties as Left Army Patrol Commissioner and Northern Waters Inspector.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Kaiping, from Eastern Head Attendant he was appointed General of the Right Weiwu Guard, serving as Left Army Patrol Commissioner and concurrently Northern Waters Inspector.

entries.zh: 凝妹為梁祖美人，故稍委心腹。
entries.en: Ning's younger sister was a favored consort of the Liang founder, and on that account he was gradually treated as an inner-circle confidant.
entries.literal: Ning's younger sister was a favored consort of the Liang founder, so he was gradually entrusted as a confidant.

entries.zh: 四年五月，授懷州刺史。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was appointed prefect of Huaizhou.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was appointed prefect of Huaizhou.

entries.zh: 乾化元年十二月，梁祖北征回，過郡，凝貢獻加等，梁祖大悅。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of the first year of Qianhua, the Liang founder returned from a northern campaign and passed through his prefecture. Ning doubled his tribute, and the founder was greatly pleased.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Qianhua, the Liang founder returned from a northern campaign and passed through the prefecture. Ning's tribute was doubled, and the founder was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 梁祖復北，凝迎奉進貢，有加於前。
entries.en: When the founder marched north again, Ning received him with tribute even more lavish than before.
entries.literal: When the founder marched north again, Ning welcomed him with tribute greater than before.

entries.zh: 梁祖次相州，刺史李思安迎奉疏怠，梁祖怒，貶思安。
entries.en: When the founder halted at Xiangzhou, Prefect Li Si'an received him with slack courtesy. The founder was enraged and demoted him.
entries.literal: When the founder halted at Xiangzhou, Prefect Li Si'an received him negligently. The founder was angry and demoted Si'an.

entries.zh: 製云：「懷州刺史段明遠，少年治郡，庶事惟公，兩度隻奉行鑾，數程宿食本界，動無遺闕，舉必周豐，蓋能罄竭於家財，務在顯酬夫明獎。
entries.en: The edict declared: "Duan Mingyuan, prefect of Huaizhou, though young in governing a commandery, conducts every affair with scrupulous fairness. Twice he alone attended the imperial carriage; for several marches he provided lodging and provisions within his jurisdiction without a single lapse, and never with less than full abundance. He has clearly drained his family fortune and seeks thereby to make plain the value of enlightened reward.
entries.literal: The edict read: "Duan Mingyuan, prefect of Huaizhou, though young in governing a commandery, handles every affair with fairness. Twice he alone attended upon the imperial carriage; for several marches he lodged and supplied provisions within his jurisdiction without omission in action or shortfall in provision. He has clearly exhausted his family wealth and strives to make manifest the reward of enlightened encouragement.

entries.zh: 觀明遠之忠勤若此，見思安之悖慢何如！」
entries.en: Compare Mingyuan's loyalty and diligence with this, and see how Si'an's insolence and neglect measure up!"
entries.literal: When one compares Mingyuan's loyalty and diligence like this, how does it compare to Si'an's defiance and negligence!"

entries.zh: 其見賞如此。
entries.en: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
entries.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

entries.zh: 其後，遷鄭州刺史，監大軍於河上。
entries.en: Thereafter he was transferred to Zheng Prefecture to supervise the army on the Yellow River front.
entries.literal: Thereafter he was transferred to Zheng Prefecture to oversee the army on the river.

entries.zh: 梁末帝以戴思遠為北面招討使。
entries.en: The last Liang emperor appointed Dai Siyuan commander-in-chief of the northern campaign.
entries.literal: The last Liang emperor appointed Dai Siyuan northern campaign commander-in-chief.

entries.zh: 行師不利，用王彥章代之，受任之翌日，取德勝之南城，軍聲大振。
entries.en: When campaigns went badly, Wang Yanzhang replaced him. The day after taking command, Yanzhang seized the southern citadel of Desheng, and army morale soared.
entries.literal: Campaigns went badly, and Wang Yanzhang was put in his place. The day after assuming command he took the southern citadel of Desheng, and army morale soared.
