entries.zh: 張漢倫等推功於凝，凝掎摭彥章之失以間之。
entries.en: Zhang Hanlun and others credited Ning with the success, and Ning seized on Yanzhang's faults to drive a wedge between them.
entries.literal: Zhang Hanlun and others attributed the credit to Ning; Ning seized on Yanzhang's faults to drive a wedge between them.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：彥章棄鄒家口，復趨楊劉。
entries.en: (According to the Zizhi Tongjian: Yanzhang abandoned Zujiakou and hurried toward Yangliu.
entries.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: Yanzhang abandoned Zujiakou and hurried to Yangliu.

entries.zh: 遊奕將李紹興敗梁遊兵於清邱縣南，段凝以為唐兵已自上流渡，驚駭失色，麵數彥章，尤其深入。）〉
entries.en: Patrol general Li Shaoxing defeated Liang scouts south of Qingqiu County. Ning concluded that Tang troops had already crossed upstream, turned pale with fright, and berated Yanzhang to his face, reproaching him above all for advancing too far.)〉
entries.literal: Patrol general Li Shaoxing defeated Liang scouts south of Qingqiu County. Ning thought Tang troops had already crossed upstream, turned pale with fright, and face-to-face berated Yanzhang, reproaching him especially for pushing too deep.)〉

entries.zh: 梁末帝怒，罷彥章兵權。
entries.en: The last Liang emperor was enraged and stripped Yanzhang of his military command.
entries.literal: The last Liang emperor was angry and removed Yanzhang's military authority.

entries.zh: 凝納賂於趙、張二族，求為招討使，敬翔、李振極言不可，竟不能止。
entries.en: Ning bribed the Zhao and Zhang clans in pursuit of the post of campaign commander-in-chief. Jing Xiang and Li Zhen argued strenuously against the appointment but could not prevent it.
entries.literal: Ning bribed the Zhao and Zhang clans to seek the post of campaign commander-in-chief. Jing Xiang and Li Zhen strongly argued against it but could not stop it.

entries.zh: 凝以眾五萬營於高陵津，裨將康延孝叛歸莊宗，延孝具陳梁軍虛實，莊宗遂決長驅之計。
entries.en: Ning encamped fifty thousand men at Gaoling Ford. Subordinate general Kang Yanxiao defected to Emperor Zhuangzong and gave a full account of the Liang army's strengths and weaknesses, and Zhuangzong thereupon resolved on a direct advance.
entries.literal: Ning encamped fifty thousand men at Gaoling Ford. Subordinate general Kang Yanxiao defected to Zhuangzong and fully reported the Liang army's strengths and weaknesses, whereupon Zhuangzong decided on a direct thrust.

entries.zh: 未幾，莊宗入汴，凝自滑率兵而南，前鋒杜晏球至封丘，解甲聽命。
entries.en: Before long Emperor Zhuangzong entered Bian. Ning led troops south from Hua, and vanguard commander Du Yanqiu reached Fengqiu, laid down his arms, and awaited orders.
entries.literal: Before long Zhuangzong entered Bian. Ning led troops south from Hua; vanguard commander Du Yanqiu reached Fengqiu and laid down arms awaiting orders.

entries.zh: 翌日，凝率大軍乞降於汴郊，莊宗釋之，復以凝為滑州兵馬留後，賜姓，名紹欽。
entries.en: The next day Ning led the main army to surrender in the suburbs of Bian. Emperor Zhuangzong spared him, reappointed him military reserve officer of Hua Prefecture, granted him the imperial surname, and gave him the name Shaoqin.
entries.literal: The next day Ning led the main army to surrender in the Bian suburbs. Zhuangzong spared him, restored him as military reserve officer of Hua Prefecture, granted the imperial surname, and gave him the name Shaoqin.

entries.zh: 有頃，正授節度，改兗州節度使。
entries.en: Shortly thereafter he received a full appointment as military commissioner and was transferred to Yanzhou.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he received full commission as military commissioner and was transferred to Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 凝初見莊宗，因伶人景進通貨於宮掖。
entries.en: When Ning first met Emperor Zhuangzong, he used the actor Jing Jin to convey gifts into the inner palace.
entries.literal: When Ning first met Zhuangzong, through the actor Jing Jin he conveyed goods into the inner palace.

entries.zh: 凝天性奸佞，巧言飾智，善候人意。
entries.en: By nature Ning was treacherous and sycophantic, skilled at polished speech and feigned wisdom, and adept at reading what others wished to hear.
entries.literal: By nature Ning was treacherous and sycophantic, skilled at artful speech and feigned wisdom, adept at reading others' wishes.

entries.zh: 其年，契丹寇幽州，命宣徽使李紹宏監護諸軍，以禦契丹，凝與董璋戍瓦橋關。
entries.en: That year the Khitan raided Youzhou. Li Shaohong, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was appointed to oversee the armies against them; Ning and Dong Zhang garrisoned Waqiao Pass.
entries.literal: That year the Khitan raided Youzhou. Li Shaohong, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was appointed to oversee all armies against the Khitan; Ning and Dong Zhang garrisoned Waqiao Pass.

entries.zh: 凝巧事紹宏，紹宏嘗乘間奏凝蓋世奇才，可以大任，屢請以兵柄委之。
entries.en: Ning skillfully ingratiated himself with Shaohong, who on one occasion memorialized that Ning was a rare genius fit for great responsibility and repeatedly asked that military command be entrusted to him.
entries.literal: Ning skillfully ingratiated himself with Shaohong, who once found occasion to memorialize that Ning was a rare genius fit for great responsibility and repeatedly asked that military authority be entrusted to him.

entries.zh: 郭崇韜曰：「段凝亡國敗軍之將，奸諂難狀，不要信也。」
entries.en: Guo Chongtao said, "Duan Ning is a defeated general of a ruined state; his treachery and flattery are beyond description—do not trust him."
entries.literal: Guo Chongtao said: "Duan Ning is a defeated general of a ruined state; his treachery and flattery are beyond description—do not trust him."

entries.zh: 凝在藩鎮，私用庫物數萬計，有司促償，中旨貰其負。
entries.en: At his fief Ning privately used treasury goods worth tens of thousands. When the relevant office pressed for repayment, an imperial order remitted his debt.
entries.literal: At his fief Ning privately used treasury goods numbering in the tens of thousands. The relevant office pressed for repayment, but an imperial order remitted his debt.

entries.zh: 同光三年四月，移授鄧州節度使。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the third year of Tongguang he was transferred to military commissioner of Deng Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Tongguang he was transferred to military commissioner of Deng Prefecture.

entries.zh: 四年二月，趙在禮據鄴城，李紹宏請用凝為大將，莊宗許之，令具方略條奏。
entries.en: In the second month of the fourth year Zhao Zaili seized Ye City. Li Shaohong asked that Ning be appointed commander; Emperor Zhuangzong agreed and ordered him to submit a detailed plan.
entries.literal: In the second month of the fourth year Zhao Zaili held Ye City. Li Shaohong asked to use Ning as commander; Zhuangzong agreed and ordered him to submit a detailed plan.

entries.zh: 凝所請偏裨皆取其己黨，莊宗疑之，乃止。
entries.en: Every subordinate commander Ning requested was from his own faction. Emperor Zhuangzong grew suspicious and halted the appointment.
entries.literal: All the subordinate commanders Ning requested were his own faction. Zhuangzong grew suspicious and stopped the appointment.

entries.zh: 明宗至洛陽，霍彥威怒其前事，與溫韜同收下獄，詔釋之，放歸田里。
entries.en: When Emperor Mingzong reached Luoyang, Huo Yanwei, angry at his past conduct, had him imprisoned together with Wen Tao. An edict released them and sent them back to their homes.
entries.literal: When Mingzong reached Luoyang, Huo Yanwei, angry at his past conduct, had him imprisoned together with Wen Tao. An edict released them and sent them home.

entries.zh: 明年，竄於遼州，竟與溫韜同製賜死。
entries.en: The following year he fled to Liaozhou and was ultimately, by edict together with Wen Tao, commanded to take his own life.
entries.literal: The next year he fled to Liaozhou and in the end was by edict together with Wen Tao ordered to take his own life.

entries.zh: 康延孝，塞北部落人也。
entries.en: Kang Yanxiao came from the northern frontier tribes.
entries.literal: Kang Yanxiao was a man of the northern frontier tribes.

entries.zh: 初隸太原，因得罪，亡命於汴梁。
entries.en: He first served under Taiyuan; after committing an offense he fled to Bianliang.
entries.literal: At first he was subordinated to Taiyuan; having offended, he fled his life to Bianliang.

entries.zh: 開平、乾化中，自隊長積勞至部校。
entries.en: During the Kaiping and Qianhua reigns he worked his way up from squad leader to company commander.
entries.literal: During Kaiping and Qianhua, through accumulated service he rose from squad leader to company commander.

entries.zh: 梁末帝時，頻立軍功。
entries.en: Under the Last Emperor of Liang he won military honors again and again.
entries.literal: Under Liang's Last Emperor, he repeatedly won military merit.

entries.zh: 同光元年八月，段凝率眾五萬營於王村，時延孝為右先鋒指揮使，率百騎來奔。
entries.en: In the eighth month of Tongguang 1, Duan Ning camped at Wang Village with fifty thousand men. Yanxiao, then Right Vanguard Commander, came over with a hundred riders.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Tongguang, Duan Ning led fifty thousand troops and encamped at Wang Village; at that time Yanxiao was Right Vanguard Commander and led a hundred horsemen to defect.

entries.zh: 莊宗得之，喜，解禦衣金帶以賜之。
entries.en: Zhuangzong welcomed him gladly, stripped off his own imperial robe and gold belt, and gave them to him.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong received him, rejoiced, and removed his imperial robe and gold belt to bestow them on him.

entries.zh: 翌日，賜田宅於鄴，以為捧日軍使兼南面招討指揮使、檢校司空，守博州刺史。
entries.en: The next day he granted him fields and a house at Ye and made him commander of the Sun-Rising Army, southern-route pacification commander, acting Sikong, and defender of Bo Prefecture.
entries.literal: The next day he bestowed fields and a residence at Ye, appointing him commander of the Sun-Rising Army and simultaneous southern-route pacification commander, acting Sikong, and defender of Bo Prefecture.

entries.zh: 莊宗屏人問梁兵機，延孝備陳利害，語在《莊宗紀》中。
entries.en: Zhuangzong sent everyone else away and asked about Liang's military situation. Yanxiao laid out the pros and cons in full; the account appears in the "Annals of Zhuangzong."
entries.literal: Zhuangzong dismissed attendants and questioned him on Liang military affairs; Yanxiao fully set forth advantages and disadvantages—the account is in the "Annals of Zhuangzong."

entries.zh: 莊宗平汴，延孝頗有力焉，以功授檢校太保、鄭州防禦使，賜姓，名紹琛。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong took Bian, Yanxiao had done much to help. For his service he was made acting Grand Guardian and Zhengzhou defense commissioner and granted the surname with the name Shaochen.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Bian, Yanxiao contributed considerably; for his merit he was appointed acting Grand Guardian and Zhengzhou defense commissioner, granted the surname with the name Shaochen.

entries.zh: 明年，郊禮畢，授保義軍節度使。
entries.en: The following year, after the suburban sacrifices, he was appointed military commissioner of the Baoyi Army.
entries.literal: The next year, after the suburban rites were completed, he was appointed military commissioner of the Baoyi Army.

entries.zh: 三年，討蜀，以延孝為西南行營馬步軍先鋒、排陣斬斫等使。
entries.en: In the third year of the campaign against Shu, Yanxiao was appointed vanguard of the Southwest Campaign Army's horse and foot forces and commissioner for battle formation and close combat.
entries.literal: In the third year, when Shu was attacked, Yanxiao was made vanguard of the cavalry and infantry of the Southwest Campaign Army and commissioner for array deployment and cutting down the enemy.

entries.zh: 延孝性驍健，徇利奮不顧身。
entries.en: Yanxiao was fierce and hardy by nature, and greedy for profit; in battle he threw himself forward without thought for his own life.
entries.literal: Yanxiao was by nature fierce and hardy; greedy for gain, he fought without regard for his own body.

entries.zh: 以前鋒下鳳州，收固鎮，降興州，敗王衍軍於三泉，所俘蜀軍皆諭而釋之，自是晝夜兼行。
entries.en: Leading the vanguard, he took Feng Prefecture, seized Gu Town, accepted the surrender of Xing Prefecture, and routed Wang Yan's army at Sanquan. Every Shu soldier taken captive was reasoned with and then set free. From that point he pressed on day and night without pause.
entries.literal: As vanguard he took Feng Prefecture, seized Gu Town, received the surrender of Xing Prefecture, and defeated Wang Yan's army at Sanquan; all captured Shu soldiers were admonished and released, and from then on he marched day and night without rest.

entries.zh: 王衍自利州奔歸成都，斷吉柏津浮梁，以絕諸軍。
entries.en: Wang Yan fled from Lizhou to Chengdu, destroyed the pontoon bridge at Jibai Ford, and thereby severed the route of the invading armies.
entries.literal: Wang Yan fled from Lizhou back to Chengdu, cut the pontoon bridge at Jibai Ford, and thereby cut off the armies.

entries.zh: 延孝復造浮梁以渡，進收綿州，王衍復斷綿江浮梁而去。
entries.en: Yanxiao built another pontoon bridge and crossed, then advanced to take Mian Prefecture. Wang Yan once more destroyed the pontoon bridge on the Mian River and withdrew.
entries.literal: Yanxiao again built a pontoon bridge to cross, advanced and took Mian Prefecture, and Wang Yan again cut the pontoon bridge on the Mian River and withdrew.

entries.zh: 水深無舟楫可渡，延孝謂招撫使李嚴曰：「吾懸軍深入，利在急兵。
entries.en: The river was too deep and there were no boats to ferry them across. Yanxiao said to the pacification commissioner Li Yan, "We have driven a detached force deep into enemy country. Our advantage lies in striking fast.
entries.literal: The water was deep and there were no boats or rafts by which to cross. Yanxiao said to the pacification commissioner Li Yan: "I have led an isolated army deep into enemy territory; the advantage lies in pressing the attack swiftly.

entries.zh: 乘王衍破膽之時，人心離沮，但得百騎過鹿頭關，彼即迎降不暇。
entries.en: While Wang Yan is still shaken and his men are losing heart, even a hundred horsemen who get through Deer Head Pass will find the enemy too busy surrendering to resist us.
entries.literal: While Wang Yan's courage is broken and men's hearts are divided and discouraged, if only a hundred horsemen can pass Deer Head Pass, the enemy will have no leisure but to welcome us in surrender.

entries.zh: 如俟修繕津梁，便留數日，若王衍堅閉近關，折吾兵勢，儻延旬浹，則勝負莫可知也，宜促騎渡江。」
entries.en: If we wait to repair the bridge and lose several days, and Wang Yan seals the passes nearby and blunts our momentum, then in ten days' time no one can say who will win. We must get the cavalry across the river immediately."
entries.literal: If we wait to repair the ford bridge and stay several days, and Wang Yan firmly closes the nearby passes and breaks our army's momentum, and if it drags on for ten days, then victory and defeat cannot be known; we should urge the cavalry to cross the river at once."

entries.zh: 因與李嚴乘馬浮江，於是得濟者僅千人，步軍溺死者亦千餘人。
entries.en: He and Li Yan then rode their horses across the swollen river. Only about a thousand men made it over; more than a thousand foot soldiers drowned.
entries.literal: Thereupon he and Li Yan rode their horses across the river floating; thus only about a thousand men got across, and more than a thousand foot soldiers drowned.

entries.zh: 延孝既濟，長驅通鹿頭，進據漢州。
entries.en: Once across, Yanxiao drove hard through Deer Head Pass and seized Han Prefecture.
entries.literal: Once Yanxiao had crossed, he drove straight through to Deer Head and advanced to occupy Han Prefecture.

entries.zh: 居三日，部下後軍方至。
entries.en: Three days passed before the rest of his army caught up.
entries.literal: After three days, the rear units of his subordinates finally arrived.

entries.zh: 偽蜀六軍使王宗弼令人持牛酒幣馬歸款。
entries.en: Wang Zongbi, commander of the Six Armies of the Shu regime, sent envoys with cattle, wine, silks, and horses to offer surrender.
entries.literal: The bogus-Shu Six Armies commissioner Wang Zongbi sent men bearing cattle, wine, silks, and horses to submit.

entries.zh: 旬日，兩川平定，延孝止漢州以俟繼岌。
entries.en: Within ten days both the eastern and western circuits of Shu were pacified. Yanxiao held Han Prefecture to await Prince Siji.
entries.literal: Within ten days the Two Chuan were pacified; Yanxiao halted at Han Prefecture to await Siji.

entries.zh: 平蜀之功，延孝居最。
entries.en: Of all who had helped conquer Shu, Yanxiao's achievement stood foremost.
entries.literal: In the merit of pacifying Shu, Yanxiao ranked first.

entries.zh: 張虔釗，遼州人也。
entries.en: Zhang Qianzhao was a native of Liao Prefecture.
entries.literal: Zhang Qianzhao was a man of Liao Prefecture.

entries.zh: 〈（《九國志》云：虔釗，遼州榆社人。
entries.en: (According to the Annals of the Nine States: Qianzhao was from Yushe in Liao Prefecture.
entries.literal: (Annals of the Nine States says: Qianzhao was a man of Yushe in Liao Prefecture.

entries.zh: 父簡，唐檢校尚書左僕射。）〉
entries.en: His father Jian had served as Honorary Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat under Tang.)〉
entries.literal: His father Jian was Tang's Honorary Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.)〉

entries.zh: 初為太原牙校，以武勇聞於流輩，武皇、莊宗之世，累補左右突騎軍使。
entries.en: He began as a military aide at Taiyuan and won a reputation for courage among his peers. Under Emperor Wuzong and Zhuangzong he rose repeatedly to command the Left and Right Flying Cavalry.
entries.literal: At first he was a military aide at Taiyuan; his martial valor was known among his peers. In the reigns of Emperor Wuzong and Zhuangzong he was repeatedly appointed commander of the Left and Right Flying Cavalry.

entries.zh: 〈（《九國志》：莊宗嘗以偏師取鎮陽，命虔釗率騎為先鋒，屢挫賊銳，遂陷其城。）〉
entries.en: (According to the Annals of the Nine States: Zhuangzong once took Zhenyang with a detached column and made Qianzhao lead the cavalry vanguard. Qianzhao repeatedly broke the enemy's best troops and finally captured the city.)〉
entries.literal: (Annals of the Nine States: Zhuangzong once took Zhenyang with a detached force, ordered Qianzhao to lead the cavalry as vanguard, repeatedly blunted the enemy's sharp edge, and finally stormed the city.)〉

entries.zh: 明宗素聞虔釗有將帥才，及即位，擢為護駕親軍都指揮使，領春州刺史。
entries.en: Mingzong had long heard of Qianzhao's gifts as a commander. When he took the throne he made Qianzhao chief commander of the imperial guard and prefect of Chun.
entries.literal: Mingzong had long heard that Qianzhao had talent as a general. When he took the throne he promoted him to chief commander of the imperial guard cavalry and made him prefect of Chun Prefecture.

entries.zh: 天成中，與諸將圍王都於中山，大敗契丹於嘉山之下，及定州平，以功授滄州節度使。
entries.en: During Tiancheng he joined other generals in besieging Wang Du at Zhongshan and routed the Khitan below Mount Jia. When Ding Prefecture fell, he was rewarded with the military governorship of Cang.
entries.literal: During Tiancheng he joined the generals in besieging Wang Du at Zhongshan, greatly defeated the Khitan below Mount Jia, and when Ding Prefecture was pacified was made military governor of Cang Prefecture for his merit.

entries.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》：虔釗鎮滄州日，因亢旱民饑，發廩賑之，方上聞，帝甚嘉獎。
entries.en: (According to Miscellaneous Tales from Northern Dreams: While Qianzhao governed Cang, a severe drought brought famine. He opened the granaries to feed the people. When the report reached court, the emperor praised him warmly.
entries.literal: (Miscellaneous Tales from Northern Dreams: When Qianzhao governed Cang Prefecture, because of severe drought the people were hungry; he opened the granaries to relieve them. The report had just reached the throne when the emperor greatly praised and rewarded him.

entries.zh: 他日秋成，倍鬥征斂，朝論鄙之。）〉
entries.en: Later, after the autumn harvest, he doubled the tax levies, and court opinion turned against him.)〉
entries.literal: Another day when the autumn harvest came in, he doubled the levies; court opinion despised him.)〉

entries.zh: 移鎮徐州。
entries.en: He was transferred to Xuzhou.
entries.literal: He was transferred to garrison Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 長興中，為山南西道節度使兼西面馬步軍都部署。
entries.en: During Changxing he served as military governor of Shannan West Circuit and chief deployer of the western horse and foot armies.
entries.literal: In Changxing he was military governor of Shannan West Circuit and concurrently chief deployer of the western horse and foot armies.

entries.zh: 及末帝起於鳳翔，閔帝詔令虔釗帥部兵會王師於岐下。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor rose at Fengxiang, Emperor Min ordered Qianzhao to lead his troops and join the imperial army at Qi.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor rose at Fengxiang, Emperor Min ordered Qianzhao to lead his troops to join the imperial army below Qi.

entries.zh: 洎西師俱變，虔釗憤惋，退歸興元，因與洋州節度使孫漢韶俱送款於蜀。
entries.en: When the western armies all turned, Qianzhao withdrew to Xingyuan in anger and grief. He and Sun Hanzhao, military governor of Yang, then both submitted to Shu.
entries.literal: When the western armies all mutinied, Qianzhao was resentful and grieved, withdrew to Xingyuan, and thereupon he and the military governor of Yang Prefecture Sun Hanzhao both sent pledges of submission to Shu.

entries.zh: 孟知祥待之尤厚，偽授本鎮節度使，俾知祥坐獲山南之地，由虔釗之故也。
entries.en: Meng Zhixiang treated him with exceptional generosity and invested him as military governor of his former circuit. It was largely through Qianzhao that Zhixiang gained the lands of Shannan without a fight.
entries.literal: Meng Zhixiang treated him with especial generosity and falsely invested him as military governor of his own circuit. That Zhixiang easily gained the lands of Shannan was owing to Qianzhao.

entries.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》：入蜀，取人產業，黷貨無厭，蜀民怨之。）〉
entries.en: (According to Miscellaneous Tales from Northern Dreams: Once in Shu he seized people's property, took bribes without limit, and earned the hatred of the Shu populace.)〉
entries.literal: (Miscellaneous Tales from Northern Dreams: After entering Shu he seized people's estates, was insatiably corrupt, and the people of Shu resented him.)〉

entries.zh: 孟昶嗣偽位，加檢校太師、兼中書令。
entries.en: When Meng Chang succeeded to the Shu throne, Qianzhao was made Honorary Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When Meng Chang succeeded to the false throne, Qianzhao was made Honorary Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 晉開運末，蜀人聞契丹入洛，令虔釗率眾數萬，將寇秦、雍。
entries.en: Late in the Kaiyun era of Jin, when Shu heard that the Khitan had entered Luoyang, Chang ordered Qianzhao to lead tens of thousands against Qin and Yong.
entries.literal: At the end of Kaiyun of Jin, the Shu people heard the Khitan had entered Luoyang and ordered Qianzhao to lead tens of thousands to invade Qin and Yong.

entries.zh: 俄聞漢高祖已定中原，虔釗無功而退。
entries.en: Soon word came that Emperor Gaozu of Han had secured the Central Plains, and Qianzhao withdrew without accomplishing anything.
entries.literal: Soon they heard Emperor Gaozu of Han had secured the Central Plains; Qianzhao withdrew without achievement.

entries.zh: 〈（《九國志》云：曆左右匡聖馬步軍都指揮使，出為昭武軍節度使。
entries.en: (According to the Annals of the Nine States: He had served in turn as chief commander of the Left and Right Kuangsheng armies and then as military governor of Zhaowu.
entries.literal: (Annals of the Nine States says: He successively served as chief commander of the Left and Right Kuangsheng horse and foot armies and went out as military governor of Zhaowu Army.

entries.zh: 及漢祖即位，乃移鎮梁州，以觀朝廷之變。
entries.en: When the Han founder took the throne, he was moved to Liang Prefecture to watch how events at court would unfold.
entries.literal: When the Han founder took the throne, he was transferred to garrison Liang Prefecture to observe changes at court.

entries.zh: 會晉昌軍節度使趙匡讚、鳳翔節度使侯益俱謀歸蜀，遂以虔釗為北面行營招討使，應接經營。
entries.en: When Zhao Kuangzan of Jinchang and Hou Yi of Fengxiang both plotted to defect to Shu, Qianzhao was made northern-campaign pacification commissioner to coordinate the effort.
entries.literal: It happened that the military governor of Jinchang Army Zhao Kuangzan and the military governor of Fengxiang Hou Yi both plotted to submit to Shu; thereupon Qianzhao was made northern-campaign pacification commissioner to receive and manage affairs.

entries.zh: 俄而趙匡讚、侯益請昶出師，掠定三秦，因命虔釗與韓保貞等總師五萬出散關，雄武軍節度使何重建出隴右，奉鑾肅衛都虞候李廷珪出子午穀，會於雍州。
entries.en: Soon Zhao and Hou urged Chang to march and seize the Three Qin. Chang ordered Qianzhao and Han Baozhen to lead fifty thousand men through San Pass, He Chongjian of Xiongwu to advance through Longyou, and Li Tinggui of the Imperial Escort to march through Ziwu Valley. All were to converge on Yong.
entries.literal: Soon Zhao Kuangzan and Hou Yi requested that Chang send troops to raid and secure the Three Qin. Thereupon he ordered Qianzhao with Han Baozhen and others to command fifty thousand troops out through San Pass, the military governor of Xiongwu Army He Chongjian out through Longyou, and the chief adjutant of the Imperial Escort Guard Li Tinggui out through Ziwu Valley, to meet at Yong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 廷珪始出子午穀，聞匡讚為王景崇所逼，棄城自拔東去，遂先退師。
entries.en: Tinggui had barely left Ziwu Valley when he learned that Kuangzan was being driven by Wang Jingchong, abandoned his position, and fled east. He was the first to withdraw.
entries.literal: Tinggui had just emerged from Ziwu Valley when he heard Kuangzan was pressed by Wang Jingchong, abandoned the city and fled east on his own, and thereupon first withdrew his army.

entries.zh: 時虔釗、福誠、保貞師次陳倉，謀不相葉，而侯益聞匡讚已去，廷珪班師，亦誠款中變，閉壘不出。
entries.en: By then Qianzhao, Fucheng, and Baozhen had halted at Chencang and could not agree among themselves. Hou Yi heard that Kuangzan was gone and Tinggui had withdrawn, changed his mind about submitting, and shut himself behind his walls.
entries.literal: At that time the armies of Qianzhao, Fucheng, and Baozhen halted at Chencang and would not cooperate with one another. Hou Yi heard Kuangzan had gone, Tinggui had withdrawn his army, and his own pledge of sincerity changed midway; he closed his ramparts and would not come out.

entries.zh: 司天監趙廷樞累以雲氣不利為諷，保貞乃與福誠率所部取隴州道，會重建歸蜀，虔釗留寶雞，以勢孤不可深入，遂班師。）〉
entries.en: The director of the Astronomical Bureau, Zhao Tingshu, repeatedly warned that the omens were unfavorable. Baozhen and Fucheng then led their men toward Long Prefecture. When He Chongjian returned to Shu, Qianzhao held Baoji but, finding his force too isolated to advance, withdrew.)〉
entries.literal: The Director of the Astronomical Bureau Zhao Tingshu repeatedly used unfavorable cloud signs as admonition. Baozhen then led his troops with Fucheng by the Long Prefecture route; when Chongjian returned to Shu, Qianzhao remained at Baoji. Seeing his position isolated and that he could not advance deeply, he thereupon withdrew his army.)〉

entries.zh: 行至興州，感憤而卒。
entries.en: He reached Xing Prefecture and died there, overcome with grief and anger.
entries.literal: Reaching Xing Prefecture, he died of grief and indignation.

entries.zh: 高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝，姓石氏，諱敬瑭，太原人也。
entries.en: Gaozu, the Sagely, Cultured, Martial, and Virtuous Emperor of Brilliant Filial Piety, was of the Shi clan; his personal name was Jingtang, and he came from Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Gaozu, the Sagely, Cultured, Martial, and Virtuous Emperor of Brilliant Filial Piety, bore the surname Shi and the taboo name Jingtang; he was a native of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 本衛大夫碏、漢丞相奮之後，漢衰，關輔亂，子孫流泛西裔，故有居甘州者焉。
entries.en: He was descended from Qi, grandee of Wei, and Fen, chancellor of Han. When the Han dynasty waned and the Guanzhong region was thrown into chaos, his forebears scattered toward the western marches, and some of the family eventually settled in Ganzhou.
entries.literal: His lineage traced to Wei grandee Qi and Han chancellor Fen; when Han declined and Guanfu fell into disorder, descendants drifted westward, and thus some came to dwell in Ganzhou.

entries.zh: 四代祖璟，以唐元和中與沙陀軍都督朱耶氏自靈武入附，憲宗嘉之，隸為河東陰山府裨校，以邊功累官至朔州刺史。
entries.en: His fourth-generation ancestor Jing, in the Yuanhe reign of Tang, entered allegiance from Lingwu together with the Zhu Ye clan, commanders of the Shatuo army. Emperor Xianzong rewarded him with appointment as a deputy officer of the Yinshan Garrison in Hedong, and through repeated frontier achievements he rose step by step to governor of Shuozhou.
entries.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor Jing, in the Yuanhe era of Tang together with Shatuo military commissioner Zhu Ye's clan, came from Lingwu to submit; Emperor Xianzong commended him, enrolled him as a deputy officer of Hedong's Yinshan Garrison, and through frontier merit rose in succession to governor of Shuozhou.

entries.zh: 天福二年，追尊為孝安皇帝，廟號靖祖，陵曰義陵。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianfu, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiao'an, with the temple name Jingzu and the mausoleum Yiling.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianfu, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Xiao'an, with temple name Jingzu and mausoleum called Yiling.

entries.zh: 祖妣秦氏，追謚為孝安元皇后。
entries.en: His ancestress Lady Qin was posthumously titled Empress Yuan of Xiao'an.
entries.literal: His ancestress, née Qin, was posthumously given the title Empress Yuan of Xiao'an.

entries.zh: 三代祖郴，早薨，贈左散騎常侍，追尊為孝簡皇帝，廟號肅祖，陵曰惠陵。
entries.en: His third-generation ancestor Chen died young. He was posthumously made Left Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary and honored as Emperor Xiaojian, with the temple name Suzu and the mausoleum Huiling.
entries.literal: His third-generation ancestor Chen died young; he was posthumously given the office of Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and honored as Emperor Xiaojian, with temple name Suzu and mausoleum Huiling.

entries.zh: 祖妣安氏，追謚孝簡恭皇后。
entries.en: His ancestress Lady An was posthumously titled Empress Gong of Xiaojian.
entries.literal: His ancestress, née An, was posthumously given the title Empress Gong of Xiaojian.

entries.zh: 皇祖諱翌，任振武防禦使，贈尚書右僕射，追尊孝平皇帝，廟號睿祖，陵曰康陵。
entries.en: His imperial grandfather, whose name was Yi, served as defense commissioner of Zhenwu. He was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and honored as Emperor Xiaoping, with the temple name Ruizu and the mausoleum Kangling.
entries.literal: His imperial grandfather, taboo name Yi, served as defense commissioner of Zhenwu; he was posthumously given the office of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and honored as Emperor Xiaoping, with temple name Ruizu and mausoleum Kangling.

entries.zh: 祖妣米氏，追謚孝平獻皇后。
entries.en: His paternal grandmother, Lady Mi, was posthumously titled Empress Xian of Xiaoping.
entries.literal: His paternal grandmother, née Mi, was posthumously given the title Empress Xian of Xiaoping.

entries.zh: 皇考諱紹雍，番字臬捩雞，善騎射，有經遠大略，事後唐武皇及莊宗，累立戰功，與周德威相亞，歷平、洺二州刺史，薨於任，贈太傅，追尊為孝元皇帝，廟號憲祖，陵曰昌陵。
entries.en: His imperial father, whose name was Shaoyong, also bore the non-Chinese name Niejieji. Skilled in horsemanship and archery and possessed of broad strategic vision, he served Later Tang's Martial Emperor and Emperor Zhuangzong, winning repeated battle honors and ranking only below Zhou Dewei. He served as prefect of Ping and Mo, died in office, was posthumously made Grand Tutor, and was honored as Emperor Xiaoyuan, with the temple name Xianzu and the mausoleum Changling.
entries.literal: His imperial father, taboo name Shaoyong, bore the barbarian name Niejieji, excelled at mounted archery, possessed far-reaching strategic vision, served Later Tang's Martial Emperor and Emperor Zhuangzong, repeatedly won battle merit ranking second only to Zhou Dewei, served as prefect of Ping and Mo prefectures, died in office, was posthumously given Grand Tutor, and honored as Emperor Xiaoyuan with temple name Xianzu and mausoleum Changling.

entries.zh: 皇妣何氏，追謚孝元懿皇后。
entries.en: His imperial mother, Lady He, was posthumously titled Empress Yi of Xiaoyuan.
entries.literal: His imperial mother, née He, was posthumously given the title Empress Yi of Xiaoyuan.

entries.zh: 帝即孝元之第二子也，以唐景福元年二月二十八日生於太原汾陽裏，時有白氣充庭，人甚異焉。
entries.en: The Emperor was the second son of Xiaoyuan. On the twenty-eighth day of the second month of the first year of Jingfu of Tang he was born in Fenyang Lane in Taiyuan. White vapor then filled the courtyard, and people were greatly astonished.
entries.literal: The Emperor was the second son of Xiaoyuan; on the twenty-eighth day of the second month of the first year of Jingfu of Tang he was born in Fenyang Lane of Taiyuan, and at that time white vapor filled the courtyard, which people regarded as very strange.

entries.zh: 及長，性沈淡，寡言笑，讀兵法，重李牧、周亞夫行事。
entries.en: As he grew to manhood, he was reserved and quiet, seldom speaking or laughing. He studied military texts and admired the careers of Li Mu and Zhou Yafu.
entries.literal: When he grew up, his nature was deep and calm; he spoke little and laughed rarely, studied military treatises, and esteemed the conduct of Li Mu and Zhou Yafu.

entries.zh: 唐明宗為代州刺史，每深心器之，因妻以愛女。
entries.en: When Emperor Mingzong of Tang was prefect of Daizhou, he took a deep liking to him and gave him his beloved daughter in marriage.
entries.literal: When Tang's Emperor Mingzong was prefect of Daizhou, he deeply valued him in his heart and therefore gave him his beloved daughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 唐莊宗聞其善射，擢居左右，明宗請隸大軍，從之。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang heard of his skill in archery, he brought him into his personal service. Mingzong asked that he be assigned to the main army, and the request was granted.
entries.literal: When Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong heard of his skill in archery, he promoted him to his personal entourage; Mingzong requested that he be assigned to the main army, and this was granted.

entries.zh: 後明宗從莊宗征行，命帝領親騎，號「三討軍」，倚以心腹。
entries.en: Later, when Mingzong followed Zhuangzong on campaign, he put the Emperor in command of the personal cavalry, a unit called the "Three Campaigns Army," and treated him as a trusted inner circle man.
entries.literal: Later, when Mingzong followed Zhuangzong on campaign, he ordered the Emperor to lead the personal cavalry, styled the "Three Campaigns Army," and relied on him as a trusted confidant.

entries.zh: 天祐十二年，莊宗並有河北之地，開府於鄴，梁遣上將劉鄩以兵五萬營於莘。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Tianyou, Zhuangzong brought all of Hebei under his control and opened his headquarters at Ye. Liang sent its senior general Liu Xun with fifty thousand troops to encamp at Shen.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianyou, Zhuangzong united the Hebei region, established his headquarters at Ye, and Liang sent its senior general Liu Xun with fifty thousand troops to encamp at Shen.

entries.zh: 十三年二月，鄩引兵突至清平，薄於城下。
entries.en: In the second month of the thirteenth year, Xun marched his army in a sudden rush to Qingping and pressed up under the city walls.
entries.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year, Xun led his troops in a sudden advance to Qingping and pressed close beneath the city walls.

entries.zh: 莊宗至自甘陵，兵未陣，多為鄩所掩。
entries.en: Zhuangzong arrived from Ganling before the army had finished forming its ranks, and many units were caught and overrun by Xun.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong arrived from Ganling before the troops had formed ranks, and many were caught and overrun by Xun.

entries.zh: 帝領十餘騎，橫槊深入，東西馳突，無敢當者，卒全部伍而還。
entries.en: The Emperor led a dozen horsemen, spear in hand, and plunged deep into the enemy lines, charging back and forth until no one dared stand against him. He finally brought the whole unit back intact.
entries.literal: The Emperor led a dozen or more horsemen, spear levelled, plunged deep in, charged east and west, and none dared oppose him; he finally brought the whole unit back intact.

entries.zh: 莊宗壯之，拊其背曰：「將門出將，言不謬爾。」
entries.en: Zhuangzong was impressed by his bravery, clapped him on the back, and said, "A general's house breeds a general—the saying is no empty phrase."
entries.literal: Zhuangzong admired his valor, clapped him on the back, and said, "A general's house produces a general—the saying is not mistaken."

entries.zh: 因頒以器帛，復親為啖酥，當時以為異恩，由是知名。
entries.en: He then awarded him vessels and silks and personally fed him butter in token of honor. At the time this was regarded as extraordinary favor, and from then on his name was widely known.
entries.literal: He thereupon bestowed vessels and silks on him and personally fed him butter in token of honor; at the time this was regarded as extraordinary favor, and from this he became well known.

entries.zh: 明年，鄩兵陣於莘之西北，明宗從莊宗酣戰。
entries.en: The following year, Xun's army drew up northwest of Shen, and Mingzong fought alongside Zhuangzong in a hard-fought battle.
entries.literal: The next year, Xun's army formed battle lines northwest of Shen, and Mingzong followed Zhuangzong in fierce fighting.

entries.zh: 久之，塵埃四合，帝與明宗俱陷陣內，帝挺身躍劍，反復轉鬥，行數十里，逐鄩於故元城之東。
entries.en: After a long while dust blotted out the field on every side. Both the Emperor and Mingzong were caught inside the enemy formation. The Emperor threw himself forward with sword drawn and fought back and forth for miles, finally driving Xun east of the old Yuancheng.
entries.literal: After a long while dust rose on all sides; the Emperor and Mingzong both fell into the midst of the enemy lines. The Emperor threw himself forward, sword drawn, and fought back and forth repeatedly, travelling several tens of li and driving Xun east of the old Yuancheng.

entries.zh: 是日，鄩軍殺傷過半。
entries.en: That day more than half of Xun's army were killed or wounded.
entries.literal: That day, more than half of Xun's army were killed or wounded.

entries.zh: 是時，秦王從榮奏：「伏見北面頻奏報，契丹族移帳近塞，吐渾、突厥已侵邊地，戍兵雖多，未有統帥，早宜命大將一人，以安雲、朔。」
entries.en: At that time Prince of Qin Congrong memorialized: "I have seen repeated reports from the northern frontier that the Khitan have moved their camps close to the border, and that the Tuyuhun and Turks have already invaded the frontier. Although garrison troops are numerous, there is no commander in chief. A great general should be appointed at once to secure Yun and Shuo."
entries.literal: At that time Prince of Qin Congrong memorialized: "I have seen repeated reports from the northern frontier that the Khitan tribes have moved their camps close to the border, and the Tuyuhun and Turks have already invaded the frontier regions; although garrison troops are numerous, there is as yet no commander—it would be well to appoint one great general early to secure Yun and Shuo."

entries.zh: 明宗曰：「卿等商量。」
entries.en: Mingzong said, "You ministers should deliberate."
entries.literal: Mingzong said, "You ministers deliberate."

entries.zh: 從榮與諸大臣奏曰：「將校之中，唯石敬瑭、康義誠二人可行。」
entries.en: Congrong and the ministers memorialized: "Among the generals and officers, only Shi Jingtang and Kang Yicheng are fit for the task."
entries.literal: Congrong and the various ministers memorialized: "Among the generals and officers, only Shi Jingtang and Kang Yicheng are fit for the task."

entries.zh: 帝素不欲為禁軍之副，即奏曰：「臣願北行。」
entries.en: The Emperor had long wished to leave his post as deputy of the palace army and immediately memorialized: "Your servant is willing to go north."
entries.literal: The Emperor had long not wished to serve as deputy of the palace army and immediately memorialized: "Your servant is willing to go north."

entries.zh: 明宗曰：「卿為吾行，事無不濟。」
entries.en: Mingzong said, "If you go for me, nothing will fail."
entries.literal: Mingzong said, "If you go for me, nothing will fail."

entries.zh: 及受詔，不落六軍副使，帝復遷延辭避。
entries.en: When he received the edict he was not removed from his deputy post in the Six Armies, and the Emperor again delayed and declined.
entries.literal: When he received the edict, he was not removed from the deputy post of the Six Armies; the Emperor again delayed and declined.

entries.zh: 十一月乙酉，明宗復謂侍臣曰：「雲州奏，契丹自幽州移帳，言就放牧，終冬不退，其患深矣。」
entries.en: On the yiyou day of the eleventh month Mingzong again told his attending ministers: "Yunzhou reports that the Khitan have moved their camps from Youzhou, saying they have come to pasture. They will not withdraw all winter. The danger is grave."
entries.literal: On the yiyou day of the eleventh month Mingzong again said to his attending ministers: "Yunzhou reports that the Khitan have moved their camps from Youzhou, saying they are coming to pasture; they will not withdraw all winter—the peril is grave."

entries.zh: 樞密使範延光奏曰：「已議石敬瑭與康義誠北行，然其定奪，即在宸旨。」
entries.en: Chief Palace Secretary Fan Yanguang memorialized: "Shi Jingtang and Kang Yicheng going north have already been discussed, but the final decision rests with Your Majesty."
entries.literal: Chief Palace Secretary Fan Yanguang memorialized: "Shi Jingtang and Kang Yicheng going north have already been discussed, but the final decision rests with Your Majesty's intent."

entries.zh: 帝奏曰：「臣雖不才，爭敢避事，但進退惟命。」
entries.en: The Emperor memorialized: "Although I lack talent, how could I dare avoid duty? I await only Your Majesty's command whether to go or stay."
entries.literal: The Emperor memorialized: "Although your servant lacks talent, how would he dare avoid duty? Only advance or retreat await Your command."

entries.zh: 明宗曰：「卿為吾行，甚葉眾議。」
entries.en: Mingzong said, "If you go for me, it accords very well with what everyone expects."
entries.literal: Mingzong said, "If you go for me, it accords very well with public opinion."

entries.zh: 由是遂定。
entries.en: From this the matter was settled.
entries.literal: From this the matter was settled.

entries.zh: 丁亥，加兼侍中、太原尹、北京留守、河東節度使，兼大同、振武、彰國、威塞等軍蕃漢馬步軍總管，改賜竭忠匡運寧國功臣。
entries.en: On the dinghai day he was additionally made Palace Attendant, prefect of Taiyuan, garrison commander of the Northern Capital, and military commissioner of Hedong, with overall command of the Han and non-Han horse and foot forces of the Datong, Zhenwu, Zhangguo, Weisai, and other armies. His title was changed to Meritorious Minister Who Exhausts Loyalty, Rectifies Fortune, and Pacifies the State.
entries.literal: On the dinghai day he was additionally made Palace Attendant, prefect of Taiyuan, garrison commander of the Northern Capital, military commissioner of Hedong, and overall commander of the Han and non-Han horse and foot forces of the Datong, Zhenwu, Zhangguo, Weisai, and other armies; his title was changed to Meritorious Minister Who Exhausts Loyalty, Rectifies Fortune, and Pacifies the State.

entries.zh: 翌日，宴於中興殿，帝捧觴上壽，因奏曰：「臣雖微怯，惟邊事敢不盡其忠力，但臣遠違玉階，無以時申補報。」
entries.en: The next day, at a banquet in the Hall of Central Revival, the Emperor raised his cup to wish the emperor long life and memorialized: "Although I am slight and timid, in frontier affairs how could I fail to give my full loyalty and strength? Yet I am far from the throne and have no means to repay Your Majesty in timely fashion."
entries.literal: The next day, at a banquet in the Hall of Central Revival, the Emperor raised his cup to offer longevity and memorialized: "Although your servant is slight and timid, in frontier affairs how would he dare not exhaust loyalty and strength? Yet your servant is far from the jade steps and has no means to offer timely recompense."

entries.zh: 帝因再拜告辭，明宗泣下沾衿。
entries.en: The Emperor bowed twice in farewell. Mingzong wept until his collar was wet.
entries.literal: The Emperor thereupon bowed twice in farewell; Mingzong wept until his collar was wet.

entries.zh: 左右怪其過傷，果與帝因此為訣，不復相見矣。
entries.en: Those at his side wondered at such excessive grief. Indeed, from this the Emperor and he took their leave of one another and never met again.
entries.literal: Those at his side wondered at such excessive grief; indeed, from this the Emperor and he took leave of one another and never met again.

entries.zh: 十二月，明宗晏駕，帝聞之，長慟若喪考妣。
entries.en: In the twelfth month Mingzong died. When the Emperor heard of it, he mourned long and deeply as if he had lost his own parents.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month Mingzong died; when the Emperor heard of it, he mourned long and deeply as if he had lost father and mother.

entries.zh: 應順元年正月，閔帝即位，加中書令，及增食邑。
entries.en: In the first month of the first year of Yingshun, Emperor Min took the throne. The Emperor was made Chief of the Secretariat and his fief was increased.
entries.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yingshun, Emperor Min took the throne; the Emperor was made Chief of the Secretariat and his fief was increased.

entries.zh: 是月，明宗入洛，嘉帝之功，自總管府都校署陜府兵馬留後。
entries.en: That month Mingzong entered Luoyang, praised the Emperor's achievements, and promoted him from chief officer of the general commander's office to military commissioner and acting prefect of Shaan.
entries.literal: That month Mingzong entered Luoyang, praised the Emperor's merit, and promoted him from chief officer of the general commander's office to military commissioner and acting prefect of Shaan prefecture.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，改元天成，五月，加帝光祿大夫、檢校司徒，充陜州保義軍節度使，歲未期而軍民之政大治焉。
entries.en: When Mingzong took the throne he changed the era name to Tiancheng. In the fifth month he gave the Emperor the titles Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Honorary Minister of Education and appointed him military commissioner of the Baoyi Army at Shaanzhou. Before a year had passed both military and civil administration were in excellent order.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he changed the era name to Tiancheng; in the fifth month he added for the Emperor the titles Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Honorary Minister of Education, and appointed him military commissioner of the Baoyi Army of Shaanzhou; before a year had passed both military and civil administration were greatly well ordered.

entries.zh: 二年二月，加檢校太傅兼六軍諸衛副使，進封開國伯，增食邑四百戶。
entries.en: In the second month of the second year he was made Honorary Grand Tutor and concurrent deputy commander of the Six Armies and various guards, advanced in enfeoffment to Baron of the Opening State, and granted four hundred additional households in his fief.
entries.literal: In the second month of the second year he was given the additional title of Honorary Grand Tutor and concurrent deputy commander of the Six Armies and various guards, advanced in enfeoffment to Baron of the Opening State, and granted four hundred additional households in his fief.

entries.zh: 是月，帝赴闕，以倅六軍諸衛事故也。
entries.en: That month the Emperor went to court in connection with his duties as deputy commander of the Six Armies and various guards.
entries.literal: That month the Emperor went to court because of his duties as deputy commander of the Six Armies and various guards.

entries.zh: 八月，加食邑八百戶，實封一百戶，旌為政之效也。
entries.en: In the eighth month his fief was increased by eight hundred households and his actual enfeoffment by one hundred households, in recognition of the effect of his governance.
entries.literal: In the eighth month his fief was increased by eight hundred households and his actual enfeoffment by one hundred households, in recognition of the effect of his governance.

entries.zh: 十月，明宗幸汴，以帝為御營使。
entries.en: In the tenth month Mingzong visited Bian and made the Emperor director of the imperial camp.
entries.literal: In the tenth month Mingzong visited Bian and made the Emperor director of the imperial camp.

entries.zh: 車駕次京水，飛報汴州節度使朱守殷叛，明宗命帝董親軍倍道星行，信宿及浚城，一戰而拔之。
entries.en: When the imperial carriage halted at Jingshui, urgent reports arrived that Zhu Shouyin, military commissioner of Bianzhou, had rebelled. Mingzong ordered the Emperor to lead the personal army by forced marches day and night. Within two nights he reached Xun city and took it in one battle.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage halted at Jingshui, urgent reports arrived that Bianzhou military commissioner Zhu Shouyin had rebelled; Mingzong ordered the Emperor to lead the personal army by forced marches day and night; within two nights he reached Xun city and took it in one battle.

entries.zh: 尋以帝為宣武軍節度使、侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使兼六軍諸衛副使，進封開國公，加食邑五百戶，賜耀忠匡定保節功臣。
entries.en: Soon he was made military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army, commander-in-chief of the personal army's horse and foot forces, and concurrent deputy commander of the Six Armies and various guards. He was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of the Opening State, granted five hundred additional households in his fief, and given the title Meritorious Minister Who Glorifies Loyalty, Rectifies and Secures, and Preserves Integrity.
entries.literal: Soon he was made military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army, commander-in-chief of the personal army's horse and foot forces, and concurrent deputy commander of the Six Armies and various guards; he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of the Opening State, granted five hundred additional households in his fief, and given the title of Meritorious Minister Who Glorifies Loyalty, Rectifies and Secures, and Preserves Integrity.

entries.zh: 三年四月，車駕還洛，制加檢校太傅、同中書門下平章事、興唐尹、鄴都留守、天雄軍節度使。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the third year, when the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang, an edict made him Honorary Grand Tutor, Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, prefect of Xingtang, garrison commander of Yedu, and military commissioner of the Tianxiong Army.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, when the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang, an edict added for him Honorary Grand Tutor, Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, prefect of Xingtang, garrison commander of Yedu, and military commissioner of the Tianxiong Army.

entries.zh: 五月丁未，加駙馬都尉。
entries.en: On the dingwei day of the fifth month he was made Commandant of the Imperial Sons-in-Law.
entries.literal: On the dingwei day of the fifth month he was made Commandant of the Imperial Sons-in-Law.

entries.zh: 長興元年二月，明宗南郊禮畢，加檢校太尉，增食邑五百戶，尋詔歸任。
entries.en: In the second month of the first year of Changxing, when Mingzong had completed the southern suburban sacrifice, he added for the Emperor the title of Honorary Grand Commandant, increased his fief by five hundred households, and soon ordered him to return to his post.
entries.literal: In the second month of the first year of Changxing, when Mingzong had completed the southern suburban sacrifice, he added for the Emperor the title of Honorary Grand Commandant, increased his fief by five hundred households, and soon ordered him to return to his post.

entries.zh: 時鄴都繁富為天下之冠，而土俗獷悍，民多爭訟，帝令投函府門，一一覽之，及逾年，盈積几案，滯於獄者甚眾，時論以此減之。
entries.en: At that time Yedu was the wealthiest place under heaven, but local customs were fierce and truculent and the people were much given to lawsuits. The Emperor ordered that complaint letters be deposited in a box at the government gate and read each one himself. After more than a year his desks were piled high, and many cases were backlogged in the courts; contemporary opinion lowered its estimate of him on this account.
entries.literal: At that time Yedu was the wealthiest place under heaven, but local customs were fierce and truculent and the people were much given to lawsuits. The Emperor ordered that complaint letters be deposited in a box at the government gate, and he read each one in turn. After more than a year the desks were piled full, and many cases were backlogged in the courts; contemporary opinion lowered its estimate of him on this account.

entries.zh: 九月，東川董璋叛，朝廷命帝為東川行營都招討使，兼知東川行府事。
entries.en: In the ninth month Dong Zhang of Dongchuan rebelled. The court appointed the Emperor commander-in-chief of the Dongchuan expeditionary forces and gave him concurrent control of the Dongchuan expeditionary headquarters.
entries.literal: In the ninth month Dong Zhang of Dongchuan rebelled; the court appointed the Emperor commander-in-chief of the Dongchuan expeditionary forces, with concurrent control of the Dongchuan expeditionary headquarters.

entries.zh: 十月，至自魏博，董眾西征。
entries.en: In the tenth month, having returned from Weibo, he led the army west on campaign.
entries.literal: In the tenth month, having returned from Weibo, he led the host west on campaign.

entries.zh: 二年春，以川路險艱，糧運不繼，詔班師。
entries.en: In the spring of the second year, because the Sichuan routes were perilous and arduous and grain transport could not keep up, an edict ordered withdrawal of the army.
entries.literal: In the spring of the second year, because the Sichuan routes were perilous and arduous and grain transport could not keep up, an edict ordered withdrawal of the army.

entries.zh: 四月，復兼六軍諸衛副使。
entries.en: In the fourth month he was again made concurrent deputy commander of the Six Armies and various guards.
entries.literal: In the fourth month he was again made concurrent deputy commander of the Six Armies and various guards.

entries.zh: 六月，改河陽節度使，仍兼兵柄。
entries.en: In the sixth month he was transferred to military commissioner of Heyang while retaining command of the army.
entries.literal: In the sixth month he was transferred to military commissioner of Heyang, while retaining command of the army.

entries.zh: 帝性簡儉，未嘗以聲色滋味輒自宴樂，每公退，必召幕客論民間利害及刑政得失，明而難犯，事多親決。
entries.en: The Emperor was simple and frugal by nature. He never indulged himself in music, women, or fine food for private pleasure. Whenever he left public duties he summoned his staff to discuss what helped or harmed the people and what was right or wrong in penal administration. He was clear-minded and hard to cross, and he decided many matters personally.
entries.literal: The Emperor's nature was simple and frugal; he never indulged himself in music, women, or fine flavors for private pleasure. Whenever he left public duties he would summon staff members to discuss the benefits and harms to the people and the gains and losses in penal administration; he was clear-minded and hard to offend against, and many affairs he decided personally.

entries.zh: 有店婦與軍士訟，云「曝粟於門，為馬所食」。
entries.en: A shopkeeper's wife sued a soldier, saying, "I spread grain to dry at the door and a horse ate it."
entries.literal: A shopkeeper's wife sued a soldier, saying, "I spread grain to dry at the door and a horse ate it."

entries.zh: 而軍士懇訴，無以自明。
entries.en: The soldier pleaded earnestly but had no way to clear himself.
entries.literal: The soldier pleaded earnestly but had no means to clear himself.

entries.zh: 帝謂鞫吏曰：「兩訟未分，何以為斷？
entries.en: The Emperor said to the examining officer: "The two suits are unresolved. How can there be a judgment?
entries.literal: The Emperor said to the examining officer: "The two suits are undivided—how can there be a judgment?

entries.zh: 可殺馬刳腸而視其粟，有則軍士誅，無則婦人死。」
entries.en: Kill the horse, open its belly, and look for grain. If there is grain, execute the soldier; if not, the woman dies."
entries.literal: You may kill the horse, open its belly, and look at the grain; if there is grain, execute the soldier; if not, the woman dies."

entries.zh: 遂殺馬，馬腸無粟，因戮其婦人。
entries.en: They killed the horse. Its intestines held no grain, and therefore they executed the woman.
entries.literal: They then killed the horse; the horse's intestines held no grain, and therefore they executed the woman.

entries.zh: 境內肅然，莫敢以欺事言者。
entries.en: Within the territory all was solemn, and none dared bring a deceitful suit.
entries.literal: Within the territory all was solemn; none dared speak of deceit in lawsuits.

entries.zh: 三月，移鎮常山。
entries.en: In the third month he was transferred to garrison Changshan.
entries.literal: In the third month he was transferred to garrison Changshan.

entries.zh: 所歷方鎮，以孝治為急，見民間父母在昆弟分索者，必繩而殺之。
entries.en: In every command where he served he made filial governance a priority. When he saw brothers dividing and seizing property while their parents were still living, he always had them bound and executed.
entries.literal: In every command where he served, he made filial governance urgent; when he saw among the people parents and sons dividing property with brothers, he always bound and executed them.

entries.zh: 勤於吏事，廷無滯訟。
entries.en: He was diligent in administrative affairs, and no lawsuit stalled in court.
entries.literal: He was diligent in administrative affairs, and in court there were no stalled lawsuits.

entries.zh: 常山屬邑曰九門，有人鬻地與異居兄，議價不定，乃移於他人。
entries.en: A subordinate county of Changshan was called Jiumen. Someone sold land to a brother living separately, but they could not agree on a price, so he sold it to someone else.
entries.literal: A subordinate county of Changshan was called Jiumen; someone sold land to a brother living separately, the price could not be settled, and he then transferred it to another person.

entries.zh: 他人須兄立券，兄固抑之，因訴於令。
entries.en: The buyer required the brother to draw up the deed, but the brother firmly refused, and therefore sued before the magistrate.
entries.literal: The other person required the brother to draw up the deed; the brother firmly refused, and therefore sued before the magistrate.

entries.zh: 令以弟兄俱不義，送府。
entries.en: The magistrate held that both brothers were in the wrong and sent the case to the prefectural office.
entries.literal: The magistrate held that both brothers were unrighteous and sent the case to the prefectural office.

entries.zh: 帝監之曰：「人之不義，由牧長新至，教化所未能及，吾甚愧焉。
entries.en: The Emperor reviewed the case and said: "Men's lack of righteousness comes from the prefect having newly arrived and instruction not yet reaching them. I am deeply ashamed.
entries.literal: The Emperor reviewed it and said: "Men's lack of righteousness comes from the prefect having newly arrived and instruction not yet reaching them—I am deeply ashamed.

entries.zh: 若以至理言之，兄利良田，弟求善價，順之則是，沮之則非，其兄不義之甚也，宜重笞焉。
entries.en: Speaking in terms of supreme principle, the elder brother wanted fertile land while the younger wanted a fair price. To go along would be right, to obstruct would be wrong. The elder brother was deeply in the wrong and deserved a heavy beating.
entries.literal: If one speaks in terms of supreme principle, the elder brother sought fertile fields while the younger sought a fair price—going along would be right, obstructing would be wrong; that elder brother was deeply unrighteous and ought to receive heavy beating.

entries.zh: 市田以高價者取之。」
entries.en: The land went to whoever bought it at the higher price."
entries.literal: The one who bought the land at the higher price took it."

entries.zh: 上下服其明。
entries.en: Superiors and subordinates alike admired his clarity of judgment.
entries.literal: Both superiors and subordinates admired his clarity.

entries.zh: 及岐陽兵亂，推潞王為天子，閔帝急詔帝赴闕，欲以社稷為托。
entries.en: When the Qiyang army rebelled and raised the Prince of Lu as emperor, Emperor Min urgently summoned the Emperor to court, intending to entrust the realm to him.
entries.literal: When the Qiyang army rebelled and raised the Prince of Lu as Son of Heaven, Emperor Min urgently summoned the Emperor to court, wishing to entrust the altars of state to him.

entries.zh: 閔帝自洛陽出奔於衛，相遇於途，遂與閔帝回入衛州。
entries.en: Emperor Min fled Luoyang toward Wei. They met on the road, and the Emperor turned back with him into Weizhou.
entries.literal: Emperor Min fled from Luoyang toward Wei; they met on the road, and the Emperor thereupon returned with Emperor Min into Weizhou.

entries.zh: 時閔帝左右將不利於帝，帝覺之，因擒其從騎百餘人。
entries.en: At that time those about Emperor Min were about to move against the Emperor. He sensed it and seized more than a hundred of their attendant horsemen.
entries.literal: At that time those about Emperor Min were about to act against the Emperor; he perceived it and therefore seized more than a hundred of their attendant horsemen.

entries.zh: 閔帝知事不濟，與帝長慟而別，帝遣刺史王宏贄安置閔帝於公舍而去，尋為潞王所害，帝後長以此愧心焉。
entries.en: Emperor Min knew the affair was lost and parted from the Emperor in long, bitter weeping. The Emperor sent Prefect Wang Hongzan to lodge Emperor Min in a public residence and then departed. Before long Emperor Min was killed by the Prince of Lu, and the Emperor carried guilt over this for the rest of his life.
entries.literal: Emperor Min knew the affair would not succeed and parted from the Emperor in long, bitter weeping; the Emperor sent prefect Wang Hongzan to lodge Emperor Min in a public residence and then departed; before long Emperor Min was killed by the Prince of Lu, and the Emperor long afterward bore this on his conscience.

entries.zh: 清泰元年五月，復授太原節度使、北京留守，充大同、振武、彰國、威塞等軍蕃漢馬步總管。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the first year of Qingtai he was again made military commissioner of Taiyuan and garrison commander of the Northern Capital, with overall command of the Han and non-Han horse and foot forces of the Datong, Zhenwu, Zhangguo, Weisai, and other armies.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Qingtai he was again appointed military commissioner of Taiyuan and garrison commander of the Northern Capital, and made overall commander of the Han and non-Han horse and foot forces of the Datong, Zhenwu, Zhangguo, Weisai, and other armies.

entries.zh: 二年夏，帝屯軍於忻州，朝廷遣使送夏衣，傳詔撫諭，後軍人遽呼萬歲者數四，帝懼，斬挾馬將李暉以下三十餘人以徇，乃止。
entries.en: In the summer of the second year the Emperor encamped at Xinzhou. The court sent envoys with summer garments and an edict of reassurance, but afterward the soldiers suddenly shouted "Long live!" four times. The Emperor was alarmed, executed the horse-gripping general Li Hui and more than thirty men as a warning, and only then did it stop.
entries.literal: In the summer of the second year the Emperor encamped his army at Xinzhou; the court sent envoys bearing summer garments and an edict of reassurance, but afterward the soldiers suddenly shouted "Long live!" four times; the Emperor was afraid, executed the horse-gripping general Li Hui and more than thirty men below him as a warning, and only then did it stop.

entries.zh: 三年五月，移授鄆州節度使，進封趙國公，仍改扶天啟運中正功臣。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the third year he was transferred to military commissioner of Yunzhou, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Zhao, and his title was changed to Meritorious Minister Who Supports Heaven, Initiates Fortune, and Upholds Rectitude.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the third year he was transferred to military commissioner of Yunzhou, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Zhao, and his title was changed to Meritorious Minister Who Supports Heaven, Initiates Fortune, and Upholds Rectitude.

entries.zh: 尋降詔促帝赴任。
entries.en: Soon an edict was issued ordering the Emperor to take up his new post at once.
entries.literal: Soon an edict was issued urging the Emperor to take up his post.

entries.zh: 帝心疑之，乃召僚佐議曰：「孤再受太原之日，主上面宣云：『與卿北門，一生無議除改。』
entries.en: The Emperor grew suspicious and summoned his staff to discuss the matter. He said, "When I received Taiyuan a second time, the ruler announced to my face: 'I give you the northern gate; in your lifetime there shall be no talk of transfer or removal.'
entries.literal: The Emperor grew suspicious in his heart and therefore summoned his staff to discuss, saying, "When I received Taiyuan a second time, the ruler announced to my face: 'I give you the northern gate; in your lifetime there shall be no talk of transfer or removal.'

entries.zh: 今忽降此命，莫是以去年忻州亂兵見迫，過相猜乎？
entries.en: Now this command suddenly arrives. Can it be that because last year at Xinzhou the mutinous troops pressed me, he suspects me beyond measure?
entries.literal: Now this command suddenly descends—can it be that because last year at Xinzhou the mutinous troops pressed me, he suspects me excessively?

entries.zh: 又今年千春節，公主入覲，當辭時，謂公主曰：『爾歸心甚急，欲與石郎反耶？』
entries.en: Moreover, at this year's Thousand Spring Festival when the princess came to court, as she was taking leave he said to her, 'Your heart to return is very urgent. Do you wish to rebel with Master Shi?'
entries.literal: Moreover, at this year's Thousand Spring Festival when the princess came to court, as she was taking leave he said to the princess, 'Your heart to return is very urgent—do you wish to rebel with Master Shi?'

entries.zh: 此疑我之狀固且明矣。
entries.en: His suspicion of me is already perfectly clear.
entries.literal: His suspicion of me is already quite clear.

entries.zh: 今天子用後族，委邪臣，沈湎荒惑，萬機停壅，失刑失賞，不亡何待！
entries.en: Now the emperor employs the empress's kin, entrusts wicked ministers, and sinks in dissipation and delusion. The myriad affairs of state are stalled, punishments and rewards are lost. If such a ruler does not perish, what is he waiting for!
entries.literal: Now the Son of Heaven employs the empress's kin, entrusts wicked ministers, sinks in dissipation and delusion, and the myriad affairs are stalled and blocked; punishments and rewards are lost—if he does not perish, what is he waiting for!

entries.zh: 吾自應順中少主出奔之日，睹人情大去，不能扶危持顛，憤憤於方寸者三年矣。
entries.en: From the day in Yingshun when the young ruler fled, I have seen popular sentiment turn away and have been unable to support what was tottering and uphold what was falling. I have burned with anger in my breast for three years.
entries.literal: From the day in Yingshun when the young ruler fled, I have seen popular sentiment largely depart and have been unable to support what was tottering and uphold what was falling; I have burned with anger in my breast for three years.

entries.zh: 今我無異志，朝廷自啟禍機，不可安然死於道路。
entries.en: Now I have no other intent. The court itself has opened the springs of disaster. I cannot die peacefully on the road.
entries.literal: Now I have no other intent; the court itself has opened the springs of disaster—I cannot die peacefully on the road.

entries.zh: 況太原險固之地，積粟甚多，若且寬我，我當奉之。
entries.en: Moreover, Taiyuan is a strong and secure place with grain stored in great abundance. If you will only spare me for now, I shall serve you.
entries.literal: Moreover, Taiyuan is a perilous and secure place with grain stored in great abundance; if you will only spare me for now, I shall serve you.

entries.zh: 必若加兵，我則外告鄰方，北構強敵，興亡之數，皎皎在天。
entries.en: If you must send troops, I shall appeal to neighboring powers and ally with strong enemies to the north. Whether we rise or fall shines bright in Heaven.
entries.literal: If you must send troops, I shall announce it abroad to neighboring regions and ally with powerful enemies to the north; the number of rise and fall shines bright in Heaven.

entries.zh: 今欲發表稱疾，以俟其意，諸公以為何如？」
entries.en: Now I wish to send in a memorial claiming illness and await his intent. What do you gentlemen think?"
entries.literal: Now I wish to send in a memorial claiming illness and await his intent—what do you gentlemen think?"

entries.zh: 〈（《玉堂閑話》：晉祖在並部，嘗從容謂賓佐云：「近因晝寢，忽夢若頃年在洛京時，與天子連鑣於路，過舊第，天子請某入其第，某遜讓者數四，不得已即促轡而入，至廳事下馬，升自阼階，西向而坐，天子已馳車去矣。
entries.en: (From 《Idle Talk of the Jade Hall》: While in Bing province, the Jin founder once said calmly to his guests and staff: "Recently, during a daytime nap, I dreamed that I was back in Luoyang years ago, riding abreast with the emperor along the road. Passing my old residence, the emperor asked me to enter. I declined several times, but unable to refuse further I urged my horse inside. Reaching the hall I dismounted, ascended from the eastern steps, and sat facing west while the emperor had already driven away.
entries.literal: (From 《Idle Talk of the Jade Hall》: The Ancestor of Jin, while in Bing province, once said calmly to his guests and staff: "Recently, because of a daytime nap, I suddenly dreamed as if in years past at Luoyang, when I and the Son of Heaven rode abreast on the road. Passing my old residence, the Son of Heaven asked me to enter his residence; I declined several times, but unable to refuse further I urged my reins and entered. Reaching the hall I dismounted, ascended from the eastern steps, and sat facing west; the Son of Heaven had already driven his carriage away.

entries.zh: 其夢如此。」
entries.en: Such was the dream."
entries.literal: The dream was like this."

entries.zh: 群僚莫敢有所答。
entries.en: None of the assembled officials dared reply.
entries.literal: None of the assembled officials dared reply.

entries.zh: 是年冬，果有鼎革之事。
entries.en: That winter there was indeed a dynastic revolution.
entries.literal: That winter there was indeed a change of the dynastic vessel.

entries.zh: 蓋晉祖懷不軌之心久矣，故托夢以惑眾也。）〉
entries.en: For the Jin founder had long harbored rebellious intent and used the dream to mislead his followers.)〉
entries.literal: For the Jin ancestor had long harbored rebellious intent and therefore used a dream to mislead the multitude.)〉

entries.zh: 掌書記桑維翰、都押衙劉知遠贊成密計，遂拒末帝之命。
entries.en: Chief secretary Sang Weihan and chief escort officer Liu Zhiyuan endorsed the secret plan, and he therefore refused the Last Emperor's command.
entries.literal: Chief secretary Sang Weihan and chief escort officer Liu Zhiyuan endorsed the secret plan, and he therefore refused the Last Emperor's command.

entries.zh: 朝廷以帝不奉詔，降旨削奪官爵，即詔晉州刺史、北面副招討使張敬達領兵圍帝於晉陽。
entries.en: Because the Emperor did not obey the edict, the court stripped his offices and titles and immediately ordered Jinzhou prefect and northern deputy campaign commander Zhang Jingda to lead troops and besiege him at Jinyang.
entries.literal: Because the Emperor did not obey the edict, the court issued an order stripping his offices and titles, and immediately ordered Jinzhou prefect and northern deputy campaign commander Zhang Jingda to lead troops and besiege the Emperor at Jinyang.

entries.zh: 帝尋命桑維翰詣諸道求援，契丹遣人復書諾之，約以中秋赴義。
entries.en: The Emperor soon sent Sang Weihan to the various circuits seeking aid. The Khitan sent a reply promising help and agreeing to come by the Mid-Autumn Festival.
entries.literal: The Emperor soon ordered Sang Weihan to go to the various circuits seeking aid; the Khitan sent men with a reply promising help, agreeing to come to his aid by the Mid-Autumn Festival.

entries.zh: 〈（《遼史太宗紀》云：七月丙申，唐河東節度使石敬瑭為其主所討，遣趙瑩求救，時趙德鈞亦遣使至，河東復遣桑維翰來告急，遂許興師。
entries.en: (The 《Basic Annals of Taizong》 in the 《History of Liao》 states: On the bingshen day of the seventh month, Tang's Hedong military commissioner Shi Jingtang was attacked by his ruler and sent Zhao Ying to seek rescue. At that time Zhao Dejun also sent envoys, and Hedong again sent Sang Weihan to report urgency, whereupon the Khitan ruler permitted the raising of troops.
entries.literal: (The 《Basic Annals of Taizong》 in the 《History of Liao》 states: On the bingshen day of the seventh month, Tang's Hedong military commissioner Shi Jingtang was attacked by his ruler and sent Zhao Ying to seek rescue; at that time Zhao Dejun also sent envoys, and Hedong again sent Sang Weihan to report urgency, whereupon he permitted the raising of troops.

entries.zh: 八月庚午，自將以援敬瑭。）〉
entries.en: On the gengwu day of the eighth month he personally led troops to rescue Jingtang.)〉
entries.literal: On the gengwu day of the eighth month he personally led troops to rescue Jingtang.)〉

entries.zh: 六月，北面招收指揮使安重榮以部曲數千人入城。
entries.en: In the sixth month, northern recruitment commander An Chongrong entered the city with several thousand men of his personal following.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, northern recruitment commander An Chongrong entered the city with several thousand men of his personal following.

entries.zh: 七月，代州屯將安元信率一軍，與西北面先鋒指揮使安審信引五百騎俱至。
entries.en: In the seventh month, Daizhou garrison commander An Yuanxin led one army, and northwest vanguard commander An Shenxin brought five hundred horsemen. All arrived together.
entries.literal: In the seventh month, Daizhou garrison commander An Yuanxin led one army, and northwest vanguard commander An Shenxin brought five hundred horsemen; all arrived together.

entries.zh: 八月，懷州彰聖軍使張萬迪等各率千餘騎來降。
entries.en: In the eighth month, Huai prefecture Zhangsheng Army commissioner Zhang Wandi and others each led more than a thousand horsemen to surrender.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, Huai prefecture Zhangsheng Army commissioner Zhang Wandi and others each led more than a thousand horsemen to surrender.

entries.zh: 是月，外眾攻我甚急，帝親當矢石，人心雖固，廩食漸困。
entries.en: That month the besieging army pressed the attack very hard. The Emperor personally faced arrows and stones. Though morale held firm, granary provisions grew strained.
entries.literal: That month the outer host pressed the attack very hard; the Emperor personally faced arrows and stones; though hearts remained firm, granary provisions grew strained.

entries.zh: 始梁開國之歲，即前唐天祐四年也，潞州行營使李思安奏：「壺關縣庶穰鄉鄉人伐樹，樹倒自分兩片，內有六字如左書，云『天十四載石進』。」
entries.en: In the year when Liang first founded its state, the fourth year of Tianyou of former Tang, Lu prefecture campaign commissioner Li Si'an memorialized: "In Shurang township of Huguan county, when villagers felled a tree, it split of itself into two pieces. Within were six characters in seal script reading 'Heaven, fourteenth year, Shi advances.'"
entries.literal: In the year when Liang first founded its state, which was the fourth year of Tianyou of former Tang, Lu prefecture campaign commissioner Li Si'an memorialized: "In Shurang township of Huguan county, when villagers felled a tree, the tree split of itself into two pieces, and within were six characters like writing in seal script, reading 'Heaven, fourteenth year, Shi advances.'"

entries.zh: 梁祖令藏於武庫，然莫詳其義。
entries.en: The Liang founder ordered it stored in the armory, yet none could make clear its meaning.
entries.literal: The Liang founder ordered it stored in the armory, yet none could make clear its meaning.

entries.zh: 至帝即位，識者曰：「『天』字取『四』字中兩畫加之於傍，則『丙』字也；
entries.en: When the Emperor took the throne, those who understood said: "If one takes the two strokes from the middle of the character for 'four' in the character for 'Heaven' and adds them to the side, one gets the character for 'bing';
entries.literal: When the Emperor took the throne, those who understood said: "If one takes the two strokes from the middle of the character for 'four' in the character for 'Heaven' and adds them to the side, one gets the character for 'bing';

entries.zh: 『四』字去中之兩畫，加『十』字，則『申』字也。」
entries.en: if one removes the two middle strokes from the character for 'four' and adds the character for 'ten,' one gets the character for 'shen.'"
entries.literal: if one removes the two middle strokes from the character for 'four' and adds the character for 'ten,' one gets the character for 'shen.'"

entries.zh: 帝即位之年乃丙申也。
entries.en: The year the Emperor took the throne was indeed bingshen.
entries.literal: The year the Emperor took the throne was indeed bingshen.

entries.zh: 又，《易》云：「晉者，進也。」
entries.en: Moreover, the Book of Changes says: "Jin means advance."
entries.literal: Moreover, the Book of Changes says: "Jin means advance."

entries.zh: 國號大晉，皆符契焉。
entries.en: The state name Great Jin accorded with all of these tokens.
entries.literal: The state name Great Jin all accorded with these tokens.

entries.zh: 又，帝即位之前一年，歲在乙未，鄴西有柵曰李固，清、淇合流在其側。
entries.en: Moreover, in the year before the Emperor took the throne, the year was yiwei. West of Ye there was a stockade called Liguo, where the Qing and Qi rivers joined beside it.
entries.literal: Moreover, in the year before the Emperor took the throne, the year was yiwei; west of Ye there was a stockade called Liguo, where the Qing and Qi rivers joined beside it.

entries.zh: 柵有橋，橋下大鼠與蛇鬥，鬥及日之申，蛇不勝而死。
entries.en: The stockade had a bridge. Below the bridge a great rat and a snake fought until the hour of shen, when the snake could not prevail and died.
entries.literal: The stockade had a bridge; below the bridge a great rat and a snake fought, and the fight lasted until the hour of shen, when the snake could not prevail and died.

entries.zh: 行人觀者數百，識者誌之。
entries.en: Several hundred passersby watched, and those who understood recorded it.
entries.literal: Several hundred passersby watched, and those who understood recorded it.

entries.zh: 後唐末帝果滅於申。
entries.en: Later Tang's Last Emperor was indeed destroyed at the hour of shen.
entries.literal: Later Tang's Last Emperor was indeed destroyed in the hour of shen.

entries.zh: 又，末帝，真定常山人也，有先人舊廬，其側有古佛剎，剎有石像，忽搖動不已，人皆異之。
entries.en: Moreover, the Last Emperor was from Zhending in Changshan. He had an ancestral residence, and beside it stood an ancient Buddhist monastery with a stone image that suddenly shook without cease. All regarded it as strange.
entries.literal: Moreover, the Last Emperor was a man of Zhending in Changshan; he had an ancestral old residence, and beside it an ancient Buddhist monastery with a stone image that suddenly shook without cease, and all regarded it as strange.

entries.zh: 及重圍晉陽，帝遣心腹何福輕騎求援北蕃，蕃主自將諸部赴之。
entries.en: When Jinyang was heavily besieged, the Emperor sent his trusted man He Fu with light cavalry to seek aid from the northern tribes. The Khitan ruler personally led his tribes to come.
entries.literal: When Jinyang was heavily besieged, the Emperor sent his trusted man He Fu with light cavalry to seek aid from the northern barbarians; the barbarian ruler personally led the various tribes to come.

entries.zh: 不以繒帛，不以珠金，若響應聲。
entries.en: Without silks, without pearls and gold, he came like an echo answering a sound.
entries.literal: Without silks, without pearls and gold, he came like an echo answering a sound.

entries.zh: 謂福曰：「吾已兆於夢，皆上帝命我，非我意也。」
entries.en: He said to Fu: "I have already been foretold in a dream. All of this is the Supreme Lord's command to me, not my own intent."
entries.literal: He said to Fu: "I have already been foretold in a dream; all is the Supreme Lord's command to me, not my own intent."

entries.zh: 〈（《契丹國志》引《紀異錄》云：契丹主德光常晝寢，夢一神人花冠美姿容，輜梅甚盛，忽自天而下，衣白衣，佩金帶，執钅骨钅朵，有異人十二隨其後，內一黑兔入德光懷而失之。
entries.en: (The 《Khitan State Annals》 cites the 《Record of Strange Events》: The Khitan ruler Deguang often napped by day and dreamed of a divine man with a flowered crown and beautiful countenance, with a very splendid covered carriage, who suddenly descended from Heaven, wore white robes, bore a golden belt, and grasped a mace. Twelve strange men followed behind him, and among them a black rabbit entered Deguang's bosom and vanished.
entries.literal: (The Khitan State Annals cites the Record of Strange Events: The Khitan ruler Deguang often napped by day and dreamed of a divine man with a flowered crown and beautiful countenance, with a very splendid covered carriage, who suddenly descended from Heaven, wore white robes, bore a golden belt, and grasped a mace; twelve strange men followed behind him, and among them a black rabbit entered Deguang's bosom and was lost.

entries.zh: 神人語德光曰：「石郎使人喚汝，汝須去。」
entries.en: The divine man said to Deguang: "Master Shi has sent men to summon you. You must go."
entries.literal: The divine man said to Deguang: "Master Shi has sent men to summon you; you must go."

entries.zh: 覺告其母，母忽之，不以為異。
entries.en: When he awoke he told his mother. She dismissed it and did not regard it as strange.
entries.literal: When he awoke he told his mother; his mother dismissed it and did not regard it as strange.

entries.zh: 後復夢，即前神人也，衣冠儀貌，儼然如故，曰：「石郎已使人來喚汝。」
entries.en: Later he dreamed again. It was the same divine man as before, robes, cap, bearing, and appearance all exactly as before, who said: "Master Shi has already sent men to summon you."
entries.literal: Later he dreamed again—it was the same divine man as before, robes, cap, bearing, and appearance all exactly as before, who said: "Master Shi has already sent men to summon you."

entries.zh: 既覺而驚，復以告母。
entries.en: When he awoke he was alarmed and again told his mother.
entries.literal: When he awoke he was alarmed and again told his mother.

entries.zh: 母曰：「可命筮。」
entries.en: His mother said: "You may order divination."
entries.literal: His mother said: "You may order divination."

entries.zh: 乃召巫筮，言：「太祖從西樓來，言中國將立天王，要爾為助，爾須去。」
entries.en: He summoned a shaman to divine, who said: "The Founding Ancestor comes from the Western Tower and says China will establish a Heavenly King and wants you to assist. You must go."
entries.literal: He thereupon summoned a shaman to divine, who said: "The Founding Ancestor comes from the Western Tower and says China will establish a Heavenly King and wants you to assist; you must go."

entries.zh: 未浹旬，唐石敬瑭反於河東，為後唐張敬達所敗，亟遣趙瑩持表重賂，許割燕雲，求兵為援，契丹主曰：「我非為石郎興師，乃奉天帝敕使也。」）〉
entries.en: Before ten days had passed, Tang's Shi Jingtang rebelled in Hedong, was defeated by Later Tang's Zhang Jingda, and urgently sent Zhao Ying with a memorial and heavy bribes, promising to cede Yan and Yun and seeking troops as aid. The Khitan ruler said, "I do not raise troops for Master Shi. I obey the Heavenly Emperor's command.".)〉
entries.literal: Before ten days had passed, Tang's Shi Jingtang rebelled in Hedong, was defeated by Later Tang's Zhang Jingda, and urgently sent Zhao Ying with a memorial and heavy bribes, promising to cede Yan and Yun and seeking troops as aid; the Khitan ruler said, "I do not raise troops for Master Shi; I obey the Heavenly Emperor's command.".)〉

entries.zh: 時援兵未至，偽將張敬達引軍逼城設柵，柵將成，必有大風暴雨，柵無以立。
