entries.en: At that time relief troops had not yet arrived. The rebel general Zhang Jingda led troops against the city and set up stockades. Whenever the stockades were about to be completed, great wind and violent rain would come, and the stockades could not stand.
entries.literal: At that time relief troops had not yet arrived; the rebel general Zhang Jingda led troops pressing the city and set up stockades; whenever the stockades were about to be completed, great wind and violent rain would come, and the stockades could not stand.

entries.zh: 後築長城，城就，又為水潦所壞，城終不能合。
entries.en: Later they built a long wall. When the wall was completed it was again destroyed by flooding, and the wall in the end could not be joined.
entries.literal: Later they built a long wall; when the wall was completed it was again destroyed by flooding, and the wall in the end could not be joined.

entries.zh: 晉陽有北宮，宮城之上有祠曰毗沙門天王，帝曾焚修默而禱之。
entries.en: Jinyang had a Northern Palace. Above the palace city was a shrine to Vaisravana, the Heavenly King. The Emperor once burned incense in cultivation and prayed to it in silence.
entries.literal: Jinyang had a Northern Palace; above the palace city was a shrine to Vaisravana, the Heavenly King; the Emperor once burned incense in cultivation and prayed to it in silence.

entries.zh: 經數日，城西北正受敵處，軍候報稱，夜來有一人長丈餘，介金執殳，行於城上，久方不見。
entries.en: After several days, at the northwest of the city where the enemy pressed directly, military scouts reported that in the night a man more than ten feet tall, armored in gold and grasping a halberd, walked upon the city wall and only after a long while vanished from sight.
entries.literal: After several days, at the northwest of the city where the enemy pressed directly, military scouts reported that in the night a man more than ten feet tall, armored in gold and grasping a halberd, walked upon the city wall and only after a long while was no longer seen.

entries.zh: 帝心異之。
entries.en: The Emperor was astonished.
entries.literal: The Emperor was astonished in his heart.

entries.zh: 又，牙城有僧坊曰崇福，坊之廡下西北隅有泥神，神之首忽一日有煙生，其騰郁如曲突之狀。
entries.en: Moreover, in the garrison city was a monks' quarter called Chongfu. In the northwest corner beneath its cloister walk stood a clay spirit, and one day smoke suddenly arose from the spirit's head, rising thick like smoke from a bent chimney.
entries.literal: Moreover, in the garrison city was a monks' quarter called Chongfu; in the northwest corner beneath its cloister walk was a clay spirit, and one day smoke suddenly arose from the spirit's head, rising thick like smoke from a bent chimney.

entries.zh: 坊僧奔赴，以為人火所延，及俯而視之，無所有焉。
entries.en: The monks of the quarter rushed there, thinking human fire had spread, but when they bent down to look, there was nothing at all.
entries.literal: The monks of the quarter rushed there, thinking human fire had spread, but when they bent down to look, there was nothing at all.

entries.zh: 事尋達帝，帝召僧之臘高者問焉，僧曰：「貧道見莊宗將得天下，曾有此煙。
entries.en: The matter soon reached the Emperor. He summoned the monk of highest monastic standing and asked him. The monk said: "This humble priest saw when Zhuangzong was about to gain the realm that there was once this smoke.
entries.literal: The matter soon reached the Emperor; he summoned the monk of highest monastic standing and asked him, and the monk said: "This humble priest saw when Zhuangzong was about to gain the realm that there was once this smoke.

entries.zh: 觀此噴湧，甚於當時，兆可知矣。」
entries.en: Observing this gushing forth, it is greater than at that time. The omen can be known."
entries.literal: Observing this gushing forth, it is greater than at that time—the omen can be known."

entries.zh: 自此，日旁多有五色雲氣，如蓮芰之狀。
entries.en: From this time, beside the sun there were often five-colored clouds in the shape of lotus leaves.
entries.literal: From this time, beside the sun there were often five-colored clouds in the shape of lotus leaves.

entries.zh: 帝召占者視之，謂曰：「此驗應誰？」
entries.en: The Emperor summoned diviners to observe them and said: "For whom is this sign fulfilled?"
entries.literal: The Emperor summoned diviners to observe them and said: "For whom is this sign fulfilled?"

entries.zh: 占者曰：「見處為瑞，更應何人！」
entries.en: The diviners said: "Where it is seen is where the auspice falls. For whom else could it be!"
entries.literal: The diviners said: "Where it is seen is where the auspice falls—for whom else could it be!"

entries.zh: 又，帝每詰旦使慰撫守陴者，率以為常。
entries.en: Moreover, every dawn the Emperor sent men to comfort and reassure those guarding the battlements, and this was his constant practice.
entries.literal: Moreover, every dawn the Emperor sent men to comfort and reassure those guarding the battlements, and this was his constant practice.

entries.zh: 忽一夕已暝，城上有號令之聲，聲不絕者三。
entries.en: Suddenly one night, already dark, there were sounds of commands on the wall, and the sounds did not cease for three rounds.
entries.literal: Suddenly one night, already dark, there were sounds of commands on the wall, and the sounds did not cease for three rounds.

entries.zh: 帝使人問之，將吏云：「從上傳來者。」
entries.en: The Emperor sent men to ask about it. The generals and officers said: "They come transmitted from above."
entries.literal: The Emperor sent men to ask about it; the generals and officers said: "They come transmitted from above."

entries.zh: 皆知神助。
entries.en: All knew it was divine assistance.
entries.literal: All knew it was divine assistance.

entries.zh: 時城中復有數家井泉，暴溢不止。
entries.en: At that time within the city several households' wells and springs also overflowed violently without cease.
entries.literal: At that time within the city several households' wells and springs also overflowed violently without cease.

entries.zh: 及蕃軍大至，合勢破之，末帝之眾，似拉朽焉。
entries.en: When the Khitan army arrived in great force and joined strength to break them, the Last Emperor's host collapsed like rotten wood pulled apart.
entries.literal: When the barbarian army arrived in great force and joined strength to break them, the Last Emperor's host was like pulling rotten wood apart.

entries.zh: 斯天運使然，非人力也。
entries.en: This was Heaven's turning made so. It was not human power.
entries.literal: This was Heaven's turning made so—it was not human power.

entries.zh: 禮畢，帝鼓吹道從而歸。
entries.en: When the ceremony was complete, the Emperor returned with drums and pipes clearing the road before him.
entries.literal: When the ceremony was complete, the Emperor returned with drums and pipes clearing the road before him.

entries.zh: 矧今中原無主，四海未寧，茫茫生民，若墜塗炭。
entries.en: Moreover, now the central plains have no ruler, the four seas are not at peace, and the vast living people are as if falling into mud and fire.
entries.literal: Moreover, now the central plains have no ruler, the four seas are not at peace, and the vast living people are as if falling into mud and fire.

entries.zh: 況萬幾不可以暫廢，大寶不可以久虛，拯溺救焚，當在此日。
entries.en: How much more may the myriad affairs of state not be briefly abandoned, nor the great treasure long left vacant. To rescue the drowning and save from burning must be done on this day.
entries.literal: How much more may the myriad affairs not be briefly abandoned, nor the great treasure long left vacant—to rescue the drowning and save from burning must be on this day.

entries.zh: 爾有庇民之德，格於上下；
entries.en: You have the virtue of sheltering the people, reaching to above and below;
entries.literal: You have the virtue of sheltering the people, reaching to above and below;

entries.zh: 爾有戡難之勛，光於區宇；
entries.en: you have the merit of quelling hardship, shining throughout the realm;
entries.literal: you have the merit of quelling hardship, shining throughout the realm;

entries.zh: 爾有無私之行，通乎神明；
entries.en: you have selfless conduct, penetrating to the spirits;
entries.literal: you have selfless conduct, penetrating to the spirits;

entries.zh: 爾有不言之信，彰乎兆庶。
entries.en: you have unspoken faithfulness, manifest among the myriad people.
entries.literal: you have unspoken faithfulness, manifest among the myriad people.

entries.zh: 予懋乃德，嘉乃丕績。
entries.en: I exalt your virtue and praise your great achievements.
entries.literal: I exalt your virtue and praise your great achievements.

entries.zh: 天之歷數在爾躬，是用命爾，當踐皇極。
entries.en: Heaven's succession rests on your person. Therefore I command you to ascend the imperial throne.
entries.literal: Heaven's succession rests on your person; therefore I command you to ascend the imperial pinnacle.

entries.zh: 仍以爾自茲並土，首建義旗，宜以國號曰晉。
entries.en: Moreover, because you in Bing province first raised the banner of righteousness, the state name shall be Jin.
entries.literal: Moreover, because you from this time in Bing province first raised the banner of righteousness, the state name should be called Jin.

entries.zh: 朕永與為父子之邦，保山河之誓。
entries.en: I shall forever be with you a realm bound as father and son, preserving the oath upon mountains and rivers.
entries.literal: I shall forever be with you a realm of father and son, preserving the oath upon mountains and rivers.

entries.zh: 於戲！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 補百王之闕禮，行茲盛典；
entries.en: Repair the deficient rites of the hundred kings and perform this great ceremony;
entries.literal: Repair the deficient rites of the hundred kings and perform this great ceremony;

entries.zh: 成千載之大義，遂我初心。
entries.en: complete the great righteousness of a thousand ages and fulfill my original intent.
entries.literal: complete the great righteousness of a thousand ages and fulfill my original intent.

entries.zh: 爾其永保兆民，勉持一德，慎乃有位，允執厥中。
entries.en: Forever preserve the myriad people, strive to hold to one virtue, be careful in your position, and truly hold fast to the center.
entries.literal: You shall forever preserve the myriad people, strive to hold to one virtue, be careful in your position, and truly hold fast to the center.

entries.zh: 亦惟無疆之休，其誡之哉！
entries.en: May there also be boundless blessing. Take this as your warning!
entries.literal: May there also be boundless blessing—take this as your warning!

entries.zh: 是日，帝言於契丹主，願以雁門已北及幽州之地為戎王壽，仍約歲輸帛三十萬，戎王許之。
entries.en: That day the Emperor spoke to the Khitan ruler, offering the lands north of Yanmen and Youzhou as a gift for the Khitan ruler's longevity and agreeing to deliver three hundred thousand bolts of silk yearly. The Khitan ruler consented.
entries.literal: That day the Emperor spoke to the Khitan ruler, wishing to give the lands north of Yanmen and Youzhou as a gift for the Rong king's longevity, and also agreed to deliver three hundred thousand bolts of silk yearly; the Rong king consented.

entries.zh: 夏五月壬子朔，帝御崇元殿受朝賀，仗衛如式。
entries.en: On the first day of the fifth month the emperor received congratulations in the Chongyuan Hall with full ceremonial guard.
entries.literal: On the first day of the fifth month of summer, renzi, the Emperor took the throne in the Chongyuan Hall to receive congratulatory homage, with guards and insignia in full form.

entries.zh: 詔洛京、魏府管內所征今年夏苗稅麥等，宜放五分之一，以微旱故也。
entries.en: Summer seedling taxes and wheat levies collected this year in the Luoyang capital and Weifu circuits were remitted by one-fifth because of slight drought.
entries.literal: An edict stated that summer seedling taxes and wheat levies collected this year within the Luoyang capital and Weifu circuits should be remitted by one-fifth, because of slight drought.

entries.zh: 丙辰，御史中丞張昭遠奏：「汴州在梁室朱氏稱制之年，有京都之號，及唐莊宗平定河南，復廢為宣武軍。
entries.en: On the bingchen day, Censor-in-Chief Zhang Zhaoyuan memorialized: "Bianzhou, in the years when the Zhu clan of Liang held power, bore the title of capital; when Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Henan it was again abolished and made Xuanwu Army.
entries.literal: On the bingchen day, Censor-in-Chief Zhang Zhaoyuan memorialized: "Bianzhou, in the years when the Zhu clan of Liang held power, bore the title of capital; when Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Henan it was again abolished and made Xuanwu Army.

entries.zh: 至明宗行幸之時，掌事者因緣修葺衙城，遂掛梁室時宮殿門牌額，當時識者或竊非之。
entries.en: When Emperor Mingzong toured, those in charge repaired the headquarters city and hung palace gate placards from Liang times—men of discernment privately disapproved.
entries.literal: When Emperor Mingzong toured, those in charge took occasion to repair the headquarters city and hung palace gate placards from Liang times—men of discernment at the time privately disapproved.

entries.zh: 一昨車駕省方，暫居梁苑，臣觀衙城內齋閣牌額，一如明宗行幸之時，無都號而有殿名，恐非典據。
entries.en: When the emperor recently toured and temporarily resided in Liangyuan, I observed placards on pavilions within the headquarters city as in Mingzong's tour—no capital designation but hall names—and fear this is not canonical precedent.
entries.literal: When the carriage recently toured the realm and temporarily resided in Liangyuan, your subject observed placards on pavilions within the headquarters city just as in Mingzong's tour—no capital designation but hall names—and fears this is not canonical precedent.

entries.zh: 臣竊尋秦、漢已來，寰海之內，鑾輿所至，多立宮名。
entries.en: Since Qin and Han, wherever the imperial carriage went within the realm, palace names were often established.
entries.literal: Your subject has traced since Qin and Han that wherever the imperial carriage went within the realm, palace names were often established.

entries.zh: 近代隋室於揚州立江都宮，太原立汾陽宮，岐州立仁壽宮。
entries.en: In recent times the Sui established the Jiangdu Palace at Yangzhou, the Fenyang Palace at Taiyuan, and the Renshou Palace at Qizhou.
entries.literal: In recent times the Sui house established the Jiangdu Palace at Yangzhou, the Fenyang Palace at Taiyuan, and the Renshou Palace at Qizhou.

entries.zh: 唐朝於太原立晉陽宮，同州立長春宮，岐州立九成宮。
entries.en: The Tang established the Jinyang Palace at Taiyuan, the Everlasting Spring Palace at Tongzhou, and the Ninefold Palace at Qizhou.
entries.literal: The Tang house established the Jinyang Palace at Taiyuan, the Everlasting Spring Palace at Tongzhou, and the Ninefold Palace at Qizhou.

entries.zh: 宮中殿閣，皆題署牌額，以類皇居。
entries.en: Halls and pavilions within the palaces all bore inscribed placards, resembling the imperial residence.
entries.literal: Halls and pavilions within the palaces all bore inscribed placards, resembling the imperial residence.

entries.zh: 請準故事，於汴州衙城門權掛一宮門牌額，則其餘齋閣並可取便為名。」
entries.en: We request following precedent to hang temporarily one palace gate placard at the Bianzhou headquarters gate; then the remaining pavilions may all be named as convenient."
entries.literal: We request following precedent to hang temporarily one palace gate placard at the Bianzhou headquarters gate; then the remaining pavilions may all be named as convenient."

entries.zh: 敕：行闕宜以大寧宮為名。
entries.en: An edict named the traveling palace the Great Tranquility Palace.
entries.literal: An edict: The traveling palace should be named the Great Tranquility Palace.

entries.zh: 湖南青草廟舊封安流侯，進封廣利公；
entries.en: The Green Grass Temple in Hunan, formerly Marquis of Anliu, was advanced to Duke of Guangli;
entries.literal: The Green Grass Temple in Hunan, formerly enfeoffed as Marquis of Anliu, was advanced to Duke of Guangli;

entries.zh: 洞庭廟進封靈濟公；
entries.en: The Dongting Shrine was promoted to Duke Spirit-Benefit;
entries.literal: The Dongting Shrine was advanced in title to Duke Spirit-Benefit;

entries.zh: 磊石廟舊封昭靈侯，進封威顯公；
entries.en: The Leishi Shrine, previously Marquis Splendid Spirit, was promoted to Duke Majestic Manifestation;
entries.literal: The Leishi Shrine, formerly enfeoffed as Marquis Splendid Spirit, was advanced to Duke Majestic Manifestation;

entries.zh: 黃陵二妃廟舊封懿節廟，改封昭烈廟，從馬希範之請也。
entries.en: At Ma Xifan's request, the shrine of the Two Consorts at Huangling, formerly the Yi Jie Shrine, was retitled the Splendid Fierce Shrine.
entries.literal: The shrine of the Two Consorts at Huangling, formerly titled the Yi Jie Shrine, was renamed the Splendid Fierce Shrine, in accordance with Ma Xifan's request.

entries.zh: 戊午，以前成德軍節度判官張彭為太府卿。
entries.en: On wuwu, Zhang Peng, former Chengde military administration judge, became Minister of the Imperial Treasury.
entries.literal: On the wuwu day, Zhang Peng, formerly adjutant to the military governor of Chengde Circuit, was appointed Minister of the Imperial Treasury.

entries.zh: 壬戌，詔在朝文武臣僚，每人各進封事一件。
entries.en: On renxu the court decreed that every civil and military official in attendance submit one sealed memorial.
entries.literal: On the renxu day, an edict ordered all civil and military officials at court to each submit one sealed memorial.

entries.zh: 仍須實封通進，務裨闕政，用副虛懷。
entries.en: Memorials were to be submitted under real seal, to remedy failings in government and answer the emperor's open-minded solicitude.
entries.literal: They were also required to submit them fully sealed, striving to remedy governmental deficiencies, to match his humble receptivity.

entries.zh: 甲子，以虞部郎中、知制誥於嶠為中書舍人，以戶部郎中於遘為虞部郎中、知制誥，故太子少保致仕朱漢賓贈司空。
entries.en: On jiazi, Yu Qiao, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works and rescript drafter, became Secretariat Drafter; Yu Hou, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, became Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works and rescript drafter; and the late retired Junior Guardian Zhu Hanbin was posthumously granted Sikong.
entries.literal: On the jiazi day, Yu Qiao, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works and drafter of edicts, was made Deputy Director of the Secretariat; Yu Hou, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, was made Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works and drafter of edicts; the late retired Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent Zhu Hanbin was posthumously granted Sikong.

entries.zh: 乙丑，六宅使王繼宏送義州衙前收管，前洺州團練使高信送復州收管。
entries.en: On yichou, Palace Attendant Wang Jihong was remanded to Yi prefectural custody, and former Mingzhou defensive commissioner Gao Xin to Fu prefecture.
entries.literal: On the yichou day, Palace Attendant Wang Jihong was sent to be detained at the Yi prefectural yamen, and former Mingzhou defensive commissioner Gao Xin was sent to be detained at Fu prefecture.

entries.zh: 二人於崇禮門內喧爭，為臺司所劾故也。
entries.en: This was because they had quarreled noisily inside the Chongli Gate and had been impeached by the censorate.
entries.literal: The reason was that the two men had quarreled loudly inside the Chongli Gate and had been impeached by the censorate.

entries.zh: 戊辰，翰林學士、戶部員外郎、知制誥竇貞固改工部郎中、知制誥；
entries.en: On wuchen, Hanlin Academician Dou Zhengu, Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and rescript drafter, became Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works and rescript drafter;
entries.literal: On the wuchen day, Hanlin Academician Dou Zhengu, Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and drafter of edicts, was transferred to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works and drafter of edicts;

entries.zh: 翰林學士、都官郎中、知制誥李慎儀改中書舍人，仍賜金紫，並依舊充職。
entries.en: Hanlin Academician Li Shenyi, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice and rescript drafter, became Secretariat Drafter, was again granted the gold seal and purple robe, and both men continued in their former capacities.
entries.literal: Hanlin Academician Li Shenyi, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice and drafter of edicts, was transferred to Deputy Director of the Secretariat, and was still granted the gold seal and purple robe; both continued in their previous posts.

entries.zh: 庚午，制封皇第二十一女為長安公主，封皇第十一妹烏氏為壽安長公主，皇第十二妹史氏為永壽長公主，皇第十三妹杜氏為樂平長公主。
entries.en: On gengwu an edict enfeoffed the emperor's twenty-first daughter as Princess of Chang'an; his eleventh younger sister, Lady Wu, as Grand Princess of Shou'an; his twelfth younger sister, Lady Shi, as Grand Princess of Yongshou; and his thirteenth younger sister, Lady Du, as Grand Princess of Leping.
entries.literal: On the gengwu day, by edict the emperor's twenty-first daughter was enfeoffed as Princess of Chang'an; the emperor's eleventh younger sister, Lady Wu, as Grand Princess of Shou'an; the twelfth younger sister, Lady Shi, as Grand Princess of Yongshou; and the thirteenth younger sister, Lady Du, as Grand Princess of Leping.

entries.zh: 壬申，天雄軍節度使、守太傅、兼中書令、興唐尹範延光進封臨清王，加食邑三千戶；
entries.en: On renshen, Fan Yanguang, Military Commissioner of Tianxiong, acting Grand Preceptor, Palace Secretariat Director, and Prefect of Xingtang, was promoted Prince of Linqing with an additional fief of three thousand households;
entries.literal: On the renshen day, Fan Yanguang, Military Commissioner of Tianxiong Army, acting Grand Preceptor, concurrent Palace Secretariat Director, and Prefect of Xingtang, was advanced to Prince of Linqing, with an additional fief of three thousand households;

entries.zh: 鳳翔節度使、檢校太師、兼中書令、西平王李從嚴進封岐王。
entries.en: Li Congyan, Military Commissioner of Fengxiang, Acting Grand Mentor, Palace Secretariat Director, and Prince of Xiping, was promoted Prince of Qi.
entries.literal: Li Congyan, Military Commissioner of Fengxiang, Acting Grand Mentor, concurrent Palace Secretariat Director, and Prince of Xiping, was advanced to Prince of Qi.

entries.zh: 丙子，平盧軍節度使、兼中書令王建立進封臨淄王；
entries.en: On bingzi, Wang Jianli, Military Commissioner of Pinglu and Palace Secretariat Director, was promoted Prince of Linzi;
entries.literal: On the bingzi day, Wang Jianli, Military Commissioner of Pinglu Army and concurrent Palace Secretariat Director, was advanced to Prince of Linzi;

entries.zh: 昭信軍節度使、侍衛馬軍都指揮使景延廣改寧江軍節度使，典軍如故。
entries.en: Jing Yanguang, Military Commissioner of Zhaoxin and commander of the palace cavalry guard, became Military Commissioner of Ningjiang while continuing to command troops as before.
entries.literal: Jing Yanguang, Military Commissioner of Zhaoxin and Commander of the Palace Guard Cavalry, was transferred to Military Commissioner of Ningjiang; he continued to command troops as before.

entries.zh: 太常卿梁文矩奏定四廟謚號、廟號、陵號，太常少卿裴垣奏定四廟皇后追尊謚號，從之。
entries.en: Minister of Rites Liang Wenju proposed posthumous titles, temple names, and tomb names for the four imperial temples; Vice Minister of Rites Pei Yuan proposed posthumous titles for the empresses honored there; both were approved.
entries.literal: Minister of Rites Liang Wenju memorialized on fixing the posthumous titles, temple names, and tomb names for the four imperial temples; Vice Minister of Rites Pei Yuan memorialized on fixing the posthumous honorific titles for the empresses of the four temples; the court approved.

entries.zh: 戊寅，以中書舍人、權知貢舉王延為御史中丞，以翰林學士、戶部侍郎、知制誥崔棁為兵部侍郎充承旨，以翰林學士承旨、兵部侍郎程遜為檢校禮部尚書、太常卿，以檢校吏部尚書、太常卿梁文矩為吏部尚書，以御史中丞張昭遠為戶部侍郎，以吏部尚書盧文紀為太子少傅。
entries.en: On wuyin, Wang Yan, Secretariat Drafter and acting chief examiner, became Censor-in-Chief; Cui Zhi, Hanlin Academician, Vice Minister of Revenue, and rescript drafter, became Vice Minister of War and chief drafter; Cheng Xun, Hanlin chief drafter and Vice Minister of War, became Acting Minister of Rites and Minister of Rites; Liang Wenju became Minister of Personnel; Zhang Zhaoyuan became Vice Minister of Revenue; and Lu Wenji became Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: On the wuyin day, Wang Yan, Secretariat Drafter and acting chief examiner, was made Censor-in-Chief; Cui Zhi, Hanlin Academician, Vice Minister of Revenue, and drafter of edicts, was made Vice Minister of War and chief drafter; Cheng Xun, Hanlin Academician, chief drafter, and Vice Minister of War, was made Acting Minister of Rites and Minister of Rites; Liang Wenju, Acting Minister of Personnel and Minister of Rites, was made Minister of Personnel; Zhang Zhaoyuan, Censor-in-Chief, was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Lu Wenji, Minister of Personnel, was made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 己卯，詔太社內先收掌唐朝罪人首級等，宜令骨肉或先舊僚屬收葬，其喪葬儀註不得過制。
entries.en: On jimao an edict ordered that severed heads of Tang convicts kept at the Altar of Earth be released to kin or former colleagues for burial, with funeral observances kept within proper bounds.
entries.literal: On the jimao day, an edict stated that the severed heads of Tang dynasty convicts previously held at the Altar of Earth should be released to their kin or former colleagues for burial, and that funeral rites must not exceed proper form.

entries.zh: 天福元年十一月己亥，帝御北京崇元殿，降制：「改長興七年為天福元年，大赦天下。
entries.en: On the jihai day of the eleventh month of Tianfu 1, the emperor entered the Chongyuan Hall at the Northern Capital and promulgated an edict: "The seventh year of Changxing is hereby renamed Tianfu 1, and a general amnesty is proclaimed for all under Heaven.
entries.literal: On the jihai day of the eleventh month of the first year of Tianfu, the Emperor took the throne in the Chongyuan Hall at the Northern Capital and issued an edict: "Let the seventh year of Changxing be changed to the first year of Tianfu, and grant a general amnesty throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 十一月九日昧爽已前，應在京及諸州諸色罪犯，及曾授偽命職掌官吏，並見禁囚徒，已結正未結正，已發覺未發覺，罪無輕重，常赦不原者，咸赦除之。
entries.en: Before dawn on the ninth day of the eleventh month, every class of offender in the capital and in the provinces, every official who had once held office under the usurper regime, and every prisoner still in custody—case closed or pending, offense known or not, grave or slight, including crimes ordinarily beyond the reach of amnesty—was pardoned and set free.
entries.literal: Before dawn on the ninth day of the eleventh month, all offenders of every category in the capital and the various prefectures, officials who had once received appointments from the false regime, and prisoners currently held in custody—whether their cases had been concluded or not, whether discovered or not, regardless of the severity of the offense, and even those normally excluded from routine amnesties—were all pardoned and released.

entries.zh: 應明宗朝所行敕命法制，仰所在遵行，不得改易。
entries.en: The edicts and statutes issued in the Tang reign of Emperor Mingzong are to be observed everywhere as written, without change.
entries.literal: As for the edicts and regulations promulgated in the reign of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, [authorities] in each locality are to follow them and may not alter them.

entries.zh: 其在京鹽貨，元是官場出糴，自今後並不禁斷，一任人戶取便糴易，仍下太原府，更不得開場糴貨。
entries.en: Salt in the capital had formerly been sold only through government markets; hereafter the trade is not to be restricted, and households may buy and sell freely. Taiyuan Prefecture was likewise ordered to cease operating state salt-purchase depots.
entries.literal: Salt goods in the capital had originally been purchased from government depots; from now on this monopoly is not to be enforced, and households may buy and sell as they please; an order was also sent to Taiyuan Prefecture that it must no longer operate purchasing depots for salt.

entries.zh: 其曲每斤與減價錢三十文。」
entries.en: The price of distilled liquor was cut by thirty cash per jin."
entries.literal: For liquor, the price per jin was to be reduced by thirty cash."

entries.zh: 以節度判官趙瑩為翰林學士承旨、守尚書戶部侍郎、知河東軍府事，以節度掌書記桑維翰為翰林學士、守尚書禮部侍郎、知樞密院事，以觀察判官薛融為吏部郎中兼侍御史、知雜事，太原縣令羅周嶽為左諫議大夫，節度推官竇貞固為翰林學士，軍城都巡檢使劉知遠為侍衛馬軍都指揮使，客將景延廣為步軍都指揮使，太原少尹李玘為尚書工部侍郎。
entries.en: Zhao Ying, judge of the military administration, was appointed Grand Academician and Drafter of the Hanlin Academy, acting Minister of Revenue, with charge of Hedong military prefecture affairs; Sang Weihan, military secretary, became Hanlin Academician, acting Minister of Rites, and Controller of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Xue Rong, observation judge, became Director in the Ministry of Personnel with concurrent Remonstrance Censor and supervising censor; Luo Zhouyue, magistrate of Taiyuan County, became Left Remonstrance Censor; Dou Zhengu, military evaluator, became Hanlin Academician; Liu Zhiyuan, chief metropolitan garrison inspector, became Commander of the Palace Guard Cavalry; Jing Yanguang, guest officer, became Commander of the Palace Guard Infantry; and Li Qi, vice magistrate of Taiyuan, became Vice Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Zhao Ying, military administration judge, was made Grand Academician and Drafter of the Hanlin Academy, acting Minister of Revenue, and in charge of Hedong military prefecture affairs; Sang Weihan, military administration secretary, was made Hanlin Academician, acting Minister of Rites, and Controller of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Xue Rong, observation administration judge, was made Director in the Ministry of Personnel with concurrent Remonstrance Censor and chief supervising censor; Luo Zhouyue, magistrate of Taiyuan County, was made Left Remonstrance Censor; Dou Zhengu, military administration evaluator, was made Hanlin Academician; Liu Zhiyuan, metropolitan garrison chief inspector, was made Commander of the Palace Guard Cavalry; Jing Yanguang, guest officer, was made Commander of the Palace Guard Infantry; Li Qi, vice magistrate of Taiyuan, was made Vice Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 七月丙午朔，差左諫議大夫薛融、秘書監呂琦、駕部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事劉皞、刑部郎中司徒詡、大理正張仁彖，同共詳定唐明宗朝編敕。
entries.en: On bingwu, the first day of the seventh month, Xue Rong, Left Remonstrance Counselor; Lü Qi, Director of the Palace Library; Liu Hao, Transport Office Vice Director and concurrent Supervising Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs; Situ Xu, Director in the Ministry of Punishments; and Zhang Rentuan, Senior Rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review, were jointly assigned to review and revise the compiled edicts of the Tang reign of Emperor Mingzong.
entries.literal: In the seventh month, on the first day (bingwu), Xue Rong, Left Remonstrance Counselor; Lü Qi, Director of the Palace Library; Liu Hao, Director of the Transport Office and concurrent Supervising Censor with charge of mixed affairs; Situ Xu, Director of the Ministry of Punishments; and Zhang Rentuan, Senior Rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review, were jointly dispatched to examine and fix the compiled edicts of the Tang reign of Emperor Mingzong.

entries.zh: 庚戌，御史中丞王延改尚書右丞，尚書右丞盧導改尚書吏部侍郎，以左諫議大夫薛融為御史中丞。
entries.en: On gengxu Wang Yan moved from censor-in-chief to right vice director of the Secretariat; Lu Dao from right vice director to vice minister of personnel; and Xue Rong from left remonstrance counselor to censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: On gengxu, Censor-in-Chief Wang Yan was changed to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; Right Vice Director Lu Dao was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel; Left Remonstrance Counselor Xue Rong was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 辛酉，制皇帝受命寶，以「受天明命，惟德允昌」為文。
entries.en: On xinyou the imperial Seal of Received Mandate was cast, inscribed "Receiving Heaven's clear mandate—only virtue brings lasting prosperity."
entries.literal: On xinyou, the Imperial Seal of Received Mandate was cast, with the inscription "Receiving Heaven's clear mandate, virtue alone brings prosperity."

entries.zh: 據《六典》，受命寶者，天子修封禪、禮神祇則用之，其始皆破皇業錢以制之。
entries.en: According to the Six Institutes, the Seal of Received Mandate was used when the Son of Heaven performed the feng and shan rites or worshipped the spirits; it was originally cast by melting imperial-estate coin.
entries.literal: According to the Six Institutes, the Seal of Received Mandate is used when the Son of Heaven performs feng and shan rites or worships the spirits; at the outset it was always cast by melting imperial-estate coin.

entries.zh: 皇業者，藩邸主事之所有也。
entries.en: Imperial-estate coin was the property held by the steward of the princely residence.
entries.literal: Imperial estate coin was what the prince's residence steward held.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：天福三年六月，中書門下奏：「準敕，制皇帝受命寶。
entries.en: (From the Institutes of the Five Dynasties: In the sixth month of Tianfu 3 the Secretariat-Chancellery reported: "Per edict, the Imperial Seal of Received Mandate was to be cast.
entries.literal: (From the Institutes of the Five Dynasties: In the sixth month of the third year of Tianfu, the Secretariat-Chancellery reported: "Per edict, cast the Imperial Seal of Received Mandate.

entries.zh: 今按唐貞觀十六年，太宗文皇帝所刻之璽，白玉為螭首，其文曰『皇帝景命，有德者昌』。」
entries.en: Examining the Tang, in Zhenguan 16 Emperor Taizong had a seal carved of white jade with a dragon head, inscribed 'The emperor's bright mandate—he who has virtue prospers.'"
entries.literal: Now examining the Tang, in the sixteenth year of Zhenguan Emperor Taizong the Cultured Emperor had a seal carved with white jade and a dragon head; its text read 'The Emperor's bright mandate—he who has virtue prospers.'"

entries.zh: 敕：「宜以『受天明命，惟德允昌』為文刻之。」）〉
entries.en: An edict ordered: "It shall be inscribed 'Receiving Heaven's clear mandate—only virtue brings lasting prosperity.'")〉
entries.literal: Edict: "The inscription shall be carved as 'Receiving Heaven's clear mandate, virtue alone brings prosperity.'")〉

entries.zh: 壬戌，虞部郎中、知制誥於遘改中書舍人。
entries.en: On renxu Yu Gou, director of the parks office and drafting official, was reassigned as palace draftsman.
entries.literal: On renxu, Yu Gou, Director of the Parks Office and Drafting Official, was changed to Palace Draftsman.

entries.zh: 宰臣趙瑩、桑維翰、李崧各改鄉里名號。
entries.en: The chief ministers Zhao Ying, Sang Weihan, and Li Song each changed their native-place designations.
entries.literal: The chief ministers Zhao Ying, Sang Weihan, and Li Song each changed their native-place designations.

entries.zh: 荊南節度使高從誨本貫汴州浚儀縣王畿鄉表節東坊，改為擁旌鄉浴鳳裏。
entries.en: Gao Conghui of Jingnan, formerly registered in Biaojie East Lane, Wangji township, Junyi county, Bian prefecture, had his registration changed to Yufeng ward, Yongjing township.
entries.literal: Gao Conghui, Military Commissioner of Jingnan, was natively registered in Wangji Township, Biaojie East Lane, Junyi County, Bian Prefecture; this was changed to Yufeng Ward, Yongjing Township.

entries.zh: 十一月甲辰，樞密直學士、祠部員外郎吳涓進金部郎中、知制誥，樞密直學士、庫部員外郎吳承範進祠部郎中、知制誥。
entries.en: On jiachen in the eleventh month Wu Juan, Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices, was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Metals and drafting official, and Wu Chengfan, Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Director of the Armory Bureau, to Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and drafting official.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiachen, Wu Juan, Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices, was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Metals and Drafting Official; Wu Chengfan, Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Director of the Armory Bureau, was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and Drafting Official.

entries.zh: 乙巳，鄆州範延光來朝。
entries.en: On yisi Fan Yanguang of Yun came to court.
entries.literal: On yisi, Fan Yanguang of Yun Prefecture came to court.

entries.zh: 丙午，封閩王昶為閩國王，加食邑一萬五千戶。
entries.en: On bingwu Prince Chang of Min was enfeoffed as king of Min with fifteen thousand additional households' fief income.
entries.literal: On bingwu, Prince Chang of Min was enfeoffed as King of Min, with fief income increased by fifteen thousand households.

entries.zh: 又以中吳建武等軍節度使、檢校太師、兼中書令、蘇州誠州刺史錢元尞為太傅，以清海軍節度使、廣州刺史錢元璹為檢校太尉、兼中書令，仍改名元懿。
entries.en: Qian Yuankuan of Zhongwu and Jianwu was made grand mentor; Qian Yuanshan of Qinghai was made honorary Grand Commandant and chief councilor and renamed Yuanyi.
entries.literal: Qian Yuankuan, Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu and Jianwu armies, Honorary Grand Preceptor, concurrent Chief Councilor, and Prefect of Suzhou and Cheng, was appointed Grand Mentor; Qian Yuanshan, Military Commissioner of the Qinghai Army and Prefect of Guang, was appointed Honorary Grand Commandant and concurrent Chief Councilor, and his name was changed to Yuanyi.

entries.zh: 應有魏府行營將校及六軍諸道、本城將校等，並與加恩。
entries.en: Officers of the Weifu field headquarters, six armies, circuits, and capital garrisons likewise received favors.
entries.literal: All officers of the Weifu field headquarters and of the six armies, circuits, and capital garrisons likewise received favors.

entries.zh: 戊申，以門下侍郎平章事、監修國史、判戶部趙瑩兼吏部尚書。
entries.en: Zhao Ying, vice director of the chancellery, grand councilor, historiography supervisor, and revenue overseer, was also made minister of personnel.
entries.literal: Zhao Ying, Vice Director of the Chancellery, Grand Councilor, Supervisor of the National History, and overseer of the Ministry of Revenue, was additionally appointed Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 以威武軍節度、福建管內觀察處置等使王繼恭為特進、檢校太傅，仍封臨海郡王。
entries.en: Wang Jigong of Weiwu and Fujian was made specially advanced honorary grand mentor and prince of Linhai.
entries.literal: Wang Jigong, Military Commissioner of the Weiwu Army and Commissioner for Observation and Disposition within Fujian, was appointed Special Advancement and Honorary Grand Mentor, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Linhai.

entries.zh: 以魏博節度使楊光遠為守太尉、洛京留守，兼河陽節度使，判六軍諸衛事。
entries.en: Yang Guangyuan of Weibo was made acting grand commandant, Luoyang regent, concurrent Heyang military commissioner, and overseer of the six armies and palace guards.
entries.literal: Yang Guangyuan, Military Commissioner of Weibo, was appointed acting Grand Commandant, Regent of Luoyang, concurrent Military Commissioner of Heyang, and overseer of the six armies and palace guards.

entries.zh: 端明殿學士、尚書禮部侍郎、判度支和凝改尚書戶部侍郎充職。
entries.en: He Ning, Duanming academician, vice minister of rites, and revenue overseer, was reassigned as vice minister of revenue.
entries.literal: He Ning, Academician of the Duanming Hall, Vice Minister of Rites, and overseer of revenue, was changed to Vice Minister of Revenue to fill the post.

entries.zh: 庚戌，鄆州範延光上表乞休退，詔不允。
entries.en: On gengxu Fan Yanguang of Yun begged to retire; the edict refused.
entries.literal: On gengxu, Fan Yanguang of Yun Prefecture submitted a memorial begging to retire; the edict did not grant it.

entries.zh: 辛亥，升廣晉府為鄴都，置留守。
entries.en: On xinhai Guangjin prefecture was elevated to the Ye metropolitan district with a regent appointed.
entries.literal: On xinhai, Guangjin Prefecture was elevated to the metropolitan district of Ye, with a regent appointed.

entries.zh: 升廣晉、元城兩縣為赤縣，屬府諸縣升為畿縣。
entries.en: Guangjin and Yuancheng became imperial counties; prefectural counties became metropolitan counties.
entries.literal: Guangjin and Yuancheng counties were elevated to imperial counties; counties under the prefecture were elevated to metropolitan counties.

entries.zh: 升相州為彰德軍，置節度觀察使，以澶、衛二州為屬郡，其澶州仍升為防禦州，移於德勝口為治所。
entries.en: Xiangzhou was elevated to the Zhangde army with an observation commissioner; Chan and Wei became subordinate prefectures; Chan was elevated to a defense prefecture with its seat moved to Desheng Ford.
entries.literal: Xiang Prefecture was elevated to the Zhangde Army, with a military commissioner for observation appointed; Chan and Wei prefectures were made subordinate prefectures; Chan was further elevated to a defense prefecture and its seat moved to Desheng Ford.

entries.zh: 升貝州為永清軍，置節度觀察使，以博、冀二州為屬郡。
entries.en: Beizhou was elevated to the Yongqing army with an observation commissioner; Bo and Ji became subordinate prefectures.
entries.literal: Bei Prefecture was elevated to the Yongqing Army, with a military commissioner for observation appointed; Bo and Ji prefectures were made subordinate prefectures.

entries.zh: 以西京留守高行周為廣晉尹、鄴都留守；
entries.en: Gao Xingzhou, regent of the Western Capital, was made Guangjin metropolitan magistrate and regent of Ye;
entries.literal: Gao Xingzhou, Regent of the Western Capital, was appointed Guangjin metropolitan magistrate and Regent of Ye;

entries.zh: 廣晉府行營中軍使、貝州防禦使王庭允加檢校太傅，充相州彰德軍節度使；
entries.en: Wang Tingyun, Guangjin middle army commissioner and Bei defense commissioner, was made honorary grand mentor and Zhangde military commissioner at Xiang;
entries.literal: Wang Tingyun, Middle Army Commissioner of the Guangjin Field Headquarters and Defense Commissioner of Bei, was promoted to Honorary Grand Mentor and Military Commissioner of the Zhangde Army at Xiang;

entries.zh: 廣晉府行營步軍都指揮使、右神武統軍王周為貝州永清軍節度使。
entries.en: Wang Zhou, Guangjin foot commander and Right Shenwu commander, was made Yongqing military commissioner at Bei.
entries.literal: Wang Zhou, Commander of the Foot Soldiers of the Guangjin Field Headquarters and Commander of the Right Shenwu Army, was appointed Military Commissioner of the Yongqing Army at Bei.

entries.zh: 甲寅，以範延光為太子太師致仕。
entries.en: On jiayin Fan Yanguang retired as grand mentor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: On jiayin, Fan Yanguang was granted retirement as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 丙辰，以秘書監呂琦為禮部侍郎，歸德軍節度使趙在禮改天平軍節度使，昭義軍節度使兼侍衛親軍馬步軍都虞候杜重威改忠武軍節度使，忠武軍節度使、侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使劉知遠改歸德軍節度使，前河陽節度使兼奉國左右廂都指揮使侯益改昭義軍節度使。
entries.en: On bingchen Lü Qi, palace library director, became vice minister of rites; Zhao Zaili of Guide became Tianping military commissioner; Du Chongwei of Zhaoyi became Zhongwu military commissioner; Liu Zhiyuan of Zhongwu became Guide military commissioner; and Hou Yi, former Heyang commissioner, became Zhaoyi military commissioner.
entries.literal: On bingchen, Lü Qi, Director of the Palace Library, was appointed Vice Minister of Rites; Zhao Zaili, Military Commissioner of the Guide Army, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Tianping Army; Du Chongwei, Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi and Chief Adjutant of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army; Liu Zhiyuan, Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Guide Army; Hou Yi, former Military Commissioner of Heyang and Commander of the Left and Right Wings of the Fengguo Army, was changed to Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi.

entries.zh: 癸亥，割濮州濮陽縣棣澶州。
entries.en: On guihai Puyang county was detached from Puzhou and attached to Chanzhou.
entries.literal: On guihai, Puyang County of Pu Prefecture was detached and attached to Chan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 詔許天下私鑄錢，以「天福元寶」為文。
entries.en: An edict permitted private coinage throughout the realm, inscribed "Tianfu Yuanbao."
entries.literal: An edict permitted private coinage throughout the realm, with the inscription "Tianfu Yuanbao."

entries.zh: 丙寅冬至，帝御崇元殿受朝賀，仗衛如式。
entries.en: On bingyin, the winter solstice, the emperor entered Chongyuan Hall for court congratulations, with guards and ceremonial escorts in full order.
entries.literal: On bingyin, the winter solstice, the Emperor took the throne in Chongyuan Hall to receive court congratulations; guards and escorts followed the prescribed form.

entries.zh: 天福三年正月戊申朔，帝御崇元殿受朝賀，仗衛如式。
entries.en: On the first day of the first month of Tianfu 3, the emperor entered Chongyuan Hall to receive the New Year court congratulations, with guards and ceremonial escorts in full order.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianfu, first month, on the first day of the month (wushen), the Emperor took the throne in Chongyuan Hall to receive court congratulations; guards and escorts followed the prescribed form.

entries.zh: 己酉，百官守司，以太史先奏日蝕故也。
entries.en: On jiyou the officials remained at their posts, since the court astrologer had already forecast an eclipse of the sun.
entries.literal: On jiyou, the hundred officials kept their posts, because the Grand Astrologer had beforehand reported a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 至是不虧，內外稱賀。
entries.en: When the moment came, the sun was not dimmed, and court and capital alike offered congratulations.
entries.literal: When it came to this, there was no eclipse; inside and outside offered congratulations.

entries.zh: 壬戌，是夜以上元張燈於京城，縱都人遊樂，帝御大寧宮門樓觀之。
entries.en: On renxu, that night the capital was hung with lanterns for the Lantern Festival, the people of the city were allowed to roam and celebrate, and the emperor took the gate tower of Daning Palace to watch.
entries.literal: On renxu, that night for the Upper Yuan Festival lamps were displayed in the capital, the metropolitan populace was allowed to revel, and the Emperor mounted the gate tower of Daning Palace to observe.

entries.zh: 丙寅，端明殿學士、禮部侍郎和凝兼判度支；
entries.en: On bingyin, He Ning, academician of the Duanming Hall and vice minister of rites, was also put in charge of the revenue bureau;
entries.literal: On bingyin, Academician of the Duanming Hall and Vice Minister of Rites He Ning was additionally appointed to oversee the Department of Revenue;

entries.zh: 工部侍郎、判度支王松改尚書刑部侍郎；
entries.en: Wang Song, vice minister of works and acting revenue overseer, was reassigned as vice minister of punishments in the Department of State Affairs;
entries.literal: Vice Minister of Works and overseer of revenue Wang Song was changed to Vice Minister of Punishments in the Department of State Affairs;

entries.zh: 戶部郎中高延賞改左諫議大夫，充諸道鹽鐵轉運副使。
entries.en: Gao Yanshang, director in the ministry of revenue, became left remonstrance counselor and deputy commissioner for salt and iron transport on all circuits.
entries.literal: Director of the Ministry of Revenue Gao Yanshang was changed to Left Remonstrance Counselor and appointed Deputy Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport on all circuits.

entries.zh: 壬申，以前右諫議大夫薛融為左諫議大夫。
entries.en: On renshen the former right remonstrance counselor Xue Rong was made left remonstrance counselor.
entries.literal: On renshen, the former Right Remonstrance Counselor Xue Rong was appointed Left Remonstrance Counselor.

entries.zh: 前興元節度使張筠卒於西京，輟視朝一日。
entries.en: Zhang Yun, former military commissioner of Xingyuan, died in the Western Capital, and court audiences were suspended for one day.
entries.literal: The former Military Commissioner of Xingyuan Zhang Yun died in the Western Capital; court audiences were suspended for one day.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：太常禮院申：「準故事，前節度使無例輟朝。」
entries.en: (From the Institutes of the Five Dynasties: the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "According to precedent, there is no example of suspending court for a former military commissioner."
entries.literal: (From the Institutes of the Five Dynasties: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "According to precedent, there is no example of suspending court for a former military commissioner."

entries.zh: 敕：「宜特輟一日朝參。」）〉
entries.en: An edict replied: "Court attendance shall be specially suspended for one day.")〉
entries.literal: Edict: "A one-day suspension of court attendance is hereby specially granted.")〉

entries.zh: 三月癸卯朔，左僕射劉句、給事中盧重自契丹使回，頒賜器幣如馮道等。
entries.en: On the first day of the third month, left vice director Liu Ju and supervising secretary Lu Chong returned from their embassy to the Khitan and received the same distribution of vessels and silks as Feng Dao and his party.
entries.literal: On the first day of the third month, the guimao day, Left Vice Director Liu Ju and Supervising Secretary Lu Chong returned from their mission to the Khitan; vessels and silks were distributed as rewards, as with Feng Dao and the others.

entries.zh: 乙巳，回鶻可汗仁美遣使貢方物，中有玉狻猊，實奇貨也。
entries.en: On the yisi day, the Uyghur qaghan Renmei sent envoys bearing tribute, including a jade suanni lion—a truly rare treasure.
entries.literal: On the yisi day, the Uyghur qaghan Renmei sent envoys to present local products; among them was a jade suanni, which was truly a rare treasure.

entries.zh: 丙午，涇州節度使張萬進卒，贈太師。
entries.en: On the bingwu day, Zhang Wanjin, military governor of Jing Prefecture, died and was posthumously granted the title Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: On the bingwu day, Zhang Wanjin, Military Governor of Jing Prefecture, died; he was posthumously awarded the title Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 己未，皇子開封尹鄭王重貴、歸德軍節度使兼侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使劉知遠、忠武軍節度使杜重威，並加同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: On the jiwei day, Prince Chonggui of Zheng, administrator of Kaifeng; Liu Zhiyuan, military governor of the Guide Army and commander of the palace guard horse and foot; and Du Chongwei, military governor of the Zhongwu Army—all were promoted to grand councilor.
entries.literal: On the jiwei day, the imperial son Chonggui, Prince of Zheng and Administrator of Kaifeng; Liu Zhiyuan, Military Governor of the Guide Army and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot; and Du Chongwei, Military Governor of the Zhongwu Army—all were promoted to Grand Councilor with the Concurrent Signatory of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 天平軍節度使趙在禮封衛國公。
entries.en: Zhao Zaili, military governor of the Tianping Army, was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
entries.literal: Zhao Zaili, Military Governor of the Tianping Army, was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

entries.zh: 庚申，遣內臣趙處比以版詔征華山隱者前右拾遺鄭雲叟、玉笥山道士羅隱之。
entries.en: On the gengshen day, the eunuch Zhao Chubi was sent with an edict to summon Zheng Yunsou, the former right reminder and recluse of Mount Hua, and Luo Yinzi, a Daoist priest of Mount Yujian.
entries.literal: On the gengshen day, the eunuch Zhao Chubi was dispatched with an edict on board to summon Zheng Yunsou, former Right Reminder and recluse of Mount Hua, and Luo Yinzi, Daoist priest of Mount Yujian.

entries.zh: 靈州戍將王彥忠據懷遠城作叛，帝遣供奉官齊延祚乘驛而往，彥忠率眾出降，延祚矯制殺之。
entries.en: Wang Yanzhong, garrison commander at Ling Prefecture, seized Huaiyuan City and rebelled. The emperor sent palace attendant Qi Yanzuo post-haste by relay; Yanzhong led his men out to surrender, but Yanzuo forged an order and had him executed.
entries.literal: Wang Yanzhong, garrison commander of Ling Prefecture, seized Huaiyuan City and rebelled; the Emperor sent the palace attendant Qi Yanzuo post-haste by relay station; Yanzhong led his troops out to surrender, and Yanzuo forged an order and killed him.

entries.zh: 詔：「齊延祚辜我誓言，擅行屠戮。
entries.en: An edict declared: "Qi Yanzuo has violated my sworn pledge and on his own authority carried out a massacre.
entries.literal: An edict stated: "Qi Yanzuo has betrayed my sworn pledge and on his own authority carried out slaughter.

entries.zh: 彰殺降之罪，隳示信之文。
entries.en: He has made manifest the crime of killing those who surrendered and has undermined our pledge of good faith.
entries.literal: He has made manifest the crime of killing those who surrendered and has destroyed the text of showing good faith.

entries.zh: 宜除名決重杖一頓配流。
entries.en: He is to be stripped of rank, given one heavy beating, and exiled by assignment.
entries.literal: He should be stripped of his name and office, sentenced to one heavy beating, and banished by assignment.

entries.zh: 王彥忠贈官收葬。」
entries.en: Wang Yanzhong was posthumously granted an office and given a proper burial."
entries.literal: Wang Yanzhong was posthumously granted an office and given burial."

entries.zh: 辛酉，封回鶻可汗仁美為奉化可汗。
entries.en: On the xinyou day, the Uyghur qaghan Renmei was enfeoffed as Qaghan of Fenghua.
entries.literal: On the xinyou day, the Uyghur qaghan Renmei was enfeoffed as Qaghan of Fenghua.

entries.zh: 癸亥，以左龍武統軍皇甫遇為鎮國軍節度使，張彥澤為彰義軍節度使。
entries.en: On the guihai day, Huangfu Yu, commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army, was appointed military governor of the Zhenguo Army, and Zhang Yanze was appointed military governor of the Zhangyi Army.
entries.literal: On the guihai day, Huangfu Yu, Commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army, was appointed Military Governor of the Zhenguo Army; Zhang Yanze was appointed Military Governor of the Zhangyi Army.

entries.zh: 九月辛未，以右羽林統軍周密為鄜州節度使。
entries.en: In the ninth month, Zhou Mi, commander of the Right Forest Guard Army, was appointed military governor of Fu Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on the xinwei day, Zhou Mi, Commander of the Right Forest Guard Army, was appointed Military Governor of Fu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 癸酉，升婺州為武勝軍額。
entries.en: On the guiyou day, Wu Prefecture was elevated to the Wusheng Army designation.
entries.literal: On the guiyou day, Wu Prefecture was promoted to the Wusheng Army designation.

entries.zh: 丁丑，宴群臣於永福殿。
entries.en: On the dingchou day, the emperor gave a banquet for the officials in the Yongfu Hall.
entries.literal: On the dingchou day, the Emperor gave a banquet to the officials in the Yongfu Hall.

entries.zh: 契丹使訥默庫來聘，
entries.en: The Khitan envoy Nemoku came on a friendly mission,
entries.literal: The Khitan envoy Nemoku came on a friendly mission,

entries.zh: 〈（《遼史》：會同二年正月戊申，晉遣金吾衛大將軍馬從斌、考功郎中劉知新來貢珍幣。
entries.en: (The 《History of Liao》 records: In the first month of the second year of Huitong, on the wushen day, Jin sent Ma Congbin, great general of the Golden Wu Guard, and Liu Zhixin, director of the Bureau of Merit, to present precious tribute.
entries.literal: (The 《History of Liao》 records: In the first month of the second year of Huitong, on the wushen day, Jin sent Ma Congbin, Great General of the Golden Wu Guard, and Liu Zhixin, Director of the Bureau of Merit, to present precious goods in tribute.

entries.zh: 丙辰，晉遣使謝免沿邊四州錢幣。
entries.en: On the bingchen day, Jin sent envoys to thank Liao for exempting the four border prefectures from coinage obligations.
entries.literal: On the bingchen day, Jin sent envoys to thank [Liao] for exempting the four border prefectures from coinage obligations.

entries.zh: 七月戊申，晉遣使進犀帶。
entries.en: In the seventh month, Jin sent envoys presenting rhinoceros-horn belts.
entries.literal: In the seventh month, on the wushen day, Jin sent envoys presenting rhinoceros-horn belts.

entries.zh: 閏月乙酉，遣使賜晉良馬。
entries.en: In the intercalary month, Liao sent envoys bestowing fine horses on Jin.
entries.literal: In the intercalary month, on the yiyou day, [Liao] sent envoys bestowing fine horses on Jin.

entries.zh: 八月己丑，晉遣使貢歲幣，奏輸戌、亥二歲金幣於燕京。）〉
entries.en: In the eighth month, Jin sent envoys presenting the annual tribute, reporting delivery of gold and silk for the xu and hai years to Yanjing.)〉
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on the jichou day, Jin sent envoys presenting the annual tribute, reporting delivery of gold and silk for the xu and hai years to Yanjing.)〉

entries.zh: 致牛馬等物。
entries.en: Presenting cattle, horses, and other goods.
entries.literal: Presenting cattle, horses, and other goods.

entries.zh: 己卯，遙領洮州保順軍節度使鮑君福加檢校太師、兼侍中，判湖州諸軍事。
entries.en: On the jimao day, Bao Junfu, nominal military governor of the Baoshun Army at Tao Prefecture, was promoted to acting grand preceptor and concurrent palace attendant and assigned to administer military affairs at Hu Prefecture.
entries.literal: On the jimao day, Bao Junfu, Military Governor of the Baoshun Army of Tao Prefecture in absentia, was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant and assigned to administer all military affairs of Hu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 辛巳，相州節度使桑維翰上言：「管內所獲賊人，從來籍沒財產，請止之。」
entries.en: On the xinsi day, Sang Weihan, military governor of Xiang Prefecture, submitted: "Within my jurisdiction the property of captured bandits has always been confiscated; I ask that this practice be stopped."
entries.literal: On the xinsi day, Sang Weihan, Military Governor of Xiang Prefecture, submitted: "Within my jurisdiction, property of captured bandits has always been confiscated; I request that this be stopped."

entries.zh: 詔：「今後凡有賊人，準格律定罪，不得沒納家資，天下諸州準此。」
entries.en: An edict declared: "Henceforth all bandits are to be sentenced according to statute; household property must not be confiscated; all prefectures throughout the empire shall follow this rule."
entries.literal: An edict stated: "Henceforth, for all bandits, sentence according to the statutes and ordinances; household property must not be confiscated; all prefectures throughout the empire shall follow this."

entries.zh: 癸未，封唐許王李從益為郇國公，奉唐之祀，服色旌旗一依舊制。
entries.en: On the guiwei day, Li Congyi, Prince of Xu of Tang, was enfeoffed as Duke of Xun to maintain the sacrifices of Tang, with ceremonial dress, colors, and banners following the old Tang regulations.
entries.literal: On the guiwei day, Li Congyi, Prince of Xu of Tang, was enfeoffed as Duke of Xun to maintain the sacrifices of Tang; ceremonial dress, colors, and banners all followed the old regulations.

entries.zh: 仍以西京至德宮為廟，牲幣器服悉從官給。
entries.en: The Zhide Palace in the Western Capital was designated the temple, with sacrificial animals, silks, vessels, and robes all supplied by the government.
entries.literal: The Zhide Palace of the Western Capital was made the temple; sacrificial animals, silks, vessels, and robes were all supplied by the government.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：九月，敕：「周受龍圖，立夏、殷之祀；
entries.en: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》: In the ninth month, an edict stated: "Zhou received the dragon chart and established sacrifices to Xia and Yin;
entries.literal: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》: In the ninth month, an edict stated: "Zhou received the dragon chart and established sacrifices to Xia and Yin;

entries.zh: 唐膺鳳歷，開酅、介之封。
entries.en: Tang received the phoenix chronology and opened the enfeoffments of Xi and Jie.
entries.literal: Tang received the phoenix chronology and opened the enfeoffments of Xi and Jie.

entries.zh: 乃眷前朝，載稽舊典，宜封土宇，俾奉宗祧。
entries.en: Mindful of the former dynasty and examining the old canons, territory should be enfeoffed so that the ancestral sacrifices may be maintained.
entries.literal: Now mindful of the former dynasty, examining the old canons, territory should be enfeoffed so that the ancestral temple may be maintained.

entries.zh: 宜以郇國三千戶封唐許王李從益為郇國公」云。）〉
entries.en: The three thousand households of Xun should enfeoff Li Congyi, Prince of Xu of Tang, as Duke of Xun," it states.)〉
entries.literal: The three thousand households of the State of Xun should enfeoff Li Congyi, Prince of Xu of Tang, as Duke of Xun," it states.)〉

entries.zh: 丙戌，高麗王王建遣使貢方物。
entries.en: On the bingxu day, Wang Jian, king of Goryeo, sent envoys bearing tribute of local products.
entries.literal: On the bingxu day, Wang Jian, King of Goryeo, sent envoys presenting local products in tribute.

entries.zh: 己丑，以中書侍郎、平章事李崧權判集賢殿事。
entries.en: On the jichou day, Li Song, grand councilor and vice director of the Secretariat, was appointed acting administrator of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.
entries.literal: On the jichou day, Li Song, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, was appointed acting administrator of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.

entries.zh: 庚寅，詔停寒食、七夕、重陽及十月暖帳內外群官貢獻。
entries.en: On the gengyin day, an edict suspended official tribute offerings on Cold Food Festival, Seventh Night, Double Ninth, and the October warming of the tent.
entries.literal: On the gengyin day, an edict suspended tribute offerings from civil and military officials at court and in the provinces on Cold Food Festival, Seventh Night, Double Ninth, and the October warming of the tent.

entries.zh: 丙申，以威勝軍節度副使羅周嶽為給事中，中書舍人李詳改禮部侍郎，禮部侍郎呂琦改刑部侍郎，刑部侍郎王松改戶部侍郎，戶部侍郎閻至改兵部侍郎，中書舍人王易簡充史館修撰，判館事。
entries.en: On the bingshen day, Luo Zhouyue was appointed supervising secretary; Li Xiang became vice minister of rites; Lü Qi, vice minister of justice; Wang Song, vice minister of revenue; Yan Zhi, vice minister of war; and Wang Yijian, compiler of the Historiography Institute, was placed in charge of its affairs.
entries.literal: On the bingshen day, Luo Zhouyue, Deputy Military Governor of the Weisheng Army, was appointed Supervising Secretary; Li Xiang, Secretariat Drafter, was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites; Lü Qi, Vice Minister of Rites, to Vice Minister of Justice; Wang Song, Vice Minister of Justice, to Vice Minister of Revenue; Yan Zhi, Vice Minister of Revenue, to Vice Minister of War; and Wang Yijian, Secretariat Drafter, was made Compiler of the Historiography Institute and administered its affairs.

entries.zh: 十一月甲戌，以太子賓客李延範為司農卿。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, Li Yanfan, guest of the heir apparent, was appointed minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on the jiaxu day, Li Yanfan, Guest of the Heir Apparent, was appointed Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.

entries.zh: 乙亥，詔立唐高祖、太宗及莊宗、明宗、閔帝五廟於洛陽。
entries.en: On the yihai day, an edict ordered five temples established at Luoyang to Gaozu and Taizong of Tang and to Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min.
entries.literal: On the yihai day, an edict ordered the establishment at Luoyang of five temples to Gaozu and Taizong of Tang and to Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min.

entries.zh: 丁丑，祠部郎中、知制誥吳承範改中書舍人，充翰林學士；
entries.en: On the dingchou day, Wu Chengfan was transferred to secretariat drafter and made Hanlin academician;
entries.literal: On the dingchou day, Wu Chengfan, Director of the Sacrificial Section and drafter of edicts, was transferred to Secretariat Drafter and made Hanlin Academician;

entries.zh: 翰林學士、中書舍人竇貞固改御史中丞；
entries.en: Dou Zhengu was transferred to vice censor-in-chief;
entries.literal: Dou Zhengu, Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafter, was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief;

entries.zh: 御史中丞薛融改尚書左丞；
entries.en: Xue Rong was transferred to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs;
entries.literal: Xue Rong, Vice Censor-in-Chief, was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs;

entries.zh: 尚書右丞王延改吏部侍郎；
entries.en: Wang Yan was transferred to vice minister of personnel;
entries.literal: Wang Yan, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel;

entries.zh: 尚書左丞崔棁改太常卿。
entries.en: and Cui Zhuo was transferred to chief minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: Cui Zhuo, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 戊寅，史館奏：「請令宰臣一人撰錄時政記，逐時以備撰述。」
entries.en: On the wuyin day, the Historiography Institute submitted: "We ask that one chief minister be ordered to compile the Record of Current Administration and keep it up to date for future historiography."
entries.literal: On the wuyin day, the Historiography Institute submitted: "We request that one chief minister be ordered to compile the Record of Current Administration, keeping it up to date for future compilation."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The request was approved.
entries.literal: The request was approved.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：史館奏：「唐長壽二年，右丞姚璹奏，帝王謨訓，不可闕文。
entries.en: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》: The Historiography Institute submitted: "In the second year of Changshou of Tang, Vice Director Yao Shuo submitted that the counsels and instructions of emperors must not lack written record.
entries.literal: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium》: The Historiography Institute submitted: "In the second year of Changshou of Tang, Vice Director Yao Shuo submitted that the counsels and instructions of emperors must not lack written record.

entries.zh: 其仗下所言軍國政事，令宰臣一人撰錄，號『時政記』。
entries.en: Matters of state and military affairs spoken below the imperial guard were to be recorded by one chief minister, titled the Record of Current Administration.
entries.literal: Matters of state and military affairs spoken below the imperial guard were to be recorded by one chief minister, titled the 'Record of Current Administration.'

entries.zh: 唐明宗朝，又委端明殿學士撰錄，逐季送付史館，伏乞遵行者。
entries.en: In the reign of Mingzong of Tang, the task was again entrusted to an academician of the Duanming Hall to compile and deliver each quarter to the Historiography Institute; we humbly request that this precedent be followed.
entries.literal: In the reign of Mingzong of Tang, the task was again entrusted to an academician of the Duanming Hall to compile and deliver it each quarter to the Historiography Institute; we humbly request that this be followed.

entries.zh: 宜令宰臣一員撰述。」）〉
entries.en: One chief minister should be ordered to compile it.")〉
entries.literal: One chief minister should be ordered to compile it.")〉

entries.zh: 己卯，吏部侍郎龍敏改尚書左丞。
entries.en: On the jimao day, Long Min was transferred to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: On the jimao day, Long Min, Vice Minister of Personnel, was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 己丑，以太子賓客楊凝式為禮部尚書致仕。
entries.en: On the jichou day, Yang Ningshi, guest of the heir apparent, was granted retirement as minister of rites.
entries.literal: On the jichou day, Yang Ningshi, Guest of the Heir Apparent, was granted retirement as Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 詔建錢爐於欒川。
entries.en: An edict ordered coin furnaces built at Luanchuan.
entries.literal: An edict ordered coin furnaces built at Luanchuan.

entries.zh: 丙申，諫議大夫致仕逍遙先生鄭雲叟卒。
entries.en: On the bingshen day, Zheng Yunsou, the retired remonstrance counselor known as Master Xiaoyao, died.
entries.literal: On the bingshen day, Zheng Yunsou, retired Remonstrance Counselor and Master Xiaoyao, died.

entries.zh: 天福四年春正月癸卯，帝御崇元殿受朝賀，仗衛如式。
entries.en: On the guimao day, the first day of the first month of spring in the fourth year of Tianfu, the emperor took the throne in the Chongyuan Hall to receive the New Year court congratulations, with the guard of honor arrayed according to custom.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tianfu, on the guimao day of the first month in spring, the Emperor took his seat in the Chongyuan Hall to receive court congratulations; the guard of honor followed the prescribed form.

entries.zh: 丙午，召太子太師致仕範延光宴於便殿。
entries.en: On the bingwu day, the emperor summoned Fan Yanguang, the retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, to a banquet in the informal hall.
entries.literal: On the bingwu day, he summoned Fan Yanguang, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent who had retired from office, and gave him a banquet in the informal hall.

entries.zh: 以延光歸命之後，慮懷疑懼，故休假之內，錫以款密。
entries.en: After Fan Yanguang had surrendered, he was troubled by suspicion and fear; during his leave of absence the emperor therefore treated him with warm and confidential kindness.
entries.literal: Because after Yanguang had submitted, he was anxious with suspicion and fear, therefore during his leave of absence the Emperor bestowed intimate attentions upon him.

entries.zh: 帝謂之曰：「無忿疾以傷厥神，無憂思以勞厥衷。
entries.en: The emperor told him, "Do not let resentment harm your spirit, and do not let anxiety wear upon your heart.
entries.literal: The Emperor said to him: "Do not let anger harm your spirit, and do not let worry and brooding weary your heart.

entries.zh: 朕方示信於四方，豈食言於汝也。」
entries.en: I am now demonstrating my good faith to the realm; I would never go back on my word to you."
entries.literal: I am now showing good faith to all quarters; I would never break my word to you."

entries.zh: 延光俯伏拜謝，其心遂安。
entries.en: Fan Yanguang prostrated himself and bowed in thanks, and his mind was finally at ease.
entries.literal: Yanguang prostrated himself and bowed in thanks, and his mind was then at ease.

entries.zh: 丁未，以西京副留守龍敏為吏部侍郎。
entries.en: On the dingwei day, Long Min, deputy stay-behind commissioner of the Western Capital, was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: On the dingwei day, Long Min, Deputy Stay-behind Commissioner of the Western Capital, was appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 戊申，盜發唐閔帝陵。
entries.en: On the wushen day, tomb robbers broke into the mausoleum of Emperor Min of Tang.
entries.literal: On the wushen day, robbers broke into the tomb of Emperor Min of Tang.

entries.zh: 己酉，朔方軍節度使張希崇卒，贈太師。
entries.en: On the jiyou day, Zhang Xichong, military governor of the Shuofang Army, died and was posthumously granted the title Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: On the jiyou day, Zhang Xichong, Military Governor of the Shuofang Army, died; he was posthumously awarded the title Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 以澶州防禦使張從恩為樞密副使。
entries.en: Zhang Cong'en, defense commissioner of Chan Prefecture, was appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: Zhang Cong'en, Defense Commissioner of Chan Prefecture, was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 甲寅，以侍衛步軍都指揮使、寧江軍節度使景延廣為義成軍節度使，以義成軍節度使馮暉為朔方軍節度使。
entries.en: On the jiayin day, Jing Yanguang, commander of the palace guard foot soldiers and military governor of the Ningjiang Army, was transferred to military governor of the Yicheng Army, and Feng Hui, military governor of the Yicheng Army, was appointed military governor of the Shuofang Army.
entries.literal: On the jiayin day, Jing Yanguang, Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Foot Soldiers and Military Governor of the Ningjiang Army, was made Military Governor of the Yicheng Army; Feng Hui, Military Governor of the Yicheng Army, was made Military Governor of the Shuofang Army.

entries.zh: 乙卯，左諫議大夫曹國珍上言：「請於內外臣僚之中，選才略之士，聚《唐六典》、前後《會要》、《禮閣新儀》、《大中統類》、律令格式等，精詳纂集，俾無漏落，別為書一部，目為《大晉政統》。」
entries.en: On the yimao day, Cao Guozhen, left remonstrance counselor, submitted: "I ask that talented officials be chosen from among court and provincial ranks to assemble the 《Tang Administrative Compendium》, the earlier and later 《Institutional Compendia》, the 《New Ritual Protocols of the Ritual Office》, the 《Comprehensive Categories of the Dazhong Era》, and the statutes, ordinances, and formats, and to compile them carefully so that nothing is left out, producing a separate work to be called 《Comprehensive Institutions of Great Jin》."
entries.literal: On the yimao day, Cao Guozhen, Left Remonstrance Counselor, submitted: "I request that from among civil and military officials at court and in the provinces men of talent and ability be selected to gather the 《Tang Administrative Compendium》, the earlier and later 《Institutional Compendia》, the 《New Ritual Protocols of the Ritual Office》, the 《Comprehensive Categories of the Dazhong Era》, statutes, ordinances, formats, and the like, compile them with care and thoroughness so that nothing is omitted, and produce a separate work entitled 《Comprehensive Institutions of Great Jin》."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The request was approved.
entries.literal: The request was approved.

entries.zh: 其詳議官，宜差太子少師梁文矩、左散騎常侍張允、大理卿張澄、國子祭酒唐汭、大理少卿高鴻漸、國子司業田敏、禮部郎中呂咸休、司勛員外郎劉濤、刑部員外郎李知損、監察御史郭延升等一十九人充。
entries.en: Nineteen officials were appointed to deliberate the project in detail, including Liang Wenju, junior preceptor of the heir apparent; Zhang Yun, left regular attendant; Zhang Cheng, chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review; Tang Rui, chancellor of the Directorate of Education; Gao Hongjian, vice chief judge; Tian Min, vice chancellor of the directorate; Lü Xianxiu, director of the Ministry of Rites; Liu Tao and Li Zhisun, vice directors of the ministries of Personnel and Justice; and Guo Yansheng, investigating censor, among others.
entries.literal: For the officials to deliberate in detail, nineteen persons were to be appointed, including Liang Wenju, Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; Zhang Yun, Left Regular Attendant; Zhang Cheng, Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review; Tang Rui, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education; Gao Hongjian, Vice Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review; Tian Min, Vice Chancellor of the Directorate of Education; Lü Xianxiu, Director of the Ministry of Rites; Liu Tao, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel; Li Zhisun, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice; and Guo Yansheng, Investigating Censor.

entries.zh: 文矩等咸曰：「改前代禮樂刑憲為《大晉政統》，則《堯典》、《舜典》當以《晉典》革名。」
entries.en: Wenju and the others all objected: "To recast the ritual, music, penal law, and statutes of former dynasties as the 《Comprehensive Institutions of Great Jin》 would mean that the 《Canon of Yao》 and the 《Canon of Shun》 would have to be renamed the 《Canon of Jin》."
entries.literal: Wenju and the others all said: "If the ritual, music, penal law, and statutes of former dynasties are changed into the 《Comprehensive Institutions of Great Jin》, then the 《Canon of Yao》 and the 《Canon of Shun》 ought to have their names changed to the 《Canon of Jin》."

entries.zh: 列狀駁之曰：
entries.en: They submitted a joint memorial in rebuttal, stating:
entries.literal: They submitted a collective memorial in rebuttal, stating:

entries.zh: 天福六年秋七月己未朔，帝御崇元殿視朝。
entries.en: On the new moon of the seventh month of autumn in Tianfu 6, the emperor held court in the Chongyuan Hall.
entries.literal: In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month of the sixth year of Tianfu (day jiwei, new moon), the emperor attended court in the Chongyuan Hall.

entries.zh: 庚申，升陳州為防禦使額。
entries.en: On gengshen, Chenzhou was raised to defense-commissioner rank.
entries.literal: On day gengshen, Chenzhou was promoted to defense commissioner status.

entries.zh: 辛酉，以前鄧州節度使焦方為貝州節度使。
entries.en: On xinyou, former Dengzhou commissioner Jiao Fang was appointed military commissioner of Beizhou.
entries.literal: On day xinyou, Jiao Fang, former military commissioner of Dengzhou, was made military commissioner of Beizhou.

entries.zh: 壬戌，涇州奏，西涼府留後李文謙，今年二月四日閉宅門自焚，遣元入西涼府譯語官與來人賫三部族蕃書進之。
entries.en: On renxu, Jingzhou reported that Li Wenqian, acting commissioner of Xiliang, had shut his gates and burned himself to death on the fourth day of the second month of this year; an envoy sent into Xiliang with an interpreter and a visiting party had presented tribal documents from three clans.
entries.literal: On day renxu, Jingzhou memorialized that Li Wenqian, acting commissioner of Xiliang Prefecture, on the fourth day of the second month of this year closed his house gates and burned himself to death; he had sent an envoy into Xiliang Prefecture together with an interpreter and the visitor, bearing tribal documents of three clans to present them.

entries.zh: 以三司使劉審交為陳州防禦使。
entries.en: Liu Shenjiao, Commissioner of the Three Departments, was appointed defense commissioner of Chenzhou.
entries.literal: Liu Shenjiao, Commissioner of the Three Departments, was made defense commissioner of Chenzhou.

entries.zh: 癸亥，以前鄆州節度使趙在禮為許州節度使，以前鄴都留守、廣晉尹高行周為河南尹、西都留守。
entries.en: On guihai, former Yunzhou commissioner Zhao Zaili became commissioner of Xu Prefecture, and Gao Xingzhou, former Yedu defender and Guangjin prefect, became Henan prefect and defender of the Western Capital.
entries.literal: On day guihai, Zhao Zaili, former military commissioner of Yunzhou, was made military commissioner of Xu Prefecture; Gao Xingzhou, former defender of Yedu and prefect of Guangjin, was made prefect of Henan and defender of the Western Capital.

entries.zh: 詔改拱辰、威和、內直等軍並為興順。
entries.en: An edict renamed the Gongchen, Weihe, Neizhi, and related armies collectively as Xingshun.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that the armies Gongchen, Weihe, Neizhi, and others all be renamed Xingshun.

entries.zh: 甲子，以宣徽使、權西京留守張從恩判三司。
entries.en: On jiazi, Palace Attendant and acting Western Capital defender Zhang Cong'en was put in charge of the Three Departments.
entries.literal: On day jiazi, Zhang Cong'en, Palace Attendant and acting defender of the Western Capital, was assigned to oversee the Three Departments.

entries.zh: 己巳，以鄴都留守兼侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使、廣晉尹劉知遠為太原尹，充北京留守、河東節度使，仍割遼、沁二州卻隸河東。
entries.en: On jisi, Yedu defender Liu Zhiyuan—who also commanded the Palace Guard horse and foot armies and served as Guangjin prefect—was made Taiyuan prefect, defender of the Northern Capital, and Hedong commissioner, with Liao and Qin prefectures restored to Hedong's jurisdiction.
entries.literal: On day jisi, Liu Zhiyuan, defender of Yedu and concurrently commander of the Palace Guard horse and foot armies and prefect of Guangjin, was made prefect of Taiyuan, appointed defender of the Northern Capital and military commissioner of Hedong, and the two prefectures Liao and Qin were cut off and returned to Hedong jurisdiction.

entries.zh: 以北京留守李德充為廣晉尹，充鄴都留守；
entries.en: Northern Capital defender Li Dechong was made Guangjin prefect and appointed Yedu defender;
entries.literal: Li Dechong, defender of the Northern Capital, was made prefect of Guangjin and appointed defender of Yedu;

entries.zh: 以昭義節度使馬全節為邢州節度使，加同平章事。
entries.en: Zhaoyi commissioner Ma Quanjie was transferred to Xingzhou and promoted to Vice Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: Ma Quanjie, military commissioner of Zhaoyi, was made military commissioner of Xingzhou and given the additional title of Vice Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 甲戌，詔：「今後諸道行軍副使，不得奏薦骨肉為殿直供奉官。」
entries.en: On jiaxu, an edict declared: "Hereafter, deputy field commanders in the circuits may not recommend close relatives for appointment as palace attendants or tribute officers."
entries.literal: On day jiaxu, an edict stated: "Henceforth deputy commanders on campaign in the various circuits may not memorialize recommending their kin as palace attendants or tribute officers."

entries.zh: 己卯，以前陜州節度使李從敏為昭義軍節度使，以陜州節度使景延廣為河陽三城節度使兼侍衛親軍馬步軍都虞候，以河陽節度使石赟為陜州節度使。
entries.en: On jimao, former Shanzhou commissioner Li Congmin became Zhaoyi commissioner; Shanzhou commissioner Jing Yanguang became Heyang Three Cities commissioner and chief adjutant of the Palace Guard; and Heyang commissioner Shi Yun was transferred to Shanzhou.
entries.literal: On day jimao, Li Congmin, former military commissioner of Shanzhou, was made military commissioner of the Zhaoyi army; Jing Yanguang, military commissioner of Shanzhou, was made military commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang and concurrently chief adjutant of the Palace Guard horse and foot armies; Shi Yun, military commissioner of Heyang, was made military commissioner of Shanzhou.

entries.zh: 壬午，突厥遣使朝貢。
entries.en: On renwu, the Turks sent envoys bearing tribute.
entries.literal: On day renwu, the Turks sent envoys to present tribute at court.

entries.zh: 以遙領壽州忠正軍節度使兼侍衛馬軍都指揮使李懷忠為同州節度使，以宣徽北院使李守貞遙領忠正軍節度使、侍衛馬軍指揮使。
entries.en: Li Huaizhong, titular Zhongzheng commissioner at Shouzhou and commander of the Palace Guard cavalry, was appointed Tongzhou commissioner; Palace Northern Bureau attendant Li Shouzhen was given titular Zhongzheng command and cavalry command.
entries.literal: Li Huaizhong, titular military commissioner of the Zhongzheng army at Shouzhou and concurrently commander of the Palace Guard cavalry, was made military commissioner of Tongzhou; Li Shouzhen, Attendant of the Northern Palace Bureau, was given titular command of the Zhongzheng army and the Palace Guard cavalry.

entries.zh: 甲申，降御劄，取八月五日暫幸鄴都，沿路供頓，並委所司以官物排比，州縣不得科率人戶。
entries.en: On jiashen, the emperor issued a rescript scheduling a temporary visit to Yedu on the fifth day of the eighth month; provisioning along the route was to come from official stores through the responsible agencies, and local governments were forbidden to impose levies on households.
entries.literal: On day jiashen, an imperial rescript was issued: a temporary visit to Yedu was set for the fifth day of the eighth month; supplies along the route were all to be arranged by the responsible offices from government stores, and prefectures and counties might not levy the populace.

entries.zh: 丙戌，以右諫議大夫趙遠為中書舍人，吏部郎中鄭受益為右諫議大夫，刑部郎中殷鵬為水部郎中、知制誥。
entries.en: On bingxu, Right Remonstrance Censor Zhao Yuan became Secretariat Drafter; Personnel Director Zheng Shouyi became Right Remonstrance Censor; and Justice Director Yin Peng became Works Director with charge of drafting edicts.
entries.literal: On day bingxu, Zhao Yuan, Right Remonstrance Censor, was made Secretariat Drafter; Zheng Shouyi, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, was made Right Remonstrance Censor; Yin Peng, Director in the Ministry of Justice, was made Director in the Ministry of Works with charge of drafting imperial documents.

entries.zh: 天福七年春正月丙辰朔，不受朝賀，用兵故也。
entries.en: On the new moon of the first month of spring in Tianfu 7, the emperor declined court congratulations because troops were in the field.
entries.literal: In spring, on the first day of the first month of the seventh year of Tianfu (day bingchen, new moon), court congratulations were not accepted, because of military operations.

entries.zh: 戊午，以前將作監李鍇為少府監。
entries.en: On wuwu, former Construction Director Li Kai became Palace Workshops director.
entries.literal: On day wuwu, Li Kai, former Director of Imperial Construction, was made Director of the Palace Workshops.

entries.zh: 北面招討使杜重威奏，今月二日收復鎮州，斬安重榮，傳首闕下。
entries.en: Northern campaign commander Du Chongwei reported that on the second of this month Zhenzhou had been retaken, An Chongrong beheaded, and his head sent to the capital.
