entries.literal: Du Chongwei, northern campaign commander, memorialized that on the second day of this month Zhenzhou had been recovered, An Chongrong was beheaded, and his head was sent to the capital.

entries.zh: 帝御乾明樓，宣露布訖，大理卿受馘，付市徇之，百官稱賀。
entries.en: The emperor mounted the Qianming Tower and proclaimed the victory bulletin; when the rites were done, the Minister of Punishments received the severed head and had it displayed in the market, and the officials offered congratulations.
entries.literal: The emperor ascended the Qianming Tower, proclaimed the victory bulletin, and when it was finished the Minister of Punishments received the severed head and handed it to the market for public display; the hundred officials offered congratulations.

entries.zh: 曲赦廣晉府禁囚。
entries.en: A partial amnesty was proclaimed for prisoners in the Guangjin jail.
entries.literal: A partial amnesty was granted to prisoners held in the Guangjin prefecture jail.

entries.zh: 〈（《遼史》云：戊辰，晉函安重榮首來獻，上數欲親討重榮，至是乃止。）〉
entries.en: (《Liao History》: On wuchen, Later Jin presented An Chongrong's head in a box; the Khitan emperor had repeatedly intended to campaign against Chongrong in person, and only then abandoned the plan.)〉
entries.literal: (The 《Liao History》 states: On day wuchen, Jin sent An Chongrong's head in a box as tribute; the emperor had several times wished to campaign against Chongrong in person, and only then stopped.)〉

entries.zh: 辛酉，追贈皇弟三人：故沂州馬步軍都指揮使、贈太傅德再贈太尉，追封福王；
entries.en: On xinyou, three imperial younger brothers received posthumous honors: De, former Yizhou horse-and-foot commander and already Grand Mentor, was raised to Grand Marshal and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Fu;
entries.literal: On day xinyou, three imperial younger brothers were posthumously honored: De, former commander of horse and foot armies at Yizhou and posthumously Grand Mentor, was again granted Grand Marshal and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Fu;

entries.zh: 故檢校太子賓客、贈太傅殷再贈太尉，追封通王；
entries.en: Yin, former Honorary Heir Apparent Tutor and Grand Mentor, was raised to Grand Marshal and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Tong;
entries.literal: Yin, former Honorary Tutor to the Heir Apparent and posthumously Grand Mentor, was again granted Grand Marshal and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Tong;

entries.zh: 故彰聖右第三軍都指揮使長州刺史、贈大傅威再贈太尉，追封廣王。
entries.en: Wei, former Zhangsheng third-right-army commander and Changzhou prefect, already Grand Mentor, was raised to Grand Marshal and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Guang.
entries.literal: Wei, former commander of the third right army of Zhangsheng and prefect of Changzhou and posthumously Grand Mentor, was again granted Grand Marshal and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Guang.

entries.zh: 壬戌，追贈皇子五人：故右衛將軍、贈太保重英再贈太傅，追封虢王；
entries.en: On renxu, five imperial sons received posthumous honors: Chongying, former Right Guard general and Grand Marshal, was raised to Grand Mentor and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Guo;
entries.literal: On day renxu, five imperial sons were posthumously honored: Chongying, former General of the Right Guard and posthumously Grand Marshal, was again granted Grand Mentor and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Guo;

entries.zh: 故權東京留守、河南尹、贈太傅重乂再贈太尉，追封壽王；
entries.en: Chong'ai, former acting Eastern Capital defender and Henan prefect, already Grand Mentor, was raised to Grand Marshal and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shou;
entries.literal: Chong'ai, former acting defender of the Eastern Capital and prefect of Henan and posthumously Grand Mentor, was again granted Grand Marshal and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Shou;

entries.zh: 故皇城副使、贈太保重裔再贈太傅，追封郯王；
entries.en: Chongyi, former Imperial City vice commissioner and Grand Marshal, was raised to Grand Mentor and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Tan;
entries.literal: Chongyi, former vice commissioner of the Imperial City and posthumously Grand Marshal, was again granted Grand Mentor and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Tan;

entries.zh: 故河陽節度使、贈太尉重信再贈太師，追封沂王；
entries.en: Chongxin, former Heyang commissioner and Grand Marshal, was raised to Grand Preceptor and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yi;
entries.literal: Chongxin, former military commissioner of Heyang and posthumously Grand Marshal, was again granted Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Yi;

entries.zh: 故左金吾衛將軍、贈太保重進再贈太傅，追封夔王。
entries.en: Chongjin, former Left Golden Crow general and Grand Marshal, was raised to Grand Mentor and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Kui.
entries.literal: Chongjin, former General of the Left Golden Crow Guard and posthumously Grand Marshal, was again granted Grand Mentor and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Kui.

entries.zh: 癸亥，改鎮州為恒州，成德軍為順國軍。
entries.en: On guihai, Zhenzhou was renamed Hengzhou and the Chengde army redesignated Shunguo.
entries.literal: On day guihai, Zhenzhou was renamed Hengzhou, and the Chengde army was renamed the Shunguo army.

entries.zh: 丙寅，以門下侍郎、平章事、監修國史趙瑩為侍中；
entries.en: On bingyin, Secretariat Vice Minister, Grand Councilor, and national-history supervisor Zhao Ying became Palace Vice Minister;
entries.literal: On day bingyin, Zhao Ying, Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, and supervisor of the compilation of the national history, was made Palace Vice Minister;

entries.zh: 青州節度使楊光遠加食邑，改賜功臣名號；
entries.en: Qingzhou commissioner Yang Guangyuan received an increased fief and a new merit epithet;
entries.literal: Yang Guangyuan, military commissioner of Qingzhou, received an increase in fief income and a change in the bestowed honorary epithet of merit;

entries.zh: 兗州節度使桑維翰加檢校太保；
entries.en: Yanzhou commissioner Sang Weihan was made Honorary Grand Guardian;
entries.literal: Sang Weihan, military commissioner of Yanzhou, was made Honorary Grand Guardian;

entries.zh: 河東節度使劉知遠加兼侍中；
entries.en: Hedong commissioner Liu Zhiyuan was also made Vice Grand Councilor;
entries.literal: Liu Zhiyuan, military commissioner of Hedong, was additionally made Vice Grand Councilor;

entries.zh: 以鄆州節度使、北面行營招討使、侍衛親軍都指揮使杜重威為恒州順國軍節度使，加兼侍中；
entries.en: Yunzhou commissioner, northern campaign commander, and Palace Guard commander Du Chongwei became Shunguo commissioner at Hengzhou and was also made Vice Grand Councilor;
entries.literal: Du Chongwei, military commissioner of Yunzhou, northern campaign commander, and commander of the Palace Guard, was made military commissioner of the Shunguo army at Hengzhou and additionally made Vice Grand Councilor;

entries.zh: 皇子廣晉尹兼功德使、齊王重貴加兼侍中；
entries.en: Prince Chonggui of Qi, Guangjin prefect and Commissioner of Meritorious Works, was also made Vice Grand Councilor;
entries.literal: Chonggui, prince, prefect of Guangjin and concurrently Commissioner of Meritorious Works and Prince of Qi, was additionally made Vice Grand Councilor;

entries.zh: 秦州節度使侯益加特進，增食邑。
entries.en: Qinzhou commissioner Hou Yi received Special Advancement and an enlarged fief.
entries.literal: Hou Yi, military commissioner of Qinzhou, was granted Special Advancement and an increase in fief income.

entries.zh: 丁卯，以判四方館事孟承誨為太府卿充職。
entries.en: On dingmao, Meng Chenghui, commissioner of the Four Directions Reception Office, was appointed Director of the Palace Storehouse.
entries.literal: On the dingmao day, Meng Chenghui, commissioner of the Four Directions Reception Office, was made Director of the Palace Storehouse with charge of the office.

entries.zh: 戊辰，以滄州節度使安叔千為邢州節度使，以北面行營副招討使、邢州節度使馬全節為定州節度使，以定州節度使王庭胤為滄州節度使，以前邢州節度使楊彥詢為華州節度使。
entries.en: On wuchen, Cangzhou commissioner An Shuqian became Xingzhou commissioner; Xingzhou commissioner and deputy northern campaign pacification commissioner Ma Quanjie became Dingzhou commissioner; Dingzhou commissioner Wang Tingyin became Cangzhou commissioner; and former Xingzhou commissioner Yang Yanxun became Huazhou commissioner.
entries.literal: On the wuchen day, An Shuqian, military commissioner of Cangzhou, was made military commissioner of Xingzhou; Ma Quanjie, deputy northern campaign pacification commissioner and military commissioner of Xingzhou, was made military commissioner of Dingzhou; Wang Tingyin, military commissioner of Dingzhou, was made military commissioner of Cangzhou; Yang Yanxun, former military commissioner of Xingzhou, was made military commissioner of Huazhou.

entries.zh: 恒州立功將校王溫以降等第除郡。
entries.en: Wang Wen, a meritorious officer of Hengzhou, received a prefectural post at a demoted rank.
entries.literal: Wang Wen, an officer of Hengzhou who had earned merit, was given a prefectural appointment at a reduced rank grade.

entries.zh: 庚午，契丹遣使來聘。
entries.en: On gengwu, Khitan envoys arrived on a friendly mission.
entries.literal: On the gengwu day, the Khitan sent envoys on a friendly visit.

entries.zh: 是日上元節，六街諸寺燃燈，禦乾明門觀之，夜半還宮。
entries.en: That day was the Lantern Festival. Lanterns blazed at temples throughout the Six Streets, and the emperor watched from Qianming Gate before returning to the palace at midnight.
entries.literal: That day was the Lantern Festival; lanterns were lit at temples throughout the Six Streets; the emperor went to Qianming Gate to view them and returned to the palace at midnight.

entries.zh: 壬申，延州節度使丁審琦加爵邑，鄧州節度使安審徽加檢校太傅，陜州節度使石赟加檢校太傅。
entries.en: On renshen, Yanzhou commissioner Ding Shenqi received ennoblement and an enlarged fief; Dengzhou commissioner An Shenhui was made Honorary Grand Mentor; and Shaanzhou commissioner Shi Yun was made Honorary Grand Mentor.
entries.literal: On the renshen day, Ding Shenqi, military commissioner of Yanzhou, received ennoblement and an increase in fief income; An Shenhui, military commissioner of Dengzhou, was made Honorary Grand Mentor; Shi Yun, military commissioner of Shaanzhou, was made Honorary Grand Mentor.

entries.zh: 乙亥，契丹遣使來聘。
entries.en: On yihai, Khitan envoys arrived on a friendly mission.
entries.literal: On the yihai day, the Khitan sent envoys on a friendly visit.

entries.zh: 河陽節度使兼侍衛馬步軍都虞候景延廣加檢校太尉，改鄆州節度使，典軍如故。
entries.en: Heyang commissioner and Palace Guard chief adjutant Jing Yanguang was made Honorary Grand Marshal, transferred to Yunzhou commissioner, and kept his army command.
entries.literal: Jing Yanguang, military commissioner of Heyang and chief adjutant of the Palace Guard horse and foot armies, was made Honorary Grand Marshal, transferred to military commissioner of Yunzhou, and retained command of the army as before.

entries.zh: 以前貝州節度使、北面行營馬步軍都虞候王周為河陽節度使，加檢校太保。
entries.en: Former Beizhou commissioner and northern campaign chief adjutant Wang Zhou became Heyang commissioner and was made Honorary Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: Wang Zhou, former military commissioner of Beizhou and chief adjutant of the northern campaign horse and foot armies, was made military commissioner of Heyang and granted Honorary Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 丁丑，以刑部侍郎竇貞固為門下侍郎，以禮部郎中邊歸讜為比部郎中、知制誥。
entries.en: On dingchou, Vice Minister of Punishments Dou Zhengu became Secretariat Vice Minister, and Rites Bureau Director Bian Guidan became Penalties Bureau Director and drafter of rescripts.
entries.literal: On the dingchou day, Dou Zhengu, Vice Minister of Punishments, was made Vice Minister of the Secretariat; Bian Guidan, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites, was made Bureau Director of Penalties and drafter of rescripts.

entries.zh: 壬午，以河陽節度使王周為涇州節度使，以恒州節度副使王欽祚為殿中監。
entries.en: On renwu, Heyang commissioner Wang Zhou became Jingzhou commissioner, and Hengzhou deputy commissioner Wang Qinzuo became Director of Palace Affairs.
entries.literal: On the renwu day, Wang Zhou, military commissioner of Heyang, was made military commissioner of Jingzhou; Wang Qinzuo, deputy military commissioner of Hengzhou, was made Director of Palace Affairs.

entries.zh: 六月丁巳，以兗州節度使桑維翰為晉昌軍節度使，以前許州節度使安審琦為兗州節度使。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on dingsi, Yanzhou commissioner Sang Weihan became Jinchang Army commissioner, and former Xu Prefecture commissioner An Shenqi became Yanzhou commissioner.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on day dingsi, Sang Weihan, military commissioner of Yanzhou, was made military commissioner of the Jinchang army; An Shenqi, former military commissioner of Xu Prefecture, was made military commissioner of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 襄州都部署高行周奏，安從進觀察判官李光圖出城請援，送赴闕。
entries.en: Xiangzhou commander Gao Xingzhou reported that An Congjin's observation judge Li Guangtu had left the city seeking reinforcements and was escorted to court.
entries.literal: Gao Xingzhou, overall commander at Xiangzhou, memorialized that Li Guangtu, observation administration judge of An Congjin, had left the city to request aid and was sent to the capital.

entries.zh: 乙丑，帝崩於保昌殿，壽五十一。
entries.en: On yichou the emperor died in the Baochang Hall at the age of fifty-one.
entries.literal: On day yichou, the emperor died in the Baochang Hall, aged fifty-one.

entries.zh: 遺制齊王重貴於柩前即皇帝位，喪紀並依舊制，山陵務從節儉，馬步諸軍優紀並從嗣君處分。
entries.en: His deathbed edict installed Prince Chonggui of Qi as emperor before the coffin. Mourning was to follow established custom, the tomb was to be kept austere, and rewards for the armies were left to the new emperor's discretion.
entries.literal: His final edict installed Chonggui, Prince of Qi, as emperor before the coffin; mourning rites were to follow the old regulations; the imperial tomb was to be kept frugal; and preferential treatment for the horse and foot armies was left to the disposition of the succeeding ruler.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒考異》云：《漢高祖實錄》：晉高祖大漸，召近臣屬之曰：「此天下，明宗之天下，寡人竊而處之久矣。
entries.en: (Examination of Variants in the Comprehensive Mirror: According to the Veritable Record of Han Gaozu, as Later Jin Gaozu lay dying he summoned his inner circle and said, "This realm belongs to Emperor Mingzong; I have held it only by usurpation for many years.
entries.literal: (Examination of Variants in the Comprehensive Mirror states: The Veritable Record of Han Gaozu records that as Later Jin Gaozu lay gravely ill, he summoned close ministers and entrusted them, saying: "This realm is the realm of Emperor Mingzong; I have held it in usurpation for long.

entries.zh: 寡人既謝，當歸許王，寡人之願也。」
entries.en: When I am gone, it should return to the Prince of Xu. That is my wish."
entries.literal: When I depart, it should return to the Prince of Xu—that is my wish."

entries.zh: 此說難信。）〉
entries.en: This account is difficult to credit.)〉
entries.literal: This account is hard to credit.)〉

entries.zh: 秋七月癸未朔，百官素服臨於天清殿。
entries.en: On the first day of the seventh month, guiwei, all officials in plain mourning dress attended at the Hall of Heavenly Clarity.
entries.literal: On the first day of the seventh month, the day guiwei, all officials in plain mourning dress attended at the Hall of Heavenly Clarity.

entries.zh: 戊子，詔應宮殿、州縣及官名、府號、人姓名，與先帝諱同音者改之。
entries.en: On wuzi, an edict ordered that palace halls, prefectures and counties, official titles, government offices, and personal names that shared the sound of the late emperor's taboo name were to be changed.
entries.literal: On wuzi, an edict ordered that wherever palace halls, prefectures and counties, official titles, government offices, or personal names shared the same sound as the late emperor's taboo name, they were to be changed.

entries.zh: 改西京明堂殿為宣德殿，中書政事堂為政事廳，堂後官房頭為錄事，余為主事。
entries.en: The Hall of Bright Virtue in the Western Capital was renamed the Hall of Proclaimed Virtue; the Secretariat's Hall of Governance became the Governance Office; the chief clerks in the rear offices were renamed recorders, and the rest were renamed section chiefs.
entries.literal: The Hall of Bright Virtue in the Western Capital was renamed the Hall of Proclaimed Virtue; the Secretariat's Hall of Governance was renamed the Governance Office; the chief clerks in the rear offices of the hall were renamed recorders, and the rest were renamed section chiefs.

entries.zh: 〈（《東都事略·陶穀傳》：穀本姓唐，避晉祖諱改姓陶，蓋當時避諱之體如此。）〉
entries.en: (The Biography of Tao Gu in Outline History of the Eastern Capital records that Gu's original surname was Tang and that he changed it to Tao to avoid the taboo of the Jin founder. Such was the practice of taboo avoidance at the time.)〉
entries.literal: (Biography of Tao Gu in Outline History of the Eastern Capital: Gu's original surname was Tang; to avoid the taboo of the Jin founder he changed his surname to Tao. Such was the practice of taboo avoidance at the time.)〉

entries.zh: 己丑，大行皇帝大祥，帝釋缞服，百官衣縿。
entries.en: On jichou, the day of the great mourning rites for the late emperor, the Emperor removed his coarse hemp mourning garments and the officials wore fine hemp mourning dress.
entries.literal: On jichou, the day of the great mourning rites for the late emperor, the Emperor removed his hemp mourning garments and the hundred officials wore garments of fine hemp.

entries.zh: 辛卯，帝除禫服，百官吉服。
entries.en: On xinmao, the Emperor ended his mourning and the officials resumed formal dress.
entries.literal: On xinmao, the Emperor removed his final mourning garments and the hundred officials wore auspicious dress.

entries.zh: 壬辰，太皇太后劉氏崩，高祖之庶母也。
entries.en: On renchen, Grand Empress Dowager Liu died; she was Gaozu's stepmother.
entries.literal: On renchen, Grand Empress Dowager Liu died; she was Gaozu's secondary mother.

entries.zh: 遺詔服紀園陵毋用後禮，皇帝不得廢軍國機務。
entries.en: Her dying edict stipulated that mourning and the imperial tomb were not to follow the rites due an empress dowager, and that the emperor was not to neglect state and military affairs.
entries.literal: Her final edict stated that the mourning period and the imperial tomb were not to follow the rites due a empress dowager, and that the emperor was not to neglect state and military affairs.

entries.zh: 既而禮官奏：「準令式，為祖父母齊缞周；
entries.en: The ritual officials then memorialized: "According to statute, mourning for grandparents requires the five-part hemp garment worn for one year;
entries.literal: Thereupon the ritual officials memorialized: "According to the statutes and regulations, mourning for grandparents is the five-part hemp garment worn for one year;

entries.zh: 又準喪葬令，皇帝本服周者，三哭而止。
entries.en: and according to the mourning and burial statutes, when the emperor's proper mourning period is one year, he should stop after three sessions of wailing.
entries.literal: and according further to the mourning and burial statutes, when the emperor's proper mourning period is one year, he should stop after three sessions of wailing.

entries.zh: 請準後唐同光三年，皇太妃北京薨，莊宗於洛京西內發哀素服，不視事三日。」
entries.en: We ask that the precedent of Later Tang Tongguang 3 be followed, when the Imperial Consort died at the Northern Capital and Emperor Zhuangzong expressed mourning in plain dress in the western inner palace at Luoyang and did not conduct affairs for three days."
entries.literal: We request that the precedent of Later Tang Tongguang 3 be followed, when the Imperial Consort died at the Northern Capital and Emperor Zhuangzong expressed mourning in plain dress within the western inner palace at Luoyang and did not conduct affairs for three days."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The request was granted.
entries.literal: Permission was granted.

entries.zh: 仍遣國子祭酒兼戶部侍郎田敏奏告高祖靈座。
entries.en: Tian Min, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and concurrent Vice Minister of Revenue, was also sent to report the matter at Gaozu's spirit seat.
entries.literal: Tian Min, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and concurrent Vice Minister of Revenue, was also dispatched to report the matter at Gaozu's spirit seat.

entries.zh: 癸巳，右諫議大夫鄭受益、中書舍人楊昭儉並停見任，以請假在外，不赴國喪故也。
entries.en: On guisi, Right Remonstrance Counselor Zheng Shouyi and Secretariat Drafting Secretary Yang Zhaojian were both dismissed from their current posts for having taken leave and failing to attend the state mourning.
entries.literal: On guisi, Right Remonstrance Counselor Zheng Shouyi and Secretariat Drafting Secretary Yang Zhaojian were both removed from their current posts because they had taken leave and were away and did not attend the state mourning.

entries.zh: 丁酉，宰臣馮道等率文武百僚詣崇德殿門拜表，請禦正殿，凡三上表，允之。
entries.en: On dingyou, Chief Councilor Feng Dao and the civil and military officials submitted memorials three times at the Gate of the Hall of Honored Virtue requesting that the Emperor hold court in the main hall, and permission was granted.
entries.literal: On dingyou, Chief Councilor Feng Dao and others led the civil and military officials to the Gate of the Hall of Honored Virtue to submit memorials requesting that the Emperor hold court in the main hall; they submitted memorials three times, and permission was granted.

entries.zh: 安州奏，水平地深七尺。
entries.en: An Prefecture reported that floodwaters stood seven feet deep on level ground.
entries.literal: An Prefecture reported that floodwaters stood seven feet deep on level ground.

entries.zh: 庚子，帝御正殿，宣制：「大赦天下，諸道州府各色罪犯，除十惡五逆、殺人強盜、官典犯贓、合作毒藥、屠牛鑄錢外，其餘罪犯，咸赦除之。
entries.en: On gengzi, the Emperor held court in the main hall and proclaimed: "A general amnesty is granted throughout the realm. For all crimes in the various circuits, prefectures, and districts, except the ten abominations, the five rebellions, murder, robbery, official corruption, compounding poison, slaughtering cattle, and counterfeiting coin, all other offenses are pardoned.
entries.literal: On gengzi, the Emperor held court in the main hall and proclaimed: "A general amnesty is granted throughout the realm. For all categories of crime in the various circuits, prefectures, and districts, except the ten abominations, the five rebellions, murder, robbery, official corruption, compounding poison, slaughtering cattle, and counterfeiting coin, all other crimes are pardoned and remitted.

entries.zh: 襄州安從進如能果決輸誠，並從釋放。
entries.en: If An Congjin of Xiang Prefecture can decisively submit his loyalty, he too shall be released.
entries.literal: If An Congjin of Xiang Prefecture can decisively submit his loyalty, he too shall be released.

entries.zh: 其中外臣僚將校，並與加恩。
entries.en: Civil and military officials and officers throughout the realm shall likewise receive added favor.
entries.literal: All civil and military officials and officers, both within and outside the capital, shall likewise receive added favor.

entries.zh: 天下有蟲蝗處，並與除放租稅。」
entries.en: Wherever locusts appear in the realm, rent and tax shall be remitted."
entries.literal: Wherever locusts appear in the realm, rent and tax shall be remitted."

entries.zh: 辛丑，恒州順國軍節度使杜威、河東節度使劉知遠，並加檢校太師，仍增爵邑。
entries.en: On xinchou, Du Wei, military governor of the Shunguo Army at Heng Prefecture, and Liu Zhiyuan, military governor of Hedong, were both further granted Honorary Grand Preceptor and given increased noble rank and fief.
entries.literal: On xinchou, Du Wei, military governor of the Shunguo Army at Heng Prefecture, and Liu Zhiyuan, military governor of Hedong, were both further granted Honorary Grand Preceptor and given increased noble rank and fief.

entries.zh: 青州平盧軍節度使楊光遠加守太師。
entries.en: Yang Guangyuan, military governor of the Pinglu Army at Qing Prefecture, was granted Acting Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Yang Guangyuan, military governor of the Pinglu Army at Qing Prefecture, was granted Acting Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 癸卯，鄆州天平軍節度使兼侍衛馬步都虞候景延廣加特進、同中書門下平章事，充侍衛親軍都指揮使。
entries.en: On guimao, Jing Yanguang, military governor of the Tianping Army at Yan Prefecture and concurrent chief adjutant of the palace guard cavalry and infantry, was granted Special Advancement and made joint director of the Secretariat-Chancellery with concurrent status as Grand Councilor, and appointed overall commander of the palace guard armies.
entries.literal: On guimao, Jing Yanguang, military governor of the Tianping Army at Yan Prefecture and concurrent chief adjutant of the palace guard cavalry and infantry, was granted Special Advancement and made a co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery with concurrent Grand Councilor status, and appointed overall commander of the palace guard armies.

entries.zh: 滑州義成軍節度使兼侍衛馬軍都指揮使李守貞，相州彰德軍節度使、侍衛步軍都指揮使郭謹，並加檢校太傅，仍增爵邑。
entries.en: Li Shouzhen, military governor of the Yicheng Army at Hua Prefecture and concurrent commander of the palace guard cavalry, and Guo Jin, military governor of the Zhangde Army at Xiang Prefecture and commander of the palace guard infantry, were both further granted Honorary Grand Preceptor and given increased noble rank and fief.
entries.literal: Li Shouzhen, military governor of the Yicheng Army at Hua Prefecture and concurrent commander of the palace guard cavalry, and Guo Jin, military governor of the Zhangde Army at Xiang Prefecture and commander of the palace guard infantry, were both further granted Honorary Grand Preceptor and given increased noble rank and fief.

entries.zh: 宰臣馮道等上表，請依舊置樞密使，略曰：「竊以樞密使創自前朝，置諸近侍，其來已久，所便尤多。
entries.en: Chief Councilor Feng Dao and others submitted a memorial asking that the office of Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs be restored as before, stating in summary: "The Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs was created in the previous dynasty and placed among the close attendants; the office has long existed and has been especially useful.
entries.literal: Chief Councilor Feng Dao and others submitted a memorial requesting that the office of Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs be restored as before, stating in summary: "We venture to observe that the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs was created in the previous dynasty and placed among the close attendants; the office has long existed and has been especially convenient.

entries.zh: 頃歲樞密使劉處讓偶屬家艱，爰拘喪制，既從罷免，暫議改更，不曾顯降敕文，永停使額。
entries.en: In recent years Commissioner Liu Churang happened to suffer a family bereavement and was bound by mourning regulations; once he was removed from office, a temporary change was discussed, but no explicit edict was ever issued permanently abolishing the commissionership.
entries.literal: In recent years Commissioner Liu Churang happened to suffer a family bereavement and was bound by mourning regulations; once he was removed from office, a temporary change was discussed, but no explicit edict was ever issued permanently abolishing the commissionership.

entries.zh: 所願各歸職分，豈敢茍避繁難。
entries.en: What we wish is that each return to his proper duties; we would not shirk difficult and burdensome affairs.
entries.literal: What we wish is that each return to his proper duties; how could we shirk difficult and burdensome affairs?

entries.zh: 伏請依舊置樞密使。」
entries.en: We humbly ask that the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs be restored as before."
entries.literal: We humbly request that the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs be restored as before."

entries.zh: 初，高祖事後唐明宗，睹樞密使安重誨秉政擅權，賞罰由己，常惡之，及登極，故斷意廢罷，一委中書。
entries.en: Earlier, when Gaozu served Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang, he saw Commissioner An Chonghui wield government power and monopolize authority, with rewards and punishments decided at his own discretion, and he often detested this. When he ascended the throne, he therefore resolved to abolish the office and entrusted everything to the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu served Later Tang's Emperor Mingzong, he saw Commissioner An Chonghui wield government power and monopolize authority, with rewards and punishments decided by himself, and he often detested this. When he ascended the throne, he therefore resolved to abolish the office and entrusted everything to the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 至是馮道等厭其事繁，故復請置之，庶分其權。
entries.en: At this time Feng Dao and the others wearied of the burden of affairs and therefore again asked that the office be established, hoping thereby to divide the authority.
entries.literal: At this time Feng Dao and the others wearied of the burden of affairs and therefore again requested that the office be established, hoping thereby to divide the authority.

entries.zh: 表凡三上，不允。
entries.en: The memorial was submitted three times, but permission was not granted.
entries.literal: The memorial was submitted three times, but permission was not granted.

entries.zh: 乙巳，徐州節度使李從溫、宋州節度使安彥威並加兼中書令，西都留守、充襄州行營都部署高行周加兼侍中，鳳翔節度使李從嚴加守太保。
entries.en: On yisi, Li Congwen, military governor of Xu Prefecture, and An Yanwei, military governor of Song Prefecture, were both additionally made concurrent Grand Councilor; Gao Xingzhou, regent of the Western Capital and overall commander of the Xiang Prefecture field headquarters, was additionally made concurrent Palace Attendant; and Li Congyan, military governor of Fengxiang, was granted Acting Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: On yisi, Li Congwen, military governor of Xu Prefecture, and An Yanwei, military governor of Song Prefecture, were both additionally made concurrent Grand Councilor; Gao Xingzhou, regent of the Western Capital and overall commander of the Xiang Prefecture field headquarters, was additionally made concurrent Palace Attendant; and Li Congyan, military governor of Fengxiang, was granted Acting Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 遣中使就中書賜宰臣馮道生辰器幣，道以幼屬亂離，早喪父母，不記生日，堅辭不受。
entries.en: An imperial envoy was sent to the Secretariat to grant Chief Councilor Feng Dao birthday gifts and ceremonial objects. Dao, having from youth lived through turmoil and separation and having lost his parents early, did not remember his birthday and firmly declined to accept.
entries.literal: An imperial envoy was dispatched to the Secretariat to grant Chief Councilor Feng Dao birthday gifts and ceremonial objects. Dao, having from youth lived through turmoil and separation and having lost his parents early, did not remember his birthday and firmly declined to accept.

entries.zh: 丙午，以給事中羅周嶽為左散騎常侍，以右諫議大夫符蒙為給事中，以秘書少監兼廣晉少尹邊蔚為右散騎常侍，以廣晉少尹張煦為右諫議大夫，以廣晉府判官、光祿少卿邊光範為右諫議大夫。
entries.en: On bingwu, Supervising Secretary Luo Zhouyue was made Left Regular Attendant; Right Remonstrance Counselor Fu Meng was made Supervising Secretary; Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Vice Governor of Guangjin Bian Wei was made Right Regular Attendant; Vice Governor of Guangjin Zhang Xu was made Right Remonstrance Counselor; and Guangjin Prefecture judge and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Bian Guangfan was made Right Remonstrance Counselor.
entries.literal: On bingwu, Supervising Secretary Luo Zhouyue was made Left Regular Attendant; Right Remonstrance Counselor Fu Meng was made Supervising Secretary; Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Vice Governor of Guangjin Bian Wei was made Right Regular Attendant; Vice Governor of Guangjin Zhang Xu was made Right Remonstrance Counselor; and Guangjin Prefecture judge and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Bian Guangfan was made Right Remonstrance Counselor.

entries.zh: 丁未，荊南節度使、南平王高從誨加兼尚書令，湖南節度使、楚王馬希範加守太傅。
entries.en: On dingwei, Gao Conghui, military governor of Jingnan and King of Nanping, was additionally made concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs; Ma Xifan, military governor of Hunan and King of Chu, was granted Acting Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: On dingwei, Gao Conghui, military governor of Jingnan and King of Nanping, was additionally made concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs; Ma Xifan, military governor of Hunan and King of Chu, was granted Acting Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 自是藩侯郡守，皆第加官封，示溥恩也。
entries.en: From this time onward, feudal lords and prefectural governors were all granted added titles and enfeoffments in turn, displaying broad favor.
entries.literal: From this time onward, feudal lords and prefectural governors were all granted added titles and enfeoffments in succession, displaying broad favor.

entries.zh: 是月，州郡十七蝗。
entries.en: That month, locusts struck seventeen prefectures and districts.
entries.literal: That month, locusts struck seventeen prefectures and districts.

entries.zh: 是歲六月十三日乙丑，高祖崩，承遺制命柩前即皇帝位。
entries.en: On the thirteenth day of the sixth month of that year, the day yichou, Gaozu died; by his dying edict the new emperor took the throne before the coffin.
entries.literal: On the thirteenth day of the sixth month of that year, on the day yichou, Gaozu died; by his final edict the Emperor ascended the throne before the coffin.

entries.zh: 帝在并州未著人望，及保釐浚郊，大有寬裕之稱。
entries.en: He had not yet won wide esteem while at Bingzhou, but once he took charge of governance and performed the suburban rites, he won a reputation for generous rule.
entries.literal: While the Emperor was in Bingzhou he had not yet won men's esteem; but once he preserved order, improved governance, and purified the suburbs, he won great repute for magnanimity.

entries.zh: 從幸鄴都，是歲遇旱，高祖遣祈雨於白龍潭，有白龍見於潭心，是夜澍雨尺餘，人皆異之，至是果登大位焉。
entries.en: When he accompanied Gaozu to the capital at Ye, drought struck that year. Gaozu sent men to pray for rain at White Dragon Pool; a white dragon appeared in the heart of the pool, and that night more than a foot of rain fell. People took it for a marvel, and now he had indeed ascended the throne.
entries.literal: When he accompanied Gaozu to the capital at Ye, that year there was drought. Gaozu sent men to pray for rain at White Dragon Pool; a white dragon appeared in the center of the pool, and that night soaking rain fell to a depth of more than a foot. All regarded it as extraordinary, and at this time he indeed ascended the great throne.

entries.zh: 丁卯，賜侍衛諸軍將校錢一百貫下至五貫，以初即位示賫也。
entries.en: On dingmao, officers of the palace guard armies were granted sums from one hundred strings of cash down to five strings, as gifts to mark his accession.
entries.literal: On dingmao, the officers of the various palace guard armies were granted money ranging downward from one hundred strings to five strings, as a gift to mark his first accession to the throne.

entries.zh: 戊辰，宰臣馮道等率百僚請聽政，凡三上表，允之。
entries.en: On wuchen, Chief Councilor Feng Dao and the other officials petitioned three times that he begin governing, and permission was granted.
entries.literal: On wuchen, the chief councilor Feng Dao and others led the hundred officials in requesting that he assume governance; they submitted memorials three times, and permission was granted.

entries.zh: 庚午，始聽政於崇德殿門偏廊，分命廷臣以嗣位奏告天地宗廟社稷。
entries.en: On gengwu, he first began to govern from the side corridor of the Gate of the Hall of Honored Virtue and dispatched court ministers to announce his succession at the altars of Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain.
entries.literal: On gengwu, he first assumed governance in the side corridor of the Gate of the Hall of Honored Virtue and separately ordered court ministers to report his succession to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain.

entries.zh: 遣右驍衛將軍石德超等押先皇御馬二匹，往相州西山撲祭，用北俗禮也。
entries.en: He sent Right Brave Guard General Shi Dechao and others to escort two of the late emperor's imperial horses to the western hills of Xiang Prefecture for the puji sacrifice, following northern custom.
entries.literal: He dispatched Right Brave Guard General Shi Dechao and others to escort two of the late emperor's imperial horses to the western hills of Xiang Prefecture for the puji sacrifice, using northern custom.

entries.zh: 丙子，以司徒、兼侍中馮道為大行皇帝山陵使，門下侍郎竇貞固副之，太常卿崔棁為禮儀使，戶部侍郎呂琦為鹵簿使，御史中丞王易簡為儀仗使。
entries.en: On bingzi, Minister of Education and concurrent Palace Attendant Feng Dao was appointed commissioner for the late emperor's mausoleum, with Vice Director of the Chancellery Dou Zhengu as deputy; Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cui Zhuo was made ritual commissioner; Vice Minister of Revenue Lü Qi was made procession commissioner; and Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yijian was made ceremonial guard commissioner.
entries.literal: On bingzi, Minister of Education and concurrent Palace Attendant Feng Dao was made commissioner for the late emperor's mausoleum, with Vice Director of the Chancellery Dou Zhengu as his deputy; Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cui Zhuo was made ritual commissioner; Vice Minister of Revenue Lü Qi was made procession commissioner; and Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yijian was made ceremonial guard commissioner.

entries.zh: 〈（徐無黨《五代史記註》云：舊史實錄無橋道頓遞使，疑不置或闕書，漢高祖亦然。）〉
entries.en: (Xu Wudang's Commentary on the Historical Records of the Five Dynasties notes that the Old History and the Veritable Records make no mention of a commissioner for bridges, roads, and relay stations; the office may never have been established, or the entry may be missing. The same holds for Han Gaozu.)〉
entries.literal: (Xu Wudang's Commentary on the Historical Records of the Five Dynasties states: The Old History and the Veritable Records contain no commissioner for bridge, road, and relay stations; it is suspected that the office was not established or that the record is missing. The same is true for Han Gaozu.)〉

entries.zh: 己卯，遣判四方館事朱崇節、右金吾大將軍梁言持國信物使於契丹。
entries.en: On jimao, he sent Zhu Chongjie, overseer of the Office for Receiving Envoys from the Four Directions, and Senior General of the Right Golden Bear Guard Liang Yan as envoys bearing state gifts to the Khitan.
entries.literal: On jimao, he dispatched Zhu Chongjie, who handled affairs of the Office for Receiving Envoys from the Four Directions, and Senior General of the Right Golden Bear Guard Liang Yan as envoys bearing state gifts to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 是時，河南、河北、關西並奏蝗害稼。
entries.en: At this time, reports came in from Henan, Hebei, and Guanxi that locusts were ravaging the crops.
entries.literal: At this time, Henan, Hebei, and Guanxi all reported locusts damaging the crops.

entries.zh: 三月己卯朔，以中書令、監修國史趙瑩為晉昌軍節度使，以晉昌軍節度使桑維翰為侍中、監修國史。
entries.en: On the first day of the third month, jimao, Zhao Ying, Grand Councilor and supervisor of the compilation of the national history, was made military governor of the Jinchang Army; and Sang Weihan, military governor of the Jinchang Army, was made Palace Attendant and supervisor of the compilation of the national history.
entries.literal: On the first day of the third month, the day jimao, Zhao Ying, Grand Councilor and supervisor of the compilation of the national history, was made military governor of the Jinchang Army; and Sang Weihan, military governor of the Jinchang Army, was made Palace Attendant and supervisor of the compilation of the national history.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》作晉昌節度使、兼侍中桑維翰為侍中。
entries.en: (Comprehensive Mirror records: Sang Weihan, military governor of Jinchang and concurrent Palace Attendant, was made Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror records: Sang Weihan, military governor of Jinchang and concurrent Palace Attendant, was made Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 胡三省註云：桑維翰始居藩鎮而兼侍中，今入朝，正為門下省長官。）〉
entries.en: Hu Sanxing's commentary states: Sang Weihan had first held a military governorship while concurrently serving as Palace Attendant; now that he entered court, he properly became chief of the Chancellery.)〉
entries.literal: Hu Sanxing's commentary states: Sang Weihan had first held a military governorship while concurrently serving as Palace Attendant; now that he entered court, he properly became chief of the Chancellery.)〉

entries.zh: 辛巳，以左散騎常侍盧重為秘書監，以東京副留守羅周嶽為右散騎常侍。
entries.en: On xinsi, Left Regular Attendant Lu Zhong was made Director of the Secretariat; and Luo Zhouyue, deputy regent of the Eastern Capital, was made Right Regular Attendant.
entries.literal: On xinsi, Left Regular Attendant Lu Zhong was made Director of the Secretariat; and Luo Zhouyue, deputy regent of the Eastern Capital, was made Right Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 癸未，青州節度使、東平王楊光遠進封壽王，北京留守劉知遠、恒州節度使杜威並加兼中書令。
entries.en: On guiwei, Yang Guangyuan, military governor of Qing Prefecture and King of Dongping, was promoted to King of Shou; Liu Zhiyuan, regent of the Northern Capital, and Du Wei, military governor of Heng Prefecture, were both additionally made concurrent Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: On guiwei, Yang Guangyuan, military governor of Qing Prefecture and King of Dongping, was advanced to King of Shou; Liu Zhiyuan, regent of the Northern Capital, and Du Wei, military governor of Heng Prefecture, were both additionally made concurrent Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 乙酉，以鄜州節度使符彥卿為河陽節度使，以權鄴都留守、前開封尹張從恩為鄴都留守、廣晉尹，以右羽林統軍丁審琪為鄜州節度使。
entries.en: On yiyou, Fu Yanqing, military governor of Fu Prefecture, was made military governor of Heyang; Zhang Cong'en, acting regent of the capital at Ye and former governor of Kaifeng, was made regent of the capital at Ye and governor of Guangjin; and Ding Shenqi, commander of the Right Forest of Feathers Army, was made military governor of Fu Prefecture.
entries.literal: On yiyou, Fu Yanqing, military governor of Fu Prefecture, was made military governor of Heyang; Zhang Cong'en, acting regent of the capital at Ye and former governor of Kaifeng, was made regent of the capital at Ye and governor of Guangjin; and Ding Shenqi, commander of the Right Forest of Feathers Army, was made military governor of Fu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 丁亥，天策上將軍、湖南節度使、楚王馬希範加守尚書令、兼中書令。
entries.en: On dinghai, Ma Xifan, Grand General of the Heavenly Strategy, military governor of Hunan, and King of Chu, was granted Acting Director of the Department of State Affairs and made concurrent Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: On dinghai, Ma Xifan, Grand General of the Heavenly Strategy, military governor of Hunan, and King of Chu, was granted Acting Director of the Department of State Affairs and made concurrent Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 己丑，桂州節度使馬希杲依前檢校太尉、兼侍中，兼知朗州軍州事；
entries.en: On jichou, Ma Xigao, military governor of Gui Prefecture, retained his former Honorary Grand Commander and concurrent Palace Attendant and was additionally given charge of military and civil affairs at Lang Prefecture;
entries.literal: On jichou, Ma Xigao, military governor of Gui Prefecture, retained his former Honorary Grand Commander and concurrent Palace Attendant and was additionally given charge of military and civil affairs at Lang Prefecture;

entries.zh: 朗州武平軍節度使馬希萼加檢校太尉，進封爵邑。
entries.en: Ma Xie, military governor of the Wuping Army at Lang Prefecture, was further granted Honorary Grand Commander and given increased noble rank and fief.
entries.literal: Ma Xie, military governor of the Wuping Army at Lang Prefecture, was further granted Honorary Grand Commander and given increased noble rank and fief.

entries.zh: 以武平軍節度副使、岳州團練使馬希瞻為檢校太尉，領盧州昭信軍節度使；
entries.en: Ma Xizhan, deputy military governor of the Wuping Army and training commissioner of Yue Prefecture, was made Honorary Grand Commander and appointed military governor of the Zhaoxin Army at Lu Prefecture;
entries.literal: Ma Xizhan, deputy military governor of the Wuping Army and training commissioner of Yue Prefecture, was made Honorary Grand Commander and appointed military governor of the Zhaoxin Army at Lu Prefecture;

entries.zh: 以武安軍節度副使、永州團練使馬希廣為檢校太尉，領洪州鎮南軍節度使；
entries.en: Ma Xiguang, deputy military governor of the Wu'an Army and training commissioner of Yong Prefecture, was made Honorary Grand Commander and appointed military governor of the Zhennan Army at Hong Prefecture;
entries.literal: Ma Xiguang, deputy military governor of the Wu'an Army and training commissioner of Yong Prefecture, was made Honorary Grand Commander and appointed military governor of the Zhennan Army at Hong Prefecture;

entries.zh: 皆楚王馬希範之弟也。
entries.en: All were younger brothers of Ma Xifan, King of Chu.
entries.literal: All were younger brothers of Ma Xifan, King of Chu.

entries.zh: 庚寅，以宣徽北院使李承福為右武衛大將軍，充宣徽南院使；
entries.en: On gengyin, Li Chengfu, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made Senior General of the Right Martial Guard and appointed commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat;
entries.literal: On gengyin, Li Chengfu, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made Senior General of the Right Martial Guard and appointed commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat;

entries.zh: 以前鄭州防禦使劉繼勛為左千牛衛大將軍，充宣徽北院使。
entries.en: Liu Jixun, former defense commissioner of Zheng Prefecture, was made Senior General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard and appointed commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: Liu Jixun, former defense commissioner of Zheng Prefecture, was made Senior General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard and appointed commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 國子祭酒兼戶部侍郎田敏以印本《五經》書上進，賜帛五十段。
entries.en: Tian Min, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and concurrent Vice Minister of Revenue, presented printed copies of the Five Classics and was granted fifty bolts of silk.
entries.literal: Tian Min, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and concurrent Vice Minister of Revenue, presented printed copies of the Five Classics and was granted fifty bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 甲午，有白烏棲作坊桐樹，作坊使周務掠捕而進之。
entries.en: On jiawu, a white crow perched in a paulownia tree at the workshops; Workshop Commissioner Zhou Wu captured it and presented it.
entries.literal: On jiawu, a white crow perched in a paulownia tree at the workshops; Workshop Commissioner Zhou Wu captured it and presented it.

entries.zh: 辛丑，引進使、太府卿孟承誨使契丹。
entries.en: On xinchou, Meng Chenghui, reception commissioner and Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, was sent as envoy to the Khitan.
entries.literal: On xinchou, Meng Chenghui, reception commissioner and Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, was sent as envoy to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 詔京百司攝官親公事及五年，與授初官。
entries.en: An edict ordered that acting officials in the capital bureaus who had personally handled official business for five years should be granted initial regular appointments.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that acting officials in the capital bureaus who had personally handled official business for five years should be granted initial regular appointments.

entries.zh: 癸卯，以左諫議大夫司徒詡為給事中，左司郎中王仁裕為右諫議大夫，前鴻臚卿王均為少府監。
entries.en: On guimao, Left Remonstrance Counselor Situ Xu was made Supervising Secretary; Left Bureau Director Wang Renyu was made Right Remonstrance Counselor; and Wang Jun, former Director of the Court of the Imperial Banquets, was made Director of the Court of the Imperial Manufactories.
entries.literal: On guimao, Left Remonstrance Counselor Situ Xu was made Supervising Secretary; Left Bureau Director Wang Renyu was made Right Remonstrance Counselor; and Wang Jun, former Director of the Court of the Imperial Banquets, was made Director of the Court of the Imperial Manufactories.

entries.zh: 五月己卯，追封皇故長姊為吳國長公主。
entries.en: In the fifth month, on jimao, the late Emperor's elder sister was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of Wu.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on jimao, the late Emperor's elder sister was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of Wu.

entries.zh: 癸未，皇侄女永福縣主薨，輟朝三日，追封平昌郡主。
entries.en: On guiwei, the Emperor's niece, Lady of Yongfu County, died; court was suspended for three days, and she was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Pingchang Commandery.
entries.literal: On guiwei, the Emperor's niece, Lady of Yongfu County, died; court was suspended for three days, and she was posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Pingchang Commandery.

entries.zh: 丁亥，皇第二叔祖贈太師萬友追封秦王；
entries.en: On dinghai, Wan You, the Emperor's second grand-uncle, posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Qin;
entries.literal: On dinghai, Wan You, the Emperor's second grand-uncle, posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Qin;

entries.zh: 皇第三叔祖贈太尉萬銓贈太師，追封趙王。
entries.en: Wan Quan, the Emperor's third grand-uncle, posthumously granted Grand Commander, was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as King of Zhao.
entries.literal: Wan Quan, the Emperor's third grand-uncle, posthumously granted Grand Commander, was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as King of Zhao.

entries.zh: 皇伯贈太傅敬儒贈太師，追封宋王；
entries.en: Jingru, the Emperor's paternal uncle, posthumously granted Grand Tutor, was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as King of Song;
entries.literal: Jingru, the Emperor's paternal uncle, posthumously granted Grand Tutor, was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as King of Song;

entries.zh: 皇叔贈太尉福王德贈太師，追封如故；
entries.en: Fude, the Emperor's paternal uncle, posthumously granted Grand Commander and King of Fu, was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as before;
entries.literal: Fude, the Emperor's paternal uncle, posthumously granted Grand Commander and King of Fu, was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as before;

entries.zh: 皇叔贈太傅暉贈太師，追封韓王；
entries.en: Hui, the Emperor's paternal uncle, posthumously granted Grand Tutor, was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as King of Han;
entries.literal: Hui, the Emperor's paternal uncle, posthumously granted Grand Tutor, was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as King of Han;

entries.zh: 皇叔贈太尉通王殷、皇叔贈太尉廣王威、皇兄贈太傅郯王重裔並贈太師，追封如故。
entries.en: Yin, the Emperor's paternal uncle, posthumously granted Grand Commander and King of Tong; Wei, the Emperor's paternal uncle, posthumously granted Grand Commander and King of Guang; and Chongyi, the Emperor's elder brother, posthumously granted Grand Tutor and King of Tan, were all posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as before.
entries.literal: Yin, the Emperor's paternal uncle, posthumously granted Grand Commander and King of Tong; Wei, the Emperor's paternal uncle, posthumously granted Grand Commander and King of Guang; and Chongyi, the Emperor's elder brother, posthumously granted Grand Tutor and King of Tan, were all posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as before.

entries.zh: 皇兄贈太師沂王重信追封楚王；
entries.en: Chongxin, the Emperor's elder brother, posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and King of Yi, was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Chu;
entries.literal: Chongxin, the Emperor's elder brother, posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and King of Yi, was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Chu;

entries.zh: 皇兄贈太傅虢王重乂、皇兄贈太師夔王重進、皇弟贈太尉陳王重杲等並贈太師，追封如故。
entries.en: Chongyi, the Emperor's elder brother, posthumously granted Grand Tutor and King of Guo; Chongjin, the Emperor's elder brother, posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and King of Kui; Chonggao, the Emperor's younger brother, posthumously granted Grand Commander and King of Chen, and others were all posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as before.
entries.literal: Chongyi, the Emperor's elder brother, posthumously granted Grand Tutor and King of Guo; Chongjin, the Emperor's elder brother, posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and King of Kui; Chonggao, the Emperor's younger brother, posthumously granted Grand Commander and King of Chen, and others were all posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as before.

entries.zh: 仍令所司擇日冊命。
entries.en: The responsible offices were further ordered to choose a day for the investiture ceremony.
entries.literal: The responsible offices were further ordered to choose a day for the investiture ceremony.

entries.zh: 辛卯，以御史中丞王易簡為尚書左丞，以禮部侍郎張允為御史中丞，以中書舍人吳承範為禮部侍郎，以吏部侍郎王延為尚書右丞，以尚書右丞王松為吏部侍郎，以兵部侍郎張昭遠為吏部侍郎，以戶部侍郎呂琦為兵部侍郎，以刑部侍郎韋勛為戶部侍郎，以工部侍郎李詳為刑部侍郎。
entries.en: On xinmao, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yijian was made Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun was made Vice Censor-in-Chief; Secretariat Drafting Secretary Wu Chengfang was made Vice Minister of Rites; Vice Minister of Personnel Wang Yan was made Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Wang Song was made Vice Minister of Personnel; Vice Minister of War Zhang Zhaoyuan was made Vice Minister of Personnel; Vice Minister of Revenue Lü Qi was made Vice Minister of War; Vice Minister of Punishments Wei Xun was made Vice Minister of Revenue; and Vice Minister of Works Li Xiang was made Vice Minister of Punishments.
entries.literal: On xinmao, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yijian was made Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun was made Vice Censor-in-Chief; Secretariat Drafting Secretary Wu Chengfang was made Vice Minister of Rites; Vice Minister of Personnel Wang Yan was made Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Wang Song was made Vice Minister of Personnel; Vice Minister of War Zhang Zhaoyuan was made Vice Minister of Personnel; Vice Minister of Revenue Lü Qi was made Vice Minister of War; Vice Minister of Punishments Wei Xun was made Vice Minister of Revenue; and Vice Minister of Works Li Xiang was made Vice Minister of Punishments.

entries.zh: 癸巳，命宰臣等分詣寺觀禱雨。
entries.en: On guisi, the chief councilors and others were ordered to go separately to temples and monasteries to pray for rain.
entries.literal: On guisi, the chief councilors and others were ordered to go separately to temples and monasteries to pray for rain.

entries.zh: 己亥，飛蝗自北翳天而南。
entries.en: On jihai, flying locusts came from the north, darkening the sky as they moved south.
entries.literal: On jihai, flying locusts came from the north, darkening the sky as they moved south.

entries.zh: 太子賓客李棁卒。
entries.en: Li Rong, Mentor of the Heir Apparent, died.
entries.literal: Li Rong, Mentor of the Heir Apparent, died.

entries.zh: 甲辰，詔：「諸道州府見禁罪人，除十惡五逆、行劫殺人、偽行印信、合造毒藥、官典犯贓各減一等外，餘並放。」
entries.en: On jiachen, an edict stated: "For prisoners currently held in the various circuits, prefectures, and districts, except the ten abominations, the five rebellions, robbery and murder, forging seals and credentials, compounding poison, and official corruption, for which sentences are each reduced by one grade, all the rest are to be released."
entries.literal: On jiachen, an edict stated: "For prisoners currently held in the various circuits, prefectures, and districts, except the ten abominations, the five rebellions, robbery and murder, forging seals and credentials, compounding poison, and official corruption, for which sentences are each reduced by one grade, all the rest are to be released."

entries.zh: 是時所在旱蝗，故有是詔。
entries.en: At this time drought and locusts prevailed everywhere, and therefore this edict was issued.
entries.literal: At this time drought and locusts prevailed everywhere, and therefore this edict was issued.

entries.zh: 乙巳，幸相國寺祈雨。
entries.en: On yisi, the Emperor visited Xiangguo Temple to pray for rain.
entries.literal: On yisi, the Emperor visited Xiangguo Temple to pray for rain.

entries.zh: 少帝，名重貴，高祖之從子也。
entries.en: Emperor Shao, whose personal name was Chonggui, was a paternal nephew of Gaozu.
entries.literal: The Young Emperor, named Chonggui, was a paternal nephew of Gaozu.

entries.zh: 考諱敬儒，母安氏，以唐天祐十一年六月二十七日生帝於太原汾陽裏。
entries.en: His father's posthumous name was Jingru, and his mother was Lady An. He was born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month of Tianyou 11 (914) at Fenyang Lane in Taiyuan.
entries.literal: His deceased father was taboo-named Jingru; his mother was the An clan. On the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month of the eleventh year of Tang Tianyou, the Emperor was born at Fenyang Lane in Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 敬儒嘗為後唐莊宗騎將，早薨，高祖以帝為子。
entries.en: Jingru had once served as a cavalry general under Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang and died young, whereupon Gaozu adopted the boy as his son.
entries.literal: Jingru had once served as a cavalry general under Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong and died young; Gaozu took the Emperor as his own son.

entries.zh: 帝少而謹厚，高祖愛之。
entries.en: From youth he was careful and honest, and Gaozu doted on him.
entries.literal: The Emperor from youth was careful and honest; Gaozu loved him.

entries.zh: 洎歷方鎮，嘗遣從行，委以庶事，但性好馳射，有祖禰之風。
entries.en: When Gaozu later held various military commands, he often had the boy travel with him and entrusted him with routine affairs, but the youth loved horsemanship and archery and bore something of his forefathers' martial spirit.
entries.literal: When he subsequently served in various defense commands, he was at times sent to accompany Gaozu on his travels and entrusted with miscellaneous affairs; yet his nature favored galloping and archery, and he had the manner of his ancestors.

entries.zh: 高祖鎮太原，命瑯琊王震以《禮記》教帝，不能領其大義，謂震曰：「非我家事業也。」
entries.en: While Gaozu was stationed at Taiyuan, he had Wang Zhen, Prince of Langya, instruct him in the Book of Rites, but he could not grasp its larger meaning and told Zhen, "This is not the calling of our house."
entries.literal: When Gaozu held Taiyuan, he ordered Wang Zhen, Prince of Langya, to teach the Emperor the Book of Rites. The Emperor could not grasp its main principles and said to Zhen: "This is not the business of our house."

entries.zh: 及高祖受圍於太原，親冒矢石，數獻可於左右，高祖愈重焉。
entries.en: When Gaozu was besieged at Taiyuan, the future emperor personally braved arrows and stones and repeatedly offered sound counsel at Gaozu's side; Gaozu came to value him all the more.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was besieged at Taiyuan, the Emperor personally braved arrows and stones, repeatedly offering feasible plans to those at Gaozu's side, and Gaozu valued him all the more.

entries.zh: 高祖受契丹冊，將入洛，欲留一子撫晉陽，先謀於戎王，戎王曰：「使諸子盡出，吾當擇之。」
entries.en: After Gaozu accepted enthronement from the Khitan and was preparing to enter Luoyang, he wished to leave one son to govern Jinyang and first sought the Prince of Rong's counsel. The Prince of Rong said, "Send all your sons out; I shall choose among them."
entries.literal: When Gaozu received investiture from the Khitan and was about to enter Luoyang, he wished to leave one son to govern Jinyang and first consulted the Prince of Rong, who said: "Have all the sons come out; I shall choose among them."

entries.zh: 乃於行中指帝謂高祖曰：「此眼大者可矣。」
entries.en: He then pointed the Emperor out among those present and told Gaozu, "This one with the large eyes will do."
entries.literal: He then pointed out the Emperor among those in attendance and said to Gaozu: "This one with the large eyes will do."

entries.zh: 遂以帝為北京留守，授金紫光祿大夫、檢校司徒，行太原尹，知河東管內節度觀察事。
entries.en: He was accordingly made regent of the Northern Capital and granted the posts of Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon and Honorary Minister of Education, with acting appointment as governor of Taiyuan and charge of the Hedong military governorship and inspection circuit.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Emperor was made regent of the Northern Capital and granted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon and Honorary Minister of Education, acting as governor of Taiyuan and overseeing the military governorship and inspection affairs within Hedong.

entries.zh: 天福二年九月，征赴闕，授光祿大夫、檢校太保、右金吾衛上將軍。
entries.en: In the ninth month of Tianfu 2 (937), he was summoned to court and granted the titles of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Honorary Grand Tutor, and Senior General of the Right Golden Bear Guard.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of Tianfu 2, he was summoned to court and granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Honorary Grand Tutor, and Senior General of the Right Golden Bear Guard.

entries.zh: 三年十二月，授開封尹，加檢校太傅，封鄭王，增食邑三千戶。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of Tianfu 3, he was appointed governor of Kaifeng, further granted Honorary Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng, and given an additional fief of three thousand households.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of year 3, he was appointed governor of Kaifeng, further granted Honorary Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng, and given an increased fief of three thousand households.

entries.zh: 俄加檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: Before long he was further granted Honorary Grand Commander and made joint director of the Secretariat-Chancellery with concurrent status as Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he was further granted Honorary Grand Commander and made a co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery with concurrent Grand Councilor status.

entries.zh: 六年，高祖幸鄴，改廣晉尹，進封齊王。
entries.en: In Tianfu 6, when Gaozu visited Ye, his title was changed to governor of Guangjin and he was promoted to Prince of Qi.
entries.literal: In year 6, when Gaozu visited Ye, he was changed to governor of Guangjin and advanced to Prince of Qi.

entries.zh: 〈（以下疑脫「七年正月，加兼侍中」八字。）〉
entries.en: (The text below is suspected of omitting eight characters: "In the first month of Tianfu 7, he was additionally made concurrent Palace Attendant.")〉
entries.literal: (It is suspected that the following eight characters are missing: "In the first month of year 7, he was additionally made concurrent Palace Attendant.")〉

entries.zh: 開運元年春正月甲戌朔，是夕陣雲掩北斗之魁星。
entries.en: On the first day jiaxu of the first month of spring in Kaiyun 1, battle clouds that night veiled the leader star of the Northern Dipper.
entries.literal: In spring, the first month, first day jiaxu of the first year of Kaiyun, that night battle clouds covered the leader star of the Northern Dipper.

entries.zh: 乙亥，滄、恒、貝、鄴馳告，契丹前鋒趙延壽、趙延昭引五萬騎入寇，將及甘陵，青州楊光遠召之也。
entries.en: On yihai Cang, Heng, Bei, and Ye sent urgent word that Khitan vanguard Zhao Yanshou and Zhao Yanzhao were leading 50,000 horsemen in invasion toward Ganling—summoned by Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou.
entries.literal: On yihai, Cang, Heng, Bei, and Ye sent urgent reports that the Khitan vanguard Zhao Yanshou and Zhao Yanzhao led fifty thousand horsemen in invasion, about to reach Ganling; Qingzhou's Yang Guangyuan had summoned them.

entries.zh: 己卯，契丹陷貝州，知州吳巒死之。
entries.en: On jimao the Khitan captured Bei; acting prefect Wu Luan was killed.
entries.literal: On jimao, the Khitan took Beizhou; Acting Prefect Wu Luan died in the fighting.

entries.zh: 庚辰，以宋州節度使高行周為北面行營都部署，以河陽節度使符彥卿為馬軍左廂排陣使，以右神武統軍皇甫遇為馬軍右廂排陣使，以陜州節度使王周為步軍左廂排陣使，以左羽林統軍潘環為步軍右廂排陣使。
entries.en: On gengchen Song commissioner Gao Xingzhou was made overall commander of the northern campaign; Heyang commissioner Fu Yanqing was left-wing horse array marshal; Right Divine Martial commander Huangfu Yu was right-wing horse marshal; Shaan commissioner Wang Zhou was left-wing foot marshal; and Left Feathered Forest commander Pan Huan was right-wing foot marshal.
entries.literal: On gengchen, Gao Xingzhou, military commissioner of Songzhou, was made overall commander of the Northern Campaign Headquarters; Fu Yanqing, military commissioner of Heyang, was made array marshal of the left wing of the horse army; Huangfu Yu, commander of the Right Divine Martial Guard, was made array marshal of the right wing of the horse army; Wang Zhou, military commissioner of Shaanzhou, was made array marshal of the left wing of the foot army; Pan Huan, commander of the Left Feathered Forest Guard, was made array marshal of the right wing of the foot army.

entries.zh: 太原奏，契丹入雁門，圍忻、代二州。
entries.en: Taiyuan reported that the Khitan had entered Yanmen Pass and besieged Xin and Dai.
entries.literal: Taiyuan memorialized that the Khitan had entered Yanmen and besieged Xinzhou and Daizhou.

entries.zh: 恒、滄、邢三州上言，契丹大至。
entries.en: Heng, Cang, and Xing reported that the Khitan had arrived in force.
entries.literal: Heng, Cang, and Xing submitted memorials that the Khitan had arrived in force.

entries.zh: 是歲，天下餓死者數十萬人，詔逐處長吏瘞之。
entries.en: That year hundreds of thousands starved to death empire-wide, and an edict ordered local officials to bury them.
entries.literal: That year, those who starved to death under Heaven numbered in the hundreds of thousands; an edict ordered local chief officials everywhere to bury them.

entries.zh: 壬午，詔取此月十三日車駕北征，以前邠州節度使李周為權東京留守。
entries.en: On renwu an edict set the thirteenth of the month for the emperor's northern expedition and made former Bin commissioner Li Zhou acting garrison commander of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: On renwu, an edict set the thirteenth day of this month for the imperial carriage's northern expedition; the former military commissioner of Binzhou, Li Zhou, was made acting garrison commander of the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 乙酉，車駕發東京。
entries.en: On yiyou the emperor departed the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: On yiyou, the imperial carriage departed the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 丁亥，敵騎至黎陽。
entries.en: On dinghai enemy cavalry reached Liyang.
entries.literal: On dinghai, enemy horsemen reached Liyang.

entries.zh: 以侍衛馬軍都指揮使李守貞為前軍都虞候。
entries.en: Palace Guards cavalry commander Li Shouzhen was made vanguard chief adjutant.
entries.literal: Li Shouzhen, commander of the Palace Guards horse army, was made chief adjutant of the vanguard.

entries.zh: 河北危蹙，諸州求救者人使相望。
entries.en: Hebei was in dire straits, and envoys begging rescue came one after another from the prefectures.
entries.literal: Hebei was in peril and pressed; among the prefectures those sending envoys to beg rescue were unceasing.

entries.zh: 戊子，車駕至澶州。
entries.en: On wuzi the emperor reached Chanzhou.
entries.literal: On wuzi, the imperial carriage reached Chanzhou.

entries.zh: 以貝州節度使王令溫為鄧州節度使，時令溫弟令崇自契丹至，訴以舉族陷於甘陵，故有是命。
entries.en: Bei commissioner Wang Lingwen was transferred to Deng because his brother Lingchong had come from the Khitan and reported that their whole clan was trapped at Ganling.
entries.literal: Wang Lingwen, military commissioner of Beizhou, was made military commissioner of Dengzhou; at the time Lingwen's younger brother Lingchong had come from the Khitan and complained that the whole clan was trapped at Ganling, hence this appointment.

entries.zh: 辛卯，鄴都留守張從恩遣人夜縋城間行，奏契丹主以鐵騎三四萬建牙帳於元城，以趙延壽為魏博節度使，改封魏王，延壽日率騎軍摩壘而退。
entries.en: On xinmao Yedu garrison commander Zhang Congen sent men down the wall by night with a secret report: the Khitan ruler had pitched camp at Yuancheng with 30,000–40,000 armored horsemen, made Zhao Yanshou Weibo commissioner and Prince of Wei, and Yanshou daily led cavalry to skirmish at the walls before withdrawing.
entries.literal: On xinmao, Zhang Congen, garrison commander of Yedu, sent men at night to lower themselves by rope from the wall and travel by secret paths, memorializing that the Khitan ruler had set up his command tent at Yuancheng with thirty or forty thousand iron cavalry, made Zhao Yanshou military commissioner of Weibo and changed his enfeoffment to Prince of Wei; Yanshou daily led cavalry to press the ramparts and then withdraw.

entries.zh: 甲午，以北京留守劉知遠為幽州道行營招討使，以恒州節度使杜威副之，定州節度使馬全節為都虞候，其職員將校委招討使便宜署置。
entries.en: On jiawu Northern Capital garrison commander Liu Zhiyuan was made pacification commissioner for the Youzhou campaign, with Heng commissioner Du Wei as deputy and Ding commissioner Ma Quanjie as chief adjutant; staff and generals were left to the commissioner's discretion.
entries.literal: On jiawu, Liu Zhiyuan, garrison commander of the Northern Capital, was made pacification commissioner of the Youzhou circuit campaign headquarters; Du Wei, military commissioner of Hengzhou, was his deputy; Ma Quanjie, military commissioner of Dingzhou, was chief adjutant; staff officers and generals were entrusted to the pacification commissioner to appoint at discretion.

entries.zh: 乙未，大霧中有白虹相偶，占者曰：「斯為海淫，其下必將有戰。」
entries.en: On yiwei a white rainbow appeared paired in heavy fog; diviners said, "This is a sign of maritime excess—battle will surely follow below."
entries.literal: On yiwei, in great fog a white rainbow paired with another; diviners said: "This is sea excess; below there will surely be battle."

entries.zh: 詔率天下公私之馬以資騎軍。
entries.en: An edict ordered all public and private horses empire-wide levied for the cavalry.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the levying of all public and private horses under Heaven to supply the cavalry.

entries.zh: 丙申，契丹攻黎陽。
entries.en: On bingshen the Khitan attacked Liyang.
entries.literal: On bingshen, the Khitan attacked Liyang.

entries.zh: 遣右武衛上將軍張彥澤等率勁騎三千以禦之。
entries.en: Right Martial Guard senior general Zhang Yanzhe and others were sent with 3,000 elite cavalry to resist them.
entries.literal: Zhang Yanzhe, senior general of the Right Martial Guard, and others were sent to lead three thousand crack cavalry to resist them.

entries.zh: 己亥，遣譯詔官孟守忠致書於契丹主，求修舊好。
entries.en: On jihai translation officer Meng Shouzhong was sent with a letter to the Khitan ruler seeking to restore the old alliance.
entries.literal: On jihai, the translation edict officer Meng Shouzhong was sent with a letter to the Khitan ruler seeking to restore the former good relations.

entries.zh: 守忠自敵帳回，契丹主復書曰：「已成之勢，不可改也。」
entries.en: When Shouzhong returned from the enemy camp, the Khitan ruler replied, "What is already settled cannot be changed."
entries.literal: Shouzhong returned from the enemy camp; the Khitan ruler replied in a letter: "The situation already formed cannot be changed."

entries.zh: 辛丑，太原奏，與契丹戰於秀谷，斬首三千級，生擒五百人，獲敵將一十七人，賊軍散入鴉鳴谷，已進軍追襲。
entries.en: On xinchou Taiyuan reported fighting the Khitan at Xiugu, beheading 3,000, capturing 500 alive and 17 enemy generals; the enemy scattered into Crow Cry Valley and pursuit was under way.
entries.literal: On xinchou, Taiyuan memorialized that it had fought the Khitan at Xiugu, beheaded three thousand, captured five hundred alive, took seventeen enemy generals; the rebel army scattered into Crow Cry Valley and the army had already advanced in pursuit.

entries.zh: 三月癸酉朔，契丹主領兵十餘萬來戰。
entries.en: On the first day guiyou of the third month the Khitan ruler brought more than a hundred thousand men to fight.
entries.literal: On the first day guiyou of the third month, the Khitan ruler led more than a hundred thousand troops to give battle.

entries.zh: 時契丹偽棄元城寨已旬日矣，伏精騎於頓丘故城，以待王師。
entries.en: The Khitan had pretended to quit Yuancheng camp for ten days, concealing crack cavalry in old Dunqiu to ambush the imperial army.
entries.literal: At the time the Khitan had feigned abandoning Yuancheng stockade for ten days already, hiding elite cavalry in the old city of Dunqiu to await the imperial army.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：鄴都留守張從恩屢奏敵已遁去，大軍欲進追之，會霖雨而止。）〉
entries.en: (Zizhi Tongjian: Yedu garrison commander Zhang Congen kept reporting the enemy gone and urging pursuit, but the advance halted in torrential rain.)
entries.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: Zhang Congen, garrison commander of Yedu, repeatedly memorialized that the enemy had fled; the main army wished to advance in pursuit but stopped when heavy rain set in.)

entries.zh: 設伏累日，人馬饑頓，趙延壽謀曰：「晉軍悉在河上，畏我鋒銳，不敢前進，不如徑造城下，四面而進，攻奪其橋梁，天下定矣。」
entries.en: After days in ambush men and horses were starving; Zhao Yanshou urged, "Jin forces are pinned on the river, afraid of our edge—strike straight for the city, attack from four sides, seize the bridges, and the realm is ours."
entries.literal: Having lain in ambush for days, men and horses were famished and exhausted; Zhao Yanshou plotted, saying: "The Jin army is all on the river; they fear our sharp edge and dare not advance; it would be better to go straight to the walls below the city, advance from all four sides, seize their bridges, and All under Heaven will be settled."

entries.zh: 契丹主然之。
entries.en: The Khitan ruler approved the plan.
entries.literal: The Khitan ruler agreed.

entries.zh: 是日，前軍高行周在戚城之南，賊將趙延壽、趙延昭以數萬騎出王師之西，契丹主自擁精騎出王師之東，兩軍接戰，交相勝負。
entries.en: That day Gao Xingzhou's vanguard stood south of Qicheng while Zhao Yanshou and Zhao Yanzhao led tens of thousands of riders against the imperial west flank and the Khitan ruler himself struck from the east; the battle seesawed.
entries.literal: That day the advance force under Gao Xingzhou was south of Qicheng; the bandit generals Zhao Yanshou and Zhao Yanzhao led tens of thousands of horsemen out to the west of the imperial army; the Khitan ruler himself with elite cavalry came out to the east; the two armies joined battle with alternating victories and defeats.

entries.zh: 至晡時，契丹主以勁兵中央出而來，帝御親軍列為後陣，東西濟河，為偃月之勢，旗幟鮮盛，士馬嚴整。
entries.en: By late afternoon the Khitan ruler committed his center; the emperor took personal command of the palace guard in reserve while forces east and west crossed the river in a crescent formation, banners bright and ranks tight.
entries.literal: By late afternoon the Khitan ruler brought strong troops out from the center; the emperor personally commanded the imperial guard arrayed as the rear formation; east and west they crossed the river in a crescent moon disposition; banners were brilliant and troops and horses were strict and orderly.

entries.zh: 契丹主望之，謂左右曰：「楊光遠言晉朝兵馬半已餓死，今日觀之，何其壯耶！」
entries.en: The Khitan ruler looked on and told his attendants, "Yang Guangyuan claimed half the Jin army had starved—yet see how strong they look today!"
entries.literal: The Khitan ruler gazed at them and said to those beside him: "Yang Guangyuan said half the Jin court's troops and horses had already starved to death — viewing them today, how strong they are!"

entries.zh: 敵騎往來馳突，王師植立不動，萬弩齊彀，飛矢蔽空，賊軍稍卻。
entries.en: Enemy cavalry wheeled and charged while the imperial line held firm; a volley of ten thousand crossbows darkened the sky and the Khitan line began to give ground.
entries.literal: Enemy horsemen galloped back and forth in raids; the imperial army stood planted unmoving; ten thousand crossbows released together; flying arrows covered the sky; the bandit army gradually fell back.

entries.zh: 會有亡者告契丹主曰：「南軍東面人少，沿河城柵不固，可以攻之。」
entries.en: A defector then told the Khitan ruler, "The southern line is weak on the east; the river forts are shaky—attack there."
entries.literal: Then a deserter told the Khitan ruler: "The southern army's eastern flank is thinly manned; the riverside fortifications are not solid — they can be attacked."

entries.zh: 契丹乃率精騎以攻東邊，王師敗走，敵騎追之。
entries.en: The Khitan sent elite cavalry against the east; the imperial army broke and fled with enemy riders in pursuit.
entries.literal: The Khitan then led elite cavalry to attack the eastern flank; the imperial army was defeated and fled; enemy horsemen pursued.

entries.zh: 時有夾馬軍士千餘人在堤間治水寨，旗幟之末出於堰埭，敵望見之，以為伏兵所起，追騎乃止。
entries.en: More than a thousand grooms were building waterworks on the dike; banner tips showed above the dam, and the pursuers mistook them for a fresh ambush and stopped.
entries.literal: At the time more than a thousand horse-grooming soldiers were building water fortifications on the embankment; the tips of their banners showed above the weir; the enemy saw them and thought ambush troops were rising; the pursuit halted.

entries.zh: 久之復戰，王師又退，李守超以數百騎短兵直起擊之，敵稍卻。
entries.en: Fighting resumed and the imperial line fell back again until Li Shouchao led several hundred horsemen in a close-quarters charge that pushed the enemy back.
entries.literal: After a long while they fought again; the imperial army retreated again; Li Shouchao with several hundred horsemen closed with short weapons and charged straight at them; the enemy fell back slightly.

entries.zh: 戰場之地，人馬死者無算，斷箭殘鏃，橫厚數寸。
entries.en: Men and horses lay dead beyond count; broken shafts and spent arrowheads carpeted the ground inches deep.
entries.literal: On the battlefield the dead among men and horses were beyond counting; broken arrows and spent bolt-heads lay piled several inches thick.

entries.zh: 遇夜，賊擊鉦抽軍而退，夜行三十里而舍焉。
entries.en: At nightfall the enemy beat gongs and pulled back, marching thirty li before making camp.
entries.literal: When night came the bandits sounded gongs and withdrew the army; they marched thirty li by night and encamped.

entries.zh: 護聖指揮使協霸
entries.en: Guardian Sage commander Xie Ba
entries.literal: Guardian Sage Guard commander Xie Ba—

entries.zh: 〈（協霸」二字上疑有脫文。）〉
entries.en: (Editorial note: text appears missing before the name Xie Ba.)
entries.literal: (Text is suspected lost above the two characters "Xie Ba".)

entries.zh: 亡入賊中，夷其族。
entries.en: He defected to the enemy and his entire clan was wiped out.
entries.literal: He fled into the enemy ranks and his clan was exterminated.

entries.zh: 護聖第二軍都指揮使安重懷、指揮使烏韓七、監軍何彥超等臨陣畏怯，手失兵仗，悉斬之。
entries.en: An Chonghuai, overall commander of the Second Army of the Guardian Sage Guard; commander Wu Hanqi; army supervisor He Yanchao and others panicked in battle and dropped their weapons—all were executed.
entries.literal: An Chonghuai, overall commander of the second army of the Guardian Sage Guard; commander Wu Hanqi; military inspector He Yanchao and others showed cowardice facing the battle line and let their weapons slip from their hands; all were beheaded.

entries.zh: 乙亥，契丹主帳內小校竊其主所乘馬來奔，云：「契丹已傳木書，收軍北去。」
entries.en: On yihai a Khitan tent guard stole his lord's horse and defected, reporting, "The Khitan have passed wooden orders to withdraw north."
entries.literal: On yihai, a petty officer within the Khitan ruler's tent stole his master's riding horse and came over in surrender, saying: "The Khitan have issued wooden tablets ordering the army to withdraw north."

entries.zh: 〈（《契丹國志》云：景延廣疑有詐，閉壁不敢追。
entries.en: (Khitan State Chronicle: Jing Yanguang feared a trap and shut the walls, refusing to pursue.
entries.literal: (Khitan State Chronicle: Jing Yanguang suspected a ruse and closed the gates, daring not pursue.

entries.zh: 遼帝北歸，所過焚掠民物殆盡。）〉
entries.en: The Liao emperor marched north, burning and looting everything in his path until little remained.)
entries.literal: The Liao emperor returned north; wherever he passed he burned and plundered the people's goods nearly to exhaustion.)

entries.zh: 齊州奏，青州賊軍寇明水鎮。
entries.en: Qi reported Qingzhou rebel troops raiding Mingshui town.
entries.literal: Qizhou memorialized that bandit troops from Qingzhou raided Mingshui town.

entries.zh: 壬午，禮部尚書盧詹卒，贈太子太保。
entries.en: On renwu Minister of Rites Lu Zhan died and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: On renwu, Lu Zhan, Minister of Rites, died and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 甲申，契丹車帳已過貝州，以趙延昭守貝州。
entries.en: On jiashen the Khitan royal train had passed Beizhou, leaving Zhao Yanzhao to hold the city.
entries.literal: On jiashen, the Khitan royal camp had already passed Beizhou; Zhao Yanzhao was left to hold Beizhou.

entries.zh: 〈（《遼史》：三月壬午，留趙延昭守貝州，徙所俘戶於內地。）〉
entries.en: (History of Liao: Third month, renwu—Zhao Yanzhao was left at Beizhou and captives were moved inland.)
entries.literal: (History of Liao: In the third month on renwu, Zhao Yanzhao was left to hold Beizhou and captured households were relocated to the interior.)

entries.zh: 辛卯，定州馬全節攻泰州，拔之，俘其兵士二千人，雜畜戎仗稱是。
entries.en: On xinmao Dingzhou's Ma Quanjie took Taizhou, capturing two thousand soldiers plus livestock and arms in proportion.
entries.literal: On xinmao, Ma Quanjie of Dingzhou attacked Taizhou and took it; two thousand of its soldiers were captured, along with miscellaneous livestock and weapons in comparable numbers.

entries.zh: 癸巳，北京留守、兼中書令劉知遠封太原王，餘如故。
entries.en: On guisi Northern Capital garrison commander Liu Zhiyuan, also Grand Councilor, was enfeoffed King of Taiyuan; other titles unchanged.
entries.literal: On guisi, Liu Zhiyuan, garrison commander of the Northern Capital and concurrent Grand Councilor, was enfeoffed as King of Taiyuan; the rest unchanged.

entries.zh: 是日，詔天下抽點鄉兵，凡七戶出一士，六戶資之，仍自具兵仗，以「武定」為軍號。
entries.en: That day an edict levied militia empire-wide: one man from every seven households, supported by six others, armed at their own expense, under the designation "Wuding".
entries.literal: That day an edict ordered conscription of militia throughout the realm: one soldier from every seven households, with six households supplying him; they were still to provide their own weapons; "Wuding" was the army designation.

entries.zh: 太常丞王緒棄市。
entries.en: Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices Wang Xu was executed publicly.
entries.literal: Wang Xu, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was executed in the marketplace.

entries.zh: 緒家於青州，常致書於楊光遠，緒有妾之兄慊緒不為赒給，遂告與光遠連謀，密書述朝廷機事，遂收捕斬之。
