entries.en: Xu, whose family was in Qingzhou, had been writing to Yang Guangyuan; his concubine's brother, angry at being denied aid, accused him of plotting with Guangyuan and leaking court secrets; Xu was arrested and beheaded.
entries.literal: Xu's family was in Qingzhou; he regularly sent letters to Yang Guangyuan; an elder brother of Xu's concubine resented that Xu did not provide relief and reported that he was in collusion with Guangyuan, with secret letters describing court secrets; he was arrested and beheaded.

entries.zh: 五月壬申朔，太原劉知遠奏，邊境未寧，軍用甚廣，所封王爵，乞未行冊命。
entries.en: On the first day renshen of the fifth month Taiyuan's Liu Zhiyuan asked to defer his royal investiture, citing an unsettled frontier and crushing military costs.
entries.literal: On the first day renshen of the fifth month, Liu Zhiyuan of Taiyuan memorialized that the border was not yet settled, military expenses were very heavy, and regarding the enfeoffment as king he begged that the investiture ceremony not yet be carried out.

entries.zh: 戊寅，遣侍衛親軍都虞候李守貞率步騎二萬，討楊光遠於青州。
entries.en: On wuyin Palace Guard deputy Li Shouzhen was dispatched with twenty thousand foot and horse to crush Yang Guangyuan at Qingzhou.
entries.literal: On wuyin, Li Shouzhen, deputy commander of the Palace Guard, was sent to lead twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to campaign against Yang Guangyuan at Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 丁亥，以鄴都留守張從恩為貝州行營都部署，
entries.en: On dinghai Yedu garrison commander Zhang Congen was named overall Beizhou camp commander,
entries.literal: On dinghai, Zhang Congen, garrison commander of Yedu, was made overall camp commander at Beizhou,

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：張從恩上言：「趙延昭雖據貝州，麾下將士久客思歸，宜速進軍攻擊。」
entries.en: (Zizhi Tongjian: Zhang Congen argued, "Zhao Yanzhao holds Beizhou, but his troops are homesick after long service abroad—we should attack at once."
entries.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: Zhang Congen submitted: "Although Zhao Yanzhao holds Beizhou, the officers and soldiers under him, long absent as guests, yearn to return home; we ought to advance quickly and attack."

entries.zh: 詔以從恩為貝州行營都部署。）〉
entries.en: An edict appointed Congen Beizhou camp commander.)
entries.literal: An edict made Congen overall camp commander at Beizhou.)

entries.zh: 以滑州節度使皇甫遇為行營都虞候，以左神武統軍潘環掌騎兵，右神武統軍張彥澤掌步兵。
entries.en: Hua commissioner Huangfu Yu became deputy camp commander; Left Divine Martial commander Pan Huan took the cavalry; Right Divine Martial commander Zhang Yanzhe took the infantry.
entries.literal: Huangfu Yu, military commissioner of Hua Prefecture, was made deputy camp commander; Pan Huan, commander of the Left Divine Martial Guard, was put in charge of cavalry; Zhang Yanzhe, commander of the Right Divine Martial Guard, was put in charge of infantry.

entries.zh: 辛卯，張從恩奏，貝州賊將趙延昭縱火大掠，棄城而遁。
entries.en: On xinmao Zhang Congen reported Zhao Yanzhao burning and looting Beizhou before abandoning the city.
entries.literal: On xinmao, Zhang Congen memorialized that the Beizhou bandit general Zhao Yanzhao set fires and plundered heavily, then abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：延昭屯於瀛、莫，阻水自固。）〉
entries.en: (Zizhi Tongjian: Yanzhao withdrew to Ying and Mo and fortified himself behind the water.)
entries.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: Yanzhao encamped at Ying and Mo, blocking the water to hold firm.)

entries.zh: 以李守貞為青州行營都部署，以河陽節度使符彥卿副之。
entries.en: Li Shouzhen was made Qingzhou theater commander with Heyang commissioner Fu Yanqing as his deputy.
entries.literal: Li Shouzhen was made overall Qingzhou camp commander; Fu Yanqing, military commissioner of Heyang, was made his deputy.

entries.zh: 戊戌，以鄧州節度使何建為貝州永清軍節度使。
entries.en: On wuxu Deng commissioner He Jian was made Yongqing Army commissioner at Beizhou.
entries.literal: On wuxu, He Jian, military commissioner of Dengzhou, was made military commissioner of Yongqing Army at Beizhou.

entries.zh: 是月，澤潞上言，餓死者凡五千餘人。
entries.en: That month Ze and Lu reported more than five thousand famine deaths.
entries.literal: That month Ze and Lu reported that over five thousand had died of starvation.

entries.zh: 六月辛丑朔，王師拔淄州，斬楊光遠偽署刺史劉翰。
entries.en: On the first day xinchou of the sixth month the imperial army captured Zizhou and executed Liu Han, Yang Guangyuan's puppet prefect.
entries.literal: On the first day xinchou of the sixth month, the imperial army took Zizhou and beheaded Liu Han, Yang Guangyuan's appointee as prefect.

entries.zh: 癸卯，以太尉、兼侍中馮道為檢校太師、兼侍中，充同州節度使。
entries.en: On guimao Grand Marshal Feng Dao was made honorary Grand Preceptor and Tong commissioner, retaining his Palace Secretary title.
entries.literal: On guimao, Feng Dao, Grand Marshal and concurrent Palace Secretary, was made honorary Grand Preceptor and concurrent Palace Secretary, serving as military commissioner of Tongzhou.

entries.zh: 丙午，詔復置樞密院。
entries.en: On bingwu an edict re-established the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: On bingwu, an edict restored the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 丁未，以侍中桑維翰為中書令，充樞密使。
entries.en: On dingwei Palace Secretary Sang Weihan became Grand Councilor and Commissioner of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: On dingwei, Sang Weihan, Palace Secretary, was made Grand Councilor and served as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 權開封府尹李周卒，輟朝，贈太師。
entries.en: Acting Kaifeng mayor Li Zhou died; court was suspended and he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Li Zhou, acting mayor of Kaifeng, died; court audience was suspended; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 辛亥，以邢州節度使安叔千為晉州節度使，加同平章事；
entries.en: On xinhai Xing commissioner An Shuqian was made Jin commissioner and appointed Grand Councilor;
entries.literal: On xinhai, An Shuqian, military commissioner of Xingzhou, was made military commissioner of Jinzhou and given the additional title of Grand Councilor;

entries.zh: 以晉州節度使宋彥筠為陜州節度使；
entries.en: Jin commissioner Song Yanyun was transferred to Shaan;
entries.literal: Song Yanyun, military commissioner of Jinzhou, was made military commissioner of Shaanzhou;

entries.zh: 以吏部郎中李穀充樞密直學士。
entries.en: Personnel bureau director Li Gu was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: Li Gu, bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel, was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 丙辰，滑州河決，漂註曹、單、濮、鄆等州之境，環梁山合於汶、濟。
entries.en: On bingchen the Yellow River broke through at Hua, inundating Cao, Dan, Pu, Yun, and neighboring prefectures; the flood wrapped around Mount Liang and merged with the Wen and Ji.
entries.literal: On bingchen, the Yellow River burst its banks at Huazhou, flooding and pouring into the territories of Cao, Dan, Pu, Yun, and other prefectures, circling Mount Liang and joining the Wen and Ji rivers.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·楊昭儉傳》：河決數郡，大發丁夫，以本部帥董其役，既而塞之。
entries.en: (History of Song, Biography of Yang Zhaojian: The breach affected several commanderies; mass corvée was levied under the local commander, and the breach was eventually closed.
entries.literal: (History of Song, Biography of Yang Zhaojian: The river burst in several commanderies; corvée laborers were levied on a great scale; the commander of the local circuit supervised the work, and afterward it was sealed.

entries.zh: 晉少主喜，詔立碑紀其事。
entries.en: Emperor Shao of Jin was pleased and ordered a monument erected to commemorate it.
entries.literal: The Young Lord of Jin was pleased and ordered a stele erected to record the affair.

entries.zh: 昭儉表諫曰：「陛下刻石紀功，不若降哀痛之詔；
entries.en: Zhaojian remonstrated: "Your Majesty, a stone monument to merit is less fitting than an edict of mourning and repentance;
entries.literal: Zhaojian memorialized in remonstrance, saying: "Your Majesty, to carve stone recording merit is not as good as issuing an edict of mourning and pain;

entries.zh: 摛翰頌美，不若頒罪己之文。」
entries.en: literary praise is less fitting than proclaiming a confession of your own errors."
entries.literal: to wield the brush in praise is not as good as promulgating a text confessing fault."

entries.zh: 言甚切至，少主嗟賞之，卒罷其事。）〉
entries.en: His words were forceful; Emperor Shao admired them and dropped the plan.)
entries.literal: His words were very earnest; the Young Lord sighed in admiration and finally abandoned the matter.)

entries.zh: 戊午，升府州為團練使額。
entries.en: On wuwu Fu Prefecture was raised to regimental commissioner rank.
entries.literal: On wuwu, Fuzhou was elevated to regimental commissioner status.

entries.zh: 庚申，襄州獻白鵲。
entries.en: On gengshen Xiang Prefecture presented a white magpie.
entries.literal: On gengshen, Xiangzhou presented a white magpie.

entries.zh: 甲子，復置翰林學士。
entries.en: On jiazi the office of Hanlin academician was restored.
entries.literal: On jiazi, Hanlin academicians were reinstated.

entries.zh: 乙丑，宰臣等三上表請聽樂，詔允之。
entries.en: On yichou the chief ministers submitted three memorials asking to resume court music; the emperor approved.
entries.literal: On yichou, the chief ministers and others thrice submitted memorials requesting permission to hear music; an edict granted it.

entries.zh: 戊辰，以門下侍郎王松為左丞；
entries.en: On wuchen Chancellery Vice Director Wang Song was made Left Vice Director;
entries.literal: On wuchen, Wang Song, Vice Director of the Chancellery, was made Left Vice Director;

entries.zh: 以右丞王易簡為吏部侍郎；
entries.en: Right Vice Director Wang Yijian was made Vice Minister of Personnel;
entries.literal: Wang Yijian, Right Vice Director, was made Vice Minister of Personnel;

entries.zh: 以右散騎常侍蕭願為秘書監；
entries.en: Right Cavalry Attendant Xiao Yuan was made Director of the Imperial Library;
entries.literal: Xiao Yuan, Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, was made Director of the Imperial Library;

entries.zh: 以右諫議大夫王仁裕為給事中；
entries.en: Right Remonstrance Grandee Wang Renyu was made Supervising Secretary;
entries.literal: Wang Renyu, Right Remonstrance Grandee, was made Supervising Secretary;

entries.zh: 以給事中李式為左散騎常侍；
entries.en: Supervising Secretary Li Shi was made Left Cavalry Attendant;
entries.literal: Li Shi, Supervising Secretary, was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry;

entries.zh: 以金部郎中、知制誥徐臺符為翰林學士；
entries.en: Revenue bureau director and edict drafter Xu Taifu was made Hanlin academician;
entries.literal: Xu Taifu, bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue and drafter of edicts, was made Hanlin academician;

entries.zh: 以禮部郎中李浣本官知制誥，充翰林學士；
entries.en: Rites bureau director Li Huan kept his rank, was made edict drafter, and appointed Hanlin academician;
entries.literal: Li Huan, bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, retained his office and served as drafter of edicts, filling the post of Hanlin academician;

entries.zh: 以刑部郎中劉溫叟改都官郎中，充翰林學士；
entries.en: Justice bureau director Liu Wensou was moved to director of the Bureau of Capital Officials and made Hanlin academician;
entries.literal: Liu Wensou, bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, was transferred to bureau director of the Capital Officials and filled the post of Hanlin academician;

entries.zh: 以主客員外郎範質充翰林學士；
entries.en: Receptions assistant director Fan Zhi was made Hanlin academician;
entries.literal: Fan Zhi, assistant director in the Ministry of Receptions, was made Hanlin academician;

entries.zh: 御史張宜改倉部員外郎、知制誥。
entries.en: Censor Zhang Yi was made assistant director in the Ministry of Granaries and edict drafter.
entries.literal: Censor Zhang Yi was transferred to assistant director in the Ministry of Granaries and made drafter of edicts.

entries.zh: 庚午，以前晉州節度使周密為左龍武統軍，以同州節度使李懷忠為左羽林統軍。
entries.en: On gengwu former Jin commissioner Zhou Mi was appointed commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard, and Tong commissioner Li Huaizhong commander of the Left Feathered Forest Guard.
entries.literal: On gengwu, Zhou Mi, former military commissioner of Jinzhou, was made commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard; Li Huaizhong, military commissioner of Tongzhou, was made commander of the Left Feathered Forest Guard.

entries.zh: 天福八年秋七月丁丑朔，京師雨水深三尺。
entries.en: On the first day dingchou of the seventh month of autumn in Tianfu 8, floodwaters in the capital stood three feet deep.
entries.literal: In the autumn, seventh month, first day dingchou of the eighth year of Tianfu, in the capital rain water stood three chi deep.

entries.zh: 辛巳，許州節度使李從溫來朝，進封楚國公。
entries.en: On xinsi Li Congwen, military commissioner of Xuzhou, arrived at court and was promoted to Duke of Chu.
entries.literal: On xinsi, Li Congwen, military commissioner of Xuzhou, came to court and was advanced to Duke of Chu.

entries.zh: 壬午，以前河陽節度使皇甫遇為右龍武統軍。
entries.en: On renwu former Heyang commissioner Huangfu Yu was appointed commander of the Right Dragon Martial Guard.
entries.literal: On renwu, the former military commissioner of Heyang, Huangfu Yu, was made commander of the Right Dragon Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 丁亥，以宣徽南院使李承福為同州節度使。
entries.en: On dinghai Li Chengfu of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat was made military commissioner of Tongzhou.
entries.literal: On dinghai, Li Chengfu, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made military commissioner of Tongzhou.

entries.zh: 癸巳，改陜州甘棠驛為通津驛，避廟諱也。
entries.en: On guisi the Sweet Pear post station in Shaan Prefecture was renamed Crossing Ford post station to avoid the imperial temple taboo.
entries.literal: On guisi, the Sweet Pear post station in Shaanzhou was renamed Crossing Ford post station, to avoid the temple taboo.

entries.zh: 甲午，正衙命冊皇太后，以宰臣李崧充使，右散騎常侍李慎儀為副。
entries.en: On jiawu the court ordered the investiture of the empress dowager, with Chief Minister Li Song as chief envoy and Right Cavalry Attendant Li Shenyi as deputy.
entries.literal: On jiawu, at the main court an order was issued to invest the empress dowager; the chief minister Li Song served as chief envoy and the Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Li Shenyi as deputy.

entries.zh: 丁酉，幸南莊，召從駕臣僚習射，路左農人各賜布衫麻屨。
entries.en: On dingyou the emperor visited South Manor and called the officials in his train to practice archery; farmers along the road were each given cloth jackets and hemp sandals.
entries.literal: On dingyou, the emperor visited South Manor, summoned the officials in his train to practice archery, and each farmer along the road was given a cloth jacket and hemp sandals.

entries.zh: 八月辛丑，命十五將以禦契丹，
entries.en: In the eighth month, on xinchou, fifteen generals were ordered to take the field against the Khitan,
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on xinchou, fifteen generals were appointed to resist the Khitan,

entries.zh: 〈（《東都事略·範質傳》：晉出帝命十五將出征。
entries.en: (From the 《Outline History of the Eastern Capital》 · Biography of Fan Zhi: The Deposed Emperor of Jin ordered fifteen generals on campaign.
entries.literal: (From the 《Outline History of the Eastern Capital》 · Biography of Fan Zhi: The Deposed Emperor of Jin ordered fifteen generals on campaign.

entries.zh: 是夕，質宿直，出帝命諸學士分草制，質曰：「宮城已閉，慮泄機事。」
entries.en: That night Fan Zhi was on palace duty. The Deposed Emperor told the academicians to divide the drafting of the edicts among themselves, but Fan Zhi said, "The palace gates are shut—we must not risk leaking military secrets."
entries.literal: That evening Fan Zhi was on night duty at court; the Deposed Emperor ordered the various academicians each to draft an edict, but Fan Zhi said, "The palace gates are already closed—there is fear of leaking military secrets."

entries.zh: 遂獨為之。）〉
entries.en: He therefore drafted them all himself.)〉
entries.literal: Thereupon he alone drafted them.)〉

entries.zh: 北京留守劉知遠充北面行營都統，鎮州節度使杜威充北面行營都招討使，鄆州節度使張從恩充馬步軍都監，西京留守景延廣充馬步軍都排陣使，徐州節度使趙在禮充馬步軍都虞候，晉州節度使安叔千充馬步軍左廂排陣使，前兗州節度使安審信充馬軍右廂排陣使，河中節度使安審琦充馬步軍都指揮使，河陽節度使符彥卿充馬軍左廂都指揮使，滑州節度使皇甫遇充馬步軍右廂都指揮使，右神武統軍張彥澤充馬軍排陣使，滄州節度使王廷胤充馬軍左廂都指揮使，陜州節度使宋彥筠充步軍右廂都指揮使，前金州節度使田武充步軍左廂排陣使，左神武統軍潘環充步軍右廂排陣使。
entries.en: Liu Zhiyuan, military commissioner of the Northern Capital, became overall commander of the northern campaign; Du Wei of Zhenzhou, overall commander for suppression; Zhang Cong'en of Yanzhou, overall supervisor of horse and foot; Jing Yanguang, military commissioner of the Western Capital, overall array marshal; Zhao Zaili of Xuzhou, overall deputy commander; An Shuqian of Jinzhou, left-wing array marshal; former Yanzhou governor An Shenxin, right-wing cavalry array marshal; An Shenqi of Hezhong, overall commander of horse and foot; Fu Yanqing of Heyang, left-wing cavalry commander; Huangfu Yu of Huazhou, right-wing horse-and-foot commander; Zhang Yanzhe of the Right Divine Martial Army, cavalry array marshal; Wang Tingyin of Cangzhou, left-wing cavalry commander; Song Yanyun of Shaanzhou, right-wing infantry commander; former Jinzhou governor Tian Wu, left-wing infantry array marshal; and Pan Huan of the Left Divine Martial Army, right-wing infantry array marshal.
entries.literal: Liu Zhiyuan, military commissioner of the Northern Capital, was made overall commander of the northern campaign headquarters; Du Wei, military governor of Zhenzhou, was made overall commander for suppression; Zhang Cong'en, military governor of Yanzhou, was made overall supervisor of horse and foot armies; Jing Yanguang, military commissioner of the Western Capital, was made overall array marshal of horse and foot armies; Zhao Zaili, military governor of Xuzhou, was made overall deputy commander of horse and foot armies; An Shuqian, military governor of Jinzhou, was made array marshal of the left wing of horse and foot armies; An Shenxin, former military governor of Yanzhou, was made array marshal of the right wing of the cavalry; An Shenqi, military governor of Hezhong, was made overall commander of horse and foot armies; Fu Yanqing, military governor of Heyang, was made overall commander of the left wing of cavalry; Huangfu Yu, military governor of Huazhou, was made overall commander of the right wing of horse and foot armies; Zhang Yanzhe, Commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, was made cavalry array marshal; Wang Tingyin, military governor of Cangzhou, was made overall commander of the left wing of cavalry; Song Yanyun, military governor of Shaanzhou, was made overall commander of the right wing of infantry; Tian Wu, former military governor of Jinzhou, was made array marshal of the left wing of infantry; Pan Huan, Commander of the Left Divine Martial Army, was made array marshal of the right wing of infantry.

entries.zh: 壬寅，閩王王延羲為其下連重遇、朱文進所害，眾推文進知留後事，稱天福年號，間道以聞。
entries.en: On renyin, King Yanxi of Min was murdered by his officers Lian Chongyu and Zhu Wenjin; the troops installed Zhu Wenjin as acting military commissioner, proclaimed the Tianfu era name, and sent word by a back channel.
entries.literal: On renyin, the King of Min Wang Yanxi was killed by his subordinates Lian Chongyu and Zhu Wenjin; the multitude pushed Zhu Wenjin to manage the affairs of military commissioner, adopted the Tianfu era name, and reported by a secret route.

entries.zh: 甲辰，太子少傅盧文紀改太子太傅，太子少保李麟改太子太保，刑部尚書李懌改戶部尚書，給事中司徒詡改右散騎常侍，以府州刺史折從阮為安北都護，充振武節度使。
entries.en: On jiachen, Lu Wenji rose from Junior to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Li Lin from Junior to Grand Guardian; Li Yi moved from Justice to Revenue; Situ Xu from Attendant Censor to Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; and She Congruan, prefect of Fu, was named Protector-General Pacifying the North and military governor of Zhenwu.
entries.literal: On jiachen, Lu Wenji, Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Li Lin, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, was transferred to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; Li Yi, Minister of Justice, was transferred to Minister of Revenue; Situ Xu, Attendant Censor, was transferred to Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; She Congruan, prefect of Fu Prefecture, was made Protector-General Pacifying the North and appointed military governor of Zhenwu.

entries.zh: 是夜，熒惑入南斗。
entries.en: That night Mars entered the mansion of the Southern Dipper.
entries.literal: That night Mars entered the Southern Dipper.

entries.zh: 乙巳，詔復置明經、童子二科。
entries.en: On yisi, an edict reinstated the Classicist and Youth examination tracks.
entries.literal: On yisi, an edict restored the two examination categories of Classicist and Youth.

entries.zh: 己酉，以鄧州節度使王令溫為延州節度使。
entries.en: On jiyou, Wang Lingwen, military governor of Dengzhou, was transferred to Yanzhou.
entries.literal: On jiyou, Wang Lingwen, military governor of Dengzhou, was made military governor of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 癸丑，以威武軍兵馬留後、權知閩國事朱文進為檢校太傅、福州威武軍節度使，知閩國事。
entries.en: On guichou, Zhu Wenjin, regent of the Weiwu Army and acting ruler of Min, received the honorary title of Grand Preceptor and was confirmed as military governor of the Weiwu Army at Fuzhou with authority over Min.
entries.literal: On guichou, Zhu Wenjin, military regent of the Weiwu Army and acting supervisor of the affairs of Min, was given the additional title of Grand Preceptor by special appointment and made military governor of the Weiwu Army at Fuzhou, with charge of the affairs of Min.

entries.zh: 癸亥，升澶州為節鎮，以鎮寧為軍額，割濮州為屬郡。
entries.en: On guihai, Chanzhou was raised to a full military commission under the army name Zhenning, with Bozhou detached to serve as its subordinate prefecture.
entries.literal: On guihai, Chanzhou was elevated to a military commission, with Zhenning as the army designation, and Bozhou was carved out as its subordinate prefecture.

entries.zh: 甲子，以延州節度使史威為澶州節度使。
entries.en: On jiazi, Shi Wei, military governor of Yanzhou, was appointed military governor of Chanzhou.
entries.literal: On jiazi, Shi Wei, military governor of Yanzhou, was made military governor of Chanzhou.

entries.zh: 閏月庚午，以楊承信為右羽林將軍，承祚為右驍騎衛將軍。
entries.en: In the intercalary month, on gengwu, Yang Chengxin was appointed General of the Right Forest of Feathers Army and Chengzuo General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.
entries.literal: In the intercalary month, on gengwu, Yang Chengxin was made General of the Right Forest of Feathers Army, and Chengzuo was made General of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.

entries.zh: 皆光遠之子，先詣闕請罪，故特授是官。
entries.en: Both were Guangyuan's sons, who had come to court first to plead guilty; they were therefore specially granted these posts.
entries.literal: Both were sons of Guangyuan who had first come to court to plead guilt, and therefore were specially granted these offices.

entries.zh: 癸酉，李守貞奏，楊光遠卒。
entries.en: On guiyou, Li Shouzhen reported that Yang Guangyuan had died.
entries.literal: On guiyou, Li Shouzhen memorialized that Yang Guangyuan had died.

entries.zh: 初，光遠既上表送降，帝以光遠頃歲太原歸命，欲曲全之，議者曰：「豈有反狀滔天而赦之也！」
entries.en: When Guangyuan had submitted his surrender memorial, the Emperor, remembering that he had once submitted at Taiyuan, wished to spare him; but critics said, "How can treason of such magnitude be pardoned!"
entries.literal: Initially, after Guangyuan had submitted his memorial offering surrender, the Emperor, because Guangyuan in recent years had submitted to the throne at Taiyuan, wished to spare him completely; but those in discussion said, "How can there be treason reaching to heaven and yet pardon him!"

entries.zh: 乃命守貞便宜處置。
entries.en: He therefore ordered Shouzhen to act as he saw fit.
entries.literal: Thereupon he ordered Shouzhen to dispose of the matter as circumstances required.

entries.zh: 守貞遣人拉殺之，以病卒聞。
entries.en: Shouzhen had him strangled and reported that he had died of illness.
entries.literal: Shouzhen sent men to strangle him to death and reported it as death from illness.

entries.zh: 乙酉，前登州刺史張萬迪削奪官爵處斬，青州節度判官楊麟配流威州，掌書記任邈配流原州，支使徐晏配流武州。
entries.en: On yiyou, Zhang Wandi, former prefect of Deng, was stripped of rank and executed; Yang Lin, Qingzhou military commissioner, was banished to Weizhou; Ren Miao, chief secretary, to Yuanzhou; and Xu Yan, administrative aide, to Wuzhou.
entries.literal: On yiyou, Zhang Wandi, former prefect of Deng Prefecture, was stripped of office and rank and executed; Yang Lin, military commissioner of Qingzhou, was banished to Weizhou; Ren Miao, chief secretary, was banished to Yuanzhou; Xu Yan, administrative aide, was banished to Wuzhou.

entries.zh: 縱逢恩赦，不在放還之限，並以楊光遠叛故也。
entries.en: Even future amnesties would not restore them—all on account of Yang Guangyuan's rebellion.
entries.literal: Even if an amnesty should occur, they were not within the scope of release and return—all because of Yang Guangyuan's rebellion.

entries.zh: 工部尚書、權知貢舉竇貞固奏：「試進士諸科舉人入策，舊例夜試，以三條燭盡為限，天成二年改令晝試，今欲依舊夜試。」
entries.en: Dou Zhengu, Minister of Works and acting chief examiner, reported: "Jinshi and other candidates taking the policy examination formerly tested at night, with a limit of three candles; in Tiancheng 2 this was changed to daytime testing, and we now ask to restore the night examination."
entries.literal: Dou Zhengu, Minister of Works and acting supervisor of the examinations, memorialized: "Candidates for the jinshi and various categories who enter the policy examination—by old custom the test was at night, limited by the burning of three candles; in the second year of Tiancheng it was changed to daytime testing, and now we wish to follow the old custom of night testing."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court approved.
entries.literal: The request was approved.

entries.zh: 曲赦青州管內罪人，立功將士各賜優給，青州吏民為楊光遠詿誤者，一切不問。
entries.en: A partial amnesty was proclaimed for criminals in Qingzhou; meritorious soldiers received generous rewards; and officials and commoners misled by Yang Guangyuan were not prosecuted.
entries.literal: A partial amnesty was granted to criminals within the jurisdiction of Qingzhou; meritorious officers and soldiers were each given generous rewards; officials and people of Qingzhou who had been misled by Yang Guangyuan were altogether not questioned.

entries.zh: 青州行營招討使、兗州節度使兼侍衛都虞候李守貞加同平章事，副招討使、河陽節度使符彥卿改許州節度使。
entries.en: Li Shouzhen, commander for suppression at the Qingzhou camp and military governor of Yanzhou with charge of the palace guard, was made Co-Grand Councilor; Fu Yanqing, deputy commander for suppression and military governor of Heyang, was transferred to Xuzhou.
entries.literal: Li Shouzhen, commander for suppression of the Qingzhou field headquarters and military governor of Yanzhou with concurrent appointment as overall deputy commander of the palace guard, was given the additional title of Co-Grand Councilor; Fu Yanqing, deputy commander for suppression and military governor of Heyang, was transferred to military governor of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 丙戌，降青州為防禦使額，以萊州刺史楊承勛為汝州防禦使。
entries.en: On bingxu, Qingzhou was downgraded to a defense command, and Yang Chengxun, prefect of Laizhou, was appointed defense commissioner of Ruzhou.
entries.literal: On bingxu, Qingzhou was reduced to a defense commission, and Yang Chengxun, prefect of Laizhou, was made defense commissioner of Ruzhou.

entries.zh: 己丑，以工部尚書竇貞固為禮部尚書，太常卿王延為工部尚書，左丞王松為太常卿，以前尚書右丞龍敏為尚書左丞。
entries.en: On jichou, Dou Zhengu moved from Works to Rites; Wang Yan from Director of Sacrifices to Works; Wang Song from Left Assistant Director to Director of Sacrifices; and former Right Assistant Director Long Min to Left Assistant Director.
entries.literal: On jichou, Dou Zhengu, Minister of Works, was made Minister of Rites; Wang Yan, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Minister of Works; Wang Song, Left Assistant Director, was made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Long Min, former Right Assistant Director, was made Left Assistant Director.

entries.zh: 癸巳，以前安州防禦使李建崇為河陽兵馬留後，以宣徽使翟光鄴為青州防禦使，以內客省使李彥韜為宣徽北院使。
entries.en: On guisi, Li Jianchong, former defense commissioner of Anzhou, became military regent of Heyang; Zhai Guangye, Palace Secretariat commissioner, defense commissioner of Qingzhou; and Li Yantao, commissioner of the Inner Clients Bureau, commissioner of the North Court of the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: On guisi, Li Jianchong, former defense commissioner of Anzhou, was made military regent of Heyang; Zhai Guangye, Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was made defense commissioner of Qingzhou; Li Yantao, Commissioner of the Inner Clients Bureau, was made Commissioner of the North Court of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 甲午，以給事中邊光範為左散騎常侍，以樞密直學士、吏部郎中李穀為給事中，依前充職。
entries.en: On jiawu, Bian Guangfan, Attendant Censor, became Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; Li Gu, Direct Academician of Military Affairs and Director of the Bureau of Personnel, was made Attendant Censor while retaining his former duties.
entries.literal: On jiawu, Bian Guangfan, Attendant Censor, was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; Li Gu, Academician Direct of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Director of the Bureau of Personnel, was made Attendant Censor and continued in his former duties.

entries.zh: 是月，契丹耶律德光與趙延壽領全軍入寇，圍恒州，分兵陷鼓城、槁城、元氏、高邑、昭慶、寧晉、蒲澤、欒城、柏鄉等縣，前鋒至邢州，河北諸州告急。
entries.en: That month Yelü Deguang of the Khitan and Zhao Yanshou invaded at the head of the full army, besieged Hengzhou, and sent detachments to seize Gucheng, Gaocheng, Yuanshi, Gaoyi, Zhaoqing, Ningjin, Puze, Luancheng, Baixiang, and other counties; the vanguard reached Xingzhou, and every prefecture in Hebei sent urgent alarms.
entries.literal: That month, Yelü Deguang of the Khitan and Zhao Yanshou led the full army in invasion, besieged Hengzhou, and with divided forces captured Gucheng, Gaocheng, Yuanshi, Gaoyi, Zhaoqing, Ningjin, Puze, Luancheng, Baixiang, and other counties; the vanguard reached Xingzhou, and all prefectures of Hebei reported urgent distress.

entries.zh: 詔張從恩、馬全節、安審琦率師屯邢州，趙在禮屯鄴都。
entries.en: An edict ordered Zhang Cong'en, Ma Quanjie, and An Shenqi to take the field and encamp at Xingzhou, while Zhao Zaili encamped at Yedu.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Zhang Cong'en, Ma Quanjie, and An Shenqi to lead their armies and encamp at Xingzhou, and Zhao Zaili to encamp at Yedu.

entries.zh: 夏四月丙子，以車駕將還京，差官往西京告天地宗廟社稷。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on bingzi, as the Emperor was about to return to the capital, envoys were sent to the Western Capital to report to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of state.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingzi, because the imperial carriage was about to return to the capital, officials were dispatched to the Western Capital to announce the fact to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain.

entries.zh: 辛巳，駕發澶州。
entries.en: On xinsi, the imperial procession left Chanzhou.
entries.literal: On xinsi, the imperial carriage departed from Chanzhou.

entries.zh: 甲申，至京師，曲赦在京禁囚。
entries.en: On jiashen, the court reached the capital and granted a partial amnesty to prisoners in the capital.
entries.literal: On jiashen, the court arrived at the capital and granted a partial amnesty to prisoners held in the capital.

entries.zh: 己亥，詔鄴都依舊為天雄軍。
entries.en: On jihai, an edict restored Yedu as headquarters of the Tianxiong Army.
entries.literal: On jihai, an edict declared that Yedu was again to be the Tianxiong Army.

entries.zh: 庚寅，河東節度使劉知遠封北平王；
entries.en: On gengyin, Liu Zhiyuan, military governor of Hedong, was enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping;
entries.literal: On gengyin, Liu Zhiyuan, military governor of Hedong, was enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping;

entries.zh: 恒州節度使杜威加守太傅；
entries.en: Du Wei of Hengzhou received the honorary title of Acting Grand Tutor;
entries.literal: Du Wei, military governor of Hengzhou, was given the additional title of Acting Grand Tutor;

entries.zh: 徐州趙在禮移鎮兗州；
entries.en: Zhao Zaili of Xuzhou was transferred to Yanzhou;
entries.literal: Zhao Zaili of Xuzhou was transferred to Yanzhou;

entries.zh: 宋州節度使兼侍衛親軍馬步都指揮使高行周移鎮鄆州，侍衛如故；
entries.en: Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Songzhou and overall commander of the palace guard horse and foot, was transferred to Yanzhou while keeping his guard command;
entries.literal: Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Songzhou with concurrent appointment as overall commander of horse and foot of the palace guard, was transferred to Yanzhou, retaining his palace guard duties;

entries.zh: 鄴都留守馬全節改天雄軍節度使；
entries.en: Ma Quanjie, military commissioner of Yedu, became military governor of the Tianxiong Army;
entries.literal: Ma Quanjie, military commissioner of Yedu, was made military governor of the Tianxiong Army;

entries.zh: 兗州節度使兼侍衛都虞候李守貞移鎮宋州，加檢校太師兼侍衛親軍副指揮使；
entries.en: Li Shouzhen of Yanzhou, deputy commander of the palace guard, was transferred to Songzhou and given the honorary title of Grand Preceptor and the post of Deputy Overall Commander of the palace guard;
entries.literal: Li Shouzhen, military governor of Yanzhou with concurrent appointment as overall deputy commander of the palace guard, was transferred to Songzhou, with the additional titles of Grand Preceptor by special appointment and Deputy Overall Commander of the palace guard;

entries.zh: 河中節度使安審琦加兼侍中，移鎮許州；
entries.en: An Shenqi of Hezhong was made Vice Grand Counselor and transferred to Xuzhou;
entries.literal: An Shenqi, military governor of Hezhong, was given the additional title of Vice Grand Counselor and transferred to Xuzhou;

entries.zh: 許州節度使符彥卿加同平章事，移鎮徐州；
entries.en: Fu Yanqing of Xu Prefecture was made Co-Grand Councilor and transferred to Xuzhou;
entries.literal: Fu Yanqing, military governor of Xu Prefecture, was given the additional title of Co-Grand Councilor and transferred to Xuzhou;

entries.zh: 滑州節度使皇甫遇加同平章事。
entries.en: Huangfu Yu of Huazhou was made Co-Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: Huangfu Yu, military governor of Huazhou, was given the additional title of Co-Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 壬辰，西京留守景延廣加邑封，改功臣；
entries.en: On renchen, Jing Yanguang, military commissioner of the Western Capital, received an enlarged fief and a new merit-title;
entries.literal: On renchen, Jing Yanguang, military commissioner of the Western Capital, was granted an increase in fief and a change of merit-title;

entries.zh: 泰州節度使侯益移鎮河中；
entries.en: Hou Yi of Taizhou was transferred to Hezhong;
entries.literal: Hou Yi, military governor of Taizhou, was transferred to Hezhong;

entries.zh: 定州節度使王周加檢校太師。
entries.en: Wang Zhou of Dingzhou received the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Wang Zhou, military governor of Dingzhou, was given the additional title of Grand Preceptor by special appointment.

entries.zh: 開運元年秋七月辛未朔，帝御崇元殿，大赦天下，改天福九年為開運元年。
entries.en: On the first day of the seventh month in autumn of Kaiyun 1, xinwei, the Emperor held court in Chongyuan Hall, granted a general amnesty, and renamed the ninth year of Tianfu as the first year of Kaiyun.
entries.literal: On the first day of the seventh month of autumn in the first year of Kaiyun, xinwei, the Emperor took the throne at Chongyuan Hall, proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm, and changed the ninth year of Tianfu to the first year of Kaiyun.

entries.zh: 河北諸州，曾經契丹蹂踐處，與免今年秋稅。
entries.en: All prefectures in Hebei that had been ravaged by the Khitan were granted exemption from this year's autumn tax.
entries.literal: In all prefectures of Hebei that had suffered Khitan ravaging and trampling, the autumn tax of this year was remitted.

entries.zh: 諸軍將士等第各賜優給。
entries.en: Soldiers and officers in the various armies received graded bonuses according to merit.
entries.literal: Officers and soldiers of the various armies were each granted generous rewards according to rank.

entries.zh: 諸州率借錢帛，赦書到日，畫時罷征，出一千貫已上者與免科徭，一萬貫已上者與授本州上佐雲。
entries.en: Forced loans of cash and silk levied by the prefectures were to stop the moment the amnesty arrived; contributors of a thousand strings or more were freed from labor corvée, and those of ten thousand strings or more were to receive senior associate appointments in their home prefecture.
entries.literal: As for the forced loans of money and silk cloth levied by the prefectures, on the day the amnesty edict arrived collection was to cease at once; those who had paid one thousand strings or more were to be exempted from labor corvée, and those who had paid ten thousand strings or more were to be appointed to senior associate posts in their home prefecture.

entries.zh: 是日宣赦未畢，會大雷雨，匆遽而罷。
entries.en: That day the amnesty proclamation had not yet finished when a violent thunderstorm broke out, and the ceremony was cut short in haste.
entries.literal: That day, before the proclamation of the amnesty was finished, a great thunderstorm occurred, and it was hurriedly brought to a close.

entries.zh: 時都下震死者數百人，明德門內震落石龍之首，識者以為石乃國姓，蓋不祥之甚也。
entries.en: Several hundred people in the capital were killed by lightning, and inside the Gate of Virtuous Clarity the head of a stone dragon was shaken loose; the learned took stone to be the dynastic surname of the house—a dire omen indeed.
entries.literal: At that time several hundred people in the capital were killed by the lightning strike; inside the Gate of Virtuous Clarity the head of a stone dragon fell from the shock, and those who understood such things held that stone was the dynastic surname—surely a most inauspicious sign.

entries.zh: 癸酉，以定州節度使馬全節為鄴都留守，加兼侍中；
entries.en: On guiyou, Ma Quanjie, military governor of Dingzhou, was appointed military commissioner of Yedu and concurrently Vice Grand Counselor;
entries.literal: On guiyou, Ma Quanjie, military governor of Dingzhou, was made military commissioner of Yedu, with the additional title of Vice Grand Counselor;

entries.zh: 以昭義節度使安審暉為邢州節度使，加檢校太師。
entries.en: An Shenhui, military governor of Zhaoyi, was transferred to Xingzhou as military governor and given the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: An Shenhui, military governor of Zhaoyi, was made military governor of Xingzhou, with the additional title of Grand Preceptor by special appointment.

entries.zh: 乙亥，前陜州節度使王周加檢校太尉，改定州節度使；
entries.en: On yihai, Wang Zhou, former military governor of Shaanzhou, was made honorary Grand Marshal and appointed military governor of Dingzhou;
entries.literal: On yihai, Wang Zhou, former military governor of Shaanzhou, was given the additional title of Grand Marshal by special appointment and transferred to military governor of Dingzhou;

entries.zh: 鄴都留守張從恩改鄆州節度使。
entries.en: Zhang Cong'en, military commissioner of Yedu, became military governor of Yanzhou.
entries.literal: Zhang Cong'en, military commissioner of Yedu, was transferred to military governor of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 禮官奏：「天子三年喪畢，祫享於太廟，高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝今年八月喪終畢，合以十月行大祫之禮，冬季祠祭，改薦為祫。」
entries.en: The ritual officials reported: "When the Son of Heaven completes three years of mourning, he offers the he sacrifice in the Grand Temple. Mourning for Emperor Gaozu, the Sagely, Cultured, Martial, and Virtuously Bright Filial Emperor, ends this eighth month; the great he rite should be held in the tenth month, and the winter seasonal sacrifices should be changed from jian to he."
entries.literal: The ritual officials memorialized: "When the Son of Heaven's three-year mourning is completed, he performs the he sacrifice in the Grand Temple. The mourning for the Sagely, Cultured, Martial, and Virtuously Bright Filial Emperor Gaozu will be completed this eighth month; it is fitting to perform the great he rite in the tenth month, and for the winter seasonal sacrifices to change the jian offering to he."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court approved.
entries.literal: The request was approved.

entries.zh: 丁丑，虞部員外郎、知制誥陶穀改倉部郎中、知制誥，大理卿吳德謙改秘書監致仕。
entries.en: On dingchou, Tao Gu moved from Vice Director of Parks and Forests with edict-drafting duties to Director of the Bureau of Granaries while retaining his drafting post; Wu Deqian, Director of the Court of Judicial Review, became Director of the Palace Library and retired.
entries.literal: On dingchou, Tao Gu, Vice Director of the Bureau of Parks and Forests and drafter of edicts, was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Granaries and continued as drafter of edicts; Wu Deqian, Director of the Court of Judicial Review, was transferred to Director of the Palace Library and retired.

entries.zh: 辛巳，以左龍武統軍李從敏為潞州節度使，天策府都護軍、桂州節度使、知郎州軍事馬希杲加檢校太師。
entries.en: On xinsi, Li Congmin, commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army, was appointed military governor of Luzhou; Ma Xigao, Protector-General of the Heavenly Stratagem Office and military governor of Guizhou with charge of Langzhou, received the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: On xinsi, Li Congmin, Commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army, was made military governor of Luzhou; Ma Xigao, Protector-General of the Heavenly Stratagem Office, military governor of Guizhou, and supervisor of military affairs in Langzhou, was given the additional title of Grand Preceptor by special appointment.

entries.zh: 壬午，降金州為防禦州，降萊州為刺史州。
entries.en: On renwu, Jinzhou was downgraded to a defense command and Laizhou to a standard prefecture.
entries.literal: On renwu, Jinzhou was reduced to a defense prefecture, and Laizhou was reduced to a prefecture under a prefect.

entries.zh: 戶部侍郎田敏改兵部侍郎；
entries.en: Tian Min, Vice Minister of Revenue, became Vice Minister of War;
entries.literal: Tian Min, Vice Minister of Revenue, was transferred to Vice Minister of War;

entries.zh: 刑部侍郎李祥改尚書右丞；
entries.en: Li Xiang, Vice Minister of Justice, was made Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs;
entries.literal: Li Xiang, Vice Minister of Justice, was transferred to Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs;

entries.zh: 以潁州團練使馮玉為戶部侍郎，充端明殿學士；
entries.en: Feng Yu, regimental commissioner of Yingzhou, was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and Academician of the Duanming Hall;
entries.literal: Feng Yu, regimental commissioner of Yingzhou, was made Vice Minister of Revenue and appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall;

entries.zh: 中書舍人趙上交改刑部侍郎。
entries.en: Zhao Shangjiao, Attendant Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat, became Vice Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: Zhao Shangjiao, Attendant Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat, was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 己丑，以樞密使、中書令桑維翰充宏文館大學士，太子太傅、譙國公劉句為守司空兼門下侍郎平章事、監修國史、判三司，宰臣李崧、和凝進封爵邑。
entries.en: On jichou, Sang Weihan, Commissioner of Military Affairs and Grand Counselor, became Grand Academician of the Hongwen Institute; Liu Gou, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Qiao, was named Acting Minister of Works with concurrent posts as Vice Director of the Chancellery, Grand Councilor, Supervisor of the National History, and Controller of the Three Commissions; chief ministers Li Song and He Ning received promotions in rank and fief.
entries.literal: On jichou, Sang Weihan, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Grand Counselor of the Secretariat, was appointed Grand Academician of the Hongwen Institute; Liu Gou, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Qiao, was made Acting Minister of Works with concurrent appointment as Vice Director of the Chancellery, Grand Councilor, Supervisor of the National History, and Controller of the Three Commissions; the chief ministers Li Song and He Ning were advanced in noble rank and fief.

entries.zh: 庚寅，宣徽北院使劉繼勛改宣徽南院使，三司使董遇改宣徽北院使。
entries.en: On gengyin, Liu Jixun moved from the North to the South Court of the Palace Secretariat; Dong Yu, Commissioner of the Three Commissions, took over the North Court post.
entries.literal: On gengyin, Liu Jixun, Commissioner of the North Court of the Palace Secretariat, was transferred to Commissioner of the South Court of the Palace Secretariat; Dong Yu, Commissioner of the Three Commissions, was transferred to Commissioner of the North Court of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 辛卯，以前陜州節度使石赟為鄧州節度使。
entries.en: On xinmao, Shi Yun, former military governor of Shaanzhou, was appointed military governor of Dengzhou.
entries.literal: On xinmao, Shi Yun, former military governor of Shaanzhou, was made military governor of Dengzhou.

entries.zh: 同州節度使李承福卒，贈太傅。
entries.en: Li Chengfu, military governor of Tongzhou, died and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: Li Chengfu, military governor of Tongzhou, died and was posthumously given the title of Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 七月壬辰，以禮部尚書王延為刑部尚書，以工部尚書王松為禮部尚書，以太常卿龍敏為工部尚書，以左丞李慎儀為太常卿，以吏部侍郎張昭遠為左丞，以右丞李詳為吏部侍郎，以前義州刺史李玘為右丞。
entries.en: On renchen of the seventh month Wang Yan moved to Justice, Wang Song to Rites, Long Min to Works, Li Shenyi to Ceremonies, Zhang Zhaoyuan to Left Vice Director, Li Xiang to Civil Vice Minister, and former Yi prefect Li Qi to Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: In the seventh month, on renchen, Wang Yan, Minister of Rites, was made Minister of Justice; Wang Song, Minister of Works, was made Minister of Rites; Long Min, Director of Ceremonies, was made Minister of Works; Li Shenyi, Left Vice Director, was made Director of Ceremonies; Zhang Zhaoyuan, Vice Minister of the Civil Office, was made Left Vice Director; Li Xiang, Right Vice Director, was made Vice Minister of the Civil Office; Li Qi, former prefect of Yi Prefecture, was made Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 前晉昌軍節度使安彥威薨，輟朝，贈太師。
entries.en: Former Jinchang commissioner An Yanwei died; audiences were suspended and he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: An Yanwei, former military commissioner of the Jinchang Army, died; court audiences were suspended, and he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 丙申，兩浙節度使、吳越國王錢宏佐加守太師，北京留守、河東節度使、北平王劉知遠加守太尉。
entries.en: On bingshen Qian Hongzuo of Wuyue became Defender of Grand Preceptor and Liu Zhiyuan of Hedong Defender of Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: On bingshen, Qian Hongzuo, military commissioner of the Two Zhes and King of Wuyue, was made Defender of Grand Preceptor; Liu Zhiyuan, garrison commander of the Northern Capital, military commissioner of Hedong, and Prince of Beiping, was made Defender of Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 滄州奏，蕃寇攻饒安縣。
entries.en: Cang Prefecture reported barbarian forces attacking Rao'an County.
entries.literal: Cang Prefecture reported that barbarian raiders were attacking Rao'an County.

entries.zh: 楊劉口河決西岸，水闊四十里。
entries.en: The Yellow River burst its west bank at Yangliu Ford; the flood spread forty li wide.
entries.literal: The Yangliu Ford on the Yellow River burst its west bank; the water spread forty li wide.

entries.zh: 以前鄧州節度使劉景巖為太子太師致仕。
entries.en: Former Deng commissioner Liu Jingyan was retired as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Liu Jingyan, former military commissioner of Deng Prefecture, was made retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 辛亥，宋州谷熟縣河水雨水一概東流，漂沒秋稼。
entries.en: On xinhai river and rain at Gushu in Song flowed east together and destroyed the autumn crop.
entries.literal: On xinhai, in Gushu County of Song Prefecture, river water and rainwater alike flowed eastward and swept away the autumn grain.

entries.zh: 丁巳，大理卿李專美卒。
entries.en: On dingsi Li Zhuanmei, Director of Judicial Review, died.
entries.literal: On dingsi, Li Zhuanmei, Director of the Court of Judicial Review, died.

entries.zh: 戊午，詔偽清泰朝經削奪官爵朱宏昭、馮赟、康義誠、王思同、藥彥稠等，並復其官爵。
entries.en: On wuwu an edict restored the ranks of Zhu Hongzhao, Feng Yun, Kang Yicheng, Wang Sitong, Yao Yanchou, and others stripped under the Qingtai reign.
entries.literal: On wuwu, an edict restored the ranks and titles of Zhu Hongzhao, Feng Yun, Kang Yicheng, Wang Sitong, Yao Yanchou, and others, who under the false Qingtai reign had been stripped of office.

entries.zh: 自夏初至是，河南、河北諸州郡餓死者數萬人，群盜蜂起，剽略縣鎮，霖雨不止，川澤泛漲，損害秋稼。
entries.en: Since early summer Henan and Hebei had seen tens of thousands starve, bandits raid towns, endless rain flood the rivers, and the autumn crop ruined.
entries.literal: From early summer until now, in the prefectures of Henan and Hebei tens of thousands died of hunger; bandits swarmed like bees, plundering counties and towns; unending rains made rivers and marshes overflow and harmed the autumn grain.

entries.zh: 秋九月壬辰，鄆州節度使、侍衛親軍都指揮使李守貞加兼侍中，滑州節度使皇甫遇進封邠國公，相州節度使張彥澤加檢校太尉。
entries.en: On renchen of the ninth autumn month Li Shouzhen of Yun became concurrent Palace Attendant, Huangfu Yu of Hua was made Duke of Bin, and Zhang Yanze of Xiang acting Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, on renchen, Li Shouzhen, military commissioner of Yun Prefecture and commander of the Palace Guards Personal Army, was made concurrent Palace Attendant; Huangfu Yu, military commissioner of Hua Prefecture, was advanced to Duke of Bin; Zhang Yanze, military commissioner of Xiang Prefecture, was given acting Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 甲午，以權知威武軍節度使李宏達為檢校太尉、同平章事，充福建節度使，知閩國事。
entries.en: On jiawu Li Hongda of Weiwu became acting Grand Marshal, Chief Counselor, Fujian commissioner, and overseer of Min.
entries.literal: On jiawu, Li Hongda, acting military commissioner of the Weiwu Army, was made acting Grand Marshal, Chief Counselor, military commissioner of Fujian, and overseer of Min affairs.

entries.zh: 乙未，前商州刺史李俊賜自盡，坐與親妹奸及行劍斫殺女使，又殺部曲孫漢榮，強奸其妻，準法棄市，詔賜死於家。
entries.en: On yiwei former Shang prefect Li Jun was allowed to kill himself at home for incest with his sister, murdering a maid and retainer Sun Hanrong and raping Sun's wife—a capital crime commuted to death at home.
entries.literal: On yiwei, Li Jun, former prefect of Shang Prefecture, was granted permission to take his own life for having committed incest with his younger sister by blood, drawn his sword and hacked a maid to death, also killed his retainer Sun Hanrong, and raped Sun's wife; by law he deserved execution in the marketplace, but an edict allowed him to die at home.

entries.zh: 己亥，張彥澤奏，破蕃賊於定州界，斬首二十餘級，追襲百餘里，生擒蕃將四人，摘得金耳環二副進呈。
entries.en: On jihai Zhang Yanze reported defeating barbarians on the Ding border, taking twenty heads, pursuing a hundred li, capturing four generals, and presenting gold earrings as trophies.
entries.literal: On jihai, Zhang Yanze reported breaking barbarian forces at the Ding Prefecture border, taking more than twenty heads, pursuing over a hundred li, capturing four barbarian generals alive, and presenting two pairs of gold earrings taken as trophies.

entries.zh: 癸卯，太原奏，破契丹於楊武谷，殺七千餘人。
entries.en: On guimao Taiyuan reported defeating the Khitan at Yangwu Valley with seven thousand killed.
entries.literal: On guimao, Taiyuan reported defeating the Khitan at Yangwu Valley and killing more than seven thousand.

entries.zh: 甲辰，以天策上將軍、江南諸道都統、楚王馬希範兼諸道兵馬都元帥。
entries.en: On jiachen Chu prince Ma Xifan became concurrent commander-in-chief of all circuits' forces.
entries.literal: On jiachen, Ma Xifan, Grand General of the Heavenly Stratagem, overall commander of the Jiangnan circuits, and Prince of Chu, was made concurrent commander-in-chief of all circuits' armies and horses.

entries.zh: 詔開封府，以霖雨不止，應京城公私僦舍錢放一月。
entries.en: Kaifeng was ordered to remit one month's rent on capital dwellings because of the endless rains.
entries.literal: An edict to Kaifeng Prefecture, because unending rains continued, ordered one month's rent remitted on public and private leased dwellings in the capital.

entries.zh: 乙巳，詔安審琦率兵赴鄴都，皇甫遇赴相州。
entries.en: On yisi An Shenqi was ordered to Ye and Huangfu Yu to Xiang.
entries.literal: On yisi, an edict ordered An Shenqi to lead troops to Ye and Huangfu Yu to Xiang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 丙午，以太子少保楊凝式為太子少傅，以刑部尚書王延為太子少保，前潁州團練使竇貞固為刑部尚書。
entries.en: On bingwu Yang Ningshi became Senior Mentor, Wang Yan Junior Mentor, and former Ying commissioner Dou Zhengu Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: On bingwu, Yang Ningshi, Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was made Senior Mentor; Wang Yan, Minister of Justice, was made Junior Mentor; Dou Zhengu, former training commissioner of Ying Prefecture, was made Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 是月，河南、河北、關西諸州奏，大水霖雨不止，溝河泛濫，水入城郭及損害秋稼。
entries.en: That month Henan, Hebei, and the western passes reported floods, endless rain, cities inundated, and crops ruined.
entries.literal: That month Henan, Hebei, and the western passes reported that great floods and unending rains made ditches and rivers overflow, water entered cities, and the autumn grain was harmed.

entries.zh: 是月，契丹瀛州刺史詐為書與樂壽將軍王巒，願以本城歸順，且言城中蕃軍不滿千人，請朝廷發軍襲取之，己為內應。
entries.en: That month the Khitan prefect of Ying forged a letter to Leshou general Wang Luan offering surrender, claiming fewer than a thousand barbarian troops in the city and asking for a strike while he acted as insider.
entries.literal: That month the Khitan prefect of Ying Prefecture forged a letter to Wang Luan, general of Leshou, offering to surrender the city and stating that barbarian troops in the city numbered fewer than a thousand, asking the court to send an army to seize it while he served as insider.

entries.zh: 又云：「今秋苦雨，川澤漲溢，自瓦橋已北，水勢無際。
entries.en: He also wrote: "This autumn's rains have flooded the rivers; north of Wagiao Bridge the waters are endless.
entries.literal: He also wrote: "This autumn's bitter rains have made rivers and marshes overflow; from Wagiao Bridge northward the waters are boundless.

entries.zh: 契丹已歸本國，若聞南夏有變，地遠阻水，雖欲奔命，無能及也。」
entries.en: The Khitan have returned home; if they hear of trouble in the south, distance and flood would prevent any timely rescue."
entries.literal: The Khitan have already returned to their own country; if they hear trouble in the Southern Court, the distance and the blocking waters mean that even if they wished to rush to the rescue, they could not arrive in time."

entries.zh: 又，巒繼有密奏，苦言瀛、鄚可取之狀。
entries.en: Wang Luan also sent secret memorials urgently arguing that Ying and Mo could be taken.
entries.literal: Moreover Luan sent further secret memorials urgently arguing that Ying and Mo could be taken.

entries.zh: 先是，前歲中車駕駐於河上，曾遣邊將遺書於幽州趙延壽，勸令歸國，延壽尋有報命，依違而已。
entries.en: Earlier, when the emperor had been on the Yellow River, border generals wrote Zhao Yanshou at Youzhou urging return; his reply was evasive.
entries.literal: Earlier, the year before when the imperial carriage was stationed on the Yellow River, border generals had been sent with letters to Zhao Yanshou at Youzhou urging him to return to the realm; Yanshou soon sent a reply, evasive and noncommittal.

entries.zh: 是歲三月，復遣鄴都杜威致書於延壽，且述朝旨，啖以厚利，仍遣洺州軍將趙行實賫書而往，潛申款密。
entries.en: That third month Du Wei of Ye again wrote Yanshou with court policy and rich inducements, sending Luozhou officer Zhao Xingshi with secret pledges.
entries.literal: In the third month of this year Du Wei of Ye was again sent with a letter to Yanshou stating court policy, tempting him with rich rewards, and the Luozhou officer Zhao Xingshi was dispatched bearing the letter to convey secret pledges in private.

entries.zh: 行實曾事延壽，故遣之。
entries.en: Xingshi had once served Yanshou and was chosen for the mission.
entries.literal: Xingshi had once served Yanshou, and therefore was sent.

entries.zh: 七月，行實自燕回，得延壽書，且言：「久陷邊庭，願歸中國，乞發大軍應接，即拔身南去。」
entries.en: In the seventh month Xingshi returned from Yan with Yanshou's letter: "Long trapped on the frontier, I wish to return to China; send a great army to meet me and I will come south at once."
entries.literal: In the seventh month Xingshi returned from Yan with Yanshou's letter, which also stated: "Long trapped on the frontier, I wish to return to China; I beg that a great army be sent to meet me, and I will at once withdraw south."

entries.zh: 敘致懇切，辭旨綿密，時朝廷欣然從之，復遣趙行實計會延壽大軍應接之所。
entries.en: The tone was earnest; the court gladly agreed and again sent Zhao Xingshi to arrange the rendezvous.
entries.literal: The tone was earnest and the wording close and careful; the court then gladly agreed and again sent Zhao Xingshi to arrange where Yanshou's great army should be met.

entries.zh: 有瀛州大將遣所親賫蠟書至闕下，告雲欲謀翻變，以本城歸命。
entries.en: A Ying general sent a sealed letter to court reporting a planned mutiny to surrender the city.
entries.literal: A great general of Ying Prefecture sent a close associate bearing a sealed wax letter to the court reporting a planned mutiny to surrender the city.

entries.zh: 未幾，會彼有告變者，事不果就。
entries.en: Soon the plot was reported on the other side and came to nothing.
entries.literal: Before long someone there reported the plot, and the affair did not succeed.

entries.zh: 至是，瀛州守將劉延祚受契丹之命，詐輸誠款，以誘我軍，國家深以為信，遂有出師之議。
entries.en: Now Ying commander Liu Yanzuo, on Khitan orders, feigned surrender to lure our army; the court believed him, and the campaign was launched.
entries.literal: At this time Liu Yanzuo, the Ying garrison commander, on Khitan orders feigned sincere submission to lure our army; the state deeply trusted him, and therefore the debate to march troops arose.

entries.zh: 開運二年夏五月丙申朔，帝御崇元殿受朝，大赦天下。
entries.en: In Kaiyun 2, on the first day bingshen of the fifth summer month, the emperor held court at Chongyuan Hall, received homage, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
entries.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun, on the first day bingshen of the fifth summer month, the emperor took the throne at Chongyuan Hall to receive court homage and proclaimed a general amnesty for all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 丁酉，以右衛上將軍馬萬為左金吾上將軍致仕。
entries.en: On dingyou Ma Wan, General of the Right Guard, was retired as General of the Left Golden Chancellery.
entries.literal: On dingyou, Ma Wan, General of the Right Guard, was made retired General of the Left Golden Chancellery.

entries.zh: 戊戌，陜州節度使宋彥筠移鎮鄧州，澶州節度使何建移鎮河陽。
entries.en: On wuxu Song Yanyun moved from Shaan to Deng Prefecture, and He Jian from Chan to Heyang.
entries.literal: On wuxu, Song Yanyun, military commissioner of Shaan Prefecture, was transferred to Deng Prefecture, and He Jian, military commissioner of Chan Prefecture, was transferred to Heyang.

entries.zh: 以左神武統軍潘環為澶州節度使，以宣徽北院使李彥韜遙領壽州節度使兼侍衛馬軍都指揮使，以滄州節度使田武遙領夔州節度使兼侍衛步軍都指揮使。
entries.en: Pan Huan became commissioner of Chan; Li Yantao held Shou remotely while commanding the palace cavalry; Tian Wu held Kui remotely while commanding the palace infantry.
entries.literal: Pan Huan, commander of the Left Divine Martial Army, was made military commissioner of Chan Prefecture; Li Yantao, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was given concurrent remote command of Shou Prefecture and made commander of the Palace Guards Cavalry; Tian Wu, military commissioner of Cang Prefecture, was given concurrent remote command of Kui Prefecture and made commander of the Palace Guards Infantry.

entries.zh: 辛亥，白虹貫日。
entries.en: On xinhai a white rainbow spanned the sun.
entries.literal: On xinhai, a white rainbow pierced the sun.

entries.zh: 壬子，宰臣桑維翰、劉句、李崧、和凝並加階爵。
entries.en: On renzi chief ministers Sang Weihan, Liu Xu, Li Song, and He Ning all received higher ranks and fiefs.
entries.literal: On renzi, the chief ministers Sang Weihan, Liu Xu, Li Song, and He Ning were all advanced in rank and enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 禮部尚書竇貞固改刑部尚書，太常寺卿王松改工部尚書。
entries.en: Dou Zhengu moved from Rites to Justice, and Wang Song from Ceremonies to Works.
entries.literal: Dou Zhengu, Minister of Rites, was changed to Minister of Justice; Wang Song, Director of the Directorate of Ceremonies, was changed to Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 以尚書左丞龍敏為太常卿；
entries.en: Long Min, Left Vice Director of State Affairs, became Director of Ceremonies;
entries.literal: Long Min, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Director of Ceremonies;

entries.zh: 以翰林學士承旨、兵部侍郎李慎儀為尚書左丞；
entries.en: Li Shenyi, Hanlin chief academician and Vice Minister of War, became Left Vice Director of State Affairs;
entries.literal: Li Shenyi, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War, was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs;

entries.zh: 以御史中丞張允為兵部侍郎、知制誥，充翰林學士承旨；
entries.en: Zhang Yun, Censor-in-Chief, became Vice Minister of War and drafter of rescripts and Hanlin chief academician;
entries.literal: Zhang Yun, Censor-in-Chief, was made Vice Minister of War, drafter of imperial rescripts, and appointed Hanlin Academician-in-Chief;

entries.zh: 以左諫議大夫顏衎為御史中丞；
entries.en: Yan Kan, Left Remonstrance Counselor, became Censor-in-Chief;
entries.literal: Yan Kan, Left Remonstrance Counselor, was made Censor-in-Chief;

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·顏衎傳》：喪亂之後，朝綱不振，衎執憲頗有風采，嘗上言：「才除御史者旋授外藩賓佐，復有以私故細事求假外拜，州郡無參謁之儀，出入失風憲之體，漸恐四方得以輕易，百辟無所準繩。
entries.en: (Song History, biography of Yan Kan: After the civil wars court discipline had slackened; Kan enforced the law with notable vigor and once memorialized: "Newly appointed censors are immediately sent as staff to frontier prefectures, and others use petty private pretexts to leave the capital for provincial posts. Prefectures then lack proper audience protocol, and the censorate loses its dignity—soon the realm may hold it in contempt and officials will have no standard.
entries.literal: (Biography of Yan Kan in the Song History: After the disorders, court discipline was slack; Kan in enforcing the law showed considerable authority and once memorialized: "Those just made censors are immediately appointed as staff to outer prefectures; moreover some seek leave for minor private matters to go out and take provincial posts, so that prefectures have no protocol for audiences, and coming and going lose the dignity proper to the censorate—gradually the four quarters may take things lightly and the hundred officials have no standard to follow.

entries.zh: 請自今藩鎮幕僚，勿得任臺官；
entries.en: Henceforth let prefectural staff not hold censorate posts;
entries.literal: I request that from now on prefectural staff may not hold censorate posts;

entries.zh: 雖親王宰相出鎮，亦不得奏充賓佐；
entries.en: even when princes or chief ministers take field commands, they may not be named as staff;
entries.literal: even when imperial princes or chief ministers go out to command prefectures, they may not be recommended as staff;

entries.zh: 非奉制勘事，勿得出京；
entries.en: and except on imperial commission to investigate, censors may not leave the capital;
entries.literal: except on imperial commission to investigate matters, they may not leave the capital;

entries.zh: 自余不令釐雜務。」
entries.en: nor handle miscellaneous duties."
entries.literal: as for the rest, do not allow them to take on miscellaneous duties."

entries.zh: 詔惟辟召入幕，余從其請。）〉
entries.en: The edict allowed only imperial summons to enter staffs; the rest was approved.)〉
entries.literal: An edict allowed only those summoned by imperial appointment to enter staffs; the rest of his requests were approved.)〉

entries.zh: 以兵部侍郎、宏文館學士、判館事田敏為國子祭酒；
entries.en: Tian Min, Vice Minister of War and Hongwen academician, became Chancellor of the Directorate of Education;
entries.literal: Tian Min, Vice Minister of War, academician of the Hongwen Hall, and overseer of the hall, was made Chancellor of the Directorate of Education;

entries.zh: 以戶部侍郎段希堯為兵部侍郎；
entries.en: Duan Xiyao, Vice Minister of Revenue, became Vice Minister of War;
entries.literal: Duan Xiyao, Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Vice Minister of War;

entries.zh: 以工部侍郎邊蔚為戶部侍郎，依前權知開封府事；
entries.en: Bian Wei, Vice Minister of Works, became Vice Minister of Revenue while retaining acting charge of Kaifeng;
entries.literal: Bian Wei, Vice Minister of Works, was made Vice Minister of Revenue and continued as before as acting overseer of Kaifeng Prefecture affairs;

entries.zh: 以左散騎常侍李式為工部侍郎；
entries.en: Li Shi, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, became Vice Minister of Works;
entries.literal: Li Shi, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, was made Vice Minister of Works;

entries.zh: 以給事中王仁裕為左散騎常侍。
entries.en: Wang Renyu, Supervising Secretary, became Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
entries.literal: Wang Renyu, Supervising Secretary, was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

entries.zh: 甲寅，以華州節度使趙瑩為開封尹，以皇弟開封尹重睿為秦州節度使，以宣徽南院使劉繼勛為華州節度使，以前鄆州節度使張從恩為晉州節度使。
entries.en: On jiayin Zhao Ying became Prefect of Kaifeng; the emperor's brother Chongrui left Kaifeng for Qin; Liu Jixun took Hua; and former Yun commissioner Zhang Cong'en took Jin.
entries.literal: On jiayin, Zhao Ying, military commissioner of Hua Prefecture, was made Prefect of Kaifeng; the emperor's younger brother Chongrui, Prefect of Kaifeng, was made military commissioner of Qin Prefecture; Liu Jixun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made military commissioner of Hua Prefecture; Zhang Cong'en, former military commissioner of Yun Prefecture, was made military commissioner of Jin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 丙辰，杜威來朝。
entries.en: On bingchen Du Wei presented himself at court.
entries.literal: On bingchen, Du Wei came to court.

entries.zh: 定州奏，大風雹，北嶽廟殿宇樹木悉摧拔之。
entries.en: Ding Prefecture reported that wind and hail had destroyed the halls and trees of the Northern Marchmount Temple.
entries.literal: Ding Prefecture reported that a great wind and hail had utterly uprooted the halls and trees of the Northern Marchmount Temple.

entries.zh: 十二月丁巳朔，
entries.en: On the dingsi new moon of the twelfth month,
entries.literal: Twelfth month, dingsi new moon,

entries.zh: 〈（案：以下有闕文。
entries.en: (There is missing text below.
entries.literal: (Note: There is missing text below.

entries.zh: 據《通鑒》云：丁巳朔，李穀自書密奏，且言大軍危急之勢，請車駕幸滑州，遣高行周、符彥卿扈從，及發兵守澶州、河陽，以備敵之奔沖。
entries.en: The Comprehensive Mirror records that on the dingsi new moon Li Gu wrote a secret memorial in his own hand describing the army's dire peril, asking that the emperor go to Huazhou with Gao Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing as escort, and that troops be sent to hold Chanzhou and Heyang against a sudden enemy thrust.
entries.literal: According to the Comprehensive Mirror: on dingsi new moon Li Gu wrote a secret memorial himself, stating also the army's grave peril, requesting the imperial carriage proceed to Huazhou, dispatching Gao Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing to escort, and sending troops to hold Chenzhou and Heyang to guard against the enemy's sudden thrust.

entries.zh: 遣軍將關勛走馬上之。）〉
entries.en: He sent the officer Guan Xun to ride posthaste with it.)〉
entries.literal: He sent the army officer Guan Xun to gallop and deliver it.)〉

entries.zh: 己未，杜威奏，駐軍於中渡橋。
entries.en: On jiwei Du Wei reported that the army was encamped at Zhongdu Bridge.
entries.literal: On jiwei Du Wei memorialized that the army was encamped at Zhongdu Bridge.

entries.zh: 庚申，以前司農卿儲延英為太子賓客。
entries.en: On gengshen former Minister of Agriculture Chu Yanying became Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: On gengshen former Minister of Revenue Chu Yanying was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 詔徐州符彥卿屯澶州。
entries.en: Fu Yanqing of Xuzhou was ordered to garrison Chenzhou.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Fu Yanqing of Xuzhou to garrison Chenzhou.

entries.zh: 辛酉，詔澤潞、鄴都、邢洺、河陽運糧赴中渡，杜威遣人口奏軍前事宜，勢迫故也。
entries.en: On xinyou Ze-Lu, Yedu, Xing-Mo, and Heyang were ordered to ship grain to Zhongdu; Du Wei sent couriers to report orally from the front because the crisis was acute.
entries.literal: On xinyou an edict ordered Ze-Lu, Yedu, Xing-Mo, and Heyang to transport grain to Zhongdu; Du Wei sent men to report orally on affairs at the front, because the situation was pressing.

entries.zh: 壬戌，又遣高行周屯澶州，景延廣守河陽。
entries.en: On renxu Gao Xingzhou was again sent to garrison Chenzhou and Jing Yanguang to defend Heyang.
entries.literal: On renxu Gao Xingzhou was again sent to garrison Chenzhou, and Jing Yanguang to hold Heyang.

entries.zh: 博野縣都監張鵬入奏蕃軍事勢。
entries.en: Zhang Peng, chief inspector of Boye county, reported to court on the Khitan army's disposition.
entries.literal: Zhang Peng, chief inspector of Boye county, entered court to report on the barbarian army's situation.

entries.zh: 丙寅，定州李殷奏，前月二十八日夜，領捉生四百人往曲陽嘉山下，逢敵軍車帳，殺千餘人，獲馬二百匹。
entries.en: On bingyin Li Yin of Dingzhou reported that on the night of the twenty-eighth of the previous month he led four hundred scouts to Jia Mountain below Quyang, struck enemy camps, killed more than a thousand men, and took two hundred horses.
entries.literal: On bingyin Li Yin of Dingzhou memorialized: on the night of the twenty-eighth of the previous month he led four hundred scouts to below Jia Mountain at Quyang, encountered enemy carts and tents, killed more than a thousand men, and captured two hundred horses.

entries.zh: 詔宋州高行周充北面行營都部署，符彥卿充副，邢州方太充都虞候，領後軍駐於河上，以備敵騎之奔沖也。
entries.en: Gao Xingzhou of Songzhou was made overall commander of the northern field army, Fu Yanqing his deputy, and Fang Tai of Xingzhou chief adjutant; they were to hold the rear army on the river against a Khitan cavalry rush.
entries.literal: An edict made Gao Xingzhou of Songzhou overall commander of the northern field headquarters, Fu Yanqing his deputy, and Fang Tai of Xingzhou chief adjutant; they were to lead the rear army to encamp on the river to guard against enemy cavalry thrusts.

entries.zh: 時契丹遊騎涉滹水而南，至欒城縣。
entries.en: Khitan raiders had crossed the Hutuo south as far as Luancheng county.
entries.literal: At that time Khitan raiding cavalry crossed the Hutuo River southward as far as Luancheng county.

entries.zh: 自是中渡寨為蕃軍隔絕，探報不通，朝廷大恐，故委行周等繼領兵師守扼津要，且以張其勢也。
entries.en: The Zhongdu camp was now cut off from the Khitans and no intelligence got through; the court was terrified, so Gao Xingzhou and the others were sent to hold the river crossings and show greater strength.
entries.literal: From this the Zhongdu camp was cut off by the barbarian army; scouts and reports could not get through; the court was greatly afraid; therefore Xingzhou and the others were entrusted to take over troops and hold the strategic crossings, and also to display greater force.

entries.zh: 己巳，邢州方太奏，此月六日，契丹與王師戰於中渡，王師不利，奉國都指揮使王清戰死。
entries.en: On jisi Fang Tai of Xingzhou reported that on the sixth of this month the Khitans fought the imperial army at Zhongdu; the imperial forces were beaten and Wang Qing, commander of the Fengguo army, was killed.
entries.literal: On jisi Fang Tai of Xingzhou memorialized: on the sixth of this month the Khitans fought the imperial army at Zhongdu; the imperial army was unfavorable; Wang Qing, commander of the Fengguo army, died in battle.

entries.zh: 庚午，幸沙臺射兔。
entries.en: On gengwu the emperor went to Shatai to hunt rabbits.
entries.literal: On gengwu the Emperor visited Shatai to shoot rabbits.

entries.zh: 壬申，始聞杜威、李守貞等以此月十日率諸軍降於契丹。
entries.en: On renshen came the first report that on the tenth Du Wei, Li Shouzhen, and the rest had surrendered the armies to the Khitans.
entries.literal: On renshen word was first received that on the tenth of this month Du Wei, Li Shouzhen, and the others had led the armies in surrender to the Khitans.

entries.zh: 是夜，相州節度使張彥澤受契丹命，率先鋒二千人，自封丘門斬關而入。
entries.en: That night Zhang Yanzhe, military governor of Xiangzhou, acting on Khitan orders led two thousand vanguard troops through Fengqiu Gate after cutting down the barrier.
entries.literal: That night Zhang Yanzhe, military governor of Xiangzhou, on Khitan orders led two thousand vanguard troops, broke through the gate at Fengqiu Gate, and entered.

entries.zh: 癸酉旦，張彥澤頓兵於明德門外，京城大擾。
entries.en: At dawn on guiyou Zhang Yanzhe encamped outside the Gate of Illustrious Virtue and the capital fell into uproar.
entries.literal: At dawn on guiyou Zhang Yanzhe halted his troops outside the Gate of Illustrious Virtue; the capital was greatly disturbed.

entries.zh: 前曹州節度使石赟死，帝之堂叔也。
entries.en: Former military governor of Caozhou Shi Yun died; he was the emperor's paternal uncle.
entries.literal: Former military governor of Caozhou Shi Yun died; he was the Emperor's paternal uncle.

entries.zh: 時自中渡寨隔絕之後，帝與大臣端坐憂危，國之衛兵，悉在北面，計無所出。
entries.en: Since the Zhongdu camp had been cut off the emperor and his ministers sat helpless in dread; the imperial guards were all in the north and no plan availed.
entries.literal: At that time, from after the Zhongdu camp was cut off, the Emperor and the great ministers sat upright in worry and peril; the state's guard troops were all in the north; no plan could be found.

entries.zh: 十六日聞滹水之降。
entries.en: On the sixteenth came word of the surrender at the Hutuo.
entries.literal: On the sixteenth they heard of the surrender at the Hutuo.

entries.zh: 是夜，偵知張彥澤已至滑州，召李崧、馮玉、李彥韜入內計事，方議詔河東劉知遠起兵赴難，至五鼓初，張彥澤引蕃騎入京。
entries.en: That night scouts reported Zhang Yanzhe at Huazhou; Li Song, Feng Yu, and Li Yantao were called in to deliberate and were debating an edict for Liu Zhiyuan of Hedong to march to the rescue when at the fifth watch Zhang Yanzhe led Khitan cavalry into the capital.
entries.literal: That night scouts learned Zhang Yanzhe had reached Huazhou; Li Song, Feng Yu, and Li Yantao were summoned within to plan; they were just discussing an edict for Liu Zhiyuan of Hedong to raise troops to the rescue when at the first watch of the fifth drum Zhang Yanzhe led barbarian cavalry into the capital.

entries.zh: 宮中相次火起，帝自攜劍驅擁后妃已下十數人，將同赴火，為親校薛超所持。
entries.en: Fires broke out across the palace; the emperor drew his sword and drove the empress, consorts, and a dozen attendants toward the flames to die with them, but his personal guard Xue Chao seized him.
entries.literal: Fires broke out one after another in the palace; the Emperor himself took a sword and drove the empress, consorts, and more than ten others below them, intending to enter the fire together; he was seized by his personal officer Xue Chao.

entries.zh: 俄自寬仁門遞入契丹主與皇太后書，帝乃止，旋令撲滅煙火。
entries.en: Soon a letter from the Khitan lord and the empress dowager was brought in at Kuanren Gate; the emperor desisted and ordered the fires put out.
entries.literal: Shortly a letter from the Khitan lord and the Empress Dowager was delivered in at Kuanren Gate; the Emperor then stopped, and immediately ordered the smoke and fire extinguished.

entries.zh: 大內都點檢康福全在寬仁門宿衛，登樓覘賊，彥澤呼而下之。
entries.en: Kang Fuquan, chief inspector of the inner palace, was on guard at Kuanren Gate; he climbed the tower to watch the enemy until Yanzhe called him down.
entries.literal: Kang Fuquan, chief inspector of the inner palace, was on night guard at Kuanren Gate; he mounted the tower to spy on the bandits; Yanzhe called him down.

entries.zh: 癸酉，帝奉表於戎主曰：
entries.en: On guiyou the emperor submitted a memorial to the Khitan lord, saying:
entries.literal: On guiyou the Emperor submitted a memorial to the barbarian lord, saying:

entries.zh: 明年正月朔，契丹主次東京城北。
entries.en: On New Year's Day of the following year the Khitan lord encamped north of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: On the new moon of the first month of the following year the Khitan lord halted north of the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 百官列班，遙辭帝於寺，詣北郊以迎契丹主。
entries.en: The officials formed ranks, bade the emperor farewell at the temple from afar, and went to the northern suburb to welcome the Khitan lord.
entries.literal: The hundred officials formed ranks, took leave of the Emperor at the temple from afar, and went to the northern suburb to welcome the Khitan lord.

entries.zh: 帝舉族出封丘門，肩轝至野，契丹主不與之見，遣泊封禪寺。
entries.en: The emperor and his clan went out Fengqiu Gate in litters to the open field; the Khitan lord refused to see them and had them lodged at Fengchan Temple.
entries.literal: The Emperor and his whole clan went out Fengqiu Gate, were carried on litters to the open field; the Khitan lord would not meet them and sent them to moor at Fengchan Temple.

entries.zh: 文武百官素服紗帽，迎謁契丹主於郊次，俯伏俟罪，契丹主命起之，親自慰撫。
entries.en: Civil and military officials in white dress and gauze caps met the Khitan lord in the suburbs, prostrated themselves to await judgment, and he ordered them up and consoled them in person.
entries.literal: Civil and military officials in plain dress and gauze caps welcomed and attended the Khitan lord at the suburban station, prostrated themselves awaiting punishment; the Khitan lord ordered them raised and personally consoled them.

entries.zh: 契丹主遂入大內，至昏出宮，是夜宿於赤堈。
entries.en: The Khitan lord then entered the inner palace, left at dusk, and that night lodged at Chikan.
entries.literal: The Khitan lord then entered the great inner palace; at dusk he left the palace; that night he lodged at Chikan.

entries.zh: 偽詔應晉朝臣僚一切仍舊，朝廷儀制並用漢禮。
entries.en: A puppet edict declared that Later Jin officials would remain in place and court ritual would follow Han practice.
entries.literal: A false edict responded that Jin dynasty officials were all to remain as before; court ritual and institutions were all to use Han rites.

entries.zh: 戊子，殺鄭州防禦使楊承勛，責以背父之罪，令左右臠割而死。
entries.en: On wuzi Yang Chengxun, defender of Zhengzhou, was executed for betraying his father and dismembered by the guards.
entries.literal: On wuzi Yang Chengxun, defender of Zhengzhou, was killed; charged with the crime of betraying his father, he was ordered dismembered by attendants until dead.

entries.zh: 〈（《遼史》：以其弟承信為平盧軍節度使，襲父爵。）〉
entries.en: (The History of Liao records that his younger brother Chengxin was made military governor of Pinglu and inherited their father's title.)〉
entries.literal: (History of Liao: his younger brother Chengxin was made military governor of Pinglu army and inherited his father's title.)〉

entries.zh: 己丑，斬張彥澤於市，以其剽劫京城，恣行屠害也。
entries.en: On jichou Zhang Yanzhe was beheaded in the market for plundering the capital and slaughtering at will.
entries.literal: On jichou Zhang Yanzhe was beheaded in the market, because he had plundered the capital and wantonly carried out slaughter.

entries.zh: 〈（《遼史》云：以張彥澤擅徙重貴開封，殺桑維翰，縱兵大掠，不道，斬於市。）〉
entries.en: (The History of Liao says Zhang Yanzhe was beheaded in the market for moving Chonggui to Kaifeng on his own authority, killing Sang Weihan, and letting his troops loot the city.)〉
entries.literal: (The History of Liao says: because Zhang Yanzhe on his own moved Chonggui to Kaifeng, killed Sang Weihan, and let his troops plunder greatly—unprincipled conduct—he was beheaded in the market.)〉

entries.zh: 庚寅，洛京留守景延廣自扼吭而死。
entries.en: On gengyin Jing Yanguang, military governor of Luoyang, killed himself by strangling.
entries.literal: On gengyin Jing Yanguang, military governor of the Luoyang capital, died by throttling his own throat.

entries.zh: 辛卯，契丹制，降帝為光祿大夫、檢校太尉，封負義侯，黃龍府安置。
entries.en: On xinmao the Khitans demoted the emperor to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Acting Grand Marshal, enfeoffed him as Marquis Who Bears Guilt, and sent him to Huanglong prefecture.
entries.literal: On xinmao by Khitan decree the demoted Emperor was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Acting Grand Marshal, enfeoffed as Marquis Who Bears Guilt, and settled at Huanglong prefecture.

entries.zh: 其地在渤海國界。
entries.en: That region lay on the border of the Bohai kingdom.
entries.literal: That place was on the border of the Bohai state.

entries.zh: 癸巳，遷帝於封禪寺，遣蕃大將崔廷勛將兵守之。
entries.en: On guisi the emperor was moved to Fengchan Temple under guard of the Khitan general Cui Tingxun and his troops.
entries.literal: On guisi the Emperor was moved to Fengchan Temple; the barbarian great general Cui Tingxun was sent with troops to guard him.

entries.zh: 癸卯，帝與皇太后李氏、皇太妃安氏、皇后馮氏、皇弟重睿、皇子延煦延寶俱北行，以宮嬪五十人、內官三十人、東西班五十人、醫官一人、控鶴官四人、禦廚七人、茶酒三人、儀鸞司三人、軍健二十人從行。
entries.en: On guimao the emperor went north with Empress Dowager Li, Grand Imperial Consort An, Empress Feng, his brother Chongrui, and Princes Yanxu and Yanbao, attended by fifty palace women, thirty eunuchs, fifty court attendants, a physician, four Crane-Control officers, seven imperial cooks, three tea and wine servants, three from the Ceremonial Parasol bureau, and twenty guards.
entries.literal: On guimao the Emperor with Empress Dowager Lady Li, Grand Imperial Consort Lady An, Empress Lady Feng, younger brother Chongrui, and princes Yanxu and Yanbao all went north together, with fifty palace women, thirty inner eunuchs, fifty eastern and western shift attendants, one medical officer, four Crane-Control officers, seven imperial kitchen staff, three tea and wine servants, three Ceremonial Parasol bureau staff, and twenty military guards accompanying.

entries.zh: 宰臣趙瑩、樞密使馮玉、侍衛馬軍都指揮使李彥韜隨帝入蕃，契丹主遣三百騎援送而去。
entries.en: Grand Counsellor Zhao Ying, Commissioner Feng Yu, and Li Yantao, commander of the Imperial Guard cavalry, accompanied the emperor into Khitan territory while the Khitan lord sent three hundred horsemen as escort.
