entries.literal: Grand Counsellor Zhao Ying, Commissioner Feng Yu, and Li Yantao, commander of the Imperial Guard horse army, followed the Emperor into the barbarians; the Khitan lord sent three hundred cavalry to escort and send them off.

entries.zh: 所經州郡，長吏迎奉，皆為契丹主阻絕，有所供饋亦不通。
entries.en: Wherever they passed local officials tried to welcome them, but the Khitan lord blocked every approach and no gifts could reach the party.
entries.literal: In every prefecture and commandery passed through, the chief officials came to welcome and attend, but all were blocked by the Khitan lord; any offerings they had could not get through.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·李穀傳》：少帝蒙塵而北，舊臣無敢候謁者，穀獨拜迎於路，君臣相對泣下。
entries.en: (Biography of Li Gu in the History of Song: when the Young Emperor was driven north in disgrace, former ministers dared not greet him; Gu alone bowed to him on the road, and ruler and subject wept together.
entries.literal: (Biography of Li Gu in the History of Song: when the Young Emperor suffered dust on the road north, old ministers dared not wait upon and attend him; Gu alone bowed and welcomed him on the road; ruler and subject faced each other and wept.

entries.zh: 穀曰：「臣無狀，負陛下。」
entries.en: Gu said, "I have disgraced myself and failed Your Majesty."
entries.literal: Gu said: "Your subject is without form, having failed Your Majesty."

entries.zh: 因傾囊以獻。）〉
entries.en: Then he emptied his purse and gave all he had.)〉
entries.literal: Thereupon he emptied his purse and presented it.)〉

entries.zh: 嘗一日，帝與太后不能得食，乃殺畜而啖之。
entries.en: One day the emperor and empress dowager could get no food and killed livestock to eat.
entries.literal: Once on a day the Emperor and Empress Dowager could not obtain food; they then killed livestock and ate it.

entries.zh: 帝過中渡橋，閱前杜威營寨之跡，慨然憤嘆，謂左右曰：「我家何負，為此賊所破，天乎！
entries.en: Crossing Zhongdu Bridge the emperor looked over Du Wei's old camp, sighed in rage, and said to his attendants, "What had my house done to be ruined by this traitor—O Heaven!
entries.literal: The Emperor passed Zhongdu Bridge, reviewed the traces of Du Wei's former camp, sighed in indignant lament, and told those beside him: "What fault has my house, that this bandit broke us—Heaven!

entries.zh: 天乎！」
entries.en: O Heaven!"
entries.literal: Heaven!"

entries.zh: 於是號慟而去。
entries.en: Then he wailed and went on.
entries.literal: Thereupon he wailed in grief and departed.

entries.zh: 至幽州，傾城士庶迎看於路，見帝慘沮，無不嗟嘆。
entries.en: At Youzhou the whole city turned out along the road; seeing the emperor's misery, everyone sighed.
entries.literal: Reaching Youzhou, the whole city's gentry and commoners came out on the road to look; seeing the Emperor's wretched dejection, none failed to sigh in lament.

entries.zh: 〈（《宣政雜錄》：徽宗北狩，經薊縣梁魚務，有還鄉橋，石少帝所命名也，里人至今呼之。）〉
entries.en: (Miscellaneous Records of Xuanzheng's Reign: when Huizong was taken north he passed Liangyu post in Jixian, where a Returning Home Bridge named by the Shi Young Emperor is still known by that name.)〉
entries.literal: (Miscellaneous Records of Xuanzheng's Reign: when Huizong went north on the hunt, passing Liangyu post in Jixian, there was a Returning Home Bridge, named by the Young Emperor of Shi; villagers to this day call it so.)〉

entries.zh: 駐留旬餘，州將承契丹命，犒帝於府署，趙延壽母以食饌來獻。
entries.en: After more than ten days' halt the prefect, on Khitan orders, entertained the emperor at the prefectural offices, and Zhao Yanshou's mother brought food.
entries.literal: They halted more than ten days; the prefectural commander, on Khitan orders, entertained the Emperor at the prefecture office; Zhao Yanshou's mother came to present food.

entries.zh: 自范陽行數十程，過薊州、平州，至榆關沙塞之地，略無供給，每至宿頓，無非路次，一行乏食，宮女、從官但采木實野蔬，以救饑弊。
entries.en: From Fanyang they marched dozens of stages through Jizhou and Pingzhou to the sandy frontier at Yuguan with almost no supplies; each night they camped by the road, and palace women and attendants gathered wild fruit and greens to stave off starvation.
entries.literal: From Fanyang they traveled several tens of stages, passed Jizhou and Pingzhou, reached the sandy frontier at Yuguan; supplies were nearly absent; whenever they halted for the night it was always by the roadside; the whole party lacked food; palace women and attendants only gathered tree fruit and wild vegetables to relieve hunger and exhaustion.

entries.zh: 又行七八日至錦州，契丹迫帝與妃後往拜安巴堅遺像，帝不勝屈辱，泣曰：「薛超誤我，不令我死，以至今日也。」
entries.en: Seven or eight days later at Jinzhou the Khitans forced the emperor and his consorts to bow before Ambaqan's portrait; overcome with shame he wept, "Xue Chao was wrong to keep me from death and bring me to this day."
entries.literal: After another seven or eight days they reached Jinzhou; the Khitans forced the Emperor and consorts to go pay respects to Ambaqan's portrait; the Emperor could not bear the humiliation and wept: "Xue Chao wronged me, not letting me die, until today."

entries.zh: 又行數十程，渡遼水，至黃龍府，即此所命安置之地也。
entries.en: After many more stages they crossed the Liao and reached Huanglong prefecture, the place where he had been ordered to live.
entries.literal: After another several tens of stages they crossed the Liao River and reached Huanglong prefecture—this was the place appointed for their settlement.

entries.zh: 開運三年冬十月甲子，正衙命使冊皇太妃安氏。
entries.en: In winter of Kaiyun 3, on the jiazi day of the tenth month, imperial envoys in full court regalia were sent to invest Grand Imperial Consort Lady An.
entries.literal: In Kaiyun 3, winter, tenth month, jiazi: court envoys in imperial accoutrements were commissioned to invest Grand Imperial Consort Lady An.

entries.zh: 己丑，以樞密直學士、禮部侍郎邊光範為翰林學士，以給事中邊歸讜為左散騎常侍，以翰林學士、祠部員外郎、知制誥張沆為右諫議大夫。
entries.en: On jichou Bian Guangfan, direct academician at the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Minister of Rites, became Hanlin academician; Bian Guiqian, Secretariat drafter, became Left Regular Attendant-in-Attendance; and Zhang Hong, Hanlin academician, outer-section vice director of the Bureau of Rites with charge of edicts, became Right Remonstrance Officer.
entries.literal: On jichou Bian Guangfan, direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Minister of Rites, was made Hanlin academician; Bian Guiqian, Secretariat drafter, was made Left Regular Attendant-in-Attendance; Zhang Hong, Hanlin academician, outer-section vice director of the Bureau of Rites with charge of edicts, was made Right Remonstrance Officer.

entries.zh: 辛未，以鄴都留守杜威為北面行營都招討使，以侍衛親軍都指揮使、鄆州節度使李守貞為兵馬都監，兗州安審琦為左右廂都指揮使，徐州符彥卿為馬軍左廂都指揮使，滑州皇甫遇為馬軍右廂都指揮使，貝州梁漢璋為馬軍都排陣使，前鄧州宋彥筠為步軍左廂都指揮使，奉國左廂都指揮使王饒為步軍右廂都指揮使，洺州團練使薛懷讓為先鋒都指揮使。
entries.en: On xinwei Du Wei, military governor of Yedu, was appointed overall commander of the northern field army; Li Shouzhen, commander of the Imperial Guard and military governor of Yunzhou, became overall supervisor of troops and horses; An Shenqi of Yanzhou commanded both wings; Fu Yanqing of Xuzhou the left wing of cavalry; Huangfu Yu of Huazhou the right wing of cavalry; Liang Hanzhang of Beizhou marshal of the cavalry array; Song Yanyun, former prefect of Dengzhou, the left wing of infantry; Wang Rao of the Fengguo left wing the right wing of infantry; and Xue Huairang, regimental trainer of Mozhou, vanguard commander.
entries.literal: On xinwei Du Wei, military governor of Yedu, was made overall commander of the Northern Circuit field headquarters; Li Shouzhen, commander of the Imperial Guard and military governor of Yanzhou, was made overall supervisor of troops and horses; An Shenqi of Yanzhou was made commander of both wings; Fu Yanqing of Xuzhou was made commander of the left wing of the horse army; Huangfu Yu of Huazhou was made commander of the right wing of the horse army; Liang Hanzhang of Beizhou was made marshal of the horse army array; Song Yanyun, former prefect of Dengzhou, was made commander of the left wing of the foot army; Wang Rao, commander of the left wing of the Fengguo army, was made commander of the right wing of the foot army; Xue Huairang, regimental trainer of Mozhou, was made vanguard commander.

entries.zh: 〈（案：《通鑒》載，當時敕榜曰：「先取瀛、鄚，安定關南；
entries.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror records that the edict placard then read: "First take Ying and Mo and secure the region south of the passes;
entries.literal: (Note: The Comprehensive Mirror records that the edict placard at the time read: "First take Ying and Mo and secure the south of the passes;

entries.zh: 次復幽、燕，蕩平塞北。」
entries.en: then recover You and Yan and sweep the northern frontier clear."
entries.literal: next recover You and Yan and sweep the northern frontier."

entries.zh: 蓋狃於陽城之役而驟驕也。）〉
entries.en: They had grown overconfident after clinging to the victory at Yangcheng.)〉
entries.literal: This was because they clung to the victory at Yangcheng and suddenly grew arrogant.)〉

entries.zh: 癸酉，冊吳國夫人馮氏為皇后。
entries.en: On guiyou Lady Feng of Wu was invested as empress.
entries.literal: On guiyou Lady Feng of Wu state was invested as empress.

entries.zh: 乙亥，以侍衛馬軍都指揮使李彥韜權知侍衛司事。
entries.en: On yihai Li Yantao, commander of the Imperial Guard cavalry, was placed in acting charge of the Imperial Guard bureau.
entries.literal: On yihai Li Yantao, commander of the Imperial Guard horse army, was made acting head of the Imperial Guard bureau.

entries.zh: 丙戌，鳳翔節度使秦王李從嚴薨，輟朝，冊贈尚書令。
entries.en: On bingxu Li Congyan, Prince of Qin and military governor of Fengxiang, died; court was suspended; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: On bingxu Li Congyan, Prince of Qin and military governor of Fengxiang, died; court audiences were suspended; posthumously he was enfeoffed as Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 丁亥，邠州節度使李德充卒，輟朝，贈太尉。
entries.en: On dinghai Li Dechong, military governor of Binzhou, died; court was suspended; he was posthumously made Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: On dinghai Li Dechong, military governor of Binzhou, died; court audiences were suspended; he was posthumously made Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 高祖皇后李氏。
entries.en: Empress Li of Gaozu.
entries.literal: Empress Li of Gaozu.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：高祖皇后李氏，唐明宗第三女。
entries.en: (From the Five Dynasties Essentials: Empress Li of Gaozu was the third daughter of Mingzong of Tang.
entries.literal: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》: Empress Li of Gaozu was Mingzong of Tang's third daughter.

entries.zh: 天成三年四月，封永寧公主；
entries.en: In the fourth month of Tiancheng 3 she was enfeoffed as Princess of Yongning;
entries.literal: In the fourth month of Tiancheng 3, she was enfeoffed as Princess of Yongning;

entries.zh: 長興四年九月，進封魏國公主；
entries.en: In the ninth month of Changxing 4 she was advanced to Princess of Wei;
entries.literal: In the ninth month of Changxing 4, she was advanced to Princess of Wei;

entries.zh: 清泰二年九月，改封晉國長公主；
entries.en: In the ninth month of Qingtai 2 she was restyled Senior Princess of Jin;
entries.literal: In the ninth month of Qingtai 2, she was changed to Princess of Jin;

entries.zh: 至天福六年十一月，尊為皇后；
entries.en: By the eleventh month of Tianfu 6 she was honored as empress;
entries.literal: By the eleventh month of Tianfu 6, she was honored as empress;

entries.zh: 七年六月，尊為皇太后。
entries.en: In the sixth month of the seventh year she was honored as empress dowager.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year, she was honored as empress dowager.

entries.zh: 開運四年三月，與少帝同遷於契丹之黃龍府。
entries.en: In the third month of Kaiyun 4 she was relocated with the Young Emperor to the Khitan seat at Yellow Dragon Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the third month of Kaiyun 4, she was moved together with the Young Emperor to the Khitan Yellow Dragon Prefecture.

entries.zh: 漢乾祐三年八月二十五日，崩於蕃中之建丘。
entries.en: On the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month of Qianyou 3 of Han she died at Jianqiu in the Khitan territories.
entries.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month of Qianyou 3 of Han, she died at Jianqiu in the barbarian lands.

entries.zh: 《文獻通考》云：天福二年，有司請立皇后，帝以宗廟未立，謙抑未遑。
entries.en: The Comprehensive Examination of Documents records that in Tianfu 2 the officials asked that an empress be installed, but the emperor, because the ancestral temple had not yet been established, modestly put the matter aside.
entries.literal: The 《Comprehensive Examination of Documents》 says: In Tianfu 2, the officials requested that an empress be installed; the emperor, because the ancestral temple had not yet been established, modestly deferred and had no leisure for it.

entries.zh: 帝崩，出帝即位，乃尊為皇太后。
entries.en: Only after the emperor's death, when the Deposed Emperor took the throne, was she honored as empress dowager.
entries.literal: When the emperor died and the Deposed Emperor acceded, only then was she honored as empress dowager.

entries.zh: 《契丹國志》載晉出帝降表云：「晉室皇太后媳婦李氏妾言：張彥澤、傅住兒等至，伏蒙皇帝阿翁降書安撫者。
entries.en: The Khitan State Annals preserves the Deposed Emperor of Jin's surrender memorial, which reads: "The daughter-in-law of the Jin imperial house, Empress Dowager Lady Li, your handmaid, says: When Zhang Yanze, Fu Zhu'er, and the others arrived, I prostrated myself and received Your Majesty the Emperor and Grandfather's gracious letter of reassurance.
entries.literal: The 《Khitan State Annals》 records the surrender memorial of the Deposed Emperor of Jin, which says: "The daughter-in-law of the Jin imperial household, empress dowager Lady Li, your handmaid, says: When Zhang Yanze, Fu Zhu'er, and the others arrived, I prostrated myself and received Your Majesty the Emperor and Grandfather's descending letter of reassurance.

entries.zh: 妾伏念先皇帝頃在並、汾，適逢屯難，危同累卵，急若倒懸，智勇俱窮，朝夕不保。
entries.en: Your handmaid humbly recalls that when the late emperor was at Bing and Fen, he suddenly met with encirclement and disaster; danger was as fragile as a pile of eggs, urgency as desperate as a man hung upside down; wisdom and courage were both spent, and from morning to evening he could not be preserved.
entries.literal: Your handmaid humbly recalls that when the late emperor was recently at Bing and Fen, he suddenly met with encirclement and hardship; danger was like a pile of eggs; urgency was like a man hung upside down; wisdom and courage were both exhausted; morning and evening he could not be preserved.

entries.zh: 皇帝阿翁發自冀北，親抵河東，跋履山川，逾越險阻，立平巨孽，遂定中原。
entries.en: Your Majesty the Emperor and Grandfather set out from north of Ji, came in person to Hedong, tramped through mountains and rivers and crossed perilous passes, swiftly pacified the great rebel, and thus settled the Central Plain.
entries.literal: Your Majesty the Emperor and Grandfather set out from north of Ji, personally reached Hedong, trampled through mountains and rivers, crossed dangerous barriers, quickly pacified the great rebel, and thus settled the Central Plain.

entries.zh: 救石氏之覆亡，立晉朝之社稷。
entries.en: He rescued the Shi clan from ruin and restored the altars of the Jin dynasty.
entries.literal: He rescued the Shi clan from overthrow and established the altars of the Jin court.

entries.zh: 不幸先帝厭代，嗣子承祧，不能繼好息民，而反虧恩辜義，兵戈屢動，駟馬難追，戚實自貽，咎將誰執。
entries.en: Unfortunately the late emperor passed away; the heir received the ancestral line yet could not continue friendship and give the people rest, but instead violated kindness and betrayed righteousness; war was raised again and again, and what four horses could not overtake was truly sorrow of our own making — upon whom shall the blame fall?
entries.literal: Unfortunately the late emperor passed from the world; the heir received the ancestral line; he could not continue friendship and rest the people, but on the contrary violated kindness and betrayed righteousness; war was raised repeatedly; four horses could not be recalled; the sorrow was truly self-inflicted — upon whom shall the blame be laid?

entries.zh: 今穹旻震怒，中外攜離，上將牽羊，六師解甲。
entries.en: Now Heaven above is enraged, the court and the realm are torn apart, the sovereign above will lead the sheep in surrender, and the six armies have laid down their arms.
entries.literal: Now Heaven above is angry; inside and outside are divided; the emperor above will lead the sheep; the six armies lay down their armor.

entries.zh: 妾舉宗負釁，視景偷生。
entries.en: Your handmaid, with the whole clan bearing guilt, clings to life while watching our own shadows.
entries.literal: Your handmaid, with the whole clan, bears punishment; looking at our shadow, we steal life.

entries.zh: 惶惑之中，撫問斯至，明宣恩旨，曲賜含容，慰諭丁寧，神爽飛越。
entries.en: Amid bewilderment your inquiry arrived; your gracious edict was clearly proclaimed; you bent favor to grant forbearance and repeated your comfort and instruction with such care that my spirit soared in exultation.
entries.literal: In bewilderment, your inquiry arrived; your gracious edict was clearly proclaimed; favor was bent to grant forbearance; comfort and instruction were repeated with care; the spirit soared in exultation.

entries.zh: 豈謂已垂之命，忽蒙更生之恩，省罪責躬，九死未報。
entries.en: Who would have thought that a life already hanging by a thread would suddenly receive the grace of rebirth? Reflecting on my guilt and blaming myself, even nine deaths would not repay it.
entries.literal: Who would have thought that a life already hanging would suddenly receive the grace of rebirth? Reflecting on guilt and blaming myself, nine deaths would not repay it.

entries.zh: 今遣孫男延煦、延寶奉表請罪，陳謝以聞。」
entries.en: Now I send my grandsons Yanxu and Yanbao to present this memorial begging forgiveness and to declare my apology for your hearing."
entries.literal: Now I send my grandsons Yanxu and Yanbao to present this memorial begging forgiveness, to declare my apology and report it."

entries.zh: 又，《帝紀》云：會同十一年正月朔，出帝、太后迎遼帝於封丘門外，帝辭不見，館於封禪寺，遣其將崔廷勛以兵守之。
entries.en: The Imperial Annals also records that on the new moon of the first month in the eleventh year of Tonghui, the Deposed Emperor and the empress dowager welcomed the Liao emperor outside the Fengqiu Gate; the emperor declined to see them, lodged them at the Fengchan Temple, and dispatched his general Cui Tingxun with troops to guard them.
entries.literal: Also, the 《Imperial Annals》 says: On the first day of the first month of the eleventh year of Tonghui, the Deposed Emperor and the empress dowager welcomed the Liao emperor outside the Fengqiu Gate; the emperor declined to see them and lodged them at the Fengchan Temple, dispatching his general Cui Tingxun with troops to guard them.

entries.zh: 是時雨雪連旬，外無供億，上下凍餒。
entries.en: At that time snow and rain lasted ten days in succession; there were no supplies from outside, and those above and below were freezing and starving.
entries.literal: At that time snow and rain continued for ten days; outside there were no supplies; above and below were freezing and starving.

entries.zh: 太后使人謂寺僧曰：「吾嘗於此飯僧數萬，今日豈不相憫耶？」
entries.en: The empress dowager sent someone to tell the temple monks: "I once fed tens of thousands of monks here — are you not moved to pity us today?"
entries.literal: The empress dowager sent someone to tell the temple monks: "I once fed tens of thousands of monks here — today are you not moved to pity?"

entries.zh: 僧辭以遼帝之意難測，不敢獻食。
entries.en: The monks refused, citing the unpredictable mood of the Liao emperor, and dared not provide food.
entries.literal: The monks declined, citing the Liao emperor's unpredictable intent, and dared not present food.

entries.zh: 少帝陰祈守者，乃稍得食。
entries.en: The Young Emperor secretly appealed to the guards, and so they were gradually able to get food.
entries.literal: The Young Emperor secretly prayed to the guards, and only then were they gradually able to obtain food.

entries.zh: 遼降少帝為光祿大夫，檢校太尉，封負義侯，遷於黃龍府，即慕容氏和龍城也。
entries.en: The Liao demoted the Young Emperor to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Inspector-General Grand Marshal, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Unrighteousness, and relocated him to Yellow Dragon Prefecture — the Murong clan's Helong City.
entries.literal: The Liao demoted the Young Emperor to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, made him Inspector-General Grand Marshal, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Unrighteousness, and moved him to Yellow Dragon Prefecture — that is, the Murong clan's Helong City.

entries.zh: 帝使人謂太后曰：「吾聞爾子重貴，不從母教而至於此，可求自便，勿與俱行。」
entries.en: The emperor sent someone to tell the empress dowager: "I hear your son Chonggui did not heed his mother's teaching and came to this — you may seek your own convenience; do not travel with him."
entries.literal: The emperor sent someone to tell the empress dowager: "I hear your son Chonggui did not obey his mother's teaching and came to this — you may seek your own convenience; do not travel together with him."

entries.zh: 太后答曰：「重貴事妾謹慎，所失者違先君之志，絕兩國之歡。
entries.en: The empress dowager replied: "Chonggui has served me with care; what was lost was going against the late sovereign's will and severing friendship between our two states.
entries.literal: The empress dowager replied: "Chonggui has been careful toward me in his service; what was lost was going against the late lord's will and severing friendship between the two states.

entries.zh: 然重貴此去，幸蒙大惠，全身保家，母不隨子，欲何所歸？」
entries.en: Yet if Chonggui goes hence, fortunately receiving great kindness and preserving body and house — if a mother does not follow her son, whither would she go?"
entries.literal: Yet if Chonggui goes hence, fortunately receiving great kindness, preserving body and house — if a mother does not follow her son, whither would she go?"

entries.zh: 於是太后與馮氏、皇弟重睿。
entries.en: Thereupon the empress dowager, Lady Feng, and the emperor's younger brother Chongrui
entries.literal: Thereupon the empress dowager, together with Lady Feng and the emperor's younger brother Chongrui

entries.zh: 子延煦延寶，舉族從晉侯而北。
entries.en: together with the sons Yanxu and Yanbao, the whole clan followed the Marquis of Jin northward.
entries.literal: along with her sons Yanxu and Yanbao, the whole clan followed the Marquis of Jin northward.

entries.zh: 天祿元年四月，帝至遼陽，晉侯白衣紗帽與太后、皇后上謁於帳中。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Tianlu the emperor reached Liaoyang; the Marquis of Jin, in white robes and gauze cap, together with the empress dowager and empress, paid homage inside the tent.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Tianlu, the emperor reached Liaoyang; the Marquis of Jin, in white robes and gauze cap, together with the empress dowager and empress, paid homage inside the tent.

entries.zh: 五月，帝上陘，取晉侯所從宦者十五人、東西班十五人及皇子延煦而去。
entries.en: In the fifth month, as the emperor ascended the pass, he took fifteen of the Marquis of Jin's attendants, fifteen men from the eastern and western shifts, and the imperial son Yanxu.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, as the emperor ascended the pass, he took fifteen of the attendants who followed the Marquis of Jin, fifteen men from the eastern and western shifts, and the imperial son Yanxu, and departed.

entries.zh: 八月，帝下陘，太后自馳至霸州謁帝，求於漢兒城側賜地耕牧以為生。
entries.en: In the eighth month, as the emperor descended the pass, the empress dowager rode in haste to Bazhou to pay homage, asking for land beside Hanz Er City to farm and herd for a living.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, as the emperor descended the pass, the empress dowager rode in haste to Bazhou to pay homage, asking that land beside Hanz Er City be granted to farm and herd for a living.

entries.zh: 許之。
entries.en: Permission was granted.
entries.literal: He granted it.

entries.zh: 帝以太后自行十餘日，遣與延煦俱還遼陽。
entries.en: After the empress dowager had traveled on her own for more than ten days, the emperor sent her back to Liaoyang with Yanxu.
entries.literal: Because the empress dowager had traveled on her own for more than ten days, the emperor sent her back to Liaoyang together with Yanxu.

entries.zh: 二年，徙晉侯、太后於建州。
entries.en: In the second year, the Marquis of Jin and the empress dowager were relocated to Jianzhou.
entries.literal: In the second year, the Marquis of Jin and the empress dowager were moved to Jianzhou.

entries.zh: 三年秋八月，晉李太后病，無醫藥，仰天號泣，戟手罵杜重威、李守貞曰：「吾死不置汝。」
entries.en: In the eighth month of autumn of the third year Empress Li of Jin fell ill; there were no medicines; she wept to Heaven and, pointing with her hand, cursed Du Chongwei and Li Shouzhen, saying: "When I die I will not let you go."
entries.literal: In the eighth month of autumn of the third year, Empress Li of Jin fell ill; there were no medicine or drugs; she wept to Heaven and, pointing with her hand, cursed Du Chongwei and Li Shouzhen, saying: "When I die I will not leave you in peace."

entries.zh: 病亟，謂晉侯曰：「吾死，焚其骨送范陽佛寺，無使吾為邊地鬼也。」）〉
entries.en: As her illness became critical, she told the Marquis of Jin: "When I die, burn my bones and send them to a Buddhist monastery in Fanyang — do not let me become a ghost of the borderlands." )〉
entries.literal: As her illness became critical, she told the Marquis of Jin: "When I die, burn my bones and send them to a Buddhist monastery in Fanyang — do not let me become a ghost of the borderlands." )〉

entries.zh: 少帝皇后張氏。
entries.en: Empress Zhang of the Young Emperor.
entries.literal: Empress Zhang of the Young Emperor.

entries.zh: 〈（案《五代會要》：天福八年十月追冊。
entries.en: (Note: According to the Five Dynasties Essentials, posthumous investiture came in the tenth month of Tianfu 8.
entries.literal: (Note: The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》: In the tenth month of Tianfu 8, posthumous investiture.

entries.zh: 考薛史《少帝紀》云：追冊故妃張氏為皇后。
entries.en: According to Xue's History, Annals of the Young Emperor, the late consort Lady Zhang was posthumously invested as empress.
entries.literal: Examining Xue's History, 《Annals of the Young Emperor》, it says: posthumously invested the late consort Lady Zhang as empress.

entries.zh: 《張從訓傳》亦云，高祖鎮太原，為少帝娶從訓長女為妃。）〉
entries.en: The Biography of Zhang Congxun also records that when Gaozu was posted at Taiyuan, he took Congxun's eldest daughter as consort for the Young Emperor.)〉
entries.literal: The 《Biography of Zhang Congxun》 also says: when Gaozu was posted at Taiyuan, he took Congxun's eldest daughter as consort for the Young Emperor.)〉

entries.zh: 皇后馮氏。
entries.en: Empress Feng.
entries.literal: Empress Feng.

entries.zh: 〈（案《五代會要》：開運三年十月冊。
entries.en: (Note: According to the Five Dynasties Essentials, investiture took place in the tenth month of Kaiyun 3.
entries.literal: (Note: The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》: Investiture in the tenth month of Kaiyun 3.

entries.zh: 《通鑒》云：天福八年冬十月戊申，立吳國夫人馮氏為皇后。
entries.en: The Comprehensive Mirror records that on wushen of the tenth month of winter in Tianfu 8, Lady Feng, Madame of Wu, was installed as empress.
entries.literal: The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: On wushen of the tenth month of winter in Tianfu 8, Lady Feng, Madame of Wu, was installed as empress.

entries.zh: 初，高祖愛少弟重胤，養以為子。
entries.en: At first Gaozu loved his youngest brother Chongyin and raised him as his own son.
entries.literal: At first Gaozu loved his youngest brother Chongyin and raised him as a son.

entries.zh: 及留守鄴都，娶副留守馮濛女為其婦，重胤早卒，馮夫人寡居，有美色，帝見而悅之。
entries.en: When he was left to garrison Yedu, he took the daughter of Vice Resident Feng Meng as wife for him; Chongyin died early; Madame Feng lived as a widow and was beautiful; the emperor saw her and was pleased with her.
entries.literal: When he was left to garrison Yedu, he took the daughter of Vice Resident Feng Meng as wife for him; Chongyin died early; Madame Feng lived as a widow; she had beautiful looks; the emperor saw her and was pleased with her.

entries.zh: 高祖崩，梓宮在殯，帝遂納之。
entries.en: While Gaozu's coffin still lay in state, the emperor took her as his consort.
entries.literal: When Gaozu died, while the coffin still lay in state, the emperor took her in.

entries.zh: 群臣皆賀，帝謂馮道等曰：「皇太后之命，與卿等不任大慶。」
entries.en: All the officials congratulated him; the emperor said to Feng Dao and the others: "By the empress dowager's command, you cannot bear the burden of grand celebration either."
entries.literal: All the officials congratulated him; the emperor said to Feng Dao and the others: "By the empress dowager's command, you and the others cannot bear the burden of grand celebration."

entries.zh: 群臣出，帝與夫人酣飲，過梓宮前，叕而告曰：「皇太后之命，與先帝不任大慶。」
entries.en: When the officials had gone out, the emperor drank heavily with the lady. Passing before the imperial coffin, he bowed twice and announced: "By the empress dowager's command, my late father cannot bear the burden of grand celebration either."
entries.literal: When the officials had gone out, the emperor drank heavily with the lady; passing before the imperial coffin, he bowed twice and announced: "By the empress dowager's command, my late father cannot bear the burden of grand celebration either."

entries.zh: 左右失笑，帝亦自笑，謂左右曰：「我今日作新婿何如？」
entries.en: Those beside him could not hold back laughter; the emperor laughed too and asked those around him: "How do I look as a new bridegroom today?"
entries.literal: Those beside him could not hold back laughter; the emperor laughed too and asked those around him: "How do I look as a new bridegroom today?"

entries.zh: 夫人與左右皆大笑。
entries.en: The lady and those beside him all laughed heartily.
entries.literal: The lady and those beside him all laughed greatly.

entries.zh: 太后雖恚，而無如之何。
entries.en: The empress dowager, though resentful, could do nothing about it.
entries.literal: The empress dowager, though resentful, could do nothing about it.

entries.zh: 既正位中宮，頗預政事。
entries.en: Once established in the central palace, she took a considerable part in government affairs.
entries.literal: Once she was established in the central palace, she took part in government affairs to a considerable degree.

entries.zh: 後兄玉，時為禮部郎中、鹽鐵判官，帝驟擢用至端明殿學士、戶部侍郎，與議政事。
entries.en: Her elder brother Yu, then a director in the Ministry of Rites and salt and iron commissioner, was suddenly promoted to Academician of the Hall of Duanming and Vice Minister of Revenue and given a voice in government affairs.
entries.literal: Her elder brother Yu, then a director in the Ministry of Rites and salt and iron commissioner, was suddenly promoted to Academician of the Hall of Duanming and Vice Minister of Revenue and given a voice in government affairs.

entries.zh: 《文獻通考》云：契丹入京師，後隨帝北遷，不知所終。
entries.en: The Comprehensive Examination of Documents records that when the Khitan entered the capital, the empress followed the emperor northward; her end is unknown.
entries.literal: The 《Comprehensive Examination of Documents》 says: When the Khitan entered the capital, the empress followed the emperor northward; her end is unknown.

entries.zh: 又，案《五代會要》載晉內職云：高祖潁川郡夫人蔡氏，天福三年八月敕。
entries.en: Also, (Note: The Five Dynasties Essentials records Jin inner offices: Lady Cai, Madame of Yingchuan Commandery — by edict of the eighth month of Tianfu 3.
entries.literal: Also, (Note: The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 records Jin inner offices: Lady Cai, Madame of Yingchuan Commandery — edict of the eighth month of Tianfu 3.

entries.zh: 少帝寶省李氏封隴西郡夫人；
entries.en: Lady Li of the Young Emperor's Baosheng Palace was enfeoffed as Madame of Longxi Commandery;
entries.literal: Lady Li of the Young Emperor's Baosheng Palace was enfeoffed as Madame of Longxi Commandery;

entries.zh: 張氏封春宮夫人，充皇后宮尚宮，並天福八年十二月二日敕。
entries.en: Lady Zhang was enfeoffed as Madame of the Spring Palace and appointed Chief Palace Officer of the empress's palace — both by edict of the second day of the twelfth month of Tianfu 8.
entries.literal: Lady Zhang was enfeoffed as Madame of the Spring Palace, serving as Chief Palace Officer of the empress's palace — both by edict of the second day of the twelfth month of Tianfu 8.

entries.zh: 前左禦正齊國夫人吳氏進封燕國夫人，書省魏國夫人崔氏進封梁國夫人，前右禦正天水郡夫人趙氏封衛國夫人，司簿孟氏封汧國夫人，前司簿李氏封隴西郡夫人，弟子院使齊氏、大使郭氏、副使賈氏並封本縣君，太后宮尚宮陳留郡夫人何氏進封鄭國夫人，河南郡夫人元氏進封齊國夫人，知客出使夫人石氏封武威郡夫人，春宮姚氏、常氏、焦氏、王氏、陶氏、魏氏、趙氏七人並超封郡夫人，寶省婉美趙氏封天水郡夫人，武氏以下十一人並授春宮，天福八年十一月敕。
entries.en: Former Left Imperial Rectifier Madame Wu of Qi was advanced to Madame of Yan; Secretariat Madame Cui of Wei was advanced to Madame of Liang; Former Right Imperial Rectifier Madame Zhao of Tianshui Commandery was enfeoffed Madame of Wei; Registrar Madame Meng was enfeoffed Madame of Qian; Former Registrar Madame Li was enfeoffed Madame of Longxi Commandery; Palace of Disciples Commissioner Qi, Grand Commissioner Guo, and Vice Commissioner Jia were all enfeoffed as Ladies of their native counties; Chief Palace Officer of the empress dowager's palace Madame He of Chenliu Commandery was advanced to Madame of Zheng; Madame Yuan of Henan Commandery was advanced to Madame of Qi; Guest Reception Envoy Madame Shi was enfeoffed Madame of Wuwei Commandery; Spring Palace ladies Yao, Chang, Jiao, Wang, Tao, Wei, and Zhao — seven in all — were exceptionally enfeoffed as Commandery Madames; Graceful Beauty Madame Zhao of the Baosheng Palace was enfeoffed Madame of Tianshui Commandery; Wu and eleven below were all appointed to the Spring Palace — by edict of the eleventh month of Tianfu 8.
entries.literal: Former Left Imperial Rectifier, Madame Wu of Qi, was advanced to Madame of Yan; Secretariat Madame Cui of Wei was advanced to Madame of Liang; Former Right Imperial Rectifier, Madame Zhao of Tianshui Commandery, was enfeoffed Madame of Wei; Registrar Madame Meng was enfeoffed Madame of Qian; Former Registrar Madame Li was enfeoffed Madame of Longxi Commandery; Palace of Disciples Commissioner Qi, Grand Commissioner Guo, and Vice Commissioner Jia were all enfeoffed as Ladies of their native counties; Chief Palace Officer of the empress dowager's palace, Madame He of Chenliu Commandery, was advanced to Madame of Zheng; Madame Yuan of Henan Commandery was advanced to Madame of Qi; Guest Reception Envoy Madame Shi was enfeoffed Madame of Wuwei Commandery; the Spring Palace ladies Yao, Chang, Jiao, Wang, Tao, Wei, and Zhao — seven persons — were all exceptionally enfeoffed as Commandery Madames; Graceful Beauty Madame Zhao of the Baosheng Palace was enfeoffed Madame of Tianshui Commandery; Wu and eleven below were all appointed to the Spring Palace — edict of the eleventh month of Tianfu 8.

entries.zh: 清河郡夫人張氏、彭城郡夫人劉氏並充太后宮司寶，南陽郡夫人路氏、出使夫人趙氏白氏並充皇后宮司賓，開運二年八月敕。
entries.en: Lady Zhang of Qinghe Commandery and Lady Liu of Pengcheng Commandery were appointed keepers of the treasury in the empress dowager's palace; Lady Lu of Nanyang Commandery and Envoy Ladies Zhao and Bai were appointed reception keepers in the empress's palace — by edict of the eighth month of the second year of Kaiyun.
entries.literal: Madame Zhang of Qinghe Commandery and Madame Liu of Pengcheng Commandery were both appointed keepers of the treasury in the empress dowager's palace; Madame Lu of Nanyang Commandery and Envoy Ladies Zhao and Bai were both appointed reception keepers in the empress's palace — edict of the eighth month of the second year of Kaiyun.

entries.zh: 又，按《薛史》不載外戚傳，據《五代會要》云：晉高祖長女長安公主降楊承祚，天福二年五月封，至六年五月卒，追封秦國公主，至七年九月，又追封梁國長公主。
entries.en: Also, examining Xue's History, it includes no biography of maternal relatives; according to the Five Dynasties Essentials, Gaozu's eldest daughter, Princess of Chang'an, was married to Yang Chengzuo; she was enfeoffed in the fifth month of Tianfu 2, died in the fifth month of the sixth year, was posthumously enfeoffed Princess of Qin, and in the ninth month of the seventh year was again posthumously enfeoffed Princess of Liang.
entries.literal: Also, examining the 《History of Xue》, it does not include a biography of maternal relatives; according to the 《Five Dynasties Essentials》, it says: Gaozu's eldest daughter, Princess of Chang'an, was married to Yang Chengzuo; enfeoffed in the fifth month of Tianfu 2; died in the fifth month of the sixth year; posthumously enfeoffed Princess of Qin; by the ninth month of the seventh year, again posthumously enfeoffed Princess of Liang.

entries.zh: 從長女高平縣主、第二女新平縣主、第三女千乘縣主、孫女永慶縣主，並天福七年五月封。）〉
entries.en: The eldest daughter of the secondary wife was enfeoffed Lady of Gaoping County; the second daughter, Lady of Xinping County; the third daughter, Lady of Qiansheng County; and the granddaughters, Ladies of Yongqing County — all in the fifth month of Tianfu 7.)〉
entries.literal: Eldest daughter of the secondary wife, Lady of Gaoping County; second daughter, Lady of Xinping County; third daughter, Lady of Qiansheng County; granddaughters, Ladies of Yongqing County — all enfeoffed in the fifth month of Tianfu 7.)〉

entries.zh: 太妃安氏。
entries.en: Grand Consort An.
entries.literal: Grand Consort An.

entries.zh: 〈（《文獻通考》：安太妃，代北人，不知其世家。
entries.en: (From the Comprehensive Examination of Documents: Grand Consort An was a native of northern Dai; her family background is unknown.
entries.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Examination of Documents》: Grand Consort An was a native of northern Dai; her lineage is unknown.

entries.zh: 生出帝，帝立，尊為皇太妃。
entries.en: She bore the Deposed Emperor; when he took the throne, she was honored as Grand Imperial Consort.
entries.literal: She bore the Deposed Emperor; when he was enthroned, she was honored as Grand Imperial Consort.

entries.zh: 《契丹國志》云：天祿二年春二月，徙晉侯、太后於建州，中途安太妃卒，遺命晉侯曰：「焚骨為灰，南向揚之，庶幾遺魂得返中國也。」）〉
entries.en: The Khitan State Annals records that in the second month of spring of the second year of Tianlu, when the Marquis of Jin and the empress dowager were relocated to Jianzhou, Grand Consort An died en route; her dying charge to the Marquis of Jin was: "Burn my bones to ash and scatter them southward — perhaps my lingering soul may return to China.")〉
entries.literal: The 《Khitan State Annals》 says: In the second month of spring of the second year of Tianlu, when the Marquis of Jin and the empress dowager were moved to Jianzhou, Grand Consort An died en route; her dying charge to the Marquis of Jin was: "Burn my bones to ash and scatter them southward — perhaps my lingering soul may return to China.")〉

entries.zh: 〈（案：《薛史·晉后妃傳》，《永樂大典》已佚，今采《五代會要》、《通鑒》、《契丹國志》、《文獻通考》所載晉后妃事，分註以補是書之闕。）〉
entries.en: (Note: The Biographies of Later Jin Empresses and Consorts in Xue's History, lost from the Yongle Encyclopedia, are here supplemented from empress and consort accounts in the Five Dynasties Essentials, Comprehensive Mirror, Khitan State Annals, and Comprehensive Examination of Documents, set out in separate notes.)〉
entries.literal: (Note: The 《Biographies of Later Jin Empresses and Consorts》 in the 《History of Xue》, lost from the 《Yongle Encyclopedia》, now gathers Later Jin empress and consort matters recorded in the 《Five Dynasties Essentials》, 《Comprehensive Mirror》, 《Khitan State Annals》, and 《Comprehensive Examination of Documents》, set out in separate notes to fill this book's lacunae.)〉

entries.zh: 廣王敬威，字奉信，高祖之從父弟也。
entries.en: Prince Jingwei of Guang, styled Fengxin, was Gaozu's younger paternal cousin.
entries.literal: Prince of Guang Jingwei, styled Fengxin, was a younger cousin of Gaozu on the paternal side.

entries.zh: 父萬詮，贈太尉，追封趙王。
entries.en: His father Wanquan was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
entries.literal: His father Wanquan was posthumously conferred Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

entries.zh: 敬威少善騎射，事後唐莊宗，以從戰有功，累歷軍職。
entries.en: From youth Jingwei excelled at horsemanship and archery. He served Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong and, for his service in battle, rose through a series of military posts.
entries.literal: From youth Jingwei was skilled in horsemanship and archery; he served Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong and, for merit in following campaigns, rose through successive military posts.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，擢為奉聖指揮使。
entries.en: When Emperor Mingzong came to the throne, Jingwei was promoted to commander of the Fengsheng Guard.
entries.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he was promoted to commander of the Fengsheng Guard.

entries.zh: 天成、應順中，凡十改軍額，累官至檢校工部尚書，賜忠順保義功臣。
entries.en: During the Tiancheng and Yingshun eras he changed army designations ten times in all, rose to Acting Minister of Works, and was granted the title of Meritorious Minister, Loyal and Obedient, Protector of Righteousness.
entries.literal: During the Tiancheng and Yingshun eras he changed army designations ten times in all, rose to Acting Minister of Works, and was granted the title Meritorious Minister Loyal and Obedient, Protector of Righteousness.

entries.zh: 清泰中，加兵部尚書、彰聖都指揮使，遙領常州刺史。
entries.en: In the Qingtai era he was further made Minister of War and commander-in-chief of the Zhangsheng Army, and held the prefecture of Changzhou in absentia.
entries.literal: In the Qingtai era he was further made Minister of War and commander-in-chief of the Zhangsheng Army, and held the post of prefect of Changzhou in absentia.

entries.zh: 及高祖建義於太原，敬威時在洛下，知禍必及，召所親謂曰：「夫人生而有死，理之常也。
entries.en: When Gaozu raised his righteous enterprise at Taiyuan, Jingwei was in Luoyang. Seeing that disaster was inevitable, he summoned his intimates and said, "That we are born only to die is the constant way of things.
entries.literal: When Gaozu raised his righteous enterprise at Taiyuan, Jingwei was then in Luoyang. Knowing that disaster was inevitable, he summoned his intimates and said, "That man is born to die is the constant principle of nature.

entries.zh: 我兄方圖大舉，餘固不可偷生待辱，取笑一時。」
entries.en: My elder brother is planning a great undertaking; I surely cannot cling to life and await disgrace, becoming a laughingstock to the age."
entries.literal: My elder brother is planning a great undertaking; as for me, I surely cannot cling to life and await disgrace, becoming a laughingstock for the age."

entries.zh: 乃自殺於私邸，人甚壯之。
entries.en: He then took his own life in his private residence, and people greatly admired his courage.
entries.literal: He then killed himself in his private residence, and people greatly admired his conduct.

entries.zh: 天福二年，冊贈太傅，葬於河南縣。
entries.en: In Tianfu 2 he was posthumously enfeoffed by edict as Grand Tutor and buried in Henan County.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he was posthumously enfeoffed by edict as Grand Tutor and buried in Henan County.

entries.zh: 六年，追封廣王。
entries.en: In the sixth year he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Guang.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Guang.

entries.zh: 韓王暉，字德昭，睿祖孝平皇帝之孫，高祖之從兄也。
entries.en: Prince Hui of Han, styled Dezhao, was a grandson of the Exalted Ancestor Emperor Xiaoping and Gaozu's paternal cousin.
entries.literal: Prince of Han Hui, styled Dezhao, was a grandson of the Exalted Ancestor Emperor Xiaoping of filial piety and peace and a paternal cousin of Gaozu.

entries.zh: 父萬友，追封秦王。
entries.en: His father Wanyou was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.
entries.literal: His father Wanyou was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qin.

entries.zh: 暉生而龐厚，剛毅雄直，有器局，行不由徑，臨事多智，故高祖於宗族之中，獨厚遇之。
entries.en: Hui was born stout and solid, firm, bold, and upright, with breadth of character. He would not take shortcuts, and in affairs he was often resourceful. Among the clan Gaozu singled him out for generous treatment.
entries.literal: Hui was born stout and solid, firm and bold, upright and heroic, possessing breadth of capacity; he would not take shortcuts in his conduct, and in handling affairs he was often resourceful. Therefore among the clan Gaozu singled him out for generous treatment.

entries.zh: 初，張敬達之圍晉陽也，高祖署暉為突騎都將，常引所部，出敵之不意，深入力戰，雖夷傷流血，矢鏃貫骨，而辭氣益厲，高祖壯之。
entries.en: Earlier, when Zhang Jingda besieged Jinyang, Gaozu appointed Hui commander of the assault cavalry. He often led his men where the enemy did not expect, plunging deep and fighting with all his strength. Though wounded and bleeding, with arrowheads driven through bone, his voice only grew fiercer, and Gaozu admired him.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Zhang Jingda besieged Jinyang, Gaozu appointed Hui commander of the assault cavalry. He would often lead his troops to strike where the enemy did not expect, plunging deep and fighting with all his strength. Though he suffered wounds and bloodshed, with arrowheads piercing bone, his tone only grew fiercer, and Gaozu admired him.

entries.zh: 天福二年，遙授濠州刺史，充皇城都部署。
entries.en: In Tianfu 2 he was appointed in absentia prefect of Hao and served as commander of the Imperial City garrison.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he was appointed in absentia as prefect of Hao Province and served as commander of the Imperial City garrison.

entries.zh: 四年，加檢校司徒，授曹州防禦使，加檢校太保。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was made Acting Grand Master and appointed defender of Cao, then further made Acting Supreme Commander.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was made Acting Grand Master and appointed defender of Cao Prefecture, then further made Acting Supreme Commander.

entries.zh: 其蒞任也，廉愛恤下，不營財利，不好伎樂，部人安之。
entries.en: In office he was frugal and caring toward his subordinates, sought no profit, and had no taste for music or performers. The people of his command lived at ease under him.
entries.literal: When he took up his post, he was frugal and loving toward his subordinates, did not pursue profit, and had no taste for music and performers. The people of his command were at peace under him.

entries.zh: 歲餘，以疾終於官，歸葬太原。
entries.en: After more than a year he died of illness in office and was buried at Taiyuan.
entries.literal: After more than a year he died of illness in office, and his remains were buried at Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 八年，冊贈太師，追封韓王。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was posthumously enfeoffed by edict as Grand Preceptor and as Prince of Han.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was posthumously enfeoffed by edict as Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Prince of Han.

entries.zh: 剡王重胤。
entries.en: Prince Chongyin of Shan.
entries.literal: Prince of Shan Chongyin.

entries.zh: 〈（案：郯王以下諸王傳，《永樂大典》原闕。
entries.en: (Note: The biographies of the princes from Prince of Tan downward were originally missing from the Yongle Encyclopedia.
entries.literal: (Note: The biographies of the princes from Prince of Tan downward were originally missing from the Yongle Encyclopedia.

entries.zh: 《歐陽史》云：重允，高祖弟也，亦不知其為親疏，然高祖愛之，養以為子，故於名加「重」而下齒諸子。
entries.en: The Ouyang History says Chongyun was Gaozu's younger brother; whether he was close or distant kin is unknown, yet Gaozu loved him and raised him as a son. Therefore "Chong" was added to his name and he was ranked below Gaozu's sons.
entries.literal: The Ouyang History says Chongyun was Gaozu's younger brother; it is also unknown whether he was close or distant kin, yet Gaozu loved him and raised him as a son. Therefore the character "Chong" was added to his name and he was ranked below the sons.

entries.zh: 《通鑒·齊王紀》：高帝少弟重胤早卒。）〉
entries.en: The Comprehensive Mirror, Annals of the Prince of Qi: Gaozu's youngest brother Chongyin died young.)〉
entries.literal: The Comprehensive Mirror, Annals of Prince of Qi: Gaozu's youngest brother Chongyin died young.)〉

entries.zh: 虢王重英。
entries.en: Prince Chongying of Guo.
entries.literal: Prince of Guo Chongying.

entries.zh: 〈（案：《虢王傳》，《永樂大典》原闕。
entries.en: (Note: The biography of the Prince of Guo was originally missing from the Yongle Encyclopedia.
entries.literal: (Note: The biography of Prince of Guo was originally missing from the Yongle Encyclopedia.

entries.zh: 考《五代會要》云：重英，高祖長子，天福四年四月追封。
entries.en: The Institutions of the Five Dynasties records that Chongying was Gaozu's eldest son, posthumously enfeoffed in the fourth month of Tianfu 4.
entries.literal: Examination of the Institutions of the Five Dynasties shows: Chongying was Gaozu's eldest son, posthumously enfeoffed in the fourth month of Tianfu 4.

entries.zh: 是書《唐紀》：清泰三年七月己丑，誅右衛上將軍石重英。）〉
entries.en: This work's Tang Annals: on jichou, the seventh month of Qingtai 3, Right Guards general Shi Chongying was executed.)〉
entries.literal: This work's Tang Annals: on jichou day in the seventh month of Qingtai 3, the Right Guards general Shi Chongying was executed.)〉

entries.zh: 楚王重信，字守孚，高祖第二子，後唐明宗之外孫也。
entries.en: Prince Chongxin of Chu, styled Shoufu, was Gaozu's second son and a maternal grandson of Later Tang's Emperor Mingzong.
entries.literal: Prince of Chu Chongxin, styled Shoufu, was Gaozu's second son and a maternal grandson of Later Tang's Emperor Mingzong.

entries.zh: 少敏悟，有智思。
entries.en: From youth he was keen and perceptive, with a thoughtful mind.
entries.literal: From youth he was keen and perceptive, with thoughtful intelligence.

entries.zh: 天成中，始授銀青光祿大夫、檢校左散騎常侍，俄加檢校刑部尚書，守相州長史。
entries.en: During Tiancheng he was first made Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Glorious Culture and Acting Left Gentleman for Leisurely Correspondence, then soon Acting Minister of Justice and chief administrator of Xiang.
entries.literal: During Tiancheng he was first given the titles Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Glorious Culture and Acting Left Gentleman for Leisurely Correspondence, then soon made Acting Minister of Justice and commander as chief of Xiang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 未幾，遷金紫光祿大夫，超拜檢校司徒，守左金吾衛大將軍。
entries.en: Before long he was made Grand Master of Golden-gleaming Purple Purpose and promoted in one step to Acting Grand Master, commanding as general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
entries.literal: Before long he was transferred to Grand Master of Golden-gleaming Purple Purpose and promoted in one step to Acting Grand Master, commanding as general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

entries.zh: 重信歷事唐明宗及閔帝、末帝，不恃貴戚，能克己復禮，常恂恂如也，甚為時論所稱。
entries.en: Chongxin served Emperors Mingzong, Min, and Mo of Tang. He did not trade on his noble kinship; he could restrain himself and return to propriety, always earnest and deferential, and won high praise from his contemporaries.
entries.literal: Chongxin served through Emperor Mingzong and Emperors Min and Mo of Tang. He did not rely on his noble kinship; he could restrain himself and return to propriety, always earnest and deferential. Contemporary opinion praised him highly.

entries.zh: 高祖即位，出鎮孟津，到任逾月，去民病十餘事，朝廷有詔褒之。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Chongxin was sent to govern Mengjin. Within a month of taking office he removed more than ten abuses afflicting the people, and the court issued an edict commending him.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Chongxin was sent out to govern Mengjin. Within a month of taking office he removed more than ten abuses afflicting the people, and the court issued an edict commending him.

entries.zh: 是歲，範延光叛命於鄴，詔遣前靈武節度使張從賓發河橋屯兵數千人，東討延光。
entries.en: That year Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye. An edict ordered the former military commissioner of Lingwu, Zhang Congbin, to mobilize several thousand troops at Heqiao and march east against Yanguang.
entries.literal: That year Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye. An edict ordered the former military commissioner of Lingwu, Zhang Congbin, to mobilize several thousand troops stationed at Heqiao and march east against Yanguang.

entries.zh: 既而從賓與延光合謀為亂，遂害重信於理所，時年二十。
entries.en: Before long Congbin joined Yanguang in plotting rebellion and murdered Chongxin at his headquarters. He was twenty.
entries.literal: Before long Congbin joined Yanguang in plotting rebellion and thereupon murdered Chongxin at his administrative quarters. He was twenty years old.

entries.zh: 遠近聞者，為之嘆惜。
entries.en: All who heard of it, near and far, sighed with regret.
entries.literal: Those far and near who heard of it sighed with regret.

entries.zh: 詔贈太尉。
entries.en: An edict posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 時執事奏曰：「兩漢子弟，生死無歷三公位者。」
entries.en: The officials at court memorialized, saying, "In the two Han dynasties, no imperial kinsman in life or death ever held one of the three top offices."
entries.literal: The officials at court memorialized, saying, "In the two Han dynasties, imperial kinsmen in life or death never held the three top offices."

entries.zh: 高祖曰：「此兒為善被禍，予甚湣之，自我作古，寧有例乎。」
entries.en: Gaozu said, "This boy did good yet suffered disaster; I pity him deeply. To break precedent myself—what example is there?"
entries.literal: Gaozu said, "This boy did good yet suffered disaster; I pity him deeply. To break precedent and establish a new rule—can there be an example?"

entries.zh: 遂行冊命。
entries.en: The enfeoffment ceremony was then carried out.
entries.literal: The enfeoffment ceremony was then carried out.

entries.zh: 以其年十月，葬河南萬安山。
entries.en: In the tenth month of that year he was buried on Mount Wan'an in Henan.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of that year he was buried on Mount Wan'an in Henan.

entries.zh: 天福七年，追封沂王，少帝嗣位，改封楚王。
entries.en: In Tianfu 7 he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yi; when Emperor Shaodi succeeded, his title was changed to Prince of Chu.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Tianfu he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yi; when Emperor Shaodi succeeded, his title was changed to Prince of Chu.

entries.zh: 妃南陽白氏，昭信軍節度使奉進之女也。
entries.en: His consort was Lady Bai of Nanyang, daughter of Fengjin, military commissioner of the Zhaoxin Army.
entries.literal: His consort was Lady Bai of Nanyang, daughter of military commissioner Fengjin of the Zhaoxin Army.

entries.zh: 重信有子二人，皆幼，長於公宮，及少帝北遷，不知其所終。
entries.en: Chongxin had two sons, both still young and raised in the palace. When Emperor Shaodi was removed northward, their ultimate fate was unknown.
entries.literal: Chongxin had two sons, both young; they were raised in the palace. When Emperor Shaodi was removed northward, their ultimate fate was unknown.

entries.zh: 壽王重乂，字宏理，高祖第三子也。
entries.en: Prince Chongyi of Shou, styled Hongli, was Gaozu's third son.
entries.literal: Prince of Shou Chongyi, styled Hongli, was Gaozu's third son.

entries.zh: 幼岐嶷，好儒書，亦通兵法，高祖素所鐘愛。
entries.en: From youth he was precocious and sharp, loved Confucian books, and also understood military strategy; Gaozu had long cherished him.
entries.literal: From youth he was precocious and sharp, loved Confucian books, and also understood military strategy; Gaozu had long cherished him.

entries.zh: 及即位，自北京皇城使拜左驍衛大將軍。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Chongyi was promoted from Beijing Imperial City commissioner to general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Chongyi was promoted from Beijing Imperial City commissioner to general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.

entries.zh: 車駕幸浚郊，加檢校司空，權東都留守。
entries.en: When the imperial carriage visited the Jun outskirts, he was made Acting Minister of Works and acting defender of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage visited the Jun outskirts, he was made Acting Minister of Works and acting defender of the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 未幾，鄴都範延光叛，朝廷遣楊光遠討之，詔前靈武節度使、洛都巡檢使張從賓發盟津屯兵赴鄴下。
entries.en: Before long Fan Yanguang rebelled at Yedu. The court sent Yang Guangyuan to suppress him and ordered former Lingwu military commissioner and Luoyang patrol commissioner Zhang Congbin to mobilize troops at Mengjin and march to Ye.
entries.literal: Before long Fan Yanguang rebelled at Yedu. The court sent Yang Guangyuan to suppress him and ordered the former military commissioner of Lingwu and Luoyang patrol commissioner Zhang Congbin to mobilize troops stationed at Mengjin and march to Ye.

entries.zh: 會從賓密通延光，與婁繼英等先劫河橋，次亂洛邑，因害重乂於河南府，時年十九。
entries.en: Congbin then secretly communicated with Yanguang. With Lou Jiying and others he first seized Heqiao Bridge, then threw Luoyang into disorder, and murdered Chongyi in Henan Prefecture. He was nineteen.
entries.literal: Congbin then secretly communicated with Yanguang. With Lou Jiying and others he first seized Heqiao Bridge, then threw Luoyang into disorder, and thereupon murdered Chongyi in Henan Prefecture. He was nineteen years old.

entries.zh: 從賓敗，高祖發哀於便殿，輟視朝三日，詔贈太傅。
entries.en: When Congbin was defeated, Gaozu expressed mourning in the side hall, suspended court audiences for three days, and issued an edict posthumously honoring Chongyi as Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: When Congbin was defeated, Gaozu expressed mourning in the side hall, suspended court audiences for three days, and issued an edict posthumously honoring Chongyi as Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 是歲冬十月，詔遣莊宅使張穎監護喪事，葬於河南府萬安山。
entries.en: In the tenth winter month that year, an edict sent Zhang Ying, commissioner of the imperial estates, to supervise the funeral and bury him on Mount Wan'an in Henan Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter that year, an edict sent Zhang Ying, commissioner of the imperial estates, to supervise the funeral and bury him on Mount Wan'an in Henan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 天福中，追封壽王。
entries.en: During Tianfu he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shou.
entries.literal: During Tianfu he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shou.

entries.zh: 妃李氏，汾州刺史玘之女也。
entries.en: His consort was Lady Li, daughter of Qi, prefect of Fen.
entries.literal: His consort was Lady Li, daughter of Qi, prefect of Fenzhou.

entries.zh: 重乂無子，妃後落發為尼，開運中，卒於京師。
entries.en: Chongyi had no sons. His consort later took the tonsure as a nun; during Kaiyun she died in the capital.
entries.literal: Chongyi had no sons. His consort later shaved her head and became a nun; during Kaiyun she died in the capital.

entries.zh: 夔王重進。
entries.en: Prince Chongjin of Kui.
entries.literal: Prince of Kui Chongjin.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》云：重進，高祖第五子，天福七年四月追封。）〉
entries.en: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties says Chongjin was Gaozu's fifth son, posthumously enfeoffed in the fourth month of Tianfu 7.)〉
entries.literal: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties says: Chongjin was Gaozu's fifth son, posthumously enfeoffed in the fourth month of Tianfu 7.)〉

entries.zh: 陳王重杲。
entries.en: Prince Chonggao of Chen.
entries.literal: Prince of Chen Chonggao.

entries.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》：高祖少子曰馮六，未名而卒，贈太傅，追封陳王，賜名重杲。）〉
entries.en: (The Ouyang History: Gaozu's youngest son was called Feng Six; he died before receiving a name, was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor, enfeoffed as Prince of Chen, and given the name Chonggao.)〉
entries.literal: (The Ouyang History: Gaozu's youngest son was called Feng Six; he died before receiving a name, was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor, enfeoffed as Prince of Chen, and given the name Chonggao.)〉

entries.zh: 重睿。
entries.en: Chongrui.
entries.literal: Chongrui.

entries.zh: 〈（案《契丹國志》：高祖憂悒成疾，一旦馮道獨對，高祖命幼子重睿出拜之，又令宦者抱置道懷中，蓋欲馮道輔立之。
entries.en: (Note: According to the Khitan State Chronicles, Gaozu, weighed down by worry, fell ill. One day Feng Dao had a private audience; Gaozu ordered his young son Chongrui to come forth and bow to him, and had a eunuch place the child in Dao's arms—apparently intending Feng Dao to assist in installing him as heir.
entries.literal: (Note: According to the Khitan State Chronicles, Gaozu, oppressed by worry, fell ill. One day Feng Dao had a private audience; Gaozu ordered the young son Chongrui to come forth and bow to him, and had a eunuch place the child in Dao's arms—apparently intending Feng Dao to assist in installing him as heir.

entries.zh: 高祖崩，道與侍衛馬步都虞候景延廣議，以國家多難，宜立長君，乃奉齊王重貴為嗣。
entries.en: When Gaozu died, Dao discussed with Jing Yanguang, chief of the palace guards infantry and cavalry, that the state faced many difficulties and a mature ruler should be installed; they thereupon enthroned Prince Chonggui of Qi as successor.
entries.literal: When Gaozu died, Dao discussed with the chief of palace guards infantry and cavalry Jing Yanguang that the state faced many difficulties and a mature ruler should be installed; they thereupon enthroned Prince of Qi Chonggui as successor.

entries.zh: 《五代會要》：重睿，高祖第七子，許州節度使，未封王。
entries.en: The Institutions of the Five Dynasties: Chongrui was Gaozu's seventh son, military commissioner of Xu, and had not yet received a princely title.
entries.literal: The Institutions of the Five Dynasties: Chongrui was Gaozu's seventh son, military commissioner of Xu Province, and had not yet received a princely title.

entries.zh: 《歐陽史》云：從出帝北遷，不知其所終。）〉
entries.en: The Ouyang History says that when he followed the deposed emperor northward, his ultimate fate was unknown.)〉
entries.literal: The Ouyang History says: when he followed the deposed emperor northward, his ultimate fate was unknown.)〉

entries.zh: 延寶。
entries.en: Yanbao.
entries.literal: Yanbao.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：延寶，少帝次子，遙領魯州節度使。
entries.en: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties: Yanbao was Emperor Shaodi's second son and held in absentia the post of military commissioner of Lu.
entries.literal: (The Institutions of the Five Dynasties: Yanbao was Emperor Shaodi's second son and held in absentia the post of military commissioner of Lu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 《通鑒》云：延煦及弟延寶皆高祖諸孫，帝養以為子。
entries.en: The Comprehensive Mirror says Yanxu and his younger brother Yanbao were all Gaozu's grandsons; the emperor raised them as sons.
entries.literal: The Comprehensive Mirror says: Yanxu and his younger brother Yanbao were all Gaozu's grandsons; the emperor raised them as sons.

entries.zh: 《會要》引實錄亦云皆帝之從子，養以為子。
entries.en: The Institutions, citing the Veritable Records, likewise says they were all the emperor's younger cousins, raised as sons.
entries.literal: The Institutions citing the Veritable Records likewise says they were all the emperor's younger cousins, raised as sons.

entries.zh: 《歐陽史》云：延煦等從帝北遷，後不知其所終。）〉
entries.en: The Ouyang History says Yanxu and the others followed the emperor northward; afterward their ultimate fates were unknown.)〉
entries.literal: The Ouyang History says: Yanxu and the others followed the emperor northward; afterward their ultimate fates were unknown.)〉

entries.zh: 宗室
entries.en: The Imperial Clan
entries.literal: Imperial Clan

entries.zh: 〈（案：《晉宗室列傳》，《永樂大典》僅存四篇，余多殘闕。）〉
entries.en: (Note: The biographies of the Jin imperial clan in the Yongle Encyclopedia survive in only four sections; most of the rest is defective or missing.)〉
entries.literal: (Note: The biographies of the Jin imperial clan in the Yongle Encyclopedia survive in only four sections; the remainder is largely defective or missing.)〉

entries.zh: 張筠，海州人也。
entries.en: Zhang Yun was a native of Haizhou.
entries.literal: Zhang Yun, was a man of Haizhou.

entries.zh: 父傳古，世為郡之大商，唐乾符末，屬江淮俶擾，遂徙家彭門。
entries.en: His father Chuangu had for generations been one of the prefecture's great merchants. At the end of the Tang Qianfu era, with the Jiang-Huai region in turmoil, he moved the family to Pengmen.
entries.literal: His father Chuangu was for generations a great merchant of the prefecture; at the end of the Qianfu era of Tang, because the Jiang-Huai region was in turmoil, he moved his household to Pengmen.

entries.zh: 時彭門連帥時溥為東南面招討使，據有數郡之地，擢筠為偏將，累有軍功，奏授宿州刺史。
entries.en: The Pengmen commander Shi Pu was then southeastern pacification commissioner, holding several prefectures. He promoted Yun to deputy general; Yun won repeated military distinction, and Pu memorialized to have him appointed prefect of Suzhou.
entries.literal: At that time the Pengmen commander Shi Pu was southeastern pacification commissioner, holding several prefectures' territory; he promoted Yun to deputy general, who repeatedly had military merit, and memorialized to appoint him Suzhou prefect.

entries.zh: 後溥與梁祖不協，梁人進攻宿州，下之，獲筠以歸。
entries.en: Later, when Pu fell out with the Liang founder, Liang forces attacked Suzhou, captured it, and took Yun back with them.
entries.literal: Later Pu was at odds with the Liang founder; Liang men advanced to attack Suzhou, took it, and captured Yun to bring back.

entries.zh: 梁方圖霸業，以筠言貌辯秀，命為四鎮客將，久之，轉長直軍使。
entries.en: With Liang then plotting supremacy, Yun's eloquence and polished appearance won him appointment as guest general of the four commands. After a long interval he was made chief of the long-duty army.
entries.literal: Liang was then plotting hegemony; because Yun's speech and appearance were eloquent and refined, he was ordered to be a guest general of the four commands; after a long time he was transferred to chief of the long-duty army.

entries.zh: 梁唐革命，遷右龍武統軍，歷客省使、宣徽使，出為復、商二州刺史，復為宣徽使。
entries.en: When Liang gave way to Tang, Yun was transferred to commander of the Right Valiant Dragons, served in succession as guest-reception commissioner and palace treasury commissioner, was sent out as prefect of Fu and Shang, and again became palace treasury commissioner.
entries.literal: When Liang underwent the Tang revolution, he was transferred to Right Valiant Dragon commander, served in succession as guest-reception commissioner and palace treasury commissioner, went out as prefect of Fu and Shang prefectures, and again became palace treasury commissioner.

entries.zh: 梁室割相、衛為昭德軍，命筠為兩使留後。
entries.en: The Liang court carved out Xiang and Wei as the Zhaode army and appointed Yun acting commissioner of both civil and military affairs.
entries.literal: The Liang house carved Xiang and Wei into the Zhaode army and ordered Yun as acting commissioner of both civil and military affairs.

entries.zh: 唐莊宗入魏，筠委城南歸，授右衛上將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang entered Wei, Yun abandoned the southern city and submitted, and was appointed General of the Right Guards.
entries.literal: When Tang Emperor Zhuangzong entered Wei, Yun abandoned the southern city and returned, and was appointed General of the Right Guards.

entries.zh: 會雍州康懷英以病告，詔筠往代之，比至，懷英已卒，因除筠為永平軍節度使、大安尹。
entries.en: When Kang Huaiying of Yongzhou reported illness, Yun was ordered to replace him. By the time he arrived, Huaiying was already dead, and Yun was appointed military commissioner of the Yongping army and Intendant of Da'an.
entries.literal: It happened that Yongzhou's Kang Huaiying reported illness; an edict ordered Yun to go replace him. By the time he arrived, Huaiying had already died, and Yun was therefore appointed Yongping army military commissioner and Da'an Intendant.

entries.zh: 懷英在長安日，家財甚厚，筠盡奪之，復於大內掘地，繼獲金玉。
entries.en: Huaiying had amassed great wealth while at Chang'an; Yun seized it all. He also dug within the inner palace grounds and unearthed gold and jade.
entries.literal: When Huaiying was at Chang'an, his household wealth was very great; Yun seized it all. Again within the great inner palace he dug the ground and subsequently obtained gold and jade.

entries.zh: 時有涇陽鎮將侯莫威，前與溫韜同剽唐氏諸陵，大貯瑰異之物，筠乃殺威而籍其家，遂蓄積巨萬。
entries.en: The Jingyang garrison commander Hou Mowei had earlier joined Wen Tao in plundering the tombs of the Tang imperial house and hoarded extraordinary treasures. Yun killed him and confiscated his property, amassing wealth in the tens of thousands.
entries.literal: At that time there was Jingyang garrison commander Hou Mowei, who earlier with Wen Tao together plundered the tombs of the Tang house and greatly stored rare and wondrous objects; Yun then killed Wei and registered his household, thereby amassing tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 然性好施，每出遇貧民於路，則給與口食衣物，境內除省賦外，未嘗聚斂，遂致百姓不撓，十年小康，秦民懷惠，呼為「佛子」。
entries.en: Yet he was generous by nature: whenever he went out and met the poor on the road, he gave them food and clothing. Apart from provincial levies, he never extorted within his jurisdiction, and the people were left unmolested. For ten years the region knew modest prosperity; the people of Qin were grateful and called him "the Buddha's son."
entries.literal: Yet his nature was fond of giving; whenever he went out and met poor people on the road, he supplied them food and clothing. Within his jurisdiction, apart from provincial levies, he never amassed and exacted, and thereby caused the common people not to be harassed; for ten years there was modest prosperity, and the Qin people cherished his kindness, calling him "Buddha's Son."

entries.zh: 同光中，從郭崇韜為劍南安撫使，蜀平歸洛，權領河南尹，俄鎮興元，所治之地，上下安之。
entries.en: During the Tongguang era he followed Guo Chongtao as Jiannan pacification commissioner. After Shu was pacified he returned to Luoyang, served provisionally as Henan Intendant, and soon took up command at Xingyuan, where high and low alike lived in peace under his rule.
entries.literal: In the Tongguang era, he followed Guo Chongtao as Jiannan pacification commissioner; when Shu was pacified he returned to Luoyang, provisionally headed Henan as Intendant, and soon garrisoned Xingyuan—the places he governed, high and low were at peace.

entries.zh: 筠時有疾，軍州官吏久不得見，副使符彥琳等面請問疾，筠又不諾，彥琳等疑其已死，慮左右有謀，遂請權交牌印，筠命左右收彥琳下獄，以叛聞。
entries.en: Yun was then ill, and the military and civil officials had long been unable to see him. Deputy commissioner Fu Yanlin and others came in person to inquire after his health, but Yun refused them again. Yanlin and the others suspected he was already dead and feared a plot among his attendants; they asked to take custody of the seals provisionally. Yun ordered his attendants to arrest Yanlin and imprison him, then reported him for rebellion.
entries.literal: Yun at that time had illness; the army and prefecture officials for a long time could not see him. The deputy commissioner Fu Yanlin and others in person requested to inquire after his illness; Yun again did not assent. Yanlin and others suspected he was already dead and feared that those around him had designs; they therefore requested to hand over the tally and seal provisionally. Yun ordered those around him to seize Yanlin and put him in prison, reporting rebellion.

entries.zh: 詔取彥琳等至洛，釋而不問，因授筠西京留守，誘離興元。
entries.en: An edict summoned Yanlin and the others to Luoyang and released them without punishment. Yun was then appointed garrison commander of the western capital, a move intended to draw him away from Xingyuan.
entries.literal: An edict took Yanlin and others to Luoyang, released them without inquiry, and thereby appointed Yun western capital garrison commander to lure him away from Xingyuan.

entries.zh: 及至長安，守兵閉門不納，筠東朝於洛，詔遣歸第。
entries.en: When he reached Chang'an, the garrison closed the gates and refused him entry. Yun went east to audience at Luoyang, where an edict sent him back to his private residence.
entries.literal: When he reached Chang'an, the garrison troops closed the gates and would not admit him. Yun went east to audience at Luoyang; an edict sent him back to his residence.

entries.zh: 筠前為京兆尹，奉詔殺偽蜀主王衍，衍之妓樂寶貨，悉私藏於家。
entries.en: Yun had earlier served as Intendant of Jingzhao and, by imperial order, executed the puppet Shu ruler Wang Yan; he then secretly kept at home all of Yan's performers, music, and valuables.
entries.literal: Previously, when Yun had been Intendant of Jingzhao, he received an edict to execute the false Shu ruler Wang Yan; Yan's entertainers, music, and treasures he secretly hoarded entirely at home.

entries.zh: 及罷歸之後，第宅宏敞，花竹深邃，聲樂飲膳，恣其所欲，十年之內，人謂「地仙」。
entries.en: After he retired and returned home, his mansion was grand and spacious, with deep groves of flowers and bamboo; music and feasting were at his pleasure. Within ten years people called him an "earth immortal."
entries.literal: When he returned after leaving office, his residence was vast and spacious, flowers and bamboo deep and secluded, music and feasting as he wished; within ten years people called him an "earth immortal."

entries.zh: 天福二年，上表乞歸長安，俄而洛下張從賓之亂，筠獨免其難，人咸謂筠有五福之具美焉。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianfu he memorialized asking to return to Chang'an. Soon afterward Zhang Congbin's rebellion erupted in Luoyang; Yun alone escaped harm, and all agreed that he truly enjoyed the full measure of the five blessings.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he memorialized asking to return to Chang'an. Soon Zhang Congbin's rebellion broke out in Luoyang; Yun alone escaped the calamity, and everyone said Yun truly possessed the full beauty of the five blessings.

entries.zh: 是歲，卒於家。
entries.en: That year he died at home.
entries.literal: That year he died at home.

entries.zh: 贈太子太師。
entries.en: He was posthumously awarded the title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 弟篯。
entries.en: Younger brother Jian.
entries.literal: Younger brother Jian.

entries.zh: 篯，字慕彭，少嗜酒無節，為鄉里所鄙。
entries.en: Jian, courtesy name Mupeng, was in his youth addicted to wine without restraint and was despised in his home district.
entries.literal: Jian, style name Mupeng, in youth was addicted to wine without restraint and was despised by his district.

entries.zh: 唐天復中，兄筠為大梁四鎮客將，篯自海州省兄，兄薦於兗州連帥王瓚，用為裨校。
entries.en: During the Tianfu era of the Tang dynasty (901–904), his elder brother Yun served as guest general of Daliang's four commands. Jian traveled from Haizhou to visit him; Yun recommended him to the Yanzhou commander Wang Zan, who took him on as adjutant.
entries.literal: In the Tianfu era of the Tang dynasty (901–904), his elder brother Yun was guest general of the four commands of Daliang; Jian came from Haizhou to visit his brother, and Yun recommended him to the Yanzhou commander Wang Zan, who employed him as adjutant.

entries.zh: 篯性桀黠，善事人，累遷軍職。
entries.en: Jian was clever and crafty by nature, adept at winning people over, and rose repeatedly through military ranks.
entries.literal: Jian's nature was clever and crafty; he was skilled at pleasing people and was repeatedly promoted in military posts.

entries.zh: 後唐莊宗都洛，筠鎮長安，自衙內指揮使授檢校司空、右千牛衛將軍同正，領饒州刺史、西京管內三白渠營田制置使。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang established his capital at Luoyang, Yun garrisoned Chang'an. From palace-inner commander he was made acting Minister of Works and Right Imperial Equerry General with concurrent appointment, and concurrently served as prefect of Raozhou and commissioner for the three Baibi canals farming administration in the western capital circuit.
entries.literal: When Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong made Luoyang his capital, Yun garrisoned Chang'an; from palace-inner commander he was appointed acting Minister of Works, Right Imperial Equerry General with concurrent appointment, and concurrently Raozhou prefect and commissioner for the three Baibi canals farming administration within the western capital circuit.

entries.zh: 同光末，筠隨魏王繼岌伐蜀，奏篯權知西京留守事。
entries.en: At the end of the Tongguang era Yun followed the Prince of Wei, Li Jiji, on the campaign against Shu and memorialized to have Jian provisionally handle western capital garrison affairs.
entries.literal: At the end of Tongguang, Yun followed the Prince of Wei Li Jiji in the expedition against Shu and memorialized to have Jian provisionally administer western capital garrison affairs.

entries.zh: 蜀平，王衍挈族入朝，至秦川驛，莊宗遣中使向延嗣乘驛騎盡戮王衍之族，所有奇貨，盡歸於延嗣。
entries.en: After Shu was pacified, Wang Yan led his clan to court. At Qinchuan post station Zhuangzong sent the palace envoy Xiang Yansi on relay horses to slaughter Wang Yan's entire clan; all rare goods went entirely to Yansi.
entries.literal: When Shu was pacified, Wang Yan led his clan to court. At Qinchuan post station Zhuangzong sent palace envoy Xiang Yansi on post-horses to slaughter Wang Yan's entire clan; all rare goods fell entirely to Yansi.

entries.zh: 俄聞莊宗遇內難，繼岌軍次興平，篯乃斷咸陽浮橋，繼岌浮渡至渭南死之，一行金寶妓樂，篯悉獲之。
entries.en: Soon word arrived that Zhuangzong had met with internal disaster. Li Jiji's army halted at Xingping; Jian cut the Xianyang floating bridge, and Jiji crossed by raft to Weinan, where he died. Jian seized the whole train of gold, jewels, and entertainers.
entries.literal: Soon word came that Zhuangzong had met internal disaster. Li Jiji's army halted at Xingping; Jian severed the Xianyang floating bridge, Jiji crossed by raft to Weinan and died there; the entire train of gold, jewels, and entertainers Jian seized entirely.

entries.zh: 俄而明宗使人誅延嗣，延嗣暗遁，
entries.en: Before long Mingzong sent men to execute Yansi; Yansi fled in secret,
entries.literal: Before long Mingzong sent men to execute Yansi; Yansi fled in secret,

entries.zh: 〈（《九國志》：明宗即位，忿閹豎輩怙勢擅權，先敕使四方及此遁不出者，皆擒戮之，死者殆盡。）〉
entries.en: (Annals of the Nine States records: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, enraged at the eunuchs who relied on power and monopolized authority, he first ordered that eunuch envoys throughout the realm and those in hiding who did not come forth be seized and executed; nearly all were killed.)〉
entries.literal: (Annals of the Nine States: When Mingzong took the throne, angry at the eunuch faction that relied on power and usurped authority, he first ordered that eunuch envoys sent to the four directions and those who had fled and did not emerge be captured and executed; nearly all died.)〉

entries.zh: 衍之行裝復為篯有，因為富家，積白金萬鎰，藏於窟室。
entries.en: Wang Yan's traveling goods again fell into Jian's hands; he thus became a wealthy man, amassing ten thousand ingots of white silver in a hidden vault.
entries.literal: Wang Yan's traveling goods again became Jian's possession; he thus became a wealthy house, amassing ten thousand ingots of white silver stored in a hidden vault.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，篯進王衍犀、玉帶各二，馬一百五十匹，魏王打球馬七十匹，旋除沂州刺史，入為西衛將軍。
entries.en: When Mingzong took the throne, Jian presented two rhinoceros-horn belts and two jade belts from Wang Yan, one hundred fifty horses, and seventy of the Prince of Wei's polo horses; he was soon made prefect of Yizhou and then appointed general of the western guards.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Jian presented two rhinoceros and jade belts each from Wang Yan, one hundred fifty horses, and seventy polo horses of the Prince of Wei; he was soon appointed Yizhou prefect and entered service as western guards general.

entries.zh: 高祖即位之明年，加檢校太保，出典密州，未幾，復居環衛。
entries.en: In the year after Gaozu's accession he was made acting Grand Guardian, sent out to govern Mizhou, and before long returned to the palace guards.
entries.literal: The year after Gaozu ascended, he was made acting Grand Guardian, sent out to govern Mizhou, and soon after returned to the palace guards.

entries.zh: 時湖南馬希範與篯有舊，奏朝廷請命篯為使，允之。
entries.en: At that time Ma Xifan of Hunan was an old acquaintance of Jian's and memorialized the court to appoint Jian as envoy; the request was granted.
entries.literal: At that time Hunan's Ma Xifan was old friends with Jian and memorialized the court to appoint Jian as envoy; approval was granted.

entries.zh: 篯密賫蜀之奇貨往售，又獲十餘萬緡以歸。
entries.en: Jian secretly took Shu's rare goods to sell and returned with more than one hundred thousand strings of cash.
entries.literal: Jian secretly carried Shu rare goods to sell and returned having gained more than one hundred thousand strings of cash.

entries.zh: 篯出入以庖者十餘人從行，食皆水陸之珍鮮，厚自奉養，無與為比。
entries.en: Whenever Jian went out, more than ten cooks attended him; his meals were delicacies from land and sea. He lived in unrivaled luxury.
entries.literal: When going out, Jian was attended by more than ten cooks; his food was delicacies from land and sea; he maintained himself lavishly, unmatched by any other.

entries.zh: 少帝嗣位，詔遣往西蕃，及回，以其馬劣，為有司所糾，復當路有不足者，遂有詔征其舊價。
entries.en: When Emperor Shaodi succeeded, an edict sent him to the western tribes. On his return his horses were judged inferior and the authorities impeached him; moreover those in power who disliked him secured an edict to recover the original purchase price.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shaodi succeeded, an edict sent him to the western tribes. On his return, because his horses were inferior, he was impeached by the authorities; furthermore there were those in power who bore him ill will, and an edict was issued to collect the old purchase price.

entries.zh: 篯上言請貨故京田業，許之，因憤惋成疾而卒。
entries.en: Jian memorialized asking to mortgage his former estates in the capital; permission was granted, but indignation and distress brought on illness and he died.
entries.literal: Jian memorialized asking to pawn his former capital estates; permission was granted, but resentment and distress brought on illness and he died.

entries.zh: 趙在禮，字翰臣，涿州人也。
entries.en: Zhao Zaili, courtesy name Hanchen, was a native of Zhuozhou.
entries.literal: Zhao Zaili, style name Hanchen, was a man of Zhuozhou.

entries.zh: 曾祖景裕，祖士廉，皆不仕。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Jingyu and grandfather Shilian both held no office.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Jingyu and grandfather Shilian both did not take office.

entries.zh: 父元德，盧臺軍使。
