entries.en: His father Yuande served as military commissioner of the Lu Terrace.
entries.literal: His father Yuande was Lu Terrace military commissioner.

entries.zh: 在禮始事燕帥劉仁恭為小校，唐光化末，仁恭遣其子守文逐浮陽節度使盧彥威，據其城，升在禮為軍使，以佐守文。
entries.en: Zaili first entered service under the Yan commander Liu Ren'gong as a junior officer. At the end of the Tang Guanghua era, Ren'gong sent his son Shouwen to expel Fuyang military commissioner Lu Yanwei and occupy his city, promoting Zaili to army commissioner to assist Shouwen.
entries.literal: Zaili at first served the Yan commander Liu Ren'gong as a junior officer; at the end of the Guanghua era of Tang, Ren'gong sent his son Shouwen to drive out Fuyang military commissioner Lu Yanwei and seize his city, promoting Zaili to army commissioner to assist Shouwen.

entries.zh: 及守文死，事其子。
entries.en: After Shouwen died, he served his son in turn.
entries.literal: When Shouwen died, he served his son.

entries.zh: 延祚為守光所害，守光子繼威復為部將張萬進所殺，在禮遂事萬進。
entries.en: Yanzuo was killed by Liu Shouguang; Shouguang's son Jiwei was in turn killed by the subordinate commander Zhang Wanjin, and Zaili then entered Wanjin's service.
entries.literal: Yanzuo was killed by Shouguang; Shouguang's son Jiwei was again killed by the subordinate commander Zhang Wanjin, and Zaili then served Wanjin.

entries.zh: 萬進奔梁，在禮乃與滄州留後毛璋歸太原。
entries.en: When Wanjin fled to Liang, Zaili returned to Taiyuan together with Cangzhou acting prefect Mao Zhang.
entries.literal: Wanjin fled to Liang; Zaili then together with Cangzhou acting prefect Mao Zhang returned to Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 同光末，為效節指揮使，屯於貝州。
entries.en: At the end of the Tongguang era he was commander of the Xiaojie army, stationed at Beizhou.
entries.literal: At the end of Tongguang, he was Xiaojie army commander and was stationed at Beizhou.

entries.zh: 會軍士皇甫暉等作亂，推指揮使楊晸為帥，晸不從，為眾所害，攜晸首以脅在禮。
entries.en: When the soldiers Huangfu Hui and others mutinied, they tried to make the commander Yang Zheng their leader. Zheng refused and was killed by the mutineers, who then brought his head to force Zaili to lead them.
entries.literal: It happened that the soldiers Huangfu Hui and others mutinied, pushing the commander Yang Zheng as leader; Zheng did not comply and was killed by the crowd, who carried Zheng's head to coerce Zaili.

entries.zh: 在禮知其不可拒，遂從之，以四年二月六日引眾入鄴，在禮自稱留後。
entries.en: Zaili knew he could not refuse, so he went along. On the sixth day of the second month of the fourth year he led his troops into Ye and styled himself acting prefect.
entries.literal: Zaili knew it could not be refused, so he followed; on the sixth day of the second month in the fourth year he led the crowd into Ye, and Zaili styled himself acting prefect.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·張錫傳》：趙在禮舉兵於鄴，瀕河諸州多構亂，錫權知棣州事，即出省錢賞軍，皆大悅，一郡獨全，棣人賴之。）〉
entries.en: (The History of Song, biography of Zhang Xi, records that when Zhao Zaili raised troops at Ye, most of the prefectures along the river fell into disorder. Xi was acting prefect of Dizhou; he immediately paid out provincial funds to reward the troops, to general delight, and that prefecture alone remained secure—the people of Di were indebted to him.)〉
entries.literal: (History of Song, Biography of Zhang Xi: When Zhao Zaili raised troops at Ye, the prefectures along the river for the most part stirred up disorder; Xi was acting prefect of Dizhou, immediately disbursed provincial funds to reward the army, all were greatly pleased, and that one prefecture alone remained intact—the people of Di relied on him.)〉

entries.zh: 唐莊宗遣明宗率師討之，會城下軍亂，在禮迎明宗入城，事具《唐書》。
entries.en: Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang sent Emperor Mingzong at the head of an army against him. When the troops below the walls mutinied, Zaili welcomed Mingzong into the city; the full account is in the Book of Tang.
entries.literal: Tang Emperor Zhuangzong sent Mingzong at the head of an army to attack him; it happened that the army below the walls mutinied, and Zaili welcomed Mingzong into the city—the matter is fully set forth in the Book of Tang.

entries.zh: 天成元年五月，授滑州節度使、檢校太保。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the first year of Tiancheng he was appointed military commissioner of Huazhou and acting Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Tiancheng, he was appointed Huazhou military commissioner and acting Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 制下，在禮密奏軍情，未欲除移，且乞更伺少頃，尋就改天雄軍兵馬留後、鄴都留守、興唐尹。
entries.en: When the appointment was announced, Zaili secretly reported on conditions in the army, saying he was not yet ready to be transferred and asking to wait a little longer. Soon afterward he was instead made acting commissioner of the Tianxiong army's horse and foot, garrison commander of the Ye capital, and prefect of Xingtang.
entries.literal: When the edict was issued, Zaili secretly memorialized on military conditions, not yet wishing to be transferred, and moreover begged to wait a little longer; soon after he was changed to Tianxiong army acting commissioner of horse and foot, Ye capital garrison commander, and Xingtang prefect.

entries.zh: 既而在禮將皇甫暉、趙進等相次除郡赴任，
entries.en: Zaili then had Huangfu Hui, Zhao Jin, and others appointed in succession to prefectural posts and sent off to take office,
entries.literal: Afterward Zaili had Huangfu Hui, Zhao Jin, and others in succession appointed to prefectures and sent to take up their posts,

entries.zh: 〈（《歐陽史·皇甫暉傳》：明宗即位，暉自軍卒擢拜陳州刺史。
entries.en: (Ouyang Xiu's history, biography of Huangfu Hui: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Hui was raised from the ranks to prefect of Chenzhou.
entries.literal: (Ouyang's History, Biography of Huangfu Hui: When Mingzong took the throne, Hui was promoted from common soldier to Chenzhou prefect.

entries.zh: 《九國誌·趙進傳》：天成初，除貝州刺史、鄴都衙內指揮使。）〉
entries.en: Annals of the Nine States, biography of Zhao Jin: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was appointed prefect of Beizhou and commander of the Ye capital inner guard.)〉
entries.literal: Annals of the Nine States, Biography of Zhao Jin: At the beginning of Tiancheng, he was made Beizhou prefect and Ye capital inner-palace army commander.)〉

entries.zh: 在禮乃上表乞移旌節。
entries.en: Zaili then memorialized, asking to be transferred to another post with full military commission.
entries.literal: Zaili then submitted a memorial begging to be moved to another command with banners and staffs.

entries.zh: 十二月，授滄州節度使。
entries.en: In the twelfth month he was appointed military commissioner of Cangzhou.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, he was appointed Cangzhou military commissioner.

entries.zh: 二年七月，移鎮兗州。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the second year he was transferred to Yanzhou.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the second year, he was transferred to garrison Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 長興元年，入為左驍衛上將軍，俄改同州節度使。
entries.en: In the first year of Changxing he was recalled to the capital as General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guards, and soon afterward was made military commissioner of Tongzhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Changxing, he entered the capital as General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guards; soon after he was changed to Tongzhou military commissioner.

entries.zh: 會高祖受明宗命統大軍伐蜀，以在禮充西川行營步軍都指揮使，收劍州而還。
entries.en: When Gaozu received orders from Emperor Mingzong to command a great army against Shu, Zaili served as overall commander of the campaign's foot forces in the west, recovered Jianzhou, and returned.
entries.literal: It happened that Gaozu received Mingzong's order to command a great army against Shu; Zaili was made overall commander of foot troops in the western Shu campaign headquarters, recovered Jianzhou, and returned.

entries.zh: 四年，移鎮襄州。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was transferred to Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to garrison Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 清泰三年，授宋州節度使，加檢校太尉、同平章事。
entries.en: In the third year of Qingtai he was appointed military commissioner of Songzhou and given the additional titles of acting Grand Marshal and Grand Councillor.
entries.literal: In the third year of Qingtai, he was appointed Songzhou military commissioner, with the added titles acting Grand Marshal and Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

entries.zh: 高祖登極，移鎮鄆州，加檢校太師、兼侍中，封衛國公。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Zaili was transferred to Yunzhou, given the additional titles of acting Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Zaili was transferred to garrison Yunzhou, with the added titles acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

entries.zh: 天福六年七月，授許州節度使。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Tianfu he was appointed military commissioner of Xu Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Tianfu, he was appointed military commissioner of Xu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 八年四月，移鎮徐州，進封楚國公。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the eighth year he was transferred to Xuzhou and advanced in rank to Duke of Chu.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, he was transferred to garrison Xuzhou and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Chu.

entries.zh: 開運元年，以契丹為患，少帝議北征。
entries.en: In the first year of Kaiyun, with the Khitan posing a threat, the Young Emperor considered a northern campaign.
entries.literal: In the first year of Kaiyun, because the Khitan were a menace, the Young Emperor deliberated a northern expedition.

entries.zh: 八月朔，降制命一十五將，以在禮為北面行營馬步都虞候。
entries.en: On the first day of the eighth month, appointments were issued for fifteen generals; Zaili was made overall adjutant of horse and foot for the northern campaign.
entries.literal: On the first day of the eighth month, edicts were issued appointing fifteen generals; Zaili was made overall adjutant of horse and foot in the northern campaign headquarters.

entries.zh: 十一月，改行營副都統，都虞候如故。
entries.en: In the eleventh month he was made deputy overall commander of the campaign, while retaining his post as overall adjutant.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, he was changed to deputy overall commander of the campaign headquarters, remaining overall adjutant as before.

entries.zh: 受詔屯澶州，再除兗州節度使，依前副都統。
entries.en: Ordered to encamp at Chanzhou, he was again appointed military commissioner of Yanzhou while continuing as deputy overall commander.
entries.literal: He received orders to station at Chanzhou, was again appointed Yanzhou military commissioner, and continued as deputy overall commander as before.

entries.zh: 三年正月，授晉昌軍節度使。
entries.en: In the first month of the third year he was appointed military commissioner of the Jinchang army.
entries.literal: In the first month of the third year, he was appointed Jinchang army military commissioner.

entries.zh: 時少帝為其子延煦娶在禮女為妻，禮會之日，其儀甚盛，京師以為榮觀。
entries.en: The Young Emperor had his son Yanxu marry Zaili's daughter. On the wedding day the ceremonies were splendid, and the capital treated the event as a spectacle of honor.
entries.literal: At that time the Young Emperor took Zaili's daughter as wife for his son Yanxu; on the day of the ceremonial meeting the rites were very grand, and the capital regarded it as an occasion of glory to behold.

entries.zh: 五月，進封秦國公，累食邑至一萬三千戶，實封一千五百戶。
entries.en: In the fifth month he was advanced to Duke of Qin, with cumulative fief households rising to thirteen thousand and actual fief households of one thousand five hundred.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Qin; his cumulative fief households reached thirteen thousand, with one thousand five hundred actual fief households.

entries.zh: 姚顗，字伯真，京兆萬年人。
entries.en: Yao Yi, courtesy name Bozhen, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
entries.literal: Yao Yi, style name Bozhen, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 曾祖希齊，湖州司功參軍。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Xiqi served as staff merit officer in Huzhou.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Xiqi was Merit Officer on the staff of Huzhou.

entries.zh: 祖宏慶，蘇州刺史。
entries.en: His grandfather Hongqing was prefect of Suzhou.
entries.literal: His grandfather Hongqing was Prefect of Suzhou.

entries.zh: 父荊，國子祭酒。
entries.en: His father Jing served as chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
entries.literal: His father Jing was Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

entries.zh: 顗少蠢，敦厚，靡事容貌，任其自然，流輩未之重，唯兵部侍郎司空圖深器之，以女妻焉。
entries.en: As a young man Yi seemed slow and unpolished, yet he was honest and steadfast, paid little heed to his looks, and let things be. His contemporaries did not think much of him, but Vice Minister of War Sikong Tu recognized his worth and married his daughter to him.
entries.literal: Yi in youth was dull and simple, honest and thick; he cared nothing for his appearance and let nature take its course. His peers did not esteem him; only Vice Minister of War Sikong Tu greatly valued him and gave him his daughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 顗性仁恕，多為仆妾所欺，心雖察之，而不能面折，終身無喜怒。
entries.en: Yi was gentle and forbearing by nature. Servants and concubines often took advantage of him; he saw through their tricks but could never bring himself to confront them openly, and he never showed anger or delight throughout his life.
entries.literal: Yi was by nature benevolent and forgiving; he was often deceived by servants and concubines. Though he perceived it in his heart, he could not reproach them to their faces, and throughout his life he showed neither anger nor joy.

entries.zh: 不知錢百之為陌，黍百之為銖，凡家人市貨百物，入增其倍，出減其半，不詢其由，無擔石之儲，心不隕獲。
entries.en: He did not even know that a hundred cash make a string or a hundred grains of millet make a measure. Whenever the household bought or sold goods, they doubled prices on purchases and cut them in half on sales, and he never asked why. He had scarcely a bushel of grain in store, yet he never fretted over his losses.
entries.literal: He did not know that a hundred coins make a string or that a hundred grains of millet make a zhu. Whenever household members bought or sold anything, they doubled the price on what came in and halved it on what went out, without his asking why. He had no stores of grain worth even a dan or shi, yet his heart never fell to despair over gain.

entries.zh: 唐末，隨計入洛，出遊嵩山，有白衣丈夫拜於路側，請為童仆。
entries.en: Late in the Tang he traveled to Luoyang for the civil service examination. On an outing to Mount Song, a man dressed in white bowed to him beside the road and asked to become his attendant.
entries.literal: In the late Tang he went to Luoyang for the provincial examination; while touring Mount Song he met a man in white robes who bowed by the roadside and asked to serve as his page.

entries.zh: 顗辭不納。
entries.en: Yi refused and would not take him in.
entries.literal: Yi declined and would not accept him.

entries.zh: 乃曰：「鬼神享於德，君子孚於信。
entries.en: The man then said, "Spirits feast on virtue, and the gentleman lives by good faith.
entries.literal: The man then said: "Spirits and ghosts feast upon virtue; the gentleman rests upon trust.

entries.zh: 余則鬼也，將以托賢者之德，通化工之信，幸無辭焉。
entries.en: I am a ghost, and I wish to rely on the virtue of a worthy man and share in the faith that moves heaven and earth. I beg you not to turn me away.
entries.literal: I am a ghost, and wish to entrust myself to the virtue of a worthy man and join in the trust of transforming creation—please do not refuse.

entries.zh: 昔余掌事陰府，承命攝人之魂氣，名氏同而其人非，且富有壽算，復而歸之，則筋骸已敗，由是獲譴，使不得為陽生。
entries.en: Long ago I held office in the realm of the dead and was charged to take charge of people's souls. When the name matched but the person did not, and the allotted span of life was still long, restoring the soul would find the body already decayed. For this I was condemned and barred from returning to life among men.
entries.literal: Formerly I managed affairs in the yin realm and received orders to seize people's vital breath. When the name was the same but the person was not, and the allotted span was still long, if I returned the breath the flesh would already be ruined. For this I was punished and forbidden to live again among the living.

entries.zh: 公中夏之相輔也，今為謁中天之祠，若以某姓名求之，神必許諾。」
entries.en: You are destined to be a chief minister of the Central Realm. Go now and offer prayers at the central shrine of Heaven; if you petition in a certain name, the spirits will surely assent."
entries.literal: You will be a chief minister of the Central Plain. Now go pay your respects at the shrine of Heaven in the Central Plain; if you pray using a certain name, the spirits will surely grant it."

entries.zh: 顗因為之虔禱而還，白衣迎於山下，曰：「余免其苦矣。」
entries.en: Yi prayed earnestly for him and returned. The man in white greeted him at the foot of the mountain and said, "I have been released from my torment."
entries.literal: Yi therefore prayed devoutly on his behalf and returned. The man in white met him at the foot of the mountain and said: "I am freed from my suffering."

entries.zh: 拜謝而退。
entries.en: He bowed in gratitude and departed.
entries.literal: He bowed in thanks and withdrew.

entries.zh: 顗次年擢進士第。
entries.en: The following year Yi passed the jinshi examination.
entries.literal: The next year Yi passed the jinshi examination.

entries.zh: 梁貞明中，歷校書郎、登封令、右補闕、禮部員外郎，召入翰林，累遷至中書舍人。
entries.en: During the Liang Zhenming era he held successive posts as collator, magistrate of Dengfeng, Right Reminder, and vice director of the Ministry of Rites, then was called into the Hanlin Academy and eventually rose to Secretariat drafter.
entries.literal: In the Zhenming era of Liang he served successively as collator, magistrate of Dengfeng, Right Reminder, and Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites; he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy and rose in stages to Secretariat Drafter.

entries.zh: 唐莊宗平梁，以例貶復州司馬，歲餘牽復，授左散騎常侍，歷兵吏部侍郎、尚書左丞。
entries.en: When Tang Zhuangzong conquered Liang, Yi was demoted under precedent to military adjutant of Fuzhou. After a year he was recalled and made Left Regular Attendant, then served as vice minister of war, vice minister of personnel, and left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: When Tang Zhuangzong conquered Liang, Yi was demoted by precedent to military adjutant of Fuzhou; after more than a year he was recalled and appointed Left Regular Attendant, then served as Vice Minister of War, Vice Minister of Personnel, and Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 唐末帝即位，講求輔相，乃書朝中清望官十餘人姓名置於瓶中，清夜焚香而挾之，既而得盧文紀與顗，遂拜中書侍郎、平章事。
entries.en: When the last Tang emperor came to the throne he sought chief ministers. He wrote the names of a dozen eminent officials on slips, placed them in a bottle, burned incense on a clear night, and drew lots. Lu Wenji and Yi were chosen, and both were appointed vice director of the Secretariat and grand councilor.
entries.literal: When the last Tang emperor took the throne he sought chief ministers; he wrote the names of more than ten officials of clear reputation in court on slips, placed them in a bottle, burned incense on a clear night, and drew them. He drew Lu Wenji and Yi, and thereupon appointed them Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 制前一日，嵩山白衣來謁，謂顗曰：「公明日為相。」
entries.en: On the eve of the appointment edict, the man in white from Mount Song came to see Yi and said, "Tomorrow you will become chief minister."
entries.literal: On the day before the edict, the man in white from Mount Song came to visit Yi and said: "Tomorrow you will become chief minister."

entries.zh: 其言無差，冥數固先定矣。
entries.en: His words proved exact; what was ordained in the unseen world had been settled long before.
entries.literal: His words were not in error; fate in the unseen realm had indeed been fixed beforehand.

entries.zh: 高祖登極，罷相為刑部尚書，俄遷戶部尚書。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne he removed Yi from the chief ministership and appointed him minister of justice, then soon made him minister of revenue.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he removed Yi from the chief ministership and made him Minister of Justice, soon transferring him to Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 天福五年冬卒，年七十五。
entries.en: He died in the winter of the fifth Tianfu year, at the age of seventy-five.
entries.literal: He died in winter of the fifth year of Tianfu, aged seventy-five.

entries.zh: 贈左僕射。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as Left Vice Director.
entries.literal: He was posthumously awarded Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 子惟和嗣。
entries.en: His son Weihe succeeded to his line.
entries.literal: His son Weihe succeeded him.

entries.zh: 顗疏於財，而禦家無術，既死，斂葬之資不備，家人俟賻物及鬻第方能舉喪而去。
entries.en: Yi was indifferent to money and inept at running his household. When he died there was not enough for burial; his family had to wait for gifts of condolence and the sale of the house before they could hold the funeral and leave.
entries.literal: Yi was careless with wealth and had no skill in managing the household. After his death the funds for burial were not ready; his family had to wait for condolence gifts and the sale of the residence before they could conduct the funeral and depart.

entries.zh: 士大夫愛其廉而鄙其拙。
entries.en: Men of letters admired his integrity but looked down on his lack of practical sense.
entries.literal: The scholar-officials admired his integrity but despised his dullness.

entries.zh: 呂琦，字輝山，幽州安次人也。
entries.en: Lü Qi, courtesy name Huishan, was a native of Anci in Youzhou.
entries.literal: Lü Qi, style name Huishan, was a man of Anci in Youzhou.

entries.zh: 祖壽，瀛州景城主簿。
entries.en: His grandfather Shou served as recorder of Jingcheng in Yingzhou.
entries.literal: His grandfather Shou was Recorder of Jingcheng in Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 父兗，滄州節度判官，累至檢校右庶子。
entries.en: His father Yan was military adjutant on the Cangzhou circuit and eventually rose to acting Right Household Companion.
entries.literal: His father Yan was military adjutant of Cangzhou and rose in stages to Acting Right Household Companion.

entries.zh: 劉守光攻陷滄州，琦父兗被擒，族之。
entries.en: When Liu Shouguang seized Cangzhou, Qi's father Yan was captured and the entire clan was put to death.
entries.literal: When Liu Shouguang captured Cangzhou, Qi's father Yan was taken and his clan exterminated.

entries.zh: 琦時年十五，為吏追攝，將就戮焉。
entries.en: Qi was only fifteen. Officials pursued and seized him, and he was on the point of execution.
entries.literal: Qi was then fifteen; officials pursued and seized him, and he was about to be executed.

entries.zh: 有趙玉者，幽、薊之義士也，久遊於兗之門下，見琦臨危，乃紿謂監者曰：「此子某之同氣也，幸無濫焉。」
entries.en: A man named Zhao Yu, a champion of You and Ji who had long been attached to Yan's household, saw Qi in mortal danger. He tricked the guard, saying, "This boy is my own brother—please do not harm him wantonly."
entries.literal: There was a Zhao Yu, a man of honor from You and Ji who had long been a guest in Yan's household. Seeing Qi in peril, he deceived the guard, saying: "This boy is my own kin—please do not kill him indiscriminately."

entries.zh: 監者信之，即引之俱去。
entries.en: The guard believed him and let them leave together.
entries.literal: The guard believed him and led them both away together.

entries.zh: 行一舍，琦困於徒步，以足病告，玉負之而行，逾數百里，因變姓名，乞食於路，乃免其禍。
entries.en: After one day's march Qi could go no farther on foot and pleaded a foot ailment. Yu carried him on his back for hundreds of miles. They changed their names and begged along the road, and so escaped disaster.
entries.literal: After traveling one stage, Qi was exhausted on foot and pleaded foot ailment. Yu carried him on his back for several hundred li. They changed their names and begged food along the road, and thus escaped the calamity.

entries.zh: 年弱冠，以家門遇禍，邈無所依，乃勵志勤學，多遊於汾、晉。
entries.en: In his early twenties, with his family destroyed and no one to turn to, he set his mind on study and traveled widely through Fen and Jin.
entries.literal: When he reached young manhood, his family having met calamity and he with nowhere to rely upon, he resolved to study diligently and traveled widely in Fen and Jin.

entries.zh: 唐天祐中，莊宗方開霸府，翹佇賢士，墨制授琦代州軍事判官，秩滿歸太原，監軍使張承業重琦器量，禮遇尤厚。
entries.en: During the Tang Tianyou era Zhuangzong was establishing his headquarters and eagerly sought talented men. By special edict he appointed Qi military adjutant of Daizhou. When his term ended Qi returned to Taiyuan, where Army Supervisor Zhang Chengye admired his character and treated him with exceptional regard.
entries.literal: In the Tianyou era of Tang, Zhuangzong was opening his hegemon's office and eagerly awaited worthy men. By imperial order on black he appointed Qi military adjutant of Daizhou. When his term ended he returned to Taiyuan; Military Commissioner Zhang Chengye valued Qi's capacity and treated him with exceptional courtesy.

entries.zh: 天成初，拜琦殿中侍御史，遷駕部員外郎，兼侍御史知雜事。
entries.en: At the start of the Tiancheng era Qi was made attending censor in the palace, then promoted to vice director of the transport office while also serving as censor-in-chief of miscellaneous affairs.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, Qi was appointed Attending Censor in the Palace and promoted to Vice Director of the Transport Office, concurrently serving as Censor-in-Chief of Miscellaneous Affairs.

entries.zh: 會河陽帑吏竊財事發，詔軍巡院鞫之。
entries.en: When a treasury clerk in Heyang was found to have embezzled funds, the court ordered the Military Patrol Office to investigate.
entries.literal: When the theft of treasury funds by a clerk in Heyang came to light, an edict ordered the Military Patrol Office to investigate.

entries.zh: 時軍巡使尹訓怙勢納賂，枉直相反，俄有訴冤於闕下者，詔琦按之，既驗其奸，乃上言請治尹訓，沮而不行。
entries.en: The military patrol commissioner Yin Xun abused his power and took bribes, perverting justice. Soon a petitioner brought a grievance to the palace. Qi was ordered to investigate; once the fraud was confirmed he memorialized for Yin Xun's punishment, but the request was blocked.
entries.literal: The Military Patrol Commissioner Yin Xun relied on power and accepted bribes, reversing right and wrong. Soon someone appealed injustice at the palace gates. Qi was ordered to investigate; having verified the wrongdoing, he submitted a memorial requesting punishment of Yin Xun, but it was blocked and not carried out.

entries.zh: 琦連奏不已，訓知其不免，自殺於家，其獄遂明，蒙活者甚眾，自是朝廷多琦之公直。
entries.en: Qi kept submitting memorials without letup. Xun knew he could not escape and killed himself at home. The case was finally cleared, and many who would have been condemned were spared. From then on the court widely praised Qi's integrity.
entries.literal: Qi submitted memorial after memorial without cease. Xun knew he could not escape and killed himself at home. The case was then cleared, and very many who would have died were spared. From this the court greatly esteemed Qi's fairness and integrity.

entries.zh: 高祖建義於太原，唐末帝幸懷州，趙德鈞駐軍於團柏谷，末帝以琦嘗在德鈞幕下，因令賫都統使官告以賜之，且犒其軍焉。
entries.en: When Gaozu raised his banner at Taiyuan, the last Tang emperor went to Huai Prefecture while Zhao Dejun camped at Tuanbai Valley. Because Qi had once served on Dejun's staff, the emperor sent him bearing the commander-in-chief's commission as a gift to Dejun and to reward his troops.
entries.literal: When Gaozu raised righteous arms at Taiyuan, the last Tang emperor went to Huai Prefecture and Zhao Dejun encamped at Tuanbai Valley. Because Qi had once served in Dejun's staff, the last emperor had him carry the commission of commander-in-chief to present to Dejun and also reward his army.

entries.zh: 及觀軍於北陲，館於忻州，會晉祖降下晉安寨，遣使告於近郡，琦適遇其使，即斬之以聞，尋率郡兵千人間道而歸。
entries.en: While inspecting troops on the northern frontier he was stationed at Xin Prefecture. The Jin founder had taken Jin'an Stockade and sent messengers to the neighboring prefectures. Qi happened upon one of them, executed him and reported it, then led a thousand local troops back by a secret route.
entries.literal: When he went to review troops on the northern frontier he lodged at Xin Prefecture. The Jin founder had taken Jin'an Stockade and sent envoys to notify nearby prefectures. Qi happened upon one of the envoys, beheaded him and reported it, then led a thousand prefectural troops by a hidden route back.

entries.zh: 高祖入洛，亦弗之責，止改授秘書監而已。
entries.en: When Gaozu entered Luoyang he did not reproach him, but only reassigned him as director of the Palace Library.
entries.literal: When Gaozu entered Luoyang he did not blame him either, merely transferring him to Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 天福中，預修《唐書》，權掌選部，皆有能名焉。
entries.en: During the Tianfu era he helped compile the History of Tang and held acting charge of the Selection Bureau, earning a name for competence in both.
entries.literal: In the Tianfu era he took part in compiling the History of Tang and held acting charge of the Selection Bureau; in all these he won a reputation for ability.

entries.zh: 累遷禮部、刑部、戶部、兵部侍郎，階至金紫光祿大夫，爵至開國子。
entries.en: He rose through successive posts as vice minister of rites, justice, revenue, and war, attaining the rank of Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Bright Hall and the title Viscount of a Founding State.
entries.literal: He rose in stages to Vice Minister of Rites, Justice, Revenue, and War, reaching the rank of Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Bright Hall and the title Baron of a founding state.

entries.zh: 琦美風儀，有器概，雖以剛直聞於時，而內實仁恕。
entries.en: Qi had a dignified presence and true breadth of character. Though famed in his day for uncompromising integrity, at heart he was gentle and forgiving.
entries.literal: Qi had fine bearing and great capacity. Though known in his time for stern uprightness, inwardly he was truly benevolent and forgiving.

entries.zh: 初，高祖謀求輔相，時宰臣李崧力薦琦於高祖，雲可大用。
entries.en: When Gaozu was seeking chief ministers, Chief Minister Li Song strongly recommended Qi to him, saying he was fit for the highest office.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu sought chief ministers, the chief minister Li Song strongly recommended Qi to Gaozu, saying he could be greatly employed.

entries.zh: 高祖數召琦於便殿，言及當世事，甚奇之，方將倚以為相，忽遇疾而逝，人皆惜之。
entries.en: Gaozu repeatedly summoned Qi to the informal hall to discuss affairs of state and came to admire him greatly. He was on the verge of making Qi chief minister when Qi suddenly fell ill and died. Everyone mourned the loss.
entries.literal: Gaozu repeatedly summoned Qi to the informal hall and spoke of current affairs; he greatly admired him and was about to rely on him as chief minister, when Qi suddenly fell ill and died. All regretted it.

entries.zh: 梁文矩，字德儀，鄆州人。
entries.en: Liang Wenju, courtesy name Deyi, was a native of Yunzhou.
entries.literal: Liang Wenju, style name Deyi, was a man of Yunzhou.

entries.zh: 父景，秘書少監。
entries.en: His father Jing served as vice director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: His father Jing was Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 梁福王友璋好接賓客，文矩少遊其門，初試太子校書，轉秘書郎。
entries.en: Prince Youzhang of Fu in Liang loved to entertain guests, and Wenju frequented his household as a young man. He first passed the examination for collator of the heir apparent, then became a secretary.
entries.literal: Prince of Fu of Liang Youzhang loved to receive guests; Wenju in youth frequented his house. He first passed the examination for collator of the Heir Apparent, then became Secretary.

entries.zh: 友璋領鄆州，奏為項城令，及移鎮徐方，辟為從事。
entries.en: When Youzhang governed Yunzhou he recommended Wenju as magistrate of Xiangcheng. When he transferred his command to Xuzhou he took Wenju on as an aide.
entries.literal: When Youzhang held Yunzhou he memorialized Wenju as magistrate of Xiangcheng; when he moved his command to Xuzhou he recruited him as aide.

entries.zh: 友璋卒，改兗州觀察判官。
entries.en: After Youzhang's death Wenju became observation commissioner adjutant of Yanzhou.
entries.literal: When Youzhang died, Wenju became observation commissioner adjutant of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 時莊宗遣明宗襲據鄆州，文矩以父母在鄆，一旦隔越，不知存亡，為子之情，戀望如灼，遂間路歸鄆，尋謁莊宗。
entries.en: Zhuangzong had sent Mingzong to seize Yunzhou by surprise. Wenju's parents were there, and overnight he was cut off from them with no word of their fate. Filial longing burned in him, and he made his way back to Yun by a hidden route, then presented himself to Zhuangzong.
entries.literal: At that time Zhuangzong sent Mingzong to seize Yunzhou by surprise. Wenju's parents were in Yun; suddenly cut off, he did not know whether they lived or died. Filial feeling burned in him like fire, and he took a secret route back to Yun, then soon presented himself to Zhuangzong.

entries.zh: 莊宗喜之，授天平軍節度掌書記，在明宗幕下。
entries.en: Zhuangzong was pleased and appointed him secretary on the Tianping military commission, serving on Mingzong's staff.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong was pleased with him and appointed him secretary on the Tianping military commission staff under Mingzong.

entries.zh: 明宗歷汴、恒二鎮，皆隨府遷職。
entries.en: Mingzong held the Bian and Heng commands in turn, and Wenju followed him in each transfer.
entries.literal: Mingzong served the two commands of Bian and Heng; Wenju followed the headquarters in each transfer of post.

entries.zh: 天成初，授右諫議大夫，知宣武軍軍州事，歷御史中丞、吏部侍郎、禮部尚書、西都副留守，判京兆府事，縱改兵部尚書。
entries.en: At the start of Tiancheng he was appointed Right Remonstrance Councilor with charge of Xuanwu military and prefectural affairs, then served as censor-in-chief, vice minister of personnel, minister of rites, deputy protector of the western capital with concurrent administration of the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture, and eventually minister of war.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was made Right Remonstrance Councilor and given charge of military and prefectural affairs of the Xuanwu Army; he served successively as Censor-in-Chief, Vice Minister of Personnel, Minister of Rites, Western Capital Deputy Protector, and concurrent administrator of the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture, and was eventually made Minister of War.

entries.zh: 文矩以嘗事霸府，每懷公輔之望。
entries.en: Having once served in the founding ruler's headquarters, he always hoped for appointment as chief minister.
entries.literal: Because Wenju had once served the hegemon's office, he always harbored hopes of becoming chief minister.

entries.zh: 時高祖自外鎮入覲，嘗薦於明宗曰：「梁文矩早事陛下，甚有勤勞，未升相輔，外論慊之。」
entries.en: When Gaozu came from a frontier command to pay court, he once said to Mingzong, "Liang Wenju served you early on with great diligence. He has not been made chief minister, and people outside the court feel the injustice of it."
entries.literal: When Gaozu came from an outer command to pay court, he once recommended to Mingzong: "Liang Wenju served Your Majesty early and with great diligence; he has not been raised to chief minister, and public opinion resents it."

entries.zh: 明宗曰：「久忘此人，吾之過也。」
entries.en: Mingzong said, "I had forgotten him entirely—that was my fault."
entries.literal: Mingzong said: "I had long forgotten this man—it is my fault."

entries.zh: 尋有旨降命，會丁外憂而止。
entries.en: An appointment edict was soon to follow, but the matter ended when he entered mourning for his father.
entries.literal: Soon an edict was about to be issued, but it stopped when he entered mourning for his father.

entries.zh: 清泰初，拜太常卿。
entries.en: At the start of the Qingtai era he was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 高祖即位，授吏部尚書，改太子少師。
entries.en: When Gaozu came to the throne he was appointed minister of personnel, then made junior tutor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he was made Minister of Personnel, then transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 文矩喜清靜之教，聚道書數千卷，企慕赤松、留侯之事，而服食尤盡其善。
entries.en: Wenju embraced the Daoist ideal of stillness and purity, gathered several thousand volumes of Daoist texts, and looked up to the legends of Master Redpine and the Marquis of Liu. In dietary alchemy he pursued the art to its fullest.
entries.literal: Wenju delighted in the teaching of stillness and purity, collected several thousand volumes of Daoist books, and yearned after the affairs of Chisong and the Marquis of Liu; in taking elixirs he especially pursued them to perfection.

entries.zh: 後因風痹，上章請退，以太子太保致仕，居洛陽久之。
entries.en: Later he developed rheumatism, submitted a memorial asking to retire, and left office as grand guardian of the heir apparent, living in Luoyang for many years.
entries.literal: Later, because of wind paralysis, he submitted a memorial requesting retirement and left office as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, residing long in Luoyang.

entries.zh: 天福八年，以疾卒，時年五十九。
entries.en: In the eighth Tianfu year he died of illness at the age of fifty-nine.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Tianfu he died of illness, aged fifty-nine.

entries.zh: 贈太子太傅。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as grand tutor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 史圭，常山人也。
entries.en: Shi Gui was a native of Changshan.
entries.literal: Shi Gui was a man of Changshan.

entries.zh: 其先與王武俊來於塞外，因家石邑。
entries.en: His forebears had come from beyond the frontier with Wang Wujun and made their home in Shiyi.
entries.literal: His ancestors came from beyond the frontier with Wang Wujun and settled their household in Shiyi.

entries.zh: 高祖曾，歷鎮陽牙校。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Zeng had served as a military clerk at Zhenyang.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Zeng had served as a military clerk at Zhenyang.

entries.zh: 父鈞，假安平、九門令。
entries.en: His father Jun had served as acting magistrate of Anping and Jiumen.
entries.literal: His father Jun had been acting magistrate of Anping and Jiumen.

entries.zh: 圭好學工詩，長於吏道。
entries.en: Gui loved learning and wrote poetry well, and he excelled in administrative affairs.
entries.literal: Gui loved learning and was skilled in poetry, excelling in the ways of administration.

entries.zh: 唐光化中，歷阜城、饒陽尉，改房子、寧晉、元氏、樂壽、博陸五邑令。
entries.en: During the Tang Guanghua era he served as assistant magistrate of Fucheng and Raoyang, then held successive magistracies in Fangzi, Ningjin, Yuanshi, Leshou, and Bolu.
entries.literal: In the Guanghua era of Tang he served as assistant magistrate of Fucheng and Raoyang, then became magistrate in turn of the five districts of Fangzi, Ningjin, Yuanshi, Leshou, and Bolu.

entries.zh: 為寧晉日，擅給驛廩，以貸饑民，民甚感之。
entries.en: As magistrate of Ningjin he on his own authority opened the post-station granaries to lend grain to the starving, and the people were deeply grateful.
entries.literal: While magistrate of Ningjin he on his own authority issued post-station grain stores to lend to famine victims; the people were deeply moved.

entries.zh: 及為樂壽令，里人為之立碑。
entries.en: When he became magistrate of Leshou, the local people erected a stele in his honor.
entries.literal: When he became magistrate of Leshou, the villagers erected a stele for him.

entries.zh: 同光中，任圜為真定尹，擢為本府司錄，不應命。
entries.en: During the Tongguang era Ren Yuan was prefect of Zhending and offered Gui the post of prefectural recorder, but Gui declined.
entries.literal: In the Tongguang era Ren Yuan was prefect of Zhending and promoted Gui to recorder of the prefecture, but he did not accept the appointment.

entries.zh: 郭崇韜領其地，辟為從事，及明宗代崇韜，以舊職縻之。
entries.en: Guo Chongtao governed the region and recruited him as an aide. When Mingzong replaced Chongtao he retained Gui in the same post.
entries.literal: Guo Chongtao held that territory and recruited him as aide; when Mingzong replaced Chongtao he kept Gui in his former post.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，入為文昌正郎，安重誨薦為河南少尹，判府事，尋命為樞密院直學士。
entries.en: When Mingzong came to the throne Gui entered court as regular gentleman of Wenchang. An Chonghui recommended him as vice prefect of Henan with charge of prefectural affairs, and soon he was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne Gui entered court as Regular Gentleman of Wenchang. An Chonghui recommended him as Vice Prefect of Henan with concurrent administration of prefectural affairs, and soon he was appointed Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 時圭以受知於重誨，重誨奏令圭與同列閻至俱升殿侍立，以備顧問，明宗可之。
entries.en: Gui had won Chonghui's confidence. Chonghui memorialized that Gui and his colleague Yan Zhi should both attend in the hall to stand ready for consultation, and Mingzong agreed.
entries.literal: At that time Gui had won Chonghui's trust. Chonghui memorialized that Gui and his colleague Yan Zhi should both ascend the hall to attend and stand by, to be ready for consultation; Mingzong approved.

entries.zh: 尋自左諫議大夫拜尚書右丞，有入相之望。
entries.en: Soon he was promoted from Left Remonstrance Councilor to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and seemed headed for the chief ministership.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted from Left Remonstrance Councilor to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with prospects of entering the chief ministership.

entries.zh: 圭敏於吏事，重誨本不知書，為事剛愎，每於明宗前可否重務，圭恬然終日，不能剖正其事。
entries.en: Gui was quick in administrative matters, but Chonghui was unlearned and headstrong. Whenever Chonghui approved or rejected weighty matters before Mingzong, Gui would sit placidly all day without correcting him.
entries.literal: Gui was sharp in administrative affairs, but Chonghui was by nature unlettered and obstinate in conduct. Whenever he approved or rejected weighty matters before Mingzong, Gui remained placid all day and could not set the affairs straight.

entries.zh: 長興中，重誨既誅，圭出為貝州刺史，未幾罷免，退歸常山。
entries.en: During the Changxing era, after Chonghui was executed, Gui was posted as prefect of Beizhou. Before long he was removed and retired to Changshan.
entries.literal: In the Changxing era, after Chonghui was executed, Gui was sent out as Prefect of Beizhou; before long he was dismissed and retired to Changshan.

entries.zh: 由是閉門杜絕人事，雖親戚故人造者不見其面，每遊別墅，則乘婦人氈車以自蔽匿，人莫知其心。
entries.en: Thereafter he shut his doors to the world. Even kin and old friends who called on him could not see his face. When he visited his country estate he rode in a woman's covered cart to conceal himself, and no one could fathom his thoughts.
entries.literal: Thereafter he shut his door and cut off all human contact; even when kin and old friends came calling he would not show his face. Whenever he visited his country villa he rode in a woman's felt cart to hide himself, and no one knew his mind.

entries.zh: 高祖登極，征為刑部侍郎，判鹽鐵副使，皆宰臣馮道之奏請也。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne Gui was summoned as vice minister of justice and deputy commissioner of the Salt and Iron Monopoly, all on Chief Minister Feng Dao's recommendation.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he was summoned as Vice Minister of Justice and concurrent Deputy Commissioner of the Salt and Iron Monopoly—all on the memorial request of Chief Minister Feng Dao.

entries.zh: 始圭在明宗時為右丞，權判銓事，道在中書，嘗以堂判衡銓司所註官，圭怒，力爭之，道亦微有不足之色，至是圭首為道所舉，方愧其度量遠不及也。
entries.en: Earlier, when Gui was Right Vice Director under Mingzong with charge of selection affairs, Dao in the Secretariat had once used a chief minister's ruling to overturn the Selection Bureau's appointments. Gui had been furious and fought him hard; Dao too had shown displeasure. Now Gui was the first person Dao recommended, and he was ashamed to find how far Dao's magnanimity surpassed his own.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Gui was Right Vice Director under Mingzong with acting charge of selection affairs, Dao was in the Secretariat and once used a chief-minister's ruling to overturn appointments registered by the Selection Bureau. Gui was angry and argued forcefully; Dao too showed a slight look of displeasure. Now Gui was the first whom Dao recommended, and he felt ashamed that his magnanimity fell far short.

entries.zh: 旋改吏部侍郎，分知銓事，而圭素厲廉守節，大著公平之譽。
entries.en: He was soon made vice minister of personnel with divided charge of selection affairs. Gui had always been strict in integrity, and he won wide renown for impartiality.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel with divided charge of selection affairs. Gui had always been strict in integrity and upholding principle, and won a great reputation for fairness.

entries.zh: 吳承範，字表微，魏州人也。
entries.en: Wu Chengfan, courtesy name Biaowei, was a native of Weizhou.
entries.literal: Wu Chengfan, style name Biaowei, was a man of Weizhou.

entries.zh: 父瓊，右金吾衛將軍，累贈太子少保。
entries.en: His father Qiong was general of the Right Gold Crow Guard and was posthumously honored on successive occasions as junior guardian of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: His father Qiong was General of the Right Gold Crow Guard and was repeatedly posthumously honored as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 承範少好學，善屬文，唐閔帝之鎮鄴都也，聞其才名，署為賓職，承範懇求隨計，閔帝許之。
entries.en: From youth Chengfan loved learning and was skilled at literary composition. When the Tang Emperor Min was stationed at Yedu, he heard of Chengfan's talent and reputation and appointed him as a guest official. Chengfan earnestly asked to accompany him on the tribute journey to the capital, and Emperor Min agreed.
entries.literal: Chengfan from youth loved learning and was skilled at literary composition. When the Tang Emperor Min was posted at Yedu, he heard of Chengfan's talent and reputation and appointed him as a guest official. Chengfan earnestly requested to accompany him on the tribute journey, and Emperor Min permitted it.

entries.zh: 長興三年春，擢進士第。
entries.en: In spring of the third year of Changxing he passed the jinshi examination.
entries.literal: In spring of the third year of Changxing, he was selected as a jinshi.

entries.zh: 及閔帝即位，授左拾遺。
entries.en: When Emperor Min took the throne, he was appointed Left Reminder.
entries.literal: When Emperor Min ascended the throne, he was appointed Left Reminder.

entries.zh: 清泰二年，以本官充史館修撰，與同職張昭遠等共修《明宗實錄》，轉右補闕，依前充職。
entries.en: In the second year of Qingtai, while retaining his existing post he was made compiler at the Historiography Institute and, together with fellow compiler Zhang Zhaoyuan and others, jointly compiled the Veritable Record of Emperor Mingzong. He was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor and continued in the same office.
entries.literal: In the second year of Qingtai, in his existing capacity he was made Compiler at the Historiography Institute and together with fellow compiler Zhang Zhaoyuan and others jointly compiled the Veritable Record of Emperor Mingzong. He was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor and continued in his former office.

entries.zh: 高祖革命，遷尚書屯田員外郎、知制誥。
entries.en: When Gaozu founded the dynasty, he was promoted to vice director of the Agricultural Colonies Bureau in the Ministry of Works and drafter of edicts.
entries.literal: When Gaozu founded the new dynasty, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Agricultural Colonies Bureau in the Ministry of Works and Drafter of Edicts.

entries.zh: 天福三年，改樞密院直學士，未幾，自祠部郎中、知制誥召充翰林學士，正拜中書舍人，賜金紫。
entries.en: In the third year of Tianfu he was made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Before long, from his post as director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and drafter of edicts he was summoned to serve as Hanlin academician, formally appointed Secretariat drafter, and granted gold and purple insignia.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianfu he was changed to Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Before long, from his post as Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and Drafter of Edicts he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician, formally appointed Secretariat Drafter, and granted gold and purple insignia.

entries.zh: 少帝嗣位，遷禮部侍郎，知貢舉，尋遘疾而卒，年四十二。
entries.en: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was promoted to vice minister of rites and placed in charge of the examinations. Soon after he fell ill and died at the age of forty-two.
entries.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and placed in charge of the examinations. Soon after he fell ill and died, aged forty-two.

entries.zh: 贈工部尚書。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as minister of works.
entries.literal: He was posthumously awarded Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 承範溫厚寡言，善希人旨，桑維翰、李崧尤重之，嘗薦於高祖，雲可大用。
entries.en: Wu Chengfan was gentle and sparing of words, adept at reading others' wishes. Sang Weihan and Li Song held him in special regard and once recommended him to Gaozu as fit for high office.
entries.literal: Chengfan was mild and reticent, skilled at discerning others' intent. Sang Weihan and Li Song especially valued him and once recommended him to Gaozu, saying he could be greatly employed.

entries.zh: 承範知之，持重自養，雖遇盛夏，而猶服襦袴，加之以純綿，蓋慮有寒濕之患也。
entries.en: Chengfan understood this and kept himself in careful reserve. Even in midsummer he still wore jacket and trousers lined with cotton, lest he suffer from cold and damp.
entries.literal: Chengfan knew this and cultivated himself with restraint. Even in midsummer he still wore jacket and trousers with pure cotton added, fearing ailments from cold and damp.

entries.zh: 然竟不獲其志，其命也夫！
entries.en: Yet in the end he never attained his ambition—such was fate!
entries.literal: Yet in the end he did not realize his ambition—such was his fate!

entries.zh: 王權，字秀山，太原人，積世衣冠。
entries.en: Wang Quan, courtesy name Xiushan, was a native of Taiyuan from a long line of officials.
entries.literal: Wang Quan, style name Xiushan, was a man of Taiyuan from a family of officials for generations.

entries.zh: 曾祖起，官至左僕射、山南西道節度使，冊贈太尉，謚曰文懿，唐史有傳。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Qi rose to Left Vice Director and military commissioner of the Shannan West circuit, was posthumously honored as grand marshal with the posthumous title Wenyi, and has a biography in the Tang histories.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Qi rose to Left Vice Director and military commissioner of the Shannan West circuit; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal with the posthumous title Weny, and has a biography in the Tang histories.

entries.zh: 祖龜，浙東觀察使。
entries.en: His grandfather Gui was observation commissioner of Zhedong.
entries.literal: His grandfather Gui was observation commissioner of Zhedong.

entries.zh: 父蕘，右司員外郎。
entries.en: His father Rao was vice director of the Right Department.
entries.literal: His father Rao was Vice Director of the Right Department.

entries.zh: 權舉進士，解褐授秘書省校書郎、集賢校理，歷左拾遺、右補闕。
entries.en: Quan passed the jinshi examination. Upon entering service he was appointed collator in the Secretariat and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then served as Left and Right Reminder.
entries.literal: Quan passed the jinshi examination; upon leaving office robes he was appointed collator in the Secretariat and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and served as Left and Right Reminder.

entries.zh: 梁祖革命，御史司憲崔沂表為侍御史，遷兼職方員外郎知雜事。
entries.en: When the Liang founder seized power, Censor-in-Chief Cui Yi recommended him as attending censor. He was promoted to concurrent vice director of the Bureau of Appointments with charge of miscellaneous affairs.
entries.literal: When the Liang founder changed the dynasty, Censor-in-Chief Cui Yi memorialized him as Attending Censor; he was promoted to concurrent Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments with charge of miscellaneous affairs.

entries.zh: 歲餘，召入翰林為學士，在院加戶部郎中、知制誥，歷左諫議大夫、給事中，充集賢殿學士判院事，俄拜御史中丞。
entries.en: After a year he was called into the Hanlin as academician, additionally made director of the Ministry of Revenue with charge of drafting edicts, then Left Remonstrance Councilor and attendant, academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the academy, and soon censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was summoned to the Hanlin as academician; while in the academy he was additionally made Director of the Ministry of Revenue with charge of drafting edicts, served as Left Remonstrance Councilor and Attendant, was made Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the academy, and soon was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 唐莊宗平梁，以例出為隨州司馬，會赦，量移許州。
entries.en: When Tang Zhuangzong conquered Liang he was demoted under precedent to military adjutant of Suizhou. An amnesty followed and he was transferred in reduced rank to Xu Prefecture.
entries.literal: When Tang Zhuangzong conquered Liang he was demoted by precedent to military adjutant of Suizhou; an amnesty came and he was transferred in reduced rank to Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 月餘，入為右庶子，遷戶兵吏三侍郎、尚書左丞、禮部尚書判銓。
entries.en: After a month he entered court as Right Household Companion, then rose through the vice ministries of revenue, war, and personnel, became Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and minister of rites with charge of selection.
entries.literal: After more than a month he entered court as Right Household Companion, then was transferred through the three vice ministries of revenue, war, and personnel, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Minister of Rites with charge of selection.

entries.zh: 清泰中，權知貢舉，改戶部尚書，華資美級，罕不由之。
entries.en: During the Qingtai era he had acting charge of the examinations and was made minister of revenue. Few splendid qualifications and fine ranks did not pass through his hands.
entries.literal: In the Qingtai era he had acting charge of the examinations and was changed to Minister of Revenue. Splendid qualifications and fine ranks rarely did not pass through his hands.

entries.zh: 高祖登極，轉兵部尚書。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne he was made minister of war.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he was transferred to Minister of War.

entries.zh: 天福中，命權使於契丹，權以前世累為將相，未嘗有奉使而稱陪臣者，謂人曰：「我雖不才，年今耄矣，豈能遠使於契丹乎！
entries.en: During the Tianfu era Quan was ordered to serve as envoy to the Khitan. His forebears for generations had been generals and chief ministers, yet none had ever been sent abroad to be called a subordinate minister. He told others, "Though I lack talent, I am old now. How could I go on a distant mission to the Khitan?
entries.literal: In the Tianfu era Quan was ordered to serve as envoy to the Khitan. Quan, whose forebears for generations had been generals and chief ministers, had never seen one sent on mission who was called a subordinate minister. He said to others: "Though I lack talent, I am now old—how could I go on a distant mission to the Khitan!

entries.zh: 違詔得罪，亦所甘心。」
entries.en: To disobey the edict and accept punishment is something I would willingly bear."
entries.literal: To disobey the edict and incur punishment is also what I would willingly accept."

entries.zh: 由是停任。
entries.en: The appointment was therefore suspended.
entries.literal: For this the appointment was suspended.

entries.zh: 先是，宰相馮道使於契丹才回，權亦自鳳翔冊禮使回，故責詞略曰：「若以道路迢遙，即鸞閣之臺臣亦往；
entries.en: Chief Minister Feng Dao had just returned from an embassy to the Khitan, and Quan had just returned from Fengxiang as investiture envoy. The reprimand therefore read in part, "If the road is long and distant, ministers of the Phoenix Pavilion also travel;
entries.literal: Earlier Chief Minister Feng Dao had just returned from an embassy to the Khitan, and Quan had also just returned from Fengxiang as envoy for investiture rites. Therefore the reprimand read in part: "If the road is far and distant, then ministers of the Phoenix Pavilion also go;

entries.zh: 若以筋骸衰減，即鳳翔之冊使才回。
entries.en: if one's body is weakened with age, the investiture envoy from Fengxiang has just returned.
entries.literal: if the sinews and bones are weakened with age, then the investiture envoy from Fengxiang has just returned.

entries.zh: 既黷憲章，須從殿黜」云。
entries.en: Having violated the statutes, he must be demoted from court," and so forth.
entries.literal: Having violated the statutes, he must be demoted from the hall," and so on.

entries.zh: 其實權不欲臣事契丹，故堅辭之，非避事以違命也。
entries.en: In truth Quan did not wish to serve the Khitan as a subject, and therefore firmly declined. He was not merely shirking duty to disobey orders.
entries.literal: In truth Quan did not wish to serve the Khitan as a subject, and therefore firmly declined; it was not that he shirked duty to disobey orders.

entries.zh: 逾歲授太子少傅致仕。
entries.en: After more than a year he was made junior tutor of the heir apparent and retired.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was granted Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and retired.

entries.zh: 六年秋，以疾卒，年七十八。
entries.en: In the autumn of the sixth year he died of illness at the age of seventy-eight.
entries.literal: In autumn of the sixth year he died of illness, aged seventy-eight.

entries.zh: 贈左僕射。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as Left Vice Director.
entries.literal: He was posthumously awarded Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 韓惲，字子重，太原晉陽人。
entries.en: Han Yun, courtesy name Zizhong, was a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Han Yun, style name Zizhong, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 曾祖俊，唐龍武大將軍。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Jun was grand general of the Tang Dragon Martial Guard.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Jun was Grand General of the Tang Dragon Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 祖士則，石州司馬。
entries.en: His grandfather Shize was military adjutant of Shi Prefecture.
entries.literal: His grandfather Shize was military adjutant of Shi Prefecture.

entries.zh: 父逵，代州刺史。
entries.en: His father Kui was prefect of Dai Prefecture.
entries.literal: His father Kui was Prefect of Dai Prefecture.

entries.zh: 惲世仕太原，昆仲為軍職，惟惲親狎儒士，好為歌詩，聚書數千卷。
entries.en: The Han family had served at Taiyuan for generations. His brothers held military posts, but Yun alone kept company with scholars, loved to write songs and poems, and collected several thousand books.
entries.literal: The Han family for generations served at Taiyuan; his brothers held military posts, but Yun alone was intimate with scholars, loved to compose songs and poems, and collected several thousand volumes of books.

entries.zh: 乾寧中，後唐莊宗納其妹為妃，初為嫡室，故莊宗深禮其家，而惲以文學署交城、文水令，入為太原少尹。
entries.en: During the Qianning era Zhuangzong of Later Tang took Yun's younger sister as consort. She was at first his principal wife, so Zhuangzong treated the family with great respect. Yun was appointed by literary merit magistrate of Jiaocheng and Wenshui, then became vice prefect of Taiyuan.
entries.literal: In the Qianning era Later Tang Zhuangzong took Yun's younger sister as consort; she was at first the principal wife, so Zhuangzong treated the family with deep courtesy. Yun was appointed by literary merit magistrate of Jiaocheng and Wenshui, then entered service as Vice Prefect of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 莊宗平定趙、魏，為魏州支使。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong pacified Zhao and Wei, Yun served as branch commissioner of Weizhou.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Zhao and Wei, Yun served as branch commissioner of Weizhou.

entries.zh: 莊宗即位，授右散騎常侍，從駕至洛陽，轉尚書戶部侍郎。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong came to the throne Yun was appointed Right Regular Attendant, accompanied the court to Luoyang, and was made vice minister of revenue in the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne Yun was appointed Right Regular Attendant, followed the imperial carriage to Luoyang, and was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue in the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 天成初，改秘書監。
entries.en: At the start of the Tiancheng era he was made director of the Palace Library.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was changed to Director of the Palace Library.

entries.zh: 俄而馮道為丞相，與惲有同幕之舊，以惲性謹厚，尤左右之，尋遷禮部尚書。
entries.en: Soon Feng Dao became chief minister. He and Yun had served on the same staff long before. Feng especially favored Yun for his careful and honest nature, and soon Yun was made minister of rites.
entries.literal: Soon Feng Dao became chief minister; he and Yun had old ties from the same staff. Because Yun was careful and honest, Feng especially favored him, and soon he was promoted to Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 丁內憂，服闋，授戶部尚書。
entries.en: After mourning for his mother he was appointed minister of revenue.
entries.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he was appointed Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 明宗晏駕，馮道為山陵使，引惲為副使。
entries.en: When Mingzong died Feng Dao was commissioner for the imperial tomb and appointed Yun his deputy.
entries.literal: When Mingzong died Feng Dao was commissioner for the imperial tomb and brought Yun in as deputy commissioner.

entries.zh: 清泰初，以充奉之勞，授檢校尚書右僕射、絳州刺史，逾年入為太子賓客。
entries.en: At the start of the Qingtai era, for his service at the funeral, he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and prefect of Jiang Prefecture. After a year he entered court as guest of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, for his labor in the funeral service, he was appointed Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Prefect of Jiang Prefecture; after more than a year he entered court as Guest of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 高祖登極，以惲先朝懿戚，深加禮遇，除授貝州刺史。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne he treated Yun with special courtesy as a kinsman of the former court and appointed him prefect of Bei Prefecture.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, because Yun was a kinsman by marriage of the former court, he treated him with deep courtesy and appointed him Prefect of Bei Prefecture.

entries.zh: 時範延光有跋扈之狀，惲懼其見逼，遲留不敢赴任，高祖不悅，復授太子賓客，尋改兵部尚書。
entries.en: Fan Yanguang was then acting insubordinately. Yun feared being caught in his power, lingered, and dared not take up the post. Gaozu was displeased, made him guest of the heir apparent again, and soon minister of war.
entries.literal: At the time Fan Yanguang showed signs of insubordination. Yun feared being pressed by him, delayed and dared not take up the post. Gaozu was displeased, again appointed him Guest of the Heir Apparent, and soon changed him to Minister of War.

entries.zh: 天福七年夏，車駕在鄴，惲病腳氣，卒於龍興寺，時年六十餘。
entries.en: In the summer of the seventh Tianfu year the court was at Ye. Yun suffered from beriberi and died at Longxing Temple, aged over sixty.
entries.literal: In summer of the seventh year of Tianfu the imperial carriage was at Ye. Yun suffered from foot ailment and died at Longxing Temple, aged over sixty.

entries.zh: 盧質，字子徵，河南人也。
entries.en: Lu Zhi, whose courtesy name was Zizheng, came from Henan.
entries.literal: Lu Zhi, courtesy name Zizheng, was a man of Henan.

entries.zh: 曾祖偲，唐太原府祁縣尉，累贈右僕射。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Si had served as county defender of Qi County in Taiyuan Prefecture under the Tang, and was posthumously promoted by successive honors to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Si was magistrate of Qi County in the Taiyuan prefecture of Tang, and was posthumously ennobled through successive promotions to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 祖衍，唐刑部侍郎、太子賓客，累贈太保。
entries.en: His grandfather Yan had been Vice Minister of Justice and Tutor to the Crown Prince under the Tang, and was posthumously raised by successive honors to Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: His grandfather Yan was Vice Minister of Justice and Tutor to the Crown Prince under Tang, and was posthumously ennobled through successive promotions to Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 父望，唐尚書司勛郎中，累贈太子少傅。
entries.en: His father Wang had served as Director in the Bureau of Merits under the Tang Ministry of Personnel, and was posthumously promoted by successive honors to Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: His father Wang was Director in the Bureau of Merits under the Ministry of Personnel of Tang, and was posthumously ennobled through successive promotions to Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 質幼聰慧，善屬文。
entries.en: From childhood Zhi was exceptionally bright and gifted at literary composition.
entries.literal: Zhi was clever from childhood and skilled at literary composition.

entries.zh: 年十六，陜帥王重盈奏授芮城令，能以色養。
entries.en: At sixteen, Wang Chongying, military governor of Shaanxi, had him appointed magistrate of Ruicheng by imperial order, and he was able to support his parents with devoted filial care.
entries.literal: At age sixteen, Wang Chongying, military governor of Shaanxi, memorialized the throne to appoint him magistrate of Ruicheng; he was able to support his parents with cheerful countenance.

entries.zh: 又為同州澄城令，從私便也。
entries.en: He later served as magistrate of Chengcheng in Tong Prefecture, a post chosen for his own convenience.
entries.literal: He also served as magistrate of Chengcheng in Tong Prefecture, following his personal convenience.

entries.zh: 秩滿改秘書郎，丁母憂，歸河南故裏。
entries.en: When his term ended he was appointed Secretary; after his mother's death he returned to his ancestral home in Henan.
entries.literal: When his term expired he was made Secretary; upon his mother's death he returned to his old home in Henan.

entries.zh: 天祐三年，北遊太原，時李襲吉在武皇幕府，以女妻之。
entries.en: In the third year of Tianyou he went north to Taiyuan, where Li Xiji was then serving on the Martial Emperor's staff and gave him his daughter in marriage.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianyou he traveled north to Taiyuan; at that time Li Xiji was on the staff of the Martial Emperor's headquarters and gave him his daughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 武皇憐其才，承制授檢校兵部郎中，充河東節度掌書記，賜緋魚袋。
entries.en: The Martial Emperor admired his talent and, acting by imperial commission, appointed him acting Director in the Bureau of Military Affairs and secretarial recorder for the Hedong military commission, granting him the scarlet robe and fish tally.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor cherished his talent and, by imperial commission, appointed him acting Director in the Bureau of Military Affairs, to serve as secretarial recorder for the Hedong military commission, and granted him the scarlet robe and fish tally.

entries.zh: 武皇厭代，其弟克寧握兵柄，有嗣襲之望，質與張承業等密謀，同立莊宗為嗣，有翊贊之功。
entries.en: After the Martial Emperor's death his younger brother Kening held the army and hoped to succeed him, but Zhi joined Zhang Chengye and others in a secret plot to install Zhuangzong as heir, earning merit for his loyal support.
entries.literal: When the Martial Emperor passed away, his younger brother Kening held military power and harbored hopes of succeeding to the position; Zhi secretly plotted with Zhang Chengye and others to install Zhuangzong as heir together, and had the merit of assisting and supporting him.

entries.zh: 及莊宗四征，質皆從行。
entries.en: On all four of Zhuangzong's major campaigns, Zhi accompanied the army.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong undertook his four campaigns, Zhi accompanied him on all of them.

entries.zh: 十六年，轉節度判官、檢校禮部尚書。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year he was made adjutant of the military commission and acting Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to military commission adjutant and acting Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 十九年，莊宗將即帝位，命為大禮使，累加至銀青光祿大夫、檢校右僕射。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year, as Zhuangzong prepared to take the throne, he was appointed Director of Grand Ceremonies and was promoted in succession to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year, as Zhuangzong was about to ascend the throne, he was appointed Director of Grand Ceremonies and was promoted in succession to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 二十年，授行臺禮部尚書。
entries.en: In the twentieth year he was appointed Minister of Rites of the mobile imperial secretariat.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Minister of Rites of the mobile imperial secretariat.

entries.zh: 莊宗既登極，欲相之，質性疏逸，不喜居高位，固辭獲免。
entries.en: Once Zhuangzong had taken the throne he wished to make Zhi chief minister, but Zhi was by nature easygoing and aloof and disliked high office; he firmly declined and was excused.
entries.literal: After Zhuangzong had ascended the throne he wished to make Zhi chief minister, but Zhi's nature was free and easy; he did not like holding high office and firmly declined, thereby being excused.

entries.zh: 尋以本官兼太原尹，充北京留守事，未赴任，改戶部尚書、知制誥，充翰林學士承旨。
entries.en: Soon he was additionally appointed Governor of Taiyuan and charged as regent of the northern capital, but before he took up the post he was reassigned as Minister of Revenue, Controller of Edicts, and Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
entries.literal: Soon thereafter, while retaining his original office, he was also made Governor of Taiyuan and charged with the duties of northern capital regent; before he took up the post he was changed to Minister of Revenue, Controller of Edicts, and Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy.

entries.zh: 同光元年冬，從平大梁，權判租庸事，逾月隨駕都洛，旋受詔權知汴州軍府事。
entries.en: In the winter of the first year of Tongguang he followed the conquest of Daliang and was temporarily placed in charge of equal-tax and corvée affairs; a month later he accompanied the court to Luoyang, and soon received orders to serve as acting administrator of the Bianzhou military headquarters.
entries.literal: In the winter of the first year of Tongguang he followed the campaign that pacified Daliang and was temporarily put in charge of the equal-tax and corvée administration; after more than a month he accompanied the imperial procession to Luoyang, and soon received an edict to act as temporary administrator of the Bianzhou military headquarters.

entries.zh: 時孔謙握利權，志在聚斂，累移文於汴，配民放絲，質堅論之，事雖不行，時論賞之。
entries.en: At that time Kong Qian controlled the finances and was intent on squeezing revenue; he repeatedly sent orders to Bian requiring the people to be levied for silk deliveries. Zhi argued vigorously against this, and although the measure was not carried out, public opinion praised him.
entries.literal: At that time Kong Qian held financial power and aimed at accumulation; he repeatedly sent documents to Bian ordering the populace levied to deliver silk, and Zhi argued against it firmly; although the matter was not carried out, contemporary opinion praised him.

entries.zh: 俄又改金紫光祿大夫、兵部尚書、知制誥、翰林學士承旨，仍賜論思匡佐功臣。
entries.en: Before long he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Minister of War, Controller of Edicts, and Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and was granted the title Meritorious Minister for Deliberation and Support.
entries.literal: Before long he was again changed to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Minister of War, Controller of Edicts, and Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and was further granted the title of Meritorious Minister for Deliberation and Support.

entries.zh: 會覆試進士，質以「後從諫則聖」為賦題，以「堯、舜、禹、湯傾心求過」為韻，舊例賦韻四平四側，質所出韻乃五平三側，由是大為識者所誚。
entries.en: When the repeat examination for presented scholars was held, Zhi set the fu topic "He who later follows remonstrance is sage" with the rhyme phrase "Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang bent their hearts to seek their faults." By precedent fu rhymes required four level tones and four oblique tones, but Zhi's set had five level and three oblique, and learned opinion mocked him roundly for it.
entries.literal: When the repeat examination for presented scholars was held, Zhi set the fu topic as "He who later follows remonstrance is sage" and the rhyme words as "Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang bent their hearts to seek their faults"; by old precedent fu rhymes were four level tones and four oblique tones, but the rhymes Zhi produced were five level and three oblique, and on this account he was greatly ridiculed by the learned.

entries.zh: 天成元年，制授特進、檢校司空、同州節度使。
entries.en: In the first year of Tiancheng he was appointed by edict Special Advancement, acting Minister of Works, and military governor of Tong Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng, by imperial edict he was appointed Special Advancement, acting Minister of Works, and military governor of Tong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 時宰相馮道以詩餞別，其警句云：「視草北來唐學士，擁旄西去漢將軍。」
entries.en: Chief Minister Feng Dao wrote a farewell poem whose memorable lines ran: "A Tang academician come from the north to draft edicts, a Han general going west bearing his commander's banner."
entries.literal: At that time Chief Minister Feng Dao composed a farewell poem; its striking lines read: "A Tang academician come from the north to draft edicts, a Han general going west bearing his commander's banner."

entries.zh: 儒者榮之。
entries.en: Men of learning regarded this as a great honor.
entries.literal: Men of learning took it as an honor.

entries.zh: 明年，改賜耀忠匡定保節功臣，就加檢校司徒。
entries.en: The following year he was granted the title Meritorious Minister for Glorious Loyalty, Rectification, and Preservation of Integrity and was further promoted to acting Minister of Education.
entries.literal: The next year he was granted the title of Meritorious Minister for Glorious Loyalty, Rectification, and Preservation of Integrity, and was further appointed acting Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 三年，入拜兵部尚書，判太僕卿事。
entries.en: In the third year he entered court as Minister of War and was concurrently charged with the duties of Director of the Imperial Stud.
entries.literal: In the third year he entered court and was appointed Minister of War, with concurrent duty as acting Director of the Imperial Stud.

entries.zh: 四年，進封開國公。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as Duke Who Establishes the State.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke Who Establishes the State.

entries.zh: 長興二年，授檢校太保、河陽節度使，未幾，移鎮滄州，入為右僕射。
entries.en: In the second year of Changxing he was appointed acting Grand Mentor and military governor of Heyang; soon he was transferred to Cang Prefecture, then recalled to court as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: In the second year of Changxing he was appointed acting Grand Mentor and military governor of Heyang; before long he was transferred to command Cang Prefecture, then entered court as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 及秦王得罪，奉詔權知河南府事。
entries.en: When the Prince of Qin fell from favor, he was ordered to serve as acting administrator of Henan Prefecture.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Qin fell from favor, he received an edict to act as temporary administrator of Henan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 應順初，遷檢校太傅，正拜河南尹，後改太子少師。
entries.en: At the beginning of Yingshun he was promoted to acting Grand Preceptor and formally appointed Governor of Henan; he was later made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yingshun he was promoted to acting Grand Preceptor and formally appointed Governor of Henan; later he was changed to Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 清泰末，復為右僕射。
entries.en: Late in Qingtai he again became Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: At the end of Qingtai he again became Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 高祖登極，質以微恙分司洛宅。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Zhi, suffering a minor illness, held a nominal post at his Luoyang residence.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Zhi, because of a minor ailment, served in a nominal post at his Luoyang residence.

entries.zh: 少帝嗣位，拜太子太保。
entries.en: When the Lesser Emperor succeeded to the throne, Zhi was appointed Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: When the Lesser Emperor succeeded to the throne, Zhi was appointed Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 天福七年秋，卒於洛陽，年七十六。
entries.en: In the autumn of the seventh year of Tianfu he died in Luoyang at the age of seventy-six.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year of Tianfu he died in Luoyang at age seventy-six.

entries.zh: 累贈太子太師，謚曰文忠。
entries.en: He was posthumously promoted by successive honors to Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince and was given the posthumous title Wenzhong.
entries.literal: He was posthumously ennobled through successive promotions to Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince, and was given the posthumous title Wenzhong.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：漢乾祐元年九月，其子尚書兵部員外郎盧瓊上章請謚，下太常議，謚曰文忠。）〉
entries.en: (From the Essentials of the Five Dynasties: In the ninth month of the first year of Gan you of Han, his son Lu Qiong, Outer Director in the Bureau of Military Affairs under the Ministry of War, submitted a memorial requesting a posthumous title; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was ordered to deliberate, and the posthumous title Wenzhong was granted.)〉
entries.literal: (From the Essentials of the Five Dynasties: In the ninth month of the first year of Gan you of Han, his son Lu Qiong, Outer Director in the Bureau of Military Affairs under the Ministry of War, submitted a memorial requesting a posthumous title; the matter was referred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for deliberation, and the posthumous title Wenzhong was granted.)〉

entries.zh: 李專美，字翊商，京兆萬年人也。
entries.en: Li Zhuanmei, whose courtesy name was Yishang, came from Wannian in Jingzhao.
entries.literal: Li Zhuanmei, courtesy name Yishang, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 曾祖隨，光祿卿。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Sui had been Director of the Imperial Banquets.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Sui was Director of the Imperial Banquets.

entries.zh: 祖正範，尚書庫部郎中。
entries.en: His grandfather Zhengfan had been Director in the Bureau of Storehouses under the Ministry of Works.
entries.literal: His grandfather Zhengfan was Director in the Bureau of Storehouses under the Ministry of Works.

entries.zh: 專美少篤學文，以父樞唐昭宗時常應進士舉，為覆試所落，不許再入，專美心愧之，由是不遊文場。
entries.en: Zhuanmei from youth was devoted to scholarship and letters. His father Shu had once taken the presented-scholar examination under Emperor Zhaozong of Tang but was failed in the repeat examination and barred from re-entry; ashamed on his father's account, Zhuanmei never entered the examination arena himself.
entries.literal: Zhuanmei from youth was devoted to learning and literature; because his father Shu in the time of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang had once entered the presented-scholar examination and was failed in the repeat examination and not permitted to enter again, Zhuanmei felt ashamed in his heart and on this account did not enter the literary arena.

entries.zh: 偽梁貞明中，河南尹張全義以專美名族之後，奏為陸渾尉，秩滿，改舞陽令。
entries.en: During the Zhenming era of the Liang, Zhang Quanyi, Governor of Henan, because Zhuanmei came from a distinguished clan, had him appointed sheriff of Luhun; when his term ended he was made magistrate of Wuyang.
entries.literal: In the Zhenming era of the false Liang, Zhang Quanyi, Governor of Henan, because Zhuanmei was descended from a famous clan, memorialized the throne to appoint him sheriff of Luhun; when his term expired he was changed to magistrate of Wuyang.

entries.zh: 專美性廉謹，大著政聲。
entries.en: Zhuanmei was by nature incorrupt and cautious, and his administrative reputation was excellent.
entries.literal: Zhuanmei's nature was incorrupt and cautious, and he won great renown for his governance.

entries.zh: 後唐天成中，安邑榷鹽使李肅辟為推官，時唐末帝鎮河中，見其敦雅，心重之。
entries.en: In the Tiancheng era of Later Tang, Li Su, commissioner for the salt monopoly at Anyi, recruited him as investigating officer. The Last Emperor of Tang was then military governor of Hezhong; seeing Zhuanmei's earnest refinement, he came to esteem him highly.
entries.literal: In the Tiancheng era of Later Tang, Li Su, commissioner for the salt monopoly at Anyi, recruited him as investigating officer; at that time the Last Emperor of Tang was military governor of Hezhong, saw his earnest refinement, and valued him in his heart.

entries.zh: 末帝一日曾召肅宴於衙署，專美亦預坐，末帝謂肅曰：「某夜來夢主上召去，與宋王同剃卻頭，何也？」
