entries.en: One day the Last Emperor summoned Su to a banquet at headquarters; Zhuanmei was also present. The Last Emperor said to Su: "Last night I dreamed that the sovereign summoned me and that the Prince of Song and I had our heads shaved together—what can this mean?"
entries.literal: One day the Last Emperor summoned Su to a banquet at the government office; Zhuanmei also took a seat. The Last Emperor said to Su: "Last night I dreamed that the sovereign summoned me away and that the Prince of Song and I had our heads shaved together—what does this mean?"

entries.zh: 坐客都無對者，專美屏人謂曰：「將來必為嗣主。」
entries.en: None of the guests could answer. Zhuanmei drew him aside and said: "You will surely become the heir sovereign."
entries.literal: None of the guests present had any reply; Zhuanmei, drawing him aside from others, said: "In the future you will certainly become the heir sovereign."

entries.zh: 由是愈重焉。
entries.en: From that time the Last Emperor valued him all the more.
entries.literal: From this he valued him all the more.

entries.zh: 末帝留守長安，奏為從事，及移鎮鳳翔，遷為記室。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor served as regent at Chang'an, he had Zhuanmei appointed as staff officer; when he was transferred to Fengxiang, Zhuanmei was promoted to recorder.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor was regent at Chang'an, he memorialized the throne to appoint Zhuanmei as staff officer; when he was transferred to command Fengxiang, Zhuanmei was promoted to recorder.

entries.zh: 末帝即位，除尚書庫部郎中，賜金紫，充樞密院直學士。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor took the throne, Zhuanmei was appointed Director in the Bureau of Storehouses, granted the gold seal and purple robe, and made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor ascended the throne, Zhuanmei was appointed Director in the Bureau of Storehouses under the Ministry of Works, granted the gold seal and purple robe, and made direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 初，末帝起自鳳翔，大許諸軍厚賞。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor first rose from Fengxiang, he had promised the armies lavish rewards.
entries.literal: At first, when the Last Emperor rose from Fengxiang, he had promised the armies lavish rewards.

entries.zh: 洎至洛陽，閱內庫金帛不過二三萬，尋又配率京城戶民，雖行捶楚，亦所獲無幾，末帝憂之。
entries.en: When he reached Luoyang and inspected the inner treasury, he found no more than twenty or thirty thousand in gold and silk. He then levied assessments on the capital's households, but even with beatings the yield was meager, and the Last Emperor was deeply troubled.
entries.literal: When he reached Luoyang and examined the inner treasury, gold and silk amounted to no more than twenty or thirty thousand; soon he also levied assessments on the households of the capital, and even though beating was applied, what was obtained was very little, and the Last Emperor was troubled.

entries.zh: 會專美宿於禁中，末帝召而讓之曰：「卿士人子弟，常言有才術，今致我至此，不能度運以濟時事，留才術何施也！」
entries.en: Once when Zhuanmei was staying in the palace, the Last Emperor summoned and rebuked him: "You are the son of a scholar-official family and always claim talent and ability—yet you have brought me to this pass and cannot read the times to rescue the situation. What good is talent left unused?"
entries.literal: Once when Zhuanmei was lodging in the palace precincts, the Last Emperor summoned and reproached him, saying: "You are the son of a scholar-official family and always speak of having talent and skill; yet you have brought me to this pass and cannot gauge the times to rescue current affairs—of what use is talent and skill left behind!"

entries.zh: 專美惶恐待罪，良久奏曰：「臣才力駑劣，屬當興運，陛下猥垂錄任，無以裨益聖朝，然府藏空竭，軍賞不給，非臣之罪也。
entries.en: Zhuanmei, trembling with fear, waited a long while and then replied: "Your servant's abilities are mean, and though I have had the honor of serving in a time of rising fortune, I have been unable to benefit the court. Yet the treasury is empty and army rewards cannot be paid—this is not my fault.
entries.literal: Zhuanmei, in fear and trembling awaiting punishment, after a long while submitted: "Your servant's talent and strength are mean and inferior; I happened to meet a time of rising fortune, and Your Majesty condescended to employ me, yet I have been unable to benefit the sagely court. Nevertheless, the treasury is empty and exhausted and army rewards cannot be supplied—this is not your servant's fault.

entries.zh: 臣思明宗棄代之際，是時府庫濫賞已竭，繼以鄂王臨朝，紀綱大壞，縱有無限之財賦，不能滿驕軍溪壑之心，所以陛下孤立岐陽而得天下。
entries.en: Consider Mingzong's death: the treasury had already been drained by reckless rewards. Then the Prince of E held court and discipline collapsed utterly. Even limitless wealth could not have satisfied the insatiable armies. That is why Your Majesty, standing alone at Qiyang, was able to win the realm.
entries.literal: Your servant reflects that at the time when Mingzong passed from the throne, the treasury had already been drained by indiscriminate rewards; this was followed by the Prince of E's holding court, when statutes and discipline were greatly ruined; even if there had been limitless wealth and revenue, it could not have filled the insatiable hearts of the arrogant armies. That is why Your Majesty, isolated at Qiyang, was able to gain the realm.

entries.zh: 臣以為國之存亡，不專在行賞，須刑政立於上，恥格行於下，賞當功，罰當罪，則近於理道也。
entries.en: I believe a state's survival does not depend on rewards alone. Punishment and government must be established above, and the sense of shame must operate below; rewards must match merit and punishments must match crimes—then one approaches the way of good governance.
entries.literal: Your servant considers that whether a state survives or perishes does not depend solely on dispensing rewards; punishments and government must be established above, and the sense of shame must operate below; rewards must match merit and punishments must match crimes—then one approaches the way of reason.

entries.zh: 若陛下不改覆車之轍，以賞無賴之軍，徒困蒸民，存亡未可知也。
entries.en: If Your Majesty does not turn from the path that overturned the cart and keeps rewarding unruly troops, you will only exhaust the people, and whether the state survives is uncertain.
entries.literal: If Your Majesty does not change the track of the overturned cart and uses rewards to satisfy unruly armies, you will only weary the common people, and whether the state survives or perishes cannot be known.

entries.zh: 今宜取見在財賦以給之，不必踐前言而希茍悅。」
entries.en: You should pay them from wealth and revenue actually on hand, and need not fulfill your earlier promises merely to win momentary favor."
entries.literal: Now you should take the wealth and revenue presently available to supply them; you need not fulfill earlier words in hope of momentary favor."

entries.zh: 末帝然之。
entries.en: The Last Emperor agreed.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor approved of this.

entries.zh: 及其行賞，雖不愜於軍士，然洛陽戶民獲免鞭笞之苦，由專美之敷揚也。
entries.en: When rewards were distributed the soldiers were dissatisfied, but the households of Luoyang were spared the lash—thanks to Zhuanmei's advocacy.
entries.literal: When rewards were distributed, although the soldiers were not satisfied, the households of Luoyang were spared the pain of the whip and cudgel—this was due to Zhuanmei's exposition and advocacy.

entries.zh: 尋轉給事中，明年，遷兵部侍郎、端明殿學士，未幾，改檢校尚書右僕射、守秘書監，充宣徽北院使。
entries.en: Soon he was made Supervising Secretary; the next year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance; before long he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, acting Director of the Imperial Library, and Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Supervising Secretary; the next year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance; before long he was changed to acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, acting Director of the Imperial Library, and Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 高祖入洛，以例除名。
entries.en: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, Zhuanmei was removed from office according to precedent.
entries.literal: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, Zhuanmei was removed from office according to precedent.

entries.zh: 三年，復授衛尉少卿，繼遷鴻臚、大理卿。
entries.en: In the third year he was again appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Insignia and was subsequently promoted to Director of the Court of State Ceremonial and Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
entries.literal: In the third year he was again appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Insignia; he was subsequently promoted to Director of the Court of State Ceremonial and Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

entries.zh: 開運中，以病卒，時年六十二。
entries.en: During the Kaiyun era he died of illness at the age of sixty-two.
entries.literal: In the Kaiyun era he died of illness at age sixty-two.

entries.zh: 專美之遠祖本出姑臧大房，與清河小房崔氏、北祖第二房盧氏、昭國鄭氏為四望族，皆不以才行相尚，不以軒冕為貴，雖布衣徒步，視公卿蔑如也。
entries.en: Zhuanmei's remote ancestors came from the great branch of the clan at Guzang. Together with the minor branch of the Cui of Qinghe, the second northern branch of the Lu, and the Zheng of Zhaoguo they formed the four eminent clans. None prized conduct or talent in one another, nor regarded rank and office as honorable; even in plain dress and on foot they looked down on dukes and ministers as beneath notice.
entries.literal: Zhuanmei's remote ancestors originally came from the great branch of the clan at Guzang; together with the minor branch of the Cui clan of Qinghe, the second branch of the northern ancestor of the Lu clan, and the Zheng clan of Zhaoguo they formed the four eminent clans. None of them valued one another for conduct or talent, nor regarded carriage and cap as honorable; even in plain cloth and on foot they looked down on dukes and ministers as if they were nothing.

entries.zh: 男女婚嫁，不雜他姓，欲聘其族，厚贈金帛始許焉。
entries.en: In marriage they would not mix with other surnames; those who wished to marry into these clans had to offer lavish gifts of gold and silk before consent was granted.
entries.literal: In marriage for men and women they did not mix with other surnames; those who wished to betroth into their clans had first to present lavish gifts of gold and silk before consent was granted.

entries.zh: 唐太宗曾降詔以戒其弊風，終莫能改。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong of Tang once issued an edict warning against this corrupt custom, yet it could never be changed.
entries.literal: Emperor Taizong of Tang once issued an edict to warn against this corrupt custom, yet in the end it could not be changed.

entries.zh: 其間有未達者，必曰：「姓崔、盧、李、鄭了，余復何求耶！」
entries.en: Those among them who had not yet attained office would say: "One has the surnames Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng—what more could one want!"
entries.literal: Among them those who had not yet attained office would invariably say: "One has the surnames Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng—what more is there to seek!"

entries.zh: 其遠者，則邈在天表，敻若千里，人罕造其門，浮薄自大，皆此類也。
entries.en: The more remote among them were as distant as the heavens, remote as a thousand li; people rarely crossed their thresholds. Frivolous, shallow, and arrogant—all were of this kind.
entries.literal: The more remote among them were as distant as the heavens above, remote as a thousand li; people rarely came to their gates. Frivolous, shallow, and arrogant—all were of this kind.

entries.zh: 唯專美未嘗以氏族形於口吻，見寒素士大夫，恒恂恂如也，人以此多之。
entries.en: Only Zhuanmei never flaunted his clan name; toward poor and plain scholar-officials he was always respectful and deferential, and people praised him for it.
entries.literal: Only Zhuanmei never let his clan name appear on his lips; when he met poor and plain scholar-officials he was always respectful and deferential, and people for this reason praised him.

entries.zh: 專美職岐下，曾夢具裳簡立嵩山之頂。
entries.en: While serving below Qi, Zhuanmei once dreamed that he stood atop Mount Song in full court dress holding bamboo slips.
entries.literal: While Zhuanmei was serving below Qi, he once dreamed that he stood atop Mount Song fully robed and holding bamboo slips.

entries.zh: 及為端明殿學士，學士李崧同列而班在其上，因以所夢告崧，且言：「某非德非勛，安可久居此位，處吾子之首乎！」
entries.en: When he became academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, Academician Li Song was his colleague, but Zhuanmei ranked above him in court order. He told Song of his dream and said: "I lack both virtue and merit—how can I long hold this position above you!"
entries.literal: When he became academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, Academician Li Song was of the same rank, but Zhuanmei stood above him in court order; he therefore told Song of his dream and moreover said: "I lack both virtue and merit—how can I long hold this position and stand above you!"

entries.zh: 因懇求他官，尋移宣徽使，崧深德之。
entries.en: He earnestly requested another post and was soon transferred to Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat; Song was deeply grateful.
entries.literal: He therefore earnestly requested another office; soon he was transferred to Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, and Song was deeply grateful to him.

entries.zh: 及高祖臨朝，崧為樞密使，與桑維翰同列，維翰與專美亦有舊，乃協力以奏之，遂復朝序，位至九卿。
entries.en: When Gaozu held court, Song was Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and sat with Sang Weihan; Weihan also had old ties with Zhuanmei, and together they memorialized on his behalf. He was restored to court rank and rose to one of the nine ministers.
entries.literal: When Gaozu held court, Song was Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and sat in the same rank as Sang Weihan; Weihan also had old ties with Zhuanmei, and they therefore joined forces to memorialize on his behalf, whereupon he was restored to court order and rose to one of the nine ministers.

entries.zh: 專美曾使閩中，遇風水漂至兩浙，逾歲無恙而還，至是善終，人以為神道福謙之所致也。
entries.en: Zhuanmei had once been sent on mission to Min; he was driven by storm to the two Zhe regions but returned unharmed after more than a year. When he now died a peaceful death, people attributed it to the spirits rewarding his modesty.
entries.literal: Zhuanmei had once been sent on mission to Min; he encountered wind and waves and was carried adrift to the two Zhe regions, but after more than a year returned unharmed; when he now died a peaceful death, people considered it the result of the spirits' blessing the modest.

entries.zh: 薛融，汾州平遙人。
entries.en: Xue Rong came from Pingyao in Fen Prefecture.
entries.literal: Xue Rong was a man of Pingyao in Fen Prefecture.

entries.zh: 性純和，以儒學為業。
entries.en: His nature was pure and gentle, and he devoted himself to Confucian learning.
entries.literal: His nature was pure and gentle; he made Confucian learning his profession.

entries.zh: 初從雲州帥李存璋為幕職，唐莊宗平河南，歷鄆、徐二鎮從事。
entries.en: He first served on the staff of Li Cunzhang, military governor of Yunzhou; after Zhuangzong of Tang pacified Henan, he held aide posts in Yun and Xu in succession.
entries.literal: At first he followed the military governor of Yun Prefecture, Li Cunzhang, as a staff member; when Zhuangzong of Tang pacified Henan, he successively served as aide in the two prefectures of Yan and Xu.

entries.zh: 明宗初，授華州節度判官。
entries.en: At the start of Mingzong's reign he was appointed military governor's aide at Hua Prefecture.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Mingzong's reign, he was appointed military governor's aide at Hua Prefecture.

entries.zh: 長興四年，入為右補闕，直宏文館，歲餘，改河東觀察判官，會高祖鎮太原，遂居於幕府。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Changxing he entered court as Right Supplements Censor and served in the Hongwen Pavilion. After a little over a year he was transferred to be aide to the Hedong observation commissioner, and when Gaozu was stationed at Taiyuan he joined the governor's staff.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing he entered court as Right Supplements Censor and served in the Hongwen Pavilion; after more than a year he was transferred to be aide to the Hedong observation commissioner. When Gaozu was stationed at Taiyuan, he thus took up residence in the military governor's staff.

entries.zh: 清泰末，高祖將舉義，延賓席而歷問之，次及融，對曰：「融本儒生，只曾讀三五卷書，至於軍旅之事，進退存亡之機，未之學也。」
entries.en: Near the end of Qingtai, as Gaozu prepared to raise the banner of rebellion, he gathered his guests and questioned each in turn. When it came to Rong, he answered, "I am only a Confucian scholar who has read a few volumes of books. As for military affairs and the timing of advance, retreat, survival, and destruction, I have never studied them."
entries.literal: At the end of Qingtai, when Gaozu was about to raise the banner of rebellion, he extended the guest seats and questioned each man in turn; when it came to Rong, he replied: "Rong is originally a Confucian scholar and has read only three or five volumes of books; as for military affairs and the timing of advance, retreat, survival, and destruction, I have not studied them."

entries.zh: 座中聳然。
entries.en: The whole assembly sat up in astonishment.
entries.literal: The assembly was stirred to attention.

entries.zh: 及登極，遷尚書吏部郎中兼侍御史知雜事。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Rong was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently appointed Attendant Censor with charge of miscellaneous censorial duties.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Rong was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently serving as Attendant Censor with charge of miscellaneous matters.

entries.zh: 天福二年，自左諫議大夫遷中書舍人，自以文學非優，不敢拜命，復為諫議。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianfu he was transferred from Left Remonstrance Grand Master to Drafting Secretary, but believing himself not strong enough in literary skill, he did not dare accept the appointment and returned to his former remonstrance post.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he was transferred from Left Remonstrance Grand Master to Drafting Secretary; deeming himself not superior in literary skill, he did not dare accept the appointment and returned to the post of remonstrance official.

entries.zh: 時詔修西京大內，融以鄴下用兵，國用不足，上疏復罷之，
entries.en: At the time an edict ordered repairs to the inner palace at the Western Capital. Rong submitted a memorial arguing that with troops engaged below Ye and state funds exhausted, the project should again be cancelled,
entries.literal: At the time an edict ordered the repair of the inner palace at the Western Capital; Rong, noting that troops were engaged below Ye and state funds were insufficient, submitted a memorial requesting that the project again be cancelled,

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：薛融諫曰：「今宮室雖經焚毀，猶侈於帝堯之茅茨；
entries.en: (Zizhi Tongjian: Xue Rong remonstrated, saying, "Although the palace halls have been burned, they are still more lavish than Emperor Yao's thatched huts;
entries.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: Xue Rong remonstrated, saying: "Although the palace halls have been burned, they are still more lavish than Emperor Yao's thatched huts;

entries.zh: 所費雖寡，猶多於漢文之露臺。
entries.en: and although the expense may be small, it is still greater than Emperor Wen of Han's open terrace.
entries.literal: Although the expense is small, it is still greater than Emperor Wen of Han's open terrace.

entries.zh: 況魏城未下，公私困窘，誠非陛下修宮館之日。
entries.en: Moreover, the city of Wei has not yet fallen and both public and private resources are strained. This is truly not the time for Your Majesty to repair palace halls.
entries.literal: Moreover, the city of Wei has not yet fallen and both public and private resources are strained—this is truly not the day for Your Majesty to repair palace halls.

entries.zh: 俟海內平寧，修之未晚。」）〉
entries.en: When the realm is pacified and tranquil, it will not be too late to repair them."）〉
entries.literal: When the realm within the seas is pacified and tranquil, it will not be too late to repair them."）〉

entries.zh: 優詔嘉許。
entries.en: An edict of warm praise commended him.
entries.literal: An edict of praise commended him.

entries.zh: 俄轉御史中丞，秩滿改尚書右丞，分司西都。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief, and when his term expired he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs at the Western Capital branch office.
entries.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief; when his term expired he was changed to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, serving at the Western Capital branch.

entries.zh: 天福六年，以疾卒，年六十餘。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Tianfu he died of illness at over sixty years of age.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu he died of illness, aged over sixty.

entries.zh: 曹國珍，字彥輔，幽州固安人也。
entries.en: Cao Guozhen, whose courtesy name was Yanfu, came from Gu'an in You Prefecture.
entries.literal: Cao Guozhen, courtesy name Yanfu, was a man of Gu'an in You Prefecture.

entries.zh: 曾祖藹，祖蟾，父絢，代襲儒素。
entries.en: His great-grandfather was Ai, his grandfather Chan, and his father Xuan; for generations the family had upheld the tradition of plain Confucian scholar-officials.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather was Ai, his grandfather Chan, and his father Xuan; generation after generation they inherited the tradition of plain Confucian scholar-officials.

entries.zh: 國珍少值燕薊亂離，因落發被緇，客於河西延州，高萬興兄弟皆好文，辟為從事。
entries.en: In his youth Guozhen lived through the chaos and displacement of Yan and Ji. He tonsured himself and wore the black robe of a monk, then lived as a guest at Yan Prefecture west of the River, where Gao Wanxing and his brothers, all lovers of literature, recruited him as an aide.
entries.literal: Guozhen in his youth encountered the chaos and displacement of Yan and Ji; he therefore tonsured himself and wore the black robe of a monk, living as a guest at Yan Prefecture west of the River. The brothers Gao Wanxing all loved literature and recruited him as an aide.

entries.zh: 國珍常以文章自許，求貢禮闈，且掌書奏，期年，入為左拾遺，累遷至尚書郎。
entries.en: Guozhen often prided himself on his writing. He sought advancement through the metropolitan examination while also managing memorial drafts, and within a year he entered court as Left Reminder, rising in succession to become a Director in the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: Guozhen often prided himself on his literary compositions; he sought advancement through the metropolitan examination and also managed memorial drafts. Within a year he entered court as Left Reminder and was promoted in succession to become a Director in the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 每與人交，傾財無吝。
entries.en: Whenever he associated with others, he spent his wealth freely and without stint.
entries.literal: Whenever he associated with others, he spent his wealth freely without stint.

entries.zh: 性頗剛僻，經藝史學，非其所長，好自矜衒，多上章疏，文字差誤，數數有之，為縉紳所誚。
entries.en: His nature was obstinate and aloof. Classical studies and historical learning were not his strengths, yet he loved to show himself off. He submitted many memorials, and textual errors in them occurred again and again, for which the gentry mocked him.
entries.literal: His nature was rather obstinate and aloof. Classical studies and historical learning were not his strengths, yet he loved to show himself off. He submitted many memorials and petitions, and textual errors in them occurred repeatedly, for which the gentry mocked him.

entries.zh: 高祖在藩時，嘗通私謁，以兄事之。
entries.en: When Gaozu was still a prince, Guozhen had once paid him a private visit and treated him as an elder brother.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was still a prince, Guozhen had once visited him privately and treated him as an elder brother.

entries.zh: 及即位，國珍自比於嚴陵，上表敘舊，由是自吏部郎中拜左諫議大夫、給事中。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Guozhen compared himself to Yan Ling and submitted a memorial recounting their old connection. He was therefore promoted from Director in the Ministry of Personnel to Left Remonstrance Grand Master and Chief Drafting Secretary.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Guozhen compared himself to Yan Ling and submitted a memorial recounting their old connection; he was therefore promoted from Director in the Ministry of Personnel to Left Remonstrance Grand Master and Chief Drafting Secretary.

entries.zh: 〈（《歐陽史·張彥澤傳》：國珍與御史中丞王易簡率三院御史詣閣門，連疏論張彥澤，不報。）〉
entries.en: (Ouyang Shi, Biography of Zhang Yanze: Guozhen and Censor-in-Chief Wang Yijian led the censors of the three bureaus to the Gate of Imperial Audience and submitted successive memorials denouncing Zhang Yanze, but received no response.)〉
entries.literal: (Ouyang Shi, Biography of Zhang Yanze: Guozhen and Censor-in-Chief Wang Yijian led the censors of the three bureaus to the Gate of Imperial Audience and submitted successive memorials denouncing Zhang Yanze, but received no response.)〉

entries.zh: 又求為御史中丞，時宰政不復為請，國珍銜之。
entries.en: He also requested appointment as Censor-in-Chief, but the chief ministers did not petition on his behalf again, and Guozhen resented it.
entries.literal: He also requested appointment as Censor-in-Chief, but the chief ministers did not again petition on his behalf; Guozhen resented this.

entries.zh: 李崧之母薨，遣諸弟護喪歸葬深州，崧既起復，乃出北郊路隅設奠，公卿大夫皆送喪而出，國珍固爭不行，眾鹹推其讜直。
entries.en: When Li Song's mother died, he sent his younger brothers to escort the body home for burial in Shen Prefecture. Song had already returned to office after mourning and set out offerings at a roadside outside the northern suburbs. High ministers and officials all went out to send off the funeral procession, but Guozhen firmly objected and refused to go, and everyone praised his forthright integrity.
entries.literal: When Li Song's mother died, he sent his younger brothers to escort the funeral home for burial in Shen Prefecture. Since Song had already returned to office after mourning, he set out offerings at a roadside outside the northern suburbs. High ministers and officials all went out to send off the funeral procession, but Guozhen firmly objected and would not go; everyone praised his forthright integrity.

entries.zh: 高祖晏駕，朝廷以宰臣馮道為山陵使，及靈盾既發，國珍上疏言：「馮道既為山陵使，不得復入都城，請除外佐，以桑維翰入輔。
entries.en: When Gaozu passed away, the court appointed Chief Minister Feng Dao commissioner for the imperial tomb. After the spirit shield had been dispatched, Guozhen submitted a memorial stating, "Since Feng Dao has been made commissioner for the imperial tomb, he should not again enter the capital. I request that outside auxiliary officials be appointed and that Sang Weihan enter to assist in governance.
entries.literal: When Gaozu passed away, the court appointed Chief Minister Feng Dao as commissioner for the imperial tomb. After the spirit shield had been dispatched, Guozhen submitted a memorial stating: "Since Feng Dao has been made commissioner for the imperial tomb, he should not again enter the capital; I request that auxiliary officials outside the capital be appointed, and that Sang Weihan enter to assist in governance.

entries.zh: 李崧請罷相位，俾持喪制。」
entries.en: Li Song should be asked to relinquish his chancellorship so that he may observe mourning."
entries.literal: Li Song should be asked to relinquish his chancellorship so that he may observe mourning."

entries.zh: 少帝覽奏，以所言侵越，出為陜州行軍司馬。
entries.en: The Lesser Emperor reviewed the memorial and, deeming his words presumptuous and overstepping, dispatched him to serve as military adjutant at Shaan Prefecture.
entries.literal: The Lesser Emperor reviewed the memorial and, deeming his words presumptuous and overstepping, dispatched him to serve as military adjutant at Shaan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 至任悒怏，遘疾而卒。
entries.en: Upon reaching his post he was discontent; he fell ill and died.
entries.literal: Upon reaching his post he was discontent; he fell ill and died.

entries.zh: 李遐，兗州人也。
entries.en: Li Xia came from Yan Prefecture.
entries.literal: Li Xia was a man of Yan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 少為儒，有節操。
entries.en: He studied Confucianism in his youth and possessed integrity.
entries.literal: He studied Confucianism in his youth and possessed integrity.

entries.zh: 歷數鎮從事，及升朝，累遷尚書庫部員外郎。
entries.en: He served as aide in several prefectures, and after entering court he rose in succession to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: He served as aide in several prefectures over the years; after entering court he was promoted in succession to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 高祖即位，以皇子重乂保釐洛邑，知遐強幹有守，除為西京留守判官，使之佐理，復重其廉勤，兼委監西京左藏庫。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, the prince Chongyi was appointed to safeguard Luoyang. Knowing that Xia was forceful and steadfast, Gaozu appointed him aide to the Western Capital commandant to assist in administration, and further valuing his integrity and diligence, also entrusted him to supervise the Western Capital's left treasury storehouse.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, the prince Chongyi was appointed to safeguard Luoyang. Knowing that Xia was forceful and steadfast, he was appointed aide to the Western Capital's commandant to assist in administration; further valuing his integrity and diligence, he was also entrusted to supervise the Western Capital's left treasury storehouse.

entries.zh: 會張從賓作亂，使人輦取繒帛以賞群逆，遐曰：「不奉詔書，安敢承命！」
entries.en: When Zhang Congbin raised rebellion, he sent men to cart away silk to reward the rebels. Xia said, "Without an imperial edict, how dare I accept the order!"
entries.literal: When Zhang Congbin raised rebellion, he sent men to cart away silk to reward the rebels. Xia said: "Without receiving an imperial edict, how dare I accept the order!"

entries.zh: 遂為其下所害。
entries.en: So he was killed by their subordinates.
entries.literal: So he was killed by their subordinates.

entries.zh: 高祖聞而嘆惜，賻贈加等，仍贈右諫議大夫。
entries.en: When Gaozu heard of it he sighed in grief, increased the funeral gifts by one grade, and posthumously granted him Right Remonstrance Grand Master.
entries.literal: When Gaozu heard of it he sighed in grief; funeral gifts were increased by one grade, and he was posthumously granted Right Remonstrance Grand Master.

entries.zh: 其母田氏，封京兆郡太君，仍給遐所食月俸，終母餘年。
entries.en: His mother, née Tian, was ennobled as Lady of Jingzhao Commandery and continued to receive the monthly salary that Xia had drawn until the end of her life.
entries.literal: His mother, née Tian, was ennobled as Lady of Jingzhao Commandery; she continued to receive the monthly salary that Xia had drawn until the end of her years.

entries.zh: 其子俟服闋與官。
entries.en: His son was granted an office after his mourning period ended.
entries.literal: His son was granted an office after his mourning period ended.

entries.zh: 後又遣兗州節度使李從溫就其舊業，賜牲幣綿帛等物，以旌其忠也。
entries.en: Later the military governor of Yan Prefecture, Li Congwen, was dispatched to attend to his old household, and sacrificial victims, ritual silks, cotton cloth, and other goods were granted to honor his loyalty.
entries.literal: Later the military governor of Yan Prefecture, Li Congwen, was dispatched to attend to his old household, and sacrificial victims, ritual silks, cotton cloth, and other goods were granted to honor his loyalty.

entries.zh: 尹玉羽，京兆長安人。
entries.en: Yin Yuyu came from Chang'an in Jingzhao.
entries.literal: Yin Yuyu was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 唐天福中，隨計京師，甚有文稱。
entries.en: During the Tianfu era he traveled to the capital for the metropolitan examination and enjoyed a considerable reputation for literary talent.
entries.literal: During the Tianfu era under Tang, he traveled to the capital for the metropolitan examination and enjoyed a considerable reputation for literature.

entries.zh: 會有苴杖之喪，累歲羸疾，冬不釋菅屨，期不變倚廬。
entries.en: When he incurred the mourning of staff and cane, for years he was emaciated and ill. In winter he did not lay aside his straw sandals, and throughout the mourning period he did not leave his mourning hut.
entries.literal: When he incurred the mourning of staff and cane, for successive years he was emaciated and ill; in winter he did not lay aside his straw sandals, and throughout the mourning period he did not leave his mourning hut.

entries.zh: 制闋，隱居杜門，無仕宦之意。
entries.en: When mourning ended, he lived in seclusion behind closed doors with no wish for office.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, he lived in seclusion behind closed doors with no mind for office.

entries.zh: 梁貞明中，劉鄩辟為保大軍節度判官，歷雍、汴、滑、兗從事。
entries.en: During Zhenming under Liang, Liu Xun recruited him as military governor's aide of the Baoda army, and he served in succession as aide in Yong, Bian, Hua, and Yan.
entries.literal: During Zhenming under Liang, Liu Xun recruited him as military governor's aide of the Baoda army; he successively served as aide in Yong, Bian, Hua, and Yan.

entries.zh: 〈（案：以下有闕。
entries.en: (Note: There is a lacuna below.
entries.literal: (Note: There is a lacuna below.

entries.zh: 考宋黎持《移石經紀》：石經舊在務本坊，自天祐中韓建築新城，而石經委棄於野。
entries.en: Examining Song Lichi's Record of Moving the Stone Classics: The stone classics formerly stood in Wuben Ward; from Tianyou onward Han Jian built the new city wall, and the stone classics were abandoned in the wild.
entries.literal: Examining Song Lichi's Record of Moving the Stone Classics: The stone classics formerly stood in Wuben Ward; from Tianyou onward Han Jian built the new city wall, and the stone classics were abandoned in the wild.

entries.zh: 至朱梁時，劉鄩守長安，從幕吏尹玉羽之請，輦入城中，置於此地，即唐尚書省之西隅也。）〉
entries.en: When the Later Liang came, Liu Xun held Chang'an; at the request of his staff officer Yin Yuyu, the classics were carted into the city and placed at this spot, at the western corner of the Tang Department of State Affairs.)〉
entries.literal: When the Zhu Liang dynasty came, Liu Xun held Chang'an; at the request of his staff officer Yin Yuyu, the classics were carted into the city and placed at this spot, at the western corner of the Tang Department of State Affairs.)〉

entries.zh: 唐清泰中，為光祿少卿，退歸秦中，以林泉詩酒自樂，自號自然先生。
entries.en: During Qingtai under Tang he served as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then retired to the Qin region and found his pleasure in forests, springs, poetry, and wine, styling himself Master Ziran.
entries.literal: During Qingtai under Tang he served as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he retired to the Qin region and found his pleasure in forests, springs, poetry, and wine, styling himself Master Ziran.

entries.zh: 宰臣張延朗手書而召，高臥不從，謂人曰：「庶孽代宗，不可仕也。」
entries.en: Chief Minister Zhang Yanlang summoned him by letter in his own hand, but he remained reclining and did not obey, telling others, "An illegitimate scion rules in place of the ancestral temple—one may not serve him."
entries.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Yanlang summoned him by letter in his own hand, but he remained reclining and did not obey, telling others: "An illegitimate scion rules in place of the ancestral temple—one may not serve him."

entries.zh: 及高祖入洛，即受詔而來，以所著《自然經》五卷貢之，且告其老。
entries.en: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, he immediately accepted the summons and came, presenting his own five-volume Classic of Nature and declaring his old age.
entries.literal: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, he immediately accepted the summons and came, presenting his own five-volume Classic of Nature and also declaring his old age.

entries.zh: 即日璽書褒美，頒其器幣，授少府監致仕，月給俸錢及冬春二時服。
entries.en: That very day an imperial letter of seal-script praise was issued, ritual vessels and silks were bestowed, and he was granted retirement as Vice Director of the Palace Revenues with monthly salary stipends and clothing for winter and spring.
entries.literal: That very day an imperial letter of seal-script praise was issued; ritual vessels and silks were bestowed, and he was granted retirement as Vice Director of the Palace Revenues, with monthly salary stipends and clothing for winter and spring.

entries.zh: 天福中，卒，有《武庫集》五十卷行於世。
entries.en: During Tianfu he died, leaving his fifty-volume Armory Collection in circulation.
entries.literal: During Tianfu he died; his fifty-volume Armory Collection circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 鄭雲叟，本名遨，雲叟其字也，以唐明宗廟諱，故世傳其字焉，本南燕人也。
entries.en: Zheng Yunsou, whose original personal name was Ao and whose courtesy name was Yunsou, was originally a man of Southern Yan. Because of the temple taboo on Mingzong of Tang, posterity transmitted his courtesy name.
entries.literal: Zheng Yunsou, original personal name Ao—Yunsou was his courtesy name; because of the temple taboo on Mingzong of Tang, posterity transmitted his courtesy name, and he was originally a man of Southern Yan.

entries.zh: 少好學，耿介不屈。
entries.en: He loved learning in his youth and was upright and unyielding.
entries.literal: He loved learning in his youth and was upright and unyielding.

entries.zh: 唐昭宗朝，嘗應進士舉，不第，因欲攜妻子隱於林壑，其妻非之，不肯行，雲叟乃薄遊諸郡，獲數百緡以贍其家，辭訣而去。
entries.en: During the reign of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he once took the Jinshi examination but failed. He therefore wished to take his wife and children and live hidden in mountains and valleys, but his wife disapproved and refused to go. Yunsou then traveled lightly through various prefectures, obtained several hundred strings of cash to support his family, bade farewell, and departed.
entries.literal: During the reign of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he once took the Jinshi examination but failed; he therefore wished to take his wife and children and live hidden in mountains and valleys. His wife disapproved and refused to go, so Yunsou traveled lightly through various prefectures, obtained several hundred strings of cash to support his family, bade farewell, and departed.

entries.zh: 尋入少室山，著《擬峰詩》三十六章，以導其趣，人多傳之。
entries.en: Soon he entered Mount Shaoshi and composed thirty-six chapters of Peak-Inspired Poetry to express his inclinations, which many people copied and circulated.
entries.literal: Soon he entered Mount Shaoshi, composed thirty-six chapters of Peak-Inspired Poetry to express his inclinations, and many people copied and circulated them.

entries.zh: 後妻以書達意，勸其還家，雲叟未嘗一覽，悉投於火，其絕累如此。
entries.en: Later his wife sent a letter expressing her wishes and urging him to return home, but Yunsou never so much as read it—he threw it all into the fire. Such was his severing of worldly ties.
entries.literal: Later his wife sent a letter expressing her wishes and urging him to return home; Yunsou never so much as read it once—he threw it all into the fire. So thorough was his severing of worldly ties.

entries.zh: 俄聞西嶽有五鬛松，淪脂千年，能去三屍，因居於華陰。
entries.en: Soon he heard that the Western Peak had a five-needled pine that oozed resin for a thousand years and could drive out the three corpses, and he therefore settled at Huayin.
entries.literal: Soon he heard that the Western Peak had a five-needled pine that oozed resin for a thousand years and could drive out the three corpses; he therefore settled at Huayin.

entries.zh: 與李道殷、羅隱之友善，時人目為「三高士」。
entries.en: He was on friendly terms with Li Daoyin and Luo Yinzhi, and people of the time regarded them as the "Three High Recluses."
entries.literal: He was on friendly terms with Li Daoyin and Luo Yinzhi; people of the time regarded them as the "Three High Recluses."

entries.zh: 道殷有釣魚之術，鉤而不餌，又能化易金石，無所不至，雲叟恒目睹其事，信而不求。
entries.en: Daoyin possessed the art of fishing with hook but no bait and could also transform and transmute metal and stone—there was nothing he could not do. Yunsou constantly witnessed these things and believed without seeking them for himself.
entries.literal: Daoyin possessed the art of fishing with hook but no bait, and could also transform and transmute metal and stone—there was nothing he could not do. Yunsou constantly witnessed these things and believed without seeking them for himself.

entries.zh: 雲叟與梁室權臣李振善，振欲祿之，拒而不諾，及振南遷，雲叟千里徒步以省之，識者高焉。
entries.en: Yunsou was on good terms with Li Zhen, the powerful minister of the Liang court. Zhen wished to give him an official salary, but Yunsou refused. When Zhen moved south, Yunsou traveled a thousand li on foot to visit him, and those who understood the matter held him in high esteem.
entries.literal: Yunsou was on good terms with Li Zhen, the powerful minister of the Liang court; Zhen wished to give him an official salary, but he refused and would not agree. When Zhen moved south, Yunsou traveled a thousand li on foot to visit him—those who understood the matter held him in high esteem.

entries.zh: 後妻兒繼謝，每聞兇服，一哭而止。
entries.en: Later his wife and children died one after another; whenever he heard that someone was in mourning, he wept once and stopped.
entries.literal: Later his wife and children died in succession; whenever he heard of mourning garments, he wept once and stopped.

entries.zh: 時惟青衿二童子、一琴、一鶴，從其遊處。
entries.en: At that time only two youths in blue collars, a zither, and a crane accompanied him wherever he went.
entries.literal: At that time only two youths in blue collars, one zither, and one crane accompanied him in his wanderings.

entries.zh: 好棋塞之戲，遇同侶則以晝繼夜，雖寒風大雪，臨檐對局，手足皸裂，亦無倦焉。
entries.en: He loved chess and pitch-and-toss; when he found companions he would play from day into night. Even in bitter wind and heavy snow, sitting under the eaves across the board from them with cracked hands and feet, he never grew weary.
entries.literal: He loved chess and pitch-and-toss games; when he met companions he would continue from day into night, and even in bitter wind and heavy snow, sitting under the eaves facing one another across the board, his hands and feet cracked with chilblains, yet he never showed weariness.

entries.zh: 唐天成中，召拜左拾遺，不起。
entries.en: In the Tiancheng era of Tang he was summoned as Left Remonstrance Aide but declined to serve.
entries.literal: In the Tiancheng era of Tang he was summoned and appointed Left Remonstrance Aide but did not take up the post.

entries.zh: 與羅隱之朝夕遊處，隱之以藥術取利，雲叟以山田自給，俱好酒能詩，善長嘯。
entries.en: He spent his days with Luo Yinzhi, who made a living through pharmaceutical arts while Yunsou supported himself from hillside fields. Both loved wine, wrote poetry well, and were skilled at long whistling.
entries.literal: He spent his days and nights in company with Luo Yinzhi; Yinzhi made a living through pharmaceutical arts, while Yunsou supported himself with hillside fields. Both loved wine and were skilled at poetry, and excelled at long whistling.

entries.zh: 有大瓠，雲可辟寒暑，置酒於其中，經時味不壞，日攜就花木水石之間，一酌一詠。
entries.en: He owned a large gourd that he said could ward off cold and heat; wine placed in it did not spoil even after a long time. Each day he carried it among flowers, trees, water, and rocks, drinking and composing a verse in turn.
entries.literal: He had a large gourd that he said could ward off cold and heat; he placed wine in it and even after a long time the flavor did not spoil. Each day he carried it among flowers, trees, water, and rocks, taking a drink and composing a verse.

entries.zh: 嘗因酒酣聯句，鄭曰：「一壺天上有名物，兩個世間無事人。」
entries.en: Once, when they were warm with wine, they composed linked verses; Zheng said, "One pot—a famous thing from heaven; two men in the world without affairs."
entries.literal: Once, when wine had warmed them, they composed linked verses; Zheng said: "One pot—a famous thing from heaven; two men in the world without affairs."

entries.zh: 羅曰：「醉卻隱之、雲叟外，不知何處是天真。」
entries.en: Luo said, "When drunk, apart from Yinzhi and Yunsou, I no longer know where true innocence lies."
entries.literal: Luo said: "When drunk, apart from Yinzhi and Yunsou, I no longer know where true innocence lies."

entries.zh: 高祖即位，聞其名，遣使賫書致禮，征為右諫議大夫，雲叟稱疾不起，上表陳謝。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne he heard of Yunsou's fame and sent an envoy with a letter and gifts to summon him as Right Remonstrance Grand Master. Yunsou pleaded illness and declined, submitting a memorial of thanks.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he heard of Yunsou's name and sent an envoy bearing a letter and gifts to summon him as Right Remonstrance Grand Master; Yunsou pleaded illness and did not rise, submitting a memorial to decline with thanks.

entries.zh: 高祖覽表嘉之，賜近臣傳觀，尋賜號逍遙先生，以諫議大夫致仕，月給俸祿。
entries.en: Gaozu read the memorial and praised it, having it passed among his close ministers for viewing. He soon granted Yunsou the title Master Free Wanderer and allowed him to retire as Remonstrance Grand Master with a monthly salary.
entries.literal: Gaozu read the memorial and praised it, ordering it passed among his close ministers for viewing; soon he granted him the title Master Free Wanderer and allowed him to retire as Remonstrance Grand Master with a monthly salary.

entries.zh: 雲叟好酒，嘗為《詠酒詩》千二百言，海內好名者書於縑緗，以為贈貺。
entries.en: Yunsou loved wine and once composed an Ode to Wine of twelve hundred characters. Admirers throughout the realm copied it onto silk and gave it as gifts.
entries.literal: Yunsou loved wine and once composed an Ode to Wine of twelve hundred characters; those throughout the realm who admired his name copied it onto silk and gave it as gifts.

entries.zh: 復有越千里之外，使畫工潛寫其形容列為屏障者焉。
entries.en: Some even from beyond a thousand li sent painters to sketch his likeness in secret and mount it on screens.
entries.literal: There were also those from more than a thousand li away who sent painters to sketch his likeness secretly and array it on screens.

entries.zh: 其為時望所重也如此。
entries.en: Such was the esteem his contemporaries accorded him.
entries.literal: Such was the esteem in which men of the age held him.

entries.zh: 天福末，以壽終，時年七十四。
entries.en: At the end of Tianfu he died a natural death at the age of seventy-four.
entries.literal: At the end of Tianfu he died a natural death at age seventy-four.

entries.zh: 有文集二十卷行於世。
entries.en: His collected works in twenty juan circulated widely.
entries.literal: A collection of writings in twenty juan circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 皇甫遇，常山人也。
entries.en: Huang Fuyu was from Changshan.
entries.literal: Huang Fuyu was a native of Changshan.

entries.zh: 父武，流寓太原，嘗為遮塞軍使。
entries.en: His father, Wu, had settled in Taiyuan as a transient and had once served as commissioner of the blockade and garrison forces.
entries.literal: His father Wu lived as a sojourner in Taiyuan and once served as commissioner of the blockade and garrison forces.

entries.zh: 遇少好勇，及壯，虬髯，善騎射。
entries.en: From youth Huang Fuyu loved boldness; in manhood he wore curling whiskers and was an expert horseman and archer.
entries.literal: Yu from youth loved bravery; when grown, he had curled whiskers and was skilled at horseback riding and archery.

entries.zh: 唐明宗在藩時，隸於麾下，累從戰有功。
entries.en: When Emperor Mingzong of Tang was still in his princely domain, Huang Fuyu entered his service and repeatedly distinguished himself in battle.
entries.literal: When Tang Emperor Mingzong was in his fief, he was attached to his command and repeatedly followed into battle with merit.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，遷龍武都指揮使，遙領嚴州刺史，出討東川，為行營左軍都指揮使。
entries.en: After Mingzong took the throne, Huang Fuyu was promoted to commander-in-chief of the Dragon Martial Guard, given nominal charge of Yan prefecture, sent to campaign against Dongchuan, and made commander-in-chief of the left wing of the expeditionary force.
entries.literal: When Mingzong ascended the throne, he was transferred to commander-in-chief of the Dragon Martial Guard, held Yanzhou prefect remotely, went out to campaign against Dongchuan, and served as commander-in-chief of the left army of the expeditionary camp.

entries.zh: 應順、清泰中，累歷團練防禦使，尋遷鄧州節度使。
entries.en: During the Yingshun and Qingtai reign periods he served in succession as militia training and defense commissioner, and soon afterward was transferred to military governor of Deng.
entries.literal: During Yingshun and Qingtai, he successively held posts as militia training and defense commissioner, and soon was transferred to military governor of Dengzhou.

entries.zh: 所至苛暴，以誅斂為務，其幕客多私去，以避其累。
entries.en: Everywhere he served he was brutal and violent, making extortion his chief occupation, and many on his staff slipped away privately to escape being dragged into his abuses.
entries.literal: Wherever he went he was harsh and violent, making extortion his business; many of his staff privately departed to escape being implicated.

entries.zh: 高祖入洛，移領中山，俄聞與鎮州安重榮為婚家，乃移鎮上黨，又改平陽，咸以憸人執事，政事隳紊。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu entered Luoyang, Huang Fuyu was transferred to Zhongshan; soon word came that he had formed a marriage alliance with An Chongrong of Zhen prefecture, so he was shifted to Shangdang and then to Pingyang. In each place scheming men ran affairs and government collapsed into disorder.
entries.literal: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, he was reassigned to govern Zhongshan; soon it was heard that he had marriage ties with An Chongrong of Zhenzhou, so he was moved to govern Shangdang, then reassigned to Pingyang; in all cases wicked men held office and government affairs fell into disorder.

entries.zh: 及鎮河陽，部內創別業，開畎水泉，以通溉灌，所經墳墓悉毀之，部民以朝廷方姑息郡帥，莫之敢訴。
entries.en: When he was posted at Heyang, he established private estates within his jurisdiction, opened ditches and springs for irrigation, and destroyed every grave in his path. The people dared not appeal because the court was then indulgent toward regional governors.
entries.literal: When he governed Heyang, within his jurisdiction he established private estates, dug irrigation channels and springs to enable irrigation, and destroyed all tombs in his path; the people of the district, because the court was then indulgent toward regional commanders, did not dare to complain.

entries.zh: 少帝即位，罷歸闕下。
entries.en: When the Young Emperor came to the throne, Huang Fuyu was recalled to the capital and relieved of command.
entries.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was dismissed and returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 二年，契丹南寇，從至澶州，戰於鄆州北津，契丹眾大敗，溺死者數千人，以功拜滑州節度使。
entries.en: In the second year, when the Khitans invaded the south, he accompanied the court to Chanzhou. At the northern crossing of Yun prefecture the Khitan force was routed and thousands drowned. For this he was appointed military governor of Hua.
entries.literal: In the second year, when the Khitans raided south, he followed the emperor to Chanzhou; at the northern ford of Yunzhou the Khitan army was utterly defeated and several thousand drowned; for this merit he was appointed military governor of Huazhou.

entries.zh: 三年，契丹率眾屯邯鄲，遇與安審琦、慕容彥超等禦之。
entries.en: In the third year the Khitans massed at Handan, and Huang Fuyu, An Shenqi, Murong Yanchao, and others went out to oppose them.
entries.literal: In the third year the Khitans led their masses to encamp at Handan; Yu, together with An Shenqi, Murong Yanchao, and others, resisted them.

entries.zh: 遇將渡漳河，契丹前鋒大至，遇引退，轉鬥二十里至鄴南榆林店。
entries.en: As Huang Fuyu was about to cross the Zhang River, the Khitan vanguard closed in. He pulled back, fighting continuously for twenty li until he reached Yulin Post south of Ye.
entries.literal: As Yu was about to cross the Zhang River, the Khitan vanguard arrived in force; Yu withdrew, fighting as he went twenty li to Yulin Post south of Ye.

entries.zh: 遇謂審琦等曰：「彼眾我寡，走無生路，不如血戰。」
entries.en: Huang Fuyu said to Shenqi and the others, "They outnumber us; retreat means death. We had better fight to the last drop of blood."
entries.literal: Yu said to Shenqi and the others, "They are many and we are few; flight offers no way to live. Better to fight to the death."

entries.zh: 遂自辰及未，戰百餘合，所傷甚眾。
entries.en: From the hour of chen until that of wei they fought more than a hundred engagements, and casualties on both sides were very heavy.
entries.literal: From the hour of chen until that of wei they fought more than a hundred engagements, and casualties on both sides were very heavy.

entries.zh: 遇所乘馬中鏑而斃，遇有紀綱杜知敏以馬授遇，遇得馬復戰，久之稍解。
entries.en: The horse Huang Fuyu was riding was struck by an arrow and killed. His retainer Du Zhimin gave him his own mount; Huang Fuyu remounted and fought on, and after a long while the pressure eased slightly.
entries.literal: The horse Yu was riding was struck by an arrow and fell dead; Yu had a retainer named Du Zhimin who gave Yu his horse; Yu obtained the horse and fought again, and after a long time the pressure eased slightly.

entries.zh: 杜知敏已為所獲，遇謂彥超曰：「知敏蒼黃之中，以馬授我，義也，安可使陷於賊中！」
entries.en: Du Zhimin had already been taken. Huang Fuyu said to Yanchao, "In the heat of battle Zhimin gave me his horse — that was an act of loyalty. We cannot leave him in enemy hands!"
entries.literal: Du Zhimin had already been captured; Yu said to Yanchao, "In the midst of confusion Zhimin gave me his horse — that was righteousness. How can we let him fall into the hands of the enemy!"

entries.zh: 遂與彥超躍馬取知敏而還，敵騎壯之。
entries.en: He and Yanchao then spurred their horses forward, snatched Zhimin back, and returned; the enemy horsemen were impressed.
entries.literal: He and Yanchao then spurred their horses, seized Zhimin, and returned; the enemy cavalry admired this.

entries.zh: 俄而生軍復合，遇不能解。
entries.en: Before long the Khitan force closed ranks again, and Huang Fuyu could not break free.
entries.literal: Soon the Khitan army closed ranks again, and Yu could not break free.

entries.zh: 時審琦已至安陽河，謂首將張從恩曰：「皇甫遇等未至，必為敵騎所圍，若不急救，則成擒矣。」
entries.en: By then Shenqi had reached the Anyang River and said to the chief commander Zhang Cong'en, "Huang Fuyu and the others have not yet arrived; they must be surrounded by enemy cavalry. If we do not rescue them immediately, they will be taken."
entries.literal: At that time Shenqi had already reached the Anyang River and said to the chief commander Zhang Cong'en, "Huang Fuyu and the others have not yet arrived; they must be surrounded by enemy cavalry. If we do not rescue them at once, they will be captured."

entries.zh: 從恩曰：「敵甚盛，無以枝梧，將軍獨往何益？」
entries.en: Cong'en said, "The enemy is too strong; we cannot hold them. What good would it do for you, General, to go alone?"
entries.literal: Cong'en said, "The enemy is very strong and we have no way to resist. What good would it do for you, General, to go alone?"

entries.zh: 審琦曰：「成敗命也。
entries.en: Shenqi said, "Success or failure is a matter of fate.
entries.literal: Shenqi said, "Success or failure is a matter of fate.

entries.zh: 設若不濟，則與之俱死。
entries.en: If we fail, I shall die with them.
entries.literal: If it should not succeed, then I shall die with them.

entries.zh: 假令失此二將，將何面目以見天子！」
entries.en: If we lose these two generals, how can we face the emperor!"
entries.literal: If we were to lose these two generals, with what face could we appear before the Son of Heaven!"

entries.zh: 遂率鐵騎北渡赴之。
entries.en: He then led his armored cavalry north across the river to their relief.
entries.literal: He then led his iron cavalry north across the river to their aid.

entries.zh: 契丹見塵起，謂救軍並至，乃引去。
entries.en: When the Khitans saw the dust rising, they thought the full relief force had arrived and withdrew.
entries.literal: When the Khitans saw the dust rising, they thought relief troops had all arrived and withdrew.

entries.zh: 遇與彥超中數創得還，時諸軍嘆曰：「此三人皆猛將也！」
entries.en: Huang Fuyu and Yanchao returned with several wounds; the armies at the time exclaimed, "These three are fierce generals!"
entries.literal: Yu and Yanchao received several wounds but got back; at the time the various armies exclaimed, "These three are fierce generals!"

entries.zh: 遇累官至檢校太師、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: Huang Fuyu rose through the ranks to honorary Grand Master and Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Chancellery.
entries.literal: Yu rose through the ranks to honorary Grand Master and Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs with the Chancellery.

entries.zh: 四年，契丹復至，從杜重威營滹水，重威送款於契丹，遇不預其議，及降，心不平之。
entries.en: In the fourth year the Khitans returned. Huang Fuyu followed Du Chongwei's encampment on the Hutuo River. Chongwei opened surrender negotiations with the Khitans; Huang Fuyu had not been party to the decision, and when the surrender came he was deeply resentful.
entries.literal: In the fourth year the Khitans came again; he followed Du Chongwei's camp at the Hutuo River; Chongwei sent overtures of surrender to the Khitans; Yu did not take part in the deliberations, and when the surrender came, his heart was not at peace with it.

entries.zh: 時契丹欲遣遇先入汴，遇辭之，因私謂人曰：「我身荷國恩，位兼將相，既不能死於軍陣，何顏以見舊主！
entries.en: The Khitans then wished to send Huang Fuyu ahead into Bian first. He declined and said privately to others, "I have personally received the state's favor and hold the rank of general and minister together. Having failed to die on the battlefield, how can I face my former sovereign!
entries.literal: At that time the Khitans wished to send Yu ahead into Bian first; Yu declined, and privately said to someone, "I have received the state's grace in person; my rank combines general and minister. Since I could not die on the battlefield, with what face could I see my former lord!

entries.zh: 更受命圖之，所不忍也。」
entries.en: To accept a new commission and plot against him is more than I can bear."
entries.literal: To accept a new commission and plot against him — that I cannot bear."

entries.zh: 明日，行至趙郡，泊其縣舍，顧從者曰：「我已信宿不食，疾甚矣，主辱臣死，無復南行。」
entries.en: The next day, as he reached Zhao Commandery and stopped at the county seat, he told his attendants, "I have eaten nothing for two nights; my illness is grave. When the sovereign is disgraced, the minister must die — I go no farther south."
entries.literal: The next day, traveling to Zhao Commandery, he lodged at the county seat and said to his attendants, "I have not eaten for two nights; my illness is severe. When the lord is shamed, the minister dies — I shall go no farther south."

entries.zh: 因絕吭而殞，遠近聞而義之。
entries.en: He then cut his throat and died; all who heard of it, near and far, honored his act.
entries.literal: He then cut his throat and died; far and near, those who heard of it honored his righteousness.

entries.zh: 漢高祖登極，詔贈中書令。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu of Han took the throne, an edict posthumously honored him as Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: When Han Gaozu ascended the throne, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 王清，字去瑕，洺州曲周人也。
entries.en: Wang Qing, styled Quxia, was from Quzhou in Ming prefecture.
entries.literal: Wang Qing, styled Quxia, was a native of Quzhou in Ming Prefecture.

entries.zh: 父度，世為農。
entries.en: His father Du came from a farming family for generations.
entries.literal: His father Du came from generations of farmers.

entries.zh: 清少以勇力端厚稱於鄉里。
entries.en: From youth Wang Qing was known in his village for courage, strength, and upright steadiness.
entries.literal: Qing from youth was known in his village for courage, strength, and upright steadiness.

entries.zh: 後唐明宗領行臺，置步直軍，清預其募，漸升為小校。
entries.en: When Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang held the mobile headquarters, he established the Foot Guard Army; Wang Qing joined the recruitment and gradually rose to junior officer.
entries.literal: When Later Tang Emperor Mingzong held the mobile headquarters, he established the Foot Guard Army; Qing joined the recruitment and gradually rose to junior officer.

entries.zh: 同光初，從戰於河上有功，賜忠烈功臣。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Tongguang era he fought on the Yellow River front with distinction and was granted the title Meritorious Loyal and Fierce Servitor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang, he followed campaigns on the Yellow River with merit and was granted the title Meritorious Loyal and Fierce Servitor.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，自天成至清泰末，歷嚴衛、寧衛指揮使，加檢校右散騎常侍。
entries.en: After Mingzong took the throne, from the Tiancheng through the Qingtai periods he served in succession as commander of the Yan and Ning Guards and was promoted to honorary Right Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
entries.literal: When Mingzong ascended the throne, from Tiancheng to the end of Qingtai he successively served as commander of the Yan and Ning Guards and was promoted to honorary Right Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 天福元年，高祖建義入洛，加檢校刑部尚書，改賜扈蹕忠孝功臣。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianfu, when Emperor Gaozu raised the banner of righteousness and entered Luoyang, Wang Qing was promoted to honorary Minister of Justice and given the new title Meritorious Escort and Filial Piety Servitor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianfu, when Gaozu raised the banner of righteousness and entered Luoyang, he was promoted to honorary Minister of Justice and his title was changed to Meritorious Escort and Filial Piety Servitor.

entries.zh: 三年，從楊光遠平範延光於鄴，改奉國軍都虞候。
entries.en: In the third year he followed Yang Guangyuan in pacifying Fan Yanguang at Ye and was transferred to chief adjutant of the Fengguo Army.
entries.literal: In the third year he followed Yang Guangyuan in pacifying Fan Yanguang at Ye and was transferred to chief adjutant of the Fengguo Army.

entries.zh: 六年，襄州安從進叛，從高行周討之，逾年不下。
entries.en: In the sixth year An Congjin of Xiangzhou rebelled; Wang Qing followed Gao Xingzhou to suppress him, and after more than a year the city still had not fallen.
entries.literal: In the sixth year An Congjin of Xiangzhou rebelled; he followed Gao Xingzhou to suppress him, and after more than a year the city had not fallen.

entries.zh: 一日，清請先登，諸軍繼其後，會有內應者，遂拔其城。
entries.en: One day Wang Qing asked to lead the assault; the other armies followed behind him. There were collaborators within, and the city was taken.
entries.literal: One day Qing requested to lead the assault; the various armies followed after him; there happened to be someone inside who responded in collusion, and they then took the city.

entries.zh: 清以中重創，有詔褒慰。
entries.en: Wang Qing was seriously wounded in the assault; an edict praised and comforted him.
entries.literal: Qing received serious wounds in the assault; an edict praised and comforted him.

entries.zh: 七年，改賜推忠保運功臣，加金紫光祿大夫，領溪州刺史。
entries.en: In the seventh year his title was changed to Meritorious Promoter of Loyalty and Guardian of Transport Servitor, he was promoted to Grand Master of the Gold Purple Light, and given nominal charge of Xi prefecture.
entries.literal: In the seventh year his title was changed to Meritorious Promoter of Loyalty and Guardian of Transport Servitor, and he was promoted to Grand Master of the Gold Purple Light and given nominal charge of Xi Prefecture.

entries.zh: 八年，詔遣以所部兵屯於鄴。
entries.en: In the eighth year an edict ordered him to encamp with his troops at Ye.
entries.literal: In the eighth year an edict dispatched him to encamp with his troops at Ye.

entries.zh: 九年春，契丹南牧，圍其城，清與張從恩守之，少帝飛蠟詔勉諭，錫之第宅。
entries.en: In the spring of the ninth year the Khitans raided south and besieged the city. Wang Qing and Zhang Cong'en held it. The Young Emperor sent urgent sealed edicts to encourage them and granted them residences.
entries.literal: In the spring of the ninth year the Khitans raided south and besieged the city; Qing and Zhang Cong'en defended it; the Young Emperor sent urgent sealed edicts to encourage and instruct them and granted them residences.

entries.zh: 契丹退，以幹城功，繼遷軍額。
entries.en: When the Khitans withdrew, for his merit in holding the city he was transferred in succession to a new army designation.
entries.literal: When the Khitans withdrew, for his merit in holding the city he was transferred in succession to a new army designation.

entries.zh: 開運二年春三月，從杜重威北征，解陽城之圍，加檢校司徒。
entries.en: In the third month, in spring of the second year of Kaiyun, he followed Du Chongwei on the northern expedition, lifted the siege of Yangcheng, and was promoted to honorary Minister of Works.
entries.literal: In the third month of spring of the second year of Kaiyun he followed Du Chongwei on the northern expedition, lifted the siege of Yangcheng, and was promoted to honorary Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 是歲秋七月，詔遣與皇甫遇援糧入易州。
entries.en: In the seventh month of that autumn an edict dispatched him with Huang Fuyu to escort grain into Yi prefecture.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of that autumn an edict dispatched him with Huang Fuyu to escort grain into Yi Prefecture.

entries.zh: 十一月，從杜重威收瀛州，聞契丹大至，重威率諸軍沿滹水而西，將保常山，及至中渡橋，契丹已屯於北岸。
entries.en: In the eleventh month he followed Du Chongwei in taking Ying prefecture. Hearing that the Khitans had arrived in force, Chongwei led the armies west along the Hutuo River intending to hold Changshan; when they reached Zhongdu Bridge the Khitans were already encamped on the north bank.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month he followed Du Chongwei in taking Ying Prefecture; hearing that the Khitans had arrived in force, Chongwei led the armies west along the Hutuo River intending to hold Changshan; when they reached Zhongdu Bridge the Khitans were already encamped on the north bank.

entries.zh: 自其月二十七日至十二月五日，軍不能解。
entries.en: From the twenty-seventh day of that month to the fifth day of the twelfth month the army could not break free.
entries.literal: From the twenty-seventh day of that month to the fifth day of the twelfth month the army could not break free.

entries.zh: 時契丹至，留騎之精者以禦我，分其弱者，自故靈都城緣其山足，涉滹沱之淺處，引眾而南，至趙郡，凡百餘里，斷我飛免，且扼歸路。
entries.en: When the Khitans arrived they left their finest cavalry to hold the army in check and sent the weaker part from the old Lingdu City along the foothills, crossing the shallows of the Hutuo and marching south to Zhao Commandery — more than a hundred li in all — cutting courier routes and blocking the line of retreat.
entries.literal: At that time when the Khitans arrived, they left their finest cavalry to hold us in check and divided off the weaker part; from the old Lingdu City they followed the foot of the mountains, crossed the shallow places of the Hutuo, and led their forces south to Zhao Commandery — more than a hundred li in all — cutting our courier routes and also blocking the road of retreat.

entries.zh: 清知勢蹙，謂重威曰：「軍去常山五里，守株於此，營孤食盡，將若之何！
entries.en: Seeing the situation was critical, Wang Qing said to Chongwei, "Changshan is only five li away. To sit here like a stump while the camp is isolated and provisions run out — what then!
entries.literal: Qing knew the situation was critical and said to Chongwei, "The army is five li from Changshan; to sit here waiting like a stump while the camp is isolated and provisions exhausted — what then!

entries.zh: 請以步兵二千為前鋒，奪橋開路，公可率諸軍繼之，期入常山，必濟矣。」
entries.en: Let me take two thousand infantry as vanguard to seize the bridge and open the road; you can lead the main force after us. If we reach Changshan as planned, we shall succeed."
entries.literal: I request two thousand infantry as vanguard to seize the bridge and open the road; you, sir, can lead the various armies after; if we enter Changshan on schedule, we shall succeed."

entries.zh: 重威可之，遣宋彥筠俱行。
entries.en: Chongwei agreed and sent Song Yanyun to go with him.
entries.literal: Chongwei agreed and dispatched Song Yanyun to go with him.

entries.zh: 清一擊獲其橋，契丹為之小卻，重威猶豫不進，密已貳於國矣。
entries.en: With one assault Wang Qing seized the bridge and the Khitans gave ground slightly; Chongwei hesitated and did not advance — secretly he had already turned traitor.
entries.literal: With one assault Qing seized the bridge; the Khitans retreated slightly on his account; Chongwei hesitated and did not advance — secretly he had already turned disloyal to the state.

entries.zh: 彥筠退走，清列陣北岸，嚴戒部曲。
entries.en: Yanyun retreated in flight; Wang Qing formed battle lines on the north bank and strictly warned his troops.
entries.literal: Yanyun retreated and fled; Qing formed battle lines on the north bank and strictly warned his troops.

entries.zh: 日暮，酣戰不息。
entries.en: At dusk the fierce fighting did not cease.
entries.literal: At dusk the fierce fighting did not cease.

entries.zh: 契丹以生軍繼至，我軍無寸刃以益之，清與其下歿焉，時年五十三。
entries.en: The Khitans sent fresh troops in succession; the army had not a single blade more to reinforce them. Wang Qing and his men died there; he was fifty-three years old.
entries.literal: The Khitans sent fresh troops in succession; our army had not a single blade more to reinforce them; Qing and his men died there; at the time he was fifty-three years old.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：清謂其眾曰：「上將握兵，坐觀吾輩困急而不救，此必有異志。
entries.en: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: Wang Qing said to his troops, "The supreme commander holds the army yet sits watching us in dire straits without rescuing us — he must have other designs.
entries.literal: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: Qing said to his troops, "The supreme commander holds the army yet sits watching us in dire straits without rescuing us — he must have a different intent.

entries.zh: 吾輩當以死報國耳！」
entries.en: We should repay the state with our deaths!"
entries.literal: We should repay the state with our deaths!"

entries.zh: 眾感其言，莫有退者，至幕，戰不息。
entries.en: The troops were moved by his words; none retreated; they fought without ceasing until night.
entries.literal: The troops were moved by his words; none retreated; they fought without ceasing until night.

entries.zh: 契丹以新兵繼之，清及眾士盡死，由是諸軍皆奪氣。）〉
entries.en: The Khitans sent fresh troops in succession; Wang Qing and all his officers and men perished; because of this the various armies all lost heart.)〉
entries.literal: The Khitans sent new troops in succession; Qing and all his officers and men died completely; because of this the various armies all lost their fighting spirit.)〉

entries.zh: 契丹尋於所戰之地，築一京觀。
entries.en: The Khitans soon built a victory mound at the battlefield.
entries.literal: The Khitans soon built a victory mound at the place of battle.

entries.zh: 及漢高祖即位，使人平之，贈清太傅。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu of Han took the throne, he sent men to level it and posthumously enfeoffed Wang Qing as Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: When Han Gaozu ascended the throne, he sent men to level it and posthumously enfeoffed Qing as Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 是歲，清子守鈞於本邑義化別業，招魂以葬之也。
entries.en: That year Wang Qing's son Shoujun performed a soul-summoning rite at the Yihua estate in their home district and buried him.
entries.literal: That year Qing's son Shoujun at the Yihua estate in his home district performed a soul-summoning rite to bury him.

entries.zh: 梁漢璋，字國寶，應州人也。
entries.en: Liang Hanzhang, styled Guobao, was from Ying prefecture.
entries.literal: Liang Hanzhang, styled Guobao, was a native of Ying Prefecture.

entries.zh: 少以勇力事唐明宗，歷突騎、奉德指揮使。
entries.en: From youth he served Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang for his courage and strength and successively commanded the Shock Cavalry and Fengde Guards.
entries.literal: From youth he served Later Tang Emperor Mingzong for courage and strength and successively served as commander of the Shock Cavalry and Fengde Guards.

entries.zh: 高祖即位之二年，遙領欽州刺史。
entries.en: In the second year after Emperor Gaozu took the throne he was given nominal charge of Qin prefecture.
entries.literal: In the second year after Gaozu ascended the throne he held Qin Prefecture in nominal charge.

entries.zh: 三年，加檢校司空，改護聖都指揮使。
entries.en: In the third year he was promoted to honorary Minister of Works and transferred to commander-in-chief of the Imperial Guard.
entries.literal: In the third year he was promoted to honorary Minister of Works and transferred to commander-in-chief of the Imperial Guard.

entries.zh: 七年，遷檢校司徒，遙領閬州團練使。
entries.en: In the seventh year he was transferred to honorary Minister over the Masses (Situ) and given nominal charge of Lang prefecture as militia training commissioner.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to honorary Minister over the Masses (Situ) and held Lang Prefecture militia training commissioner in nominal charge.

entries.zh: 八年，授陳州防禦使，從少帝澶州還，改檢校太保、鄭州防禦使，充侍衛馬軍都指揮使，旋除永清軍兵馬留後，俄正授節制。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was appointed defense commissioner of Chen prefecture. Returning from Chanzhou with the Young Emperor, he was made honorary Grand Guardian and defense commissioner of Zheng prefecture, appointed commander-in-chief of the Palace Horse Guard, soon given military commissioner-retainee of the Yongqing Army, and shortly afterward confirmed as full military governor.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed defense commissioner of Chen Prefecture; returning from Chanzhou with the Young Emperor, he was changed to honorary Grand Guardian and defense commissioner of Zheng Prefecture, appointed commander-in-chief of the Palace Horse Guard, soon appointed military commissioner-retainee of the Yongqing Army, and shortly afterward given full appointment as military governor.

entries.zh: 是歲，詔領千騎戍冀州，尋以杜重威北討，詔以漢璋充北面馬軍都排陣使，遣收淤口關，與契丹騎五千相遇於浮陽之北界，苦戰竟日，以眾寡不侔，為流矢所中，歿於陣，即是歲十一月也，時年四十九。
entries.en: That year an edict ordered him to lead a thousand cavalry to garrison Ji prefecture. Soon, on Du Chongwei's northern campaign, an edict appointed Hanzhang chief array marshal of the northern horse army and sent him to recover Yukou Pass. He met five thousand Khitan cavalry at the northern border of Fuyang and fought bitterly all day. Outnumbered, he was struck by a stray arrow and died in the line — it was the eleventh month of that year; he was forty-nine.
entries.literal: That year an edict ordered him to lead a thousand cavalry to garrison Ji Prefecture; soon, with Du Chongwei's northern campaign, an edict appointed Hanzhang chief array marshal of the northern horse army, dispatched to recover Yukou Pass; he met five thousand Khitan cavalry at the northern border of Fuyang; they fought bitterly all day; because the numbers were unequal he was struck by a stray arrow and died in the battle line — it was the eleventh month of that year; at the time he was forty-nine years old.

entries.zh: 漢璋熟於戎馬，累有軍功，及為藩郡，所至好聚斂，無善政可紀。
entries.en: Hanzhang was skilled in military affairs and had repeated battlefield merit; as a regional governor he loved to amass wealth wherever he went, and nothing in his governance is worth recording.
entries.literal: Hanzhang was skilled in military affairs and repeatedly had military merit; when he became a regional governor, wherever he went he loved to amass wealth and there was no good governance to record.

entries.zh: 及鎮甘陵，甚有平契丹之志，但以所領偏師，驟逢敵，故有是衄焉。
entries.en: When he governed Ganling he was strongly determined to pacify the Khitans, but leading only a detached force he suddenly met the enemy and suffered this defeat.
entries.literal: When he governed Ganling he had a strong will to pacify the Khitans, but because he led only a detached force and suddenly met the enemy, he suffered this defeat.

entries.zh: 是月，其子海榮進漢璋所乘鞭馬及器仗，帝傷之，乃贈太尉。
entries.en: That month his son Hairong presented Hanzhang's riding whip, horse, and weapons and armor; the emperor grieved and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: That month his son Hairong presented Hanzhang's riding whip, horse, and weapons and armor; the emperor grieved and posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 白奉進，字德升，雲州清塞軍人也。
entries.en: Bai Fengjin, styled Desheng, was from the Qingsai Army in Yun prefecture.
entries.literal: Bai Fengjin, styled Desheng, was a native of the Qingsai Army in Yun Prefecture.

entries.zh: 父曰達子，世居朔野，以弋獵為事。
entries.en: His father was named Dazi; the family had lived for generations on the northern frontier and made their living by hunting with bow and arrow.
entries.literal: His father was named Dazi; the family for generations lived in the northern frontier and made hunting with bow and arrow their occupation.

entries.zh: 奉進少善騎射，後唐武皇鎮太原，奉進謁於軍門，以求自效，武皇納於麾下。
entries.en: From youth Fengjin was skilled at horseback riding and archery. When the Martial Emperor of Later Tang governed Taiyuan, Fengjin presented himself at the army gate seeking service, and the Martial Emperor took him into his command.
entries.literal: Fengjin from youth was skilled at horseback riding and archery; when Later Tang Martial Emperor governed Taiyuan, Fengjin presented himself at the army gate seeking to serve; the Martial Emperor took him into his command.

entries.zh: 莊宗之破夾寨也，奉進挺身首犯賊鋒，莊宗睹而壯之。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong broke the encircled camps, Fengjin was the first to charge the enemy vanguard; Zhuangzong saw this and admired his valor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong broke the encircled camps, Fengjin thrust himself forward as the first to strike the enemy vanguard; Zhuangzong saw this and admired his valor.

entries.zh: 後從戰山東河上，繼以功遷龍武指揮使。
entries.en: Later he fought east of the mountains and on the Yellow River and was repeatedly promoted for merit to commander of the Dragon Martial Guard.
entries.literal: Later he followed campaigns east of the mountains and on the Yellow River and was repeatedly promoted for merit to commander of the Dragon Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 同光中，魏王繼岌伐蜀，擢為親軍指揮使。
entries.en: During Tongguang, when the Prince of Wei Jiji attacked Shu, he was promoted to commander of the personal guard.
entries.literal: During Tongguang, when Prince of Wei Jiji attacked Shu, he was promoted to commander of the personal guard.

entries.zh: 天成、長興中，統上軍，加檢校右散騎常侍。
entries.en: During Tiancheng and Changxing he commanded the upper army and was promoted to honorary Right Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
entries.literal: During Tiancheng and Changxing he commanded the upper army and was promoted to honorary Right Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 應順中，轉捧聖右廂都指揮使、檢校刑部尚書，賜忠順保義功臣，遙領封州刺史。
entries.en: During Yingshun he was transferred to commander of the right wing of the Fengsheng Guard and honorary Minister of Justice, granted the title Loyal and Obedient Preserver of Righteousness Servitor, and given nominal charge of Feng prefecture.
entries.literal: During Yingshun he was transferred to commander of the right wing of the Fengsheng Guard and honorary Minister of Justice, granted the title Loyal and Obedient Preserver of Righteousness Servitor, and held Feng Prefecture in nominal charge.

entries.zh: 清泰中，加檢校右僕射、唐州刺史，治郡逾年，甚有政績。
entries.en: During Qingtai he was promoted to honorary Right Vice Director and prefect of Tang prefecture; governing the prefecture for more than a year he achieved very good results.
entries.literal: During Qingtai he was promoted to honorary Right Vice Director and Prefect of Tang Prefecture; governing the prefecture for more than a year he had very good administrative achievements.

entries.zh: 高祖即位，征赴闕，超加檢校司徒，充護聖左廂都指揮使，遙領歙州刺史。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he was summoned to court, promoted beyond the usual to honorary Minister over the Masses (Situ), appointed commander of the left wing of the Imperial Guard, and given nominal charge of She prefecture.
entries.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he was summoned to court and promoted beyond the usual to honorary Minister over the Masses (Situ), appointed commander of the left wing of the Imperial Guard, and held She Prefecture in nominal charge.

entries.zh: 始奉進有女嫁於皇子重信，故高祖尤所倚愛。
entries.en: Fengjin had earlier given a daughter in marriage to the prince Chongxin, so Emperor Gaozu especially relied upon and favored him.
entries.literal: At first Fengjin had a daughter who married the prince Chongxin, so Gaozu especially relied upon and favored him.

entries.zh: 二年，改護聖左右廂都指揮使。
entries.en: In the second year he was made commander of both wings of the Imperial Guard.
entries.literal: In the second year he was changed to commander of both wings of the Imperial Guard.

entries.zh: 是歲，車駕幸夷門。
entries.en: That year the imperial carriage visited Yimen.
entries.literal: That year the imperial carriage visited Yimen.

entries.zh: 五月，領昭信軍節度，充侍衛馬軍都指揮使。
entries.en: In the fifth month he was given nominal charge of the Zhaoxin Army and appointed commander-in-chief of the Palace Horse Guard.
entries.literal: In the fifth month he was given nominal charge of the Zhaoxin Army and appointed commander-in-chief of the Palace Horse Guard.

entries.zh: 六月，範延光據鄴為亂，詔遣率騎軍三千北屯滑臺。
entries.en: In the sixth month Fan Yanguang held Ye in rebellion; an edict dispatched him to lead three thousand cavalry north to encamp at Huatai.
entries.literal: In the sixth month Fan Yanguang held Ye in rebellion; an edict dispatched him to lead three thousand cavalry north to encamp at Huatai.
