entries.zh: 時符彥饒為滑州節度使，一夕，有軍士夜掠居人，奉進捕之，凡獲五盜，三在奉進本軍，二在彥饒麾下，尋命俱斬之。
entries.en: At the time Fu Yanrao was military governor of Hua prefecture. One night soldiers plundered the populace; Fengjin captured them — five thieves in all, three from his own army and two from Yanrao's command — and soon ordered all beheaded.
entries.literal: At the time Fu Yanrao was military governor of Hua Prefecture; one night some soldiers plundered the populace by night; Fengjin captured them — five thieves in all, three from Fengjin's own army and two from Yanrao's command — and soon ordered all beheaded.

entries.zh: 彥饒怒其不先告，深銜之。
entries.en: Yanrao was angry that he had not been informed beforehand and deeply resented the affront.
entries.literal: Yanrao was angry that he had not been told beforehand and deeply harbored resentment.

entries.zh: 明日，奉進左右勸奉進面謝，奉進然之，以從騎數人候彥饒於牙城，既入，且述其過。
entries.en: The next day Fengjin's attendants urged him to apologize in person. He agreed, and with several mounted followers waited for Yanrao at the headquarters gate. Once inside, he also explained his fault.
entries.literal: The next day Fengjin's attendants urged Fengjin to go in person to apologize; Fengjin agreed, and with several mounted followers waited for Yanrao at the headquarters gate; once inside, he also explained his fault.

entries.zh: 彥饒曰：「軍中法令，各有部分，何得將滑州兵士一例處斬，殊無主客之義乎！」
entries.en: Yanrao said, "Military law in the army has its respective jurisdictions — how could you execute Hua prefecture soldiers indiscriminately, with no regard for the propriety between host and guest!"
entries.literal: Yanrao said, "Military law in the army has its respective jurisdictions — how could you execute Hua Prefecture soldiers indiscriminately, utterly without the propriety of host and guest!"

entries.zh: 奉進曰：「軍士抵法，寧有彼我，今仆以咎自陳，而公怒不息，莫是與範延光同反耶！」
entries.en: Fengjin said, "When soldiers violate the law, there is no 'them' and 'us.' I come to confess my fault, yet your anger does not cease — are you rebelling along with Fan Yanguang!"
entries.literal: Fengjin said, "When soldiers violate the law, how can there be 'them' and 'us'? Now I come to confess my fault, yet your anger does not cease — could it be that you are rebelling along with Fan Yanguang!"

entries.zh: 因拂衣而起，彥饒不留。
entries.en: He then shook out his robes and rose; Yanrao did not detain him.
entries.literal: He then shook out his robes and rose; Yanrao did not detain him.

entries.zh: 其帳下介士大噪，擒奉進殺之。
entries.en: The guard soldiers under his command raised a great clamor, seized Fengjin, and killed him.
entries.literal: The guard soldiers under his command raised a great clamor, seized Fengjin, and killed him.

entries.zh: 是日，步軍都校馬萬、次校盧順密聞奉進遇害，率其步眾攻滑之子城，執彥饒送於京師，戮於班荊館北。
entries.en: That day the foot army commander Ma Wan and the second commander Lu Shunmi, hearing that Fengjin had been killed, led their foot troops to attack the inner city of Hua, seized Yanrao, and sent him to the capital, where he was executed north of Banjing Lodge.
entries.literal: That day the foot army commander Ma Wan and the second commander Lu Shunmi, hearing that Fengjin had met with disaster, led their foot troops to attack the inner city of Hua, seized Yanrao, and sent him to the capital, where he was executed north of Banjing Lodge.

entries.zh: 高祖以奉進倉卒遇禍，嘆惜久之，詔贈太傅。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu, because Fengjin had met with sudden calamity, sighed in regret for a long time and issued an edict posthumously enfeoffing him as Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: Gaozu, because Fengjin had met with sudden calamity, sighed in regret for a long time and issued an edict posthumously enfeoffing him as Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 盧順密，汶陽人也。
entries.en: Lu Shunmi was from Wenyang.
entries.literal: Lu Shunmi was a native of Wenyang.

entries.zh: 初事梁將戴思遠為步校。
entries.en: At first he served the Later Liang general Dai Siyuan as a foot officer.
entries.literal: At first he served the Later Liang general Dai Siyuan as a foot officer.

entries.zh: 思遠為鄆州節度使，領部兵屯德勝渡，留順密守其城，順密睹北軍日盛，遂遁歸莊宗，且言鄆城方虛，可以襲而取之。
entries.en: When Siyuan was military governor of Yun prefecture, he led his troops to encamp at Desheng Crossing and left Shunmi to defend the city. Shunmi saw the northern armies growing stronger daily, fled back to Zhuangzong, and reported that Yun City was then undefended and could be taken by surprise.
entries.literal: When Siyuan was military governor of Yun Prefecture, he led his troops to encamp at Desheng Crossing and left Shunmi to defend the city; Shunmi saw the northern armies growing daily stronger, then fled back to Zhuangzong and said that Yun City was then empty and could be taken by surprise.

entries.zh: 莊宗信之，尋遣明宗率眾趨鄆，果拔之，由順密之始謀也。
entries.en: Zhuangzong believed him and soon dispatched Mingzong to lead the army toward Yun; they indeed took it — this was due to Shunmi's original plan.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong believed him and soon dispatched Mingzong to lead the masses toward Yun; they indeed took it — this was due to Shunmi's original plan.

entries.zh: 莊宗尋以順密列於帳下，累遷為軍校。
entries.en: Zhuangzong soon placed Shunmi in his personal command and promoted him in succession to army officer.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong soon placed Shunmi in his personal command and promoted him in succession to army officer.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，歷數郡刺史。
entries.en: When Mingzong ascended the throne, he successively served as prefect of several prefectures.
entries.literal: When Mingzong ascended the throne, he successively served as prefect of several prefectures.

entries.zh: 順密性篤厚，臨諸軍，撫百姓，皆有仁愛之譽。
entries.en: Shunmi was by nature sincere and generous; in commanding armies and comforting the people he earned a reputation for benevolence.
entries.literal: Shunmi by nature was sincere and generous; in commanding armies and comforting the people, he had a reputation for benevolence.

entries.zh: 及高祖車駕幸夷門，範延光據鄴城叛，高祖命諸將相次領軍討之，順密亦預其行。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu's imperial carriage visited Yimen and Fan Yanguang held Ye City in rebellion, the emperor ordered the generals in succession to lead armies to suppress him; Shunmi also took part in the expedition.
entries.literal: When Gaozu's imperial carriage visited Yimen and Fan Yanguang held Ye City in rebellion, Gaozu ordered the various generals in succession to lead armies to suppress him; Shunmi also took part in the expedition.

entries.zh: 時騎將白奉進屯於滑州，尋為滑帥符彥饒所殺，軍眾大亂，爭荷戈拔刃，啖呼於外，時馬萬為步軍都校，不為遏之。
entries.en: At the time the cavalry general Bai Fengjin was encamped at Hua prefecture and was soon killed by the Hua commander Fu Yanrao. The army fell into great disorder, shouldering spears and drawing blades and shouting outside. Ma Wan was foot army commander at the time and did not restrain them.
entries.literal: At the time the cavalry general Bai Fengjin was encamped at Hua Prefecture and was soon killed by the Hua commander Fu Yanrao; the army masses fell into great disorder, all shouldering spears and drawing blades, shouting outside; at the time Ma Wan was foot army commander and did not restrain them.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：馬萬惶惑不知所為，率步兵欲從亂。）〉
entries.en: (The Zizhi Tongjian states: Ma Wan was confused and did not know what to do; he led the foot soldiers intending to join the disorder.)
entries.literal: (The Zizhi Tongjian states: Ma Wan was confused and did not know what to do; he led the foot soldiers intending to join the disorder.)

entries.zh: 順密未明其心，乃率部曲數百，趨謂諸軍及萬曰：「滑臺去行闕二百里，我等家屬在闕下，爾輩如此，不思血族乎？
entries.en: Shunmi had not yet understood his intent and therefore led several hundred of his personal troops, hastening to say to the various armies and to Wan, "Huatai is two hundred li from the traveling palace; our families are at the capital — if you act like this, do you not think of your blood kin!
entries.literal: Shunmi had not yet understood his intent and therefore led several hundred of his personal troops, hastening to say to the various armies and to Wan, "Huatai is two hundred li from the traveling palace; our families are at the capital — if you act like this, do you not think of your blood kin!

entries.zh: 奉進見殺，過在彥饒，擒送天子，必立大功。
entries.en: Fengjin was killed; the fault lies with Yanrao. Seize him and send him to the emperor — you will surely achieve great merit.
entries.literal: Fengjin was killed; the fault lies with Yanrao. Seize him and send him to the Son of Heaven — you will surely achieve great merit.

entries.zh: 順我者賞之，不順我者殺之。」
entries.en: Those who follow me I shall reward; those who do not follow me I shall kill."
entries.literal: Those who follow me I shall reward; those who do not follow me I shall kill."

entries.zh: 萬曰：「善。」
entries.en: Wan said, "Good."
entries.literal: Wan said, "Good."

entries.zh: 諸軍遂不敢動。
entries.en: The various armies then did not dare to move.
entries.literal: The various armies then did not dare to move.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》云：萬所部兵尚有呼躍者，順密殺數人，眾莫敢動。）〉
entries.en: (The Zizhi Tongjian states: Among the troops under Wan's command there were still some shouting and leaping; Shunmi killed several men and the masses did not dare to move.)
entries.literal: (The Zizhi Tongjian states: Among the troops under Wan's command there were still some shouting and leaping; Shunmi killed several men and the masses did not dare to move.)

entries.zh: 乃引軍北攻牙城，執彥饒於樓上，使裨將方太押送赴闕，滑城遂定。
entries.en: He then led the army north to attack the headquarters, seized Yanrao on the tower, and had the subordinate general Fang Tai escort him to the capital; Hua City was then settled.
entries.literal: He then led the army north to attack the headquarters, seized Yanrao on the tower, and had the subordinate general Fang Tai escort him to the capital; Hua City was then settled.

entries.zh: 朝廷即以馬萬為滑州節度使，時飛奏皆以萬為首故也。
entries.en: The court immediately appointed Ma Wan as military governor of Hua prefecture — at the time urgent memorials all listed Wan first for this reason.
entries.literal: The court immediately appointed Ma Wan as military governor of Hua Prefecture — at the time urgent memorials all listed Wan first for this reason.

entries.zh: 後數日，高祖知功由順密，尋以順密為涇州留後，至鎮未幾而卒。
entries.en: Several days later Emperor Gaozu learned that the merit was due to Shunmi and soon appointed Shunmi acting commissioner of Jing prefecture; after reaching his post he died before long.
entries.literal: Several days later Gaozu learned that the merit was due to Shunmi and soon appointed Shunmi as acting commissioner of Jing Prefecture; after reaching his post he died before long.

entries.zh: 高祖甚悼之，贈驍衛上將軍。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu deeply mourned him and posthumously honored him as General-in-Chief of the Valiant Guard.
entries.literal: Gaozu deeply mourned him and posthumously honored him as General-in-Chief of the Valiant Guard.

entries.zh: 周瑰，晉陽人也。
entries.en: Zhou Gui was from Jinyang.
entries.literal: Zhou Gui was a native of Jinyang.

entries.zh: 少端厚，善書計，自高祖時歷鎮藩翰，用為腹心，累職至牙門都校，凡帑廩出納，咸以委瑰，經十餘年，未嘗以微累見誤，高祖甚重之。
entries.en: From youth he was upright and steady and skilled at writing and reckoning. From Emperor Gaozu's time he successively served in regional governorships as a trusted confidant, rising to commander of the Gate Guard. All treasury receipts and disbursements were entrusted to him — for more than ten years he was never once faulted for minor errors, and the emperor greatly valued him.
entries.literal: From youth he was upright and steady, skilled at writing and reckoning; from Gaozu's time he successively served in regional governorships and was used as a trusted confidant, rising through posts to commander of the Gate Guard; all treasury receipts and disbursements were entrusted to Gui — for more than ten years he was never once faulted for minor errors; Gaozu greatly valued him.

entries.zh: 及即位，命權判三司事，未幾，辭曰：「臣才輕任重，懼終不濟，茍以避事，冒寵獲罪。
entries.en: When the emperor ascended the throne, he was ordered to serve provisionally as director of the Three Departments. Before long he declined, saying, "Your servant's talent is light and his burden heavy; I fear I shall ultimately not succeed. If I avoid affairs while accepting favor, I shall incur guilt for presumption.
entries.literal: When he ascended the throne, he was ordered to serve provisionally as director of the Three Departments; before long he declined, saying, "Your servant's talent is light and his burden heavy; I fear I shall ultimately not succeed. If I avoid affairs while accepting favor, I shall incur guilt for presumption.

entries.zh: 願陛下哀其疲駑，優以散秩，臣之幸也。」
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to pity my worn-out nag and grant me an honorary rank — that would be my good fortune."
entries.literal: I beg Your Majesty to pity my worn-out nag and grant me an honorary rank — that would be my good fortune."

entries.zh: 高祖可之。
entries.en: The emperor granted this.
entries.literal: Gaozu granted this.

entries.zh: 尋命權總河陽三城事，數月改授安州節度使。
entries.en: Soon he was ordered to provisionally oversee the affairs of the three cities of Heyang; several months later he was transferred and appointed military governor of An prefecture.
entries.literal: Soon he was ordered to provisionally oversee the affairs of the three cities of Heyang; several months later he was transferred and appointed military governor of An Prefecture.

entries.zh: 臨民有惠，禦軍甚嚴，一境安之。
entries.en: In dealing with the people he showed kindness; in commanding the army he was very strict — the whole territory was at peace.
entries.literal: In dealing with the people he showed kindness; in commanding the army he was very strict — the whole territory was at peace.

entries.zh: 先是，威和指揮使王暉領部下兵屯於安陸，瑰至鎮，待之甚厚。
entries.en: Earlier, the Weihe commander Wang Hui led his subordinate troops to encamp at Anlu; when Gui reached his post he treated him very generously.
entries.literal: Earlier, the Weihe commander Wang Hui led his subordinate troops to encamp at Anlu; when Gui reached his post he treated him very generously.

entries.zh: 俄聞範延光叛於魏博，張延賓寇於汜水，暉以瑰高祖之元臣也，幸國朝方危，遂害瑰於理所，自總州事，以為延光勝則附之，敗則渡江而遁，斯其計也。
entries.en: Soon word came that Fan Yanguang had rebelled in Weibo and Zhang Yanbin was raiding at Sishui. Hui, because Gui was a founding minister of Emperor Gaozu and the dynasty was then in peril, killed Gui at the administrative office and himself assumed control of the prefecture, thinking that if Yanguang won he would attach himself to him, and if he lost he would cross the river and flee — such was his plan.
entries.literal: Soon it was heard that Fan Yanguang had rebelled in Weibo and Zhang Yanbin was raiding at Sishui; Hui, because Gui was a founding minister of Gaozu and the dynasty was then in peril, then killed Gui at the administrative office and himself assumed control of the prefecture, thinking that if Yanguang won he would attach himself to him, and if he lost he would cross the river and flee — such was his plan.

entries.zh: 既而襄陽安從進遣行軍司馬張朏，會復州兵於要路以僥之，李金全承詔繼至，暉遂掠城中財帛士女，欲奔江南，尋為其下所殺。
entries.en: Before long An Congjin of Xiangyang dispatched the campaign marshal Zhang Fei to join Fuzhou troops at a strategic point to intercept him; Li Jinquan arrived by imperial order in succession. Hui then plundered the city's wealth, goods, and women and intended to flee to Jiangnan; soon he was killed by his subordinates.
entries.literal: Before long An Congjin of Xiangyang dispatched the campaign marshal Zhang Fei to join Fuzhou troops at a strategic point to intercept him; Li Jinquan arrived by imperial order in succession; Hui then plundered the city's wealth, goods, and women and intended to flee to Jiangnan; soon he was killed by his subordinates.

entries.zh: 金全至，盡誅其黨。
entries.en: When Jinquan arrived, he executed all his faction to the last man.
entries.literal: When Jinquan arrived, he executed all his faction to the last man.

entries.zh: 高祖聞瑰遇害，嘆息久之，詔贈太傅。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu, hearing that Gui had met with disaster, sighed for a long time and issued an edict posthumously honoring him as Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: Gaozu, hearing that Gui had met with disaster, sighed for a long time and issued an edict posthumously honoring him as Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 吳巒，字寶川，汶陽盧縣人也。
entries.en: Wu Luan, styled Baochuan, was from Lu County in Wenyang.
entries.literal: Wu Luan, styled Baochuan, was a native of Lu County in Wenyang.

entries.zh: 少好學，以經業從鄉試下第。
entries.en: From youth he loved learning; he took the district examination in the classics and failed.
entries.literal: From youth he loved learning; taking the classics he followed the district examination and failed.

entries.zh: 唐長興初，為沙彥珣從事，累遷大同軍節度判官。
entries.en: At the beginning of Changxing of Tang he served Sha Yanxun as an aide and was repeatedly promoted to administrative aide to the military governor of Datong.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Changxing of Tang he served Sha Yanxun as an aide and was repeatedly promoted to administrative aide to the military governor of Datong.

entries.zh: 高祖建號，契丹之援太原也，彥珣據雲中，二三顧望，及契丹還塞，彥珣出城迎謁，尋為所擄。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu established his reign title, the Khitans came to aid Taiyuan. Yanxun held Yunzhong and wavered back and forth; when the Khitans returned to the frontier, Yanxun went out of the city to meet and pay respects and was soon captured by them.
entries.literal: When Gaozu established his reign title, the Khitans came to aid Taiyuan; Yanxun held Yunzhong and wavered back and forth; when the Khitans returned to the frontier, Yanxun went out of the city to meet and pay respects and was soon captured by them.

entries.zh: 時巒在城中，謂其眾曰：「豈有禮義之人而臣於異姓乎！」
entries.en: At the time Luan was in the city and said to his followers, "How can a man of ritual and righteousness serve an alien ruler!"
entries.literal: At the time Luan was in the city and said to his masses, "How can there be a man of ritual and righteousness who serves an alien surname!"

entries.zh: 即與雲州將吏闔門拒守。
entries.en: He then together with the Yun prefecture generals and officials closed the gates and resisted in defense.
entries.literal: He then together with the Yun Prefecture generals and officials closed the gates and resisted in defense.

entries.zh: 契丹大怒，攻之，半歲不能下。
entries.en: The Khitans were greatly angered and attacked; for half a year they could not take it.
entries.literal: The Khitans were greatly angered and attacked; for half a year they could not take it.

entries.zh: 高祖致書於契丹，乃解圍而去。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu sent a letter to the Khitans, and they then lifted the siege and departed.
entries.literal: Gaozu sent a letter to the Khitans, and they then lifted the siege and departed.

entries.zh: 召巒歸闕，授徐州節度使，再遷右諫議大夫，為復州防禦使，數年罷歸。
entries.en: Luan was summoned back to court and appointed military governor of Xu prefecture; he was transferred again to Right Grand Master of Remonstrance and served as defense commissioner of Fu prefecture; after several years he was dismissed and returned.
entries.literal: Luan was summoned back to court and appointed military governor of Xu Prefecture; he was transferred again to Right Grand Master of Remonstrance and served as defense commissioner of Fu Prefecture; after several years he was dismissed and returned.

entries.zh: 初，國家以甘陵水陸要沖之地，慮契丹南侵，乃飛免芻粟，以實其郡，為大軍累年之備。
entries.en: At first the state, because Ganling was a strategic place by land and water, feared Khitan southern invasion and therefore exempted fodder and grain taxes to fill the prefecture, making preparations for a large army over many years.
entries.literal: At first the state, because Ganling was a strategic place by land and water, feared Khitan southern invasion and therefore exempted fodder and grain taxes to fill the prefecture, making preparations for a large army over many years.

entries.zh: 王令溫之為帥也，有軍校邵珂者，性兇率悖慢，令溫因事使人代之，不復齒用，閑居城中。
entries.en: When Wang Lingwen was commander, there was an army officer named Shao Ke who by nature was fierce, reckless, and insolent. Lingwen on a pretext sent someone to replace him and no longer employed him in rank; he lived idle in the city.
entries.literal: When Wang Lingwen was commander, there was an army officer named Shao Ke who by nature was fierce, reckless, and insolent; Lingwen on a pretext sent someone to replace him and no longer employed him in rank; he lived idle in the city.

entries.zh: 其子殺人，以重賂償之，其事方解，尋為州吏所恐，又悉財以彌其口。
entries.en: His son killed a man; with heavy bribes the matter was just settled. Soon he was intimidated by prefectural clerks and again gave all his wealth to silence them.
entries.literal: His son killed a man; with heavy bribes the matter was just settled; soon he was intimidated by prefectural clerks and again gave all his wealth to silence them.

entries.zh: 自是尤蓄怨恨，因使無賴者亡入契丹，言：「州有積粟，內無勁兵，圍而攻之，克之必矣。」
entries.en: From this he especially harbored resentment; he therefore sent ruffians to flee into Khitan territory, saying, "The prefecture has stored grain; within there are no strong troops — surround and attack it and you will surely take it."
entries.literal: From this he especially harbored resentment; he therefore sent ruffians to flee into Khitan territory, saying, "The prefecture has stored grain; within there are no strong troops — surround and attack it and you will surely take it."

entries.zh: 及令溫入朝，執政者以巒雲中之難，有善守之功，遂令乘軺而往，權知貝州軍州事。
entries.en: When Lingwen entered court, the administrators, because Luan had endured the hardship at Yunzhong and had the merit of good defense, therefore ordered him to go by light carriage and provisionally govern the military and civil affairs of Bei prefecture.
entries.literal: When Lingwen entered court, the administrators, because Luan had the hardship at Yunzhong and the merit of good defense, therefore ordered him to go by light carriage and provisionally govern the military and civil affairs of Bei Prefecture.

entries.zh: 既至，會大寒，軍士無衣者悉衣之，平生廉儉，囊無資用，以至壞帳幕以赒之，其推心撫士如此。
entries.en: After he arrived, it happened to be bitter cold; he clothed all soldiers who had no garments. All his life he was frugal and plain, his purse had no funds for use, so much so that he tore up worn tent curtains to give relief — such was his wholehearted care for the troops.
entries.literal: After he arrived, it happened to be bitter cold; he clothed all soldiers who had no garments; all his life he was frugal and plain, his purse had no funds for use, so much so that he tore up worn tent curtains to give relief — such was his wholehearted care for the troops.

entries.zh: 邵珂一見，因求自效，即聽而任之。
entries.en: At first sight Shao Ke therefore requested to serve at his own initiative; Luan heard him and entrusted him with the task.
entries.literal: At first sight Shao Ke therefore requested to serve at his own initiative; he was heard and entrusted with the task.

entries.zh: 巒素為書生，旁無爪牙，珂慷慨自陳，願效死左右，巒遣督義兵，守城之南門。
entries.en: Luan had always been a scholar and had no strong supporters at his side. Ke declared himself generously and volunteered to die at his side; Luan dispatched him to supervise the volunteer militia and defend the south gate of the city.
entries.literal: Luan had always been a scholar and had no strong supporters at his side; Ke declared himself generously and volunteered to die at his side; Luan dispatched him to supervise the volunteer militia and defend the south gate of the city.

entries.zh: 天福九年正月，契丹大至。
entries.en: In the first month of the ninth year of Tianfu the Khitans arrived in force.
entries.literal: In the first month of the ninth year of Tianfu the Khitans arrived in force.

entries.zh: 其一日大噪環其城，明日陳攻具於四墉，三日契丹主躬率步奚及渤海夷等四面進攻。
entries.en: On the first day they raised a great clamor encircling the city; the next day they deployed siege engines on the four walls; on the third day the Khitan ruler personally led the steppe Xi and Bohai barbarians and others to attack from all four sides.
entries.literal: On the first day they raised a great clamor encircling the city; the next day they deployed siege engines on the four walls; on the third day the Khitan ruler personally led the steppe Xi and Bohai barbarians and others to attack from all four sides.

entries.zh: 巒眾投薪於夾城中，繼以炬火，敵之梯沖，焚爇殆盡。
entries.en: Luan's forces threw firewood into the inter-wall space, followed by torch fire; the enemy's scaling ladders and battering rams were burned nearly to destruction.
entries.literal: Luan's masses threw firewood into the inter-wall space, followed by torch fire; the enemy's scaling ladders and battering rams were burned nearly to destruction.

entries.zh: 是日，敵復合圍，郡中丁壯皆登城守陴。
entries.en: That day the enemy closed ranks again; all able-bodied men in the prefecture mounted the walls to defend the parapets.
entries.literal: That day the enemy closed ranks again; all able-bodied men in the prefecture mounted the walls to defend the parapets.

entries.zh: 俄而珂自南門引敵騎同入，巒守東門，未知其事，左右告曰：「邵珂背矣！」
entries.en: Before long Ke from the south gate led enemy cavalry in together. Luan was defending the east gate and did not yet know of the matter; his attendants reported, "Shao Ke has turned traitor!"
entries.literal: Before long Ke from the south gate led enemy cavalry in together; Luan was defending the east gate and did not yet know of the matter; his attendants reported, "Shao Ke has turned traitor!"

entries.zh: 巒顧城中已亂，即馳馬還公館，投井而死，契丹遂屠其城。
entries.en: Luan looked back and the city was already in disorder. He immediately spurred his horse back to the official residence, threw himself into a well, and died; the Khitans then massacred the city.
entries.literal: Luan looked back and the city was already in disorder; he immediately spurred his horse back to the official residence and threw himself into a well and died; the Khitans then massacred the city.

entries.zh: 朝野士庶，聞者鹹嘆惜之。
entries.en: Officials and commoners throughout the court and countryside, when they heard of it, all sighed in regret.
entries.literal: Officials and commoners throughout the court and countryside, when they heard of it, all sighed in regret.

entries.zh: 翟璋，未詳何許人也。
entries.en: Di Zhang — his place of origin is not recorded.
entries.literal: Di Zhang — it is not clear from where he came.

entries.zh: 好勇多力，時目為大蟲，即「虎癡」之稱也。
entries.en: Brave and powerfully built, he was at the time called the "Great Worm"—the nickname "Tiger Fool."
entries.literal: He was brave and possessed great strength; at the time people called him the "Great Worm," that is, the sobriquet "Tiger Fool."

entries.zh: 後唐天成初，自鄴都馬步軍都指揮使領平州刺史，尋改復州防禦使。
entries.en: At the beginning of Tiancheng of Later Tang, from commandant of cavalry and infantry at the Yedu capital he was made prefect of Ping prefecture; soon he was made defense commissioner of Fu prefecture.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng of Later Tang, from commandant of cavalry and infantry at the capital at Yedu he took office as prefect of Ping Prefecture; soon he was changed to defense commissioner of Fu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 三年三月，遷新州威塞軍兩使留後。
entries.en: In the third year, third month, he was transferred to acting commissioner of the dual posts of the Weisai Army at Xin prefecture.
entries.literal: In the third year, third month, he was transferred to acting commissioner of both offices of the Weisai Army at Xin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 四年五月，正授旄節。
entries.en: In the fourth year, fifth month, he was formally granted a command baton and military commission.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, fifth month, he was formally granted the command baton and flag.

entries.zh: 長興元年二月，加檢校太保，入為右領軍衛上將軍，轉左羽林統軍。
entries.en: In the first year of Changxing, second month, he was promoted honorary Grand Guardian, entered court as senior general of the Right Leading Army Guard, and was made commander of the Left Imperial Forest Army.
entries.literal: In the first year of Changxing, second month, he was promoted to honorary Grand Guardian, entered court as senior general of the Right Leading Army Guard, and transferred to commander of the Left Imperial Forest Army.

entries.zh: 清泰中，復領新州。
entries.en: During Qingtai he again held Xin prefecture.
entries.literal: During Qingtai he again held Xin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 高祖建義，割新州屬契丹。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu raised his righteous cause, Xin prefecture was ceded to the Khitans.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu raised his righteous campaign, Xin Prefecture was ceded to the Khitans.

entries.zh: 時契丹大軍歸國，遣璋於管內配率犒宴之資，須及十萬緡，山後地貧，民不堪命。
entries.en: At that time the main Khitan army was returning home and ordered Zhang to levy within his jurisdiction supplies to reward and feast them, amounting to one hundred thousand strings of cash; the region beyond the mountains was poor and the people could not bear it.
entries.literal: At that time the Khitan great army was returning home; they sent Zhang to levy within his jurisdiction supplies for rewarding and feasting them, which had to reach one hundred thousand strings of cash; the land beyond the mountains was poor and the people could not bear the burden.

entries.zh: 始契丹以軟語撫璋，璋謂必得南歸，及委璋平叛奚、圍雲州皆有功，故留之不遣。
entries.en: At first the Khitans reassured Zhang with gentle words, and Zhang believed he would surely return south; when they later entrusted him with pacifying the rebellious Xi and besieging Yun prefecture he succeeded in both, so they kept him and would not send him away.
entries.literal: Initially the Khitans comforted Zhang with gentle words, and Zhang believed he would surely be allowed to return south; later when they entrusted Zhang to pacify the rebellious Xi and besiege Yun Prefecture he had merit in both, so they kept him and did not send him away.

entries.zh: 璋郁郁不得志，遇疾尋卒焉。
entries.en: Depressed and unable to fulfill his ambitions, Zhang fell ill and soon died.
entries.literal: Zhang was depressed and unfulfilled; he fell ill and soon died there.

entries.zh: 郭璘，邢州人也。
entries.en: Guo Lin was from Xing prefecture.
entries.literal: Guo Lin was a native of Xing Prefecture.

entries.zh: 初事後唐明宗，漸升為軍校。
entries.en: At first he served Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang and gradually rose to army officer.
entries.literal: At first he served Later Tang Emperor Mingzong and gradually rose to army officer.

entries.zh: 天福中，為奉國指揮使，歷數郡刺史。
entries.en: During Tianfu he was commander of the Fengguo Army and successively served as prefect of several prefectures.
entries.literal: During Tianfu he was commander of the Fengguo Army and successively served as prefect of several prefectures.

entries.zh: 開運中，移領易州，契丹攻其郡，璘率厲士眾，同其甘苦，敵不能克。
entries.en: During Kaiyun he was transferred to nominal charge of Yi prefecture. The Khitans attacked his prefecture; Lin led and encouraged the soldiers and masses, sharing their hardships; the enemy could not take it.
entries.literal: During Kaiyun he was transferred to nominal charge of Yi Prefecture; the Khitans attacked his prefecture; Lin led and encouraged the soldiers and masses, sharing their hardships; the enemy could not take it.

entries.zh: 復以州兵擊賊，數獲其利，朝廷嘉之，就加檢校太保。
entries.en: Again with prefectural troops he struck the bandits and repeatedly gained advantage; the court praised this and on the spot added honorary Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: Again with prefectural troops he struck the bandits and repeatedly gained advantage; the court praised this and on the spot added honorary Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 契丹主嘗謂左右曰：「吾不畏一天下，乃為此人所抑挫！」
entries.en: The Khitan ruler once said to his attendants, "I fear not all under heaven — yet I am checked and frustrated by this man!"
entries.literal: The Khitan ruler once said to his attendants, "I fear not all under heaven — yet I am checked and frustrated by this man!"

entries.zh: 重威降，契丹使通事耿崇美誘其民眾，璘不能制，城既降，為崇美所害。
entries.en: When Chongwei surrendered, the Khitans sent the interpreter Geng Chongmei to entice his populace; Lin could not control them. Once the city had surrendered, he was killed by Chongmei.
entries.literal: When Chongwei surrendered, the Khitans sent the interpreter Geng Chongmei to entice his populace; Lin could not control them; once the city had surrendered, he was killed by Chongmei.

entries.zh: 漢高祖即位，詔贈太傅。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozu of Han took the throne, an edict posthumously honored him as Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: When Han Gaozu ascended the throne, an edict posthumously honored him as Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 陳保極，閩中人也。
entries.en: Chen Baoji was a native of Fujian.
entries.literal: Chen Baoji was a man of Minzhong.

entries.zh: 好學，善屬文，後唐天成中擢進士第，秦王從榮聞其名，辟為從事。
entries.en: Fond of study and skilled in prose, he passed the jinshi examination in the Tiancheng era of Later Tang. When Prince of Qin Congrong heard of him, he took him on as a staff officer.
entries.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at literary composition. In the Tiancheng era of Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination. Prince of Qin Congrong heard his name and recruited him as an aide.

entries.zh: 從榮素急暴，後怒保極不告出遊宰相門，以馬箠鞭之，尋出為定州推官。
entries.en: Congrong was naturally violent and impulsive. He later flew into a rage because Baoji had visited the chief ministers without telling him, and lashed him with a riding crop. Baoji was soon transferred out to serve as investigating officer in Dingzhou.
entries.literal: Congrong was by nature violent and quick-tempered. Later he grew angry that Baoji had gone out to visit the chief ministers' gates without informing him, and beat him with a horse whip; soon afterward he was sent out as investigating officer of Ding prefecture.

entries.zh: 從榮敗，執政知其屈，擢居三署，歷禮部、倉部員外郎。
entries.en: After Congrong's downfall the court recognized that Baoji had been treated unjustly and promoted him into the Three Bureaus, where he served successively as vice director in the ministries of rites and of granaries.
entries.literal: When Congrong was defeated, those in power knew he had been wronged and promoted him to the Three Bureaus, serving in succession as vice director in the Ministries of Rites and of Granaries.

entries.zh: 初，桑維翰登第之歲，保極時在秦王幕下，因戲謂同輩曰：「近知今歲有三個半人及第。」
entries.en: When Sang Weihan took his degree, Baoji was still on the prince of Qin's staff. He joked to his colleagues, "I've just heard that three and a half men passed the examination this year."
entries.literal: Earlier, in the year Sang Weihan passed the examination, Baoji was then on the Prince of Qin's staff. In jest he told his colleagues: "I have just learned that this year three and a half men passed."

entries.zh: 蓋其年收四人，保極以維翰短陋，故謂之半人也。
entries.en: Four candidates had in fact passed that year, but because Weihan was short and plain-looking, Baoji counted him as only half a man.
entries.literal: For that year four were admitted; Baoji, because Weihan was short and homely, therefore called him half a man.

entries.zh: 天福中，維翰既居相位，保極時在曹郎，慮除官差跌，心不自安，乃乞假南遊，將謀退跡。
entries.en: In the Tianfu era, once Weihan had become chief minister, Baoji was serving as a bureau secretary. Fearful of being demoted, he grew uneasy and asked leave to travel south, planning to retire from office.
entries.literal: During Tianfu, after Weihan had taken the chief ministership, Baoji was then a bureau secretary. Fearing a demotion in office, he was ill at ease in mind and asked leave to travel south, intending to withdraw from public life.

entries.zh: 既而襄、鄧長吏以行止入奏，維翰乃奏於高祖曰：「保極閩人，多狡，恐逃入淮海。」
entries.en: Soon the senior officials of Xiang and Deng reported his movements to court. Weihan then told Gaozu, "Baoji is a Fujian man and notoriously cunning; I fear he may flee to the Huaihai region."
entries.literal: Soon the chief officials of Xiang and Deng reported his movements to the throne. Weihan then memorialized Gaozu: "Baoji is a man of Min, very crafty; I fear he may flee into the Huaihai region."

entries.zh: 即以詔追赴闕，將下臺鍛成其事，同列李崧極言以解之，因令所司就所居鞫之，貶為衛尉寺丞，仍奪金紫。
entries.en: An edict immediately recalled him to the capital. The authorities were about to hand him over to the censorate and manufacture a criminal case, but his colleague Li Song argued forcefully on his behalf. The court then ordered an inquiry at his home. He was demoted to assistant director in the Court of Imperial Regalia and stripped of his gold seal and purple robe.
entries.literal: An edict at once recalled him to court. They were about to send him to the censorate and forge the case into a crime, but his colleague Li Song spoke strongly to clear him. Thereupon the authorities were ordered to try him at his residence. He was demoted to assistant director of the Court of Imperial Regalia and stripped of his gold seal and purple robe.

entries.zh: 尋復為倉部員外郎，竟以銜憤而卒。
entries.en: He was soon restored as vice director in the ministry of granaries, but in the end died still brooding over the injustice.
entries.literal: Soon he was restored as vice director in the Ministry of Granaries, but in the end died nursing resentment.

entries.zh: 王瑜，其先范陽人也。
entries.en: Wang Yu's family came from Fanyang.
entries.literal: Wang Yu's ancestors were from Fanyang.

entries.zh: 父欽祚，仕至殿中監，出為義州刺史。
entries.en: His father Qinhuo rose to director of the palace domestic service and was later posted as prefect of Yi.
entries.literal: His father Qinhuo rose in office to Director of the Palace Domestic Service and went out as prefect of Yi.

entries.zh: 瑜性兇狡，然雋辯驍果，騎射刀筆之長，亦稱於當代。
entries.en: Yu was by nature violent and treacherous, yet he was quick-witted, eloquent, and bold in battle, and his skill at riding, archery, and administrative writing also won him a name in his day.
entries.literal: Yu by nature was fierce and cunning, yet he was eloquent, brave, and resolute; his skill in horsemanship, archery, and the brush also won praise in his generation.

entries.zh: 起家累為從事。
entries.en: He began his career as a series of staff appointments.
entries.literal: From his first appointment he repeatedly served as an aide.

entries.zh: 天福中，授左贊善大夫。
entries.en: In the Tianfu era he was appointed left mentor.
entries.literal: During Tianfu he was appointed Left Mentor.

entries.zh: 會濮郡秋稼豐衍，稅籍不均，命乘使車，按察定計。
entries.en: When Pu prefecture had a bumper autumn harvest but uneven tax rolls, he was sent out in the envoy carriage to inspect the district and set the levies right.
entries.literal: It happened that in Pu prefecture the autumn harvest was abundant but the tax registers were uneven, so he was ordered to ride the envoy carriage and inspect and fix the assessments.

entries.zh: 既至郡，謂校簿吏胡蘊、惠鶚曰：「余食貧久矣，室無增資，為我致意縣宰，且求假貸。」
entries.en: On reaching the prefecture he told the registry clerks Hu Yun and Hui E, "I have been poor for years and my household has no spare funds. Pass word to the county magistrates for me and ask them for a loan."
entries.literal: When he reached the prefecture he said to the registry clerks Hu Yun and Hui E: "I have been poor in food for a long time and my household has no added wealth. Convey my regards to the county magistrates and ask them for loans."

entries.zh: 由是濮之部內五邑令長共斂錢五十萬，私獻於瑜。
entries.en: The magistrates of the five counties in Pu then pooled five hundred thousand cash and secretly gave it to Yu.
entries.literal: Thereupon the magistrates of the five districts within Pu together collected five hundred thousand cash and privately presented it to Yu.

entries.zh: 瑜即以書上奏，高祖覽章嘆曰：「廉直清慎有如此者，誠良臣也。」
entries.en: Yu then submitted a memorial. When Gaozu read it he exclaimed, "Such integrity, uprightness, purity, and caution—this is truly a fine minister."
entries.literal: Yu thereupon memorialized in writing. Gaozu read the memorial and sighed: "Integrity, uprightness, purity, and caution such as this—truly a fine minister."

entries.zh: 於是二吏五宰即時停黜，擢瑜為太府少卿。
entries.en: The two clerks and five magistrates were immediately dismissed, and Yu was promoted to vice director of the imperial storehouse.
entries.literal: Thereupon the two clerks and five magistrates were at once dismissed, and Yu was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse.

entries.zh: 杜重威之鎮東平也，瑜父欽祚為節度副使，及重威移鎮常山，瑜乃詭計於重威，使奏己為恒州節度副使，竟代其父位。
entries.en: While Du Chongwei held Dongping, Yu's father Qinhuo served as his deputy. When Chongwei was transferred to Changshan, Yu persuaded him by a ruse to recommend him as deputy military governor of Hengzhou, and in the end took his father's place.
entries.literal: When Du Chongwei governed Dongping, Yu's father Qinhuo was military governor's deputy. When Chongwei was transferred to govern Changshan, Yu devised a stratagem with Chongwei and had him memorialize that Yu himself should be deputy military governor of Heng, and in the end replaced his father's post.

entries.zh: 歲餘，入為刑部郎中。
entries.en: After a little more than a year he was recalled to the capital as director in the ministry of punishments.
entries.literal: After more than a year he entered the capital as Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

entries.zh: 丙午歲，父欽祚刺舉義州，瑜歸寧至郡。
entries.en: In the bingwu year his father Qinhuo was posted as investigating commissioner of Yi prefecture, and Yu went to visit him there.
entries.literal: In the bingwu year his father Qinhuo was investigating commissioner of Yi prefecture, and Yu went home on a visit to the prefecture.

entries.zh: 會契丹據有中夏，何建以秦州歸蜀，瑜說欽祚曰：「若不西走，當屬契丹矣！」
entries.en: The Khitans had seized the heartland, and He Jian had surrendered Qinzhou to Shu. Yu urged his father, "If we do not flee west, we shall end up under Khitan rule!"
entries.literal: It happened that the Khitans held the Central Plains and He Jian surrendered Qin prefecture to Shu. Yu urged Qinhuo: "If we do not flee west, we shall fall under the Khitans!"

entries.zh: 厲色數諫，其父怒而不從。
entries.en: He remonstrated again and again with a fierce expression, but his father grew angry and refused.
entries.literal: With stern countenance he remonstrated repeatedly; his father grew angry and would not follow.

entries.zh: 因其臥疾涉旬，瑜仗劍而脅之曰：「老懦無謀，欲趨炮烙。
entries.en: When his father had been bedridden for more than ten days, Yu drew his sword and threatened him: "You old fool without a plan—you are rushing straight toward the stake.
entries.literal: Because he had lain ill for more than ten days, Yu took sword in hand and threatened him: "Old coward without a plan—you wish to rush toward the burning stake.

entries.zh: 不即為計，則死於刃下。」
entries.en: If you do not act now, you die by this blade."
entries.literal: If you do not decide at once, you die beneath the blade."

entries.zh: 父不得已而聽之。
entries.en: His father had no choice but to yield.
entries.literal: His father had no choice but to obey.

entries.zh: 時隴東屯兵扼其川路，將北趣蕃部假途，而因與郡盜酋長趙徽歃血為約，以兄事之。
entries.en: Garrison troops in eastern Long blocked the river routes, so they planned to head north through tribal territory and borrow a passage. Yu then swore a blood oath with Zhao Hui, a local bandit chieftain, and treated him as an elder brother.
entries.literal: At that time Longdong garrison troops blocked the river routes. They intended to go north toward the tribal lands to borrow a passage, and therefore with Zhao Hui, chieftain of the local bandits in the prefecture, they made a blood oath and treated him as an elder brother.

entries.zh: 謂徽曰：「西至成都，余身為相，余父為將，爾當領一大郡，能遂行乎？」
entries.en: He told Hui, "When we reach Chengdu, I shall become chief minister and my father a general, and you shall govern a great prefecture. Will you go through with this?"
entries.literal: He said to Hui: "When we reach Chengdu in the west, I shall become chief minister and my father a general; you shall hold a great prefecture. Can you go through with the journey?"

entries.zh: 徽曰：「諾。」
entries.en: Hui answered, "Agreed."
entries.literal: Hui said: "Agreed."

entries.zh: 瑜慮為所賣，先致其妻孥，館於郡中。
entries.en: Fearing betrayal, Yu first sent Hui's wife and children to stay in the prefectural seat as hostages.
entries.literal: Yu feared being betrayed and first sent Hui's wife and children to lodge in the prefectural city.

entries.zh: 行有期矣，徽潛召其黨，伺於郊外。
entries.en: When the day of departure was fixed, Hui secretly gathered his men and waited in ambush outside the city.
entries.literal: When the day of departure was set, Hui secretly summoned his followers and lay in wait in the suburbs.

entries.zh: 子夜，瑜舉族行，輜重絡繹十有餘里。
entries.en: At midnight Yu set out with his entire clan, their baggage train stretching more than ten li along the road.
entries.literal: At midnight Yu moved with his whole clan; baggage trains stretched in an unbroken line for more than ten li.

entries.zh: 徽之所親，循溝澮而遁，至馬峽路隅，舉燧相應，其黨起於伏莽，斷欽祚之首，貫諸長矛。
entries.en: Hui's men stole along ditches and canals until, at a bend on the Maxia road, they lit signal fires. His band sprang from the brush, cut off Qinhuo's head, and spitted it on a long spear.
entries.literal: Hui's intimates stole along ditches and canals. At a corner of the road at Maxia they raised beacon fires in answer to one another; his band rose from ambush in the thickets, cut off Qinhuo's head, and threaded it on a long spear.

entries.zh: 平生聚蓄金幣萬計，皆為賊所掠，少長百口，殺之殆盡。
entries.en: The gold and cash he had amassed over a lifetime—tens of thousands in all—were looted by the bandits, and of more than a hundred kin young and old, nearly all were slaughtered.
entries.literal: Gold and coin he had amassed in his lifetime, numbering in the tens of thousands, were all plundered by the bandits; of more than a hundred persons young and old, nearly all were killed.

entries.zh: 瑜尚獨戰千人，矢不虛發，手無射捍，其指流血。
entries.en: Yu still fought on alone against a thousand men; every arrow he loosed found its mark. He had no archer's thumb guard, and his fingers ran with blood.
entries.literal: Yu still fought alone against a thousand; not an arrow missed its mark. He had no thumb guard for shooting, and his fingers bled.

entries.zh: 及窘，乃夜竄山谷，落發為僧。
entries.en: When he was cornered, he fled by night into the hills, shaved his head, and took the tonsure.
entries.literal: When hard pressed, he fled by night into the mountains and valleys, shaved his head, and became a monk.

entries.zh: 月餘，為樵人所獲，縶送岐州，為侯益所殺，時年三十九。
entries.en: After more than a month woodcutters captured him and sent him bound to Qizhou, where Hou Yi had him executed. He was thirty-nine.
entries.literal: After more than a month he was seized by woodcutters, bound, and sent to Qi prefecture, where Hou Yi had him killed. He was thirty-nine.

entries.zh: 張繼祚，故齊王全義之子也。
entries.en: Zhang Jizuo was a son of the former prince of Qi, Quanyi.
entries.literal: Zhang Jizuo was a son of the former Prince of Qi, Quanyi.

entries.zh: 始為河南府衙內指揮使，全義卒，除金吾將軍，旋授蔡州刺史，累官至檢校太保。
entries.en: He began as commander of the Henan prefectural guard. After Quanyi's death he was made a general of the golden crow guard, soon received appointment as prefect of Cai, and eventually rose to honorary grand guardian.
entries.literal: At first he was commander of the Henan prefectural guard; when Quanyi died he was made general of the Golden Crow guard, soon appointed prefect of Cai, and rose in office to honorary Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 明宗郊天，充供頓使，復除西衛上將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Mingzong sacrificed to Heaven at the suburbs, Jizuo served as provisioning commissioner and was again appointed general of the western guard.
entries.literal: When Emperor Mingzong performed the suburban sacrifice to Heaven, he served as provisioning commissioner and was again appointed general of the Western Guard.

entries.zh: 唐清泰末，丁母憂。
entries.en: At the end of Tang's Qingtai era he went into mourning for his mother.
entries.literal: At the end of the Qingtai era of Tang he entered mourning for his mother.

entries.zh: 天福初，喪制未闋，會張從賓作亂，發兵迫脅，取赴河陽，令知留守事。
entries.en: Early in the Tianfu era, before his mourning period had ended, Zhang Congbin rebelled, raised troops, and forced him along. He was taken to Heyang and put in charge of the regency.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, before his mourning term had ended, Zhang Congbin rebelled, raised troops, and coerced him; he was taken to Heyang and ordered to manage the regency affairs.

entries.zh: 從賓敗，與二子詔戮於市。
entries.en: When Congbin was defeated, he and his two sons were executed by imperial order in the marketplace.
entries.literal: When Congbin was defeated, he and his two sons were executed by imperial edict in the marketplace.

entries.zh: 始繼祚與範延光有舊，嘗遣人以馬遺之。
entries.en: Jizuo had earlier been on friendly terms with Fan Yanguang and once sent him horses as a gift.
entries.literal: Earlier Jizuo had been on friendly terms with Fan Yanguang and once sent someone to present him with horses.

entries.zh: 屬朝廷起兵，將討鄴城，為巡兵所獲，奏之，高祖深忌之。
entries.en: When the court marched to attack Ye, patrol troops seized the gift and reported it, and Gaozu took deep offense.
entries.literal: When the court raised troops to attack Ye, the gift was seized by patrol soldiers and reported; Gaozu deeply resented it.

entries.zh: 及敗，宰臣桑維翰以父珙早事齊王，奏欲雪之，高祖不允，
entries.en: After the defeat, chief minister Sang Weihan—whose father Gong had long served the prince of Qi—memorialized to clear the family's name, but Gaozu refused,
entries.literal: When he was defeated, the chief minister Sang Weihan, because his father Gong had long served the Prince of Qi, memorialized to clear the family, but Gaozu would not agree,

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：史館修撰李濤上言：張全義有再造洛邑之功，乞免其族。
entries.en: (Comprehensive Mirror: Li Tao of the historiography institute memorialized that Zhang Quanyi had restored Luoyang and asked that his clan be spared.
entries.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: Li Tao, reviser of the Historiography Institute, memorialized: Zhang Quanyi had the merit of restoring Luoyang; I beg that his clan be spared.

entries.zh: 遂止誅繼祚妻子。）〉
entries.en: The execution of Jizuo's wife and children was then halted.)〉
entries.literal: Thereupon the execution of Jizuo's wife and children was halted.)〉

entries.zh: 遂止罪繼祚一房，不累其族。
entries.en: Punishment was thus limited to Jizuo's own household and did not extend to his wider clan.
entries.literal: Thus punishment stopped at Jizuo's own household and did not extend to his clan.

entries.zh: 鄭阮，洺州人也。
entries.en: Zheng Ruan was a native of Mingzhou.
entries.literal: Zheng Ruan was a man of Mingzhou.

entries.zh: 少為本部牙將，唐莊宗略地山東，以阮首歸義旗，繼遷軍職。
entries.en: In youth he served as a military adjutant of his circuit. When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang conquered eastern Shandong, Ruan was the first to rally to the loyalist cause and thereafter rose through military ranks.
entries.literal: In youth he served as a military adjutant of his circuit. When Tang Zhuangzong swept through eastern Shandong, Ruan was the first to join the loyalist banner, and thereafter rose through military posts.

entries.zh: 阮有子，自幼事明宗中門使安重誨，重誨以其桀黠，愛之。
entries.en: Ruan had a son who from childhood served An Chonghui, Mingzong's middle-gate commissioner. Chonghui took a liking to him for his clever boldness.
entries.literal: Ruan had a son who from childhood served An Chonghui, the middle-gate commissioner under Emperor Mingzong. Chonghui loved him for his shrewd boldness.

entries.zh: 及明宗即位，擢阮至鳳翔節度副使。
entries.en: When Mingzong took the throne, Ruan was promoted to deputy military governor of Fengxiang.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Ruan was promoted to deputy military governor of Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 會末帝鎮其地，阮稍狎之。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor governed the region, Ruan grew somewhat familiar with him.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor governed that region, Ruan grew somewhat familiar with him.

entries.zh: 末帝嗣位，以阮為趙州刺史。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor succeeded to the throne, he appointed Ruan prefect of Zhao.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor succeeded to the throne, he appointed Ruan prefect of Zhao.

entries.zh: 而阮性貪濁，民間細務，皆密察而紀之，令納賂以贖罪。
entries.en: But Ruan was greedy and corrupt. He secretly investigated and recorded every petty matter among the people and demanded bribes to redeem offenses.
entries.literal: But Ruan was greedy and corrupt. He secretly investigated and recorded every petty matter among the people and ordered bribes to redeem offenses.

entries.zh: 有屬邑令，因科醵拒命，密以束素募人陰求其過，後竟停其職，人甚非之。
entries.en: When a subordinate county magistrate refused a levy assessment, Ruan secretly hired men with cloth bribes to find his faults; the magistrate was eventually removed from office, to widespread condemnation.
entries.literal: A subordinate county magistrate, refusing a levy assessment, was secretly pursued by men hired with cloth bribes to find his faults; he was eventually removed from office, to public condemnation.

entries.zh: 又嘗以郡符取部內兇肆中人隸其籍者，遣於青州，舁喪至洺，郡人憚其遠，願輸直百緡以免其行，阮本無喪，即受直放還。
entries.en: He also once used a prefectural order to take a registered man from an undertaker's shop in his territory and send him to Qingzhou to carry a coffin back to Ming. Dreading the distance, the people offered one hundred strings of cash to be spared the journey. Ruan had no bereavement of his own, yet accepted the payment and released the man.
entries.literal: He also once used a prefectural order to take a registered man from the undertaker's shop within his territory and send him to Qingzhou to bear a coffin back to Ming; the people, dreading the distance, offered one hundred strings of cash to be spared the journey. Ruan had no actual bereavement, yet accepted the payment and released the man.

entries.zh: 識者曰：「此非吉兆也。」
entries.en: The knowing said, "This is no good omen."
entries.literal: The knowing said, "This is no good omen."

entries.zh: 未幾，改曹州刺史，為政愈弊。
entries.en: Before long he was transferred to be prefect of Cao, and his governance grew still more corrupt.
entries.literal: Before long he was transferred to be prefect of Cao, and his governance grew still more corrupt.

entries.zh: 高祖建義入洛，阮自郡來朝，旋為本州指揮使石重立所殺，舉族無孑遺。
entries.en: When Gaozu raised the righteous cause and entered Luoyang, Ruan came from his prefecture to court and was soon killed by Shi Chongli, commander of his native prefecture, with his entire clan wiped out to the last.
entries.literal: When Gaozu raised the righteous cause and entered Luoyang, Ruan came from his prefecture to court and was soon killed by Shi Chongli, commander of his native prefecture, with his entire clan wiped out to the last.

entries.zh: 劉遂清，字得一，青州北海人，梁開封尹鄩之猶子也。
entries.en: Liu Suiqing, styled Deyi, was from Beihai in Qingzhou and was a nephew by marriage of Zheng, Liang's chief minister of Kaifeng.
entries.literal: Liu Suiqing, style Deyi, was a man of Beihai in Qing prefecture, a nephew by marriage of Zheng, chief minister of Kaifeng under Liang.

entries.zh: 父琪，以鴻臚卿致仕。
entries.en: His father Qi had retired as minister of the court of imperial entertainments.
entries.literal: His father Qi retired as Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

entries.zh: 遂清少敏惠，初仕梁為保鑾軍使，歷內諸司使，莊宗入汴，不改其職。
entries.en: Suiqing was clever from youth. He first served Liang as commissioner of the palace guard, then held a series of posts as commissioner of the inner bureaus; when Zhuangzong entered Bian his offices were left unchanged.
entries.literal: Suiqing in youth was quick and clever. He first served Liang as commissioner of the Palace Guard and passed through the posts of commissioner of the inner bureaus; when Zhuangzong entered Bian he did not change his office.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，加檢校尚書僕射，委以西都監守。
entries.en: When Mingzong took the throne he was given the honorary title of vice director of the masters of writing and charged with guarding the western capital.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he was given the honorary title of Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and entrusted with guarding the western capital.

entries.zh: 逾歲，以中山王都有不臣之跡，除遂清為易州刺史，俾遏其寇沖，既至郡，大有禦侮之略，境內賴焉。
entries.en: A year later, when Wang Du of Zhongshan showed signs of rebellion, Suiqing was appointed prefect of Yi to block his raids. On reaching the prefecture he devised strong defenses, and the region came to rely on him.
entries.literal: After a year, because Wang Du of Zhongshan showed signs of disloyalty, Suiqing was appointed prefect of Yi to block his raiding thrusts. Once he reached the prefecture he had great plans for defense, and the territory relied on him.

entries.zh: 王都平，加檢校司空，遷棣州刺史。
entries.en: After Wang Du was pacified he was given the honorary title of minister of works and transferred to prefect of Di.
entries.literal: When Wang Du was pacified he was given the honorary title of Minister of Works and transferred to prefect of Di.

entries.zh: 天成、長興中，歷典淄、興、登三郡，咸有善政。
entries.en: During the Tiancheng and Changxing eras he governed in turn Zi, Xing, and Deng, and in each place earned a reputation for good government.
entries.literal: During Tiancheng and Changxing he governed in succession the three prefectures of Zi, Xing, and Deng, and in each had good administration.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒潞王紀》：帝之起鳳翔也，召興州刺史劉遂清，遲疑不至。
entries.en: (Comprehensive Mirror, Annals of the Prince of Lu: When the emperor rose at Fengxiang he summoned Liu Suiqing, prefect of Xing, but Suiqing hesitated and did not come.
entries.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror, Annals of Prince of Lu: When the emperor rose at Fengxiang he summoned Liu Suiqing, prefect of Xing, but he hesitated and did not come.

entries.zh: 聞帝入洛，乃悉集三泉、西縣、金牛、桑林戍兵以歸，自散關以南，城鎮悉棄之，皆為蜀人所有。
entries.en: On hearing that the emperor had entered Luoyang, he gathered the garrisons of Sanquan, Xixian, Jinniu, and Sanglin and withdrew. From Sanguan Pass southward he abandoned every town and fort, and all fell to Shu.
entries.literal: When he heard that the emperor had entered Luoyang, he then gathered all the garrison troops of Sanquan, Xixian, Jinniu, and Sanglin and withdrew. From Sanguan Pass southward, every town and fort was abandoned and all fell into Shu hands.

entries.zh: 入朝，帝欲治罪，以其能自歸，乃赦之。）〉
entries.en: When he presented himself at court the emperor wished to punish him, but because he had come back of his own accord he was pardoned.)〉
entries.literal: When he came to court the emperor wished to punish him, but because he had returned of his own accord he was pardoned.)〉

entries.zh: 高祖即位之二年，授鳳州防禦使，加檢校司徒，會丁母憂，起復，授內客省使、右監門衛大將軍。
entries.en: In the second year of Gaozu's reign he was made defense commissioner of Fengzhou and given the honorary title of minister of education. When his mother died he was recalled from mourning and appointed commissioner of the inner guests bureau and great general of the right gate guard.
entries.literal: In the second year after Gaozu's accession he was made defense commissioner of Feng prefecture and given the honorary title of Minister of Education. When he entered mourning for his mother he was recalled from mourning and appointed commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau and great general of the Right Gate Guard.

entries.zh: 六年，駕幸鄴都，轉宣徽北院使兼判三司，加檢校太保。
entries.en: In the sixth year, when the emperor visited Yedu, he was made commissioner of the northern bureau of the palace secretariat with concurrent charge of the three bureaus and given the honorary title of grand guardian.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, when the imperial carriage visited Yedu, he was transferred to commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat with concurrent charge of the Three Bureaus and given the honorary title of Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 七年，少帝嗣位，加右領軍衛上將軍，仍賜竭誠翊戴保節功臣。
entries.en: In the seventh year, when the young emperor succeeded, he was made general of the right army guard and granted the title of meritorious minister for devoted loyalty in supporting the throne and preserving integrity.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, when the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made general of the Right Army Guard and was also granted the title of meritorious minister of devoted loyalty in supporting the throne and preserving integrity.

entries.zh: 八年，出領鄭州，加檢校太傅。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was posted to govern Zhengzhou and given the honorary title of grand tutor.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he went out to govern Zheng prefecture and was given the honorary title of Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 開運二年，遷安州防禦使。
entries.en: In the second Kaiyun year he was transferred to defense commissioner of Anzhou.
entries.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun he was transferred to defense commissioner of An prefecture.

entries.zh: 未幾，上表稱疾，詔許就便，回至上蔡，終於郵舍，時三年四月也。
entries.en: Before long he memorialized that he was ill; the court allowed him to retire where he pleased. On his way back to Shangcai he died at a courier station in the fourth month of the third year.
entries.literal: Before long he memorialized claiming illness; an edict permitted him to retire as convenient. Returning to Shangcai, he died at a post station in the fourth month of the third year.

entries.zh: 房暠，京兆長安人也。
entries.en: Fang Gao was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
entries.literal: Fang Gao was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 少為唐宰臣崔魏公家臣，後因亂，客於蒲州。
entries.en: In youth he served as a household retainer of the Tang chief minister, the Duke of Wei surnamed Cui; later, amid the turmoil, he sojourned in Puzhou.
entries.literal: In youth he served as a household retainer of the Tang chief minister Duke of Wei surnamed Cui; later, amid the turmoil, he sojourned in Puzhou.

entries.zh: 天成中，唐末帝出鎮河中，暠於路左迎謁，求事軍門，末帝愛之，使治賓客。
entries.en: During Tiancheng, when the Last Emperor of Tang went out to govern Hezhong, Gao met him at the roadside and sought service at headquarters. The Last Emperor took a liking to him and put him in charge of guests.
entries.literal: During Tiancheng, when the Last Emperor of Tang went out to govern Hezhong, Gao met him at the roadside and sought service at headquarters. The Last Emperor took a liking to him and had him manage guests.

entries.zh: 及末帝登極，歷南北院宣徽使，尋與趙延壽同為樞密使。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor ascended the throne, Gao served successively as commissioner of the southern and northern palace secretariat bureaus, and soon shared the post of confidential commissioner with Zhao Yanshou.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor ascended the throne, Gao served successively as commissioner of the southern and northern bureaus of the Palace Secretariat, and soon shared the post of confidential commissioner with Zhao Yanshou.

entries.zh: 時薛文遇、劉延朗之徒居中用事，暠雖處密地，其聽用之言，十不得三四，但隨勢可否，不為事先。
entries.en: At that time Xue Wenyü, Liu Yanlang, and their like held sway at court. Though Gao sat in the innermost councils, only three or four of every ten words he spoke were heeded; he merely assented or demurred as the tide flowed, never taking the lead.
entries.literal: At that time Xue Wenyü, Liu Yanlang, and their like held sway at court. Though Gao sat in the innermost councils, only three or four of every ten words he spoke were heeded; he merely assented or demurred as the tide flowed, never taking the lead.

entries.zh: 每朝廷有大事，暠與端明學士等環坐會議，多於眾中俯首而睡，其避事也如此。
entries.en: Whenever the court faced a great matter, Gao would sit in conference with the academicians of the Hall of Bright Clarity and the like, and often slept with bowed head among the assembly—such was his way of avoiding responsibility.
entries.literal: Whenever the court faced a great matter, Gao would sit in conference with the academicians of the Hall of Bright Clarity and the like, and often slept with bowed head among the assembly—such was his way of avoiding responsibility.

entries.zh: 高祖即位，以暠濡足閏朝，不專與奪，故特恩原之，命為左驍衛大將軍，留西京。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, since Gao had served under two dynasties and had not monopolized decisions on life and death, he was specially shown grace and pardoned, appointed grand general of the Left Valiant Guards, and kept at the western capital.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, since Gao had wet his feet in two courts and had not monopolized decisions on life and death, he was specially shown grace and pardoned, appointed grand general of the Left Valiant Guards, and kept at the western capital.

entries.zh: 開運元年春，卒於洛陽。
entries.en: In spring of the first year of Kaiyun he died at Luoyang.
entries.literal: In spring of the first year of Kaiyun he died at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 孟承誨，大名人也。
entries.en: Meng Chenghui was a native of Daming.
entries.literal: Meng Chenghui was a man of Daming.

entries.zh: 始為本府牙校，遇高祖臨其地，升為客將。
entries.en: At first he was a military adjutant of his prefecture; when Gaozu came to the region, he was promoted to guest officer.
entries.literal: At first he was a military adjutant of his prefecture; when Gaozu came to the region, he was promoted to guest officer.

entries.zh: 後奏為宗城令，秩滿，以百姓舉留，為常山槁城令，皆有善政。
entries.en: He was later recommended as magistrate of Zongcheng, and when his term ended the people petitioned to keep him; he was made magistrate of Gaocheng in Changshan, showing good governance in both posts.
entries.literal: He was later recommended as magistrate of Zongcheng, and when his term ended the people petitioned to keep him; he was made magistrate of Gaocheng in Changshan, showing good governance in both posts.

entries.zh: 高祖有天下，擢為閣門副使，累遷宣徽使，官至檢校司空、太府卿、右武衛大將軍。
entries.en: After Gaozu possessed the realm, Chenghui was promoted to deputy gate commissioner, rose through posts to palace secretariat commissioner, and reached the offices of honorary minister of works, grand minister of the court treasury, and grand general of the Right Martial Guards.
entries.literal: After Gaozu possessed the realm, Chenghui was promoted to deputy gate commissioner, rose through posts to palace secretariat commissioner, and reached the offices of honorary minister of works, grand minister of the court treasury, and grand general of the Right Martial Guards.

entries.zh: 及少帝嗣位，以植性纖巧，善於希旨，復與權臣宦官密相表裏，凡朝廷恩澤美使，必承誨為之，一歲之中，數四不已。
entries.en: When the young emperor succeeded, because of his subtle, crafty nature and skill at reading intentions, he again worked in secret concert with powerful officials and eunuchs; every grace mission or favor-bearing embassy from the court went through Chenghui, several times within a single year without cease.
entries.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, because of his subtle, crafty nature and skill at reading intentions, he again worked in secret concert with powerful officials and eunuchs; every grace mission or favor-bearing embassy from the court went through Chenghui, several times within a single year without cease.

entries.zh: 由是居第華敞，財帛累積。
entries.en: Hence his residence grew splendid and broad, and wealth piled up.
entries.literal: Hence his residence grew splendid and broad, and wealth piled up.

entries.zh: 及契丹入汴，張彥澤引兵逼宮城，少帝召承誨計之，承誨匿身不赴。
entries.en: When the Khitans entered Bian, Zhang Yanzhe led troops to press the palace walls. The young emperor summoned Chenghui to counsel him, but Chenghui hid himself and did not come.
entries.literal: When the Khitans entered Bian, Zhang Yanzhe led troops to press the palace walls. The Young Emperor summoned Chenghui to counsel him, but Chenghui hid himself and did not come.

entries.zh: 少帝既出宮，寓於開封府舍，具以承誨背恩之事告彥澤，令捕而殺之，其妻女並配部族。
entries.en: After the young emperor left the palace and lodged at the Kaifeng prefectural offices, he fully told Yanzhe of Chenghui's betrayal of favor and ordered him captured and killed; his wife and daughters were both assigned to tribal peoples.
entries.literal: After the Young Emperor left the palace and lodged at the Kaifeng prefectural offices, he fully told Yanzhe of Chenghui's betrayal of favor and ordered him captured and killed; his wife and daughters were both assigned to tribal peoples.

entries.zh: 漢高祖即位，詔贈太保。
entries.en: When Gaozu of Han took the throne, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: When Gaozu of Han took the throne, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 劉繼勛，衛州人也。
entries.en: Liu Jixun was a native of Weizhou.
entries.literal: Liu Jixun was a man of Weizhou.

entries.zh: 唐天成中，高祖鎮鄴都，繼勛時為客將，高祖愛其端謹，籍其名於帳下，從歷數鎮。
entries.en: During Tang's Tiancheng era, when Gaozu governed Yedu, Jixun served as a guest officer. Gaozu admired his steady, careful manner, kept him on his staff register, and took him through several provincial postings.
entries.literal: During Tiancheng of Tang, when Gaozu governed Yedu, Jixun was then a guest officer. Gaozu loved his upright caution and registered his name in his staff, following him through several postings.

entries.zh: 及即位，擢為閣門使，出為淄州刺史，遷澶州防禦使，俄改鄭州，自宣徽北院使拜華州刺史。
entries.en: After Gaozu took the throne, Jixun was made gate commissioner, then prefect of Zi, defense commissioner of Chan, and soon of Zheng; from commissioner of the northern palace secretariat bureau he was appointed prefect of Hua.
entries.literal: When he took the throne Jixun was promoted to gate commissioner, sent out as prefect of Zi, transferred to defense commissioner of Chan, soon changed to Zheng, and from commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat was appointed prefect of Hua.

entries.zh: 歲餘，鎮同州。
entries.en: After a little more than a year he was posted to govern Tongzhou.
entries.literal: After more than a year he governed Tong prefecture.

entries.zh: 始少帝與契丹絕好，繼勛亦預其謀，及契丹主至闕，繼勛自鎮來朝，契丹責之。
entries.en: When the young emperor broke with the Khitans, Jixun had helped plan it. When the Khitan ruler reached the capital, Jixun came from his post to court, and the Khitans rebuked him.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the Young Emperor broke with the Khitans, Jixun also took part in the plot. When the Khitan ruler reached the capital, Jixun came from his post to court and the Khitans reproached him.

entries.zh: 時馮道在側，繼勛事急，指道曰：「少帝在鄴，道為首相，與景延廣謀議，遂致南北失歡。
entries.en: Feng Dao stood nearby. In his panic Jixun pointed at him and said, "When the young emperor was at Ye, Dao was chief minister and plotted with Jing Yanguang, which is what ruined relations between north and south.
entries.literal: Feng Dao was then at his side. Jixun, in his extremity, pointed at Dao and said: "When the Young Emperor was at Ye, Dao was chief minister and plotted with Jing Yanguang, thereby causing north and south to lose harmony.

entries.zh: 臣位至卑，未嘗措言，今請問道，道細知之。」
entries.en: My rank was too low for me to speak then. Question Dao—he knows every detail."
entries.literal: My post was utterly low and I never spoke a word. Now I ask that Dao be questioned—Dao knows the details."

entries.zh: 契丹主曰：「此老子不是好鬧人，無相牽引，皆爾輩為之。」
entries.en: The Khitan ruler said, "This old man is no troublemaker—do not implicate him. You people did it yourselves."
entries.literal: The Khitan ruler said: "This old fellow is not one to make trouble—do not drag him in. You lot did it all."

entries.zh: 繼勛不敢復對。
entries.en: Jixun did not dare answer further.
entries.literal: Jixun dared not reply again.

entries.zh: 繼勛時有疾，契丹主因令人候其疾狀，雲有風痹，契丹主曰：「北方地涼，居之此疾可愈。」
entries.en: Jixun was ill at the time, and the Khitan ruler sent someone to inquire; he was told Jixun had rheumatic paralysis. The Khitan ruler said, "The north is cool—live there and the illness will pass."
entries.literal: Jixun was then ill, and the Khitan ruler had someone inquire after his condition; it was reported that he had wind paralysis. The Khitan ruler said: "The northern lands are cool; living there this illness can be cured."

entries.zh: 乃命鎖繼勛。
entries.en: He then ordered Jixun shackled.
entries.literal: He then ordered Jixun put in chains.

entries.zh: 尋解之，以疾終於家。
entries.en: He was soon released and died of illness at home.
entries.literal: Soon he was released and died of illness at home.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：契丹主聞趙在禮死，乃釋繼勛，繼勛憂憤而卒。）〉
entries.en: (Comprehensive Mirror: When the Khitan ruler heard of Zhao Zaili's death, he released Jixun, who then died of grief and resentment.)〉
entries.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: When the Khitan ruler heard that Zhao Zaili had died, he then released Jixun; Jixun died of grief and anger.)〉

entries.zh: 漢高祖入汴，贈太尉。
entries.en: When Han Gaozu entered Bian, Jixun was posthumously made grand commandant.
entries.literal: When Han Gaozu entered Bian, he was posthumously made Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 鄭受益，
entries.en: Zheng Shouyi,
entries.literal: Zheng Shouyi,

entries.zh: 〈（《新唐書·宰相世系表》：字謙光。）〉
entries.en: (New Book of Tang, Tables of Chief Ministers' Lineages: styled Qianguang.)〉
entries.literal: (New Book of Tang, Tables of Chief Ministers' Lineages: style Qianguang.)〉

entries.zh: 唐宰相餘慶之曾孫也。
entries.en: He was a great-grandson of Yuqing, a Tang chief minister.
entries.literal: He was a great-grandson of Yuqing, chief minister of Tang.

entries.zh: 余慶生浣，浣生從讜，兩為太原節度使，再登相位。
entries.en: Yuqing's son was Huan; Huan's son was Congdan, who twice served as military governor of Taiyuan and twice rose to chief minister.
entries.literal: Yuqing begot Huan; Huan begot Congdan, who twice was military governor of Taiyuan and twice reached the chief ministership.

entries.zh: 從讜兄處誨，為汴州節度使。
entries.en: Congdan's elder brother Chuhui was military governor of Bianzhou.
entries.literal: Congdan's elder brother Chuhui was military governor of Bian prefecture.

entries.zh: 家襲清儉，深有士風，中朝禮法，以鄭氏為甲。
entries.en: The family was known for austerity and integrity and for true scholarly bearing; at court the Zheng were regarded as foremost in ritual propriety.
entries.literal: The family inherited purity and frugality and had a deep gentleman's air; in court ritual and law the Zheng clan ranked first.

entries.zh: 處誨生受益。
entries.en: Chuhui was Shouyi's father.
entries.literal: Chuhui begot Shouyi.

entries.zh: 受益亦以文學致身，累歷臺閣，自尚書郎遷右諫議大夫。
entries.en: Shouyi likewise rose through scholarship, served in a series of central offices, and was promoted from director in the masters of writing to right remonstrance adviser.
entries.literal: Shouyi also rose through literary learning, passing through the terrace offices in succession, and from director in the Masters of Writing was promoted to right remonstrance adviser.

entries.zh: 天福七年夏，以張彥澤數為不道，上章請行國典，旬日不報。
entries.en: In the summer of the seventh Tianfu year, citing Zhang Yanzhe's repeated outrages, he memorialized that the law be enforced against him; for ten days the court gave no answer.
entries.literal: In the summer of the seventh year of Tianfu, because Zhang Yanzhe had repeatedly acted against the Way, he memorialized asking that the national statutes be applied; for ten days there was no reply.

entries.zh: 又貢表切言，訐直無所忌，執政稍惡之。
entries.en: He submitted another memorial speaking bluntly and without fear, and the chief ministers grew to dislike him.
entries.literal: He again presented a memorial speaking bluntly, exposing wrongs without reserve, and those in power gradually came to dislike him.

entries.zh: 俄而以病請告，歸長安。
entries.en: Soon he asked leave for illness and returned to Chang'an.
entries.literal: Soon he asked leave on grounds of illness and returned to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 高祖晏駕，以不赴國哀停任，會赦，拜京兆少尹。
entries.en: When Gaozu died he was suspended for failing to attend the state mourning; after an amnesty he was appointed vice prefect of the capital district.
entries.literal: When Gaozu died he was suspended from office for not attending the national mourning; when an amnesty came he was appointed vice prefect of the capital district.

entries.zh: 宰相趙瑩出鎮鹹秦，以受益朝班舊僚，眷待甚至。
entries.en: When chief minister Zhao Ying was posted to Xian and Qin, he treated Shouyi, an old court colleague, with exceptional favor.
entries.literal: Chief minister Zhao Ying went out to govern Xian and Qin and, because Shouyi was an old colleague from court, treated him with exceptional favor.

entries.zh: 屬天下率借金谷，乃謂瑩曰：「京兆戶籍登耗，民力虛實，某備知之矣，品而定之，可使平允。」
entries.en: When the empire levied grain and cash loans, he told Ying, "I know the capital district's household registers, gains and losses, and the people's real capacity. Grade them properly and the levies can be made fair."
entries.literal: When the empire levied loans of grain and cash, he said to Ying: "The capital district's household registers, gains and losses, and the people's strength, empty or full—I know them all. Grade and fix them and fairness can be achieved."

entries.zh: 瑩信之，因使與王人同掌其事。
entries.en: Ying believed him and therefore had him manage the matter jointly with the imperial commissioner.
entries.literal: Ying trusted him and therefore had him jointly manage the matter with the king's commissioner.

entries.zh: 受益既經廢棄，薄於仕宦，遂阿法射利，冀為生生之資；
entries.en: Having already been cast aside, Shouyi cared little for office and bent the law for profit, hoping to secure a living;
entries.literal: Shouyi, having already been cast aside, was indifferent to office and therefore bent the law to seek profit, hoping for means of livelihood;

entries.zh: 又素恃門望，陵轢同幕，內奸外直，群情無相洽者。
entries.en: he also relied on his family's prestige, bullied colleagues on the staff, was treacherous within and upright in appearance, and won the goodwill of none around him.
entries.literal: he also by nature relied on his family's standing, bullied his colleagues on the staff, was inwardly treacherous and outwardly upright, and among the group none were on good terms with him.

entries.zh: 及贓汙事發，騰於眾口，瑩不得已，遂按之，其直百萬。
entries.en: When the bribery scandal broke and public outcry mounted, Ying had no choice but to investigate; the sum involved reached a million cash.
entries.literal: When the bribery affair broke out it spread on every tongue; Ying had no choice but to investigate, and the value reached a million.

entries.zh: 八年冬，賜死於家。
entries.en: In the winter of the eighth year he was ordered to take his own life at home.
entries.literal: In the winter of the eighth year he was granted death at home.

entries.zh: 受益數世公臺，一朝自棄，士君子皆惜之。
entries.en: For generations his family had held the highest offices, yet in a single stroke he ruined himself, and men of worth all lamented it.
entries.literal: Shouyi's family for generations had held the highest offices, yet in a single morning he threw himself away; gentlemen all regretted it.

entries.zh: 李郁，字文緯，唐之宗屬也。
entries.en: Li Yu, styled Wenwei, was a member of the Tang imperial clan.
entries.literal: Li Yu, style Wenwei, was a kinsman of Tang.

entries.zh: 少歷宗寺官，天成、長興中，累遷為宗正卿。
entries.en: In youth he served in the clan temple offices; during Tiancheng and Changxing he rose step by step to director of the imperial clan court.
entries.literal: In youth he passed through offices of the clan temple; during Tiancheng and Changxing he was promoted in succession to director of the Imperial Clan Court.

entries.zh: 性平允，所歷無愛憎毀譽。
entries.en: He was even-tempered and fair-minded; in every post he aroused neither special favor nor hostility, neither praise nor blame.
entries.literal: His nature was even and fair; in every post he drew neither favor nor hatred, neither praise nor blame.

entries.zh: 高祖登極，授光祿卿。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne he was appointed minister of imperial entertainments.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he was made Minister of Imperial Entertainments.

entries.zh: 一日晝寢，夢食巨棗，覺而有疾，謂其親友曰：「嘗聞『棗』字重『來』，呼魂之象也。
entries.en: One afternoon he napped and dreamed of eating huge jujubes. When he woke he fell ill and told his friends, "They say the character for 'jujube' contains the character for 'come'—a sign that one's soul is being summoned back.
entries.literal: One day he napped by day and dreamed of eating huge jujubes. On waking he fell ill and told his kin and friends: "I have heard that the character zao ('jujube') contains the character lai ('come')—a sign of calling back the soul.

entries.zh: 余神氣逼抑，將不免乎！」
entries.en: My spirit feels crushed—I shall not escape death!"
entries.literal: My vital spirit is pressed down—I shall not escape death!"

entries.zh: 天福五年夏卒。
entries.en: He died in the summer of the fifth Tianfu year.
entries.literal: He died in the summer of the fifth year of Tianfu.

entries.zh: 贈太子太保。
entries.en: He was posthumously made grand tutor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 馬重績，字洞微。
entries.en: Ma Zhongji, styled Dongwei.
entries.literal: Ma Zhongji, style Dongwei.

entries.zh: 少學數術，明太一、五紀、八象、三統大歷，居於太原。
entries.en: From youth he studied numerology and mastered the Great One, Five Registers, Eight Images, and Great Calendar of the Three Unifications; he lived at Taiyuan.
