entries.literal: In youth he studied numerology and was versed in the Great One, the Five Registers, the Eight Images, and the Great Calendar of the Three Unifications; he lived at Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 仕晉，拜太子右贊善大夫，遷司天監。
entries.en: Under Jin he was appointed right mentor of the heir apparent and then director of the astronomy bureau.
entries.literal: Serving Jin, he was made Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent and transferred to director of the Astronomy Bureau.

entries.zh: 天福三年，重績上言：「歷象，王者所以正一氣之元，宣萬邦之命，而古今所記，考審多差。
entries.en: In the third Tianfu year Zhongji memorialized, "Calendars and celestial observations are how kings set the origin of cosmic order and proclaim the mandate to all states, yet records ancient and modern, when examined closely, contain many errors.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianfu, Zhongji memorialized: "The calendar and celestial signs are what kings use to rectify the origin of the single qi and proclaim the mandate to the myriad states, yet what ancient and modern records preserve, on examination, contains many errors.

entries.zh: 《宣明》氣朔正而星度不驗，《崇元》五星得而歲差一日。
entries.en: The Xuanming calendar's qi phases and new moons are correct, but its star positions fail verification; the Chongyuan tracks the five planets correctly but the year is off by a day.
entries.literal: The Xuanming calendar's qi and new moons are correct but the star degrees do not check; the Chongyuan gets the five planets right but the year differs by a day.

entries.zh: 以《宣明》之氣朔，合《崇元》之五星，二歷相參，然後符合。
entries.en: Combine the Xuanming calendar's qi phases and new moons with the Chongyuan's planetary tables; only when the two calendars are cross-checked do they agree.
entries.literal: Take the qi and new moons of the Xuanming and combine them with the five planets of the Chongyuan; when the two calendars are cross-checked, then they accord.

entries.zh: 自前世諸歷，皆起天正十一月為歲首，用太古甲子為上元，積歲愈多，差闊愈甚。
entries.en: Earlier calendars all began the year in the eleventh month of the celestial standard and used the primordial jiazi cycle as the superior origin; the more years accumulated, the wider the error grew.
entries.literal: From former ages all calendars have taken the eleventh month of the celestial standard as year-start and used the primordial jiazi cycle as superior origin; the more years accumulate, the wider the discrepancy grows.

entries.zh: 臣輒合二歷，創為新法，以唐天寶十四載乙未為上元，雨水正月中氣為氣首。」
entries.en: I have combined the two calendars into a new method, taking the yiwei year (Tang Tianbao 14) as the superior origin and the mid-qi of the first month of Rain Water as the start of the qi cycle."
entries.literal: Your servant has combined the two calendars and created a new method, taking the yiwei year, the fourteenth year of Tang Tianbao, as superior origin and the mid-qi of the first month of Rain Water as the head of qi."

entries.zh: 詔下司天監趙仁琦、張文皓等考核得失，仁琦等言：「明年庚子正月朔，用重績歷考之，皆合無舛。」
entries.en: The court ordered Zhao Renqi, Zhang Wenhao, and others at the astronomy bureau to review it. They reported, "On the new year's day of the coming gengzi year, Zhongji's calendar matches observation in every respect."
entries.literal: An edict sent the matter to Zhao Renqi, Zhang Wenhao, and others of the Astronomy Bureau to examine gains and losses. Renqi and the rest said: "On the new moon of the first month of next year, the gengzi year, if examined by Zhongji's calendar, all will accord without error."

entries.zh: 乃下詔班行之，號《調元曆》。
entries.en: An edict was issued to promulgate it under the title Calendar for Adjusting the Origin.
entries.literal: An edict was then issued to promulgate it; it was titled the Calendar for Adjusting the Origin.

entries.zh: 行之數歲輒差，遂不用。
entries.en: After a few years in use it began to drift, and the court abandoned it.
entries.literal: After a few years in use it soon showed discrepancy and was then abandoned.

entries.zh: 重績又言：「漏刻之法，以中星考晝夜為一百刻，八刻六十分刻之二十為一時，時以四刻十分為正，此自古所用也。
entries.en: Zhongji also argued, "The clepsydra method divides day and night into one hundred marks by observing culmination stars; eight marks plus twenty sixtieths make one double-hour, with the fourth mark and ten parts as the standard—this is the ancient practice.
entries.literal: Zhongji also said: "The method of clepsydra graduations takes the culmination stars to divide day and night into one hundred ke; eight ke and twenty sixtieths of a ke make one double-hour, and the double-hour takes the fourth ke and ten parts as correct—this is what has been used since antiquity.

entries.zh: 今失其傳，以午正為時始，下侵未四刻十分而為午，由是晝夜昏曉，皆失其正，請依古改正。」
entries.en: That tradition is now lost: noon is taken as the start of the hour, pushing true noon down into the fourth mark and ten parts of the wei period, so day, night, dusk, and dawn are all wrong. I ask that the ancient method be restored."
entries.literal: Now the transmission is lost: they take noon as the start of the double-hour and push noon down into the fourth ke and ten parts of wei, so that day, night, dusk, and dawn all lose their correctness. I ask that it be corrected according to antiquity."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court agreed.
entries.literal: The request was granted.

entries.zh: 重績卒年六十四。
entries.en: Zhongji died at sixty-four.
entries.literal: Zhongji died at the age of sixty-four.

entries.zh: 陳元，京兆人也。
entries.en: Chen Yuan was a native of the capital district.
entries.literal: Chen Yuan was a man of Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 家世為醫，初事河中王重榮。
entries.en: His family had practiced medicine for generations; he first served Wang Chongrong of Hezhong.
entries.literal: His family for generations practiced medicine; at first he served Wang Chongrong of Hezhong.

entries.zh: 乾符中，後唐武皇自太原率師攻王行瑜，路出於蒲中，時元侍湯藥，武皇甚重之。
entries.en: During Qianfu, Later Tang's martial emperor marched from Taiyuan against Wang Xingyu and passed through Pu. Yuan attended him with medicines, and the martial emperor held him in high regard.
entries.literal: During Qianfu, Later Tang's Martial Emperor led troops from Taiyuan to attack Wang Xingyu, passing through Pu. Yuan then attended him with medicines and decoctions, and the Martial Emperor greatly valued him.

entries.zh: 及還太原，日侍左右。
entries.en: When the emperor returned to Taiyuan, Yuan attended him daily.
entries.literal: When he returned to Taiyuan he attended him daily at his side.

entries.zh: 武皇性剛暴，樂殺人，無敢言者。
entries.en: The martial emperor was fierce and violent by nature and delighted in killing; no one dared remonstrate with him.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor by nature was fierce and violent, delighted in killing, and none dared speak to him.

entries.zh: 元深測其情，每有暴怒，則從容啟諫，免禍者不一，以是晉人深德之，勛貴賂遺盈門。
entries.en: Yuan read his moods well; whenever rage seized him, Yuan would calmly remonstrate and save many from death. The people of Jin were deeply grateful, and gifts from nobles filled his gate.
entries.literal: Yuan deeply gauged his moods; whenever there was violent rage he would calmly remonstrate, and not a few were spared calamity. For this the people of Jin deeply thanked him, and meritorious nobles' gifts filled his gate.

entries.zh: 性好酒樂施，隨得而無私積。
entries.en: He loved wine and delighted in giving away whatever came to hand, keeping nothing for himself.
entries.literal: By nature he loved wine and delighted in giving; whatever he received he kept no private store.

entries.zh: 明宗朝，為太原少尹，入為太府卿。
entries.en: Under Mingzong he served as vice prefect of Taiyuan, then entered the capital as minister of the imperial storehouse.
entries.literal: In the reign of Mingzong he was vice prefect of Taiyuan and entered the capital as minister of the Imperial Storehouse.

entries.zh: 長興中，集平生所驗方七十五首，並修合藥法百件，號曰《要術》，刊石置於太原府衙門之左，以示於眾，病者賴焉。
entries.en: During Changxing he compiled seventy-five prescriptions he had tested in life and a hundred compounding methods under the title Essential Methods, had them carved on stone and set to the left of the Taiyuan government gate for all to see; the sick benefited from them.
entries.literal: During Changxing he collected seventy-five prescriptions he had verified in his lifetime, together with a hundred methods of compounding medicines, titled Essential Methods, carved them on stone and set them to the left of the Taiyuan prefectural yamen gate to show the public; the sick relied on them.

entries.zh: 天福中，以耄期上表求退，以光祿卿致仕，卒於晉陽，年八十餘。
entries.en: In his old age during Tianfu he memorialized to retire and left office as minister of imperial entertainments; he died at Jinyang in his eighties.
entries.literal: During Tianfu, in his great age, he memorialized asking to retire and left office as Minister of Imperial Entertainments; he died at Jinyang aged more than eighty.

entries.zh: 孔崇弼，初仕後唐，自吏部郎中授給事中，時族兄昭序繇給事中改左常侍，兄弟同居門下，時論榮之。
entries.en: Kong Chongbi began his career under Later Tang. Promoted from director in the Ministry of Personnel to supervising censor, he served at the same time as his older kinsman Zhaoxu, who had moved from supervising censor to left regular attendant. With both brothers holding posts in the Secretariat, contemporaries took it as a mark of family distinction.
entries.literal: Kong Chongbi at first served Later Tang; from Director in the Ministry of Personnel he was appointed Supervising Censor. At that time his clansman elder brother Zhaoxu moved from Supervising Censor to Left Regular Attendant. The brothers both dwelt together under the Gate of the Imperial Secretariat, and contemporaries regarded it as an honor.

entries.zh: 崇弼，天福中遷左散騎常侍。
entries.en: During the Tianfu era Chongbi was promoted to left regular attendant of the cavalry.
entries.literal: Chongbi, during Tianfu, was transferred to Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

entries.zh: 無他才，但能談笑，戲玩人物，揚眉抵掌，取悅於人。
entries.en: He possessed no other ability, yet he could banter and jest, mock people to their faces, arch his brows and clap his hands in amusement, and win others' favor.
entries.literal: He had no other talent but could jest and banter, play with people's characters, arch his brows and slap his palms together, and please others.

entries.zh: 五年，詔令泛海使於杭越。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the reign he was ordered by imperial edict to go by sea as envoy to Hang and Yue.
entries.literal: In the fifth year an edict ordered him as envoy by sea to Hang and Yue.

entries.zh: 先是，浙中贈賄，每歲恒及萬緡，時議者曰：「孔常侍命奇薄，何消盈數，有命即無財，有財即無命。」
entries.en: Before this, tribute gifts from Zhejiang routinely amounted to ten thousand strings of cash a year. People at court remarked, "Vice Censor Kong's fate is unusually meager—why should he need a fortune? Appointment and profit never come together for him: if he gets the post he will have no money, and if he has money he will not live to enjoy it."
entries.literal: Previously, gifts from Zhe reached ten thousand strings of cash every year. Commentators of the time said: "Vice Censor Kong's fate is strangely thin—why need such a full sum? When there is an appointment there is no wealth; when there is wealth there is no life."

entries.zh: 明年使還，果海中船壞，空手而歸。
entries.en: The following year, when the mission returned, the ships were indeed lost at sea, and he came home with nothing.
entries.literal: The next year when the envoy returned, indeed the ships were wrecked at sea, and he came back empty-handed.

entries.zh: 〈（案：以下殘闕。）〉
entries.en: (Editor's note: the passage below is missing.)
entries.literal: (Note: the text below is defective.)

entries.zh: 高祖睿文聖武昭肅孝皇帝，姓劉氏，諱暠，本名知遠，及即位改今諱。
entries.en: Gaozu, the Sagely, Cultured, Sacred, Martial, Illustrious, and Solemnly Filial Emperor, was of the Liu clan; his taboo name was Gao. He had been born Zhiyuan and took the present taboo name when he came to the throne.
entries.literal: Gaozu, the Sagely, Cultured, Sacred, Martial, Illustrious, and Solemnly Filial Emperor, bore the surname Liu; his taboo name was Gao; his original name was Zhiyuan, which upon his accession he changed to the present taboo name.

entries.zh: 其先本沙陀部人也。
entries.en: His forebears were originally of the Shatuo tribe.
entries.literal: His ancestors were originally people of the Shatuo tribe.

entries.zh: 四代祖諱湍，帝有天下，追尊為明元皇帝，廟號文祖，陵曰懿陵；
entries.en: His fourth-generation ancestor was named Tuan; once the emperor held the realm, Tuan was posthumously honored as Emperor Mingyuan, with the temple name Wenzu and the tomb Yiling;
entries.literal: His fourth-generation ancestor was named Tuan; after the Emperor possessed All Under Heaven, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Mingyuan, with temple name Wenzu and tomb called Yiling;

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：湍為東漢顯宗第八子淮陽王丙之後。）〉
entries.en: (Five Dynasties Essentials records that Tuan was descended from Bing, Prince of Huaiyang, the eighth son of Emperor Xianzong of Eastern Han.))〉
entries.literal: (Five Dynasties Essentials: Tuan was a descendant of Bing, Prince of Huaiyang, the eighth son of Emperor Xianzong of Eastern Han.))〉

entries.zh: 高祖母隴西李氏，追謚明貞皇后。
entries.en: His great-great-grandmother, Lady Li of Longxi, was posthumously titled Empress Mingzhen.
entries.literal: His great-great-grandmother was Lady Li of Longxi, posthumously honored as Empress Mingzhen.

entries.zh: 曾祖諱昂，晉贈太保，追尊為恭僖皇帝，朝號德祖，陵曰沛陵；
entries.en: His great-grandfather Ang was posthumously made Grand Guardian by Jin and honored as Emperor Gongxi, with the temple name Dezu and the tomb Peiling;
entries.literal: His great-grandfather was named Ang; Jin posthumously granted him Grand Guardian; he was honored as Emperor Gongxi, with temple name Dezu and tomb called Peiling;

entries.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：懿陵、沛陵皆無陵所，遙申朝拜。）〉
entries.en: (Five Dynasties Essentials notes that Yiling and Peiling had no known burial sites and were worshipped only from a distance.))〉
entries.literal: (Five Dynasties Essentials: Yiling and Peiling both had no actual tomb sites; worship was offered to them from afar.))〉

entries.zh: 曾祖母虢國太夫人楊氏，追謚恭惠皇后。
entries.en: His great-grandmother, Lady Yang of Guo, was posthumously titled Empress Gonghui.
entries.literal: His great-grandmother was Lady Yang, Lady of Guo, posthumously honored as Empress Gonghui.

entries.zh: 祖諱僎，晉贈太傅，追尊為昭獻皇帝，廟號翼祖，陵曰威陵；
entries.en: His grandfather Zhuan was posthumously made Grand Tutor by Jin and honored as Emperor Zhaoxian, with the temple name Yizu and the tomb Weiling;
entries.literal: His grandfather was named Zhuan; Jin posthumously granted him Grand Tutor; he was honored as Emperor Zhaoxian, with temple name Yizu and tomb called Weiling;

entries.zh: 祖母魯國太夫人李氏，追謚為昭穆皇后。
entries.en: His grandmother, Lady Li of Lu, was posthumously titled Empress Zhaomu.
entries.literal: His grandmother was Lady Li, Lady of Lu, posthumously honored as Empress Zhaomu.

entries.zh: 皇考諱琠，事後唐武皇帝為列校，晉贈太師，追尊為章聖皇帝，廟號顯祖，陵曰肅陵；
entries.en: His father Juan had served Later Tang's Emperor Wu as a field officer; Jin posthumously made him Grand Preceptor and honored him as Emperor Zhangsheng, with the temple name Xianzu and the tomb Suling;
entries.literal: His imperial father was named Juan; he served Emperor Wu of Later Tang as a commander in the ranks; Jin posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor; he was honored as Emperor Zhangsheng, with temple name Xianzu and tomb called Suling;

entries.zh: 皇妣吳國太夫人安氏，追謚章懿皇后。
entries.en: His mother, Lady An of Wu, was posthumously titled Empress Zhangyi.
entries.literal: His imperial mother was Lady An, Lady of Wu, posthumously honored as Empress Zhangyi.

entries.zh: 後以唐乾寧二年，歲在乙卯，二月四日生帝於太原。
entries.en: He was born at Taiyuan on the fourth day of the second month of 895, the second year of Tang Qianning.
entries.literal: Later, in the second year of Tang Qianning, the year yimao, on the fourth day of the second month, the Emperor was born at Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 帝弱不好弄，嚴重寡言，及長，面紫色，目睛多白。
entries.en: As a boy he was delicate and uninterested in games, solemn and taciturn; in adulthood his complexion was purplish and his eyes showed much white.
entries.literal: As a child the Emperor was frail and did not care for play; he was grave and sparing of speech; when grown, his face was purplish and the whites of his eyes showed much.

entries.zh: 初事唐明宗，列於麾下。
entries.en: He first entered the service of Tang Mingzong and served in his entourage.
entries.literal: He first served Tang Mingzong and was enrolled under his command.

entries.zh: 明宗與梁人對柵於德勝，時晉高祖為梁人所襲，馬甲連革斷，帝輟騎以授之，取斷革者自跨之，徐殿其後，晉高祖感而壯之。
entries.en: When Mingzong faced the Liang behind palisades at Desheng, Jin Gaozu was ambushed by Liang troops and the leather straps of his horse armor snapped in succession. The future emperor gave up his own horse for Gaozu, mounted another whose straps had already broken, and fell in slowly at the rear. Gaozu was deeply moved and impressed by his valor.
entries.literal: Mingzong faced the Liang with palisades at Desheng; at that time Jin Gaozu was attacked by Liang forces and his horse's armor straps broke one after another; the Emperor gave up his mount and handed it to him, himself mounting one whose straps had broken, and slowly brought up the rear; Jin Gaozu was moved and admired his courage.

entries.zh: 明宗踐阼，晉高祖為北京留守，以帝前有護援之力，奏移麾下，署為牙門都校。
entries.en: After Mingzong acceded, Jin Gaozu was stay-behind governor of the Northern Capital; remembering the emperor's earlier rescue, he had him transferred to his own command and appointed him commander of the gate guards.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Jin Gaozu was military governor of the Northern Capital; because the Emperor had earlier rendered protective aid, he memorialized to have him transferred under his command and appointed him commander of the gate guards.

entries.zh: 應順初，晉高祖鎮常山，唐明宗召赴闕，會閔帝出奔，與晉高祖相遇於途，遂俱入衛州，泊於郵舍。
entries.en: Early in the Yingshun era, while Jin Gaozu held Changshan, Tang Mingzong summoned him to court. Emperor Min was then fleeing, and the two met on the road; they entered Weizhou together and stayed at a relay inn.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yingshun, Jin Gaozu was stationed at Changshan; Tang Mingzong summoned him to court; it happened that Emperor Min fled, and he met Jin Gaozu on the road; they then both entered Weizhou and lodged at a post station.

entries.zh: 閔帝左右謀害晉高祖，帝密遣禦士石敢袖鎚立於晉高祖後，及有變，敢擁晉高祖入一室，以巨木塞門，敢尋死焉。
entries.en: Min's courtiers plotted to kill Jin Gaozu. The future emperor secretly posted the guard Shi Gan behind him with a hammer hidden in his sleeve. When the attack came, Gan hustled Gaozu into a room, barred the door with a heavy beam, and was killed in the fight.
entries.literal: Emperor Min's attendants plotted to harm Jin Gaozu; the Emperor secretly sent the guard Shi Gan, hammer concealed in his sleeve, to stand behind Jin Gaozu; when trouble arose, Gan shielded Jin Gaozu into a room, blocked the door with a great beam, and soon died.

entries.zh: 帝率眾盡殺閔帝左右，遂免晉高祖於難。
entries.en: He then led his men in slaughtering Min's entire retinue and so saved Jin Gaozu from the plot.
entries.literal: The Emperor led his men and killed all of Emperor Min's attendants, thus delivering Jin Gaozu from peril.

entries.zh: 〈（《通鑒考異》引《漢高祖實錄》云：是夜，偵知少帝伏甲，欲與從臣謀害晉高祖，詐屏人對語，方坐庭廡。
entries.en: (Zizhi Tongjian Collation, citing the Veritable Record of Han Gaozu, says that night he learned the young emperor had hidden troops and meant with his followers to kill Jin Gaozu; he pretended to dismiss everyone for a private talk and was sitting in the corridor.
entries.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian Collation cites the Veritable Record of Han Gaozu as saying: That night, having learned that the Young Emperor had hidden armed men and intended with his followers to plot against Jin Gaozu, he feigned a private conversation and was just then seated in the portico.

entries.zh: 帝密遣禦士石敢袖鎚立於後，俄頃伏甲者起，敢有勇力，擁晉高祖入一室，以巨木塞門，敢力當其鋒，死之。
entries.en: He secretly posted Shi Gan behind Gaozu with a hammer in his sleeve. Moments later the ambush sprang; Gan, a man of great strength, dragged Gaozu into a room, wedged the door with a beam, held the attackers at bay, and was killed.
entries.literal: The Emperor secretly sent the guard Shi Gan, hammer in sleeve, to stand behind; presently the hidden armed men rose; Gan was strong and brave, shielded Jin Gaozu into a room, blocked the door with a great beam, met their charge with force, and died.

entries.zh: 帝解佩刀，遇夜晦，以在地葦炬未然者奮擊之，眾謂短兵也，遂散走。
entries.en: He drew his sword; in the darkness he snatched up an unlit reed torch from the ground and struck wildly. The assailants took it for a close weapon and fled.
entries.literal: The Emperor drew his belt sword; the night was dark; he seized an unlit reed torch on the ground and struck fiercely; the crowd thought it was a short weapon and scattered in flight.

entries.zh: 帝乃匿身長垣下，聞帝親將李洪信謂人曰：「石太尉死矣。」
entries.en: He hid along a long wall and heard the imperial general Li Hongxin tell someone, "Grand Marshal Shi is dead."
entries.literal: The Emperor then hid beneath a long wall and heard the imperial general Li Hongxin say to someone: "Grand Marshal Shi is dead."

entries.zh: 帝隔垣呼洪信曰：「太尉無恙。」
entries.en: He called over the wall to Hongxin, "The Grand Marshal is safe."
entries.literal: The Emperor called across the wall to Hongxin: "The Grand Marshal is unharmed."

entries.zh: 乃逾垣出就洪信兵，共護晉高祖，殺建謀者，以少主授王宏贄。）〉
entries.en: He climbed the wall, joined Hongxin's force, protected Jin Gaozu together with them, killed the conspirators, and delivered the young emperor to Wang Hongzan.))〉
entries.literal: He then climbed over the wall, joined Hongxin's troops, together protected Jin Gaozu, killed the plotters, and handed the young ruler over to Wang Hongzan.))〉

entries.zh: 清泰元年，晉高祖復鎮河東。
entries.en: In the first year of Qingtai (934), Jin Gaozu was restored as military governor of Hedong.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qingtai, Jin Gaozu again took command at Hedong.

entries.zh: 三年夏，移鎮汶陽。
entries.en: In the summer of the third year he was reassigned to Wenyang.
entries.literal: In summer of the third year he transferred his command to Wenyang.

entries.zh: 帝勸晉高祖舉義，贊成密計，經綸之始，中外賴之。
entries.en: He urged Jin Gaozu to rebel, helped plan the coup in secret, and from the outset of the enterprise both the court and the realm relied on him.
entries.literal: The Emperor urged Jin Gaozu to raise righteous arms, approved secret plans, and at the start of grand strategy both court and country relied on him.

entries.zh: 晉高祖以帝為北京馬步軍都指揮使。
entries.en: Jin Gaozu appointed him commander of the Northern Capital horse-and-foot forces.
entries.literal: Jin Gaozu made the Emperor commander of the Northern Capital horse-and-foot army.

entries.zh: 及契丹以全軍赴難，大破張敬達之眾於晉陽城下，有降軍千餘人，晉高祖將置之於親衛，帝盡殺之。
entries.en: When the Khitan marched in full force to relieve the siege, they routed Zhang Jingda's army below Jinyang. More than a thousand surrendered troops were to be enrolled in Gaozu's personal guard, but the future emperor had them all slaughtered.
entries.literal: When the Khitan came with their full army to aid him, they greatly defeated Zhang Jingda's forces below Jinyang; there were more than a thousand surrendered troops; Jin Gaozu intended to place them in his personal guard; the Emperor killed them all.

entries.zh: 晉國初建，加檢校司空，充侍衛馬步都指揮使，權點檢隨駕六軍諸衛事，尋改陜州節度使，充侍衛親軍馬步都虞候。
entries.en: When Jin was first founded he was made Acting Minister of Works and commander of the palace horse-and-foot guard, with acting oversight of the six armies and palace guards on campaign; soon afterward he was transferred to military governor of Shaanzhou and made chief aide of the palace guard.
entries.literal: When the Jin state was first established, he was promoted to Acting Minister of Works, made commander of the palace horse-and-foot guard with acting inspection of the six armies and guards attending the emperor, and soon made military governor of Shaanzhou and chief registrar of the palace guard horse-and-foot forces.

entries.zh: 契丹主送晉高祖至上黨，指帝謂高祖曰：「此都軍甚操剌，無大故不可棄之。」
entries.en: The Khitan ruler escorted Jin Gaozu to Shangdang. Pointing at the future emperor, he told Gaozu, "This commander is very fierce and capable—without grave cause do not cast him aside."
entries.literal: The Khitan ruler escorted Jin Gaozu to Shangdang, pointed at the Emperor and said to Gaozu: "This commander is very caola; without a major cause do not abandon him."

entries.zh: 晉高祖入洛，委帝巡警，都邑肅然，無敢犯令。
entries.en: When Jin Gaozu entered Luoyang he entrusted him with patrol duties, and the capital grew so orderly that none dared break the law.
entries.literal: Jin Gaozu entered Luoyang, entrusted the Emperor with patrol duties, and the capital grew orderly; none dared violate the law.

entries.zh: 天福十二年春正月丁亥朔，契丹主入東京。
entries.en: On New Year's Day of the twelfth year of Tianfu the Khitan ruler entered the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: On the first day dinghai of the first month of spring in the twelfth year of Tianfu, the Khitan ruler entered the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 癸巳，晉少帝蒙塵於封禪寺。
entries.en: On guisi the young emperor of Jin was held captive at Fengchan Temple.
entries.literal: On the day guisi the Young Emperor of Jin suffered disgrace at Fengchan Temple.

entries.zh: 癸卯，少帝北遷。
entries.en: On guimao the young emperor was sent north.
entries.literal: On the day guimao the Young Emperor was moved north.

entries.zh: 二月丁巳朔，契丹主具漢法服，禦崇元殿受朝，制改晉國為大遼國，大赦天下，號會同十年。
entries.en: On New Year's Day of the second month the Khitan ruler put on Chinese court robes, held audience in Chongyuan Hall, renamed Jin as Great Liao, declared a general amnesty, and proclaimed the tenth year of Huitong.
entries.literal: On the first day dingsi of the second month the Khitan ruler donned Han court dress, ascended Chongyuan Hall to receive court, and by edict changed the state of Jin to Great Liao, proclaimed a general amnesty, and styled the era the tenth year of Huitong.

entries.zh: 是月，帝遣牙將王峻奉表於契丹，契丹主賜詔褒美，呼帝為兒，又賜木拐一。
entries.en: That month he sent Wang Jun with a memorial to the Khitan court; the Khitan ruler replied with praise, called him "son," and gave him a wooden staff.
entries.literal: That month the Emperor sent his guard officer Wang Jun to present a memorial to the Khitan; the Khitan ruler issued an edict praising him, called the Emperor "son," and also bestowed one wooden staff.

entries.zh: 蕃法，貴重大臣方得此賜，亦猶漢儀賜几杖之比也。
entries.en: By Khitan custom only the most honored ministers received such a gift, the equivalent in Han ritual of granting a seat and staff.
entries.literal: By tribal law only honored great ministers received this gift, comparable in Han ritual to the bestowal of an armrest and staff.

entries.zh: 王峻持持而歸，契丹望之皆避路。
entries.en: Wang Jun carried it home, and Khitan onlookers cleared the road at the sight of it.
entries.literal: Wang Jun carried it back; when the Khitan saw it they all gave way on the road.

entries.zh: 及峻至太原，帝知契丹政亂，乃議建號焉。
entries.en: When Jun reached Taiyuan and reported that Khitan rule was falling apart, the emperor began to consider proclaiming a new dynasty.
entries.literal: When Jun reached Taiyuan, the Emperor knew the Khitan government was in disorder and then deliberated on establishing a dynastic title.

entries.zh: 是月，秦州節度使何建以其地入於蜀。
entries.en: That month He Jian of Qinzhou surrendered his territory to Shu.
entries.literal: That month He Jian, military governor of Qinzhou, surrendered his territory to Shu.

entries.zh: 戊辰，河東行軍司馬張彥威與文武將吏等，以中原無主，帝威望日隆，群情所屬，上箋勸進，帝謙讓不允。
entries.en: On wuchen Zhang Yanwei of Hedong and the civil and military officers, seeing the Central Plains without a ruler and the emperor's prestige growing daily, submitted a memorial urging him to take the throne; he modestly refused.
entries.literal: On the day wuchen Zhang Yanwei, campaigning marshal of Hedong, together with civil and military officers, because the Central Plains had no ruler and the Emperor's prestige daily rose and all hearts turned to him, submitted a memorial urging accession; the Emperor modestly declined and would not agree.

entries.zh: 自是群官三上箋，諸軍將吏、緇黃耆耋，相次迫請，教答允之。
entries.en: Thereafter officials memorialized three times, and officers, clergy, and elders pressed him in turn until an edict in reply accepted.
entries.literal: From then on the officials submitted memorials three times; military officers, monks and priests, and elders in succession pressed the request, and an edict in reply agreed.

entries.zh: 庚午，陜府屯駐奉國指揮使趙暉、侯章、都頭王晏殺契丹監軍及副使劉願，暉自稱留後。
entries.en: On gengwu Zhao Hui of the Fengguo command at Shaan, Hou Zhang, and Wang Yan killed the Khitan supervisor and vice commissioner Liu Yuan; Hui declared himself acting military governor.
entries.literal: On the day gengwu Zhao Hui, commander of the Fengguo army stationed at Shaan prefecture, Hou Zhang, and company head Wang Yan killed the Khitan military supervisor and vice commissioner Liu Yuan; Hui styled himself acting military governor.

entries.zh: 契丹因授暉陜州兵馬留後，侯章為本州馬步軍都指揮使，王晏為副都指揮使，暉等不受命。
entries.en: The Khitan then appointed Hui acting military governor of Shaanzhou's forces, Hou Zhang commander of the prefecture's cavalry and infantry, and Wang Yan vice commander, but they refused the orders.
entries.literal: The Khitan thereupon appointed Hui acting military governor of Shaanzhou's forces, Hou Zhang commander of the prefecture's cavalry and infantry, and Wang Yan vice commander; Hui and the others did not accept the appointments.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·王晏傳》：開運末，與本軍都校趙暉、忠衛都校侯章等戍陜州。
entries.en: (Song History, Biography of Wang Yan: At the end of Kaiyun he was posted to Shaanzhou with Zhao Hui, commander of the main force, Hou Zhang of the Zhongwei guard, and others.
entries.literal: (Song History, Biography of Wang Yan: At the end of Kaiyun he garrisoned Shaanzhou with the army commander Zhao Hui, the Zhongwei commander Hou Zhang, and others.

entries.zh: 會契丹至汴，遣其將劉願據陜，恣行暴虐。
entries.en: When the Khitan reached Bian they sent Liu Yuan to hold Shaan, and he ravaged the people.
entries.literal: It happened that the Khitan reached Bian and sent their general Liu Yuan to hold Shaan, who indulged in violence and cruelty.

entries.zh: 晏與暉等謀曰：「今契丹南侵，天下洶洶，英雄豪傑固當乘時自奮。
entries.en: Yan said to Hui and the others, "The Khitan are invading the south and the realm is in uproar; men of spirit ought to seize the moment.
entries.literal: Yan plotted with Hui and the others, saying: "Now the Khitan invade the south and the realm is in turmoil; heroes and great men ought surely to seize the moment and rouse themselves.

entries.zh: 且聞太原劉公，威德遠被，人心歸服，若殺願送款河東，為天下倡首，則取富貴如反掌耳！」
entries.en: We hear that Lord Liu of Taiyuan's fame reaches far and the people look to him. If we kill Yuan and submit to Hedong, leading the realm, wealth and rank will come as easily as turning one's hand!"
entries.literal: Moreover we hear that Lord Liu of Taiyuan's prestige and virtue extend far and men's hearts submit to him; if we kill Yuan and send allegiance to Hedong, taking the lead for the realm, then winning wealth and rank will be like turning the hand!"

entries.zh: 暉等然之。
entries.en: Hui and the others agreed.
entries.literal: Hui and the others agreed.

entries.zh: 晏乃率敢死士數人，夜逾城入府署，劫庫兵給其徒。
entries.en: Yan led a few daredevils over the wall by night into the government compound, seized weapons from the arsenal, and armed his men.
entries.literal: Yan then led several dare-to-die men, by night scaled the wall and entered the government compound, seized arms from the arsenal and supplied his followers.

entries.zh: 遲明，斬願首懸府門外。
entries.en: At dawn they beheaded Yuan and hung his head outside the gate.
entries.literal: At dawn he beheaded Yuan and hung the head outside the government gate.

entries.zh: 眾請暉為帥，章為本城副指揮使、內外巡檢使兼都虞候，乃遣其子漢倫奉表晉陽。）〉
entries.en: The troops made Hui commander, Zhang vice commander of the prefecture, inner and outer patrol commissioner and chief disciplinary officer, and sent his son Hanlun to Jinyang with a memorial of submission.))〉
entries.literal: The crowd asked Hui to be commander, Zhang to be vice commander of the prefecture, inner and outer patrol commissioner and chief disciplinary officer, and then sent his son Hanlun to present a memorial at Jinyang.))〉

entries.zh: 辛未，帝於太原宮受冊，即皇帝位，制改晉開運四年為天福十二年。
entries.en: On xinwei he received the seal at the Taiyuan palace and took the throne, renaming Jin's fourth year of Kaiyun as the twelfth year of Tianfu.
entries.literal: On the day xinwei the Emperor received the seal at the Taiyuan palace, ascended the imperial throne, and by edict changed Jin's fourth year of Kaiyun to the twelfth year of Tianfu.

entries.zh: 〈（《契丹國志》云：漢祖仍稱天福年號，曰：「予未忍忘晉也。」）〉
entries.en: (Khitan State Chronicle says the Han founder kept the Tianfu reign title, saying, "I cannot yet forget Jin."))〉
entries.literal: (Khitan State Chronicle says: Han's founder still used the Tianfu reign title, saying: "I cannot bear to forget Jin."))〉

entries.zh: 甲戌，帝以晉帝舉族北遷，憤惋久之。
entries.en: On jiaxu, learning that the Jin emperor and his entire clan had been sent north, he brooded in anger and grief for a long while.
entries.literal: On the day jiaxu, because the Jin emperor and his whole clan were moved north, the Emperor was angry and grieved for a long time.

entries.zh: 是日，率親兵趨土門路，邀迎晉帝至壽陽，聞其已過，乃還。
entries.en: That same day he led his personal guard toward Tumen to intercept the Jin emperor, reaching Shouyang, but hearing the party had already passed, he turned back.
entries.literal: That day he led his personal troops toward the Tumen road to intercept and welcome the Jin emperor as far as Shouyang; hearing that he had already passed, he then returned.

entries.zh: 契丹聞帝建號，偽制削奪帝官爵。
entries.en: When the Khitan learned he had proclaimed a dynasty, they issued a counterfeit edict stripping him of rank and office.
entries.literal: When the Khitan heard that the Emperor had established a dynastic title, by a spurious edict they stripped him of his offices and ranks.

entries.zh: 以通事耿崇美為潞州節度使，高唐英為相州節度使，崔廷勛為河陽節度使，以扼要害之地。
entries.en: They appointed Geng Chongmei to Luzhou, Gao Tangying to Xiangzhou, and Cui Tingxun to Heyang to hold the strategic passes.
entries.literal: They appointed the interpreter Geng Chongmei military governor of Luzhou, Gao Tangying of Xiangzhou, and Cui Tingxun of Heyang, to choke the strategic places.

entries.zh: 丁丑，磁州賊帥梁暉據相州。
entries.en: On dingchou the bandit leader Liang Hui of Cizhou seized Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: On the day dingchou the bandit chief Liang Hui of Cizhou seized Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 己卯，帝遣都將史宏肇率兵討代州，平之。
entries.en: On jimao he sent Shi Hongzhao against Daizhou and pacified it.
entries.literal: On the day jimao the Emperor sent the commander Shi Hongzhao to lead troops against Daizhou and pacified it.

entries.zh: 初，代州刺史王暉叛歸契丹，宏肇一鼓而拔之，斬暉以徇。
entries.en: Wang Hui of Daizhou had earlier defected to the Khitan; Hongzhao took the city at the first assault and executed Wang Hui as an example.
entries.literal: Earlier Wang Hui, prefect of Daizhou, had rebelled and submitted to the Khitan; Hongzhao took the city at the first assault and beheaded Hui as a warning.

entries.zh: 庚辰，權晉州兵馬留後張晏洪奏，軍亂，殺知州副使駱從朗及括錢使、諫議大夫趙熙，以城歸順。
entries.en: On gengchen Zhang Yanhong, acting military governor of Jinzhou, reported that the garrison had mutinied, killed Vice Prefect Luo Conglang and Tax Commissioner Zhao Xi, and surrendered the city.
entries.literal: On the day gengchen Zhang Yanhong, acting military governor of Jinzhou's forces, memorialized that the army had mutinied, killed the vice prefect Luo Conglang and the tax-collecting commissioner, Remonstrance Grandee Zhao Xi, and surrendered the city in allegiance.

entries.zh: 時晉州留後劉在明赴東京，朝於契丹，從朗知軍州事，帝方遣使張晏洪、辛處明等告諭登極，從朗囚之本城。
entries.en: Liu Zaiming of Jinzhou had gone to the Eastern Capital to pay court to the Khitan, leaving Conglang in charge; when the emperor sent Zhang Yanhong and Xin Chuming to announce his accession, Conglang imprisoned them in the city.
entries.literal: At that time Liu Zaiming, acting military governor of Jinzhou, had gone to the Eastern Capital to attend court before the Khitan; Conglang was managing military and prefectural affairs; the Emperor had just sent envoys Zhang Yanhong, Xin Chuming, and others to announce his accession, and Conglang imprisoned them in the prefectural city.

entries.zh: 大將藥可儔殺從朗於理所，州民相率害趙熙，三軍請晏洪為留後，處明為都監。
entries.en: General Yao Keshou killed Conglang in the government hall; the townspeople killed Zhao Xi; the army then asked for Yanhong as acting governor and Chuming as chief supervisor.
entries.literal: The great general Yao Keshou killed Conglang at the government office; the prefectural people together killed Zhao Xi; the three armies asked Yanhong to be acting military governor and Chuming to be chief supervisor.

entries.zh: 辛巳，權陜州留後趙暉、權潞州留後王守恩，並上表歸順。
entries.en: On xinsi Zhao Hui of Shaan and Wang Shouen of Lu both submitted memorials of allegiance.
entries.literal: On the day xinsi Zhao Hui, acting military governor of Shaanzhou, and Wang Shouen, acting military governor of Luzhou, both submitted memorials of submission.

entries.zh: 癸未，澶州賊帥王瓊與其眾斷本州浮橋，瓊敗，死之。
entries.en: On guiwei the bandit Wang Qiong of Chanzhou cut the pontoon bridge with his followers; Qiong was defeated and killed.
entries.literal: On the day guiwei the bandit chief Wang Qiong of Chanzhou and his followers cut the prefecture's pontoon bridge; Qiong was defeated and died.

entries.zh: 時契丹以族人朗鄂為澶州節度使，朗鄂性貪虐，吏民苦之。
entries.en: The Khitan had appointed their kinsman Lang'e military governor of Chanzhou; greedy and brutal, he made life miserable for officials and commoners alike.
entries.literal: At that time the Khitan appointed their clansman Lang'e military governor of Chanzhou; Lang'e was greedy and cruel by nature, and officials and people suffered under him.

entries.zh: 瓊為水運什長，乃構夏津賊帥張乙，得千餘人，沿河而上，中夜竊發，自南城殺守將，絕浮航，入北城，朗悟據牙城以拒之。
entries.en: Qiong, a river-transport chief, allied with the bandit Zhang Yi of Xiajin and raised more than a thousand men. They moved upriver and struck at midnight, killing the southern garrison commander, severing the pontoon bridge, and entering the north city while Lang'e barricaded himself in the headquarters.
entries.literal: Qiong was a chief of ten in river transport; he then joined with the bandit chief Zhang Yi of Xiajin, mustering more than a thousand men; they went upriver, at midnight launched a surprise attack, from the south city killed the defending general, cut the pontoon crossing, entered the north city, and Lang'e held the headquarters compound to resist them.

entries.zh: 數日，會契丹救至，瓊敗死焉。
entries.en: Within days Khitan reinforcements arrived; Qiong was defeated and killed.
entries.literal: After several days Khitan relief arrived; Qiong was defeated and died.

entries.zh: 契丹主初聞其變也，懼甚，由是大河之南無久留之意，尋遣天雄軍節度使杜重威歸鎮。
entries.en: When the Khitan ruler first heard of the uprising he was deeply alarmed and lost any wish to stay south of the Yellow River; he soon sent Du Chongwei of Tianxiong back to his command.
entries.literal: When the Khitan ruler first heard of the revolt he was greatly afraid; from this he had no intention of remaining long south of the Great River, and soon sent Du Chongwei, military governor of the Tianxiong army, back to his post.

entries.zh: 夏四月己未，以北京馬軍都指揮使、集州刺史劉信為滑州節度使，充侍衛馬軍都指揮使、檢校太傅；
entries.en: In the fourth month, on jiwei, Liu Xin was made military governor of Huazhou and commander of the palace guard cavalry with the rank of Acting Grand Tutor;
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the day jiwei, Liu Xin, Commander of the Northern Capital's cavalry and Prefect of Jizhou, was made military governor of Huazhou, serving as Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard cavalry and Acting Grand Tutor;

entries.zh: 以北京隨使、右都押衙楊邠為權樞密使、檢校太保；
entries.en: Yang Bin was made acting Commissioner of Military Affairs and Acting Grand Guardian;
entries.literal: Yang Bin, attendant of the Northern Capital and right chief registrar, was made acting Commissioner of Military Affairs and Acting Grand Guardian;

entries.zh: 以北京武節都指揮使、雷州刺史宏肇為許州節度使，充待衛步軍都指揮使、檢校太傅；
entries.en: Shi Hongzhao was made military governor of Xu Prefecture and commander of the palace guard infantry with the rank of Acting Grand Tutor;
entries.literal: Hongzhao, commander of the Wujie army of the Northern Capital and Prefect of Leizhou, was made military governor of Xuzhou, serving as Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard infantry and Acting Grand Tutor;

entries.zh: 以北京牢城都指揮使、壁州刺史常思為鄧州節度使、檢校太傅兼權北京馬步軍都指揮使、三城巡檢使；
entries.en: Chang Si was made military governor of Dengzhou, Acting Grand Tutor, and acting commander of the Northern Capital forces and inspector of the three cities;
entries.literal: Chang Si, commander of the Laocheng army of the Northern Capital and Prefect of Bizhou, was made military governor of Dengzhou, Acting Grand Tutor, and additionally acting Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Capital's cavalry and infantry and inspector of the three cities;

entries.zh: 以河東行軍司馬張彥威為同州節度使、檢校太保；
entries.en: Zhang Yanwei was made military governor of Tongzhou and Acting Grand Guardian;
entries.literal: Zhang Yanwei, campaigning marshal of Hedong, was made military governor of Tongzhou and Acting Grand Guardian;

entries.zh: 以蕃漢兵馬都孔目官郭威為權樞密使、檢校司徒；
entries.en: Guo Wei was made acting Commissioner of Military Affairs and Acting Minister of Works;
entries.literal: Guo Wei, chief clerk of tribal and Han forces, was made acting Commissioner of Military Affairs and Acting Minister of Works;

entries.zh: 以河東左都押衙扈彥珂為宣徽南院使、檢校司徒；
entries.en: Hu Yanke was made commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and Acting Minister of Works;
entries.literal: Hu Yanke, left chief registrar of Hedong, was made commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and Acting Minister of Works;

entries.zh: 以右都押衙王浩為宣徽北院使、檢校司徒；
entries.en: Wang Hao was made commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and Acting Minister of Works;
entries.literal: Wang Hao, right chief registrar, was made commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and Acting Minister of Works;

entries.zh: 以兩使都孔目官王章為權三司使、檢校太保。
entries.en: Wang Zhang was made acting Commissioner of the Three Departments and Acting Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: Wang Zhang, chief clerk of the two bureaus, was made acting Commissioner of the Three Departments and Acting Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 是日，契丹主取相州，殺留後梁暉。
entries.en: That day the Khitan ruler took Xiangzhou and killed Liang Hui, the acting governor.
entries.literal: That day the Khitan ruler took Xiangzhou and killed the acting military governor Liang Hui.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·李穀傳》：潛遣河朔酋豪暉入據安陽，契丹主患之，即謀北旋，會有告契丹以城中虛弱者，契丹還攻安陽，陷其城。）〉
entries.en: (Song History, Biography of Li Gu: Li Gu secretly sent the Hebei leader Hui to hold Anyang. The Khitan ruler, alarmed, planned to withdraw north, but when someone reported the city was weakly defended, he turned back, took Anyang, and captured it.))〉
entries.literal: (Song History, Biography of Li Gu: He secretly sent the Hebei chieftain Hui to seize and hold Anyang; the Khitan ruler was troubled by this and at once planned to turn north; it happened that someone informed the Khitan that the city was weakly held, and the Khitan returned to attack Anyang and captured the city.))〉

entries.zh: 暉，磁州滏陽人，少為盜，會契丹入汴，暉收集徒黨，先入磁州，無所侵犯，遣使送款於帝。
entries.en: Hui was from Fuyang in Cizhou and had been a bandit in his youth. When the Khitan entered Bian he rallied his followers, took Cizhou without looting it, and sent envoys to submit to the emperor.
entries.literal: Hui was a man of Fuyang in Cizhou; in youth he was a bandit; when the Khitan entered Bian he gathered his followers, first entered Cizhou without harming anyone, and sent envoys to offer allegiance to the Emperor.

entries.zh: 暉偵知相州頗積兵仗，且無守備，遂以三月二十一日夜與其徒逾垣而入，殺契丹數十人，奪器甲數萬計，遂據其城。
entries.en: Learning that Xiangzhou held large stores of weapons but was poorly defended, he scaled the walls with his men on the night of the twenty-first of the third month, killed dozens of Khitan, seized tens of thousands of arms, and seized the city.
entries.literal: Hui learned by reconnaissance that Xiangzhou had stored considerable arms yet lacked defenses; on the night of the twenty-first day of the third month he and his followers scaled the wall and entered, killed several tens of Khitan, seized arms and armor numbering in the tens of thousands, and then held the city.

entries.zh: 契丹主先遣偽命相州節度使高唐英率兵討之。
entries.en: The Khitan ruler first sent the puppet governor Gao Tangying against him.
entries.literal: The Khitan ruler first sent Gao Tangying, spuriously appointed military governor of Xiangzhou, to lead troops against him.

entries.zh: 未幾，契丹主至城下，是月四日攻拔之，遂屠其城。
entries.en: Soon the Khitan ruler arrived, stormed the city on the fourth of the month, and put it to the sword.
entries.literal: Before long the Khitan ruler reached the foot of the city; on the fourth day of that month he stormed and took it, then massacred the city.

entries.zh: 翌日，契丹主北去，命高唐英鎮之，唐英閱城中遺民，得男女七百人而已。
entries.en: The next day the Khitan ruler marched north and left Gao Tangying in charge; a count of survivors found only seven hundred men and women.
entries.literal: The next day the Khitan ruler went north and ordered Gao Tangying to garrison it; Tangying reviewed the survivors in the city and found only seven hundred men and women.

entries.zh: 乾祐中，王繼宏鎮相州，奏於城中得髑髏十餘萬，殺人之數，從可知也。
entries.en: During Qianyou, when Wang Jihong governed Xiangzhou, he reported finding more than a hundred thousand skulls in the city — from which the scale of the slaughter may be guessed.
entries.literal: In the Qianyou era Wang Jihong was stationed at Xiangzhou and memorialized that more than a hundred thousand skulls were found in the city; the number of those killed can thus be inferred.

entries.zh: 庚申，以石州刺史易全章為洺州團練使，以前遼州刺史安真為宿州團練使，以嵐州刺史孟行超為潁州團練使，以汾州刺史武彥宏為曹州防禦使，以前憲州刺史慕容信為齊州防禦使，以遼州刺史薛瓊為亳州防禦使，以沁州刺史李漢韜為汝州防禦使。
entries.en: On gengshen the emperor appointed Yi Quanzhang regimental commissioner of Mingzhou, An Zhen of Suzhou, Meng Xingchao of Yingzhou, Wu Yanhong defender of Caozhou, Murong Xin defender of Qizhou, Xue Qiong defender of Bozhou, and Li Hantao defender of Ruzhou.
entries.literal: On the day gengshen Yi Quanzhang, Prefect of Shizhou, was made regimental commissioner of Mingzhou; An Zhen, former Prefect of Liaozhou, regimental commissioner of Suzhou; Meng Xingchao of Lanzhou, regimental commissioner of Yingzhou; Wu Yanhong of Fenzhou, Defender of Caozhou; Murong Xin, former Prefect of Xianzhou, Defender of Qizhou; Xue Qiong of Liaozhou, Defender of Bozhou; and Li Hantao of Qinzhou, Defender of Ruzhou.

entries.zh: 癸亥，冊魏國夫人李氏為皇后。
entries.en: On guihai Lady Li of Wei was enthroned as empress.
entries.literal: On the day guihai Lady Li, Lady of Wei, was invested as empress.

entries.zh: 甲子，以皇長子承訓為左衛上將軍，第二子承祐為左衛大將軍，第三子承勛為右衛大將軍，皇女彭城郡君宋氏封永寧公主，皇侄承赟為右衛上將軍。
entries.en: On jiazi the eldest son Chengxun was made general-in-chief of the Left Guard, the second son Chengyou great general of the Left Guard, and the third son Chengxun great general of the Right Guard; Lady Song of Pengcheng was created Princess Yongning, and the nephew Chengyun was made general-in-chief of the Right Guard.
entries.literal: On the day jiazi the eldest imperial son Chengxun was made General-in-Chief of the Left Guard; the second son Chengyou, Great General of the Left Guard; the third son Chengxun, Great General of the Right Guard; the imperial daughter, Lady Song of Pengcheng commandery, was enfeoffed as Princess Yongning; and the imperial nephew Chengyun was made General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.

entries.zh: 以河東節度判官蘇逢吉為中書侍郎、同平章事、集賢殿大學士，以河東觀察判官蘇禹珪為中書侍郎、同平章事。
entries.en: Su Fengji, aide to the Hedong military governor, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, Co-Manager of Affairs, and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy; Su Yugui, aide to the Hedong surveillance commissioner, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Manager of Affairs.
entries.literal: Su Fengji, aide of the Hedong military governor, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, Co-Manager of Affairs, and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy; Su Yugui, aide of the Hedong surveillance commissioner, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Manager of Affairs.

entries.zh: 升府州為節鎮，加永安軍額。
entries.en: Fuzhou was elevated to a full military commission under the title Yong'an army.
entries.literal: Fuzhou was raised to a military commission and given the designation Yong'an army.

entries.zh: 以振武節度使、府州團練使折從阮為永安軍節度使，行府州刺史、檢校太尉；
entries.en: Zhe Congruan was made military governor of Yong'an, acting prefect of Fuzhou, and Acting Grand Marshal;
entries.literal: Zhe Congruan, military governor of Zhenwu and regimental commissioner of Fuzhou, was made military governor of the Yong'an army, acting Prefect of Fuzhou and Acting Grand Marshal;

entries.zh: 以北京隨使、左都押衙劉銖為河陽節度使；
entries.en: Liu Zhu was made military governor of Heyang;
entries.literal: Liu Zhu, attendant of the Northern Capital and left chief registrar, was made military governor of Heyang;

entries.zh: 以河東支使韓祚為左諫議大夫，充樞密直學士。
entries.en: Han Zuo was made Left Remonstrance Grandee and academician directly attached to the Military Affairs Commission.
entries.literal: Han Zuo, branch commissioner of Hedong, was made Left Remonstrance Grandee and appointed Academician Directly Attached to the Military Affairs Commission.

entries.zh: 乙丑，遣史宏肇率兵一萬人趨潞州。
entries.en: On yichou Shi Hongzhao was dispatched with ten thousand men toward Luzhou.
entries.literal: On the day yichou Shi Hongzhao was sent to lead ten thousand troops toward Luzhou.

entries.zh: 丙寅，以權知潞州軍州事、左驍衛大將軍王守恩為潞州節度使、檢校太保；
entries.en: On bingyin Wang Shouen was made military governor of Luzhou and Acting Grand Guardian;
entries.literal: On the day bingyin Wang Shouen, acting administrator of Luzhou's military and prefectural affairs and Great General of the Left Xiaowei Guard, was made military governor of Luzhou and Acting Grand Guardian;

entries.zh: 以權點檢延州軍州事高允權為延州節度使、檢校太保；
entries.en: Gao Yunquan was made military governor of Yanzhou and Acting Grand Guardian;
entries.literal: Gao Yunquan, acting inspector of Yanzhou's military and prefectural affairs, was made military governor of Yanzhou and Acting Grand Guardian;

entries.zh: 以岢嵐軍使鄭謙為忻州刺史，遙領應州節度使，充忻、代二州義軍都部署。
entries.en: Zheng Qian was made prefect of Xinzhou, titular military governor of Yingzhou, and overall deployer of the volunteer forces of Xin and Dai.
entries.literal: Zheng Qian, commander of the Kelan army, was made Prefect of Xinzhou, held Yingzhou military governorship in absentia, and served as overall deployer of the volunteer armies of Xin and Dai.

entries.zh: 丁卯，以河東都巡館驛、沿河巡檢使閻萬進為嵐州刺史，領朔州節度使，充嵐、憲二州義軍都制置。
entries.en: On dingmao Yan Wanjin was made prefect of Lanzhou, titular military governor of Shuozhou, and overall commander of the volunteer forces of Lan and Xian.
entries.literal: On the day dingmao Yan Wanjin, Hedong inspector of relay stations and river patrols, was made Prefect of Lanzhou, held Shuozhou military governorship, and served as overall commander of the volunteer armies of Lan and Xian.

entries.zh: 戊辰，權河陽留後武行德以城來歸。
entries.en: On wuchen Wu Xingde of Heyang surrendered his city.
entries.literal: On the day wuchen Wu Xingde, acting military governor of Heyang, surrendered the city in allegiance.

entries.zh: 初，契丹主將發東京，船載武庫兵仗，自汴浮河，欲置之於北地，遣奉國都虞候武行德部送，與軍士千餘人並家屬俱行。
entries.en: When the Khitan ruler prepared to leave the Eastern Capital, he loaded captured arms onto boats from Bian to ship north and sent Wu Xingde of Fengguo to escort them with more than a thousand soldiers and their families.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the Khitan ruler was about to leave the Eastern Capital, he loaded the arsenal's arms on boats, floated them down from Bian on the river, intending to place them in the northern lands, and sent Wu Xingde of the Fengguo army as chief registrar to escort them, with more than a thousand soldiers and their families traveling together.

entries.zh: 至河陰，軍亂，奪兵仗，殺契丹監吏，眾推行德為帥，與河陰屯駐軍士合，乃自汜水抵河陽。
entries.en: At Heyin the troops mutinied, seized the weapons, killed the Khitan overseers, and made Xingde their leader; joining the Heyin garrison, they marched from Sishui to Heyang.
entries.literal: At Heyin the army mutinied, seized the arms, killed the Khitan supervising officials, and the crowd made Xingde commander; joining with the garrison at Heyin, they then went from Sishui to Heyang.

entries.zh: 河陽偽命節度使崔廷勛率兵拒之，兵敗，行德等追躡之，廷勛棄城而遁，行德因據其城。
entries.en: The puppet governor Cui Tingxun resisted and was defeated; Xingde pursued him, Tingxun fled, and Xingde took the city.
entries.literal: Cui Tingxun, spuriously appointed military governor of Heyang, led troops to resist; he was defeated; Xingde and the others pursued him; Tingxun abandoned the city and fled; Xingde then seized it.

entries.zh: 〈（《東都事略武行德傳》：行德陷於契丹，偽請自效，因遣送將校數十人護所取尚方鎧甲還北方。
entries.en: (Eastern Capital Outline, Biography of Wu Xingde: Captured by the Khitan, Xingde pretended to serve them and was sent north with several dozen officers to escort seized imperial armor.
entries.literal: (Eastern Capital Outline, Biography of Wu Xingde: Xingde had fallen into Khitan hands and falsely offered to serve them; he was therefore sent with several tens of officers to escort the imperial armor taken back to the north.

entries.zh: 至河陰，行德謂眾曰：「我與若等能為邊地鬼耶？」
entries.en: At Heyin he told the men, "Are we to become ghosts on the northern frontier?"
entries.literal: At Heyin Xingde said to the crowd: "Are you and I to become ghosts on the borderlands?"

entries.zh: 眾素伏其威名，皆曰：「惟命。」
entries.en: The men, who had long respected him, answered, "We follow your lead."
entries.literal: The crowd had long submitted to his martial renown and all said: "We obey your command."

entries.zh: 遂攻孟州，走其節度使崔廷勛，悉以府庫分諸校，而權領州事。
entries.en: They attacked Mengzhou, routed Cui Tingxun, divided the treasury among the officers, and Xingde took charge of the prefecture.
entries.literal: They then attacked Mengzhou, drove off its military governor Cui Tingxun, divided the treasury among the officers, and he acted as administrator of prefectural affairs.

entries.zh: 遣其弟行友詣太原勸進。）〉
entries.en: He sent his brother Xingyou to Jinyang to urge the emperor to take the throne.))〉
entries.literal: He sent his younger brother Xingyou to Jinyang to urge accession.))〉

entries.zh: 偽命西京留守劉晞棄洛城，南走許州，遂奔東京，洛京巡檢使方太自署知留守事。
entries.en: The puppet Western Capital regent Liu Xi abandoned Luoyang, fled south to Xuzhou, then to the Eastern Capital; Fang Tai, patrol commissioner of Luoyang, declared himself acting regent.
entries.literal: Liu Xi, spuriously appointed Western Capital regent, abandoned Luoyang, fled south to Xuzhou, then ran to the Eastern Capital; Fang Tai, patrol commissioner of the Luo capital, styled himself acting regent.

entries.zh: 未幾，太為武行德所害。
entries.en: Soon Fang Tai was killed by Wu Xingde.
entries.literal: Before long Tai was killed by Wu Xingde.

entries.zh: 是日，蕃將耿崇美屯澤州，史宏肇遣先鋒將馬誨率兵擊之，崇美退保懷州。
entries.en: That day the Khitan general Geng Chongmei held Zezhou; Shi Hongzhao sent Ma Hui against him, and Chongmei fell back to Huaizhou.
entries.literal: That day the tribal general Geng Chongmei was encamped at Zezhou; Shi Hongzhao sent the vanguard general Ma Hui to lead troops against him; Chongmei withdrew to defend Huaizhou.

entries.zh: 崔廷勛以契丹眾攻武行德於河陽，行德出戰，為廷勛所敗。
entries.en: Cui Tingxun attacked Wu Xingde at Heyang with Khitan troops and defeated him in battle.
entries.literal: Cui Tingxun with Khitan forces attacked Wu Xingde at Heyang; Xingde went out to battle and was defeated by Tingxun.

entries.zh: 汴州蕭翰遣蕃將高牟翰將兵援送劉晞復歸於洛。
entries.en: Xiao Han of Bian sent the tribal general Gao Mouhan to escort Liu Xi back to Luoyang.
entries.literal: Xiao Han of Bianzhou sent the tribal general Gao Mouhan to lead troops in support and escort Liu Xi back to Luo.

entries.zh: 牟翰至，殺前澶州節度使潘環於洛陽。
entries.en: When Mouhan arrived he killed the former Chanzhou governor Pan Huan in Luoyang.
entries.literal: When Mouhan arrived he killed Pan Huan, former military governor of Chanzhou, at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 辛未，以河陽都部署武行德為河陽節度使、檢校太尉，充一行馬步軍都部署。
entries.en: On xinwei Wu Xingde was made military governor of Heyang and Acting Grand Marshal and overall commander of the campaign horse and foot.
entries.literal: On the day xinwei Wu Xingde, overall deployer of Heyang, was made military governor of Heyang and Acting Grand Marshal, serving as overall deployer of the campaign's cavalry and infantry.

entries.zh: 甲戌，潞州節度使王守恩加檢校太尉，以前棣州刺史慕容彥超為澶州節度使、檢校太保。
entries.en: On jiaxu Wang Shouen was made Acting Grand Marshal and the former Dizhou prefect Murong Yanchao was made military governor of Chanzhou and Acting Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: On the day jiaxu Wang Shouen, military governor of Luzhou, was promoted to Acting Grand Marshal, and Murong Yanchao, former Prefect of Dizhou, was made military governor of Chanzhou and Acting Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 丙子，契丹主耶律德光卒於鎮之欒城。
entries.en: On bingzi the Khitan ruler Yelü Deguang died at Luancheng in Zhen prefecture.
entries.literal: On the day bingzi the Khitan ruler Yelü Deguang died at Luancheng in Zhen.

entries.zh: 趙延壽於鎮州自稱權知國事。
entries.en: At Zhenzhou Zhao Yanshou declared himself acting administrator of state affairs.
entries.literal: At Zhenzhou Zhao Yanshou styled himself acting administrator of state affairs.

entries.zh: 辛巳，陜州節度使趙暉加檢校太尉，華州節度使兼陜州馬步軍都指揮使侯章加檢校太傅，以陜府馬步軍副都指揮使兼絳州防禦使王晏為晉州節度使、檢校太傅，以丹州都指揮使、權知軍州事高彥珣為丹州刺史。
entries.en: On xinsi Zhao Hui was made Acting Grand Marshal, Hou Zhang Acting Grand Tutor, Wang Yan military governor of Jinzhou and Acting Grand Tutor, and Gao Yanqi prefect of Danzhou.
entries.literal: On the day xinsi Zhao Hui, military governor of Shaanzhou, was promoted to Acting Grand Marshal; Hou Zhang, military governor of Huazhou and Commander-in-Chief of Shaanzhou's cavalry and infantry, was promoted to Acting Grand Tutor; Wang Yan, vice commander of Shaan prefecture's horse and foot and Defender of Jiangzhou, was made military governor of Jinzhou and Acting Grand Tutor; and Gao Yanqi, commander of Danzhou and acting administrator of military and prefectural affairs, was made Prefect of Danzhou.

entries.zh: 天福十二年夏五月乙酉朔，契丹所署大丞相、政事令、東京留守、燕王趙延壽為永康烏裕所縶，既而烏裕召蕃漢臣僚於鎮州牙署，矯其主遣詔，命烏裕嗣位，於是發哀成服。
entries.en: On the first day of the fifth month in summer of the twelfth year of Tianfu, Zhao Yanshou—the Khitan appointee as Grand Chancellor, Director of Government Affairs, Eastern Capital defender, and Prince of Yan—was seized by Yongkang Wu Yu. Wu Yu then gathered Khitan and Chinese officials at the Zhenzhou headquarters, forged an edict in the Khitan emperor's name naming himself successor, and proclaimed mourning and donned mourning dress.
entries.literal: In summer, on the first day (yiyou) of the fifth month of the twelfth year of Tianfu, Zhao Yanshou—whom the Khitan had appointed Grand Chancellor, Director of Government Affairs, Defender of the Eastern Capital, and Prince of Yan—was seized by Yongkang Wu Yu. Thereupon Wu Yu summoned Khitan and Chinese officials at the headquarters in Zhenzhou, forged an edict in his lord's name appointing Wu Yu to succeed to the throne, and then proclaimed mourning and assumed mourning garments.

entries.zh: 辛卯，詔取五月十二日車駕南幸。
entries.en: On xinmao an edict set the twelfth day of the fifth month for the emperor's southward progress.
entries.literal: On xinmao an edict fixed the twelfth day of the fifth month for the imperial carriage to proceed south.

entries.zh: 甲午，以判太原府事劉崇為北京留守，命皇子承訓。
entries.en: On jiawu Liu Chong, provisional administrator of Taiyuan, was appointed Defender of the Northern Capital, and Imperial Prince Chengxun received his commission.
entries.literal: On jiawu Liu Chong, who was administering Taiyuan Prefecture, was made Defender of the Northern Capital, and Imperial Prince Chengxun was given orders.

entries.zh: 武德使李暉大內巡檢。
entries.en: Li Hui, commissioner of the Wude office, was appointed grand inspector of the inner palace.
entries.literal: Li Hui, Wude Commissioner, was made Grand Inner Inspector.

entries.zh: 丙申，帝發河東，取陰地關路幸東京。
entries.en: On bingshen the emperor left Hedong and, by way of Yindi Pass, set out for the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: On bingshen the Emperor departed Hedong, taking the Yindi Pass route on his progress to the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 時星官言，太歲在午，不利南巡，故路出陰地。
entries.en: The court astronomers had warned that with Jupiter in the Horse sign a southern tour was ill-omened, so the route was diverted through Yindi instead.
entries.literal: At the time the astronomers said that with the Year Star in the noon position, a southern tour was inauspicious, and therefore the route went out by way of Yindi.

entries.zh: 丁酉，史宏肇奏，澤州刺史翟令奇以郡來降。
entries.en: On dingyou Shi Hongzhao reported that Ze Prefecture governor Zhai Lingqi had submitted the district.
entries.literal: On dingyou Shi Hongzhao reported that Zhai Lingqi, prefect of Ze Prefecture, had surrendered the commandery.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·李萬超傳》：史宏肇路經澤州，刺史翟令奇堅壁拒命。
entries.en: (The Song History biography of Li Wanchao adds that when Shi Hongzhao marched through Ze, Prefect Zhai Lingqi held the walls and defied him.)
entries.literal: (According to the Song History, Biography of Li Wanchao: Shi Hongzhao passed through Ze Prefecture, and the prefect Zhai Lingqi shut the walls and refused to submit.)

entries.zh: 萬超馳至城下，諭之曰：「今契丹北遁，天下無主，并州劉公，仗大義，定中土，所向風靡，後服者族，盍早圖之。」
entries.en: Wanchao rode to the foot of the walls and urged him: 'The Khitan have withdrawn north; the empire has no ruler. Liu of Bingzhou acts in the name of righteousness to pacify the heartland, and resistance crumbles before him. Latecomers face extinction of their clans—why not decide now?'
entries.literal: Wanchao galloped to below the walls and instructed him, saying: 'Now the Khitan have fled north and the realm has no master. Lord Liu of Bingzhou, upholding the great cause, is settling the central lands; wherever he turns, men yield like wind before a storm. Those who submit late will have their clans exterminated—why not plan early?'

entries.zh: 令奇乃開門迎納，宏肇即留萬超權州事。）〉
entries.en: Thereupon Lingqi opened the gates and admitted them, and Hongzhao left Wanchao in temporary charge of the prefecture.)〉
entries.literal: Lingqi then opened the gates and received them; Hongzhao at once left Wanchao in provisional charge of the prefecture.)〉

entries.zh: 是日，契丹所署汴州節度使蕭翰迎郇國公李從益至東京，請從益知南朝軍國事。
entries.en: That same day Xiao Han, the Khitan-appointed governor of Bian, brought Li Congyi, Duke of Xun, to the Eastern Capital and asked him to take charge of the Southern Court's military and civil affairs.
entries.literal: That day Xiao Han, military governor of Bian Prefecture as appointed by the Khitan, welcomed the Duke of Xun, Li Congyi, to the Eastern Capital and requested that Congyi administer the military and state affairs of the Southern Court.

entries.zh: 己亥，蕭翰發離東京北去。
entries.en: On jihai Xiao Han left the Eastern Capital and marched north.
entries.literal: On jihai Xiao Han set out from the Eastern Capital and departed north.

entries.zh: 乙巳，契丹永康王烏裕自鎮州還蕃，行次定州，以定州節度副使耶律忠為定州節度使，孫方簡為雲州節度使。
entries.en: On yisi Khitan Prince Yongkang Wu Yu withdrew from Zhenzhou toward home; pausing at Dingzhou he appointed Yelü Zhong, Ding's deputy governor, as governor of Ding, and Sun Fangjian as governor of Yun.
entries.literal: On yisi the Khitan Prince of Yongkang, Wu Yu, returned to the Khitan lands from Zhenzhou; halting at Ding Prefecture, he made Yelü Zhong, deputy military governor of Ding, military governor of Ding, and Sun Fangjian military governor of Yun.

entries.zh: 方簡不受命，遂歸狼山。
entries.en: Fangjian refused the commission and withdrew to Langshan.
entries.literal: Fangjian did not accept the appointment and thereupon returned to Lang Mountain.

entries.zh: 戊申，車駕至絳州，本州刺史李從朗以郡降。
entries.en: On wushen the emperor reached Jiang Prefecture, where the incumbent governor Li Conglang submitted the district.
entries.literal: On wushen the imperial carriage reached Jiang Prefecture; Li Conglang, the native prefect, surrendered the commandery.

entries.zh: 初，契丹遣偏校成霸卿、曹可璠等守其郡，帝建義之始，不時歸命，及車駕至，帝耀兵於城下，不令攻擊，從朗等遂降。
entries.en: Earlier the Khitan had left subordinate officers Cheng Baqing and Cao Kefan to garrison the prefecture; they had not come in when the emperor first raised his banner. When he arrived he paraded troops before the walls without ordering an assault, and Conglang and his party surrendered.
entries.literal: Earlier the Khitan had sent the junior commanders Cheng Baqing, Cao Kefan, and others to hold the commandery; from the beginning of the Emperor's upholding of righteousness they had not promptly submitted. When the imperial carriage arrived, the Emperor displayed troops below the walls but did not order an attack, and Conglang and the others thereupon surrendered.

entries.zh: 六月乙卯，契丹河中節度使趙贊起復河中節度使。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on yimao, Zhao Zan—Khitan appointee as Hezhong governor—was reinstated as governor of Hezhong.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on yimao, Zhao Zan, Khitan military governor of Hezhong, was restored to military governor of Hezhong.

entries.zh: 是日，契丹右僕射兼中書侍郎、平章事張礪卒於鎮州。
entries.en: That day Zhang Li, the Khitan right vice director and grand councillor, died at Zhenzhou.
entries.literal: That day Zhang Li, Khitan Right Vice Director, concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Grand Councillor, died at Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 丙辰，車駕至洛，兩京文武百僚自新安相次奉迎。
entries.en: On bingchen the emperor reached Luoyang, where civil and military officials from both capitals met him in succession from Xin'an.
entries.literal: On bingchen the imperial carriage reached Luo; civil and military officials of the two capitals, in succession from Xin'an, came forward to welcome it.

entries.zh: 郇國公李從益、唐明宗淑妃王氏皆賜死於東京。
entries.en: At the Eastern Capital, Duke of Xun Li Congyi and Tang Mingzong's Honored Consort Wang were both ordered to take their own lives.
entries.literal: The Duke of Xun, Li Congyi, and the Honored Consort Wang of Emperor Mingzong of Tang were both granted death at the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 甲子，車駕至東京。
entries.en: On jiazi the emperor entered the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: On jiazi the imperial carriage reached the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 丙寅，以漢州就糧歸捷指揮使張建雄為濮州刺史，以金州守禦指揮使康彥環為金州防禦使。
entries.en: On bingyin Zhang Jianxiong, commander of the Han provisioning victory corps, was appointed prefect of Pu, and Kang Yanhuan, Jin's defense commander, was made defense commissioner of Jin.
entries.literal: On bingyin Zhang Jianxiong, commander of the Return-to-Victory Army for Provisioning at Han Prefecture, was made prefect of Pu; Kang Yanhuan, commander of the Jin Prefecture Defense Army, was made defense commissioner of Jin.

entries.zh: 建雄、彥環皆因亂害本州刺史，自知州事，故有是命。
entries.en: During the chaos Jianxiong and Yanhuan had each killed his prefect and taken charge of the prefecture himself, which led to these commissions.
entries.literal: Jianxiong and Yanhuan had each, amid the turmoil, killed the native prefect of their prefecture and themselves administered prefectural affairs; therefore these appointments were made.

entries.zh: 以北京知進奏王從璋為內客省使。
entries.en: Wang Congzhang, Beijing liaison for memorials to court, was appointed commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau.
entries.literal: Wang Congzhang, who handled memorials from the Northern Capital, was made commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau.

entries.zh: 戊辰，制：「大赦天下。
entries.en: On wuchen an edict declared: 'Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm.
entries.literal: On wuchen an edict proclaimed: 'A general amnesty is granted throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 應天福十二年六月十五日昧爽已前，天下見禁罪人，已結正未結正，已發覺未發覺，除十惡五逆外，罪無輕重，咸赦除之。
entries.en: All prisoners held anywhere in the realm before dawn on the fifteenth day of the sixth month, Tianfu twelve—whether their cases were closed or still pending, known or still concealed—are pardoned without regard to severity, except for the ten capital crimes and the five treasons.
entries.literal: For all prisoners now under restraint throughout the realm before dawn on the fifteenth day of the sixth month of the twelfth year of Tianfu—whether judgment has been finalized or not, whether the crime has been discovered or not—apart from the ten abominations and the five rebellions, crimes regardless of severity are all pardoned and remitted.

entries.zh: 諸州去年殘稅並放。
entries.en: Last year's unpaid taxes in every prefecture are cancelled.
entries.literal: Outstanding taxes of last year in all prefectures are remitted.

entries.zh: 東、西京一百里內，放今年夏稅；
entries.en: Within a hundred li of the two capitals, this summer's land tax is waived;
entries.literal: Within a hundred li of the Eastern and Western Capitals, this year's summer tax is remitted;

entries.zh: 一百里外及京城，今年屋稅並放一半。
entries.en: beyond that radius and in the capital districts, half of this year's dwelling tax is remitted.
entries.literal: beyond a hundred li and in the capital cities, this year's dwelling tax is remitted by half.

entries.zh: 契丹所授職任，不議改更。
entries.en: Posts granted by the Khitan regime will not be reviewed for replacement.
entries.literal: Offices conferred by the Khitan are not to be discussed for change or replacement.

entries.zh: 諸貶降官，未量移者與量移；
entries.en: Demoted officials not yet reassigned will receive new postings;
entries.literal: For all demoted and degraded officials, those not yet given a measured transfer shall receive one;

entries.zh: 已量移者與敘錄。
entries.en: those already transferred will be restored to the rolls.
entries.literal: those already given a measured transfer shall receive reinstatement in the registers.

entries.zh: 徒流人並放還。
entries.en: Convicts serving penal labor or exile are all sent home.
entries.literal: Those sentenced to penal servitude or exile are all released and sent home.

entries.zh: 應系欠省錢，家業抵當外並放。
entries.en: Debts to the provincial treasury beyond what household assets can cover are forgiven.
entries.literal: All arrears owed to the provincial treasury beyond what household property can secure are remitted.

entries.zh: 宜以國號為大漢，年號依舊稱『天福』」云。
entries.en: The realm shall be called Great Han, and the reign era shall still be Tianfu.' So it was proclaimed.
entries.literal: The state name should be Great Han, and the reign title should continue to be called "Tianfu."' Thus it was.

entries.zh: 己巳，詔青州、襄州、安州復為節鎮，曹、陳二州依舊為郡。
entries.en: On jisi an edict restored Qing, Xiang, and An to full military governorships while Cao and Chen remained ordinary prefectures.
entries.literal: On jisi an edict restored Qing, Xiang, and An prefectures to circuit-military status; Cao and Chen prefectures remained commanderies as before.

entries.zh: 壬申，北京留守劉崇加同平章事。
entries.en: On renshen Northern Capital defender Liu Chong was made grand councillor of the second rank.
entries.literal: On renshen Liu Chong, Defender of the Northern Capital, was given the additional title of Grand Councillor of the Second Class.

entries.zh: 以中書舍人劉繼儒為宗正卿；
entries.en: Secretariat drafter Liu Jiru was appointed director of the imperial clan;
entries.literal: Liu Jiru, Secretariat drafter, was made Director of the Imperial Clan;

entries.zh: 翰林學士承旨、尚書兵部侍郎張允落職守本官；
entries.en: Zhang Yun, Hanlin expositor-in-chief and vice minister of war, was reduced to his substantive rank alone;
entries.literal: Zhang Yun, Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War in the Ministry of War, was stripped of his additional posts and retained his base office;

entries.zh: 以尚書左丞張昭為吏部侍郎；
entries.en: left vice director Zhang Zhao was made vice minister of personnel;
entries.literal: Zhang Zhao, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Vice Minister of Personnel;

entries.zh: 以左散騎常侍邊歸讜為禮部侍郎；
entries.en: left cavalry attendant Bian Guidan was made vice minister of rites;
entries.literal: Bian Guidan, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, was made Vice Minister of Rites;

entries.zh: 以左散騎常侍王仁裕為戶部侍郎，充翰林學士承旨；
entries.en: left cavalry attendant Wang Renyu was made vice minister of revenue and Hanlin expositor-in-chief;
entries.literal: Wang Renyu, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, was made Vice Minister of Revenue and served as Hanlin Academician Expositor-in-Chief;

entries.zh: 以右諫議大夫張沆為左散騎常侍，充翰林學士；
entries.en: right remonstrance grandee Zhang Hong was made left cavalry attendant and Hanlin academician;
entries.literal: Zhang Hong, Right Remonstrance Grandee, was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and served as Hanlin Academician;

entries.zh: 以戶部侍郎李式為光祿卿；
entries.en: vice minister of revenue Li Shi was appointed director of the court of imperial entertainments;
entries.literal: Li Shi, Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments;

entries.zh: 以翰林學士、尚書禮部侍郎邊光範為衛尉卿。
entries.en: Hanlin academician and vice minister of rites Bian Guangfan was appointed director of the Court of the Imperial Insignia.
entries.literal: Bian Guangfan, Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Rites in the Ministry of Rites, was made Director of the Court for the Imperial Clan.

entries.zh: 甲戌，詔：「文武臣僚，每遇內殿起居，輪次上封事。」
entries.en: On jiaxu an edict ordered that at each inner-court audience civil and military officials should take turns submitting sealed memorials.'
entries.literal: On jiaxu an edict proclaimed: 'Civil and military officials, whenever they attend inner-court levee, shall in rotation submit sealed memorials.'

entries.zh: 丁丑，以湖南節度使馬希範卒，輟視朝三日。
entries.en: On dingchou court was closed for three days upon the death of Hunan governor Ma Xifan.
entries.literal: On dingchou, because Ma Xifan, military governor of Hunan, had died, court audiences were suspended for three days.

entries.zh: 是月，契丹所命相州節度使高唐英為屯駐指揮使王繼宏、楚暉所殺。
entries.en: That month Gao Tangying, the Khitan-appointed governor of Xiang, was killed by garrison commanders Wang Jihong and Chu Hui.
entries.literal: That month Gao Tangying, military governor of Xiang Prefecture as appointed by the Khitan, was killed by Wang Jihong and Chu Hui, commanders of the Garrison Army.

entries.zh: 秋七月己丑，以御史中丞趙上交為太僕卿，以戶部侍郎邊蔚為御史中丞。
entries.en: In the seventh month, on jichou, censor-in-chief Zhao Shangjiao became director of the imperial stud and vice minister of revenue Bian Wei became censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jichou Zhao Shangjiao, Censor-in-Chief, was made Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Bian Wei, Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 甲午，武安軍節度副使、水陸諸軍副都指揮使、判內外諸司、江南西道觀察等使、檢校太尉馬希廣加檢校太師、兼中書令，行潭州大都督、天策上將軍，充武安軍節度、湖南管內觀察使、江南諸道都統，封楚王。
entries.en: On jiawu Ma Xiguang—deputy Wu'an governor, joint land-and-sea commander, and Jiangnan West observer—was promoted to honorary grand preceptor and director of the secretariat, given acting rank as Tanzhou grand general and heavenly-strategies supreme general, confirmed as Wu'an governor, Hunan observer, and commander of all Jiangnan circuits, and enfeoffed as Prince of Chu.
entries.literal: On jiawu Ma Xiguang, deputy military governor of the Wu'an Army, deputy overall commander of land and water forces, administrator of inner and outer offices, Jiangnan West Circuit observation commissioner, and Honorary Grand Commandant, was given the additional titles of Honorary Grand Preceptor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat; he acted as Grand General of Tan Prefecture and Supreme General of the Heavenly Strategies, filled the posts of Wu'an military governor, Hunan circuit observation commissioner, and overall commander of the Jiangnan circuits, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Chu.

entries.zh: 丙申，以鄴都留守、天雄軍節度使、檢校太師、守太傅、兼中書令、衛國公杜重威為宋州節度使，加守太尉；
entries.en: On bingshen Yedu defender and Tianxiong governor Du Chongwei, Duke of Wei, was transferred to Songzhou and promoted to acting grand guardian;
entries.literal: On bingshen Du Chongwei, Defender of Yedu, military governor of the Tianxiong Army, Honorary Grand Preceptor, Acting Grand Tutor, concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and Duke of Wei, was made military governor of Song and given the additional Acting Grand Guardian;

entries.zh: 以宋州節度使、檢校太師、兼中書令高行周為鄴都留守，加守太傅；
entries.en: Song governor Gao Xingzhou became Yedu defender with the added rank of acting grand tutor;
entries.literal: Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Song, Honorary Grand Preceptor, and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, was made Defender of Yedu and given the additional Acting Grand Tutor;

entries.zh: 以鄆州節度使、檢校太師、兼侍中李守貞為河中節度使，加兼中書令；
entries.en: Yanzhou governor Li Shouzhen was moved to Hezhong and made concurrent director of the secretariat;
entries.literal: Li Shouzhen, military governor of Yan, Honorary Grand Preceptor, and concurrent Palace Attendant, was made military governor of Hezhong and given the additional concurrent Director of the Secretariat;

entries.zh: 以河中節度使、檢校太尉趙贊為晉昌軍節度使；
entries.en: Hezhong governor Zhao Zan was transferred to the Jinchang command;
entries.literal: Zhao Zan, military governor of Hezhong and Honorary Grand Commandant, was made military governor of the Jinchang Army;

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·趙贊傳》：贊懼漢疑己，潛遣親吏趙仙奉表歸蜀。
entries.en: (The Song History biography of Zhao Zan records that fearing Han suspicion, he secretly sent his aide Zhao Xian with a memorial offering submission to Shu.)
entries.literal: (According to the Song History, Biography of Zhao Zan: Zan feared that the Han court suspected him and secretly sent his personal clerk Zhao Xian to present a memorial and submit to Shu.)

entries.zh: 判官李恕者，趙延壽賓佐，深所委賴，至家事亦參之，及贊出鎮，從為上介。
entries.en: His aide Li Shu had been Zhao Yanshou's trusted adviser, even consulted on family matters; when Zan took up his governorship Shu went with him as chief administrator.
entries.literal: The administrative aide Li Shu had been a guest-official of Zhao Yanshou, deeply relied upon—even household affairs were entrusted to him—and when Zan went out to a command, Shu followed as chief aide.

entries.zh: 至是，恕語贊曰：「燕王入遼，非所願也，漢方建國，必務懷柔。
entries.en: Now Shu told Zan: 'The Prince of Yan's captivity in Liao was not his choice. The new Han regime will surely seek to win men over gently.
entries.literal: At this time Shu said to Zan: 'The Prince of Yan's going into Liao was not of his own wish. The Han are just establishing their state and are sure to practice gentle reassurance.

entries.zh: 公若泥首歸朝，必保富貴；
entries.en: If you prostrate yourself and return to court, your wealth and rank are secure;
entries.literal: If you bow your head and return to court, you are certain to preserve wealth and rank;

entries.zh: 狼狽入蜀，理難萬全。
entries.en: fleeing in disarray to Shu can scarcely be a safe course.
entries.literal: to flee in disorder into Shu can hardly be fully safe in reason.

entries.zh: 儻若不容，後悔無及。
entries.en: If they reject you, it will be too late for regret.
entries.literal: If perchance you are not accepted, regret will come too late.

entries.zh: 公能聽納，請先入朝為公申理。」
entries.en: If you agree, let me go to court first and explain your situation.'
entries.literal: If you can heed and accept this, allow me to enter court first and plead your case on your behalf.'

entries.zh: 贊即遣恕詣闕。
entries.en: Zan immediately sent Shu to the capital.
entries.literal: Zan at once sent Shu to the palace.

entries.zh: 漢祖見恕，問贊何以附蜀。
entries.en: The Han founder received Shu and asked why Zhao Zan had sought Shu.
entries.literal: The Han Founder received Shu and asked why Zan had attached himself to Shu.

entries.zh: 恕曰：「贊家在燕薊，身受契丹之命，自懷憂恐，謂陛下終不能容，招引西軍，蓋圖茍免。
entries.en: Shu replied: 'Zan's kin are in Yanji. Bound to the Khitan, he feared Your Majesty would never trust him; reaching out to western forces was only a desperate bid to survive.
entries.literal: Shu said: 'Zan's family is in Yan and Ji. He bore an appointment from the Khitan and inwardly feared that Your Majesty would never tolerate him; summoning western troops was merely plotting to save himself as best he could.
