entries.zh: 臣意國家甫定，務安臣民，所以令臣乞哀求覲。」
entries.en: I believed the new dynasty would seek to reassure its subjects, and so I came to beg an audience on his behalf.'
entries.literal: I thought the state had just been settled and would strive to reassure officials and people, and therefore had me beg humbly to request an audience.'

entries.zh: 漢祖曰：「贊之父子，亦吾人也，事契丹出於不幸。
entries.en: The founder said: 'The Zans are our own people; serving the Khitan was misfortune.
entries.literal: The Han Founder said: 'Zan and his father are also our people; serving the Khitan came from misfortune.

entries.zh: 今聞延壽落於陷阱，吾忍不容贊耶！」
entries.en: Now that Yanshou is trapped, how could I refuse to accept Zan!'
entries.literal: Now I hear Yanshou has fallen into a trap—how could I bear not to tolerate Zan!'

entries.zh: 恕未還，贊巳離鎮入朝，即命為左驍衛將軍。）〉
entries.en: Before Shu returned, Zan had already left his post for court and was immediately appointed general of the left valiant cavalry guard.)〉
entries.literal: Before Shu returned, Zan had already left his command and entered court, and was at once appointed General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.)〉

entries.zh: 以晉昌軍節度使張彥超為鄜州節度使，加檢校太師。
entries.en: Jinchang governor Zhang Yanchao was transferred to Yanzhou and made honorary grand preceptor.
entries.literal: Zhang Yanchao, military governor of the Jinchang Army, was made military governor of Yan and given the additional Honorary Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 庚子，以徐州節度使、檢校太師、同平章事、岐國公符彥卿為兗州節度使，加兼侍中；
entries.en: On gengzi Xu governor Fu Yanqing, Duke of Qi, was moved to Yanzhou and made concurrent palace attendant;
entries.literal: On gengzi Fu Yanqing, military governor of Xu, Honorary Grand Preceptor, Grand Councillor of the Second Class, and Duke of Qi, was made military governor of Yan and given the additional concurrent Palace Attendant;

entries.zh: 以鄧州節度使、檢校太師王周為徐州節度使，加同平章事；
entries.en: Deng governor Wang Zhou became Xu governor and grand councillor of the second rank;
entries.literal: Wang Zhou, military governor of Deng and Honorary Grand Preceptor, was made military governor of Xu and given Grand Councillor of the Second Class;

entries.zh: 以許州節度使、檢校太保劉重進為鄧州節度使，加檢校太傅；
entries.en: Xu governor Liu Chongjin was transferred to Deng and promoted to honorary grand tutor;
entries.literal: Liu Chongjin, military governor of Xu and Honorary Grand Mentor, was made military governor of Deng and given the additional Honorary Grand Tutor;

entries.zh: 以兗州節度使、檢校太師、兼侍中安審琦為襄州節度使；
entries.en: Yanzhou governor An Shenqi was appointed governor of Xiang;
entries.literal: An Shenqi, military governor of Yan, Honorary Grand Preceptor, and concurrent Palace Attendant, was made military governor of Xiang;

entries.zh: 檢校太師、莒國公李從敏為西京留守，加同平章事；
entries.en: Li Congmin, Duke of Ju, became Western Capital defender and grand councillor;
entries.literal: Li Congmin, Honorary Grand Preceptor and Duke of Ju, was made Defender of the Western Capital and given Grand Councillor of the Second Class;

entries.zh: 以鳳翔節度使、檢校太師、同平章事侯益依前鳳翔節度使，加兼侍中。
entries.en: Fengxiang governor Hou Yi kept his post and was made concurrent palace attendant.
entries.literal: Hou Yi, military governor of Fengxiang, Honorary Grand Preceptor, and Grand Councillor of the Second Class, remained as before military governor of Fengxiang and was given the additional concurrent Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 辛丑，故守司空兼門下侍郎、平章事、譙國公劉旬贈太保。
entries.en: On xinchou the late grand councillor Liu Xun, Duke of Qiao, was posthumously honored as grand tutor.
entries.literal: On xinchou the late Acting Minister of Works, concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery, Grand Councillor, and Duke of Qiao, Liu Xun, was posthumously given Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 甲辰，華州節度使侯章、同州節度使張彥威、涇州節度使史威，並加檢校太尉。
entries.en: On jiachen the governors of Hua, Tong, and Jing—Hou Zhang, Zhang Yanwei, and Shi Wei—were all promoted to honorary Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: On jiachen Hou Zhang, military governor of Hua; Zhang Yanwei, military governor of Tong; and Shi Wei, military governor of Jing, were all given the additional Honorary Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 以晉昌軍節度使、檢校太保劉銖為青州節度使，加檢校太尉、同平章事；
entries.en: Jinchang governor Liu Zhu was made Qing governor with the added ranks of honorary Grand Commandant and grand councillor;
entries.literal: Liu Zhu, military governor of the Jinchang Army and Honorary Grand Guardian, was made military governor of Qing and given the additional Honorary Grand Commandant and Grand Councillor of the Second Class;

entries.zh: 以河中節度使、檢校太尉白文珂為鄆州節度使，加同平章事；
entries.en: Hezhong governor Bai Wenke was transferred to Yunzhou and made grand councillor;
entries.literal: Bai Wenke, military governor of Hezhong and Honorary Grand Commandant, was made military governor of Yun and given Grand Councillor of the Second Class;

entries.zh: 以青州節度使楊承信為安州節度使，加檢校太傅；
entries.en: Qing governor Yang Chengxin was moved to Anzhou and made honorary grand tutor;
entries.literal: Yang Chengxin, military governor of Qing, was made military governor of An and given the additional Honorary Grand Tutor;

entries.zh: 滑州節度使兼侍衛馬軍都指揮使劉信、許州節度使兼侍衛步軍都指揮使史宏肇，並加檢校太尉。
entries.en: Hua governor and horse-guard commander Liu Xin and Xu governor and foot-guard commander Shi Hongzhao were both promoted to honorary Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: Liu Xin, military governor of Hua and concurrent overall commander of the palace horse guards, and Shi Hongzhao, military governor of Xu and concurrent overall commander of the palace foot guards, were both given the additional Honorary Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 庚戌，以司天監任延浩為殿中監，以司天少監杜升為司天監。
entries.en: On gengxu astronomical director Ren Yanhao became director of the palace library, and deputy director Du Sheng succeeded him as astronomical director.
entries.literal: On gengxu Ren Yanhao, Director of the Astronomical Bureau, was made Director of the Palace Library; Du Sheng, Deputy Director of the Astronomical Bureau, was made Director of the Astronomical Bureau.

entries.zh: 是月，契丹永康王烏裕囚祖母舒嚕氏於木葉山。
entries.en: That month Khitan Prince Yongkang Wu Yu imprisoned his grandmother Lady Shulu on Mount Muye.
entries.literal: That month the Khitan Prince of Yongkang, Wu Yu, imprisoned his grandmother Lady Shulu on Muye Mountain.

entries.zh: 閏月辛酉，以左衛上將軍皇甫立為太子太師致仕。
entries.en: In the intercalary month, on xinyou, left guards general Huangfu Li was made grand preceptor of the heir apparent and retired from office.
entries.literal: In the intercalary month, on xinyou Huangfu Li, General of the Left Guards, was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired.

entries.zh: 乙丑，禁造契丹樣鞍轡、器械、服裝。
entries.en: On yichou the court banned the manufacture of Khitan-style saddlery, arms, and dress.
entries.literal: On yichou the manufacture of Khitan-style saddles and bridles, weapons, and clothing was forbidden.

entries.zh: 故開封尹桑維翰贈尚書令，故西京留守景延廣贈中書令，以前衛尉卿薛仁謙為司農卿。
entries.en: The late Kaifeng prefect Sang Weihan was posthumously honored as director of the department of state affairs, the late Western Capital defender Jing Yanguang as director of the secretariat, and former imperial-clan court director Xue Renqian was appointed director of the national granaries.
entries.literal: The late Prefect of Kaifeng Sang Weihan was posthumously given Director of the Department of State Affairs; the late Defender of the Western Capital Jing Yanguang was posthumously given Director of the Secretariat; the former Director of the Court for the Imperial Clan Xue Renqian was made Director of the Court of the National Granaries.

entries.zh: 丙寅，唐故樞密使郭崇韜贈中書令，故河中節度使安重誨贈尚書令，故華州節度使毛璋贈侍中，故汴州節度使朱守殷贈中書令。
entries.en: On bingyin the late Tang military commissioner Guo Chongtao, late Hezhong governor An Chonghui, late Hua governor Mao Zhang, and late Bian governor Zhu Shouyin received posthumous honors as director of the secretariat, director of the secretariat, palace attendant, and director of the secretariat respectively.
entries.literal: On bingyin the late Tang Commissioner of Military Affairs Guo Chongtao was posthumously given Director of the Secretariat; the late military governor of Hezhong An Chonghui was posthumously given Director of the Secretariat; the late military governor of Hua Mao Zhang was posthumously given Palace Attendant; the late military governor of Bian Zhu Shouyin was posthumously given Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 丁卯，故青州節度楊光遠贈尚書令，追封齊王，仍令所司追謚立碑。
entries.en: On dingmao the late Qing governor Yang Guangyuan was posthumously made director of the secretariat and Prince of Qi, with orders to grant a posthumous name and set up a memorial stele.
entries.literal: On dingmao the late military governor of Qing Yang Guangyuan was posthumously given Director of the Secretariat, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, and the responsible offices were ordered to confer a posthumous title and erect a stele.

entries.zh: 唐故河中節度使、西平王朱友謙追封魏王，故樞密使馮赟贈中書令，故河陽節度使、判六軍康義誠贈中書令。
entries.en: The late Tang Hezhong governor and Prince of Xiping Zhu Youqian was posthumously made Prince of Wei; the late military commissioner Feng Yun and late Heyang governor Kang Yicheng, who had administered the six armies, were posthumously honored as directors of the secretariat.
entries.literal: The late Tang military governor of Hezhong and Prince of Xiping Zhu Youqian was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wei; the late Commissioner of Military Affairs Feng Yun was posthumously given Director of the Secretariat; the late military governor of Heyang and administrator of the Six Armies Kang Yicheng was posthumously given Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 故西京留守、京兆尹王思同、故邠州節度使藥彥稠、故襄州節度使安重進、故鎮州節度使安重榮，並贈侍中。
entries.en: The late Western Capital defender and Jingzhao prefect Wang Sitong, late Bin governor Yao Yanchou, late Xiang governor An Chongjin, and late Zhen governor An Chongrong were all posthumously honored as palace attendants.
entries.literal: The late Defender of the Western Capital and Prefect of Jingzhao Wang Sitong; the late military governor of Bin Yao Yanchou; the late military governor of Xiang An Chongjin; and the late military governor of Zhen An Chongrong were all posthumously given Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 庚午，以前延州留後薛可言為宣徽北院使，以監察御史王度為樞密直學士。
entries.en: On gengwu former Yanzhou acting prefect Xue Keyan became commissioner of the northern palace secretariat bureau, and investigating censor Wang Du became direct academician of the military affairs commission.
entries.literal: On gengwu the former acting prefect of Yan Xue Keyan was made commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat; the investigating censor Wang Du was made direct academician of the Military Affairs Commission.

entries.zh: 新授宋州節度使杜重威據鄴都叛，詔削奪重威官爵，貶為庶人。
entries.en: Du Chongwei, newly appointed to Song but holding Yedu, rebelled; an edict stripped him of rank and reduced him to commoner status.
entries.literal: The newly appointed military governor of Song Du Chongwei, holding Yedu, rebelled; an edict stripped Chongwei of office and rank and degraded him to commoner.

entries.zh: 以高行周為行營都部署，率兵進討。
entries.en: Gao Xingzhou was appointed overall campaign commander and marched to suppress the rebellion.
entries.literal: Gao Xingzhou was made overall commander of the campaign army and led troops forward to attack.

entries.zh: 辛未，以權樞密使楊邠為樞密使，加檢校太傅；
entries.en: On xinwei acting military commissioner Yang Bin became full commissioner with the added rank of honorary grand tutor;
entries.literal: On xinwei Yang Bin, acting Commissioner of Military Affairs, was made Commissioner of Military Affairs and given the additional Honorary Grand Tutor;

entries.zh: 以權樞密副使郭威為副樞密使，加檢校太保；
entries.en: acting deputy commissioner Guo Wei was confirmed as deputy commissioner and made honorary grand mentor;
entries.literal: Guo Wei, acting Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs, was made Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs and given the additional Honorary Grand Mentor;

entries.zh: 以權三司使王章為三司使，加檢校太傅。
entries.en: acting finance commissioner Wang Zhang was made full commissioner with the added rank of honorary grand tutor.
entries.literal: Wang Zhang, acting Commissioner of the Three Departments, was made Commissioner of the Three Departments and given the additional Honorary Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 壬申，故晉昌軍節度使趙在禮贈中書令，故曹州節度使石赟贈侍中，故滑州節度使皇甫遇贈中書令。
entries.en: On renshen the late Jinchang governor Zhao Zaili and late Hua governor Huangfu Yu were posthumously made directors of the secretariat, and the late Cao governor Shi Yun was made palace attendant.
entries.literal: On renshen the late military governor of the Jinchang Army Zhao Zaili was posthumously given Director of the Secretariat; the late military governor of Cao Shi Yun was posthumously given Palace Attendant; the late military governor of Hua Huangfu Yu was posthumously given Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 故曹州節度使劉繼鄖、故滑州節度使梁漢璋，皆贈太尉；
entries.en: The late Cao governor Liu Jiyun and late Hua governor Liang Hanzhang were both posthumously honored as grand guardian;
entries.literal: The late military governor of Cao Liu Jiyun and the late military governor of Hua Liang Hanzhang were both posthumously given Grand Guardian;

entries.zh: 故宣徽使孟承誨贈太保。
entries.en: The late palace domestic commissioner Meng Chenghui was posthumously honored as grand preceptor.
entries.literal: The late Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service Meng Chenghui was posthumously given Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 丁丑，有彗出於張，旬日而滅。
entries.en: On dingchou a comet appeared in the Zhang asterism and faded after ten days.
entries.literal: On dingchou a comet appeared in the Zhang constellation; in ten days it vanished.

entries.zh: 己卯，陜州節度使趙暉加階爵，晉州節度使王晏加檢校太尉，河陽節度使武行德加階爵，延州節度使高允權加檢校太尉。
entries.en: On jimao Shan governor Zhao Hui received a higher noble rank, Jin governor Wang Yan was made honorary Grand Commandant, Heyang governor Wu Xingde was promoted in rank, and Yan governor Gao Yunquan was made honorary Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: On jimao Zhao Hui, military governor of Shan, was given added rank and enfeoffment; Wang Yan, military governor of Jin, was given the additional Honorary Grand Commandant; Wu Xingde, military governor of Heyang, was given added rank and enfeoffment; Gao Yunquan, military governor of Yan, was given the additional Honorary Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 鄧州節度使常思加檢校太尉，移鎮潞州。
entries.en: Deng governor Chang Si was made honorary Grand Commandant and transferred to Lu Prefecture.
entries.literal: Chang Si, military governor of Deng, was given the additional Honorary Grand Commandant and transferred to garrison at Lu.

entries.zh: 庚辰，追尊六廟，以太祖高皇帝、世祖光武皇帝為不祧之廟，高曾已下四朝，追尊謚號，已載於前矣。
entries.en: On gengchen the court enshrined the six ancestral temples, setting Emperor Gaozu the High and Emperor Guangwu the Bright Martial as permanent temples never to be removed, while the posthumous titles of the four earlier generations had already been given above.
entries.literal: On gengchen the six ancestral temples were posthumously honored; the High Ancestor Emperor Gaozu and the Bright Martial Ancestor Emperor Guangwu were made undislodgeable temples; the four preceding generations from the High and Remote Ancestors downward had posthumous titles already recorded above.

entries.zh: 是日，權太常卿張昭上六廟樂章舞名：太祖高皇帝室酌獻，請依舊奏《武德之舞》；
entries.en: That day acting minister of rites Zhang Zhao submitted the ritual music and dances for the six temples: for the libation at Emperor Gaozu the High's shrine, he asked that the old Dance of Martial Virtue be performed as before;
entries.literal: That day Acting Minister of Rites Zhang Zhao submitted the names of the music and dances for the six temples: for the libation offering at the shrine of Emperor Gaozu the High, he requested that the old "Dance of Martial Virtue" be performed as before;

entries.zh: 世祖光武皇帝室酌獻，請依舊奏《大武之舞》；
entries.en: for Emperor Guangwu the Bright Martial's shrine, he asked that the old Great Martial Dance be performed as before;
entries.literal: for the libation offering at the shrine of Emperor Guangwu the Bright Martial, he requested that the old "Great Martial Dance" be performed as before;

entries.zh: 文祖明元皇帝室酌獻，請奏《靈長之舞》；
entries.en: for Emperor Mingyuan the Literary Ancestor's shrine, he proposed the Dance of Enduring Spirit;
entries.literal: for the libation offering at the shrine of Emperor Mingyuan the Literary Ancestor, he requested the performance of "Dance of Enduring Spirit";

entries.zh: 德祖恭僖皇帝室酌獻，請奏《積善之舞》；
entries.en: for Emperor Gongxi the Reverent and Joyful Ancestor's shrine, the Dance of Accumulated Goodness;
entries.literal: for the libation offering at the shrine of Emperor Gongxi the Reverent and Joyful Ancestor, he requested the performance of "Dance of Accumulated Goodness";

entries.zh: 翼祖昭獻皇帝室酌獻，請奏《顯仁之舞》；
entries.en: for Emperor Zhaoxian the Assisting Ancestor's shrine, the Dance of Manifest Benevolence;
entries.literal: for the libation offering at the shrine of Emperor Zhaoxian the Assisting Ancestor, he requested the performance of "Dance of Manifest Benevolence";

entries.zh: 顯祖章聖皇帝室酌獻，請奏《章慶之舞》。
entries.en: for Emperor Zhangsheng the Illustrious Ancestor's shrine, the Dance of Glorious Celebration.
entries.literal: for the libation offering at the shrine of Emperor Zhangsheng the Illustrious Ancestor, he requested the performance of "Dance of Glorious Celebration."

entries.zh: 其六廟歌詞，文多不錄。
entries.en: The hymn texts for the six temples are largely omitted here.
entries.literal: As for the hymn texts of the six temples, most of the wording is not recorded here.

entries.zh: 八月壬午朔，鎮州駐屯護聖左廂都指揮使白再榮等，逐契丹所命節度使麻答，復其城。
entries.en: On the first day of the eighth month, Bai Zairong, left-wing commander of the imperial guard at Zhenzhou, expelled the Khitan appointee Mada and recaptured the city.
entries.literal: On the first day (renwu) of the eighth month, Bai Zairong and others, Left Wing overall commander of the Imperial Guard garrisoned at Zhenzhou, drove out Mada, the military governor appointed by the Khitan, and recovered the city.

entries.zh: 麻答與河陽節度使崔廷勛、洛京留守劉晞，並奔定州。
entries.en: Mada fled with Heyang governor Cui Tingxun and Luoyang defender Liu Xi, all making for Ding Prefecture.
entries.literal: Mada, together with Cui Tingxun, military governor of Heyang, and Liu Xi, defender of the Luoyang capital, all fled to Dingzhou.

entries.zh: 馳驛以聞。
entries.en: Word was sent to court by urgent relay.
entries.literal: An express relay was dispatched to report it.

entries.zh: 庚寅，以洺州團練使薛懷讓為邢州節度使。
entries.en: On gengyin Luo regimentation commissioner Xue Huairang was appointed military governor of Xing.
entries.literal: On gengyin Xue Huairang, regimentation commissioner of Luo, was made military governor of Xing.

entries.zh: 辛卯，詔恒州復為鎮州，順國軍復為成德軍。
entries.en: On xinmao an edict restored the name Heng Prefecture to Zhen and the Shunguo Army to Chengde.
entries.literal: On xinmao an edict restored Heng Prefecture to Zhen Prefecture and the Shunguo Army to the Chengde Army.

entries.zh: 乙未，以護聖左廂都指揮使、恩州團練使白再榮為鎮州留後。
entries.en: On yiwei Bai Zairong, left-wing imperial guard commander and En regimentation commissioner, was made acting governor of Zhen.
entries.literal: On yiwei Bai Zairong, Left Wing overall commander of the Imperial Guard and regimentation commissioner of En, was made acting military governor of Zhen.

entries.zh: 丙申，詔天下凡關賊盜，不計贓物多少，案驗不虛，並處死。
entries.en: On bingshen an edict ruled that anyone convicted of robbery or banditry anywhere in the realm, whatever the value stolen, was to be executed once the case was substantiated.
entries.literal: On bingshen an edict declared that throughout the realm, in all cases of robbery and banditry, regardless of the amount of stolen goods, if investigation proved the charges true, all were to be put to death.

entries.zh: 以兩浙節度使、守太師、兼中書令、吳越國王錢宏佐薨，廢朝三日。
entries.en: Upon the death of Qian Hongzuo, governor of the Two Zhes, defender grand preceptor, director of the secretariat, and king of Wuyue, court was closed for three days.
entries.literal: Because Qian Hongzuo, military governor of the Two Zhes, Defender Grand Preceptor, concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and King of Wuyue, had died, court audiences were suspended for three days.

entries.zh: 丙午，以吐渾府節度使、檢校太尉王義宗為沁州刺史，依前吐渾節度使。
entries.en: On bingwu Tuyuhun governor Wang Yizong was appointed prefect of Qin while retaining his Tuyuhun command.
entries.literal: On bingwu Wang Yizong, military governor of the Tuyuhun Prefecture and Honorary Grand Commandant, was made prefect of Qin while continuing as before as military governor of Tuyuhun.

entries.zh: 己酉，以刑部尚書竇貞固為吏部尚書。
entries.en: On jiyou Minister of Justice Dou Zhengu was appointed minister of personnel.
entries.literal: On jiyou Dou Zhengu, Minister of Justice, was made Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 是日，薛懷讓奏，收復邢州，殺偽命節度副使、知州事劉鐸。
entries.en: That day Xue Huairang reported the recovery of Xing Prefecture and the killing of Liu Duo, the illicitly appointed deputy governor and acting prefect.
entries.literal: That day Xue Huairang memorialized that Xing Prefecture had been recovered and that Liu Duo, illicitly appointed deputy military governor and acting prefect, had been killed.

entries.zh: 初，懷讓為洺州防禦使，契丹麻答發健步督洺州糧運，懷讓殺之以聞。
entries.en: Earlier, while Huairang was defense commissioner of Luo, the Khitan Mada had sent swift couriers to oversee grain shipments; Huairang killed them and reported the matter.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Huairang was defense commissioner of Luo, the Khitan Mada sent swift runners to supervise grain transport from Luo; Huairang killed them and reported it.

entries.zh: 帝遣郭從義與懷讓攻取邢州，蕃將楊袞來援鐸，懷讓拒之，不勝，退保洺州，敵騎掠其部，民大被其苦。
entries.en: The emperor sent Guo Congyi to join Huairang in attacking Xing. The Khitan general Yang Gun came to Liu Duo's aid; Huairang resisted but was beaten back to Luo, and enemy cavalry ravaged the region, inflicting great suffering on the people.
entries.literal: The Emperor dispatched Guo Congyi together with Huairang to seize Xing; the foreign general Yang Gun came to aid Duo; Huairang resisted but was defeated, withdrew to hold Luo, and enemy cavalry plundered his territory, so the people suffered greatly.

entries.zh: 會鎮州逐麻答，楊袞收兵退，鐸乃上表請命。
entries.en: When Zhen expelled Mada, Yang Gun withdrew; Liu Duo then memorialized requesting formal appointment.
entries.literal: When Zhen drove out Mada, Yang Gun withdrew his troops; Duo then submitted a memorial requesting official appointment.

entries.zh: 懷讓乘其無備，遣人紿鐸云：「奉詔襲契丹，請置頓於郡。」
entries.en: Taking advantage of Duo's unpreparedness, Huairang sent a man to deceive him, saying, "By imperial order we are marching against the Khitan; please allow us to encamp in the prefectural city."
entries.literal: Huairang, seizing his lack of preparedness, sent a man to deceive Duo, saying: 'By imperial order we are striking the Khitan; please allow us to encamp in the prefectural seat.'

entries.zh: 鐸開門迎之，即為懷讓所害，時人冤之。
entries.en: Duo opened the gates to welcome them and was immediately killed by Huairang; contemporaries regarded it as a grievous injustice.
entries.literal: Duo opened the gates to welcome them and was immediately killed by Huairang; people of the time considered it an injustice.

entries.zh: 鐸初受契丹命為邢州都指揮使，及永康王以高奉明為節度使，滿達勒署鐸為邢州副使兼都指揮使。
entries.en: Liu Duo had first received Khitan appointment as commander of Xing; when Prince Yongkang installed Gao Fengming as governor, Manduolie made Duo deputy governor of Xing while retaining command.
entries.literal: At first Duo received Khitan appointment as overall commander of Xing; when Prince Yongkang made Gao Fengming military governor, Manduolie appointed Duo deputy military governor of Xing and concurrent overall commander.

entries.zh: 帝至東京，奉明歸鎮州，令鐸知邢州事，至是遇害。
entries.en: When the emperor reached the Eastern Capital, Gao Fengming returned to Zhen and put Liu Duo in charge of Xing; it was then that Duo was killed.
entries.literal: When the Emperor reached the Eastern Capital, Fengming returned to Zhen and ordered Duo to administer the affairs of Xing; at this time he met his death.

entries.zh: 庚戌，文武百僚上表，請以二月四日降誕日為聖壽節，從之。
entries.en: On gengxu the civil and military officials memorialized that the emperor's birthday, the fourth day of the second month, be observed as the Sacred Longevity Festival; the request was granted.
entries.literal: On gengxu the civil and military officials submitted a memorial requesting that the fourth day of the second month, the day of the Emperor's birth, be made the Sacred Longevity Festival; the request was granted.

entries.zh: 前晉昌軍節度副使李肅加左驍衛上將軍致仕。
entries.en: Li Su, former deputy governor of Jinchang, was promoted to left general of the valiant cavalry guard and granted retirement.
entries.literal: Li Su, former deputy military governor of the Jinchang Army, was made Left General of the Valiant Cavalry Guard and retired.

entries.zh: 是月，遣使諸道和市戰馬。
entries.en: That month envoys were sent to the circuits to procure war horses through official purchase.
entries.literal: That month envoys were dispatched to the various circuits to purchase war horses at fair prices.

entries.zh: 九月甲子，宰臣蘇逢吉兼戶部尚書，蘇禹珪兼刑部尚書。
entries.en: On jiazi in the ninth month chief minister Su Fengji was given concurrent appointment as minister of revenue and Su Yugui as minister of justice.
entries.literal: On jiazi in the ninth month Chief Minister Su Fengji was made concurrent Minister of Revenue and Su Yugui concurrent Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 丁卯，以吏部侍郎、權判太常卿事張昭為太常卿。
entries.en: On dingmao vice minister of personnel Zhang Zhao, acting minister of rites, was appointed minister of rites.
entries.literal: On dingmao Zhang Zhao, Vice Minister of Personnel and acting Minister of Rites, was made Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 戊辰，故易州刺史郭璘贈太傅。
entries.en: On wuchen the late Yi prefect Guo Lin was posthumously honored as grand tutor.
entries.literal: On wuchen the late Prefect of Yi Guo Lin was posthumously given Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 甲戌，宰臣蘇逢吉加左僕射、監修國史，蘇禹珪加右僕射、集賢殿大學士，以吏部尚書竇貞固為守司空兼門下侍郎、平章事、宏文館大學士，
entries.en: On jiaxu chief minister Su Fengji became left vice director and supervisor of the national history; Su Yugui became right vice director and grand academician of the hall of assembled worthies; and minister of personnel Dou Zhengu was appointed defender minister of works, vice director of the chancellery, grand councillor, and grand academician of the hall of broad culture,
entries.literal: On jiaxu Chief Minister Su Fengji was made Left Vice Director and Supervisor of the National History; Su Yugui was made Right Vice Director and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; Dou Zhengu, Minister of Personnel, was made Defender Minister of Works, concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery, Grand Councillor, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Broad Culture,

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·竇貞固傳》：初，帝與貞固同事晉祖，甚相得。
entries.en: (The Song History biography of Dou Zhengu notes that the emperor and Zhengu had once served together under Jin Gaozu and were on excellent terms.
entries.literal: (According to the Song History, Biography of Dou Zhengu: At first the Emperor and Zhengu had served Emperor Gaozu of Jin together and were very well matched.

entries.zh: 時蘇逢吉、蘇禹珪自霸府僚佐驟居相位，思得舊臣冠首，以貞固持重寡言，有時望，乃拜司空、門下侍郎、平章事。）〉
entries.en: Su Fengji and Su Yugui had risen abruptly from the Prince of Wei's staff to the chief ministership; wishing a senior minister at their head, and finding Zhengu steady, reserved, and widely respected, they appointed him minister of works, vice director of the chancellery, and grand councillor.)〉
entries.literal: At that time Su Fengji and Su Yugui had risen abruptly from staff officers of the Prince of Wei's domain to the chief ministership; wishing to place an old minister at their head, and because Zhengu was steady, sparing of speech, and enjoyed public esteem, he was appointed Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Grand Councillor.)〉

entries.zh: 以翰林學士、行中書舍人李濤為中書侍郎兼戶部尚書、平章事。
entries.en: Hanlin academician and acting secretariat drafter Li Tao was appointed vice director of the secretariat, concurrent minister of revenue, and grand councillor.
entries.literal: Li Tao, Hanlin Academician and acting Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of Revenue, and Grand Councillor.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·李濤傳》：杜重威據鄴叛，高祖命高行周、慕容彥超討之，二帥不協，濤密疏親征。
entries.en: (The Song History biography of Li Tao records that when Du Chongwei rebelled and held Ye, Gaozu ordered Gao Xingzhou and Murong Yanchao to suppress him; the two commanders failed to cooperate, and Tao submitted a secret memorial urging the emperor to lead the campaign in person.
entries.literal: (According to the Song History, Biography of Li Tao: When Du Chongwei held Ye and rebelled, Emperor Gaozu ordered Gao Xingzhou and Murong Yanchao to suppress him; the two commanders were not in accord, and Tao submitted a secret memorial urging the Emperor to take the field in person.

entries.zh: 高祖覽奏，以濤堪任宰輔，即拜中書侍郎兼戶部侍郎、平章事。）〉
entries.en: Gaozu read the memorial and, judging Tao fit for high office, immediately appointed him vice director of the secretariat, concurrent vice minister of revenue, and grand councillor.)〉
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu read the memorial and, judging Tao fit for the chief ministership, immediately appointed him Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Vice Minister of Revenue, and Grand Councillor.)〉

entries.zh: 是日，權太常卿張昭上疏，奏改一代樂名。
entries.en: That day acting minister of rites Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial proposing changes to the dynasty's ritual music titles.
entries.literal: That day Acting Minister of Rites Zhang Zhao submitted a memorial proposing a change in the names of music for one generation.

entries.zh: 戊寅，詔以杜重威叛命，取今月二十九日暫幸澶、魏。
entries.en: On wuyin an edict declared that because Du Chongwei had rebelled, the emperor would temporarily proceed to Chan and Wei on the twenty-ninth day of that month.
entries.literal: On wuyin an edict declared that because Du Chongwei had rebelled against his commission, on the twenty-ninth day of this month the Emperor would temporarily visit Chan and Wei.

entries.zh: 己卯，以前樞密使李崧為太子太傅，以前左僕射和凝為太子太保。
entries.en: On jimao former military commissioner Li Song was appointed grand tutor of the heir apparent, and former left vice director He Ning grand preceptor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: On jimao the former Commissioner of Military Affairs Li Song was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and the former Left Vice Director He Ning was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 庚辰，車駕發京師。
entries.en: On gengchen the emperor departed the capital.
entries.literal: On gengchen the imperial carriage departed the capital.

entries.zh: 冬十月癸未，以太子太保李鏻為司徒，以太子太傅盧文紀為太子太師，以前磁州刺史李穀為左散騎常侍。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter, on guiwei, grand preceptor of the heir apparent Li Lin was appointed minister of education; grand tutor Lu Wenji was made grand preceptor of the heir apparent; and former Ci prefect Li Gu was appointed left cavalry attendant.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on guiwei Li Lin, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, was made Minister of Education; Lu Wenji, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; Li Gu, former Prefect of Ci, was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·李蒨傳》：舊制，罷外郡歸本官，至是進秩，獎之也。）〉
entries.en: (The Song History biography of Li Qian notes that by custom dismissal from an external post meant return to one's former office; on this occasion advancement in rank served as the reward.)〉
entries.literal: (According to the Song History, Biography of Li Qian: Under the old system, when one was removed from an external prefecture one returned to one's original office; on this occasion he was promoted in rank as a reward.)〉

entries.zh: 甲申，車駕次韋城。
entries.en: On jiashen the emperor encamped at Weicheng.
entries.literal: On jiashen the imperial carriage halted at Weicheng.

entries.zh: 詔：「河北諸州見禁罪人，自十月五日昧爽以前，常赦所不原者，咸赦除之。」
entries.en: An edict declared: "Among prisoners held in Hebei prefectures as of dawn on the fifth day of the tenth month—including offenses never covered by routine amnesties—all are to be fully pardoned."
entries.literal: An edict proclaimed: 'Among prisoners currently held in the prefectures of Hebei, all those held before dawn on the fifth day of the tenth month—even crimes not pardoned by ordinary amnesties—are hereby fully pardoned and released.'

entries.zh: 壬辰，日有黑子如雞卵。
entries.en: On renchen dark blemishes appeared on the sun, each as large as a hen's egg.
entries.literal: On renchen dark spots appeared on the sun, each the size of a hen's egg.

entries.zh: 丙申，以相州留後王繼宏為相州節度使，加檢校太傅。
entries.en: On bingshen Xiang acting prefect Wang Jihong was appointed military governor of Xiang and made honorary grand tutor.
entries.literal: On bingshen Wang Jihong, acting prefect of Xiang, was made military governor of Xiang and given the additional Honorary Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 至鄴都城下。
entries.en: The army arrived beneath the walls of Ye.
entries.literal: They reached below the walls of the Ye capital.

entries.zh: 丙午，詔都部署高行周督眾攻城，帝登高阜以觀之，時眾議未欲攻擊，副部署慕容彥超堅請攻之。
entries.en: On bingwu an edict put Grand Marshal Gao Xingzhou in charge of the siege; the emperor watched from a hilltop while his commanders still debated holding back—until Deputy Marshal Murong Yanchao pressed hard for an attack.
entries.literal: On bingwu an edict ordered Grand Marshal Gao Xingzhou to oversee the mass assault on the city; the Emperor climbed a high mound to watch. At the time the consensus was against attacking, but Deputy Marshal Murong Yanchao insistently urged an assault.

entries.zh: 是日，王師傷夷者萬餘人，不克而退。
entries.en: That day the imperial forces lost more than ten thousand men, failed to breach the city, and fell back.
entries.literal: That day the imperial army suffered more than ten thousand casualties and failed to take the city, then withdrew.

entries.zh: 十二月辛巳朔，以護聖左廂都指揮使、岳州防禦使李洪信為遂州節度使，充侍衛步軍都指揮使；
entries.en: On the new moon of the twelfth month, left-wing imperial guard commander and Yue defense commissioner Li Hongxin was made Sui governor and concurrent palace foot-guard commander;
entries.literal: On the first day (xinsi) of the twelfth month, Li Hongxin, Left Wing overall commander of the Imperial Guard and defense commissioner of Yue, was made military governor of Sui and concurrently overall commander of the palace foot guards;

entries.zh: 以護聖右廂都指揮使、永州防禦使尚洪遷為夔州節度使，充侍衛步軍都指揮使。
entries.en: Right-wing imperial guard commander and Yong defense commissioner Shang Hongqian was made Kui governor and concurrent palace foot-guard commander.
entries.literal: Shang Hongqian, Right Wing overall commander of the Imperial Guard and defense commissioner of Yong, was made military governor of Kui and concurrently overall commander of the palace foot guards.

entries.zh: 丙戌，車駕發鄴都歸京。
entries.en: On bingxu the emperor left Yedu and returned to the capital.
entries.literal: On bingxu the imperial carriage departed Yedu and returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 癸巳，至自鄴都。
entries.en: On guisi he returned from Yedu.
entries.literal: On guisi he returned from Yedu.

entries.zh: 甲午，以皇子開封尹承訓薨。
entries.en: On jiawu imperial prince Chengxun, Kaifeng prefect, died.
entries.literal: On jiawu the imperial prince Chengxun, Kaifeng prefect, died.

entries.zh: 廢朝三日，追封魏王。
entries.en: Court was closed for three days, and he was posthumously created Prince of Wei.
entries.literal: Court audiences were suspended for three days; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.

entries.zh: 丁酉，帝舉哀於太平宮。
entries.en: On dingyou the emperor mourned at Taiping Palace.
entries.literal: On dingyou the Emperor held mourning rites at Taiping Palace.

entries.zh: 庚子，司徒李鏻薨。
entries.en: On gengzi minister of education Li Lin died.
entries.literal: On gengzi Minister of Education Li Lin died.

entries.zh: 辛丑，以前鄜州節度使郭謹為滑州節度使，加檢校太尉。
entries.en: On xinchou former Fu governor Guo Jin was appointed Hua governor and promoted to honorary Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: On xinchou Guo Jin, former military governor of Fu, was made military governor of Hua and given the additional Honorary Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 戊申，宿州奏，部民餓死者八百六十有七人。
entries.en: On wushen Suzhou reported that 867 local commoners had died of starvation.
entries.literal: On wushen Suzhou memorialized that among the local populace eight hundred sixty-seven had died of starvation.

entries.zh: 乾祐元年正月辛亥朔，帝不受朝賀。
entries.en: On the new moon of the first month in the first year of Qianyou, the emperor declined the usual court congratulations.
entries.literal: On the first day (xinhai) of the first month in the first year of Qianyou, the Emperor did not receive court congratulations.

entries.zh: 乙卯，制：「大赦天下，改天福十三年為乾祐元年。
entries.en: On yimao a decree proclaimed: "A general amnesty is granted throughout the realm, and the thirteenth year of Tianfu is changed to the first year of Qianyou.
entries.literal: On yimao a decree proclaimed: 'A general amnesty is granted throughout the realm, and the thirteenth year of Tianfu is changed to the first year of Qianyou.

entries.zh: 自正月五日昧爽已前，犯罪人除十惡五逆外，罪無輕重，咸赦除之。」
entries.en: All crimes committed before dawn on the fifth day of the first month—save the ten abominations and five capital offenses, regardless of severity—were to be wholly pardoned.'
entries.literal: For all offenders before dawn on the fifth day of the first month, save the ten abominations and five capital crimes, crimes great and small alike are fully pardoned and released.'

entries.zh: 己未，改御名為暠。
entries.en: On jiwei the emperor's personal name was changed to Gao.
entries.literal: On jiwei the imperial given name was changed to Gao.

entries.zh: 辛酉，詔：「諸道行軍副使、兩使判官並不得奏薦。
entries.en: On xinyou an edict ruled: "Army march deputy commissioners and judicial officers of the two commissions may no longer submit recommendations by memorial.
entries.literal: On xinyou an edict proclaimed: 'Army march deputy commissioners and judicial officers of the two commissions may not submit memorial recommendations.

entries.zh: 帶使相節度使許奏掌書記、支使、節度推官；
entries.en: Governors who also held commissioner grand councillor rank might recommend chief secretaries, staff officers, and military-law examiners;
entries.literal: Military governors holding commissioner grand councillor status may recommend chief secretaries, staff officers, and military-law examiners;

entries.zh: 不帶使相節度使，許奏掌書記、節度推官。
entries.en: Governors without that rank might recommend chief secretaries and military-law examiners.
entries.literal: Military governors without commissioner grand councillor status may recommend chief secretaries and military-law examiners.

entries.zh: 其防禦團練判官、軍事判官等聽奏。
entries.en: Judicial officers of defense and training commissions, military judicial officers, and the like remained free to submit recommendations.
entries.literal: Defense and training commissioner judicial officers, military judicial officers, and the like may submit recommendations.

entries.zh: 所薦州縣官，帶使相節度使許薦三人；
entries.en: For prefecture and county posts, governors with commissioner grand councillor rank might recommend three men;
entries.literal: For recommending prefecture and county officials, military governors with commissioner grand councillor status may recommend three persons;

entries.zh: 不帶使相二人；
entries.en: those without it, two;
entries.literal: those without commissioner status, two;

entries.zh: 防禦、團練、刺史一人」云。
entries.en: defense commissioners, training commissioners, and prefects, one each,' the edict concluded.
entries.literal: defense commissioners, training commissioners, and prefects, one each,' it stated.

entries.zh: 以前鄧州節度使、燕國公馮道為守太師，進封齊國公。
entries.en: Feng Dao, former Deng governor and Duke of Yan, was made acting grand preceptor and elevated to Duke of Qi.
entries.literal: Feng Dao, former military governor of Deng and Duke of Yan, was made Acting Grand Preceptor and advanced to Duke of Qi.

entries.zh: 甲子，帝不豫。
entries.en: On jiazi the emperor fell ill.
entries.literal: On jiazi the Emperor was unwell.

entries.zh: 庚午，以前宗正卿石光贊為太子賓客，以太僕卿趙上交為秘書監。
entries.en: On gengwu Shi Guangzan, former director of the imperial clan court, became mentor to the heir apparent, and Zhao Shangjiao, director of the imperial stud, was appointed director of the secretariat library.
entries.literal: On gengwu Shi Guangzan, former Director of the Imperial Clan Court, was made Mentor to the Heir Apparent, and Zhao Shangjiao, Director of the Imperial Stud, was made Director of the Secretariat Library.

entries.zh: 丁丑，故尚書左丞韓祚贈司徒。
entries.en: On dingchou the late left vice director Han Zuo was posthumously honored as minister of works.
entries.literal: On dingchou the late Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Han Zuo was posthumously given Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 二十七日丁丑，帝崩於萬歲殿，時年五十四。
entries.en: On the twenty-seventh day, dingchou, the emperor died in Wansui Hall. He was fifty-four.
entries.literal: On the twenty-seventh day, dingchou, the Emperor died in Wansui Hall at the age of fifty-four.

entries.zh: 秘不發喪。
entries.en: The court kept his death secret and did not yet proclaim mourning.
entries.literal: The death was kept secret and no mourning was proclaimed.

entries.zh: 庚辰，太傅杜重威伏誅。
entries.en: On gengchen Grand Tutor Du Chongwei was put to death.
entries.literal: On gengchen Grand Tutor Du Chongwei was executed.

entries.zh: 〈（《契丹國志》云：漢祖召蘇逢吉、楊邠、史宏肇入受顧命，曰：「承祐幼弱，後事托在卿輩。」
entries.en: (The Records of the Khitan State relate that the Han founder summoned Su Fengji, Yang Bin, and Shi Hongzhao to receive his deathbed charge, saying, "Chengyou is still a child; I entrust what follows to you."
entries.literal: (According to the Records of the Khitan State: The Han Founder summoned Su Fengji, Yang Bin, and Shi Hongzhao to receive his final testament, saying: 'Chengyou is young and weak; the affairs that follow I entrust to you.'

entries.zh: 又曰：「善防杜重威。」
entries.en: He added, "Guard yourselves against Du Chongwei."
entries.literal: He also said: 'Guard carefully against Du Chongwei.'

entries.zh: 是日殂。
entries.en: That same day he expired.
entries.literal: That same day he died.

entries.zh: 逢吉等秘不發喪，下詔稱：「重威父子，因朕小疾，謗議搖眾，皆斬之。」
entries.en: Fengji and his colleagues concealed the death and issued an edict in the emperor's name: "Du Chongwei and his son, exploiting my minor illness, spread slander and unsettled the people—both shall be executed."
entries.literal: Fengji and the others kept the death secret and issued an edict declaring: 'Du Chongwei, father and son, taking advantage of my slight illness, slandered and stirred the multitude—all are to be beheaded.'

entries.zh: 磔死於市，市人爭啖其肉。）〉
entries.en: They were torn apart and executed in the market; townspeople fought over their flesh.)〉
entries.literal: They were dismembered and put to death in the marketplace; townspeople vied to eat their flesh.)〉

entries.zh: 二月辛巳朔，內降遺制，皇子周王承祐可於柩前即皇帝位。
entries.en: On the new moon of the second month a testamentary edict issued from within the palace: Imperial Prince Zhou Wang Chengyou was to ascend the throne immediately before the coffin.
entries.literal: On the first day (xinsi) of the second month an edict was issued from within proclaiming the testamentary ordinance: Imperial Prince Zhou Wang Chengyou may immediately ascend the throne before the coffin.

entries.zh: 是日發哀。
entries.en: That day the court publicly proclaimed the mourning.
entries.literal: That day mourning was proclaimed.

entries.zh: 其年二月，太常卿張昭上謚曰睿文聖武昭肅孝皇帝，廟號高祖。
entries.en: Later that second month, Minister of Rites Zhang Zhao proposed the posthumous title Sagaciously Cultured, Sacredly Martial, Solemnly Reverent, and Filially Devoted Emperor, with the temple name Gaozu.
entries.literal: In the second month of that year, Minister of Rites Zhang Zhao submitted a posthumous title: Sagaciously Cultured, Sacredly Martial, Solemnly Reverent, and Filially Devoted Emperor; temple name Gaozu.

entries.zh: 十一月壬申，葬於睿陵，宰臣蘇禹珪撰謚冊、哀冊文雲。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, on renshen, he was buried at Ruiling; Chief Minister Su Yugui wrote the texts for the posthumous-title scroll and the lamentation scroll.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month on renshen he was buried at Ruiling; Chief Minister Su Yugui composed the eulogy scroll and lamentation scroll texts.

entries.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：高祖嘗在晉祖麾下，晉祖既起太原，因高祖遂有天下。
entries.en: (The Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties records that Gaozu had once served under Jin Gaozu; when the Jin founder rose at Taiyuan, it was through Gaozu that the house came to rule the realm.
entries.literal: (According to the Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Gaozu once served under Emperor Gaozu of Jin; when the Jin founder rose at Taiyuan, it was through Gaozu that he thereafter possessed the realm.

entries.zh: 先是，豫章有僧號上藍者，精於術數，自唐末著讖云：「石榴花發石榴開。」
entries.en: Earlier, at Yuzhang, a monk called Shanglan, skilled in divination, had composed a prophecy in late Tang times: "When the pomegranate blooms, the pomegranate opens."
entries.literal: Earlier, in Yuzhang there was a monk called Shanglan skilled in numerology who from the late Tang composed a prophecy saying: 'When the pomegranate flowers, the pomegranate opens.'

entries.zh: 議者以「石榴」則晉、漢之謂也，再言「石榴」者，明享祚俱不過二世矣。）〉
entries.en: Commentators read "pomegranate" as a reference to Jin and Han; the doubled "pomegranate" showed that both dynasties would rule for no more than two generations.)〉
entries.literal: Commentators took 'pomegranate' to refer to Jin and Han; to speak of 'pomegranate' twice made clear that both would enjoy the throne for no more than two generations.)〉

entries.zh: 史臣曰：在昔皇天降禍，諸夏無君。
entries.en: The historian writes: In former times Heaven sent calamity upon the land, and the Chinese realms were left without a ruler.
entries.literal: The historiographer states: In former times Heaven on High sent down calamity, and the myriad Chinese lands had no ruler.

entries.zh: 漢高祖肇起並、汾，遄臨汴、洛，乘虛而取神器，因亂而有帝圖，雖曰人謀，諒由天啟。
entries.en: Han Gaozu first rose in Bing and Fen, then swiftly advanced on Bian and Luoyang, seized the imperial regalia when the realm lay open, and won his imperial design amid chaos—though men called it human contrivance, it was surely Heaven's opening.
entries.literal: Han Gaozu first rose in Bing and Fen, swiftly came to Bian and Luo, seized the regalia of rule by exploiting a void, and through turmoil obtained the imperial design; though called human planning, surely it was opened by Heaven.

entries.zh: 然帝昔蒞戎藩，素虧物望，洎登宸極，未厭人心，徒矜拯溺之功，莫契來蘇之望。
entries.en: Yet when he had held a military command, he had long lacked public esteem; once enthroned he still failed to win men's hearts, boasting only of rescuing the drowning while never fulfilling the people's hope of renewal.
entries.literal: Yet when the Emperor formerly held a military fief, he had long fallen short of public esteem; when he ascended the imperial throne, he did not satisfy the people's hearts, boasting only the merit of rescuing the drowning while failing to meet the hope of returning life to ease.

entries.zh: 良以急於止殺，不暇崇仁。
entries.en: This was because he was intent on stopping the killing and had no time to cultivate benevolent rule.
entries.literal: Truly he was eager to stop killing and had no leisure to exalt benevolence.

entries.zh: 燕薊降師，既連營而受戮；
entries.en: Troops who had surrendered from Yan and Ji were put to the sword camp after camp;
entries.literal: Surrendered troops of Yan and Ji were slaughtered camp after camp;

entries.zh: 鄴臺叛帥，因閉壘以偷生。
entries.en: while the rebel commander at Ye preserved his life by shutting himself within the fortress.
entries.literal: the rebel commander at Ye, by shutting the fortress, stole his life.

entries.zh: 蓋撫禦以乖方，俾征伐之不息。
entries.en: In the end his methods of pacification and control were misapplied, and warfare never ceased.
entries.literal: In sum, his pacification and control were at odds with the proper method, so that campaigns and attacks never ceased.

entries.zh: 及回鑾輅，尋墮烏號，故雖有應運之名，而未睹為君之德也。
entries.en: When the imperial carriage returned, he soon fell from his horse; thus, though he bore the name of a man who answered his age, the virtue of true kingship was never seen in him.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, he soon fell from the Black-haired Bow; therefore, though he bore the name of one who answered the age, one did not yet see the virtue of a true ruler.

entries.zh: 三月甲寅，帝始禦廣政殿，群臣起居。
entries.en: On jiayin of the third month the emperor held his first audience in the Hall of Broad Governance, and the ministers presented their formal greetings.
entries.literal: On jiayin of the third month, the Emperor for the first time held court in the Hall of Broad Governance, and the assembled ministers performed the ceremony of inquiry after audience.

entries.zh: 殿中少監胡崧上言：「請禁砍伐桑棗為薪，城門所由，專加捉搦。」
entries.en: Hu Song, Junior Supervisor of the Palace, memorialized: "I ask that felling mulberry and jujube trees for fuel be banned, and that gate officers be assigned solely to apprehend offenders."
entries.literal: Hu Song, Junior Supervisor of the Palace, submitted a memorial: "I request that cutting mulberry and jujube trees for firewood be forbidden, and that the gate officers be charged exclusively with apprehending violators."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The request was granted.
entries.literal: The request was granted.

entries.zh: 丙辰，鄴都留守、太尉、中書令、臨清王高行周進封鄴王；
entries.en: On bingchen Gao Xingzhou, Yedu garrison commander, Grand Commandant, Chief Councilor, and Prince of Linqing, was promoted to Prince of Ye;
entries.literal: On bingchen, Gao Xingzhou, Yedu garrison commander, Grand Commandant, Chief Councilor, and Prince of Linqing, was advanced in enfeoffment to Prince of Ye;

entries.zh: 北京留守、檢校太尉、同平章事劉崇加宋州節度使兼侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使、檢校太尉、同平章事史宏肇，並加檢校太師、兼侍中；
entries.en: Liu Chong, Northern Capital garrison commander, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, and Shi Hongzhao, military governor of Songzhou, commander-in-chief of the palace guard cavalry and infantry, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, were both additionally made Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant;
entries.literal: Liu Chong, Northern Capital garrison commander, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, and Shi Hongzhao, military governor of Songzhou, overall commander of the palace guard cavalry and infantry, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, were both additionally made Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant;

entries.zh: 前邢州節度使安叔千以太子太師致仕。
entries.en: An Shuqian, former military governor of Xingzhou, retired with the title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: An Shuqian, former military governor of Xingzhou, retired with the title of Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 戊午，以右諫議大夫於德辰為兵部侍郎。
entries.en: On wuwu Yu Dechen, Right Remonstrating Censor, was appointed Vice Minister of War.
entries.literal: On wuwu, Yu Dechen, Right Remonstrating Censor, was made Vice Minister of War.

entries.zh: 庚申，河中節度使、檢校太師、兼中書令李守貞加守太傅，進封魯國公；
entries.en: On gengshen Li Shouzhen, military governor of Hezhong, Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Chief Councilor, was made Acting Grand Tutor and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu;
entries.literal: On gengshen, Li Shouzhen, military governor of Hezhong, Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Chief Councilor, was made Acting Grand Tutor and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Lu;

entries.zh: 襄州節度使、檢校太師、兼中書令、虢國公安審琦加守太保，進封齊國公；
entries.en: An Shenqi, military governor of Xiangzhou, Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Chief Councilor, and Duke of Guo, was made Acting Grand Guardian and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi;
entries.literal: An Shenqi, military governor of Xiangzhou, Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Chief Councilor, and Duke of Guo, was made Acting Grand Guardian and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Qi;

entries.zh: 兗州節度使、檢校太師、兼侍中、岐國公符彥卿加兼中書令，進封魏國公；
entries.en: Fu Yanqing, military governor of Yanzhou, Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and Duke of Qi of Fengxiang, was also made Concurrent Chief Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei;
entries.literal: Fu Yanqing, military governor of Yanzhou, Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and Duke of Qi of Fengxiang, was additionally made Concurrent Chief Councilor and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Wei;

entries.zh: 許州節度使兼侍衛親軍副都指揮使、檢校太尉、同平章事劉信加檢校太師。
entries.en: Liu Xin, military governor of Xu Prefecture, deputy commander of the palace guard, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Liu Xin, military governor of Xu Prefecture, deputy overall commander of the palace guard, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was made Acting Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 壬戌，以宰臣竇貞固為山陵使，吏部侍郎段希堯為副使，太常卿張昭為禮儀使，兵部侍郎盧價為鹵簿使，御史中丞邊蔚為儀仗使。
entries.en: On renxu chief minister Dou Zhengu was appointed commissioner for the imperial tomb; Duan Xiyao, Vice Minister of Personnel, deputy commissioner; Zhang Zhao, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, commissioner of rites; Lu Jia, Vice Minister of War, commissioner of the guard of honor; and Bian Wei, Censor-in-Chief, commissioner of ceremonial regalia.
entries.literal: On renxu, the chief minister Dou Zhengu was made commissioner for the imperial tomb; Duan Xiyao, Vice Minister of Personnel, was made deputy commissioner; Zhang Zhao, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made commissioner of rites; Lu Jia, Vice Minister of War, was made commissioner of the imperial guard of honor; Bian Wei, Censor-in-Chief, was made commissioner of ceremonial regalia.

entries.zh: 丙寅，以前鳳翔節度使兼西南面兵馬都部署、檢校太師、兼侍中侯益為開封尹、加兼中書令；
entries.en: On bingyin Hou Yi, former military governor of Fengxiang and overall commander of southwestern forces, Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant, was made Prefect of Kaifeng and additionally Concurrent Chief Councilor;
entries.literal: On bingyin, Hou Yi, former military governor of Fengxiang and overall commander of southwestern forces, Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant, was made Prefect of Kaifeng and additionally Concurrent Chief Councilor;

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·侯益傳》：益率數十騎奔入朝，隱帝遣侍臣問益連結蜀軍之由，益對曰：「臣欲誘之出關，掩殺之耳。」
entries.en: (From the Biography of Hou Yi in the History of Song: Yi fled to court at the head of several dozen horsemen. Emperor Yin sent a palace attendant to ask why he had linked up with Shu forces. Yi answered: "I meant to lure them out of the pass and destroy them in an ambush."
entries.literal: (From the Biography of Hou Yi in the History of Song: Yi led several dozen horsemen in flight to court. Emperor Yin sent a palace attendant to ask Yi the reason for his collusion with the Shu army. Yi replied: "Your subject wished to lure them out of the pass and then ambush and destroy them."

entries.zh: 隱帝笑之。
entries.en: The emperor laughed at this.
entries.literal: Emperor Yin laughed at this.

entries.zh: 益厚賂史宏肇輩，言王景崇之橫恣，諸權貴深庇護之，乃授以開封尹、兼中書令。）〉
entries.en: Yi lavished gifts on Shi Hongzhao and his allies, accusing Wang Jingchong of arrogance and abuse while the powerful protected him; only then was Yi given the posts of Prefect of Kaifeng and Concurrent Chief Councilor.)〉
entries.literal: Yi lavished bribes on Shi Hongzhao and his circle, alleging Wang Jingchong's arrogance and tyranny, while the powerful deeply sheltered him; only then was Yi granted Prefect of Kaifeng and Concurrent Chief Councilor.)〉

entries.zh: 西京留守、檢校太師、平章事、莒國公李從敏，夏州節度使、檢校太師、同平章事李彜殷，並加兼侍中；
entries.en: Li Congmin, Western Capital garrison commander, Acting Grand Preceptor, Councilor of the Second Rank, and Duke of Ju, and Li Yiyin, military governor of Xiazhou, Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, were both additionally made Concurrent Palace Attendant;
entries.literal: Li Congmin, Western Capital garrison commander, Acting Grand Preceptor, Councilor of the Second Rank, and Duke of Ju, and Li Yiyin, military governor of Xiazhou, Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, were both additionally made Concurrent Palace Attendant;

entries.zh: 青州節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事劉銖，鄆州節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事慕容彥超，並加檢校太師。
entries.en: Liu Zhu of Qingzhou and Murong Yanchao of Yunzhou, each Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, were both promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Liu Zhu, military governor of Qingzhou, Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, and Murong Yanchao, military governor of Yunzhou, Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, were both made Acting Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 詔改廣晉府為大名府，晉昌軍為承興軍。
entries.en: An edict renamed Guangjin Prefecture to Daming Prefecture and Jinchang Circuit to Chengxing Circuit.
entries.literal: An edict changed Guangjin Prefecture to Daming Prefecture and Jinchang Circuit to Chengxing Circuit.

entries.zh: 戊辰，靈州節度使、檢校太師、同平章事馮暉加兼侍中；
entries.en: On wuchen Feng Hui, military governor of Lingzhou, Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was additionally made Concurrent Palace Attendant;
entries.literal: On wuchen, Feng Hui, military governor of Lingzhou, Acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was additionally made Concurrent Palace Attendant;

entries.zh: 河陽節度使武行德、滄州節度使王景、華州節度使侯章、晉州節度使王晏，並依前檢校太尉，加同平章事。
entries.en: Wu Xingde of Heyang, Wang Jing of Cangzhou, Hou Zhang of Huazhou, and Wang Yan of Jinzhou each retained the rank of Acting Grand Commandant and was made Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank.
entries.literal: Wu Xingde, military governor of Heyang; Wang Jing of Cangzhou; Hou Zhang of Huazhou; and Wang Yan of Jinzhou—all retained their former rank of Acting Grand Commandant and were made Concurrent Councilors of the Second Rank.

entries.zh: 庚午，涇州節度使史懿、潞州節度使常思、同州節度使張彥威、延州節度使高允權，並依前檢校太尉，加同平章事；
entries.en: On gengwu Shi Yi of Jingzhou, Chang Si of Luzhou, Zhang Yanwei of Tongzhou, and Gao Yunquan of Yanzhou each retained Acting Grand Commandant and was made Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank;
entries.literal: On gengwu, Shi Yi of Jingzhou, Chang Si of Luzhou, Zhang Yanwei of Tongzhou, and Gao Yunquan of Yanzhou—all retained their former rank of Acting Grand Commandant and were made Concurrent Councilors of the Second Rank;

entries.zh: 澶州節度使郭從義、邢州節度使薛懷讓，並自檢校太傅加檢校太尉；
entries.en: Guo Congyi of Chanzhou and Xue Huairang of Xingzhou were each promoted from Acting Grand Tutor to Acting Grand Commandant;
entries.literal: Guo Congyi, military governor of Chanzhou, and Xue Huairang of Xingzhou were both advanced from Acting Grand Tutor to Acting Grand Commandant;

entries.zh: 以前奉國右廂都指揮使王饒為鄜州留後。
entries.en: Wang Rao, former commander of the right wing of the Fengguo Army, was appointed acting governor of Fuzhou.
entries.literal: Wang Rao, former overall commander of the right wing of the Fengguo Army, was made acting governor of Fuzhou.

entries.zh: 甲戌，以邠州節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事王守恩為永興軍節度使，加檢校太師；
entries.en: On jiaxu Wang Shou'en, military governor of Binzhou, Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was transferred to military governor of the Yongxing Army and promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor;
entries.literal: On jiaxu, Wang Shou'en, military governor of Binzhou, Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was made military governor of the Yongxing Army and additionally Acting Grand Preceptor;

entries.zh: 以滑州節度使、檢校太尉郭謹為邠州節度使；
entries.en: Guo Jin, military governor of Hua Prefecture and Acting Grand Commandant, was made military governor of Binzhou;
entries.literal: Guo Jin, military governor of Hua Prefecture and Acting Grand Commandant, was made military governor of Binzhou;

entries.zh: 以前鎮州留後、檢校太傅白再榮為滑州節度使，加檢校太尉；
entries.en: Bai Zairong, former acting governor of Zhenzhou and Acting Grand Tutor, was appointed military governor of Hua Prefecture with the additional rank of Acting Grand Commandant;
entries.literal: Bai Zairong, former acting governor of Zhenzhou and Acting Grand Tutor, was made military governor of Hua Prefecture and additionally Acting Grand Commandant;

entries.zh: 以陜州節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事趙暉為鳳翔節度使；
entries.en: Zhao Hui, military governor of Shanzhou, Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was transferred to military governor of Fengxiang;
entries.literal: Zhao Hui, military governor of Shanzhou, Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was made military governor of Fengxiang;

entries.zh: 以前河中節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事白文珂為陜州節度使。
entries.en: Bai Wenke, former military governor of Hezhong, Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was appointed military governor of Shanzhou.
entries.literal: Bai Wenke, former military governor of Hezhong, Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank, was made military governor of Shanzhou.

entries.zh: 殿中監任延皓配流鄜州，坐為劉崇所奏故也。
entries.en: Ren Yanhao, Director of the Palace, was exiled to Fuzhou because Liu Chong had impeached him.
entries.literal: Ren Yanhao, Director of the Palace, was sentenced to penal exile in Fuzhou on account of having been impeached by Liu Chong.

entries.zh: 丙子，鄧州節度使劉重進、相州節度使王繼宏、安州節度使楊信，並自檢校太傅加檢校太尉；
entries.en: On bingzi Liu Zhongjin of Dengzhou, Wang Jihong of Xiangzhou, and Yang Xin of Anzhou were each promoted from Acting Grand Tutor to Acting Grand Commandant;
entries.literal: On bingzi, Liu Zhongjin of Dengzhou, Wang Jihong of Xiangzhou, and Yang Xin of Anzhou were all advanced from Acting Grand Tutor to Acting Grand Commandant;

entries.zh: 以鎮州留後兼幽州一行馬步軍都部署、檢校太傅劉在明為鎮州節度使，加檢校太師，部署如故；
entries.en: Liu Zaiming, acting governor of Zhenzhou and overall commander of Youzhou's horse and foot forces, Acting Grand Tutor, was made military governor of Zhenzhou and Acting Grand Preceptor while retaining his deployment command;
entries.literal: Liu Zaiming, acting governor of Zhenzhou, overall commander of the cavalry and infantry of the Youzhou command, and Acting Grand Tutor, was made military governor of Zhenzhou and additionally Acting Grand Preceptor, his deployment command remaining as before;

entries.zh: 貝州節度使、檢校太傅李殷加檢校太尉；
entries.en: Li Yin, military governor of Beizhou and Acting Grand Tutor, was promoted to Acting Grand Commandant;
entries.literal: Li Yin, military governor of Beizhou and Acting Grand Tutor, was made Acting Grand Commandant;

entries.zh: 定州節度使、檢校太尉孫方簡，府州節度使、檢校太傅折從阮，並加檢校太師。
entries.en: Sun Fangjian of Dingzhou, Acting Grand Commandant, and Zhe Congruan of Fuzhou, Acting Grand Tutor, were both promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Sun Fangjian, military governor of Dingzhou and Acting Grand Commandant, and Zhe Congruan, military governor of Fuzhou and Acting Grand Tutor, were both made Acting Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 丁丑，中書侍郎兼戶部尚書、平章事李濤罷免，勒歸私第。
entries.en: On dingchou Li Tao, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Concurrent Minister of Revenue, and Councilor of the Second Rank, was dismissed and sent home.
entries.literal: On dingchou, Li Tao, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Concurrent Minister of Revenue, and Councilor of the Second Rank, was dismissed and ordered to return to his private residence.

entries.zh: 時蘇逢吉等在中書，樞密使楊邠、副樞密使郭威等，權勢甚盛，中書每有除授，多為邠等所抑。
entries.en: At this time Su Fengji and his colleagues held the Secretariat, while Military Affairs Commissioner Yang Bin, Deputy Commissioner Guo Wei, and others wielded great power; many Secretariat appointments were blocked by Bin's faction.
entries.literal: At this time Su Fengji and others were in the Secretariat, while Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Yang Bin, Deputy Commissioner Guo Wei, and others held very great power; whenever the Secretariat had appointments to make, they were often blocked by Bin and his associates.

entries.zh: 濤不平之，因上疏請出邠等，以藩鎮授之，樞密之務，宜委逢吉、禹珪。
entries.en: Tao resented this imbalance and memorialized that Bin and his allies be sent out to frontier commands while Military Affairs affairs be entrusted to Fengji and Yugui.
entries.literal: Tao was resentful of this and therefore submitted a memorial requesting that Bin and the others be sent out and granted frontier commands, and that the affairs of the Bureau of Military Affairs be entrusted to Fengji and Yugui.

entries.zh: 疏入，邠等知之，乃見太后泣訴其事，太后怒，濤由是獲譴。
entries.en: When the memorial arrived, Bin and his allies learned of it and went weeping before the Empress Dowager to plead their case. She grew angry, and Tao was punished as a result.
entries.literal: When the memorial entered, Bin and the others learned of it and then went before the Empress Dowager weeping and pleading their case. The Empress Dowager was angry, and Tao thereby received punishment.

entries.zh: 先是，中書廚釜鳴者數四，未幾，濤罷免。
entries.en: Earlier the cauldrons in the Secretariat kitchen had rung several times; not long afterward Tao was dismissed.
entries.literal: Earlier, the cauldrons in the Secretariat kitchen had rung several times; before long, Tao was dismissed.

entries.zh: 西道諸州奏，河中李守貞謀叛，發兵據潼關。
entries.en: Memorials from the western circuits reported that Li Shouzhen of Hezhong was plotting rebellion and had sent troops to seize Tong Pass.
entries.literal: The western circuits memorialized that Li Shouzhen of Hezhong was plotting rebellion and had raised troops to seize Tong Pass.

entries.zh: 夏四月辛巳，陜州兵馬監押王玉奏，收復潼關。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on xinsi, Wang Yu, military supervisor of Shanzhou, reported the recovery of Tong Pass.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinsi, Wang Yu, military supervisor of Shanzhou, memorialized that Tong Pass had been recovered.

entries.zh: 定州孫方簡奏，三月二十七日，契丹棄定州遁去。
entries.en: Sun Fangjian of Dingzhou reported that on the twenty-seventh day of the third month the Khitan abandoned Dingzhou and withdrew.
entries.literal: Sun Fangjian of Dingzhou memorialized that on the twenty-seventh day of the third month the Khitan abandoned Dingzhou and fled.

entries.zh: 壬午，以樞密使楊邠為中書侍郎兼吏部尚書、平章事，使如故；
entries.en: On renwu Yang Bin, Military Affairs Commissioner, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, Concurrent Minister of Personnel, and Councilor of the Second Rank while retaining his commission;
entries.literal: On renwu, Yang Bin, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, Concurrent Minister of Personnel, and Councilor of the Second Rank, his commission remaining as before;

entries.zh: 以副樞密使郭威為樞密使，加檢校太尉；
entries.en: Guo Wei, Deputy Commissioner, was promoted to Commissioner with the additional rank of Acting Grand Commandant;
entries.literal: Guo Wei, Deputy Commissioner, was made Commissioner and additionally Acting Grand Commandant;

entries.zh: 三司使王章加檢校太尉、同平章事。
entries.en: Wang Zhang, Commissioner of the Three Departments, was made Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank.
entries.literal: Wang Zhang, Commissioner of the Three Departments, was made Acting Grand Commandant and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank.

entries.zh: 郢州刺史尹實奏，荊南起兵在境上，欲攻城。
entries.en: Yin Shi, prefect of Yingzhou, reported that Jingnan had mobilized troops on the border and intended to attack his city.
entries.literal: Yin Shi, prefect of Yingzhou, memorialized that Jingnan had raised troops on the border and intended to attack the city.

entries.zh: 是日，以澶州節度使郭從義為永興軍一行兵馬都部署。
entries.en: That same day Guo Congyi, military governor of Chanzhou, was appointed overall commander of the Yongxing Army's horse and foot forces.
entries.literal: That day, Guo Congyi, military governor of Chanzhou, was made overall commander of the cavalry and infantry of the Yongxing Army command.

entries.zh: 時供奉官時知化、王益，自鳳翔部署前永興節度使趙贊部下牙兵趙思綰等三百餘人赴闕，三月二十四日，行次永興，思綰等作亂，突入府城，據城以叛，故命從義帥師以討之。
entries.en: At this time palace attendants Shi Zhihua and Wang Yi were escorting more than three hundred troops formerly under Zhao Zan, ex-governor of Yongxing in the Fengxiang command, including Zhao Sixuan, to court. On the twenty-fourth day of the third month, passing through Yongxing, Sixuan and his men mutinied, stormed the prefectural seat, and seized the city in rebellion; Congyi was therefore ordered to lead an expedition against them.
entries.literal: At this time the palace attendants Shi Zhihua and Wang Yi, escorting more than three hundred men-at-arms under Zhao Zan, former military governor of Yongxing in the Fengxiang deployment—including Zhao Sixuan—were proceeding to court. On the twenty-fourth day of the third month, while passing through Yongxing, Sixuan and the others mutinied, burst into the prefectural city, seized the city in rebellion, and therefore Congyi was ordered to lead troops to suppress them.

entries.zh: 甲申，王景崇奏，趙思綰叛，見起兵攻討。
entries.en: On jiashen Wang Jingchong reported that Zhao Sixuan had rebelled and that he had already mobilized forces to attack him.
entries.literal: On jiashen, Wang Jingchong memorialized that Zhao Sixuan had rebelled and that he had already raised troops to attack and suppress him.

entries.zh: 丁亥，幸道宮、佛寺禱雨。
entries.en: On dinghai the emperor visited Daoist temples and Buddhist monasteries to pray for rain.
entries.literal: On dinghai, the Emperor visited Daoist temples and Buddhist monasteries to pray for rain.

entries.zh: 戊子，東南面兵馬都元帥、兩浙節度使、檢校太師、兼中書令、吳越國王錢宏倧加諸道兵馬都元帥，天策上將軍、湖南節度使、檢校太師、兼中書令、楚王馬希廣加守中書令，以陜州節度使白文珂為河中府城下一行都部署。
entries.en: On wuzi Qian Hongzong, Grand Marshal of the southeast, military governor of the Two Zhes, Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Chief Councilor, and King of Wuyue, was additionally made Grand Marshal of all circuits; Ma Xiguang, General-in-Chief of the Heavenly Strategy, military governor of Hunan, Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Chief Councilor, and Prince of Chu, was made Acting Chief Councilor; and Bai Wenke, military governor of Shanzhou, was appointed overall commander of the forces besieging Hezhong.
entries.literal: On wuzi, Qian Hongzong, Grand Marshal of the southeastern forces, military governor of the Two Zhes, Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Chief Councilor, and King of Wuyue, was additionally made Grand Marshal of all circuits; Ma Xiguang, General-in-Chief of the Heavenly Strategy, military governor of Hunan, Acting Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Chief Councilor, and Prince of Chu, was made Acting Chief Councilor; Bai Wenke, military governor of Shanzhou, was made overall commander of the forces below the walls of Hezhong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 庚寅，宰臣竇貞固、蘇逢吉、蘇禹珪並進封開國公。
entries.en: On gengyin chief ministers Dou Zhengu, Su Fengji, and Su Yugui were all enfeoffed as Dukes Who Founded the State.
entries.literal: On gengyin, the chief ministers Dou Zhengu, Su Fengji, and Su Yugui were all advanced in enfeoffment to Dukes Who Founded the State.

entries.zh: 辛卯，削奪李守貞在身官爵。
entries.en: On xinmao Li Shouzhen was stripped of all current offices and titles.
entries.literal: On xinmao, Li Shouzhen's current offices and titles were stripped.

entries.zh: 甲午，以翰林學士承旨、戶部侍郎王仁裕為戶部尚書，以翰林學士、左散騎常侍張沆為工部尚書，以翰林學士、中書舍人範質為戶部侍郎，以樞密直學士、尚書比部員外郎王度為祠部郎中，並依前充職。
entries.en: On jiawu Wang Renyu, chief Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Revenue, became Minister of Revenue; Zhang Hong, Hanlin academician and Left Regular Attendant, Minister of Works; Fan Zhi, Hanlin academician and Secretariat Drafter, Vice Minister of Revenue; and Wang Du, direct academician of Military Affairs and outer vice director of the Revenue Scrutiny Bureau, Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices—all while retaining their existing duties.
entries.literal: On jiawu, Wang Renyu, Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy and Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Minister of Revenue; Zhang Hong, Academician and Left Regular Attendant, was made Minister of Works; Fan Zhi, Academician and Secretariat Drafter, was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Wang Du, Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Outer Vice Director of the Revenue Scrutiny Bureau, was made Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices—all continuing in their former duties.

entries.zh: 以侍衛步軍都指揮使尚洪遷充西南面行營都虞候，以客省使王峻為西南面行營兵馬都監。
entries.en: Shang Hongqian, commander of the palace guard infantry, was appointed chief adjutant of the southwestern campaign headquarters, and Wang Jun, commissioner of the Reception Bureau, overall supervisor of its horse and foot forces.
entries.literal: Shang Hongqian, overall commander of the palace guard infantry, was made chief adjutant of the southwestern campaign headquarters; Wang Jun, commissioner of the Reception Bureau, was made overall supervisor of the cavalry and infantry of the southwestern campaign headquarters.

entries.zh: 戊戌，以宣徽南院使扈彥珂為左金吾上將軍。
entries.en: On wuxu Hu Yanke, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was appointed General of the Left Golden Crow.
entries.literal: On wuxu, Hu Yanke, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made General of the Left Golden Crow.

entries.zh: 庚子，以左金吾大將軍、充兩街使、檢校太傅劉承赟為徐州節度使。
entries.en: On gengzi Liu Chengyun, General of the Left Golden Crow, commissioner of the Two Streets, and Acting Grand Tutor, was appointed military governor of Xuzhou.
entries.literal: On gengzi, Liu Chengyun, General of the Left Golden Crow, commissioner of the Two Streets, and Acting Grand Tutor, was made military governor of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 甲辰，以宣徽北院使薛可言為右金吾上將軍，以皇城使李暉為宣徽南院使。
entries.en: On jiachen Xue Keyan, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, became General of the Right Golden Crow, and Li Hui, commissioner of the Imperial City, commissioner of the Southern Bureau.
entries.literal: On jiachen, Xue Keyan, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made General of the Right Golden Crow; Li Hui, commissioner of the Imperial City, was made commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 乙巳，定州節度使孫方簡奏，復入於本州。
entries.en: On yisi Sun Fangjian, military governor of Dingzhou, reported that he had re-entered his prefecture.
entries.literal: On yisi, Sun Fangjian, military governor of Dingzhou, memorialized that he had re-entered his own prefecture.

entries.zh: 初，方簡為狼山寨主，叛晉歸契丹，及契丹降中渡之師，乃以方簡為定州節度使。
entries.en: Earlier Fangjian had been chieftain of Langshan Stockade. He defected from Jin to the Khitan, and when the Khitan surrendered at Zhongdu he was appointed military governor of Dingzhou.
entries.literal: Earlier, Fangjian had been chieftain of Langshan Stockade. He rebelled against Jin and submitted to the Khitan; when the Khitan surrendered the army at Zhongdu, Fangjian was then made military governor of Dingzhou.

entries.zh: 契丹主死，永康王嗣位，即以蕃將耶律忠代之，移方簡為雲州節度使，方簡不受命，遂歸狼山。
entries.en: After the Khitan ruler died, Prince Yongkang succeeded him and replaced Fangjian with the Khitan general Yelü Zhong as military governor of Dingzhou, transferring Fangjian to Yunzhou. Fangjian refused the appointment and returned to Langshan.
entries.literal: When the Khitan ruler died, Prince Yongkang succeeded to the throne and immediately replaced him with the barbarian general Yelü Zhong, transferring Fangjian to military governor of Yunzhou. Fangjian did not accept the order and therefore returned to Langshan.

entries.zh: 高祖至闕，方簡歸款，復以中山命之。
entries.en: When Gaozu reached the capital, Fangjian submitted in allegiance and was again appointed to Zhongshan.
entries.literal: When Gaozu reached the court, Fangjian submitted in allegiance and was again appointed to Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 是歲三月二十七日，契丹棄定州，隳城壁，焚室廬，盡驅人民入蕃，惟余空城瓦礫而已。
entries.en: That year, on the twenty-seventh day of the third month, the Khitan abandoned Dingzhou, demolished the walls, burned the buildings, and drove the entire population into Khitan territory, leaving only an empty ruin of tile and rubble.
entries.literal: That year, on the twenty-seventh day of the third month, the Khitan abandoned Dingzhou, destroyed the walls, burned the houses, and drove all the people into the barbarian lands, leaving only an empty city of tiles and rubble.

entries.zh: 至是，方簡自狼山回保定州。
entries.en: At this point Fangjian returned from Langshan to Dingzhou.
entries.literal: At this time, Fangjian returned from Langshan to Dingzhou.

entries.zh: 是月，河決原武縣，河北諸州旱，徐州餓死民九百三十有七。
entries.en: That month the Yellow River broke through at Yuanwu County, Hebei circuits suffered drought, and in Xuzhou 937 commoners died of starvation.
entries.literal: That month the Yellow River burst its banks at Yuanwu County; the prefectures of Hebei suffered drought; in Xuzhou nine hundred thirty-seven commoners died of starvation.

entries.zh: 六月戊寅朔，日有食之。
entries.en: On the first day of the sixth month, wuyin, there was a solar eclipse.
entries.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, wuyin, there was a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 庚辰，以內客省使王峻為宣徽北院使，依前永興城下兵馬都監。
entries.en: On gengchen Wang Jun, commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau, was appointed commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat while continuing as overall supervisor of the forces below the walls of Yongxing.
entries.literal: On gengchen, Wang Jun, commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau, was made commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, continuing as before as overall supervisor of the cavalry and infantry below the walls of Yongxing.

entries.zh: 以冀州牢城指揮使張廷翰為冀州刺史，時廷翰殺本州刺史何行通，自知州事，故有是命。
entries.en: Zhang Tinghan, commander of the Jizhou prison garrison, was appointed prefect of Jizhou after he had killed the incumbent He Xingtong and taken charge of the prefecture himself.
entries.literal: Zhang Tinghan, commander of the Jizhou prison garrison, was made prefect of Jizhou. At this time Tinghan had killed the prefect He Xingtong and had himself assumed prefectural affairs; therefore this appointment was made.

entries.zh: 甲申，以皇弟右衛大將軍承勛為興元節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事，豐州節度使郭勛加檢校太師。
entries.en: On jiashen the emperor's younger brother Chengxun, General of the Right Guard, was appointed military governor of Xingyuan, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank; Guo Xun, military governor of Fengzhou, was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: On jiashen, the emperor's younger brother Chengxun, General of the Right Guard, was made military governor of Xingyuan, Acting Grand Commandant, and Concurrent Councilor of the Second Rank; Guo Xun, military governor of Fengzhou, was made Acting Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 辛卯，永興兵馬都部署郭從義奏，得王景崇報，有兵自隴州來，欲投河中，追襲至鄜城。
entries.en: On xinmao Guo Congyi, overall commander of Yongxing's horse and foot forces, reported that he had received word from Wang Jingchong that troops from Long Prefecture were heading to defect to Hezhong; he pursued and attacked them as far as Fucheng.
entries.literal: On xinmao, Guo Congyi, overall military deployment commissioner of Yongxing, memorialized that he received a report from Wang Jingchong: troops had come from Long Prefecture intending to defect to Hezhong; they were pursued and attacked as far as Fucheng.

entries.zh: 荊南節度使高從誨上表歸命，從誨嘗拒朝命，至是方遣牙將劉扶詣闕請罪。
entries.en: Gao Conghui, military governor of Jingnan, submitted a memorial accepting imperial authority. He had once defied court orders; only now did he send his adjutant Liu Fu to the capital to plead guilty.
entries.literal: Gao Conghui, military governor of Jingnan, submitted a memorial submitting to imperial authority. Conghui had once defied court orders; only now did he dispatch his adjutant general Liu Fu to the capital to plead guilty.

entries.zh: 丙申，鎮州奏，節度使劉在明卒。
entries.en: On bingshen Zhen Prefecture reported that Military Governor Liu Zaiming had died.
