entries.literal: Earlier, the emperor had sent Yan Tuo to spy on where the Yedu army was going; he was captured by roaming scouts. Guo Wei immediately sent him back, thereby ordering him to attach a memorial of his intent to proceed to court, and also placed a secret memorial in Yan Tuo's collar.

entries.zh: 帝覽奏，即召李業示之，聶文進、郭允明在傍，懼形於色。
entries.en: The emperor read it, summoned Li Ye, and Nie Wenjin and Guo Yunming beside him showed their fear.
entries.literal: The emperor viewed the memorial and immediately summoned Li Ye to show it; Nie Wenjin and Guo Yunming were beside him, fear showing on their faces.

entries.zh: 初議車駕幸澶州，及聞鄴兵已至河上，乃止。
entries.en: They had planned an imperial visit to Chanzhou but halted when news came that the Yedu army had reached the Yellow River.
entries.literal: At first they discussed the imperial carriage going to Chanzhou, but on hearing the Yedu army had already reached the river, they stopped.

entries.zh: 帝大懼，私謂宰臣竇貞固等曰：「昨來之事，太草草耳！」
entries.en: Terrified, he told chief minister Dou Zhengu, "Yesterday's business was far too rash!"
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly afraid and privately said to chief minister Dou Zhengu and others: "Yesterday's affair was far too rash!"

entries.zh: 李業等請帝傾府庫以給諸軍，宰相蘇禹珪以為未可。
entries.en: Li Ye urged emptying the treasury for the troops; Su Yugui objected.
entries.literal: Li Ye and others asked the emperor to empty the treasury to pay the armies; chief minister Su Yugui thought it could not be done.

entries.zh: 業拜禹珪於帝前，曰：「相公且為官家，莫惜府庫。」
entries.en: Ye bowed to Yugui before the emperor: "Minister, serve the ruler—spare not the treasury."
entries.literal: Ye bowed to Yugui before the emperor and said: "Minister, think of the ruler—do not be sparing of the treasury."

entries.zh: 遂下令侍衛軍人給二十緡，下軍各給十緡，其北來將士亦準此。
entries.en: Orders followed: twenty strings for palace guards, ten for lower guards, the same for northern troops.
entries.literal: Thereupon orders were issued: palace guard soldiers twenty strings of cash each, lower guard ten strings each, and northern soldiers likewise.

entries.zh: 仍遣北來將士在營子弟各賫家問，向北諭之。
entries.en: Sons and brothers of northern troops in camp were sent family messages to carry north.
entries.literal: Northern soldiers' sons and younger brothers still in camp were also each sent family inquiries to be carried north and announced to them.

entries.zh: 壬午，鄴軍至封丘。
entries.en: On renwu the Yedu army reached Fengqiu.
entries.literal: On day renwu, the Yedu army reached Fengqiu.

entries.zh: 慕容彥超自鎮馳至，帝遂以軍旅之事委之。
entries.en: Murong Yanchao raced from his province and the emperor put the campaign in his hands.
entries.literal: Murong Yanchao hurried from his post; the emperor then entrusted military affairs to him.

entries.zh: 〈（《宋史·侯益傳》云：周太祖起兵，隱帝議出師禦之。
entries.en: (From the History of Song, biography of Hou Yi: when Guo Wei rebelled, Emperor Yin debated marching against him.
entries.literal: (From the biography of Hou Yi in the History of Song: when the Zhou founding ancestor raised troops, Emperor Yin discussed sending an army to resist.

entries.zh: 益獻計曰：「王者無敵於天下，兵不宜輕出，況大名戍卒，家屬盡在京城，不如閉關以挫其銳，遣其母妻發降以招之，可不戰而定。」
entries.en: Yi proposed: "The Son of Heaven has no peer—armies should not march lightly. Daming troops have kin in the capital; close the passes, send their families with surrender appeals, and win without fighting."
entries.literal: Yi presented a plan: "A king is without enemy under Heaven; troops should not lightly go out. Moreover the Daming garrison soldiers all have families in the capital—it is better to close the passes to blunt their edge, send out their mothers and wives with surrender messages to summon them, and they can be settled without battle.

entries.zh: 慕容彥超以為益衰老，作懦夫計，沮之。）〉
entries.en: Murong Yanchao called Yi senile and his plan cowardly, and blocked it.)〉
entries.literal: Murong Yanchao considered Yi old and offering a coward's plan, and obstructed it.)〉

entries.zh: 彥超謂帝曰：「陛下勿憂，臣當生致其魁首。」
entries.en: Yanchao told the emperor, "Do not worry, Majesty—I will take their leader alive."
entries.literal: Yanchao said to the emperor: "Your Majesty need not worry; your subject will capture their leader alive.

entries.zh: 彥超退，見聶文進，詢北來兵數及將校名氏，文進告之。
entries.en: Afterward Yanchao asked Nie Wenjin the northern army's strength and commanders.
entries.literal: Yanchao withdrew and saw Nie Wenjin, inquiring about the numbers of northern troops and the names of commanders; Wenjin told him.

entries.zh: 彥超懼，曰：「大是劇賊，不宜輕耳！」
entries.en: Yanchao grew afraid: "These are fierce enemies—not to be treated lightly!"
entries.literal: Yanchao feared and said: "They are fierce rebels indeed—not to be taken lightly!

entries.zh: 又遣袁鳷、劉重進、王知則等出師，以繼前軍。
entries.en: He sent Yuan Ji, Liu Zhongjin, Wang Zhize, and others to reinforce the vanguard.
entries.literal: He also sent Yuan Ji, Liu Zhongjin, Wang Zhize, and others to take the field to follow the earlier army.

entries.zh: 慕容彥超以大軍駐於七里郊，掘塹以自衛，都下率坊市出酒食以餉軍。
entries.en: Yanchao encamped at Seven-Li, dug trenches, and the city markets supplied food and drink.
entries.literal: Murong Yanchao stationed his great army at the Seven-Li suburb, dug trenches for self-defense, and the capital's wards and markets turned out wine and food to feed the army.

entries.zh: 癸未，車駕勞軍，即日還宮。
entries.en: On guimao the emperor reviewed the troops and returned the same day.
entries.literal: On day guimao, the imperial carriage went to comfort the army and that day returned to the palace.

entries.zh: 翌日，慕容彥超揚言曰：「官家宮中無事，明日再出，觀臣破賊。」
entries.en: Next day Yanchao announced, "The palace is secure; tomorrow the emperor will watch me break the rebels."
entries.literal: The next day Murong Yanchao proclaimed: "All is well in the palace; tomorrow the ruler will come out again to watch your subject break the rebels.

entries.zh: 甲申，車駕復出，幸七里店軍營。
entries.en: On jiashen the emperor again visited the Seven-Li camp.
entries.literal: On day jiashen, the imperial carriage again went out and visited the Seven-Li camp.

entries.zh: 王師陣於劉子陂，與鄴軍相望。
entries.en: Imperial forces formed at Liuzi Slope opposite the Yedu army.
entries.literal: The imperial army formed at Liuzi slope, facing the Yedu army across the distance.

entries.zh: 太后以帝至晚在外，遣中使謂聶文進曰：「賊軍在近，大須用意！」
entries.en: The dowager, worried the emperor was out late, told Nie Wenjin, "The rebels are close—take care!"
entries.literal: The empress dowager, because the emperor was out late, sent a palace envoy to tell Nie Wenjin: "The rebel army is near—you must be very careful!

entries.zh: 文進曰：「有臣在，必不失策，縱有一百個郭威，亦當生擒之耳！」
entries.en: Wenjin replied, "I am here—we cannot fail; even a hundred Guo Weis I would seize alive!"
entries.literal: Wenjin said: "With your subject here, policy will not fail; even a hundred Guo Weis would be captured alive!"

entries.zh: 彥超輕脫，先擊北軍，郭威命何福進、王彥超、李筠等大合騎以乘之。
entries.en: Yanchao rashly attacked the northern wing; Guo Wei sent He Fujin, Wang Yanchao, Li Yun, and others with massed cavalry against him.
entries.literal: Yanchao was rash; he struck the northern army first. Guo Wei ordered He Fujin, Wang Yanchao, Li Yun, and others to mass cavalry and press them.

entries.zh: 彥超退卻，死者百餘人，於是諸軍奪氣，稍稍奔於北軍。
entries.en: Yanchao retreated with a hundred-odd dead; imperial morale collapsed and men drifted to Guo Wei.
entries.literal: Yanchao fell back; more than a hundred died, and then the armies lost heart and gradually ran to the northern army.

entries.zh: 吳虔裕、張彥超等相繼而去，慕容彥超以部下十數騎奔兗州。
entries.en: Wu Qianyu and Zhang Yanchao fled; Murong Yanchao escaped to Yanzhou with a dozen horsemen.
entries.literal: Wu Qianyu, Zhang Yanchao, and others left in succession; Murong Yanchao fled to Yanzhou with a dozen-odd riders of his command.

entries.zh: 是夜，帝與宰臣從官宿於野次，侯益、焦繼勛潛奔鄴軍。
entries.en: That night the emperor camped in the open with his ministers; Hou Yi and Jiao Jixun defected to Guo Wei.
entries.literal: That night the emperor and chief ministers and attendants lodged in the open field; Hou Yi and Jiao Jixun secretly fled to the Yedu army.

entries.zh: 乙酉旦，帝策馬至元化門，劉銖在門上，問帝左右：「兵馬何在？」
entries.en: At dawn on yiyou the emperor rode to Yuanhua Gate; Liu Zhu on the wall asked his escort, "Where is the army?"
entries.literal: At dawn on yiyou the emperor spurred his horse to the Yuanhua Gate; Liu Zhu was on the gate and asked the emperor's attendants: "Where are the troops?"

entries.zh: 乃射左右。
entries.en: Then he shot at the attendants.
entries.literal: Then he shot the attendants.

entries.zh: 帝回，與蘇逢吉、郭允明詣西北村舍，郭允明知事不濟，乃剚刃於帝而崩，時年二十。
entries.en: The emperor turned back with Su Fengji and Guo Yunming to a northwest village; Yunming, seeing all was lost, killed the emperor with his blade. He was twenty.
entries.literal: The emperor turned back and went with Su Fengji and Guo Yunming to a village house northwest of the city; Guo Yunming, knowing affairs could not succeed, drew his blade on the emperor and he perished, aged twenty.

entries.zh: 蘇逢吉、郭允明皆自殺。
entries.en: Su Fengji and Guo Yunming also killed themselves.
entries.literal: Su Fengji and Guo Yunming both killed themselves.

entries.zh: 是日，周太祖自迎春門入，諸軍大掠，煙火四發，翌日至晡方定。
entries.en: That day Guo Wei entered by Yingchun Gate; troops looted until fires burned everywhere and order returned only by the next dusk.
entries.literal: That day the Zhou founding ancestor entered through the Yingchun Gate; the armies plundered greatly, fires blazed on four sides, and only by the next day's dusk was it settled.

entries.zh: 前滑州節度使白再筠為亂兵所害，吏部侍郎張允墜屋而死。
entries.en: Former Huazhou commissioner Bai Zaiyun was killed by mutineers; personnel vice minister Zhang Yun fell from a building and died.
entries.literal: Bai Zaiyun, former Huazhou commissioner, was killed by mutinous soldiers; Vice Minister of Personnel Zhang Yun fell from a house and died.

entries.zh: 周太祖既入京城，命有司遷帝梓宮於太平宮。
entries.en: Once in the capital, Guo Wei ordered the emperor's coffin moved to Taiping Palace.
entries.literal: After the Zhou founding ancestor had entered the capital, he ordered the relevant offices to move the emperor's coffin to the Taiping Palace.

entries.zh: 或曰：「可依魏高貴鄉公故事，以公禮葬之。」
entries.en: Some said, "Follow the Wei noble village lord precedent and bury him with ducal rites."
entries.literal: Someone said: "It may follow the precedent of the noble village lord of Wei and bury him with ducal rites."

entries.zh: 周祖曰：「予顛沛之中，不能護衛至尊，以至於此，若又貶降，人謂我何！」
entries.en: Guo Wei said, "In my wanderings I could not protect the emperor and it came to this—if I demote him too, what will men say of me?"
entries.literal: The Zhou founder said: "In Our wandering distress We could not protect the exalted ruler and it came to this; if We also demote him, what will people say of Us!"

entries.zh: 於是詔擇日舉哀，命前宗正卿劉皞主喪。
entries.en: An edict set a mourning day and named former imperial-clan director Liu Hao to direct the rites.
entries.literal: Thereupon an edict chose a day for mourning and ordered former director of the imperial clan Liu Hao to preside.

entries.zh: 丙戌，太后誥曰：
entries.en: On bingxu the dowager issued a proclamation:
entries.literal: On day bingxu, the empress dowager's proclamation stated:

entries.zh: 高祖皇帝翦亂除兇，變家為國，救生靈於塗炭，創王業於艱難，甫定寰區，遽遺弓劍。
entries.en: Founding emperor Gaozu ended chaos, made the house a state, rescued the people, and built the dynasty in hardship; he had barely settled the realm when he died.
entries.literal: The founding emperor Gaozu cut disorder and removed the violent, changed the family into a state, saved the living from charcoal and fire, and created royal enterprise amid hardship; he had just settled the realm when he suddenly left bow and sword.

entries.zh: 樞密使郭威楊邠、侍衛使史弘肇、三司使王章親承顧命，輔立少君，協力同心，安邦定國。
entries.en: Bureau commissioner Guo Wei, Yang Bin, guard commander Shi Hongzhao, and three-departments commissioner Wang Zhang received the deathbed charge, installed the young ruler, and together stabilized the realm.
entries.literal: Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Guo Wei, Yang Bin, guard commander Shi Hongzhao, and three-departments commissioner Wang Zhang personally received the dying charge, assisted and established the young ruler, and with combined strength pacified the state.

entries.zh: 旋屬四方多事，三叛連衡，吳、蜀內侵，契丹啟釁，烝黎兇懼，宗社阽危。
entries.en: Soon rebellions linked, Wu and Shu invaded, the Khitan raided, and the people and altars trembled.
entries.literal: Soon thereafter the four quarters had many affairs; the three rebellions linked in alliance; Wu and Shu invaded within; the Khitan opened provocation; the people were fierce with fear and the altars were in peril.

entries.zh: 郭威授任專征，提戈進討，躬當矢石，盡掃煙塵，外寇蕩平，中原寧謐。
entries.en: Guo Wei took command, fought in person, swept the field, pacified foreign enemies, and quieted the heartland.
entries.literal: Guo Wei received appointment for a dedicated campaign, raised the spear and advanced, himself met stones and arrows, swept away all dust and smoke, outer enemies were pacified, and the central plains were tranquil.

entries.zh: 復以強敵未殄，邊塞多艱，允賴寶臣，往臨大鄴，疆場有藩籬之固，朝廷寬宵旰之憂。
entries.en: With foes still active he was sent to Yedu to secure the frontier and ease the court's vigilance.
entries.literal: Again, because a strong enemy was not destroyed and the borders had many hardships, reliance was placed on a treasured minister to go to great Yedu; the frontier had the solidity of a fence and the court was eased of night-watch anxiety.

entries.zh: 不謂兇豎連謀，群小得志，密藏鋒刃，竊發殿庭，已殺害其忠良，方奏聞於少主，無辜受戮，有口稱冤。
entries.en: Yet villains conspired, hid blades in the hall, murdered loyal ministers, and lied to the young emperor; innocents were slaughtered and cried injustice.
entries.literal: Who would have thought vicious fellows would link in conspiracy and petty men would gain their wish, secretly hiding blades and stealing to strike in the palace hall—they had already killed loyal ministers and were just then reporting to the young ruler; the innocent received slaughter and had mouths that called it injustice.

entries.zh: 而又潛差使臣，矯賫宣命，謀害樞密使郭威、宣徽使王峻、侍衛步軍都指揮使王殷等。
entries.en: They also sent secret agents with forged orders to kill Guo Wei, Wang Jun, and Wang Yin.
entries.literal: Moreover they secretly sent envoys, falsely bearing imperial orders, plotting to kill bureau commissioner Guo Wei, palace commissioner Wang Jun, and guard foot commander Wang Yin.

entries.zh: 人知無罪，天不助奸。
entries.en: Men knew they were guiltless; Heaven would not help traitors.
entries.literal: People knew they were without crime; Heaven did not aid the wicked.

entries.zh: 今者，郭威，王峻，澶州節度使李洪義，前曹州防禦使何福進，前復州防禦使王彥超，前博州刺史李筠，北面行營馬步都指揮使郭崇，步軍都指揮使曹英，護聖都指揮使白重贊、索萬進、田景鹹、樊愛能、李萬全、史彥超，奉國都指揮使張鐸、王暉、胡立，弩手指揮使何赟等，徑領兵師，來安社稷。
entries.en: Now Guo Wei, Wang Jun, Li Hongyi, military commissioner of Chanzhou, former defenders He Fujin of Caozhou and Wang Yanchao of Fuzhou, former Bozhou prefect Li Yun, northern field horse-and-foot commander Guo Chong, infantry commander Cao Ying, Guarding-the-Sacred commanders Bai Chongzan, Suo Wanjin, Tian Jingxian, Fan Aineng, Li Wanquan, and Shi Yanchao, Serving-the-State commanders Zhang Duo, Wang Hui, and Hu Li, crossbow commander He Yun, and others have led their armies directly here to secure the altars of state.
entries.literal: Now Guo Wei, Wang Jun, Chanzhou commissioner Li Hongyi, former Caozhou defender He Fujin, former Fuzhou defender Wang Yanchao, former Bozhou prefect Li Yun, northern field horse-and-foot commander Guo Chong, foot commander Cao Ying, guard-for-the-sacred commanders Bai Chongzan, Suo Wanjin, Tian Jingxian, Fan Aineng, Li Wanquan, Shi Yanchao, nation-supporting commanders Zhang Duo, Wang Hui, Hu Li, crossbow commander He Yun, and others directly led armies to settle the altars.

entries.zh: 逆黨皇城使李業、內客省使閻晉卿、樞密都承旨聶文進、飛龍使後贊、翰林茶酒使郭允明等，脅君於大內，出戰於近郊，及至力窮，遂行弒逆，冤憤之極，今古未聞。
entries.en: Rebels Li Ye, Yan Jinqing, Nie Wenjin, Hou Zan, Guo Yunming, and others coerced the emperor, fought at the suburbs, and when spent murdered him—a crime unheard of in history.
entries.literal: The rebel party—palace envoy Li Ye, inner-service commissioner Yan Jinqing, bureau herald Nie Wenjin, flying-dragon commissioner Hou Zan, Hanlin tea-and-wine commissioner Guo Yunming, and others—coerced the ruler in the inner palace and went out to battle in the near suburbs; when their strength was exhausted they then carried out regicide; the extremity of wronged rage is unheard of in past and present.

entries.zh: 樞密使郭威以蕭墻變起，宗祏無奉，率群臣候太后，請定所立，且言：「開封尹承勛，高祖皇帝之愛子也，請立為嗣。」
entries.en: Guo Wei, with no heir at the altars, asked the dowager to choose a successor and said, "Kaifeng mayor Chengxun is Gaozu's beloved son—please establish him as successor."
entries.literal: Bureau commissioner Guo Wei, because trouble arose within the curtained wall and the ancestral temple had no one to receive sacrifice, led the civil and military officials to wait on the dowager and request fixing who should be established, and said: "Kaifeng mayor Chengxun is the founding emperor's beloved son—please establish him as successor.

entries.zh: 太后告以承勛羸病日久，不能自舉。
entries.en: The dowager said Chengxun had been gravely ill and could not govern.
entries.literal: The dowager reported that Chengxun had long been ill with weakness and could not rise.

entries.zh: 周太祖與諸將請視承勛起居，及視之，方信，遂議立高祖從子、徐州節度使赟為嗣。
entries.en: Guo Wei and the generals inspected Chengxun, found it true, and settled on Gaozu's nephew, Xuzhou commissioner Yun.
entries.literal: The Zhou founding ancestor and the generals asked to view Chengxun's condition; when they viewed it they believed it, and then deliberated establishing Gaozu's younger brother's son, Xuzhou commissioner Yun, as successor.

entries.zh: 己丑，太后誥曰：「天未悔禍，喪亂宏多，嗣王幼沖，群兇蔽惑，構奸謀於造次，縱毒蠆於斯須，將相大臣，連頸受戮，股肱良佐，無罪見屠，行路咨嗟，群心扼腕，則高祖之洪烈將墜於地。
entries.en: On jichou the dowager proclaimed: "Heaven has not yet repented of calamity; disorder and ruin are many; the young successor is deceived; vicious men formed wicked plots in haste; ministers and loyal assistants were slaughtered without cause; travelers sighed and hearts clutched their wrists—Gaozu's great enterprise would fall to earth.
entries.literal: On day jichou, the dowager's proclamation stated: "Heaven has not yet repented of calamity; disorder and ruin are many; the successor king is young; vicious fellows deceived him; they formed wicked plots in haste and released poison in a moment; ministers and great officials were slaughtered neck to neck; loyal assistants were killed without crime; travelers sighed and all hearts clutched their wrists—then the founding emperor's great enterprise would fall to earth.

entries.zh: 賴大臣郭威等，激揚忠義，拯濟顛危，除惡蔓以無遺，俾綴旒之不絕。
entries.en: Guo Wei and loyal ministers had crushed the villains and preserved the line.
entries.literal: Relying on great ministers Guo Wei and others, who roused loyal righteousness and rescued peril, removed the wicked root without remnant, and kept the suspended pearl from being cut off.

entries.zh: 宗祧事重，纘繼才難，既聞將相之謀，復考蓍龜之兆，天人協贊，社稷是依。
entries.en: With omens and ministers aligned, succession must proceed.
entries.literal: The ancestral temple affair is weighty and succession is hard; having heard the ministers' and generals' plan and again examined the tortoise and milfoil omens, Heaven and men together approve and the altars rely on it.

entries.zh: 徐州節度使赟，稟上聖之資，抱中和之德，先皇如子，鐘愛特深，固可以子育兆民，君臨萬國，宜令所司擇日備法駕奉迎即皇帝位。
entries.en: Xuzhou commissioner Yun, deeply loved by the late emperor, should be welcomed to the throne on a chosen day.
entries.literal: Xuzhou commissioner Yun possesses the substance of the supreme sage and embraces the virtue of centrality and harmony; the former emperor treated him as a son and loved him especially deep—he can certainly nurture the myriad people and rule the myriad states; the relevant offices should choose a day, prepare the imperial equipage, and welcome him to the throne.

entries.zh: 於戲！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 神器至重，天步方艱，致理保邦，不可以不敬，貽謀聽政，不可以不勤，允執厥中，祗膺景命。」
entries.en: The throne is weighty, the times hard—rule with reverence and diligence and hold the center."
entries.literal: The sacred vessel is supremely weighty; the heavenly step is just then difficult; to bring order and preserve the state cannot but be reverent; to hand down plans and hear government cannot but be diligent; hold the center and reverently receive the bright mandate."

entries.zh: 是日，遣前太師馮道等往徐奉迎。
entries.en: That day former grand preceptor Feng Dao was sent to Xu to escort him.
entries.literal: That day former Grand Preceptor Feng Dao and others were sent to Xu to welcome him.

entries.zh: 周太祖以嗣君未至，萬機不可暫曠，率群臣請太后臨朝，誥答曰：「昨以奸邪構釁，亂我邦家，勛德效忠，剪除兇慝，俯從人欲，已立嗣君，宗社危而再安，紀綱壞而復振。
entries.en: With the heir not yet arrived, Guo Wei asked the dowager to rule temporarily; her proclamation answered: "Yesterday vicious traitors disturbed our state; loyal merit cut down the villains; bowing to popular will a successor was established; the altars were perilous and again secure, statutes broken and again restored.
entries.literal: Because the successor ruler had not arrived and the myriad affairs could not briefly be vacant, the Zhou founding ancestor led the civil and military officials to ask the dowager to preside at court; the proclamation answered: "Yesterday vicious traitors formed calamity and disturbed Our state; meritorious virtue showed loyalty and cut down the vicious; bowing to human desire, a successor ruler has already been established; the altars were perilous and again secure, the statutes broken and again restored.

entries.zh: 皇帝法駕未至，庶事方殷，百辟上言，請予蒞政，宜允輿議，權總萬機，止於浹旬，即復明辟」云。
entries.en: Until the emperor arrives she would temporarily rule the myriad affairs for ten days, then restore him."
entries.literal: The emperor's imperial equipage has not arrived and the myriad affairs are still pressing; the hundred officials above speak and request that We preside over government—it should accord with public deliberation and temporarily total the myriad affairs, stopping at ten days, then restore the bright ruler."

entries.zh: 按前代故事，太上皇稱誥，太皇太后、皇太后曰令，今雲誥，有司誤也。
entries.en: By precedent retired emperors used proclamation and dowagers used order; here proclamation was an error of the offices.
entries.literal: According to earlier dynasties' precedents, the retired emperor was styled proclamation, the retired grand empress dowager and empress dowager were styled order; now it says proclamation—the relevant offices erred.

entries.zh: 以宣徽南院使王峻為樞密使，右神武統軍袁鳷為宣徽南院使，陳州刺史李穀權判三司，步軍都指揮使王殷為侍衛親軍馬步都指揮使，護聖左廂都指揮使郭崇為侍衛馬軍都指揮使，奉國左廂都指揮使曹英為侍衛步軍都指揮使。
entries.en: Wang Jun became bureau commissioner, Yuan Ji southern commissioner, Li Gu acting three departments, Wang Yin guard commander, Guo Chong horse commander, Cao Ying foot commander.
entries.literal: Wang Jun was made bureau commissioner, Yuan Ji southern palace commissioner, Chenzhou prefect Li Gu acting three departments, foot commander Wang Yin overall palace guard horse-and-foot commander, guard-for-the-sacred left commander Guo Chong guard horse commander, nation-supporting left commander Cao Ying guard foot commander.

entries.zh: 鎮州、邢州馳奏，契丹寇洺州，陷內丘縣。
entries.en: Zhenzhou and Xingzhou reported Khitan raids on Mingzhou and the fall of Neiqiu.
entries.literal: Zhenzhou and Xingzhou sent urgent memorials that the Khitan were raiding Mingzhou and had taken Neiqiu county.

entries.zh: 時契丹永康王烏裕率部族兩道入邊，內丘城小而固，契丹攻之，五日不下，敵人傷者甚眾。
entries.en: Khitan prince Wuyu invaded in two columns; Neiqiu, though small, held five days and inflicted heavy Khitan losses.
entries.literal: At the time the Khitan Yongkang king Wuyu led two columns of his tribes into the borders; Neiqiu city was small but firm; the Khitan attacked five days without taking it and the enemy wounded were very many.

entries.zh: 時有官軍五百，在城防戍，攻急，官軍降於敵，屠其城而去。
entries.en: Five hundred defenders surrendered under pressure; the Khitan sacked the city and withdrew.
entries.literal: At the time five hundred government troops were in the city on garrison defense; when the attack was urgent the government troops surrendered to the enemy, who slaughtered the city and left.

entries.zh: 〈（《遼史·世宗紀》：十月，自將南伐，攻下安平、內丘、束鹿等城，大獲而還。）〉
entries.en: (From the History of Liao, Annals of Emperor Shizong: in the tenth month he campaigned south, took Anping, Neiqiu, Shulu, and others, and returned with great spoils.)
entries.literal: (From the History of Liao, Annals of Emperor Shizong: in the tenth month he personally led a southern campaign, attacked and took Anping, Neiqiu, Shulu, and other cities, and returned with great booty.)

entries.zh: 庚寅，樞密使郭威奏，左軍巡勘得飛龍使後贊款伏，與蘇逢吉、李業、閻晉卿、聶文進、郭允明等同謀，令散員都虞候奔德等下手殺害史宏肇等。
entries.en: On gengyin Guo Wei reported Hou Zan's confession of plotting with Su Fengji, Li Ye, and others to murder Shi Hongzhao.
entries.literal: On day gengyin, bureau commissioner Guo Wei memorialized that the left army patrol had obtained Hou Zan's confession that he, together with Su Fengji, Li Ye, Yan Jinqing, Nie Wenjin, Guo Yunming, and others, had plotted to have the loose-duty commander Ben De and others strike and kill Shi Hongzhao.

entries.zh: 權開封尹劉銖具伏，朋附李業為亂，屠害將相家屬。
entries.en: Acting Kaifeng mayor Liu Zhu confessed he had followed Li Ye and massacred ministers' families.
entries.literal: Acting Kaifeng mayor Liu Zhu confessed that he had attached himself to Li Ye in the disorder and slaughtered the families of ministers and generals.

entries.zh: 其劉銖等準誥旨處置訖，並蘇逢吉、郭允明、閻晉卿、聶文進首級，並梟於南北市，其骨肉放棄。
entries.en: Liu Zhu and the rest were executed; Su Fengji, Guo Yunming, Yan Jinqing, and Nie Wenjin's heads were displayed in both markets.
entries.literal: Liu Zhu and the others were disposed of according to the proclamation's order; the heads of Su Fengji, Guo Yunming, Yan Jinqing, and Nie Wenjin were all exposed in the northern and southern markets, and their flesh and bone were abandoned.

entries.zh: 辛卯，河北諸州馳報，契丹深入。
entries.en: On xinmao Hebei reported deep Khitan penetration.
entries.literal: On day xinmao, the Hebei prefectures sent urgent reports that the Khitan had penetrated deeply.

entries.zh: 太后誥曰：「王室多故，邊境未寧，內難雖平，外寇仍熾。
entries.en: The dowager proclaimed: "The house has many troubles; borders are unsettled; though internal strife is over, foreign foes still rage.
entries.literal: The dowager's proclamation stated: "The royal house has many affairs; the borders are not yet calm; internal trouble is though pacified, outer enemies still blaze.

entries.zh: 據北面奏報，強敵奔沖，繼發兵師，未聞平殄，須勞上將，暫自臨戎。
entries.en: Northern reports say the enemy rushes in; armies have failed— a senior general must take the field.
entries.literal: According to northern reports, a strong enemy rushes in conflict; troops were sent in succession but no word of pacification is heard—a senior general must temporarily go to the army in person.

entries.zh: 宜令樞密使郭威部署大軍，早謀掩擊。
entries.en: Guo Wei should deploy the main force and strike quickly.
entries.literal: Bureau commissioner Guo Wei should deploy the great army and early plan a concealed strike.

entries.zh: 其軍國庶事，權委宰臣竇貞固、蘇禹珪、樞密使王峻等商量施行。
entries.en: State affairs are temporarily entrusted to Dou Zhengu, Su Yugui, Wang Jun, and others.
entries.literal: Military and civil affairs of the state are temporarily entrusted to chief ministers Dou Zhengu and Su Yugui, bureau commissioner Wang Jun, and others for deliberation and execution.

entries.zh: 在京馬步兵士，委王殷都大提舉。」
entries.en: Capital palace horse and foot troops were placed under Wang Yin's overall command."
entries.literal: Palace guard horse and foot soldiers in the capital were entrusted to Wang Yin's overall command."

entries.zh: 十二月甲午朔，郭威領大軍北征。
entries.en: At the twelfth-month new moon Guo Wei led the main army north.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day (day jiawu, new moon), Guo Wei led the great army on a northern campaign.

entries.zh: 丁酉，以翰林學士、尚書戶部侍郎、知制誥範質為樞密副使。
entries.en: On dingyou, Hanlin academician and revenue vice minister Fan Zhi became bureau vice commissioner.
entries.literal: On day dingyou, Fan Zhi, Hanlin academician, Vice Minister of Revenue, and drafter of edicts, was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 〈（《東都事略》：周太祖征李守貞，每朝廷遣使賫詔，處分軍事，皆中機會，太祖問：「誰為此辭？」
entries.en: (From the Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital: campaigning against Li Shouzhen, Guo Wei found every court edict on military affairs perfectly timed and asked, "Who wrote them?"
entries.literal: (From the Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital: when the Zhou founding ancestor campaigned against Li Shouzhen, whenever the court sent envoys bearing edicts to dispose military affairs, all hit the opportune moment. The founding ancestor asked: "Who composes this language?"

entries.zh: 使者以範質對，太祖曰：「宰相器也。」
entries.en: The envoy named Fan Zhi; Guo Wei said, "Chief-minister timber."
entries.literal: The envoy answered that it was Fan Zhi. The founding ancestor said: "Material for a chief minister."

entries.zh: 太祖起兵入京師，遽令草太后誥及議迎湘陰公儀註。
entries.en: Entering the capital he ordered Fan Zhi to draft the dowager's proclamation and rites to welcome the lord of Xiangyin.
entries.literal: When the founding ancestor raised troops and entered the capital, he urgently ordered drafting the dowager's proclamation and the protocol for welcoming the lord of Xiangyin.

entries.zh: 乃白太后，以質為兵部侍郎、樞密副使。）〉
entries.en: He then had Zhi made war vice minister and bureau vice commissioner.)〉
entries.literal: He then reported to the dowager and made Zhi Vice Minister of War and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau.)〉

entries.zh: 陜州李洪信奏，馬步都指揮使聶召、奉國指揮使楊德、護聖指揮使康審澄等，與節度使判官路濤、掌書記張洞、都押衙楊紹等，同情謀叛，並殺之。
entries.en: Li Hongxin reported Nie Zhao, Yang De, Kang Shencheng, and others plotting with his staff Lu Tao, Zhang Dong, and Yang Shao—all were executed.
entries.literal: Shaanzhou's Li Hongxin memorialized that horse-and-foot commander Nie Zhao, nation-supporting commander Yang De, guard-for-the-sacred commander Kang Shencheng, and others, together with the commissioner's judicial officer Lu Tao, secretary Zhang Dong, chief military adjutant Yang Shao, and others, sympathized and plotted rebellion—all were killed.

entries.zh: 惟康審澄夜中放火斬關，奔歸京師。
entries.en: Only Kang Shencheng burned the gate at night and fled to the capital.
entries.literal: Only Kang Shencheng at night set fire, cut the pass, and fled back to the capital.

entries.zh: 初，朝議以諸道方鎮皆是勛臣，不諳政理，其都押衙孔目官，令三司軍將內選才補之，藩帥不悅，故洪信因朝廷多故，誣奏加害焉。
entries.en: The court had wanted to replace merit-commanders' staff with three-departments talent; the commanders resented it, and Hongxin used the crisis to frame them.
entries.literal: Earlier, court deliberation held that the regional commanders in all circuits were merit ministers unfamiliar with government; their chief adjutants and clerks should be filled from talented three-departments army officers, which the military commissioners did not like; therefore Hongxin, taking advantage of the court's many troubles, falsely memorialized to harm them.

entries.zh: 壬寅，湖南上言，朗州馬希萼引五谿蠻及淮南洪州軍來攻當道，望量差兵士於淮境牽引。
entries.en: Hunan reported Ma Xie of Langzhou attacking with Five-Divine-Man tribes and Hongzhou troops and asked for troops on the Huainan border to distract them.
entries.literal: On day renyin, Hunan memorialized that Ma Xie of Langzhou had led Five-Divine-Man barbarians and Huainan Hongzhou troops to attack that circuit, hoping troops might be sent in some measure to the Huainan border to pull them away.

entries.zh: 乙巳，遣前淄州刺史陳恩讓領軍入淮南界，以便宜進取。
entries.en: On yisi former Zizhou prefect Chen Enrang entered Huainan with orders to act as circumstances allowed.
entries.literal: On day yisi, former Zizhou prefect Chen Enrang was sent to lead troops into Huainan territory to advance as opportunity allowed.

entries.zh: 辛亥，遣宰相蘇禹珪及朝臣十員，往宋州迎奉嗣君。
entries.en: On xinhai chief minister Su Yugui and ten officials went to Songzhou to welcome the heir.
entries.literal: On day xinhai, chief minister Su Yugui and ten court officials were sent to Songzhou to welcome the successor ruler.

entries.zh: 壬子，樞密使郭威次澶州，何福進已下及諸軍將士，扶擁威請為天子，即日南還。
entries.en: On renzi Guo Wei stopped at Chanzhou; He Fujin and the commanders forced him to become emperor and turned south the same day.
entries.literal: On day renzi, bureau commissioner Guo Wei halted at Chanzhou; He Fujin and those below and all military commanders supported and urged Wei to become Son of Heaven, and that day returned south.

entries.zh: 威上章於太后，言為諸軍所迫班師。
entries.en: Guo Wei memorialized the dowager that the armies had forced his return.
entries.literal: Wei submitted a memorial to the dowager saying he was compelled by the armies to withdraw the campaign.

entries.zh: 庚申，威至北郊，駐軍於臯門村。
entries.en: On gengshen he reached the northern suburb and camped at Gaomen village.
entries.literal: On day gengshen, Wei reached the northern suburb and encamped at Gaomen village.

entries.zh: 許州巡檢、前申州刺史馬鐸奏，節度使劉信自殺。
entries.en: Xu Prefecture inspector Ma Duo reported that military commissioner Liu Xin had committed suicide.
entries.literal: Xu Prefecture inspector and former prefect of Shenzhou Ma Duo memorialized that military commissioner Liu Xin had killed himself.

entries.zh: 壬戌，奉太后誥，命樞密使侍中郭威監國，中外庶事，並取監國處分。
entries.en: On renxu the dowager ordered vice grand councilor Guo Wei to supervise the state with full civil and military authority.
entries.literal: On day renxu, following the dowager's proclamation, bureau commissioner and Vice Grand Councilor Guo Wei was ordered to supervise the state; civil and military affairs within and without were all taken at the supervisor's disposal.

entries.zh: 先是，樞密使王峻以湘陰公已在宋州，慮聞澶州之事，左右變生，遣侍衛馬軍指揮使郭崇率七百騎往衛之。
entries.en: Earlier Wang Jun, fearing trouble when the lord of Xiangyin heard of Chanzhou, sent Guo Chong with seven hundred cavalry to guard him.
entries.literal: Earlier, bureau commissioner Wang Jun, because the lord of Xiangyin was already at Songzhou, feared that on hearing of the Chanzhou affair trouble would arise at his side, and sent guard horse commander Guo Chong with seven hundred riders to guard him.

entries.zh: 〈（《東都事略·郭崇傳》：王峻遣崇率七百騎拒瑽，遇於睢陽，崇曰：「澶州兵變，遣崇來衛乘輿，非有他也。」
entries.en: (From the Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital, biography of Guo Chong: Jun sent Chong with seven hundred riders to meet Yun at Suiyang. Chong said, "The Chanzhou troops mutinied; I came only to guard the imperial carriage—there is no other intent."
entries.literal: (From the biography of Guo Chong in the Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital: Wang Jun sent Chong with seven hundred riders to resist Yun; they met at Suiyang. Chong said: "There was mutiny at Chanzhou; Chong was sent to guard the imperial carriage—there is no other intent."

entries.zh: 具言軍情有屬，天命已定，瑽執崇手而泣，崇即送瑽就館。）〉
entries.en: He said the army's will was settled and Heaven's mandate fixed; Yun wept, grasped his hand, and Chong escorted him to his quarters.)〉
entries.literal: He fully explained that army sentiment had its object and the mandate of Heaven was fixed; Yun grasped Chong's hand and wept; Chong immediately escorted Yun to his lodging.)〉

entries.zh: 己未，太后誥曰：「比者，樞密使郭威，誌安社稷，議立長君，以徐州節度使赟，高祖近親，立為漢嗣，爰自藩鎮，征赴京師。
entries.en: On jiwei the dowager proclaimed: "Recently Guo Wei, intending to settle the altars, deliberated establishing a senior ruler; Xuzhou commissioner Yun, Gaozu's close kinsman, was established as Han successor and summoned from his post to the capital.
entries.literal: On day jiwei, the dowager's proclamation stated: "Recently bureau commissioner Guo Wei, intending to settle the altars, deliberated establishing a senior ruler; Xuzhou commissioner Yun, a close kinsman of Gaozu, was established as Han successor; from his post he was summoned to the capital.

entries.zh: 雖誥命尋行，而軍情不附，天道在北，人心靡東，適當改卜之初，俾膺分土之命。
entries.en: Though the edict went out, the armies would not follow; Heaven favored the north, not the east; at the change of fortune he received a new mandate.
entries.literal: Although the proclamation order was soon issued, army sentiment did not attach; the Way of Heaven was in the north, human hearts did not turn east; just as the divination for change began, he was made to receive the mandate of enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 赟可降授開府儀同三司、檢校太師、上柱國，封湘陰公，食邑三千戶，食實封五百戶。」
entries.en: Yun was demoted to acting grand master of the palace, inspecting grand preceptor, pillar of state, duke of Xiangyin with three thousand households and five hundred seal."
entries.literal: Yun may be demoted and appointed Acting Grand Master of the Palace, Grand Preceptor with inspection, Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyin with three thousand households' revenue and five hundred households' actual seal.

entries.zh: 明年正月丁卯，太后誥，奉符寶於監國，可即皇帝位。
entries.en: Next year's first month, dingmao, the dowager delivered the regalia to the regent to take the throne.
entries.literal: In the first month of the next year, on day dingmao, the dowager's proclamation delivered the talismans and treasures to the supervisor of state, who might immediately take the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 周太祖踐阼，奉太后為母，遷於西宮，上尊號曰昭聖太后。
entries.en: When Guo Wei took the throne he honored the dowager as mother, moved her to the western palace, and titled her Zhaosheng Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: When the Zhou founding ancestor ascended the throne, he honored the dowager as mother, moved her to the western palace, and gave the exalted title Zhaosheng Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 是月十五日，周太祖與百僚詣帝殯宮，成服親奠，不視朝七日。
entries.en: On the fifteenth the Zhou founder and officials went to the late emperor's hall, mourned in person, and suspended court seven days.
entries.literal: On the fifteenth day of that month the Zhou founding ancestor with the hundred officials went to the emperor's mourning hall, completed mourning garments, and personally offered sacrifice; he did not hold court for seven days.

entries.zh: 又詔太常定謚曰「隱」。
entries.en: An edict fixed his posthumous title as "Yin."
entries.literal: Another edict ordered the director of sacrifices to fix the posthumous title as "Yin."

entries.zh: 以其年八月二日，復遣前宗正卿劉皞護靈盾，備儀仗，葬於許州陽翟縣之潁陵，祔神主於高祖之寢宮。
entries.en: On the second of the eighth month Liu Hao escorted the coffin with full rites to Ying tomb in Yangdi, Xuzhou, and placed the tablet in Gaozu's shrine.
entries.literal: On the second day of the eighth month of that year, former director of the imperial clan Liu Hao was again sent to escort the spirit shield, with full ceremonial guard burying him at Ying tomb in Yangdi county, Xuzhou; the spirit tablet was attached in Gaozu's sleeping palace.

entries.zh: 帝姿貌白晰，眉目疏朗，未即位時，目多閃掣，唾洟不止，即位之始，遽無此態，及內難將作，復如故。
entries.en: He was fair-skinned with clear, sparse brows and eyes; before reigning his eyes twitched and he spat constantly—at his accession this stopped, but it returned when the palace coup neared.
entries.literal: The emperor's bearing was fair-skinned; eyebrows and eyes sparse and clear. Before he took the throne his eyes often flickered and he could not stop spitting; at the beginning of his reign this manner suddenly ceased; when internal trouble was about to arise it returned as before.

entries.zh: 帝自關西平定之後，稍自驕易，然畏憚大臣，未至縱恣。
entries.en: After the northwest was pacified he grew somewhat arrogant but still feared his senior ministers and did not run wild.
entries.literal: After the pacification of the pass west, the emperor gradually became somewhat proud and easy, yet he still feared the great ministers and did not reach unrestrained license.

entries.zh: 嘗因乾象差忒，宮中或有怪異，召司天監趙延乂訊其休咎，延乂對以修德即無患，既退，遣中使就問延乂曰：「何者為德？」
entries.en: Once, troubled by omens or palace omens, he asked astronomer Zhao Yanyi about fortune; Yanyi said cultivate virtue. The emperor then asked, "What is virtue?"
entries.literal: Once because celestial signs were irregular or there were strange things in the palace, he summoned director of astronomy Zhao Yanyi to inquire of fortune and misfortune; Yanyi answered that cultivating virtue would remove worry. After he withdrew, the emperor sent a palace envoy to ask Yanyi: "What counts as virtue?"

entries.zh: 延乂勸讀《貞觀政要》。
entries.en: Yanyi urged him to read the Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Reign.
entries.literal: Yanyi urged reading the Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Reign.

entries.zh: 邇後與聶文進、郭允明、後贊狎習，信其邪說，以至於敗。
entries.en: Later he grew close to Nie Wenjin, Guo Yunming, and Hou Zan, trusted their evil counsel, and was ruined.
entries.literal: Later he became intimate with Nie Wenjin, Guo Yunming, and Hou Zan, trusted their wicked words, and thereby reached ruin.

entries.zh: 高祖之征鄴城也，一日，帝語太祖曰：「我夜來夢爾為驢，負我升天，既舍爾，俄變為龍，舍我南去，是何祥也？」
entries.en: During Gaozu's Yedu campaign the emperor told Guo Wei, "I dreamed you were a donkey carrying me to Heaven, then a dragon that left me south—what omen is that?"
entries.literal: When Gaozu was campaigning at Yedu, one day the emperor said to the founding ancestor: "Last night I dreamed you were a donkey carrying me up to Heaven; after setting you down you suddenly became a dragon, left me, and went south—what omen is this?"

entries.zh: 周太祖撫掌而笑。
entries.en: Guo Wei clapped and laughed.
entries.literal: The Zhou founding ancestor clapped his hands and laughed.

entries.zh: 冥符蚃，豈偶然哉！
entries.en: Heaven's hidden mandate—hardly accidental!
entries.literal: Hidden mandate thick with blessing—how could it be accidental!

entries.zh: 史臣曰：隱帝以尚幼之年，嗣新造之業。
entries.en: The historian writes: Emperor Yin took a newly founded realm while still very young.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Emperor Yin, at a still tender age, succeeded a newly made enterprise.

entries.zh: 受命之主，德非禹、湯；
entries.en: The ruler who received the mandate lacked the virtue of Yu or Tang;
entries.literal: The ruler who received the mandate—his virtue was not that of Yu or Tang;

entries.zh: 輔政之臣，復非伊、呂。
entries.en: and his ministers were no Yi or Lü.
entries.literal: the ministers who assisted government were again not Yi or Lü.

entries.zh: 將欲保延洪之運，守不拔之基，固不可得也。
entries.en: To wish to preserve lasting fortune and an unshakable foundation was impossible.
entries.literal: To wish to preserve a perpetually grand fortune and guard an unshakable foundation was impossible to obtain.

entries.zh: 然西摧三叛，雖僅滅於欃槍，而內稔群兇，俄自取於狼狽。
entries.en: He crushed the three western rebellions yet nurtured palace villains and fell to their treachery.
entries.literal: Yet though he in the west crushed the three rebellions and barely extinguished them at the comet's banner, within he ripened a pack of villains and soon took ruin in wolfish disarray.

entries.zh: 自古覆宗絕祀之速者，未有如帝之甚也。
entries.en: No house in history fell faster than his.
entries.literal: From antiquity, none who overturned the clan and cut off sacrifice were as swift as this emperor.

entries.zh: 噫！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 蓋人謀之弗臧，非天命之遽奪也。
entries.en: It was bad human counsel, not Heaven suddenly withdrawing the mandate.
entries.literal: It was that human plans were not good—not that Heaven's mandate was suddenly snatched away.

entries.zh: 乾祐三年春正月己亥朔，帝不受朝賀。
entries.en: On the new moon of the first month of spring in Qianyou 3, the emperor declined the usual court congratulations.
entries.literal: In spring, on the first day of the first month of the third year of Qianyou (day jihai, new moon), the emperor did not accept court congratulations.

entries.zh: 鳳翔行營都部署趙暉奏，前月二十四日，收復鳳翔，逆賊王景崇舉族自燔而死。
entries.en: Zhao Hui, commander of the Fengxiang field headquarters, reported that on the twenty-fourth of the previous month Fengxiang had been retaken and that the rebel Wang Jingchong had burned himself to death along with his whole family.
entries.literal: Zhao Hui, overall commander of the mobile camp at Fengxiang, memorialized that on the twenty-fourth of the previous month he had recovered Fengxiang; the rebel Wang Jingchong burned himself to death together with his entire clan.

entries.zh: 丁未，鳳翔節度使、充西南行營都部署趙暉加兼侍中。
entries.en: On dingwei, Zhao Hui—Fengxiang commissioner and commander of the southwestern campaign—was also made Vice Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: On day dingwei, Zhao Hui, military commissioner of Fengxiang and overall commander of the southwestern field army, was additionally appointed Vice Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 戊申，密州刺史王萬敢奏，奉詔領兵入海州界，至荻水鎮，俘掠焚蕩，更請益兵。
entries.en: On wushen, Mizhou prefect Wang Wang'an reported that under imperial orders he had marched into Haizhou territory, raided and burned Dishui town, and now asked for more troops.
entries.literal: On day wushen, Wang Wang'an, prefect of Mizhou, memorialized that in obedience to an edict he had led troops into the border of Haizhou; at Dishui town he captured, plundered, and burned, and further requested reinforcements.

entries.zh: 詔前沂州刺史郭瓊率禁軍赴之。
entries.en: The court ordered former Yizhou prefect Guo Qiong to march the palace guard to reinforce him.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Guo Qiong, former prefect of Yizhou, to lead the imperial guard to go to his aid.

entries.zh: 庚午，前永興軍節度副使安友規除名，流登州沙門島。
entries.en: On gengwu, An Yougui, former deputy commissioner at Yongxing, was disgraced and exiled to Shamen Island off Dengzhou.
entries.literal: On day gengwu, An Yougui, former vice commissioner of the Yongxing army, was stripped of his name and banished to Shamen Island in Dengzhou.

entries.zh: 先是，友規權知永興軍府事，及趙思綰之奔沖，友規失守城池，至是乃正其罪焉。
entries.en: Yougui had been acting commander at Yongxing; when Zhao Siyun made his sudden assault he lost the city, and only now was he punished for it.
entries.literal: Earlier, Yougui had held acting authority over the Yongxing headquarters; when Zhao Siyun launched his assault, Yougui lost the city. Only now was his crime formally judged.

entries.zh: 癸亥，以前邠州節度使宋彥筠為太子太師致仕。
entries.en: On guihai, former Binzhou commissioner Song Yanyun was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired from office.
entries.literal: On day guihai, Song Yanyun, former commissioner of Binzhou, was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired.

entries.zh: 丙寅，分命使臣赴永興、鳳翔、河中，收葬用兵已來所在骸骨。
entries.en: On bingyin, the court sent separate envoys to Yongxing, Fengxiang, and Hezhong to gather and bury the war dead scattered since hostilities began.
entries.literal: On day bingyin, separate orders dispatched envoys to Yongxing, Fengxiang, and Hezhong to collect and bury the bones of the dead from all the places where troops had been engaged since the wars began.

entries.zh: 時已有僧聚髑髏二十萬矣。
entries.en: Monks had already collected two hundred thousand skulls.
entries.literal: By then monks had already gathered two hundred thousand skulls.

entries.zh: 前沂州刺史郭瓊奏，部署兵士，深入海州賊界。
entries.en: Former Yizhou prefect Guo Qiong reported that he had pushed his troops deep into Haizhou rebel territory.
entries.literal: Guo Qiong, former prefect of Yizhou, memorialized that he had deployed his soldiers deep into the rebel territory of Haizhou.

entries.zh: 是月，有狐登明德樓，主者獲之，狐毛長而腹下別有二足。
entries.en: That month a fox climbed Mingde Tower; when attendants caught it, its fur was unusually long and it had a second pair of feet under its belly.
entries.literal: That month a fox climbed the Mingde Tower; the custodian seized it—the fox's fur was long, and beneath its belly there were two separate feet.

entries.zh: 高祖皇后李氏，晉陽人也。
entries.en: Empress Li, consort of Later Han Gaozu, came from Jinyang.
entries.literal: Empress Li of Gaozu was a native of Jinyang.

entries.zh: 高祖微時，嘗牧馬於晉陽別墅，因夜入其家，劫而取之。
entries.en: While Liu Zhiyuan was still a nobody, he tended horses at a Jinyang country house, slipped in one night, and carried her off.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was still obscure, he once pastured horses at a villa outside Jinyang, and because of that entered her house by night, seized her, and took her away.

entries.zh: 及高祖領藩鎮，累封魏國夫人。
entries.en: Once he held a frontier command she rose step by step to Lady of Wei.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took charge of a military province, she was repeatedly ennobled as lady of Wei.

entries.zh: 高祖建義於太原，欲行頒賚於軍士，以公帑不足，議率井邑，助成其事。
entries.en: At Taiyuan he meant to pay the troops but the state coffers ran dry, so his council weighed a levy on town and countryside to fund the bonuses.
entries.literal: When Gaozu raised the righteous cause at Taiyuan and wished to distribute largess among the soldiers, because the public treasury was insufficient they deliberated levying the towns and villages to help accomplish the matter.

entries.zh: 後聞而諫曰：「自晉高祖建義，及國家興運，雖出於天意，亦土地人民福力同致耳，未能惠其眾而欲奪其財，非新天子恤隱之理也。
entries.en: The empress heard of it and remonstrated, saying, "From the time Jin Gaozu raised the righteous cause down to our dynasty's rise to fortune, although it came from Heaven's will, it was also because the blessing-power of the land and the people arrived together; to fail to show kindness to the multitude yet wish to strip their wealth is not the way a new Son of Heaven should pity the distressed.
entries.literal: The empress heard of it and remonstrated, saying, "From the time Jin Gaozu raised the righteous cause down to our dynasty's rise to fortune, although it came from Heaven's will, it was also because the blessing-power of the land and the people arrived together; to fail to show kindness to the multitude yet wish to strip their wealth is not the way a new Son of Heaven should pity the distressed.

entries.zh: 今後宮所積，宜悉以散之，設使不厚，人無怨言。」
entries.en: Empty the palace hoards first; even thin gifts will silence grumbling."
entries.literal: What the rear palace has stored up ought all to be scattered among them; even if the gifts are not lavish, the people will have no cause for complaint."

entries.zh: 高祖改容曰：「敬聞命矣。」
entries.en: The emperor colored and said, "Your counsel is taken."
entries.literal: Gaozu changed countenance and said, "I respectfully accept the command."

entries.zh: 遂停斂貸之議。
entries.en: He dropped the plan for forced loans.
entries.literal: Thereupon he stopped the proposal to collect loans.

entries.zh: 後傾內府以助之，中外聞者，無不感悅。
entries.en: She then opened the privy purse to make up the sum, and word of it gladdened the whole court and camp.
entries.literal: Later she poured out the inner treasury to assist it; those who heard of it within and without were all moved and pleased.

entries.zh: 天福十二年，冊為皇后。
entries.en: In Tianfu 12 she received the empress's seals.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianfu she was invested as empress.

entries.zh: 隱帝即位，尊為皇太后。
entries.en: When Emperor Yin succeeded she became empress dowager.
entries.literal: When the Yin Emperor ascended the throne, she was honored as empress dowager.

entries.zh: 〈（案：以下疑有闕文。
entries.en: Editor's note: the passage below is likely corrupt.
entries.literal: Annotation: the text that follows is probably defective.

entries.zh: 據《通鑒》云：隱帝與李業等謀誅楊邠等，議既定，入白太后，太后曰：「茲事何可輕發，更宜與宰相議之。」
entries.en: The 《Zizhi tongjian》 records that Emperor Yin and Li Ye resolved to kill Yang Bin; when they told the dowager she said, "Do not rush this; take it to the chief ministers first."
entries.literal: According to the 《Zizhi tongjian》: the Yin Emperor plotted with Li Ye and others to execute Yang Bin and the rest; when the plan was settled they entered to report to the empress dowager, and the empress dowager said, "How can such a matter be lightly set in motion? You should further discuss it with the chief ministers."

entries.zh: 業時在旁曰：「先帝嘗言，朝廷大事不可謀及書生，懦怯誤人。」
entries.en: Li Ye at her elbow said, "The late emperor warned never to plot great matters with pedants—they only breed cowardice."
entries.literal: Ye, who was at the side at the time, said, "The late emperor once said that great affairs of the court must not be plotted with bookish men—timidity misleads men."

entries.zh: 太后復以為言，帝忿曰：「國家之事，非閨門所知。」
entries.en: She pressed again; the emperor snapped, "State business is no concern of women's quarters."
entries.literal: The empress dowager repeated her words, and the emperor angrily said, "Affairs of the state are not for the inner chambers to know."

entries.zh: 拂衣而出。
entries.en: He flung aside his robe and left.
entries.literal: He shook out his sleeves and went out.

entries.zh: 又云：南北軍遇於劉子陂，帝欲自出勞軍，太后曰：「郭威吾家故舊，非死亡切身，何以至此！
entries.en: The same work adds: at Liuzipo the young ruler meant to ride out to hearten the lines; the dowager cried, "Guo Wei is family to us—would he rebel without mortal cause!
entries.literal: It also says: when the northern and southern armies met at Liuzipo, the emperor wished to go out himself to encourage the troops, and the empress dowager said, "Guo Wei is an old friend of our house—unless death pressed close, how could matters come to this!

entries.zh: 但按兵守城，飛詔諭之，觀其志趣，必有辭理，則君臣之禮尚全，慎勿輕出。」
entries.en: Keep the gates shut, send him a clear edict, and read his answer; lord and minister may yet mend their breach—do not rashly ride forth."
entries.literal: Only hold the troops and guard the city, fly an edict to instruct him, observe his intentions—surely there will be words of reason, and then the rites between lord and minister can still remain whole; be careful not to go out lightly."

entries.zh: 帝不從。）〉
entries.en: The young ruler brushed aside her warning. (End of editorial note.)〉
entries.literal: The emperor did not comply. (End of editorial note.)〉

entries.zh: 周太祖入京，凡軍國大事，皆請後發教令以行之。
entries.en: After Guo Wei took the capital he still had her issue the orders that ran the realm.
entries.literal: When Zhou Taizu entered the capital, for every great affair of army and state he all asked the empress dowager to issue instructional orders to carry them out.

entries.zh: 是歲，議立徐州節度使赟為帝，以迎奉未至，周太祖乃率群臣拜章，請後權臨朝聽政，後於是稱誥焉。
entries.en: That year they planned to enthrone Liu Yun, the Xuzhou military commissioner; because the welcoming escort had not yet arrived, Guo Wei led the ministers to memorialize the dowager to hold court temporarily as regent, and she thereupon spoke in edict form.
entries.literal: That year they deliberated establishing the Xuzhou military commissioner Yun as emperor; because the welcoming escort had not yet arrived, Zhou Taizu thereupon led the host of ministers to submit a memorial and asked the empress dowager temporarily to attend court and hear government, and the empress dowager thereupon spoke in the manner of an edict.

entries.zh: 及周太祖為六軍推戴，上章具述其事，且言願事後為慈母。
entries.en: When the Six Armies raised Guo Wei, his memorial laid out every step and vowed to honor her as a mother.
entries.literal: When Zhou Taizu was acclaimed by the Six Armies, he submitted a memorial setting forth the affair in detail and moreover said he wished to serve the empress dowager as a kind mother.

entries.zh: 後下誥答曰：「侍中功烈崇高，德聲昭著，翦除禍亂，安定乾坤，謳歌有歸，歷數攸屬，所以軍民推戴，億兆同歡。
entries.en: "Your merit towers high and your virtuous name shines bright; you have cut away turmoil and steadied heaven and earth. Song and acclaim have found their lord, the mandate is rightly yours, and army and people together rejoice.
entries.literal: The empress dowager issued an answering edict saying, "The attendant-in-chief's merit and achievement are lofty, his virtuous name shines bright; he has cut away calamity and disorder and stabilized heaven and earth; songs of praise have a proper object, the celestial succession belongs where it ought—therefore army and people have pushed him forward and a hundred million share the joy.

entries.zh: 老身未終殘年，屬茲多難，惟以衰朽，托於始終。
entries.en: I am old and worn, yet live through this storm; I can only lean on you to the end.
entries.literal: I, old woman, have not yet finished my remaining years, yet meet these many hardships; I can only, in my decay, entrust myself from beginning to end.

entries.zh: 載省來箋，如母見待，感念深意，涕泗橫流」云。
entries.en: Your words treat me as a mother might be treated—I weep as I read them."
entries.literal: Having read your letter, you treat me as a mother; I am moved by the deep meaning and tears and mucus stream across my face," and so on.

entries.zh: 仍出戎衣、玉帶以賜周太祖。
entries.en: She sent him a field robe and a jade belt as gifts.
entries.literal: She moreover presented a campaign robe and jade belt to bestow on Zhou Taizu.

entries.zh: 周太祖即位，上尊號曰德聖皇太后，居於太平宮。
entries.en: Once Guo Wei took the throne he styled her the Virtuous and Sagely Empress Dowager and housed her at Taiping Palace.
entries.literal: When Zhou Taizu ascended the throne, he honored her with the title Virtuous and Sagely Empress Dowager and she dwelt at the Palace of Great Peace.

entries.zh: 周顯德元年春薨。
entries.en: She died in the spring of Zhou Xiande 1.
entries.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xiande of Zhou she died.

entries.zh: 〈（案：隱帝未立皇后，據薛史《張彥成傳》云：隱帝娶彥成女。
entries.en: Editor's note: Yin never crowned a queen; the Old History biography of Zhang Yancheng says he wed Zhang Yancheng's daughter.
entries.literal: Annotation: Emperor Yin never invested an empress; according to the 《Zhang Yancheng zhuan》 in Xue's history, Yin married Yancheng's daughter.

entries.zh: 《楊邠傳》云：隱帝所愛耿夫人，欲立為後，邠以為太速，夫人卒，隱帝欲以後禮葬，邠又止之。
entries.en: The 《Yang Bin zhuan》 adds that Yin doted on Lady Geng and wanted her as empress; Yang Bin called it premature. When she died Yin demanded an empress's funeral, and Yang Bin blocked that too.
entries.literal: The 《Yang Bin zhuan》 states: the Lady Geng whom Yin favored he wished to establish as empress, but Bin thought it too soon; when the lady died Yin wished to bury her with empress rites, and Bin again stopped him.

entries.zh: 蓋隱帝在位三年，崩時年二十，故未及冊立皇后也。
entries.en: He ruled barely three years and died at twenty, so he never crowned a queen.
entries.literal: Probably because Yin reigned only three years and was twenty sui when he perished, therefore he had not yet reached the investiture of an empress.

entries.zh: 又，《五代會要》載：漢高祖長女永寧公主，降宋延渥，天福十二年四月封，至乾祐二年十二月，追封秦國長公主。）〉
entries.en: The 《Wudai hui yao》 also notes Gaozu's eldest daughter, Princess Yongning, wed Song Yanwo, was titled in Tianfu 12, and was posthumously raised to princess of Qin in Qianyou 2. (End of editorial note.)〉
entries.literal: Moreover, the 《Wudai hui yao》 records: Han Gaozu's eldest daughter, the Princess of Yongning, was married to Song Yanwo; she was enfeoffed in the fourth month of Tianfu 12, and in the twelfth month of the second year of Qianyou was posthumously advanced to elder princess of Qin. (End of editorial note.)〉

entries.zh: ◎宗室魏王承訓，字德輝，高祖之長子也。
entries.en: ◎ Prince Wei Cheng Xun of the imperial house, courtesy name Dehui, was eldest son of Later Han Gaozu.
entries.literal: ◎ Prince Wei of the Imperial House Cheng Xun, courtesy name Dehui, was Gaozu's eldest son.

entries.zh: 少溫厚，美姿儀，高祖尤鐘愛。
entries.en: As a youth he was mild and warm-hearted, handsome in bearing, and Gaozu doted on him above all.
entries.literal: In youth he was gentle and warm-hearted, with handsome features; Gaozu especially cherished him.

entries.zh: 在晉累官至檢校司空，國初授左衛上將軍。
entries.en: In Jin service he rose step by step to honorary Minister of Works; at the dynasty's founding he was made Left Guard Grand General.
entries.literal: While at Jin he rose through repeated offices to honorary Minister of Works; at the founding of the state he was made Left Guard Grand General.

entries.zh: 高祖將赴洛，命承訓北京大內巡檢，未幾，詔赴闕，授開封尹、檢校太尉、同平章事。
entries.en: As Gaozu prepared to go to Luoyang, he ordered Cheng Xun to inspect the inner palace at the Northern Capital; soon an edict recalled him to court and made him Kaifeng prefect, honorary Grand Marshal, and vice grand councilor.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was about to go to Luoyang, he ordered Cheng Xun to inspect the inner palace at the Northern Capital; before long an edict summoned him to court, and he was given the posts of Kaifeng prefect, honorary Grand Marshal, and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

entries.zh: 以天福十二年十二月十一日薨於府署，年二十六。
entries.en: On the eleventh day of the twelfth month of Tianfu 12 he died at his yamen, aged twenty-six.
entries.literal: On the eleventh day of the twelfth month in the twelfth year of Tianfu he died at his yamen, aged twenty-six.

entries.zh: 高祖發哀於太平宮，哭之大慟，以至於不豫。
entries.en: Gaozu mourned at Taiping Palace and wept so bitterly that he fell ill.
entries.literal: Gaozu held mourning rites at Taiping Palace, weeping with such anguish that he fell ill.

entries.zh: 是月，追封魏王。
entries.en: That month he was posthumously created Prince of Wei.
entries.literal: That month he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.

entries.zh: 歸葬於太原。
entries.en: He was returned to Taiyuan for burial.
entries.literal: His body was returned for burial at Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 陳王承勛，高祖之幼子也。
entries.en: Cheng Xun, Prince of Chen, was Gaozu's youngest son.
entries.literal: Prince Chen Cheng Xun was Gaozu's youngest son.

entries.zh: 國初授右衛大將軍。
entries.en: At the dynasty's founding he was made Right Guard Grand General.
entries.literal: At the founding of the state he was made Right Guard Grand General.

entries.zh: 隱帝嗣位，加檢校太尉、同平章事，遙領興元尹，俄代侯益為開封尹，進位檢校太師、兼侍中。
entries.en: When Emperor Yin succeeded, he was made honorary Grand Marshal and vice grand councilor, with distant command as Xingyuan prefect; soon he replaced Hou Yi as Kaifeng prefect and was promoted to honorary Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: When the Hidden Emperor succeeded, he was given the additional titles of honorary Grand Marshal and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and concurrently held distant command as prefect of Xingyuan; soon he replaced Hou Yi as Kaifeng prefect and was advanced to honorary Grand Preceptor and concurrent Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 乾祐三年冬十一月，蕭墻之亂，隱帝崩，軍情欲立勛為嗣。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of Qianyou 3, at the palace upheaval Emperor Yin died, and the armies wanted to make Xun heir.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of winter in the third year of Qianyou, at the palace upheaval the Hidden Emperor perished, and the army's sentiment was to establish Xun as heir.

entries.zh: 時勛已病，大臣及諸將請候勛起居，太后令左右以臥榻舁之以見，諸將就視，知勛之不能興，故議立劉赟。
entries.en: Xun was already ill; ministers and generals asked to call on him, and the dowager had attendants carry him on a couch to be seen; when the generals looked and saw he could not rise, they turned to naming Liu Yun heir.
entries.literal: Xun was already ill; the chief ministers and generals requested to call on his health, and the empress dowager had attendants carry him on a couch to be seen; the generals went up and looked, and knowing he could not rise, they therefore deliberated on establishing Liu Yun as heir.

entries.zh: 周廣順元年春卒。
entries.en: He died in the spring of Guangshun 1.
entries.literal: In the spring of the first year of Zhou Guangshun he died.

entries.zh: 周太祖下詔封陳王。
entries.en: Zhou Taizu issued an edict creating him Prince of Chen.
entries.literal: Zhou Taizu issued an edict enfeoffing him as Prince of Chen.

entries.zh: 蔡王信，高祖之從弟也。
entries.en: Prince Cai Xin was a cousin of Later Han Gaozu.
entries.literal: Prince of Cai Xin was a collateral younger male relative of Gaozu.

entries.zh: 少從軍，漸至龍武小校。
entries.en: He entered the army young and slowly worked his way up to a junior post in the Dragon Martial Guard.
entries.literal: In youth he followed the army and gradually rose to junior officer of the Dragon Martial Guard.

entries.zh: 漢祖鎮并州，為興捷軍都將，領龔州刺史、檢校太保。
entries.en: While Liu Zhiyuan governed Bingzhou, Xin became commander of the Xingjie Army and also served as prefect of Gong and honorary Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: When the Han founder held Bingzhou, he served as commander-in-chief of the Xingjie Army, and concurrently held the posts of prefect of Gongzhou and honorary Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 國初，為侍衛馬軍都指揮使、檢校太傅兼義成軍節度使，尋移鎮許州，加太尉、同平章事。
entries.en: At the dynasty's founding he commanded the palace horse guard, served as honorary Grand Mentor and military governor of Yicheng, then was shifted to Xu Prefecture with the added titles of Grand Marshal and vice grand councilor.
entries.literal: At the founding of the state he was made commander of the palace horse guard, honorary Grand Mentor and concurrently military governor of the Yicheng circuit; soon he was transferred to hold Xuzhou, and was further given Grand Marshal and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

entries.zh: 高祖寢疾大漸，楊邠受密旨遣信赴鎮，信即時戒路，不得奉辭，雨泣而去。
entries.en: As Gaozu lay dying, Yang Bin carried a secret order to send Xin back to his post; Xin set out at once without a farewell audience and left in tears through the rain.
entries.literal: When Gaozu's illness grew grave, Yang Bin received a secret order to send Xin back to his command; Xin at once made ready to depart, could not take formal leave, and went away weeping in the rain.

entries.zh: 隱帝即位，加檢校太師。
entries.en: After Emperor Yin succeeded, Xin was made honorary Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: When the Hidden Emperor took the throne, Xin was given the additional title of honorary Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 關輔賊平，就加侍中。
entries.en: Once the Guanzhong rebels were crushed, he received the post of Palace Attendant on the spot.
entries.literal: When the rebels in the Guanzhong region were pacified, he was thereupon made Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 信性昏懦，黷貨無厭，喜行酷法。
entries.en: Xin was stupid and spineless, greedy beyond satiety, and fond of cruel law.
entries.literal: Xin's nature was dull and timid; he was insatiable in corrupt gain and delighted in harsh punishments.

entries.zh: 掌禁軍時，左右有犯罪者，召其妻子，對之臠割，令自食其肉，或從足支解至首，血流盈前，而命樂對酒，無仁湣之色。
entries.en: While commanding the imperial guard, if a subordinate broke the law he would call in the man's wife and children, hack them apart before his eyes, and force him to eat their flesh—or slice him from foot to head until blood pooled at his feet—then order music and drink across the carnage without a trace of mercy.
entries.literal: While he commanded the forbidden troops, when attendants committed offenses he would summon their wives and children, cut them to pieces before their eyes, and make them eat their own flesh; or he would dismember them from the feet up to the head, blood filling the ground before him, yet he would order music and drink wine opposite them, with no look of pity or compassion.

entries.zh: 未嘗接延賓客。
entries.en: He never entertained guests.
entries.literal: He never once received or entertained guests.

entries.zh: 在鎮日，聚斂無度，會高祖山陵梓宮經由境上，信率掠吏民，以備迎奉，百姓苦之。
entries.en: In his province he levied without measure; when Gaozu's coffin passed through on its way to the tomb, Xin stripped officials and commoners alike to fund the reception, and the people groaned under it.
entries.literal: During his days in command he extorted without limit; it happened that Gaozu's mountain tomb and the imperial coffin passed through his territory, and Xin led the plunder of officials and commoners to prepare for the welcoming ceremony—the people suffered bitterly.

entries.zh: 初，聞殺楊邠、史宏肇，遽啟宴席，集參佐賓幕，令相致賀。
entries.en: When word came that Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao had been killed, he at once threw a banquet, gathered his staff and secretariat advisers, and told them to congratulate one another.
entries.literal: At first, when he heard that Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao had been killed, he hastily opened a feast, gathered his staff and secretariat guests, and had them offer congratulations to one another.

entries.zh: 曰：「我謂天無眼，令我三年不能適意。
entries.en: He said, "I used to think Heaven was blind—three years I could not do as I pleased.
entries.literal: He said: "I thought Heaven had no eyes, keeping me from satisfaction for three years.

entries.zh: 主上孤立，幾落賊手。
entries.en: The emperor stood alone and nearly fell into the rebels' clutches.
entries.literal: The sovereign stood alone and nearly fell into the rebels' hands.

entries.zh: 諸公勸我一杯可也。」
entries.en: Gentlemen, you may press a cup on me—that will do."
entries.literal: You gentlemen may urge me to take a cup—that will do."

entries.zh: 俄蕭墻之變，憂不能食。
entries.en: Before long came the palace upheaval, and he was too anxious to eat.
entries.literal: Soon came the turmoil within the palace walls, and in his anxiety he could not eat.

entries.zh: 尋有太后令，言立湘陰公，即令其子往徐州奉迎。
entries.en: Soon the dowager issued an order to install the Duke of Xiangyin as heir, and Xin immediately sent his son to Xuzhou to escort him.
entries.literal: Before long there was an order from the empress dowager saying that the Duke of Xiangyin was to be established as heir; he at once sent his son to Xuzhou to welcome him.

entries.zh: 數日，陳思讓率馬軍經過城西，但令供頓，不敢出城。
entries.en: A few days later Chen Siran marched the horse guard past the west wall; Xin supplied their rations but dared not leave the city.
entries.literal: Several days later Chen Siran led the horse guard past the west of the city; Xin only ordered provisions supplied and did not dare leave the city.

entries.zh: 未幾，澶州軍變，王峻遣前申州刺史馬鐸領軍赴州巡檢，鐸引軍入城，信惶惑自殺。
entries.en: Not long after, the Chanzhou garrison mutinied; Wang Jun sent the former Shen prefect Ma Duo to inspect the prefecture, and Duo marched into the city—whereupon Xin, distraught, took his own life.
entries.literal: Before long there was a mutiny in the army at Chanzhou; Wang Jun sent the former prefect of Shenzhou Ma Duo to lead troops to the prefecture on an inspection tour, and Duo led his army into the city; Xin, in panic and confusion, killed himself.

entries.zh: 廣順初，追封蔡王。
entries.en: Early in the Guangshun reign he was posthumously created Prince of Cai.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Guangshun era he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cai.

entries.zh: 湘陰公赟，為徐州節度使。
entries.en: The Duke of Xiangyin, Yun, held the Xuzhou military governorship.
entries.literal: The Duke of Xiangyin, Yun, was military governor of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 乾祐元年八月中，有雲見五色。
entries.en: In the eighth month of Qianyou 1, five-colored clouds were seen.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Qianyou, clouds appeared in five colors.

entries.zh: 明年冬杪，有鳥翔集於鮮碧堂庭樹，黃質朱喙，金目青翼，紺趾黑尾，有類於鳳。
entries.en: Late the following winter a bird settled on a tree in the Fresh Green Hall courtyard—yellow-bodied, vermilion-beaked, with golden eyes, blue-green wings, violet feet, and a black tail, rather like a phoenix.
entries.literal: At the end of winter the next year a bird alighted on a tree in the courtyard of the Fresh Green Hall: yellow body, vermilion beak, golden eyes, blue-green wings, dark purple feet and black tail—rather like a phoenix.

entries.zh: 有賓佐嘆曰：「野鳥入室，主人將去。」
entries.en: One of his advisers sighed and said, "When a wild bird flies indoors, the master is about to leave."
entries.literal: A staff member sighed and said: "When a wild bird enters the house, the master is about to depart."

entries.zh: 旬浹而不知所之。
entries.en: Ten days later it was gone, and no one knew where.
entries.literal: After ten days and more it vanished, no one knew where.

entries.zh: 乾祐三年冬十一月，周太祖駐軍於京師，議立嗣君，奉太后誥，立赟為嗣。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of Qianyou 3, Zhou Taizu camped at the capital to choose an heir; obeying the dowager's patent, he named Yun successor.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of winter in the third year of Qianyou, Zhou Taizu stationed his army at the capital, deliberated on establishing an heir, and in accordance with the dowager's patent established Yun as successor.

entries.zh: 傳誥之際，馮道笏墜於地，左右惡之。
entries.en: As the patent was read out, Feng Dao's tablet slipped to the floor—those around him took it as a bad sign.
entries.literal: At the moment the patent was transmitted, Feng Dao's court tablet fell to the ground, and those beside him regarded it as ill-omened.

entries.zh: 馮道至，赟出郊迎，常所乘馬比甚馴服，至是馬蹄嚙奔逸，人不可制，乃以他馬代之，時以為不祥。
entries.en: When Feng Dao arrived, Yun rode out to meet him; the horse he always used had been thoroughly tame, but now it champed the bit and bolted beyond control, so they switched mounts—people read it as an ill omen.
entries.literal: When Feng Dao arrived, Yun went out to the suburbs to welcome him; the horse he usually rode had always been very docile, but this time it bit at its bit and bolted, beyond human control, so another horse was substituted—at the time this was taken as inauspicious.

entries.zh: 將離彭城，嘗一日，天有白光一道自西來，照城中如晝，有聲如雷，時人謂之天裂；
entries.en: On the eve of leaving Pengcheng, one day a shaft of white light shot in from the west and lit the city like noon, with a thunderous roar—folk called it Heaven splitting;
entries.literal: As he was about to leave Pengcheng, on one day a streak of white light came from the west, illuminating the city as if at noon, with a sound like thunder—people of the time called it a rending of Heaven;

entries.zh: 又有巨星墜於徐野，殷然有聲，或謂之天狗。
entries.en: and a great star crashed on the Xuzhou plain with a deep boom—some called it the Heavenly Dog.
entries.literal: there was also a great star that fell on the Xuzhou plain with a deep rumbling sound, and some called it the Heavenly Dog.

entries.zh: 後赟果廢死。
entries.en: Yun was indeed later deposed and killed.
entries.literal: Later Yun was indeed deposed and died.

entries.zh: 〈（案：《湘陰公傳》原本殘闕，考《十國春秋·湘陰公傳》云：湘陰公赟，世祖子也，高祖愛之，以為己子。
entries.en: (Editor's note: the base 《Biography of the Duke of Xiangyin》 is corrupt; the 《Ten States Spring and Autumn》 account reads: the Duke of Xiangyin Yun was a son of Shizu; Gaozu doted on him and raised him as his own.
entries.literal: (Note: the original text of the 《Biography of the Duke of Xiangyin》 is defective; consulting the 《Biography of the Duke of Xiangyin》 in the Ten States Spring and Autumn, it says: the Duke of Xiangyin Yun was a son of Shizu; Gaozu loved him and treated him as his own son.

entries.zh: 乾祐元年，拜武寧軍節度使。
entries.en: In Qianyou 1 he was made military governor of Wuning.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianyou he was appointed military governor of the Wuning circuit.

entries.zh: 二年，加同平章事。
entries.en: The next year he was made vice grand councilor.
entries.literal: In the second year he was given the additional title of Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

entries.zh: 郭威既敗慕容彥超於北郊，隱帝遇弒，威入京師，謂諸大臣密相推戴，及見宰相馮道等，道殊無意。
entries.en: After Guo Wei routed Murong Yanchao north of the capital and Emperor Yin was murdered, Wei entered the city and asked the chief ministers to back him in secret; when he met Feng Dao and the rest, Dao showed no inclination whatsoever.
entries.literal: After Guo Wei had defeated Murong Yanchao at the northern suburb and the Hidden Emperor met assassination, Wei entered the capital and told the chief ministers to confer secretly on enthroning him; when he met the chief councilor Feng Dao and others, Dao showed no intention at all.

entries.zh: 威不得已，見道下拜，而道猶受拜如平時，徐勞之曰：「公行良苦。」
entries.en: Wei had no choice but to bow to Dao; Dao accepted the bow as usual and said slowly, "You have had a hard road of it."
entries.literal: Wei had no choice; he met Dao and bowed, yet Dao still received the bow as in ordinary times and slowly comforted him, saying: "Your journey has been truly arduous."

entries.zh: 威意色皆沮，以為大臣未有推己意，又難於自立，因與王峻入白太后，推擇漢嗣。
entries.en: Wei's face fell; he took it that the ministers were not yet backing him and that seizing the throne on his own would be hard, so he and Wang Jun went in to the dowager to have a Later Han heir selected.
entries.literal: Wei's expression and color were altogether dejected; he thought the great ministers had not yet shown intent to support him, and that it was again difficult to establish himself on his own; he therefore entered with Wang Jun to report to the empress dowager and have a Han heir chosen.

entries.zh: 群臣乃共奏曰：「武寧節度使赟，高祖愛以為子，宜立為嗣。」
entries.en: The ministers jointly memorialized: "Wuning governor Yun, whom Gaozu loved as a son, should be made heir."
entries.literal: The assembled ministers then jointly memorialized, saying: "The military governor of Wuning, Yun, whom Gaozu loved and treated as a son, should be established as heir."

entries.zh: 乃遣太師馮道率百官往迎，道揣威意不在赟，直前問曰：「公此舉由衷乎？」
entries.en: Grand Preceptor Feng Dao was sent at the head of the bureaucracy to escort him; sensing that Wei did not mean Yun, Dao stepped forward and asked, "Does this come from your heart?"
entries.literal: They then sent Grand Preceptor Feng Dao at the head of the hundred officials to welcome him; Dao guessed that Wei's mind was not on Yun, stepped forward and asked: "Is this move of yours from the heart?"

entries.zh: 威指天為誓。
entries.en: Wei swore by Heaven.
entries.literal: Wei pointed to Heaven and swore.

entries.zh: 道既行，語左右曰：「吾生平不能謬語人，今謬語矣。」
entries.en: Once on the road, Dao told his attendants, "I have never lied to anyone in my life—today I have lied."
entries.literal: After Dao had set out, he said to those beside him: "All my life I have been unable to speak falsely to people; today I have spoken falsely."

entries.zh: 道見，傳太后意召之。
entries.en: When Dao met Yun, he relayed the dowager's summons.
entries.literal: When Dao met him, he conveyed the dowager's intent and summoned him.

entries.zh: 赟行至宋州，威已自澶州為兵士擁還京師。
entries.en: Yun reached Songzhou while Wei had already been carried back to the capital from Chanzhou by his troops.
entries.literal: When Yun reached Songzhou, Wei had already been escorted back to the capital from Chanzhou by the soldiers.

entries.zh: 王峻慮赟左右生變，遣侍衛馬軍指揮使郭崇威以兵七百騎衛赟。
entries.en: Wang Jun feared trouble from Yun's entourage and sent palace horse-guard commander Guo Chongwei with seven hundred cavalry to escort him.
entries.literal: Wang Jun feared that those around Yun might stir up trouble, and sent the commander of the palace horse guard Guo Chongwei with seven hundred horsemen to guard Yun.

entries.zh: 崇威至宋州，赟登樓問崇威所以來之意，崇威曰：「澶州軍變，懼未察之，遣崇威護衛，非惡意也。」
entries.en: At Songzhou, Yun climbed a tower and asked why Chongwei had come; Chongwei said, "The Chanzhou garrison mutinied—we feared you had not heard and sent me to guard you, not to harm you."
entries.literal: When Chongwei reached Songzhou, Yun ascended a tower and asked the purpose of Chongwei's coming; Chongwei said: "There was a mutiny in the army at Chanzhou; fearing you had not grasped it, they sent Chongwei to guard you—there is no ill intent."

entries.zh: 赟召崇威，崇威不敢進。
entries.en: Yun summoned him, but Chongwei dared not come up.
entries.literal: Yun summoned Chongwei, but Chongwei did not dare enter.

entries.zh: 馮道出與崇威語，崇威乃登樓見赟。
entries.en: Feng Dao went out to speak with him, and only then did Chongwei mount the tower to see Yun.
entries.literal: Feng Dao went out to speak with Chongwei, and only then did Chongwei ascend the tower to see Yun.

entries.zh: 時護聖指揮使張令超帥步兵為赟宿衛，判官董裔說赟曰：「觀崇威瞻視舉措，必有異謀。
entries.en: Inspired Guard commander Zhang Lingchao led infantry on Yun's night watch; aide Dong Yi urged him, "From Chongwei's bearing and movements, he clearly has another plot.
entries.literal: At that time the commander of the Inspired Guard Zhang Lingchao led foot soldiers to camp as Yun's night guard; the administrative aide Dong Yi urged Yun, saying: "Judging from Chongwei's looks and movements, he must have some other design.

entries.zh: 道路皆言郭威已為天子，而陛下深入不止，禍其至哉。
entries.en: Travelers all say Guo Wei is already emperor, yet you press on—will disaster not soon arrive?
entries.literal: Everyone on the road says Guo Wei is already Son of Heaven, yet Your Majesty presses deeper without stopping—will not disaster soon arrive?

entries.zh: 請急召令超，諭以禍福，使夜以兵劫崇威所屬士卒，明日掠睢陽金帛，募士卒，北走太原。
entries.en: Summon Lingchao at once, show him the stakes, and have him seize Chongwei's men by night; tomorrow strip Suiyang of gold and silk, raise troops, and flee north to Taiyuan.
entries.literal: I beg you urgently to summon Lingchao, explain the fortune or ruin to him, and have him by night with troops seize the soldiers under Chongwei's command; tomorrow plunder the gold and silks of Suiyang, recruit soldiers, and flee north to Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 彼新定京邑，未暇追我，此策之上也。」
entries.en: They will have just taken the capital and will not have time to chase us—that is the best plan."
entries.literal: They have newly secured the capital and will have no leisure to pursue us—this is the best stratagem."

entries.zh: 赟猶豫未決。
entries.en: Yun wavered and could not decide.
entries.literal: Yun hesitated and could not decide.
